I've got the Dutch oven out. Do the apples go in before anything else?
Yes, put the cored, sliced tart apples straight into the Dutch oven.
The pot is full of apples. Should I add the cider all at once or hold some back?
Pour in the full 6 cups of apple cider with the apples.
The cider is in. What heat should I use to get it going?
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cook it over medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
While it cooks, what texture am I watching for before I move on?
Look for the apples to be fully softened so the mixture can pass smoothly through a food mill.
The apples are soft after the cooking time. How do I make it smooth for serving?
Press the softened apple mixture through a food mill, then plate it with that single off-center garnish.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Make the sauce sturdy rather than runny, and swipe on only a thin coat inside the bread or wrap for this batch.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Easy Fried Eggplant, I'm serving it in sandwiches or wraps with a creamy sauce—maybe a dip, dressing, pasta sauce, or peanut sauce. How thick should I make the sauce so the fried slices hold up?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Keep the sauce thick and spread it in a thin layer on the bread or wrap.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Easy Fried Eggplant as a sandwich or wrap with a creamy sauce, dip, dressing, pasta sauce, or peanut sauce. How should I set the texture?

messages.content: For this batch of Easy Fried Eggplant, I'm serving it in sandwiches or wraps with a creamy sauce—maybe a dip, dressing, pasta sauce, or peanut sauce. How thick should I make the sauce so the fried slices hold up?
Make the sauce sturdy rather than runny, and swipe on only a thin coat inside the bread or wrap for this batch.
Great, that's for tonight's sandwiches. Before I turn on the stove, what should I get ready?
Peel and slice 1 large eggplant, beat 3 eggs in a shallow bowl, and pour 2 cups dry bread crumbs onto a plate. Keep 2 tablespoons canola oil by the stove.
The eggplant is sliced, the eggs are beaten, and the crumbs are on a plate. What pan setup do I need?
Use a large skillet. Add the 2 tablespoons canola oil and heat it over medium-high heat until it's hot enough for frying.
While the oil heats, should I coat all the eggplant at once or work in batches?
Work a few slices at a time. Dip each eggplant slice in the beaten egg, coat it with dry bread crumbs, then place it carefully in the hot oil.
The first slices are in the skillet. How long should I leave them before flipping?
Fry them for 2 to 3 minutes on the first side, or until the underside looks golden brown.
They're browning now. Do I cook the second side the same way?
Yes. Turn them carefully and fry the other side for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's golden brown as well.
I have another batch waiting, and the crumbs are starting to clump. How do I keep the coating neat?
Let extra egg drip off before the crumb coating, press the crumbs on lightly, and avoid crowding the skillet so the coating fries instead of steaming.
The last pieces are golden. Where should they go, and when should I add the sandwich sauce?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain. When you build the sandwiches or wraps, add that thick sauce in a thin layer so it doesn't soak the crust.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this platter, brush on a very light glaze across the whole top, and keep one corner unglazed.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm doing Deep Fried Turkey as the savory centerpiece for a gift box-style dessert spread with fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, and sweets. For this one, what should the top look like?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a thin full-surface glaze and leave one corner plain.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Deep Fried Turkey for a gift box or dessert platter with fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, or desserts. How should I finish the top?

messages.content: I'm doing Deep Fried Turkey as the savory centerpiece for a gift box-style dessert spread with fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, and sweets. For this one, what should the top look like?
For this platter, brush on a very light glaze across the whole top, and keep one corner unglazed.
Perfect, that's just for this batch. Before I touch the fryer, what ingredients should I pull out?
Set out 3 gallons peanut oil for frying, or enough for your fryer, plus 1 whole 12 pound turkey with the neck and giblets removed.
The turkey is out of the fridge and the oil jug is ready. Are there any seasonings or extras I'm missing?
You'll also need 1/4 cup Creole seasoning and 1 white onion on the counter.
Got them. I'm setting up outside with the turkey fryer now—what should I do with the oil?
Pour the peanut oil into the large stockpot or turkey fryer, making sure there is still room for the turkey so the oil will not spill over.
I've left headroom in the pot. What temperature am I aiming for?
Heat the oil to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
While the oil climbs, what should I prepare for draining or resting the turkey?
Layer a large platter with food-safe paper bags so it is ready when you need it.
The platter is lined. Should I do anything to the turkey before seasoning or lowering it near the fryer?
Rinse the turkey, then pat it thoroughly dry with paper towels.
It's rinsed and I'm taking extra time drying the skin and cavity. Is that the last prep note from the recipe?

Yes. Once it is thoroughly dry, you have the listed prep covered: the 12 pound turkey, peanut oil, Creole seasoning, white onion, hot oil target, spillover space, and lined platter are all accounted for.
Help me stay organized for Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men. What comes first? I'm setting up my mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Put a large bowl on your counter and gather 1/2 cup margarine and 1/2 cup sugar so you can cream them together.
The bowl is ready, and I've measured the margarine and sugar. Should the margarine go in first?
Yes, add the margarine and sugar to the large bowl, then beat or stir them together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
It's starting to look creamy. I also have molasses nearby—how much am I using?
Measure 1/2 cup molasses, and separate 1 egg yolk. Once the margarine and sugar are smooth, stir both of those into the bowl.
The molasses and egg yolk are mixed in, and the dough base looks glossy and dark. What dry ingredients come next?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg. Stir them together well before adding them to the molasses mixture.
I've got the dry bowl mixed. Should I dump it all in or add it slowly?
Add the dry mixture gradually if that's easier to manage, stirring as you go. Keep blending until the dough is smooth and there are no dry streaks left.
The dough is thick now, and I don't see loose flour. Is this the point where it needs to rest?
Yes. Cover the bowl tightly, then chill the dough for at least one hour so it firms up before shaping the gingerbread men.
I'll cover it and put it in the refrigerator. Any quick cleanup tip while it chills?
Scrape down the mixing tools right away, especially anything with molasses on it, then wash or soak them before the dough firms up on the utensils.
I'm starting Cucumber Sandwiches; can you walk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Pull out 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese spread, 2 teaspoons ranch salad dressing mix, 12 slices pumpernickel rye bread, and 2 medium cucumbers.
I have the bread and cucumbers on the counter. Should I mix the spread before slicing anything?
Yes. In a bowl, stir the cream cheese spread together with the ranch salad dressing mix until the seasoning is evenly blended through the cream cheese.
The cream cheese is soft enough to stir. Do I need any special tool for spreading it on the pumpernickel?
A butter knife or small offset spatula works well. Spread the cream cheese mixture on one side of each of the 12 slices of pumpernickel rye bread.
All 12 slices have spread on one side. For the cucumbers, should I peel them first?
Peel the 2 medium cucumbers if you want a softer look and texture; leaving the peel on is fine too. Either way, slice them thinly.
I left some peel on for color and sliced them thin. How many bread slices get cucumber?
Arrange the cucumber slices over six of the spread-side-up bread slices, keeping the layer fairly even so the sandwiches close neatly.
The cucumbers are on six slices, and the other six slices are just spread. Do I press them together?
Place the remaining six bread slices on top, spread side down, to make the sandwiches. Press gently so they hold without squeezing out the filling.
They're assembled. Any serving tip before I put them on the tray?
If you like, trim or cut them into smaller pieces for serving, then arrange them on the tray with the cucumber layer kept level so the sandwiches stay tidy.
I pulled up Broiled Egg Salad Sandwiches. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got the hard-cooked eggs ready and chopped.
Absolutely. Put the 3 chopped hard-cooked eggs in a mixing bowl, then add 1/4 cup crushed saltine crackers, 1/4 cup chopped celery, and 1 tablespoon diced pimientos.
The crackers are crushed pretty fine, and the celery is chopped small. Should I mix those together now?
Yes, gently toss the eggs, crackers, celery, and pimientos together so they're evenly distributed without mashing the eggs too much.
That bowl looks evenly mixed. I see the recipe has a second bowl—what goes in there?
In the other bowl, combine the mayonnaise, milk, salt, garlic salt, and pepper. Stir until the dressing looks smooth and well blended.
I'm whisking it with a fork. Should it be thin or more like a creamy dressing?
Aim for creamy and spoonable. The milk loosens the mayonnaise a bit, but it should still coat the egg mixture rather than run off it.
The dressing is smooth now. Do I pour it all over the egg mixture?
Yes, add the dressing to the egg mixture and stir gently until everything is coated.
It's combined and looks like egg salad. I have muffin halves on the counter—how much goes on each one?
Spoon about 1/3 cup of the egg salad onto each muffin half, spreading it lightly so it sits evenly.
Should I grease the baking sheet before I put the muffin halves on it?
No greasing is needed. Arrange the topped muffin halves on an ungreased baking sheet, keeping them in a single layer so they're ready for broiling or serving according to your recipe plan.
Today I'm tackling Apple Pie 2. Can you help me line up the prep? I've got a big stockpot out and want to be sure I start with the right amounts.
Absolutely. Pour 1 gallon apple juice and 1 gallon apple cider into the large pot. Keep the heat off for the moment so you can mix everything evenly before bringing it up to temperature.
Both gallons are in the pot. I'm measuring the sweetener now—how much sugar goes in?
Add 3 cups white sugar to the pot, then drop in 8 cinnamon sticks. Give it a good stir so the sugar starts dissolving into the juice and cider.
The sugar is mostly dissolved, and the cinnamon sticks are floating around. Should I turn on the burner now?
Yes. Set the pot over heat and bring the mixture to a boil. Stir occasionally, especially along the bottom, so the sugar doesn't settle while it heats.
It's steaming and just starting to bubble at the edges. Do I need a hard boil?
Let it reach a full boil, then remove the pot from the heat. Once it has boiled, the next important part is cooling it completely.
I've moved it off the burner. Can I leave the cinnamon sticks in while it cools?
Yes, leave the cinnamon sticks in during the cool-down. Set the pot somewhere safe and let the juice mixture cool all the way before adding anything else.
It's still warm, but I'm trying to plan ahead. When does the grain alcohol go in?
Wait until the juice mixture is completely cool, then stir in the grain alcohol. Don't add it while the mixture is hot.
Got it. Once it's cool and the alcohol is stirred in, is there anything else I should do before serving or storing it?

After the grain alcohol is stirred in, make sure everything is evenly mixed. You can remove or leave the cinnamon sticks depending on how you plan to store or serve it, then transfer the finished Apple Pie 2 into clean containers.
I have Chocolate Covered Pretzels planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got pretzels and chocolate out, but I want to be sure I'm set up right.

Absolutely. You'll need 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. Set out a double boiler, a spoon or spatula for stirring, and wax paper for cooling the dipped pretzels.
I have the pretzels, 2 cups of semisweet chocolate chips, and the cream. Should I get the wax paper ready before heating the chocolate?
Yes, lay the wax paper out before you start melting. Once the chocolate mixture is very warm and smooth, you'll want to dip quickly, so having the cooling area ready will help.
The double boiler is on the stove. Do I add the chocolate chips and the 1 tablespoon of heavy whipping cream together?
Add them together in the top of the double boiler, then keep the heat low. Stir constantly as the semisweet chocolate chips and cream melt so the coating stays smooth.
It's starting to melt around the edges. Should I turn up the heat to speed it along?
Keep it on low heat. Just keep stirring constantly until the chocolate and cream are fully melted together; gentle heat is better for a smooth coating.
The chocolate looks smooth and glossy now. How should I dip the pretzels without making a mess?
Dip the pretzels one at a time while the mixture is still very warm. Work quickly, coat each pretzel, let excess chocolate drip back into the boiler, then move it to the wax paper.
I'm dipping from the first 10 ounce package now, and the coating is going on well. Should the pretzels touch on the wax paper?
Leave a little space between them on the wax paper so they can set cleanly and won't stick together as they cool.
All the dipped pretzels are on the wax paper. Is there anything else to do before serving them?
Let them sit on the wax paper until the chocolate has set and cooled. Once firm, they're ready to serve or move to a container.
I want to get Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I right. What should I handle first? I'm setting out the mixing bowls now.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it can heat while you mix the dough.
Oven is heating. For the wet bowl, what should I measure first?
Measure 1 cup shortening into your main mixing bowl, then add 1 cup packed brown sugar.
The shortening and brown sugar are in. Do I add the other sugar before the eggs?
Yes. Add 1/2 cup white sugar, then crack in 2 eggs. Add the vanilla too, since the recipe creams it with the shortening, sugars, and eggs.
I've got those in the bowl. What texture am I looking for when I cream it?
Beat it thoroughly until the mixture looks blended and a bit lighter, with the sugars worked into the shortening rather than sitting in streaks.
That looks creamy now. I have another bowl ready for the dry ingredients.
Use that separate bowl to mix together the dry ingredients. Leave the candies out for this part.
The dry bowl is mixed, and I kept the candies aside. Should I dump it all into the creamed mixture?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture, preferably in a couple of additions so it's easier to combine, and mix well.
The dough is coming together. Should it be completely smooth before the candies go in later?
It should be evenly mixed with no obvious dry patches. Don't worry if it's thick; once the base dough is mixed well, you're ready for the candy-coated milk chocolate pieces.

source_seed.recipe_title: Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this one, put the two garnishes in separate small containers and add them only after the bowl has been reheated.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of German Chocolate Brownie Cookies, I'm treating it like a packed brothy bowl for lunch today. What's the best way to handle the finish when I reheat it later?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Pack both garnishes separately and add them after reheating.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making German Chocolate Brownie Cookies as a packed soup, stew, bean dish, or brothy bowl. How should I finish it?

messages.content: For this batch of German Chocolate Brownie Cookies, I'm treating it like a packed brothy bowl for lunch today. What's the best way to handle the finish when I reheat it later?
For this one, put the two garnishes in separate small containers and add them only after the bowl has been reheated.
Great, that's exactly the special setup I need today. While I'm still in the kitchen, can you walk me through the cookie base from the beginning?
Set a large mixing bowl on the counter and measure in 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar and 2/3 cup shortening.
The bowl is out, and I have the brown sugar packed firmly. Do I add the liquids right away?
Yes. Add 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to that same large bowl with the brown sugar and shortening.
Should I cream those together before I deal with the eggs?
Cream the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla together until the mixture looks evenly blended and soft.
It's thick but blended. Where do the eggs fit in?
Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture, adding them to that bowl and mixing until they are fully incorporated.
The wet mixture looks smooth now. I want to keep the counter organized—what should go in the second bowl?
In another bowl, combine the dry ingredients: flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda.
The dry bowl is mixed. Should I dump it all in or work it in more gently?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix only until just blended, so the dough does not get overworked.
So once there are no dry streaks, I should stop mixing?
Exactly. Stop as soon as the flour and cocoa mixture is incorporated into the creamed mixture and the dough looks just blended.
I'm making Almond Buttercrunch today. Can you guide me while I set up the pan and ingredients?

Absolutely. Butter a large cookie sheet before the candy gets hot, because you'll need somewhere ready to pour it. For the ingredients, measure out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips.
The cookie sheet is buttered, and I've measured the butter and sugar. Should the almonds go in right away?
Yes. Put the butter, the 2 cups white sugar, and the 1 cup chopped almonds into a saucepan over low heat. Use a pan with enough room for the mixture to boil without crowding.
They're in the saucepan over low heat. Do I keep moving it with a spoon while the butter melts?
Keep stirring constantly as it melts and comes together. Stay with it until the mixture reaches a boil.
It's starting to bubble around the edges and the sugar mixture looks more fluid. What should I watch for next?
Once it is boiling, stop stirring. Don't shake or jostle the saucepan from here; let the heat do the work.
Got it. I'll leave it alone. What temperature am I aiming for on the candy thermometer?
Heat it to 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. That's the hard-crack stage for this buttercrunch.
If my thermometer seems slow, is there another way to check that stage?
Yes. Drop a small amount of the syrup into cold water. It should form hard, brittle threads; that means it has reached the right texture.
It's at 305 degrees F and the cold-water drop snapped into brittle threads. How do I get it out of the pan safely?

Carefully pour the hot mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet you prepared. Tilt the pan only as needed and keep your hands clear of the syrup. The 2 cups milk chocolate chips are part of your measured ingredients, so keep them nearby for serving or any topping step you plan to use, but the recipe's listed cooking instructions end with pouring the candy onto the buttered sheet.
I'm making Eggplant Mixed Grill and want to get the marinade started before the vegetables go in. Can you guide me?
Absolutely. Set out a large resealable plastic bag and add 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil.
The herbs and oil are in the bag. What else goes into that marinade?
Add the vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic to the same bag, then gently work the bag or stir inside it so the oil, herbs, and seasonings are mixed together.
The marinade smells good. I've got onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and both bell peppers ready on the counter.
Great. Put the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper into the bag with the marinade.
They're all in, but the bag is pretty full. Should I just close it and shake it?
Seal the bag well, then turn it gently instead of shaking hard so the vegetables get coated without tearing. Place it in the refrigerator to marinate for 2 hours, turning it occasionally.
It's in the fridge. When should I deal with the grill?
Toward the end of the marinating time, preheat the grill for high heat so it's ready when the vegetables come out of the refrigerator.
The 2 hours are almost up and the grill is heating. Anything to do before the vegetables hit the grate?
Yes—lightly oil the grill grate before adding the marinated vegetables. That helps reduce sticking, especially with the eggplant and peppers.
The grate is oiled. Do I need any more marinade prep before grilling?
No extra marinade step is needed. Once the vegetables are coated, marinated, the grill is on high heat, and the grate is lightly oiled, you're ready to grill the Eggplant Mixed Grill.
I want to get Chicken with Vegetables right. What should I handle first?
Absolutely. Set up your slow cooker and gather 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms, 4 skinless chicken drumsticks, 4 skinless chicken thighs, and 4 sliced celery ribs.
The slow cooker is on the counter, and I have the mushrooms and chicken ready. Should the chicken go in whole?
Yes, keep the drumsticks and thighs whole, with the skin removed. Place the mushrooms into the slow cooker, then add the chicken pieces on top or nestled among them.
They're in. The celery is sliced too. What other vegetables and seasonings go with it?
Add the sliced celery along with zucchini, carrots, onion, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper. Spread everything around so the vegetables and liquid are evenly distributed.
I've added the vegetables, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper. Should I stir it a lot?
A gentle stir around the edges is enough. Try not to break up the chicken; just make sure the seasonings and liquid are worked through the vegetables.
The lid is on. What setting and timing should I use?
Keep the pot covered and cook on low for 5 hours, stopping once the chicken is fully cooked and the meat juices run clear.
If I check it later, what should I look for besides the juices running clear?
The chicken should be tender, the vegetables softened, and the pieces should lift out easily without looking pink near the bone.
It's done and smells good. How do I serve it without everything cooling off?
Remove the chicken and vegetables from the slow cooker and keep them warm until serving. Spoon some of the cooking liquid over the top if you want it moist.
I'm getting ready for Chocolate Covered Pretzels. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got pretzels on the counter and want to set up before melting anything.

Absolutely. You'll need 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. Set out wax paper too, since the coated pretzels need a place to cool and set.
I have the pretzels and chocolate chips. For melting, should I use a double boiler instead of a regular saucepan?
Yes, use a double boiler over low heat. Add the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream, then stir constantly so the chocolate melts smoothly without scorching.
The cream is measured, and the water underneath is warm. How smooth should the chocolate get before I start dipping?
Wait until the chocolate and cream are fully melted together and glossy. Keep it over low heat and keep stirring; the mixture should stay very warm for dipping.
It's melted and shiny now. I'm worried the pretzels will break if I leave them in too long.
Dip them one at a time and work quickly. You only need each pretzel in the warm chocolate long enough to coat it, then lift it out and let any extra chocolate drip back into the boiler.
I've dipped a few, but the chocolate is starting to thicken around the edges. Should I pause?
Keep the mixture gently warm over the double boiler and stir it back together. Since the recipe relies on dipping while it's still very warm, a little steady heat will make the coating easier.
The coated pretzels are ready to come off my fork. Where should I put them so they don't stick?
Lay each coated pretzel on wax paper in a single layer. Give them a little space so the chocolate can set cleanly as they cool.
They're all on the wax paper now. Do I need to do anything else before serving?
Just let the chocolate-covered pretzels cool and set on the wax paper. Once the coating feels firm, they're ready to serve or store.
I'm planning Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon for dinner. Can you help me get set up before I start soaking anything?
Absolutely. You'll need a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank and 6 salmon fillets, each about 4 ounces. Make sure the plank is untreated since it will be going on the grill with the fish.
I found the plank and the salmon. What else should be on the counter?
Set out 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil and 1 large red onion, chopped. You'll also want coarse salt ready for the plank once it goes onto the grill.
The onion is chopped. Should I oil the salmon now or deal with the cedar plank first?
Start with the plank. Submerge the untreated cedar plank fully in water so it can absorb moisture before grilling.
It's floating a bit in the sink. How long does it actually need to stay under water?
Soak it for approximately 12 hours, or overnight. If it wants to float, weigh it down with a bowl or pan so the whole plank stays submerged.
The plank soaked overnight and the salmon fillets are still chilled. What should I do at the grill?
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat. Let it get properly hot before you put the cedar plank on.
The grill is hot. Do I put the salmon on the plank first, or warm the plank by itself?
Place the prepared plank on the grill first, then sprinkle it with coarse salt.
The salted plank is on the grill. Any quick check before I bring over the 6 fillets and the olive oil?

Keep the plank positioned securely on the hot grill and have the 6 4-ounce salmon fillets, the 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, and the chopped red onion ready beside you so you can continue without leaving the grill unattended.
Garlic Chicken Stir Fry is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a wok out and want to keep the timing tight.
Absolutely. Set up your ingredients before the heat goes on: 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped.
The garlic, ginger, and green onions are prepped. Should the peanut oil go in before the wok is hot?
Add the peanut oil to the wok or a large skillet and heat it until it's very hot. You're looking for the oil to just begin to smoke.
It's starting to smoke lightly. I don't want the garlic to burn—what goes in right now?
Move quickly here: stir in 2 cloves of the minced garlic, the grated ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving as soon as it hits the oil.
The aromatics are sizzling hard and I'm stirring constantly. How long should this part take?
Stir fry until the green onion turns translucent, about 2 minutes. Keep the heat high and the motion steady.
The onions look softer and a little translucent now. Is this when the chicken goes in?
Yes. Add the chicken to the wok and stir it through the aromatics so the pieces spread out and cook evenly.
The chicken pieces are in. What visual cue should I use instead of guessing?
Stir until the chicken turns opaque all over, about 3 minutes. Keep tossing and scraping the wok so nothing sits in one spot too long.
The chicken is opaque and the green onions are mixed through. Anything else before I serve it?
Once the chicken is opaque after that quick stir fry, take it off the heat and serve it right away while the garlic, ginger, and green onions are still bright and aromatic.
Can you talk me through Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip? I'm setting out the casserole dish and want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish, and start by getting the creamy base ready: 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream.
Mayonnaise and sour cream are on the counter. What should I prep from the pantry and cans?
You'll need 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, plus 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts. Drain the artichokes well and chop them before they go in.
The artichokes are drained and chopped. Should I turn the oven on before mixing?
Yes, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's hot by the time the dip is assembled.
Oven is heating. Do I mix this in a bowl first or straight in the baking dish?
Mix it right in the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish if there's room. Add the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat.
I'm folding it together now. Should the crab be completely broken up?
Fold gently so the crab meat is evenly distributed but not mashed. The mixture should look creamy, with artichoke pieces and crab spread throughout.
It's mixed and spread in the dish. Do I need foil or a lid?
Leave it uncovered. Bake the dip at 350 degrees F for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, what should I do for serving?
Take it out carefully and serve immediately while it's hot and creamy.
I'm setting up for Chili For Two; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got a small saucepan ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can of chili beans. Keep the beans undrained since the liquid goes into the chili.
I have the beef and onion measured, and the garlic is minced. Should I open the beans now or wait?
You can open them now so they're ready, but don't add them yet. Start by putting the beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic into the saucepan over medium heat.
The beef is in the pan with the onion and garlic. How cooked should it get before I add anything else?
Cook it until the meat is no longer pink, stirring and breaking up the beef as it browns. The onion can soften right alongside it.
There's a little fat in the saucepan and the beef isn't pink anymore. Do I pour that off?
Yes, drain the fat from the saucepan carefully, then return the beef, onion, and garlic mixture to the heat.
Drained and back on the burner. Is this when the chili beans go in?
Yes. Stir in the entire 15.5 ounce can of chili beans, including the liquid, until everything is evenly mixed.
The beans are stirred in. Should I keep it at medium heat?
Keep enough heat under it to bring the chili to a boil, stirring occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't stick.
It just started bubbling. What should I do for the simmer?
Reduce the heat, cover the saucepan, and let it simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the chili is heated through. Give it an occasional stir, then serve it hot.
Help me stay organized for Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks. What comes first? I'm setting out the marinade ingredients and a large resealable bag.
Absolutely. Put a medium bowl on the counter and measure in 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, and 2 tablespoons sherry.
Those are measured into the bowl. I also have fresh ginger root out—how much should I grate?
Grate 1 teaspoon fresh ginger root into the bowl. Add the garlic called for in the marinade as well, then whisk everything until the oil and soy sauce look evenly blended.
The marinade is whisked together, but the oil separates a little when it sits. Is that a problem?
That's fine for this marinade. Give it another quick whisk right before transferring it so the soy sauce, vegetable oil, sherry, ginger, and garlic are well distributed.
I've got the large resealable bag open in a bowl so it won't spill. Do I pour all the mixture in?
Yes, pour the full marinade mixture into the large resealable bag, keeping the bag supported so the liquid doesn't run over the edge.
The marinade is in the bag. Should the swordfish steaks go in one at a time or together?
Place the swordfish steaks into the bag with the mixture. If they fit without crowding, they can go in together; then seal the bag securely.
They're sealed in the bag. How much should I shake it?
Shake and turn the bag gently until the swordfish steaks are coated on all sides with the marinade. You're aiming for even coverage, not rough handling.
The steaks look coated. What's the timing from here if I'm cooking later?
Lay the sealed bag in the refrigerator and let the swordfish steaks marinate at least 4 hours. Keep it flat if you can, and turn the bag once during the chill if you want the coating to stay even.
I'm starting Chicken Tortilla Soup IV; can you walk me through the setup? I'm starting by checking what needs to be on the counter.
Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil, 6 corn tortillas that are 6 inches each and cut into 1/2 inch strips, 3 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin.
The tortillas are sliced. Do I need a skillet or a pot for the tortilla strips?
Use a large pot. Pour in 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil and warm it over medium heat.
The pot is heating. Should all the tortilla strips go in at once?
Add only half of the tortilla strips for this batch. Stir them often so they crisp evenly instead of sitting in the oil.
They're starting to firm up and get crisp around the edges. What texture am I aiming for before I pull them?
Let them get crisp throughout, with no soft bends left in the strips. Once they're crisp, lift them out of the pot.
I've taken out the first batch. Where should I put them so they don't get oily?
Drain them on paper towels in a loose layer so the extra oil can wick away and the strips stay crisp.
The first batch is draining. I still have the other half of the tortilla strips left.
Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of vegetable oil to the pot, then cook the remaining tortilla strips the same way, stirring often until crisp.
Second batch is crisp now. Do I mix these into the broth right away?
For this part, set the crisp tortilla strips aside after draining them on paper towels. Keep the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready for the soup base.
Let's work through Chicken Tortilla Soup IV today. Where should I begin? I've got my pot out and want to start with the tortilla strips.

Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil, 6 corn tortillas that are 6 inches each, 3 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin. Cut the tortillas into 1/2 inch strips before you turn on the heat.
The tortillas are cut into thin strips, and I measured the oil. Do I use all 2 1/2 teaspoons at once?
Not all at once. Pour 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil into a large pot and warm it over medium heat.
The pot is heating on medium. Should the strips go in together or in batches?
Use batches. Add half of the tortilla strips to the pot, and stir them often so they crisp evenly instead of sitting in one spot.
They're starting to stiffen and look crisp around the edges. Should I let them get darker?
Once they're crisp, lift them out before they overbrown. Spread them on paper towels so the extra oil drains off.
The first batch is draining on paper towels. There's only a little oil left in the pot.
Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon vegetable oil to the same large pot and keep the heat at medium.
The last bit of oil is in. Do I cook the rest of the strips the same way?
Yes. Add the remaining tortilla strips and stir often until they turn crisp, matching the texture of the first batch.
The second batch is crisp now. What should I do with the strips while I get ready for the broth and cumin?
Drain this batch on paper towels too, then set all the crisp tortilla strips aside. Keep the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin nearby for the soup base.
Let's work through Dads BBQ Roast today. Where should I begin? I've got the counter cleared and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 envelopes of dry onion soup mix, and a 5 pound beef rump roast. You'll also need a small bowl, paper towels, and aluminum foil.
I found the mustard and the onion soup mix. Are the envelopes supposed to be the 1 ounce size?
Yes, use 2 dry onion soup mix envelopes, 1 ounce each. Measure the yellow mustard into the small bowl, then stir in both envelopes until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The mustard mixture is thick and speckled with the soup mix. Should I prep the foil before touching the roast?
That's a good idea. Tear off two long sheets of aluminum foil and lay them crosswise, making a plus-sign shape so the roast can sit in the center and be wrapped later.
The foil is crossed on the counter. Do I need to trim the roast or just dry it?
For this recipe, just pat the beef rump roast dry with paper towels. Getting the surface dry helps the mustard mixture cling instead of sliding off.
It's dry now, and I moved it onto the middle of the foil. Should the fat side face any particular direction?
Place it in the center in the most stable position so it won't roll while you coat it. The key instruction here is that the roast is dry and centered on the crossed foil.
Okay, it's sitting steady. How much of the mustard mixture should go on it?
Use the mustard-onion mixture generously over the roast. Spread it across the top and sides so the beef is well coated.
Some of the coating is pooling near the bottom on the foil. Should I scrape that back up?
Yes, spoon or smear any extra mixture from the foil back onto the roast so the coating stays mostly on the meat. Once it's generously covered, you're done with the prep described for Dads BBQ Roast.
Butterscotch Basketball Cookies is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a microwave-safe bowl and a mixing bowl out.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup softened butter—use real butter, no substitutes for this recipe.
The chips and softened butter are on the counter. Which sugars should I measure?
Measure 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them close to the mixing bowl since they'll be creamed with the butter.
Both sugars are measured. Should the butterscotch chips go in the mixer or the microwave first?
Microwave the butterscotch chips until melted, then let them cool for 10 minutes before adding them to anything else.
They're melted and cooling. While I wait, can I start the butter mixture?
Yes. Put the softened butter in the mixing bowl with the sugar and packed brown sugar, then cream them together until the mixture looks blended and lighter.
The butter and sugars are creamed. What should I add before the melted chips?
Add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so everything is evenly combined.
The wet ingredients are mixed in, and the melted butterscotch has cooled for the 10 minutes.
Great timing. Pour in the melted butterscotch chips and beat them into the dough until the color and texture look consistent.
It's coming together and smells very butterscotch-y. Anything I should check before moving on?
Check that there are no streaks of melted chips or unmixed butter-sugar pockets. Once it looks smooth and evenly mixed, you're through the listed prep for the cookie dough.
I have Caramel Shortbread Squares planned for today. What should I set up first? I'm setting out the ingredients and the pan.
Absolutely. You'll need 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, and 1/2 cup butter. Also have a 9 inch square baking pan ready.
I've got the 9 inch pan out. Should the oven be heating while I measure?
Yes, turn the oven on to 350 degrees F, or 176 degrees C, so it can preheat while you make the shortbread base.
The oven is heating. For the mixing bowl, which ingredients go in together?
Use a medium bowl and add the 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour.
Do I cream it smooth, or am I looking for a different texture?
Mix those together until the mixture is evenly crumbly rather than smooth. It should look like a consistent shortbread crumb mixture.
It's crumbly all the way through. How firmly should I put it into the pan?
Press the mixture into the 9 inch square baking pan in an even layer, making sure the corners are filled and the surface is fairly level.
The pan is filled and leveled. How long does it bake?
Bake it in the preheated 350 degrees F oven for 20 minutes.
While it bakes, should I do anything special with the extra butter listed?

For the steps we're following here, the baked shortbread portion uses the 2/3 cup butter, sugar, and flour mixture. Keep the listed 1/2 cup butter set aside for any later caramel layer or topping instructions you're using with these squares.
I'm setting up for Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2; what should happen before the heat goes on? I'm setting out the mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on your counter and gather the measured fats and sugars: 1 cup butter, softened; 1 cup sugar; 1 cup confectioners' sugar; and 1 cup vegetable oil.
The butter is soft, and I've got both sugars plus the oil measured. Should everything go in together?
Yes. Add the softened butter, sugar, confectioners' sugar, and vegetable oil to the large bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and well blended.
It's starting to look creamy, but the oil took a minute to work in. Is that normal?
That's fine. Keep mixing just until the butter, sugars, and oil come together evenly, with no obvious streaks of oil around the bowl.
The bowl looks uniform now. I have eggs and vanilla nearby—do those go in next?
They do. Add the eggs and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so the wet ingredients are fully incorporated.
The mixture loosened up after the eggs and vanilla. What dry ingredients should I add?
Add the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and cream of tartar. Mix them in gradually if that's easier to control, especially to keep flour from puffing out of the bowl.
I've added the dry ingredients, and the dough is thickening. Should I keep beating it hard?
Once the dry ingredients are mostly absorbed, slow down and mix only until the dough is combined. Scrape the sides of the bowl so the cinnamon and leavening are evenly distributed.
The dough looks even now. I also have pecans, but I'm not sure whether they're required.
They're optional. If you want them, stir in the pecans gently until they're spread through the dough; if not, you can leave the dough as it is.
I pulled up Gingery Fish Kabobs. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got a small saucepan out.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cups pineapple juice, 1 tablespoon cornstarch, 2 tablespoons light soy sauce with 50% less sodium, and 1 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar.
The pineapple juice and cornstarch are measured. Should the pan be on the heat yet?
Keep it off the heat for the moment. Pour the pineapple juice into the small saucepan and whisk in the cornstarch until it dissolves and there are no dry clumps.
It looks smooth in the pan now. I also have the soy sauce and vinegar nearby.
Add the light soy sauce and white vinegar to the saucepan, then stir in the garlic and ginger so everything is evenly mixed.
The garlic and ginger are in. What heat should I use for simmering?
Use medium heat and bring it to a gentle simmer, stirring often so the cornstarch thickens the sauce evenly instead of settling on the bottom.
It's starting to bubble around the edges. Do I start timing from here?
Yes. Once it is gently simmering, cook it until slightly thickened, about 7 minutes, keeping the bubbles steady rather than vigorous.
What texture am I looking for after those 7 minutes?
It should look glossy and just a bit thicker than when it started, enough to lightly coat a spoon while still being pourable.
It's lightly coating the spoon now. Should I use it hot on the kabobs?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the sauce cool before using it with the Gingery Fish Kabobs.
I'm getting ready for Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got pork chops out and want to set up the counter before I start.

Absolutely. You'll need 6 center cut pork chops with any visible fat trimmed off, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon seasoning salt, and 1 egg, beaten with the egg substitute mixture. Also set out a small bowl for the egg mixture, plus flour and bread crumbs for coating.
The chops are trimmed. Should I turn on the oven now or wait until they're coated?
Turn it on now so it's ready when the coating is done. set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Oven is heating. Do I need to wash the pork chops before seasoning?
Yes, follow the recipe here: rinse the pork chops, then pat them dry really well. Once the surface is dry, season them with the garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste.
They're rinsed and dried. I don't want the coating to slide off—anything I should watch for?
Drying them well is the big thing. After seasoning, keep your coating stations close together: flour first, then the beaten egg and egg substitute mixture in a small bowl, then bread crumbs.
I've got the small bowl ready. How much egg goes in there?
Use the 1 egg, beaten with the egg substitute mixture, and place that mixture in the small bowl for dipping.
The flour and crumbs are in separate dishes. What order should I coat each chop?
Dredge each pork chop lightly in flour, dip it into the egg mixture, then coat it liberally with bread crumbs. Press the crumbs on gently so they cling.
All 6 are breaded. Is there anything else from the recipe before they go toward the oven?
That covers the listed prep: oven at 350 degrees F/175 degrees C, chops rinsed, patted dry, seasoned, dipped in the beaten egg mixture, and coated with bread crumbs after a light flour dredge.

source_seed.recipe_title: Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version

messages.content: Before I get moving on Chicken Vegetable Stew, what should I have ready? I've got a large pot out and want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into bite size pieces, and chop 1 onion. Keep the large pot nearby since everything will go in there together.
The chicken is cut up and the onion is chopped. I still need to check the vegetables—what should I add with them?
You'll also need 1/2 pound baby carrots and 4 potatoes. If the potatoes are large, cut them into stew-friendly chunks so they cook more evenly with the chicken and carrots.
Potatoes are chopped and the baby carrots are ready. Do I brown the chicken first or just load the pot?
For this recipe, load the large pot directly with the chopped onion, chicken breast meat, baby carrots, and potatoes. Spread them out a bit so the vegetables aren't all piled on one side.
Everything is in the pot. It looks full but not overflowing—what seasoning goes in now?
Add the salt and turmeric over the ingredients. Give the pot a gentle stir so the seasoning starts to coat the chicken and vegetables.
Salt and turmeric are stirred in. I have tomato paste on the counter—does that go straight into the pot?
Dissolve the tomato paste in water first, then pour that mixture into the pot. That helps the tomato paste spread through the stew instead of staying in clumps.
The tomato paste is mixed with water and added. Should I add anything else before it cooks down?
If you'd like, season it with garlic powder and ground black pepper. Those are optional, so add them to taste rather than treating them as required.
I added a little garlic powder and black pepper. Any quick check before I let it simmer?

Make sure the chicken, onion, carrots, and potatoes are settled in the liquid with the tomato paste mixture distributed through the pot. Then cook it gently until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes and carrots are tender.
I'm making Frosted Ruby Punch for later—can you guide me through what to set out?
Absolutely. You'll need 4 cups cranberry juice, 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups lemon juice, and 1 cup orange juice. Also have a 5-cup ring mold and a punch bowl ready.
I've got the juices and sugar out. The ring mold holds 5 cups—does the cranberry juice go in by itself?
Yes, pour the 4 cups cranberry juice into the 5-cup ring mold by itself so it can freeze into the ice ring.
It's poured in. Should I cover it before it goes into the freezer?
Cover it if you can, then freeze it overnight so the cranberry ring becomes solid enough to unmold and float in the punch.
The cranberry ring is frozen now. I'm ready to mix the punch base—what goes into the bowl?
In the punch bowl, combine the 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups lemon juice, and 1 cup orange juice.
The sugar is sitting at the bottom. Do I just keep stirring?
Keep stirring until the sugar dissolves into the lemon and orange juices and the mixture no longer looks grainy.
It looks clear and smooth now. The recipe mentions ginger ale—when does that go in?
Stir in the ginger ale after the sugar has dissolved. Add it gently so you keep as much fizz as possible.
The ginger ale is mixed in. How do I get the frozen cranberry ring into the bowl without breaking it?
Remove the ice ring from the mold, loosening it carefully if needed, then float it in the punch to serve the Frosted Ruby Punch chilled.
Help me stay organized for Diegos Special Beef Stew. What comes first? I've got the slow cooker out but haven't started prepping the beef yet.

Absolutely. Set out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat, 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 teaspoons butter. You'll also want a resealable plastic bag, a skillet, and your slow cooker nearby.
The beef is on a plate, and I found the flour and a gallon-size bag. Should the beef go in dry?
Yes, keep it as dry as you can so the flour clings well. Put the cubed beef stew meat into the resealable plastic bag, then add the 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour.
The beef and flour are in the bag. I'm trying not to make a mess on the counter.
Seal the bag tightly, leaving a little air inside, then shake and turn it until the beef is evenly coated with flour. If flour collects in one corner, massage the bag gently to distribute it.
It looks coated now, with just a light flour layer on the pieces. Should I heat the skillet before adding anything?
Place the skillet over medium heat, then add the 2 tablespoons olive oil. Let it warm until the oil looks loose and glossy across the pan.
The oil is warmed. Where does the butter come in?
Add the 2 teaspoons butter to the skillet with the oil. Once it melts, swirl the pan so the fat coats the bottom evenly.
The butter has melted, and the pan is ready. Do I dump in all the beef at once?
Add the coated beef to the skillet in a single layer if it fits. Brown the beef on all sides over medium heat, turning the pieces so each side gets color rather than just steaming.
The beef is browned around the edges and smells good. What should I do with the skillet contents now?
Transfer the browned beef from the skillet into the slow cooker. Scrape in any flavorful browned bits you can easily lift, then you're ready for the next slow-cooker stage of the stew.
I'm setting up for Cake Doughnuts; what should happen before the heat goes on? I'm setting out the mixing bowl and measuring cups now.
Absolutely. Put a large bowl on the counter and measure out 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour and 1/2 cup white sugar to start.
Flour and sugar are measured. I'm checking the cabinet for the leavener and salt—what amounts should I pull?
You'll need 1 tablespoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Keep those with the flour and sugar so the dry mix is ready.
Got them. Do the spices go in with the dry ingredients too?
Yes. In the large bowl, stir together the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, and nutmeg until everything looks evenly distributed.
The dry ingredients look mixed, and I don't see any pockets of baking powder. What should I do before adding the wet ingredients?
Make a well in the center of the dry mixture so the wet ingredients have a place to land without spilling over the sides.
There's a well in the middle. I have milk, an egg, butter, and vanilla nearby.
Pour the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla into that well, then start mixing from the center outward so the flour gradually pulls in.
It's coming together, but there are still a few dry streaks on the side of the bowl.
Scrape around the bowl and keep mixing just until the dough is well blended. Stop once it looks evenly combined rather than overworking it.
The dough looks blended now. Should I shape it right away or let it rest?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dough for 1 hour. After that rest, it should be easier to handle for the next part of the doughnut-making process.
A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got the blender out.
Absolutely. Set out 1 (10 ounce) package of frozen mixed berries, 1 (15 ounce) can of sliced peaches that you've drained, and 2 tablespoons of honey.
The berries are still frozen, and I drained the peaches. Should they both go in as-is?
Yes. Add the frozen mixed berries straight to the blender, then add the drained sliced peaches. The frozen berries help give the smoothie a thick, cold texture.
They're in the blender. The peaches are sitting on top of the berries.
Great. Drizzle in the 2 tablespoons of honey over the fruit so it can blend through evenly.
Honey is added. Do I need any liquid before blending?
For this recipe, no extra liquid is listed. Start blending with just the frozen fruit, drained canned fruit, and honey.
The blender is struggling a little at the beginning. What should I do?
Pause and scrape or nudge the fruit down toward the blades, then blend again. Use short pulses at first if your blender needs help catching the frozen berries.
It's moving better now, but I still see a few berry pieces.
Keep blending until the mixture looks smooth throughout, with no visible chunks of berries or peach slices.
It looks smooth and thick now. Is it ready to pour?
Yes, once it's smooth, the smoothie is done. Pour it into glasses and serve it right away while it's cold and thick.
I'm making Dilly Chicken and Potatoes. Can you guide me from the prep through the skillet part?
Absolutely. Have a cut-up 3 1/2 pound broiler-fryer chicken ready, plus 1 pound new potatoes cut into chunks. You'll also need a large skillet for browning everything together.
The chicken is cut up and the potatoes are in chunky pieces. What should I put next to the stove?
Set out 2 tablespoons cooking oil and 1 cup half-and-half cream. Keep salt and pepper nearby too, since they go into the cream mixture later.
I've got a large skillet on the burner. Should the heat be high to brown the chicken faster?
Use medium heat instead. Add the cooking oil, then place the chicken and potato chunks in the skillet so they can brown without scorching.
How long should I let them cook before I start moving things around?
Brown the chicken and potatoes in the oil for 10-15 minutes total, turning the pieces occasionally so the chicken gets color and the potatoes pick up some browning too.
They've browned and there are some drippings in the pan. Do I leave everything in there?
Take the chicken and potatoes out of the skillet and set them aside on a plate or platter for the moment.
The skillet has more fat than I expected. How much should stay behind?
Discard the excess drippings, but leave 1 tablespoon in the skillet. That small amount will help flavor the cream sauce.
I've left about a tablespoon. What do I stir in before bringing the chicken and potatoes back?
Pour the 1 cup half-and-half cream into the drippings, then add salt and pepper. Stir to mix it into a smooth, seasoned sauce base.
I'd like to make British Bread Pudding. Can you guide me while I get the ingredients out?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 6 1/4 cups cubed whole wheat bread and 1 1/4 cups milk. You'll also need 1 egg, beaten, and 1/3 cup butter, softened.
The bread is cubed, and the milk is measured. Should I turn the oven on before mixing?
Yes, get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it can heat while the bread soaks.
Oven is heating. What bowl size should I use for the bread and milk?
Use a large bowl so the bread has room to absorb the milk evenly. Add the cubed whole wheat bread and pour in the 1 1/4 cups milk.
It's all in the bowl. How long should I leave it before adding anything else?
Let the bread and milk sit for 5 minutes. Give it a gentle press or stir once if some pieces look dry.
The bread has soaked and looks soft. I have the beaten egg and softened butter ready.
Stir in the beaten egg and the 1/3 cup softened butter. Then add the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
Should the butter be completely blended in, or is it okay if there are small bits?
Mix until everything is well combined and the spices and fruit are distributed through the softened bread. Small traces of softened butter are fine as long as there are no large unmixed lumps.
The mixture looks evenly combined. Is there anything else before it goes into the baking dish?

That completes the listed prep: preheated oven, bread soaked with milk for 5 minutes, then egg, butter, raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon mixed in well. Transfer it to your baking dish when you're ready to bake.
I'm ready to cook Baked Salmon with Herbs. What should be ready before I begin? I'm getting my counter set up now.

Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs, 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese, and 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes. You'll also be using thyme, rosemary, salt, pepper, butter, salmon, foil, and nonstick cooking spray.
I've got the crumbs, garlic, Parmesan, and parsley measured. What pan should I use?
Use a 15-in baking pan. Line it with foil, then coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray so the salmon and crumb topping release more easily.
Pan is lined and sprayed. Should I mix the topping right in a bowl?
Yes. In a bowl, combine the soft bread crumbs, minced garlic, grated Parmesan, dried parsley flakes, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Stir until the herbs and cheese are spread through the crumbs.
The crumb mixture is together, but it looks pretty dry. Is that expected before the butter?
Yes, that's fine. Add the butter next, then toss everything until the crumbs are evenly coated rather than clumping in one spot.
Okay, the butter is mixed in and the crumbs look evenly coated. Where does the salmon go?
Place the salmon on the prepared foil-lined pan. Try to set it flat so the topping can sit evenly over the surface.
Salmon is on the pan. Should I put the crumb mixture on right away?
Yes, spoon the herb crumb mixture over the salmon and spread it gently so the bread crumbs, garlic, Parmesan, and herbs are distributed across the fish.
The topping is on. Anything I should tidy or check before it goes further?

Check that the foil edges aren't folded over the salmon, the pan is still lightly coated underneath, and loose crumbs are mostly on the fish rather than scattered around the pan. Then you're set up for baking.
Help me stay organized for Dilled Garlic. What comes first? I've got peeled garlic ready, but I want to make sure I set it up correctly.

Absolutely. You'll need 2 pounds of peeled garlic, 1 sprig of chopped fresh dill, cayenne pepper to taste, and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar. Also have sterile containers ready before you start filling them.
The containers are sterilized and on the counter. Should I pack the garlic in tightly?

Fill the sterile containers with the peeled garlic, chopped fresh dill, and cayenne pepper, leaving about an inch of space at the top. Pack the garlic in, but don't force it so tightly that the hot vinegar mixture can't flow around it.
I added the dill and a little cayenne. The jars are filled to about an inch from the top.
Good. Set those containers aside for a moment. In a medium saucepan, combine the distilled white vinegar with salt.
How much vinegar goes into the saucepan again?
Use the full 4 1/2 cups of distilled white vinegar in the saucepan, mixed with the salt.
The vinegar and salt are in the pan. Should I heat it gently or bring it up fast?
Bring the vinegar and salt mixture to a boil. Keep an eye on it since vinegar can smell sharp once it gets hot.
It's boiling now. Do I let it simmer, or pour it right away?
Once it has reached a boil, carefully pour the hot distilled white vinegar and salt mixture into the containers over the garlic, dill, and cayenne.
Should the liquid cover the garlic completely while still leaving that space at the top?
Yes, pour enough hot vinegar mixture to surround the garlic mixture while keeping the containers filled to within about an inch of the top. Work carefully because the liquid is hot.
Avocado Tzatziki is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got a bowl out but haven't started prepping yet.
Absolutely. Start by getting the main ingredients ready: 1 large avocado, peeled and pitted, and 2 cloves garlic, minced.
The avocado is ripe and the garlic is minced. Do I need lemon and dairy too?
Yes. Juice 1 lemon, and if you want it creamier, measure out 1/4 cup sour cream. The sour cream is optional.
I'm using the sour cream. What should go into the bowl together?
Add the avocado, minced garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber to your medium bowl.
How finely should the cucumber be cut before I add it?
Small pieces work best so the dip stays scoopable and mixes evenly. Once it's in the bowl, you're ready to mash everything together.
I've got everything in the bowl. Should this be chunky or totally smooth?
Mash it with a fork until smooth. A little texture is fine, but the avocado should be well blended with the lemon, garlic, sour cream, and cucumber.
It's mostly smooth now. What seasonings go in?
Stir in red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper, then mix well so the herbs and seasoning are evenly distributed.
It tastes good. Can I serve it right away, or does it need to sit?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate it for 1 hour before serving. That chill time helps the flavors come together.
I'm making Beet and Pear Puree and want to stay on track. Can you guide me while I prep?
Absolutely. Set out 8 medium beets, 1 pound unsalted butter, 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions, and 4 Bosc pears that are peeled, cored, and minced.
The beets and butter are out; I still need to finish mincing the onions and pears. Should I heat anything yet?
Yes—go ahead and set the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). While it heats, finish the onion and pear prep.
Oven is heating, and the pears are peeled and cored. What should I do with the beets before roasting?
Wash the beets well, then place them in a roasting pan. Keep them whole for this step.
They're in the roasting pan now. How long should they bake, and what am I looking for?
Bake the beets for 45 minutes to 1 hour, or until they're tender. Once they're done, set them aside to cool.
They've been roasting about 45 minutes. If they feel tender, do I take them out right away?
Yes. If they're tender at 45 minutes, remove the pan from the oven and let the beets cool before you handle them further.
The beets are cooling. I've got a large skillet ready for the next part—what goes in first?
Place the large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1 pound unsalted butter in it.
The butter is melting. Should I keep the heat at medium while I get the onions and pears nearby?
Keep it at medium and have the 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions and the 4 minced Bosc pears ready beside the skillet so you can continue smoothly.
Chicken Tacos is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got chicken breast out but want to be sure I prep it right.
Absolutely. Cut 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite-size pieces, and set a large skillet on the stove for cooking over medium heat.
The chicken is cut up. What should I put in the skillet with it?
Add the chicken to the skillet along with 1 cup lemonade, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce.
That combination is in the pan. Should I stir it before heating?
Yes, give everything a quick stir so the chicken pieces are coated and sitting in the liquid evenly, then keep the skillet over medium heat.
I'm ready to season it. Which seasonings go in?
Season the skillet with garlic powder, onion powder, and a bay leaf. Stir gently so the seasonings spread through the lemonade-lime mixture.
It's starting to bubble lightly. Do I cover it or just let it cook down?
Let it simmer steadily until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear, about 15 to 20 minutes. Stir occasionally so the bite-size pieces cook evenly.
I'm about halfway through that simmer. When should I deal with the tortillas?
While the chicken finishes, warm the tortillas in the oven or microwave until they're soft and easy to fold.
The chicken looks cooked through and the tortillas are soft. Anything to check before serving?
Check that the chicken pieces are no longer pink in the center and that the juices run clear. Remove the bay leaf, then spoon the chicken into the warm tortillas for your Chicken Tacos.
I'm starting Easy Pot Roast; can you walk me through the setup? I've got the chuck roast out but want to make sure I'm set up right.

Absolutely. You'll need a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast, 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. You'll also want a medium sized oven bag ready.
I have the roast, water, soup mix, and Worcestershire sauce. Should the oven be heating before I prep the meat?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. While it heats, you can set the oven bag in a baking dish so it's easier to load.
The oven is heating. For scoring the roast, how much cutting am I doing?
Make shallow cuts across the top and sides of the roast. You're just scoring the surface, not slicing deeply into it, then place the roast in the medium sized oven bag.
The roast is scored and in the bag. Do I mix the liquid separately or pour everything in one at a time?
Mix it separately: combine the 2 cups water, the dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce until blended, then pour that mixture over the roast in the bag.
The sauce is in. I was planning to add vegetables too; where should they go?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag so they sit in the flavorful liquid as the roast cooks.
Should I put any of the vegetables on top of the roast, or keep them around the sides?
Keep them mostly around the sides of the meat. That leaves the scored top exposed to the sauce while the vegetables cook alongside it.
Everything is in the oven bag now. Anything I should check before it goes into the oven?

Make sure the roast is centered, the liquid is in the bag, and the vegetables are arranged around the meat. Once the bag is properly closed according to its package directions, place the dish in the 350 degrees F oven.

Yes, heat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C. While it comes up to temperature, keep the garlic head whole and get a sharp knife ready.

Rub off only the loose outer paper, but don't separate the cloves. Slice just enough off the top of the head to expose the tops of the cloves.

Wrap it securely in aluminum foil, closed enough to trap steam around the garlic. Put the packet in the 400 degree F oven once it's sealed.

Set it for 20 minutes. It's ready when the cloves feel soft and slip from their skins when you gently push them.

Open it carefully because steam can rush out. Press a clove gently; if it slides from the skin easily and feels soft all the way through, the garlic is ready.

messages.content: I'm ready to cook Buffalo Chicken Wings I. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a deep fryer and want to keep the steps organized.
Absolutely. Set out 24 chicken wings and 2 quarts vegetable oil for deep frying. You'll also need 4 tablespoons butter, 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar, hot sauce, plus salt and pepper to taste.
The wings are ready. Should the oil go into the fryer now?
Yes. Add the vegetable oil to the deep fryer, or use a large skillet if that's what you have. Once the oil is ready for frying, cook the chicken wings until done, about 10 minutes.
I'm using the deep fryer. How do I know when to pull them?
After about 10 minutes, the wings should be cooked through and browned. Lift them out carefully and let the excess oil drain off.
They're out and draining. Do I keep the oil in the fryer or move on to the sauce?
Move on to the sauce. Remove the chicken and oil from the skillet or fryer area you were using, drain the oil safely, and reserve the cooked chicken wings.
The oil is handled and the wings are set aside. What goes into the skillet now?
Melt 4 tablespoons butter in the skillet. Once it's melted, stir in 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar and the hot sauce.
Should that sauce cook for a while, or just come together?
Just let it come together in the skillet so the butter, vinegar, and hot sauce blend smoothly. Keep the heat controlled so the butter doesn't scorch.
The sauce looks smooth. How should I finish the wings for serving?
Add the reserved wings back to the sauce and toss or coat them well. Season with salt and pepper to taste, then serve the Buffalo chicken wings while they're hot.
I'm starting BBQ Chicken Wings; can you walk me through the setup? I've got the wings out and want to make sure I mix the sauce correctly.
Absolutely. For the sauce base, measure 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce and 1 cup oyster sauce into a large bowl. Use a bowl big enough to hold the wings later, too.
The bowl is large enough. I've added those 2 sauces—what goes in with them?
Add 1/4 cup soy sauce and 1/4 cup ketchup to the same bowl. Then stir in the garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar until the marinade looks evenly blended.
Should the marinade be smooth before I add the chicken, or is it okay if the ketchup streaks a little?
Give it another quick whisk or stir until the ketchup is fully worked in and the color looks even. That helps the wings get coated consistently.
Okay, the marinade is mixed and the wings are ready beside the bowl.
Place the chicken wings into the bowl and turn them so they're coated all over. Cover the bowl well, then put it in the refrigerator to marinate for 8 hours or overnight.
I'm planning to cook them tonight after the full marinating time. What should I set up at the grill?
When you're ready to cook, preheat the grill for low heat. Give it a little time to warm evenly rather than rushing it.
The grill is heating on low. Do I need to do anything to the grate before the wings go on?
Yes—lightly oil the grill grate so the wings are less likely to stick when they hit the heat.
Got it. Any quick serving or cleanup tip while I'm waiting on the grill?
Keep the marinating bowl and any raw-chicken utensils separate from serving dishes, and wash them before reuse. Once the oiled grate is ready, you can move the marinated wings onto the grill.
I'm starting Chocolate Chews; can you walk me through the setup? I've got a saucepan and mixing bowl out, but I want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar.
The chocolate chips and sugars are measured. Should the butter be soft enough to press easily?
Yes, softened butter should give when pressed but not be melted. That will help it cream smoothly with the white sugar and packed brown sugar later.
For the chocolate, should I use the heavy saucepan now or wait until after mixing the butter?
Use the heavy saucepan now. Put the semisweet chocolate chips in it and melt them over very low heat so they don't scorch.
They're starting to soften around the edges. Do I leave them alone or keep moving them?
Stir gently as they melt so the chocolate becomes even and smooth throughout.
The chocolate looks smooth now. While it cools a bit, can I start on the butter and sugars?
Yes. In the mixing bowl, cream together the softened butter, white sugar, and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks light.
It's lighter and a little fluffy. What texture am I aiming for before adding anything else?
That light, creamy texture is right. Scrape the bowl if needed so the butter and both sugars are evenly blended.
I'm ready for the eggs. Should they go in all at once?
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing after each addition so the dough base stays smooth.
