original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Baked Fettuccine Lasagna as a single-serving recipe with stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan routes. Which route should I take?

messages.content: For tonight's single-serving Baked Fettuccine Lasagna, I can use the stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan approach. Which one fits this situation best?
Go with the stovetop approach today, then let it sit covered for a short rest before serving.
Great, I'm setting up the counter now. Which ingredients should be in reach before I turn on heat?
Have the pasta and protein ready: 12 ounces dry fettuccine pasta, plus 1 pound lean ground beef if you're using the optional beef.
The fettuccine is out, and I'm using the beef. What vegetables do I need beside the skillet?
Set out 1 cup chopped onion and 1 cup chopped red bell pepper so they're ready when you need them.
Vegetables are chopped. What pot or pan should I start with?
Put a large pot on for the pasta and fill it with lightly salted water; bring it to a boil.
The water is heating. Should I do anything with the skillet while I wait?
Yes, place a large skillet on the stove so it's ready for the beef, but focus on getting the water boiling before the pasta goes in.
The pot is boiling now. How long should the fettuccine cook?
Add the fettuccine and cook it for 8 to 10 minutes, just until al dente, then drain it.
Pasta is draining. I've got the beef next to the skillet—what heat and what texture am I looking for?
Brown the beef in the large skillet over medium heat, breaking it up as it cooks so no pink remains.
The beef is browned, and there's fat in the pan. How should I finish this part cleanly?
Drain the fat from the pan, then transfer the meat to a bowl. After that, keep the stovetop version covered briefly so it can settle before you serve.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Leave the tender herbs fairly leafy and gather them off to one side of the bowl so they stay fresh and easy to mix in as you eat.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: Tonight I'm turning Chunky Pizza Dip into a rice or noodle bowl, and I might use cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on top. What's the best way to treat those tender herbs for this bowl?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Keep the soft herbs in larger leaves and place them in a small pile at one edge of the bowl.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Chunky Pizza Dip as a rice or noodle bowl with optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. How should I handle the soft herbs?

messages.content: Tonight I'm turning Chunky Pizza Dip into a rice or noodle bowl, and I might use cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on top. What's the best way to treat those tender herbs for this bowl?
Leave the tender herbs fairly leafy and gather them off to one side of the bowl so they stay fresh and easy to mix in as you eat.
Great, I'll set the herbs aside like that. For the sauce base, what should I put near the stove before I start cooking?
Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil and mince 3 garlic cloves. Use a large saucepan or Dutch oven so the tomatoes have room to simmer down.
Garlic is minced, and the Dutch oven is on the burner. Which tomato ingredients do I need opened?
Open 2 cans of petite diced tomatoes, 14.5 ounces each, and measure 1/4 cup tomato paste so it can go in without slowing you down.
Tomatoes are open and the paste is measured. Should the oil go in cold with the garlic, or do I heat it first?
Add the olive oil and minced garlic to the pan together, then heat them until the garlic starts to sizzle and turns golden.
It's sizzling now, and the garlic is just starting to color. I don't want it to burn—what goes in right away?
Stir in the petite diced tomatoes and the tomato paste. Add the basil and oregano too, then bring everything up to a simmer.
The sauce is bubbling gently. Since I'm using it over rice or noodles, how thick should I let it get?
Let it simmer uncovered until it's thick enough for dipping, about 15 to 20 minutes. For a bowl, that should also make it cling nicely instead of running straight to the bottom.
I'm at about 15 minutes, and it's chunky but still a little loose. Should I keep reducing?
Yes, give it a few more minutes uncovered, stirring now and then, and stop once it looks spoonable and concentrated rather than watery.
It's thick now. I'm not serving all of it immediately—what should I do with the extra?
Let the extra sauce cool, then refrigerate it.
I'm making Adobo Chicken with Ginger tonight—can you guide me through it while I prep?
Absolutely. Start by getting a Dutch oven ready and cutting 1 whole chicken, about 3 pounds, into 8 pieces if it isn't already cut.
The chicken is in pieces and the Dutch oven is on the counter. What liquids should I measure?
Measure 1/2 cup soy sauce and 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar. Those will form the braising liquid for the chicken.
Measured. I also have a whole bulb of garlic—how should I prep it?
Peel the 1 bulb of garlic and crush the cloves. Have the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns nearby too, since they go into the pot with everything else.
Garlic is crushed, and I've got the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns ready. Do I add everything cold?
Yes. Put the chicken into the Dutch oven, then add the soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns all together before heating.
Everything is in the Dutch oven. What heat should I use to get it started?
Set it over medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil. Keep an eye on it so the liquid comes up steadily without boiling over.
It's starting to bubble around the edges but not fully boiling yet. Should I stir or leave it?
You can gently shift the chicken pieces so they're coated in the sauce, then let it keep coming to a full boil over medium heat.
It's boiling now. How do I cook it from here?
Reduce the heat to a simmer, cover the pot, and cook for 30 minutes. During that time, baste the chicken occasionally with the sauce so the pieces stay flavorful and evenly coated.
I'm making Best Macaroni Salad and want to get everything laid out before I boil the pasta.
Great. Set out 1 (16 ounce) package macaroni, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup cucumber that's peeled, seeded, and chopped, and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion.
Macaroni, mayo, cucumber, and dried minced onion are on the counter. Do I need a big pot and a mixing bowl?
Yes—use a large pot for the salted boiling water and a large bowl for mixing the salad once the pasta is cooled and drained.
The water is salted and boiling. How firm should I cook the macaroni?
Cook the macaroni until it's al dente, so it's tender but still has a little bite and won't get mushy in the salad.
It's cooked. Should I let it sit hot, or cool it right away?
Rinse it under cold water right away, then drain it well so the salad doesn't turn watery.
The pasta is cold and drained. I've got the large bowl ready.
Add the drained macaroni to the bowl, spoon in the 1/2 cup mayonnaise, and mix until the pasta is evenly coated.
The mayo is mixed through. When do the cucumber and dried onion go in?
Stir in the chopped cucumber and the 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. The recipe also has you stir in ham and cheese at this point.
Everything is in the bowl now. Should I do anything else before serving?
Give it one more thorough mix so the cucumber, onion, ham, and cheese are distributed evenly through the macaroni salad.
I want to make Chipotle Mayo Relish. Can you guide me through it while I get set up?
Absolutely. Pull out 1 cup light mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, 1/4 cup chopped green onion, and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish.
I found the mayo, onions, and relish. The chipotle peppers are still in the can with the adobo—do I need to prep them before blending?
Yes. Take out 2 tablespoons of the canned chipotle peppers, seed them, and mince them. Keep the adobo sauce nearby in case you want to add a little more heat and flavor.
The peppers are seeded and minced. Should I use a bowl, or does this need the food processor?
Use the food processor for the base. Add the 1 cup light mayonnaise and the minced chipotle peppers, then process until the mixture looks smooth and well blended.
It's blended and looks orange-pink. It smells smoky but not too strong.
Taste a tiny bit. If you want a bit more adobo flavor, blend in a little extra sauce; about 1/2 teaspoon is a good amount.
I added the 1/2 teaspoon of sauce and pulsed it again. What should the texture be now?
It should be creamy and mostly smooth, with the chipotle worked evenly through the mayonnaise. Once it looks blended, transfer it to a serving bowl.
It's in the bowl. Do the green onion and pickle relish go in the processor too?
Stir them in by hand instead. Add the 1/4 cup chopped green onion and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish to the bowl, then mix until they're evenly distributed.
That's mixed. I'm serving it later with sandwiches—should it sit out or go in the fridge?
Put it in the refrigerator and chill until serving. Give it a quick stir before setting it out, especially if it has been chilling for a while.
I want to make Chocolate Covered Pretzels. Can you guide me while I get everything ready?

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler, a spoon or spatula, and wax paper for cooling.
I have the pretzels and chocolate chips on the counter. The cream is measured too. How should I set up the pan?
Put the double boiler over low heat. Add the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream to the top section, then stir constantly as they melt together.
The chocolate is starting to soften, but there are still some chips showing. Should I turn the heat up?
Keep it on low heat and keep stirring. The goal is a smooth, warm coating without scorching the chocolate.
It looks glossy now and the cream seems fully mixed in. Do I start dipping right away?
Yes, while the mixture is still very warm. Dip the pretzels one at a time and work quickly so each one gets coated before the chocolate starts to thicken.
Should I drop a handful in at once, or is one at a time really better?
One at a time is better for this recipe. It gives you more even coating and helps keep the pretzels from clumping together in the chocolate.
I've dipped several, and they're a little drippy when I lift them out. Where should I put them?
Lay each coated pretzel on wax paper. Leave a bit of space between them so they can set and cool without sticking to each other.
They're all on the wax paper now. Is there anything else I need to do before serving?
Let them cool until the chocolate coating has set. Once firm, you can lift them from the wax paper and serve or store them.
I want to make Curried Winter Squash and I've already got cooked squash. Can you guide me from setup to serving?
Absolutely. Measure out 3 cups cooked, mashed winter squash into a medium microwave-safe bowl. Keep 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder nearby too.
The squash is in the bowl, and I have the curry powder measured. What else goes with it?
Add 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, plus 2 tablespoons maple syrup. Those go into the same bowl with the squash and curry powder.
Should the butter be melted before I stir it in, or can it go in solid?

It can go in as-is if it's soft enough to mix, since the microwave will heat everything through. Stir the squash, curry powder, butter or margarine, and maple syrup together in the medium bowl until the curry is evenly distributed.
It's mixed, though I still see a few small bits of butter. Is that okay before microwaving?
Yes, that's fine. Microwave the bowl on high until the squash mixture is heated through, about 5 minutes.
Do I need to stop and stir during those 5 minutes?
If your microwave heats unevenly, pause once around the middle and give it a quick stir, then continue until it's hot all the way through.
It's hot now and smells like curry and maple. The surface looks a little plain—anything to add?
If you'd like, sprinkle coconut over the top. It's optional, so you can skip it if you want the squash served just as the warm curried mixture.
I'll add a small sprinkle of coconut. How should I serve it?
Spoon it into a serving dish while it's hot, keeping the coconut on top if you added it. Then serve the Curried Winter Squash right away.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Cut the allium into a very fine dice, then give it a quick rinse and drain before you fold it in.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: For today's Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, I'm treating it like a fresh salsa, salad, relish, or raw topping, and I may use onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot. What's the best way to handle that allium?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Dice the allium very small and rinse it briefly before adding it.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip as a fresh salsa, salad, relish, or raw topping with onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot. How should I handle the allium?

messages.content: For today's Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, I'm treating it like a fresh salsa, salad, relish, or raw topping, and I may use onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot. What's the best way to handle that allium?
Cut the allium into a very fine dice, then give it a quick rinse and drain before you fold it in.
Perfect. I have the mixing bowl out, but I'm not sure whether this belongs in that or a baking dish.
Use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish for the main mix so it can go straight into the oven later.
Casserole dish is on the counter. Which creamy ingredients go in?
Add 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream to the dish, and stir them together until smooth.
That base is smooth. I have a small packet and the can of artichokes sitting here.
Stir in 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, then add 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped.
The artichokes are chopped and in. Do I need to heat the oven yet?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you finish combining everything.
Oven is heating. The dish still looks a little sparse for a crab dip.
Fold in the cheese and crab meat with the mayonnaise, sour cream, soup mix, and artichoke hearts until the mixture is evenly combined.
It's all mixed in the casserole dish. Should I cover it before baking?
Leave it uncovered and bake it for 30 minutes.
Timer's done and it's bubbling at the edges. How should I serve it?
Bring it out while it's hot and serve immediately.
I want to make Gelatin Fruit Salad. Can you guide me through it while I get everything ready?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple. Keep the pineapple undrained for this recipe.
I've got the applesauce and gelatin on the counter. Should I open the soda and pineapple now too?
Yes, open them so they're ready to add smoothly later. Since the mixture comes together quickly once the applesauce is hot, it helps to have the soda and undrained crushed pineapple nearby.
What size pan should I use for heating the applesauce?
Use a small to medium saucepan with enough room to stir in the gelatin without spilling. Pour in the 1 cup applesauce and heat it until it comes to a boil.
The applesauce is bubbling. Do I keep it on the burner when I add the gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat before adding the gelatin. Stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin until the powder is fully dissolved and the mixture looks smooth.
It's dissolved now, but it's pretty hot. How do I add the soda without it foaming over?
Pour the 12 ounce can of lemon-lime soda in slowly, stirring gently as you go. Adding it gradually will help control the fizz.
Soda is mixed in. The pineapple can has juice with it; does all of that go in?
Yes, add the entire 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple, including the liquid. Stir just enough to distribute the fruit evenly through the gelatin mixture.
It's all combined. Should I put it in one dish or smaller cups?
Either works. Pour it into a serving dish or individual cups, then refrigerate until firm. Once it has set, it's ready to serve chilled.
I want to make Chicken Fiesta Salad. Can you guide me while I get the chicken and bean mixture going?

Absolutely. Set out 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, 1 packet of dry fajita seasoning that is 1.27 ounces, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, and 1 can of black beans that is 15 ounces, rinsed and drained.
I have the chicken, seasoning, oil, and the rinsed black beans. The recipe also mentions corn and salsa—should I keep those near the stove?
Yes, keep the corn and salsa ready for the saucepan step. For the chicken, divide the fajita seasoning in half and rub the chicken evenly with 1/2 of it.
The chicken is coated. What pan setup do I need before it goes in?
Put a skillet over medium heat and add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil. Once the oil is hot enough to shimmer lightly, lay in the seasoned chicken.
It's in the skillet. How long should I cook it before turning?
Cook the chicken for 8 minutes on the first side, then flip it and cook another 8 minutes on the other side, or until the juices run clear.
The juices look clear now. Do I slice it right away or move on to the beans?
Set the chicken aside for the moment so it can rest while you warm the bean mixture.
I've got a large saucepan out. What goes into it?
Add the rinsed and drained black beans, the corn, the salsa, and the other 1/2 of the fajita seasoning to the large saucepan. Stir so the seasoning is distributed through the mixture.
Everything is stirred together in the saucepan. What should the heat be?
Warm it over medium heat until the mixture is heated through. Once it's warm, serve it with the cooked chicken for the Chicken Fiesta Salad.
I'm setting up for Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad; what should happen before the heat goes on? I'm starting with the skillet and chicken out.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided, and 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, about 6 ounces each.
Chicken and oil are ready. What seasonings should be on the counter before I turn on the stove?
You'll need 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning and 2 cloves garlic, crushed. Keep the garlic close to the skillet so it can go in once the chicken is cooking.
Got it. Should I use all the oil in the pan right away?
Use 1 tablespoon olive oil for the cooking step. Warm it in a large skillet over medium heat until the oil looks loose and shimmery.
The oil is warming. Do I season the chicken before it hits the pan?
Yes. Coat both sides of the chicken breasts with the Cajun seasoning, then lay them into the hot oil.
They're in the skillet and starting to sizzle. Where does the crushed garlic come in?
Stir the crushed garlic into the skillet around the chicken so it flavors the oil while the chicken cooks.
The garlic smells good. How long should I leave the chicken before flipping?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on the first side, then turn it over and cook 5 minutes on the other side.
After the second side, how do I know it's done enough to serve?
Check that the juices run clear. Once they do, take the chicken off the heat and let it rest briefly before slicing it for the salad.
I'd like to make Easy Fried Eggplant. Can you guide me while I get the ingredients and pan ready?

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons canola oil, 1 large eggplant that's peeled and sliced, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 cups dry bread crumbs. You'll also want a large skillet and some paper towels for draining.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced, and I have the eggs beaten in a shallow bowl. Should the crumbs go in another dish?
Yes, put the dry bread crumbs in a separate shallow dish so you can dip each eggplant slice in egg first, then coat it with crumbs.
I've got the bread crumbs set up next to the eggs. When do I heat the oil?
Pour the 2 tablespoons canola oil into a large skillet and heat it over medium-high heat. Let it get hot before you add the coated eggplant.
The skillet is heating. How do I know the slices are ready to go in?
Once each slice has been dipped in the beaten egg and then covered with bread crumbs, place it carefully into the hot oil in a single layer.
I'm coating them now. Should I crowd the pan if they don't all fit?
Avoid crowding if you can. Cook them in batches so the slices can fry evenly and brown instead of steaming.
The first batch is in the skillet. How long should each side cook?
Fry the eggplant for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, or until the coating turns golden brown.
They're golden now, and I'm taking them out. What's the best way to finish them?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels and let them drain briefly before serving.
I'm making German Chocolate Brownie Cookies and want to get the mixing right. Can you guide me from setup?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and gather 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I've got the large bowl out. Should the brown sugar be packed firmly before measuring?
Yes, pack the brown sugar into the measuring cup so you get the full 1 1/2 cups, then add it to the large bowl with the 2/3 cup shortening.
The sugar and shortening are in. Do I add the water and vanilla before creaming?
Add the 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to that same bowl, then combine everything until the mixture looks creamy and evenly blended.
It's looking creamy now. I have eggs nearby, but the ingredient list I'm using didn't show an amount.
Use the eggs called for by your full recipe, and beat them into the creamed brown sugar and shortening mixture until they're incorporated.
The eggs are mixed in and the bowl looks smoother. What should I use for the dry ingredients?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda. Stir them together so the cocoa and leavening are evenly distributed before they go into the wet mixture.
Dry bowl is mixed. Should I dump it all in or add it gradually?
Add the dry mixture into the creamed mixture and mix only until just blended. Stop once you no longer see dry streaks so the cookie dough doesn't get overworked.
The dough is combined and looks thick. Is that the stopping point for this part?

Yes, that's the right point to stop mixing for German Chocolate Brownie Cookies: the wet mixture, eggs, and dry ingredients are combined until just blended, with a thick brownie-cookie style dough ready for the next recipe step.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this lunch, tuck the soft herbs into a separate small container or bag, then add them after you open it so they stay fresh.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For today's packed-lunch version of Cosmopolitan, I'm bringing optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on the side. How should I keep those soft herbs from wilting?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Pack the soft herbs in a separate small container and add them after opening the lunch.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Cosmopolitan as a packed lunch with optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. How should I handle the soft herbs?

messages.content: For today's packed-lunch version of Cosmopolitan, I'm bringing optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on the side. How should I keep those soft herbs from wilting?
For this lunch, tuck the soft herbs into a separate small container or bag, then add them after you open it so they stay fresh.
Perfect, that's the version I'm doing today. Before the ice starts melting, what bottles and measures should I set out?
Put out the vodka and Cointreau first: you'll need 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger vodka and 1/2 fluid ounce Cointreau.
The jigger and shaker are on the counter. What smaller ingredients should I prep next?
Measure 1 teaspoon fresh lime juice and 1 1/2 fluid ounces cranberry juice, and have lots of ice ready for the shaker.
Should any of the herbs go into the shaker, or do they stay with the packed lunch part?
Keep the herbs separate for the lunch. For the Cosmopolitan itself, only the vodka, Cointreau, fresh lime juice, and cranberry juice go into the shaker with the ice.
Ice is in the shaker now. Does the pouring order matter?
No special order is needed. Pour all the measured ingredients over the ice, then seal the shaker tightly.
How forcefully should I shake it, and for about how long?
Shake it vigorously for several seconds, just until the shaker feels well chilled on the outside.
The shaker feels cold and a little frosty. What should I strain it into?
Strain the drink into a cocktail glass, leaving the ice behind in the shaker.
I have a lime peel ready. Is that the last touch before I close up the herb container?
Garnish the Cosmopolitan with a lime twist, then keep the cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions in their separate container to add after opening lunch.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Warm a little of the brine right in the pan—about a spoonful—and skip adding the chopped pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: Tonight I'm doing Crawfish Etouffee III in a warm skillet style, and I want the pickle/caper/olive/pepperoncini kind of briny note just for this batch. What's the best way to add that without making it chunky?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a spoonful of brine in the warm pan and leave the solid briny pieces out.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Crawfish Etouffee III as a warm skillet version with pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini. How should I handle the briny ingredient?

messages.content: Tonight I'm doing Crawfish Etouffee III in a warm skillet style, and I want the pickle/caper/olive/pepperoncini kind of briny note just for this batch. What's the best way to add that without making it chunky?
Warm a little of the brine right in the pan—about a spoonful—and skip adding the chopped pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces.
Perfect, that's exactly the direction I want for this one. I've got a large saucepan out; what ingredients should I prep first?
Chop 1 onion, then set out 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed tomato soup so it's ready to go in after the onion softens.
The onion is chopped and the tomato soup is open. Which cans should I grab before I turn on the heat?
You'll need 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup and 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers.
All three cans are beside the stove. Do I add oil, or just start the onion in the saucepan?
The recipe simply says to saute the chopped onion in a large saucepan over medium heat until it turns clear, so start there and stir as it softens.
The onion is turning translucent and the pan is warm. Is this where the brine goes in?
Yes, add that spoonful of brine now while the pan is warm, stir it through the onion, and keep the solid briny pieces out.
Brine is stirred in. Should the soups and tomatoes all go in together?
Add the condensed tomato soup, the condensed cream of mushroom soup, and the diced tomatoes with green chile peppers to the saucepan, then stir until the mixture looks even.
It's combined and bubbling gently. How long should I let this part cook before the crawfish?
Keep it at a gentle simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally so the soups don't stick to the bottom.
The 15 minutes are up and the sauce has thickened. What's the last move with the crawfish?
Place the crawfish into the pan, stir it into the sauce, and simmer everything for 25 minutes before serving.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this version, add just the smallest pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Cindis Egg Rolls, I'm turning them into a chilled fruit dessert and I only want that sweet-spiced angle today. If I have cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, and nutmeg nearby, what should go in?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Cindis Egg Rolls as a chilled fruit dessert with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. How should I use the warm spices?

messages.content: For this batch of Cindis Egg Rolls, I'm turning them into a chilled fruit dessert and I only want that sweet-spiced angle today. If I have cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, and nutmeg nearby, what should go in?
For this version, add just the smallest pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
Perfect, that keeps it light for serving cold. Before I start cooking, what should I set on the counter?
Set out 1 pound ground pork and 4 cups shredded cabbage first, since those anchor the filling prep.
The pork and cabbage are out. I'm clearing space beside the cutting board—what produce comes next?
Add 1 large shredded carrot and 1/2 green bell pepper cut into thin strips to your prep area.
Carrot is shredded and the pepper is sliced thin. Should I heat the wok now?
Yes. Put a large wok over medium-high heat, then cook the ground pork in it until it's cooked through.
The pork is cooked and there's some liquid in the wok. Do I keep any of that?
Drain the pork, then set it aside while you handle the vegetable mixture.
Pork is drained. I've got a large bowl ready—what goes into it?
In the large bowl, mix the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger.
I added the vegetables and aromatics. Since this is the chilled dessert-style one, I'm using only that tiny ginger pinch.
That's right for this batch. Keep it very subtle so the cold filling doesn't taste overly spiced.
The bowl is mixed. What sauce mixture should I make before combining anything else?
In a small bowl, stir the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses together until the mixture is smooth.
I want to make Bacon Wrapped Hotdogs in the slow cooker. Can you guide me from prep through cooking?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 10 hot dogs, 15 slices of bacon, toothpicks, your slow cooker, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar.
For the hot dogs and bacon, how should I cut everything before wrapping?
Cut each hot dog into thirds. Then cut each bacon slice in half, so each hot dog piece gets wrapped with a half slice of bacon.
I've got a pile of hot dog thirds and bacon halves. Do I wrap them tightly?
Wrap each piece of hot dog with 1/2 slice of bacon snugly enough that it stays in place, but not so tight that the bacon tears.
They're wrapped, but a few are trying to unroll. Is that where the toothpicks come in?
Yes. Push a toothpick through each wrapped piece to secure the bacon around the hot dog.
All secured. Should I grease the slow cooker or just add them in?
The recipe just has you place the wrapped hot dogs into the slow cooker. Arrange them in the insert, then set it to low heat.
They're in on low. Where does the brown sugar go?
Sprinkle the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar over the hot dogs as evenly as you can so it melts down over the bacon while they cook.
How long should I leave them, and what tells me they're ready?
Let them cook on low for 5 to 6 hours, until the bacon is cooked. Before serving, remove the toothpicks or remind everyone they're in there.
I'm making Banana Bran Muffins today. What's the best place to start? I've got a muffin pan out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar first, since those get creamed together. You'll also want 3 bananas mashed and 1/4 cup milk ready nearby.
The butter is soft and the brown sugar is measured. Should I start the oven before I mash the bananas?
Yes, bring the oven up to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) now so it can heat while you prep the pan and batter.
Oven is heating. For the pan, is greasing enough or should I use liners?
Either works for this recipe: grease the muffin pan well or line the cups with paper muffin liners. Liners make cleanup easier, but a greased pan is fine.
I'll use liners. The bananas are mashed too—should they be totally smooth?
They can be mostly mashed with a few small soft lumps. Once the pan is lined, put the 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar into a large mixing bowl.
They're in the bowl. What texture should I get before adding anything else?
Cream the butter and brown sugar together until the mixture looks fluffy and lighter, with the sugar worked evenly through the butter.
That looks fluffy now. I have the mashed bananas and 1/4 cup milk ready—what goes in with them?
Add the mashed bananas and 1/4 cup milk to the bowl, along with the vanilla and eggs called for in the recipe, then mix well until everything is combined.
The batter is mixed. Anything I should check before I start filling the muffin cups?
Check that there aren't streaks of butter or egg left in the bowl and that the oven is still at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Then you're ready to portion the batter into the prepared muffin pan.
I want to make Broccoli Cheese Crepes and I'm getting my counter set up. What should I measure for the crepe batter?
For the batter, measure 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. A blender will make the batter smooth quickly.
I've got the blender out. Do the eggs and water go in before the flour, or does it matter?
Add the eggs, water, flour, and salt to the blender together. If you want to make blending easier, put the eggs and water in first, then the flour and salt on top.
Everything is in the blender. How smooth should I make it?
Cover the blender and process until the batter looks smooth, with no dry flour streaks or obvious lumps.
The batter looks smooth now. Do I use it right away for the crepes?
Let it stand for 15 minutes before cooking. That rest helps the flour hydrate and gives you a better crepe texture.
While it rests, I see the filling step mentions onion and butter. What pan should I use?
Use a small saucepan. Add the butter and saute the onion in it until the onion is tender.
The onion is softening. Should I be looking for browning or just tenderness?
Aim for tender onion rather than deep browning. A little color is fine, but keep the heat controlled so the butter doesn't burn.
The onion is tender now, and I'm ready for the thickening part. What happens next?
Stir in the flour until it's blended with the onion and butter. Keep stirring so it forms an even mixture with no dry flour patches.
I'm making Cinnamon Rolls I and want to use my bread machine for the dough. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Start by checking the dough ingredients you'll measure into the machine: 1 cup warm water at 110 degrees F, 1 egg, 3 cups bread flour, and 1/4 cup white sugar.
I've got the water warming and the egg is out. Do I add the flour and sugar right away, or wait?

Add them according to your bread machine manufacturer's order. The recipe has you place the water, egg, bread flour, white sugar, powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast into the bread machine in that order if that matches your machine's guidance.
My machine says liquids first, then dry ingredients, with yeast last. The butter is measured too.

That fits well: pour in the warm water and egg, add the bread flour and white sugar with the powdered milk and salt, then add the 5 tablespoons butter and keep the yeast for the top so it stays separate until mixing begins.
Everything is in the pan and the yeast is on top. Which program should I choose?
Select the DOUGH setting and turn the bread machine on. Let it handle the mixing and rising while you make the buttery topping on the stove.
The dough cycle has started. What pan and saucepan work best for the topping?
Use a small saucepan for the topping. While the dough runs, melt 1/3 cup butter in that saucepan over gentle heat so it doesn't brown before the sugar goes in.
The butter is melted and looks smooth. What goes into it next?
Stir in 1/2 cup brown sugar and the ice cream. Bring that mixture to a boil, then cook it for 2 minutes, stirring so it stays even and doesn't scorch.
After the 2 minutes, should the sauce be thick or still pourable?
It should be glossy and pourable, a little thicker than when it started. Take it off the heat once the 2 minutes are up, and keep it ready for when the dough cycle is done.
I want to make Crawfish Etouffee III. Can you guide me while I get the saucepan ready?

Absolutely. Set out a large saucepan and keep the heat at medium when you start cooking. For ingredients, you'll need 1 chopped onion, 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed tomato soup, 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup, and 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers, plus the crawfish for the end.
I've got the onion chopped and the cans on the counter. Do I need to open everything before the pan heats?
That would help. Open the tomato soup, cream of mushroom soup, and the diced tomatoes with green chile peppers so they can go in right after the onion softens.
The saucepan is on medium heat. How long should I cook the onion, and what should it look like?
Add the chopped onion to the large saucepan and sauté it on medium heat until it turns clear and softened. Stir it now and then so it doesn't catch on the bottom.
The onion is looking translucent. Should I pour in the soups one at a time or all together?

You can add them all in now: the condensed tomato soup, the condensed cream of mushroom soup, and the 10 ounce can of diced tomatoes with green chile peppers. Stir until the mixture looks evenly combined.
Everything is mixed, but it's thick from the condensed soups. Is that okay before simmering?
Yes, that thickness is expected. Keep it over medium enough heat to bring it to a gentle simmer, then let it simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
The 15 minutes are almost up. When do the crawfish go in?
Once that 15-minute simmer is done, place the crawfish into the pan and stir them through the sauce so they're coated evenly.
Crawfish are in. Should I keep it bubbling hard or lower it?
Keep it at a steady simmer rather than a hard boil, and let the crawfish simmer in the sauce for 25 minutes. Stir occasionally, then it's ready to serve.
I'm making Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon, and I've got the figs on the counter. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Set up 6 figs, halved, along with 6 ounces goat cheese, 1/2 cup toasted chopped pecans, and 3 slices bacon cut in half. Keep toothpicks nearby for securing the wrapped figs.
The figs are halved. Should I turn on the broiler before I start filling them?
In this Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon step, yes, preheat the broiler now so it's ready when the figs are assembled.
While that heats, how much goat cheese goes into each fig half?
Divide the 6 ounces goat cheese among the fig halves. Spoon or press it into the cut side of each fig so the cheese sits neatly in the center.
The cheese is in, but it's soft. Do the pecans go on top or mixed into it?
Press the toasted, chopped pecans directly into the goat cheese on each fig half. That helps them stick and gives every bite some crunch.
I've added the pecans. The bacon pieces are half-slices; is that right for wrapping?
That's right. Use half a slice of bacon for each stuffed fig half, wrapping it around the fig and cheese filling.
Some of them want to open back up. How should I secure them?
Push a toothpick through each wrapped fig to hold the bacon in place. Try to catch both ends of the bacon with the toothpick so it stays snug.
They're all wrapped and secured. Anything else before they go under the broiler?

Give them a quick check: each fig half should be stuffed with goat cheese, pecans pressed into the cheese, wrapped with a half-slice of bacon, and secured with a toothpick. Then they're ready for the preheated broiler.

source_seed.recipe_title: Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon

messages.content: I want to make Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing for lunch. Can you guide me while I prep everything?

Absolutely. Start by setting out a medium mixing bowl for the salad and a small bowl for the dressing. For the salad base, you'll need 4 cups rotisserie chicken, skinned and boned, with the meat shredded into bite-sized pieces.
The chicken is shredded. What should I chop before it goes in the bowl?
Dice 2 medium celery ribs into small pieces, slice 2 medium green onions thin, and chop 1/4 cup honey-roasted peanuts. Add all of those to the medium bowl with the shredded chicken.
I've got the chicken, celery, green onions, and peanuts together. Should I mix it a lot?
Give it a gentle toss, just enough to distribute the celery, green onions, and peanuts through the chicken without breaking the chicken down too much.
Salad base is mixed. What goes into the dressing bowl?
In the small bowl, whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, sugar, red pepper, cilantro, mint, and 2 Tbs. water until the sugar starts to dissolve and the herbs are evenly mixed in.
The dressing smells strong from the fish sauce. Is that okay before it hits the salad?
Yes, that's expected. Once it's tossed with the chicken mixture, the lime juice, sugar, herbs, and water help balance the fish sauce so it seasons the salad rather than tasting harsh.
The dressing is whisked. Do I pour it all in at once?
Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and toss gently so everything gets coated. Scrape the small bowl so you don't leave the ginger, cilantro, or mint behind.
It's coated now. How should I plate it?

Serve the dressed chicken salad on a bed of Boston lettuce, with the suggested accompaniments alongside if you're using them. It's ready to eat once the salad is evenly dressed and settled on the lettuce.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing

messages.content: I'm making Delicious Artichoke Dip—can you guide me while I get the ingredients and dish ready?

Absolutely. Pull out 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 (14 ounce) can of artichoke hearts, drained. You'll also want a medium mixing bowl and a shallow baking dish nearby.
I've got the mayo, sour cream, Parmesan, and the drained artichokes. Should I start heating the oven now?
Yes, set the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), so it's ready when the dip is mixed.
Oven is set to 400. Do I chop the artichoke hearts or leave them whole?
If the artichoke hearts are large, give them a rough chop so they spread through the dip evenly. They don't need to be minced—bite-size pieces are perfect.
They're chopped. What goes into the bowl first?
In the medium-sized mixing bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, grated Parmesan cheese, and onion until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The base is mixed and looks creamy. Is this when the artichokes go in?
Yes. Fold in the drained artichoke hearts, then mix in the lemon juice, salt, and pepper so the seasoning is distributed through the creamy base.
Everything is mixed. How should the texture look before baking?
It should be thick, creamy, and spoonable, with the artichoke pieces suspended throughout rather than watery or runny.
Looks right. What baking dish setup do you want?
Transfer the mixture into a shallow baking dish and spread it into an even layer so it heats consistently in the oven.
I want to make Chili For Two tonight. Can you guide me while I get the saucepan ready?
Absolutely. Set a saucepan on the stove, and gather 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can of chili beans. Leave the beans undrained.
I've got the beef and onion measured. Should the garlic go in with them right away?
Yes. Put the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic into the saucepan together over medium heat.
The pan is heating. How do I know when the beef is ready?
Cook and stir until the beef is no longer pink and the onion has softened a bit. Break the meat up as it cooks so the chili has an even texture.
There's some grease in the pan now. Do I leave it for flavor?
Drain it off before you continue, keeping the cooked beef, onion, and garlic in the saucepan.
Okay, it's drained. The can says chili beans, 15.5 ounces. Do I pour in the liquid too?
Yes, add the whole can of chili beans, liquid included. Stir everything together in the saucepan.
It's mixed. Should I crank the heat up or keep it at medium?
Bring the chili to a boil, adjusting the heat as needed so it comes up steadily without scorching on the bottom.
It just started bubbling. How long should it simmer before serving?
Reduce the heat, cover the saucepan, and simmer for 10-15 minutes, until the chili is heated through. Give it an occasional stir, then serve it hot.
I'm making Chicken Fried Chops 2 and have pork chops ready. Can you guide me from the coating through the slow cooker part?

Absolutely. Set out a shallow bowl for the dredge, a skillet for browning, and your slow cooker. For the coating, measure 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground mustard, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder.
The shallow bowl is out. Do I mix all the dry ingredients together before touching the chops?
Yes. Stir the flour, salt, ground mustard, and garlic powder together until the seasoning looks evenly distributed. Then dredge each pork chop in that mixture so the surfaces are coated.
Some coating is clumping on the damp spots. Should I press it on or shake it off?
Press lightly so the flour mixture adheres, then shake off any loose excess. You want an even coating rather than thick patches that might fall off in the skillet.
Skillet is heating. The recipe says brown them in oil, but doesn't give an amount—what should I do without changing the recipe?
Use enough oil to coat the bottom of the skillet so the chops can brown. Once the oil is hot, add the dredged chops and brown them on both sides.
They're browning now. Am I trying to cook them through here or just get color?
Just focus on browning both sides in the skillet. The recipe then moves the chops into the slow cooker, so this stage is mainly for color and the fried-style coating.
Both sides have color and I've cleared space in the slow cooker. Should they go in flat?
Place the browned chops in the slow cooker. If they fit in a single layer, that's ideal; if not, arrange them as evenly as you can.
They're in. I still need to handle the soup and water—how do I add that without disturbing the coating too much?
Combine the soup and water separately, then pour the mixture over the chops in the slow cooker. Pour gently so the coating stays mostly in place.
I'm making Easy Pot Roast and have a 4 pound boneless chuck roast. Can you talk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Set the roast out, and gather 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. You'll also want a medium sized oven bag ready.
I found the oven bag and the soup mix. Should I turn the oven on before prepping the meat?
Yes, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's hot by the time the roast is bagged and sauced.
The oven is heating. Do I need to season the roast separately before it goes in the bag?
For this recipe, the dry onion and mushroom soup mix plus Worcestershire sauce provide the seasoning. Score the roast across the top and sides, then place it in the medium sized oven bag.
When you say score it, how deep should I cut?
Make shallow cuts rather than slicing deeply into the meat. You're just opening the surface a bit so the sauce can settle into the top and sides.
The roast is scored and sitting in the bag. How do I mix the liquid?
In a bowl or measuring cup, combine the 2 cups water, the 1 ounce package of dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. Stir until the mix is dispersed.
It's mixed. Should I pour it on one spot or try to coat the whole roast?
Pour it over the roast so it runs across the scored top and down the sides. Keep the roast inside the oven bag while you do this so the liquid stays with the meat.
I have some vegetables ready too. Where should they go?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag, keeping the roast centered. Once everything is settled, you're ready to close the bag according to its directions and move it to the oven.
I want to make Chicken Stuffed Buns for dinner. Can you guide me while I get the ingredients onto the counter?
Absolutely. Set out 6 large sourdough buns and 2 cups cooked, diced boneless chicken breast halves. Those will be the base and main filling.
The buns and chicken are ready. For the cheeses, what should I have softened or shredded before we start?
Have 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese softened, plus 1 cup shredded Pepper Jack cheese. The filling also calls for Parmesan cheese, garlic, and spinach, so keep those nearby too.
Got it. Should I heat the oven before I start cutting into the buns?
Yes, turn the oven on to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, so it can preheat while you prepare the buns.
The oven is heating. What's the neatest way to prep the sourdough buns without ruining the tops?
Use a serrated knife to slice the top off each bun in one piece, and keep those tops. Try to cut just low enough to make a lid without taking away too much of the bun.
The lids are off and saved. How much bread should I take out of the middle?
Hollow out each bun so it forms a sturdy shell. Leave enough bread around the sides and bottom that the filling will stay contained.
All 6 buns are hollowed out. Should I mix the filling by hand or use a mixer?

A medium bowl and a spoon or spatula are fine. Combine the diced chicken, softened cream cheese, shredded Pepper Jack cheese, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and spinach until the mixture looks evenly blended.
The filling looks creamy and everything is mixed through. Do the saved tops go back on before baking?
Yes, spoon the chicken-cheese mixture into the hollowed buns, then place the saved tops back on. Once filled, they're ready for the oven that's already at 350 degrees F.
I'm making Dads BBQ Roast and want to get the counter set up before I handle the meat.
Great. Pull out 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 envelopes of dry onion soup mix, and a 5 pound beef rump roast. You'll also want a small bowl, paper towels, and aluminum foil.
Mustard and soup mix are out. Do I mix both soup envelopes into the mustard?
Yes. Empty both 1 ounce envelopes of dry onion soup mix into the yellow mustard, then stir until the mixture looks evenly combined.
It's thick and a little grainy from the soup mix. Is that right?
That's right for this roast. The mustard will act as the coating, and the dry onion soup mix will stay a bit textured.
I have regular foil. How should I lay it out so the roast doesn't leak everywhere?
Tear off two long sheets of aluminum foil and lay them crosswise, like a plus sign, so the roast can sit in the center with plenty of foil to wrap around it.
The foil is crossed on the counter. Should I season or dry the beef before it goes on?
Pat the beef rump roast dry with paper towels, then place it right in the center of the crossed foil. The recipe's main seasoning is the mustard and onion soup mixture.
The roast is centered. Do I coat just the top, or the sides too?
Coat it generously all over with the mustard mixture, including the top and sides. Use a spoon or spatula to spread it so the beef is well covered.
There's a little mustard mixture left in the bowl. Should I save it or put it on the roast?
Put the remaining mixture onto the roast if you can spread it without making a mess. Once it's coated, keep the foil ready to bring up around the roast for the next stage.
I want to make Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon on the grill. Can you guide me through what to get ready?
Absolutely. Set out a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank and 6 salmon fillets, each 4 ounces. Make sure the plank is untreated so it is safe for grilling.
I found the plank and the salmon. Are there any other ingredients before I start soaking anything?
Yes, you'll also need 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil and 1 large red onion, chopped.
The onion is chopped. What should I do with the cedar plank?
Put the untreated cedar plank fully under water so it can soak evenly.
How long does the plank need to stay submerged?
Let it soak approximately 12 hours, or overnight. That helps it handle the high heat of the grill.
It soaked overnight, and I'm ready to cook outside. What should I do with the grill?
Preheat your outdoor grill for high heat while you keep the soaked plank nearby.
The grill is heating. Do I put the salmon on right away?
Start by placing the prepared cedar plank on the grill, then sprinkle it with coarse salt.
So the plank goes on the hot grill with coarse salt before I arrange the salmon fillets?
Yes. Once the soaked plank is on the high-heat grill and sprinkled with coarse salt, you're set up for the salmon fillets and the remaining ingredients.
I'm about to start Chocolate Chews. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a saucepan out but want to make sure I start in the right place.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. A heavy saucepan is best for melting the chocolate gently.
The chocolate chips are measured, and the butter is soft. Should the saucepan be on low?
Use very low heat. Add the semisweet chocolate chips to the heavy saucepan and let them melt slowly so they don't scorch.
They're starting to soften around the edges. Do I leave them alone or stir?
Stir them as they melt so the chocolate becomes smooth and evenly melted. Keep the heat very low the whole time.
The chocolate looks smooth now. Should I take it off the heat while I work on the butter and sugars?
Yes, move the melted chocolate off the heat. In a separate bowl, cream together the softened butter, white sugar, and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks lighter.
I'm creaming the butter with both sugars. What texture am I looking for before I stop?
It should look lighter in color and more fluffy than when you started, with the sugars worked evenly into the butter.
That looks right. I noticed eggs are part of the next instruction—how should I add them?
Beat in the eggs one at a time. Add one, mix until it's incorporated, then add the next so the mixture stays even.
Got it. Should I worry if the mixture looks a little glossy after the eggs?

A little gloss is fine after the eggs are beaten in. At this point, you've melted the 1 cup chocolate chips, creamed the 1/2 cup butter with the 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and added the eggs one at a time.
Fudge Drops is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got a heavy saucepan out, but I want to make sure I start with the right amounts.
Absolutely. Measure out 1 2/3 cups sugar and open 1 (5 ounce) can evaporated milk. Keep the saucepan nearby because those will go in together.
Sugar and evaporated milk are measured. Do I need anything else before I turn on the burner?
Yes—add 2 tablespoons butter or margarine and 1/2 teaspoon salt to your setup. You'll also want waxed paper-lined baking sheets ready for dropping the candies later.
The baking sheets are lined, and the butter and salt are beside the stove. Should everything go into the pan cold?
Yes. Put the sugar, evaporated milk, butter or margarine, and salt into the heavy saucepan before heating.
They're all in the saucepan. The mixture looks grainy from the sugar—is that okay?
That's fine at this point. Set the pan over medium heat and stir constantly as it comes up to a boil.
It's starting to bubble around the edges. Should I keep stirring or let it boil on its own?
Keep stirring constantly. Let it reach a boil over medium heat while you continue moving the mixture so it doesn't scorch.
Okay, it has come to a boil and I've kept it moving. What happens once it's boiled?
Take the saucepan off the heat, then stir in the remaining ingredients called for in your Fudge Drops recipe.
Everything is stirred in off the heat. What's the neatest way to portion them?
Use a tablespoon to drop spoonfuls of the mixture onto the waxed paper-lined baking sheets, spacing them a little so they can set without touching.
I pulled up Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got a bowl of new potatoes ready to cut.
Absolutely. Cut 1 1/2 pounds of new potatoes into wedges, and keep 4 tablespoons of butter nearby for coating them.
The potatoes are wedged. Should I prep the seasoning before the skillet gets hot?
Yes. Measure out 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, then have salt and pepper ready to add to taste.
Seasoning is ready. What temperature should the oven be at?
Set the oven to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C, so it can preheat while you handle the butter.
Oven is heating. I'm using a skillet—how hot should it be before the butter goes in?
Use a hot skillet, then melt the 4 tablespoons butter in it. Keep an eye on it so it melts without browning too much.
The butter is melted and foamy. Do I add the rosemary directly to that?
Yes, stir the fresh rosemary into the melted butter, along with salt and pepper to taste.
It smells good. Should the potatoes go into the skillet or should I pour the butter over them?
Either way is fine as long as the wedges get coated evenly with the rosemary butter. Toss them gently so all the cut sides pick up some of the butter.
They're glossy and evenly coated. Is there anything else I should check before they go into the oven?
Just make sure the potatoes are spread out after coating so they're not clumped together, and that the oven has reached 450 degrees F before you roast them.

source_seed.recipe_title: Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes

messages.content: I'd like to put together Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies as a jar gift. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need a clean wide-mouth 1 liter glass jar for layering.
The jar is washed and dry. Should I mix anything before it goes in?

Yes. In a bowl, combine the 4 cups all-purpose flour with the 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. The recipe also says to mix in salt and nutmeg at this stage, though it doesn't give amounts for those.
I whisked the flour mixture so it looks even. What goes into the jar first?
Add the 1 1/2 cups white sugar to the bottom of the clean wide-mouth 1 liter jar. Tap the jar gently on the counter so the sugar settles into a level layer.
The sugar layer is flat, but the flour mix looks like a lot. Do I add it all at once?
Spoon in the flour mixture gradually over the sugar. Pause every so often to nudge it into the corners and keep the layer even, especially near the glass where it will show.
It's all in, but the top is a bit fluffy and close to the rim.
Press the dry ingredients firmly in place so the jar packs down neatly. Use the back of a spoon or a clean flat-bottomed cup, then seal the jar once the lid fits securely.
The lid is on. I want to add the instruction card—what exactly should it say?
Write this on the card: "In a large bowl, beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy." Attach the card to the sealed jar.
Should I include anything else on the tag for clarity?

You can label it "Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies" and list the jar contents: white sugar, flour, baking powder, baking soda, plus the salt and nutmeg included in the flour mixture if you used them. Keep the mixing instruction with 1 egg and 1 cup softened butter or margarine clearly visible.
I want to make Chocolate Covered Banana Pie. Can you guide me without rushing? I've got a 9 x 13 inch pan out.
Absolutely. Start by checking the ingredients: you'll need 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers, 1/2 cup chopped pecans, 2/3 cup melted butter, and 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips.
The wafers are crushed and the pecans are chopped. Should the butter be fully melted before I mix anything?
Yes, melt the butter completely so it can coat the crumbs and pecans evenly. While you do that, heat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Oven is heating, and I have the melted butter ready. What bowl step should I do?
In a mixing bowl, combine the crushed vanilla wafer crumbs, the chopped pecans, and the melted butter or margarine. Stir until the crumbs look evenly moistened.
The mixture is damp and crumbly, not like dough. Is that right for pressing into the pan?
That's right. Transfer it into the 9 x 13 inch pan and press it firmly across the bottom so the crust is even, especially into the corners.
I pressed it down with the bottom of a measuring cup. How thick should it look before baking?
It should look like a compact, even crumb layer rather than a loose pile. Once it's pressed flat, put the pan in the 375 degrees F oven.
It's in the oven now. How long does this crust bake?
Bake it for 5 minutes at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C. It's a short bake to set the wafer-pecan crust.
Timer went off. The kitchen smells toasted; should I do anything with the chocolate chips yet?
Take the pan out and let the crust cool. Keep the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips ready for the pie, but the provided steps end with cooling the baked crust.
I'm setting up for Fruit Dip 2; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to get the ingredients lined up.
Absolutely. Set out 8 ounces cream cheese so it's soft enough to blend, plus 1/2 cup marshmallow creme. Those will make the base of the dip.
The cream cheese is softened and the marshmallow creme is measured. What else goes in?
You'll also need 2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, and 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice. Keep the juice nearby because you'll add only enough to loosen the dip to a good dipping consistency.
The whipped topping is thawed. Should I use a hand mixer or just a spoon?

A hand mixer will make it smoother, but a sturdy spoon or spatula can work if the cream cheese is soft. Blend the cream cheese, marshmallow creme, and thawed whipped topping together until the mixture looks even and creamy.
I used the hand mixer, and it's mostly smooth with a few tiny cream cheese streaks.
Give it another brief mix, scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl so the cream cheese fully combines with the marshmallow creme and whipped topping.
Okay, it's smooth now. The pineapple juice is measured in a 1/4 cup. Do I pour all of it in?
Add the unsweetened pineapple juice gradually, mixing as you go, until the dip is thin enough for fruit to scoop easily. You may use the full 1/4 cup if that gives you the texture you want.
It looks creamy and dippable after mixing in the juice. Does it need to chill before serving?
For Fruit Dip 2, cover the bowl and chill the fruit dip for 1 hour so it firms slightly and the flavors settle.
For Fruit Dip 2, after the 1 hour chill, what's the best way to serve it?
Give it a quick stir, transfer it to a serving bowl if you like, and serve it cold with fruit for dipping. Keep any leftovers covered in the refrigerator.
Grand Marnier Chicken is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got the chicken out but haven't started cutting it yet.
Absolutely. For this recipe you'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, plus 1 cup milk for soaking them after they're cut.
Milk is ready. Before I get my hands messy, what should I set out for the coating?
Set out 1 cup dry bread crumbs and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese. You can keep them nearby while we prep the chicken.
I have a cutting board and a sharp knife. How thin should I slice the chicken?
Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thirds, so the 4 breasts become 12 thin chicken fillets.
Some of the pieces are a little uneven. Do I need to flatten them more?
Yes, lightly pound each piece so the fillets are more even. They don't need to be paper-thin; just gently level them out.
Should I use a zip-top bag or plastic wrap while pounding?
Either works well. Cover the chicken with plastic wrap or place pieces in a bag, then pound lightly to keep splatter down and protect the meat.
The chicken is flattened. What kind of dish should I put it in for the milk?
Use a shallow dish that can hold the fillets in an even layer or slight overlap. Place the chicken in the dish and pour the milk over the pieces.
The milk is poured over them. How long should I leave it, and should I start cleaning up?
Let the chicken soak for 10 minutes. While it sits, you can wash the cutting board and knife, then keep the bread crumbs and Parmesan ready for the next stage.
I'm ready to cook French Spring Soup. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a large pot out and want to cook along without missing anything.
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup butter, 1 pound chopped leeks, 1 chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice ready for the later step.
The leeks are chopped, but they still look a little gritty. Should I rinse them before they go in?
Yes, rinse the chopped leeks well and drain them so grit doesn't end up in the soup. Once they're clean, keep the onion nearby too.
Leeks are washed and drained. Do I start heating the pot before adding anything?
Put the large pot over medium heat and add the 1/4 cup butter. Let it melt gently; you want it liquid and foamy, not browned.
The butter is melted and smells good. Should the leeks and onion go in together?
Yes, stir in the chopped leeks and the chopped onion together. Cook them in the butter until they turn tender, stirring so they soften evenly.
They're softening, but I'm not sure what tender should look like here.
Look for the onion to lose its sharp raw look and the leeks to become silky and softened. They don't need to brown; just keep them moving until they're tender.
Okay, the vegetables are soft and not browned. Is the water next?
Pour the 2 quarts water into the pot and stir, scraping up anything flavorful from the bottom as it loosens into the liquid.
Water is in. I have the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice beside the stove—how do I bring it together?
Mix the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice into the pot so everything is evenly distributed. Let the soup continue cooking until those additions are tender and the rice is cooked through.
I'm making Chicken Marsala with Portobello Mushrooms. Can you help me get set up before I turn anything on?
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup butter, divided, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided. You'll also need a skillet and something to cover the mushrooms once they're cooked.
I've got the butter, oil, and skillet out. Are the mushrooms and garlic the only prep items right now?
Yes—prep 4 portobello mushroom caps by slicing them, and chop 1 clove garlic. Keep them near the stove so the skillet step goes smoothly.
The mushrooms are sliced and the garlic is chopped. Should I preheat the oven yet?
For Chicken Marsala with Portobello Mushrooms, set up the bake by preheating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
Oven is heating. For the skillet, how much butter and oil go in first?
Melt 1/2 cup butter in the skillet and add 1 tablespoon vegetable oil. Keep the heat at medium so the butter melts without browning too fast.
The butter is melted and the oil is shimmering a little. Do the portobellos go in now?
Yes, add the sliced portobello mushroom caps to the skillet. Cook and stir them until they turn tender.
They're giving off moisture and getting darker. Should I add anything else or just keep stirring?
For this part, just keep cooking and stirring the mushroom slices until they're tender throughout. Adjust the heat only if the butter starts to scorch.
The mushrooms feel tender now. What do I do with them while I continue the recipe?
Remove the skillet from the heat, cover the mushrooms to keep them warm, and set them aside.
I'm making German Chocolate Brownie Cookies and want to get the mixing started. What should I set out first?
Set out 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar and 2/3 cup shortening. Those are the base for the creamed mixture, so have a large bowl ready too.
Large bowl is on the counter. Do I need the liquid ingredients right away?
Yes. Measure 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so they can go into the bowl with the brown sugar and shortening.
I've got the brown sugar, shortening, water, and vanilla measured. Should I soften the shortening or just mix it as is?

If the shortening is very firm, let it sit briefly so it mixes more easily, then combine the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla in the large bowl until the mixture looks creamy.
The mixture is creamy now. I have eggs nearby—do they go in one at a time?
Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture. Add them gradually if that helps you keep the texture smooth, and scrape the sides of the bowl as needed.
That looks smooth. I don't want to dump the dry ingredients straight into this bowl yet—what should I use?
Use a separate bowl for the dry mixture. Combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda there so they're evenly distributed before they meet the creamed mixture.
Dry bowl is mixed. Should I stir it hard once I add it, or keep it gentle?
Keep it gentle. Mix the dry mixture into the creamed mixture only until just blended, stopping when you no longer see streaks of flour or cocoa.
The dough has come together and looks uniform. Anything I should check before I clean up the bowls?
Check that the dough is evenly mixed but not overworked, with no dry pockets at the bottom or sides of the bowl. Once it's just blended, you're ready for the next part of the cookie process.
I want to make Banana Chip Muffins I. Can you help me get set up at the counter?
Absolutely. Put out a large mixing bowl and measure the dry ingredients: 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour and 1/2 cup white sugar.
Flour and sugar are in the bowl. Which small measurements come next?
Add 1 tablespoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt to that same large bowl.
Those are added. I also see chocolate chips mentioned in the directions—do they go in with the dry ingredients?
Yes, measure the chocolate chips into the large bowl with the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Everything dry is in the bowl. Should I stir gently or really combine it?
Mix it thoroughly so the baking powder and salt are evenly distributed, then make a well in the center of the dry mixture.
The well is made. I have a small bowl ready—what goes there?
Crack the egg into the small bowl and beat it until it looks frothy.
The egg is foamy now. I'm lining up the wet ingredients—what should I mix into it?
Stir the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the beaten egg.
The banana mixture is combined. Is the texture supposed to be completely smooth?
It can have some banana texture, but the egg, oil, milk, and bananas should be mixed together before you combine them with the dry bowl.
I'm making Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks and want to get the marinade started. Can you talk me through it?
Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl, a whisk, and a large resealable bag. For the marinade, you'll need 3 tablespoons soy sauce and 1/2 cup vegetable oil.
Soy sauce and oil are measured. What else goes into the bowl?
Add 2 tablespoons sherry and 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root. The recipe also has you whisk in garlic with those marinade ingredients.
The ginger is grated and everything is in the bowl. Should I whisk until it looks smooth?
Yes, whisk until the soy sauce, vegetable oil, sherry, ginger root, and garlic are well combined. It may still look a little separated because of the oil, but it should be evenly mixed.
It's mixed. I don't want to splash marinade everywhere when moving it.
Open the large resealable bag inside a bowl or measuring cup to hold it steady, then pour the marinade mixture into the bag.
The bag is filled. I have the swordfish steaks ready on a plate.
Place the swordfish steaks into the bag with the marinade, then seal it most of the way, press out extra air, and close it fully.
They're sealed in the bag. How do I make sure the fish is coated without damaging it?
Gently turn and shake the bag so the marinade coats all sides of the swordfish steaks. Use your hands to nudge the marinade around rather than squeezing the fish hard.
Looks coated. How long does it need to sit before I cook it later?
Put the sealed bag in the refrigerator and let the swordfish steaks marinate at least 4 hours. Keep the bag on a plate or in a shallow dish in case of leaks.
I want to make Black Forest Dump Cake II. Can you stay with me while I set everything up?
Absolutely. Pull out 1 (21 ounce) can cherry pie filling, 1 (16.5 ounce) can pitted dark sweet cherries, 1 (18.25 ounce) package chocolate cake mix, and 1 cup chopped walnuts.
The cans, cake mix, and walnuts are on the counter. What pan and oven setting do I need?
Use a 9x13 baking dish, and set the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Oven is heating. Should I grease the dish before the fruit goes in?
Yes. Coat the 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray so the cherry layer spreads easily and releases better later.
The dish is sprayed. Do I open both cherry cans now?
Open the cherry pie filling first. Dump the whole 21 ounce can into the prepared dish and spread it into an even layer.
It's thick, but I've got it mostly even. What should I do with the dark sweet cherries?
Add the 16.5 ounce can of pitted dark sweet cherries right over the pie filling, including the juice. Spread them across the surface too.
So I shouldn't drain that second can?
Correct, keep the juice with the cherries for this recipe. It goes into the dish along with the fruit.
The cherry layers are in the pan. I still have the chocolate cake mix and chopped walnuts ready.

Great. At this point the recipe has you set up with the cherry pie filling spread evenly and the dark sweet cherries added with their juice, while the 18.25 ounce chocolate cake mix and 1 cup chopped walnuts are ready for the next part.

messages.content: I'm about to make Chicken Tortilla Soup IV. Before I heat the pot, what should I prep first?

A light stir is fine. You're just helping the milk distribute through the bread, not trying to mash it completely.

Keep mixing until it looks evenly combined. The final direction is simply to mix well, so aim for no obvious butter streaks and a consistent speckling of fruit and spice throughout.

Yes. Once it has cooked and stirred for about 2 minutes and is thickened enough to coat the spoon, take it off the heat and you're ready to use it with the burritos.

Add the mashed bananas, the 1/4 cup milk, the vanilla, and the eggs to the bowl, then mix well until the batter comes together.

Make sure there aren't dry pockets or large streaks of butter-sugar mixture left in the bowl. Once it looks evenly mixed, you're ready to portion it into the prepared muffin pan for baking.
