messages.content: Tonight I'm making Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches as a one-off warm skillet take, and I want the tang from pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini without chunky bits. How should I handle that?
For this pan version, splash in a spoonful of the briny liquid as it warms, and keep the pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces out.
Great, just for tonight. I've got a cutting board and a baking sheet out; what vegetable prep comes first?
Prep 1 eggplant by seeding it and cutting it lengthwise into 1/4 inch slices. Then slice 1 red bell pepper into thin strips.
The eggplant slices are on the board and the pepper strips are in a bowl. What else should be nearby?
Keep salt and pepper within reach for seasoning, and set out 1 French baguette for the sandwiches.
The baguette is still wrapped, and I'm clearing counter space. Should I start heating anything?
Yes, preheat the oven broiler so it's ready when the vegetables go in.
Broiler is heating. I lined a medium baking sheet to make cleanup easier.
Arrange the eggplant and red bell pepper on the medium baking sheet, spreading them out as much as you can, then season them with salt and pepper.
For the skillet twist, when should that briny liquid come into play?
When the pan is warm, add that spoonful of brine so it can season the vegetables lightly; leave the solid briny pieces out.
The vegetables are seasoned and going under the broiler now. What texture am I watching for?
Broil them for 5 to 10 minutes, until the eggplant and pepper are tender and slightly browned.
They're soft with some browned edges. How should I get the bread ready?
Cut the French baguette in half lengthwise, then use it to build the warm eggplant and pepper sandwiches.
I'd like to make Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme. Can you guide me from the marinade setup onward?
Absolutely. For the marinade ingredients you've listed, pull out 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt or sour cream, 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce, and 1/2 teaspoon celery seed.
I have plain yogurt, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and celery seed on the counter. What bowl should I use?

Use a large bowl, since the chicken needs room to sit in the mixture and be turned to coat. Add the marinade ingredients there; the recipe direction is to combine the first eight ingredients in that bowl.
The yogurt mixture is in the large bowl. Should it be totally smooth before the chicken goes in?

Stir until the yogurt or sour cream, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and celery seed are evenly combined. It doesn't need to be whipped—just blended enough that the chicken can be coated consistently.
Okay, it looks evenly mixed. I'm ready to add the chicken.
Place the chicken in the mixture and turn each piece so it's coated all over. Use tongs or clean hands, and make sure the marinade touches every side.
The pieces are coated. Do I leave them in this same bowl overnight?
Yes. Cover the bowl well and marinate the chicken overnight in the refrigerator. Keep it chilled the whole time.
It's the next day, and I've taken the bowl out of the fridge. What should I do before coating with crumbs?
Lift the chicken out of the marinade and let the excess drip back into the bowl so the coating can stick without getting too soggy.
The chicken has drained a bit. How do I handle the crumb coating?
Coat each piece with crumbs, pressing gently so they adhere to the marinated surface. After that, the chicken is ready for the next baking step in your full recipe.
I'm ready to cook Cake Doughnuts. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a mixing bowl out but haven't measured anything yet.
Absolutely. Measure 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour and 1/2 cup white sugar, and keep the large bowl ready for the dry ingredients.
Flour and sugar are measured. What else should I put near the bowl before I start stirring?
Set out 1 tablespoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need cinnamon and nutmeg for the dry mix, plus milk, egg, butter, and vanilla for the wet ingredients.
I have the baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg. How much cinnamon goes in?
Use 1 teaspoon of cinnamon. Stir it into the large bowl with the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg until everything looks evenly combined.
The dry mixture looks even. Should I add the wet ingredients straight on top?
Make a well in the center first, like a little dip in the dry mixture. Pour the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla into that well.
The wet ingredients are sitting in the well. Do I whisk hard or fold it together?
Mix until it's well blended, using steady strokes and scraping the sides of the bowl so there aren't dry pockets of flour left.
It's coming together, but I don't want to overmix it. What texture am I looking for?
Stop once the mixture looks evenly blended and cohesive. It doesn't need extra beating beyond that.
The dough is blended. What do I do with the bowl now?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dough for 1 hour before continuing with the doughnuts.
I'm making Corned Beef Hash today. What's the best place to start? I've got a large deep skillet ready.
Absolutely. Start by getting 6 large potatoes peeled and diced, a 1 (12 ounce) can of corned beef cut into chunks, 1 medium onion chopped, and 1 cup beef broth measured out.
The potatoes are diced, and the corned beef is in chunks. Should the onion go in at the same time?
Yes, the onion goes in with everything else. Set the skillet over medium heat, then add the diced potatoes, corned beef chunks, chopped onion, and beef broth all together.
Everything is in the skillet now. It looks like the broth is just sitting around the potatoes.
That's fine. Give it a quick stir so the onion and corned beef are distributed, then cover the skillet and let it simmer over medium heat.
How do I know when it has simmered long enough?
Check the potatoes. They should be soft enough to mash easily, and most of the beef broth should have cooked away.
The potatoes are getting soft, but there's still some liquid in the bottom.
Keep it covered a bit longer and continue simmering until the liquid is almost gone. If it's bubbling too hard, lower the heat slightly so it doesn't scorch.
Now the liquid is nearly gone, and the potatoes break apart when I press them.
Great. Mix everything well in the skillet so the softened potatoes, corned beef, and onion come together into a hash.
It's mixed together and looks hearty. Is it ready to serve straight from the skillet?
Yes. Once it's well mixed and the potatoes are at that mashing consistency, serve the Corned Beef Hash warm.
I want to make Caramel Chocolate Corn. Can you guide me from the setup so I don't miss anything?
Absolutely. Start by making sure you have 16 cups popped popcorn and 1 cup roasted peanuts ready, since those form the base of the snack.
The popcorn is popped and measured, and I have the peanuts. What else should be on the counter?
You'll need 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter for the caramel mixture. The method also uses corn syrup, vanilla, and salt, so set those nearby too.
Got it. What pans or tools should I prep before the caramel starts getting sticky?
Grease your cookie sheets now so the coated popcorn can spread out without sticking later.
The cookie sheets are greased. Should the popcorn go straight onto them?
Not yet. Put the popped popcorn and roasted peanuts into a paper bag first; that gives you room to coat everything together.
Okay, the popcorn and peanuts are in the paper bag. Do I shake it now or leave it alone?
Leave the bag set aside for the moment while you make the sugar mixture.
I have a microwave-safe bowl out. What goes into it?
For this batch of Caramel Chocolate Corn, combine the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt in that microwave-safe bowl.
So the bowl has the sugar mixture, and the popcorn-peanut bag is waiting. Is that the correct stopping point for this part?
Yes. At this stage, your cookie sheets are greased, the 16 cups popcorn and 1 cup peanuts are together in the paper bag, and the caramel ingredients are combined in the microwave-safe bowl.
I'm making Basil Burgers on the outdoor grill. Can you help me get the ingredients measured before I touch the meat?

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil or enough to suit your taste, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt. You'll also need a little pepper for the mix.
Everything is measured. Should the grill be heating while I mix the patties?
Yes, preheat the outdoor grill on high heat now so it's ready when the patties are formed.
The grill is heating. I have a bowl ready—do I add everything to it at once?
Add the ground beef, Worcestershire sauce, dried basil, garlic salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix gently just until the seasonings are evenly spread through the beef.
The mixture smells good, and I don't want to overwork it. How many burgers am I shaping?
Shape the mixture into 4 burger patties. Try to keep them even in thickness so they cook at the same pace.
The 4 patties are on a plate. Should I oil the burgers or the grill grate?
Lightly oil the grill grate before the patties go on. That helps prevent sticking while the burgers sear over the high heat.
They're on the grill now. How long should I cook them before checking?
Cook them for about 6 minutes total, turning once during that time. Use a thermometer if you can—the safe internal temperature is 160 degrees F, which is 70 degrees C.
I turned them once, and the thermometer is reading 160. Can I pull them off now?
Yes, at 160 degrees F (70 degrees C) they're ready. Take the Basil Burgers off the grill, let them rest briefly, and serve them however you like.
Avocado Tzatziki is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a medium bowl out and want to make sure I prep the ingredients in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting 1 large avocado peeled and pitted, and mince 2 cloves of garlic. Keep the bowl nearby so you can add everything as it's ready.
The avocado is peeled and the garlic is minced. I also have a lemon on the counter—does that go in now?
Yes. Juice 1 lemon, then add the avocado, minced garlic, and lemon juice to the medium bowl. If you're using it, measure 1/4 cup sour cream and add that too.
I'm using the sour cream. The recipe mentions cucumber in the mixing step—should I add it with these even though I didn't see it in my ingredient list?
Add the cucumber at this point if you have it prepared, since the method calls for combining it with the avocado, garlic, lemon juice, and sour cream.
Everything is in the bowl now. Should I use a blender, or is a fork better for the texture?
Use a fork here. Mash the mixture until it's smooth, pressing the avocado into the sour cream and lemon juice so the dip comes together evenly.
It's mostly smooth, with just a few tiny bits left. What seasonings go in?
Stir in red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper. Mix well so the herbs and seasoning are spread through the avocado mixture.
The herbs are mixed in. Should I taste it before chilling, or wait until after the fridge time?
You can taste it now for salt and pepper, then cover the bowl. After that, refrigerate it for 1 hour before serving.
It's covered and going into the fridge. Any serving advice when the hour is up?
After 1 hour, give it a quick stir and serve it chilled. It should be smooth, creamy, bright from the lemon, and ready as a dip or sauce.
I'm planning to make Cinnamon Rolls I with the bread machine. Can you help me get the dough started and keep the sauce timing straight?
Absolutely. Set up your bread machine and start by checking that you have 1 cup warm water at 110 degrees F, 1 egg, 3 cups bread flour, and 1/4 cup white sugar ready.
The water is warm and I've got the egg, flour, and white sugar measured. What else goes into the machine with those?
The machine step also calls for powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast. Add everything to the bread machine in the order suggested by your manufacturer.
My machine manual says liquids first, then dry ingredients, with yeast last. Does that fit here?
Yes, that works well: water and egg can go in first, then the bread flour, white sugar, powdered milk, and salt, followed by the butter and yeast according to your machine's guidance.
Everything is loaded in the pan. Which setting am I using?
Choose the DOUGH setting, then turn the bread machine on so it can mix and rise the dough.
The dough cycle is running. Should I make the topping while it works?
Yes. While the machine runs, place a small saucepan on the stove and melt 1/3 cup butter.
The 1/3 cup butter is melted. What goes in next, and how hot should I take it?
Add 1/2 cup brown sugar and the ice cream to the melted butter. Bring the mixture to a boil.
It just started bubbling. How long do I cook the sauce once it boils?
Keep it boiling for 2 minutes, stirring as needed so it stays smooth and doesn't scorch.
I want to make Artichoke Hummus as a quick dip. Can you help me get everything ready?
Absolutely. Set up a food processor and drain 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, also called garbanzo beans. You'll also need 1 clove of garlic.
The chickpeas are drained and the garlic is peeled. What else goes into this?
Add 1/2 cup drained marinated artichoke hearts to your counter, plus 2 tablespoons lemon juice. Those are the remaining ingredients for the hummus base.
Do I need to chop the artichoke hearts or garlic before they go in the processor?
A rough chop is helpful if your processor is small, but it isn't required. Put the chickpeas, garlic, artichoke hearts, and lemon juice into the work bowl of the food processor.
Everything is in the processor bowl. The recipe mentions parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks—do those go in too?
No, keep those out of the processor. The instruction is to combine all ingredients except parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks in the food processor bowl.
Got it. How should I blend it so the texture is right?
Pulse the mixture until it turns smooth. Stop and scrape down the sides as needed so the chickpeas and artichokes blend evenly.
It looks smooth now, maybe a little thick but spreadable. What should I do with it?
Spoon the hummus out of the processor and transfer it to a serving bowl.
It's in the bowl. I'm not serving it for another hour—how do I hold it?
Cover the serving bowl and refrigerate the Artichoke Hummus until you're ready to serve.
Let's work through Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches today. Where should I begin? I've got a broiler and a sheet pan ready.
Absolutely. Start by checking the prep: you'll need 1 eggplant, seeded and sliced lengthwise into 1/4 inch slices, plus 1 red bell pepper cut into thin strips.
The eggplant is sliced lengthwise and the pepper is in strips. Should I get anything else out before turning on the heat?
Yes—keep salt and pepper nearby, and have 1 French baguette ready for the sandwich bread. You can also set out a medium baking sheet if it isn't already on the counter.
Everything is on the counter. Do I start with the broiler or arrange the vegetables first?
Preheat the oven broiler now so it's hot when the vegetables go in.
The broiler is heating. How should I lay out the eggplant and pepper?
Spread the eggplant slices and red bell pepper strips on the medium baking sheet in a fairly even layer, then season them with salt and pepper to taste.
They're seasoned on the pan. Should the sheet pan go close to the broiler?
Place it under the broiler and watch closely. Broil the vegetables for 5 to 10 minutes, until they're tender and slightly browned.
I'm a few minutes in, and the pepper edges are starting to color. What texture am I looking for on the eggplant?
The eggplant should soften through and pick up a little browning, not dry out. If it looks tender before the full 10 minutes, you can pull the pan out.
The vegetables look tender and lightly browned. What do I do with the baguette?
Cut the French baguette in half lengthwise so it's ready to hold the broiled eggplant and pepper.
I want to make Grand Marnier Chicken, but I'm only at the prep stage. Can you guide me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Put out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, 1 cup milk, 1 cup dry bread crumbs, and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese.
I have the chicken and milk ready. Should the crumbs and Parmesan be measured now too?
Yes, measure 1 cup dry bread crumbs and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese so they're ready when the chicken is done soaking.
Okay, my cutting board is out. How should I cut the chicken?
Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thirds. With 4 breast halves, that will give you 12 thin chicken fillets.
Some pieces are a little uneven after slicing. Do I need to flatten them?
Yes. Lightly pound each piece, just enough to even out the thickness without tearing the chicken.
I've pounded them gently. What kind of dish should I use for the milk?
Use a shallow dish or baking dish that can hold the fillets in a fairly even layer, then place the chicken pieces in it.
The chicken is in the dish. Do I pour all the milk over it?
Pour the full 1 cup milk over the chicken, making sure the pieces get moistened.
The fillets are sitting in the milk now. How long should they soak?
Let them soak for 10 minutes. While they sit, keep the bread crumbs and Parmesan nearby for the next coating step.
I'm cooking Black Bean Chili and I've got a large saucepan ready. Can you guide me from the start?
Absolutely. Set out 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 chopped onion, 2 red bell peppers that are seeded and chopped, and 1 jalapeno pepper that's seeded and minced.
The onion and peppers are prepped. Should the pan be hot before the oil goes in?
Put the large saucepan over medium-high heat, then heat the olive oil in it so it's ready for the vegetables.
The oil is heating. Do I add all the chopped vegetables together?
Add the onion, red bell peppers, jalapeno, mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn to the saucepan.
They're in the pan. What texture am I looking for as they cook?
Sautee them for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onions turn translucent.
The onions are starting to look clear and the peppers have softened. What seasonings go in?
Season the mixture with black pepper, cumin, and chili powder, and stir so the spices coat the vegetables evenly.
The spices smell toasted now. What goes into the chili base?
Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt, making sure the beans are mixed through the seasoned vegetables.
Everything is combined in the saucepan. Should I clean up while it settles?
Yes, wipe down the prep area and rinse the cutting board and knife while the chili comes together in the pan.
I want to make German Chocolate Brownie Cookies. Can you help me get the bowl started without getting ahead of the recipe?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and measure 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The brown sugar is packed, and I have the shortening measured. Should the water and vanilla go in with those right away?
Yes. Put the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla into the large bowl together.
They're in the bowl. What texture am I aiming for when I mix this part?
Cream them together until the mixture looks combined and softer, with the sugar and shortening worked together rather than sitting in separate streaks.
It looks creamy now. I see eggs in the directions, but I don't have a quantity listed here.
Use the eggs called for by your recipe source, then beat them into the creamed mixture until they're incorporated.
The eggs are mixed in. Do I add the flour and cocoa straight into this bowl?
Not yet. In a separate bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda so the dry ingredients are evenly distributed first.
The dry bowl looks even, with no cocoa clumps. How do I bring the two bowls together?
Add the flour-cocoa mixture to the creamed mixture and mix only until just blended. Stop once you don't see dry patches.
The dough has come together. Should I keep mixing to make it smoother?
No, stop there. For this recipe, the key is mixing the dry mixture into the creamed mixture until just blended, not beating it further.
Let's work through Grandmas Gingersnaps today. Where should I begin? I've got a mixing bowl out, but I want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.

Absolutely. For the wet base, set out 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. You'll also need the dry ingredients mentioned in the recipe: flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt.
The margarine and sugar are measured, and the egg and molasses are on the counter. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). That way it's ready by the time the dough comes together.
Oven is on. I'm using a medium bowl—do the margarine and sugar go in together?
They do. Put the 3/4 cup margarine and 1 cup white sugar into the medium bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's getting lighter and smoother, but there are still a few soft streaks of margarine. Is that okay?
Keep mixing a little longer until those streaks are mostly gone. You're aiming for an even, smooth margarine-sugar mixture before adding the egg and molasses.
Okay, it looks smooth now. Should I crack in the egg before the molasses?
Yes. Add the 1 egg, then pour in the 1/4 cup molasses, and beat everything together until it's well blended.
The mixture is glossy and smells like molasses. What do I do with the spices and dry stuff?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt. Once those dry ingredients are evenly mixed, stir them into the molasses mixture.
Should I dump all the dry mixture in at once, or add it gradually so the dough doesn't get messy?
Add it gradually if that's easier to control, stirring after each addition. Keep going just until it forms a dough and there are no dry pockets left.
I want to make A Surprise Inside French Toast. Can you guide me while I prep the filling and bread?
Absolutely. Set out 6 slices of French bread, each about 2 inches thick. You'll also need 1/4 cup ricotta cheese, 1/4 cup whipped cottage cheese, and 2 tablespoons lowfat cream cheese.
The bread is on the board, but I'm not sure how deep to cut it without slicing all the way through.
Use a small sharp knife and cut a pocket into the side of each thick slice. Keep the opening wide enough for filling, but stop before you break through the back or bottom.
I've made the pockets. A couple of them feel a little tight near the opening.
Gently open each pocket with your fingers or the tip of the knife, working slowly so the bread doesn't tear. You just want enough space inside to hold the cheese mixture.
Okay, the pockets are open. Should I mix the cheeses in a small bowl or something larger?
Use a large bowl so you have room to beat everything smooth. Add the ricotta, whipped cottage cheese, and lowfat cream cheese together.
All three cheeses are in the bowl. The cream cheese is a bit firm—will that be a problem?
It's fine; just press it against the side of the bowl as you mix. Once the cheeses start combining, add the sugar and flavoring extract, then beat until the filling looks smooth.
The mixture is smoothing out now. What texture am I aiming for before I put it in the bread?
Aim for a creamy, spreadable filling with no large lumps of cream cheese or cottage cheese. It should be soft enough to spoon into the pockets without tearing the bread.
That makes sense. Any quick cleanup or serving prep I should do before stuffing them?

Wipe any cheese from the rim of the bowl and keep a spoon or small spatula handy for filling the pockets neatly. Once the mixture is smooth, you're ready to tuck it carefully into the opened French bread slices.
I pulled up Diegos Special Beef Stew. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got the slow cooker out but want to start at the stove correctly.
Here, for this part of the stew, set out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat, 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 teaspoons butter.
The beef is cubed already. Should the flour go in a bowl, or is there an easier way to coat it?
Use a resealable plastic bag. Put the cubed beef and the flour into the bag so the coating stays contained and cleanup is easier.
Okay, beef and flour are in the bag. Do I just toss it around gently?
Seal the bag well, then shake it until the beef pieces are evenly coated with flour. You're looking for a light, even dusting rather than clumps.
The beef looks coated. I'm putting a skillet on the burner—what heat should I use?
Heat the olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Let it warm before adding the beef so the pieces brown instead of just steaming.
Do I add the butter with the oil, or hold it back?
Keep the 2 teaspoons butter ready with the other ingredients, but the listed cooking step here is to heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat before browning the beef.
The oil is shimmering a bit. Should I crowd all the beef in at once?
Add the coated beef to the skillet and brown it on all sides. If your skillet is small, give the pieces room so they can make contact with the pan.
The pieces have color on the outside now. Where do they go next?
Transfer the browned beef to the slow cooker. Scrape up any loose browned bits you can move easily from the skillet, since they'll add flavor to the stew base.
I'm making Dads BBQ Roast today and have the counter cleared. Can you guide me through the setup?

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 (1 ounce) envelopes dry onion soup mix, and 1 (5 pound) beef rump roast. You'll also want a small bowl, paper towels, and two long sheets of aluminum foil.
I've got the mustard and both onion soup mix envelopes. Should I combine them before touching the roast?
For this batch of Dads BBQ Roast, in the small bowl, stir the yellow mustard and dry onion soup mix together until the soup mix is evenly worked through the mustard.
The mixture is thick and a little grainy from the soup mix. Is that right?
That's right. It should look like a thick mustard paste with bits of onion seasoning throughout.
I'm ready with the foil, but I'm not sure how to arrange the sheets.
Lay out two long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise, making a plus-sign shape. Put them on a sturdy surface so the roast can sit in the center where the sheets overlap.
The foil is crossed and the roast is still in its wrapping. What should I do before putting it down?
Unwrap the 5 pound beef rump roast and pat it dry well with paper towels. Then place it in the center of the crossed foil.
It's on the foil now. Do I need to coat every side or just the top?
Generously coat the roast with the mustard mixture, spreading it over the top and around the sides so the surface is well covered.
Some mustard mixture is getting on the foil while I spread it. Is that a problem?
No problem. Keep most of the coating on the roast, but a little on the foil is fine. Once the roast is generously covered, you've completed the recipe's prep steps.
Help me stay organized for chicken pot pie ix. What comes first? I've got a saucepan out but want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the oven heating to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) so it's ready when you need it.
Oven is on. For the filling, how much chicken should I cube?
Use 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut into cubes.
Chicken is cubed. I'm slicing vegetables now—what amounts am I aiming for?
You'll need 1 cup sliced carrots and 1/2 cup sliced celery.
Carrots and celery are ready. Do the peas go in frozen, and how much?
Yes, use 1 cup frozen green peas. Add them with the chicken, carrots, and celery in the saucepan.
Everything is in the saucepan. Should I add broth or just water?
For this step, add water—just enough to cover the chicken and vegetables.
The water is covering everything. How long should it boil, and am I looking for anything specific?
Bring it to a boil and let it cook for 15 minutes. The chicken and vegetables should be heated through and softened for the pot pie filling.
The 15 minutes are up. What do I do with the saucepan now?
Take the saucepan off the heat, drain the chicken and vegetables, and set them aside for the next part of the pot pie.
I pulled up Delicious Artichoke Dip. Can you guide the first few moves? I'm setting things out on the counter now.
Absolutely. Pull out 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 (14 ounce) can of artichoke hearts, drained.
I've got the mayo, sour cream, Parmesan, and the drained artichokes. What should I do with the oven?
Set the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it can heat while you mix the dip.
Oven is preheating. Should I use a big bowl or something smaller?
A medium-sized mixing bowl is right. Add the mayonnaise, sour cream, grated Parmesan cheese, and onion, then stir until they look evenly combined.
The base is mixed together. The onion is in there too. Do the artichokes go in whole?
Add the drained artichoke hearts now, along with lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix them through the creamy base until everything is distributed.
It's coming together, but I'm wondering about the texture before it bakes.
It should look thick, creamy, and chunky from the artichoke hearts, not completely smooth. Just make sure there aren't big unmixed pockets of sour cream or mayonnaise.
Looks evenly mixed. What kind of dish should I put it in?
Spoon the mixture into a shallow baking dish and spread it into an even layer so it heats consistently.
It's in the shallow dish now. Anything to clean up before it goes further?
You can rinse the mixing bowl and spatula now, then keep the baking dish ready for the preheated 400 degrees F oven.
I want to make apple butter spice cake today. Can you guide me while I get the pan and ingredients set up?
Absolutely. Set your oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, and spray or grease one 9x13 inch pan so it's ready when the batter is mixed.
The oven is heating and the 9x13 pan is greased. What should I pull out for the topping?
Have 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and 1/2 cup chopped pecans measured out for the topping.
I've got the brown sugar packed and the spices measured. Do the pecans just go in with everything?
Yes. Stir the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and chopped pecans together in a bowl until the spices are evenly worked through the sugar.
The topping smells great. Should I start on the dry ingredients for the cake batter?
Yes, sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Sifting will help keep the dry mix light and evenly combined.
Dry ingredients are sifted. I've got butter and sugar in the mixing bowl—what texture am I aiming for?
Blend the butter and sugar together until they're well combined and creamy-looking, then add the eggs and beat the mixture well.
The eggs are beaten in. Where do the apple butter and other add-ins fit?
Mix in the apple butter and vanilla, then add the wheat germ or bran cereal. Scrape the bowl as needed so the mixture stays even.
That's mixed. I still have the sifted dry ingredients and sour cream waiting—how do I combine them without overmixing?
Add the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream, mixing well after each addition. Once the batter is evenly mixed, spread it in the prepared pan and add the topping you made earlier.
I want to get Black Bean Chili right. What should I handle first? I've got a large saucepan out but want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 tablespoon olive oil and chopping 1 onion. Keep the saucepan nearby since the oil will go in there over medium-high heat.
The onion is chopped. I also have red bell peppers on the counter—how should I prep those?
Seed and chop 2 red bell peppers. You'll also want 1 jalapeno pepper, seeded and minced, so the vegetables are ready to go in together.
Jalapeno is minced. Should I heat the pan before adding the vegetables?
Yes. Heat the olive oil in the large saucepan over medium-high heat until it looks loose and shimmery, then you'll be ready for the vegetables.
Oil is hot. Do the onions go in alone, or with the peppers?
Add the onion, red bell peppers, jalapeno, mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn together. Sautee them for 10 minutes, or until the onions turn translucent.
They're cooking now. What texture am I looking for besides the onions turning translucent?
The peppers should soften a bit, and the mixture should look juicy from the tomatoes and corn. Stir occasionally so nothing sticks while it sautes.
The vegetables look softened and the onions are translucent. When do the spices go in?
Season the vegetable mixture with black pepper, cumin, and chili powder. Stir well so the spices coat everything evenly.
Spices are mixed in and it smells good. What's the last part?
Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt. Once they're combined, let everything heat through in the saucepan before serving.
I'm ready to cook Easy Pavlova. What should be ready before I begin? I want to get everything set up before I start whisking.
Absolutely. For this pavlova, have 4 egg whites ready along with 1 1/4 cups white sugar. Since the egg whites need volume, use a large clean bowl if you can.
I've got the eggs separated and the sugar measured. Are there any small flavor ingredients I should pull out too?
Yes—set out 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and 1 teaspoon lemon juice. Those are the remaining ingredients for this recipe.
Great. I'm clearing space on the counter now. What should happen with the oven?
set the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C), so it can come up to temperature while you prepare the meringue.
Oven is heating. What pan setup do I need for the pavlova shape?
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. That will keep the pavlova from sticking and makes it easier to handle later.
Parchment is down, but I'm not sure how big to make it.
Draw a 9 inch circle on the parchment paper as your guide. If you draw in pencil, flip the parchment over so the marked side is underneath before adding the meringue.
The circle is marked and flipped. Should I start beating the egg whites now?
Yes. Put the 4 egg whites in a large bowl and beat them until they're stiff but not dry. You're looking for peaks that stand up without the mixture looking clumpy or dull.
If the whites look glossy and hold their shape, is that the right point to stop?
That sounds right: stiff peaks with a glossy look are good, as long as they have not turned dry or broken-looking. Stop there so the pavlova base stays light.
I'm making Baked Fish and Rice 2 and I've got an 11-in. baking dish out. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Grease that 11-in. baking dish, and have 1 1/2 cups boiling chicken broth and 1/2 cup uncooked long grain rice ready to go.
The dish is greased, and the broth is boiling. Should the rice go in dry?
Yes, use the rice uncooked. Add the dry long grain rice to the baking dish with the boiling chicken broth.
Got it. I also see Italian seasoning and garlic powder on the counter—how much of each?
Measure in 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, then stir everything in the dish so the seasoning is spread through the broth and rice.
It's mixed. Do I cover it before it goes in the oven?
Yes. Cover the baking dish and bake it at 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, for 10 minutes.
The 10 minutes are up. The rice has started to absorb liquid but it's not finished yet.
That's right for this point. Take the dish out carefully, uncover it, and add the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, and half of the onions.
Should I stir those into the rice or leave them mostly on top?
Gently mix the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, and half of the onions into the rice mixture so they're distributed without packing the rice down.
Okay, the mixture is even. I have the fish fillets ready—where do they go?
Lay the fish fillets over the rice mixture in the baking dish, then sprinkle the tops with paprika before continuing with the bake.
I'm ready to cook Chicken with Vegetables. What should be ready before I begin?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms, plus 4 chicken drumsticks and 4 chicken thighs with the skin removed.
The chicken is skinned, and I have the mushrooms sliced. Do I need to prep celery too?
Yes, slice 4 celery ribs. You'll also want zucchini, carrots, onion, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper ready for the pot.
Slow cooker is on the counter. Should the mushrooms go in before the chicken?
Place the mushrooms and the chicken into the slow cooker together, spreading them out so the pieces sit fairly evenly.
The drumsticks and thighs are in. I'm trying not to pack everything too tightly.
That's fine. Add the sliced celery, zucchini, carrots, onion, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper over the chicken and mushrooms.
Everything is added, and there's liquid around the vegetables. Do I stir it?
You can gently nudge the vegetables into the liquid, but don't worry about a full stir. Cover the slow cooker and cook on low for 5 hours.
After the 5 hours, what should I check on the chicken?
Check that the meat juices run clear. The chicken should be cooked through and tender, with the vegetables softened.
It looks done. How do I handle it so it doesn't cool off while I get plates ready?
Remove the chicken and vegetables from the slow cooker and keep them warm until serving.

memory_annotations.support_assistant_cue: With any raw add-ins like cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish, cut them into small, distinct bits so they scatter evenly without turning mushy. For the steak, set out 3 tablespoons crushed black peppercorns and 2 (8 ounce) beef top sirloin steaks.
memory_annotations.support_feedback_cue: I like that small raw texture here; it works better for this dish. The peppercorns are pressed in now.
memory_annotations.support_user_cue: I'm about to make Brandy Flamed Peppercorn Steak and want to get the counter organized before the pan goes on. Can you talk me through it?

messages.content: I'm about to make Brandy Flamed Peppercorn Steak and want to get the counter organized before the pan goes on. Can you talk me through it?

With any raw add-ins like cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish, cut them into small, distinct bits so they scatter evenly without turning mushy. For the steak, set out 3 tablespoons crushed black peppercorns and 2 (8 ounce) beef top sirloin steaks.
The steaks are out, and I have the crushed peppercorns in a shallow dish. Should I season before heating the skillet?
Yes. Press the crushed black peppercorns firmly into both sides of each steak so they stick well before the meat hits the pan.
I like that small raw texture here; it works better for this dish. The peppercorns are pressed in now.
Good. Sprinkle the steaks with 1 tablespoon lemon pepper and 1 teaspoon salt, getting both sides lightly and evenly covered.
Seasoning is on. I'm clearing the board so I don't track pepper everywhere.
Nice move. Once the board is clear, put a large skillet over medium-high heat and melt the butter in it.
The skillet is heating, but the butter amount wasn't listed. Should I just use enough to coat the bottom?
Use enough butter to coat the bottom of the large skillet in a thin layer, then let it melt and foam over medium-high heat.
The butter is melted and starting to foam. Do the steaks go in now?
Yes, lay the peppercorn-coated steaks into the hot skillet carefully so the crust stays in place.
They're in the skillet. I have garlic and wine nearby for the next part.
After the steaks have had their pan time, stir in the garlic and wine, then cook that mixture for 1 minute.
That minute is easy to track. Anything I should watch for right at the end?
Look for the garlic and wine to smell rounded and slightly reduced, then spoon the pan juices over the steaks and serve with the raw add-ins kept crisp on the side or scattered over the plate.
Let's work through Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style today. Where should I begin? I've got the squash on the counter but haven't started cutting yet.
Absolutely. For the ingredients, you'll need 1 spaghetti squash, halved lengthwise and seeded, plus 1 chopped onion.
The onion is chopped, and I'm about to scoop the seeds from the squash. Are there any other ingredients I should set out?
Set out 2 tablespoons minced garlic and 2 (14 ounce) cans stewed tomatoes as well.
Everything is on the counter now. What temperature should I set the oven to before I deal with the baking sheet?
Start Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style by heating the oven to 325 degrees F, or 165 degrees C.
The oven is heating. What should I do to keep the squash from sticking?
Spray a baking sheet with a thin layer of cooking spray.
Baking sheet is sprayed. Should the squash face up or down while it bakes?
Place the squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.
They're on the sheet cut side down. How long should I bake them, and what texture am I looking for?
Bake the squash for 35 minutes in the preheated oven, or until a knife can be easily inserted.
If the knife slides in easily at that point, is the squash ready to come out?
Yes. Once a knife goes in easily, take the squash out carefully and let it cool enough to handle before continuing with the lasagna-style filling steps.
Help me stay organized for Chicken Stuffed Buns. What comes first? I've got the sourdough buns on the counter and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 6 large sourdough buns and 2 cups of cooked, diced boneless chicken breast halves so they're ready to go.
The chicken is diced, and the buns are ready. What dairy should I have softened or shredded before I start?
You'll need 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese, softened, plus 1 cup shredded Pepper Jack cheese. Keep the Parmesan cheese nearby too, since it goes into the filling.
Got it. Should the oven be heating while I work on the buns?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's hot by the time the stuffed buns are assembled.
Oven is heating. What's the cleanest way to cut the buns without wrecking the tops?
Use a serrated knife to slice the top off each bun, cutting carefully so the tops stay intact. Set those tops aside because you'll save them.
The tops are off and saved. How much bread should I pull out from the middle?
Hollow out each bun enough to make room for the filling, but leave a sturdy shell so the buns can hold the chicken mixture without tearing.
I've made the shells. Can I mix the filling in one bowl, or should the cheeses be combined separately?
One medium bowl is fine. Combine the diced chicken, softened cream cheese, shredded Pepper Jack cheese, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and spinach until the filling looks evenly mixed.
The filling is mixed and creamy. Before I spoon it in, anything I should check about texture or the bun shells?

Check that the shells are deep enough for the filling and still firm around the edges. If the mixture is evenly combined and scoopable, spoon it into the hollowed buns, then place the saved tops back on.

original_cues.support_assistant_cue: For the grain side, hold back a little broth, cooking water, or sauce, then stir it in at the end only if the rice or grains need loosening. For the pie, start by getting out 6 apples and 1 (16 ounce) can whole cranberry sauce.
original_cues.support_feedback_cue: I like that move with the grain side; it keeps it from getting pasty, and that's exactly what I wanted here.
original_cues.support_user_cue: I'm making Cranberry Apple Pie II for dinner and I've got a simple grain side going too. Can you help me line up the prep?

For the pie, set out 6 apples and the 1 (16 ounce) can of whole cranberry sauce so the filling ingredients are ready.
memory_annotations.support_feedback_cue: I like that grain-side move; it keeps the rice loose instead of pasty, and that's exactly what I wanted for this meal.
memory_annotations.support_user_cue: I'm starting Cranberry Apple Pie II, and I've got a plain grain side on the stove too. Can you help me time the prep so I'm not scrambling?

messages.content: I'm starting Cranberry Apple Pie II, and I've got a plain grain side on the stove too. Can you help me time the prep so I'm not scrambling?

For the grain side, keep a small splash of broth, cooking water, or sauce aside, and stir it in at the end only if the grains need loosening. For the pie, set out 6 apples and the 1 (16 ounce) can of whole cranberry sauce so the filling ingredients are ready.
The apples and cranberry sauce are out. I haven't turned on the oven yet, and the pie plate is still empty.
Turn the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C. While it heats, get your pastry ready for lining the pie plate.
Oven is heating, and the pastry is unwrapped. Should I measure the sugar and flour now or wait until the apples are cut?
Measure them now so you can mix quickly once the fruit is sliced: 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour.
I like that grain-side move; it keeps the rice loose instead of pasty, and that's exactly what I wanted for this meal.
Perfect. Press the pastry into the pie plate now, easing it into the bottom and up the sides without stretching it.
The pastry is in the plate, and the dry ingredients are measured. I'm ready to deal with the apples.
Peel, core, and slice all 6 apples. Try to keep the slices fairly even so they coat well with the cranberry sauce.
The apple slices are piling up in my bowl. Should the cranberry sauce go straight in with them?
Yes, spoon the whole cranberry sauce into a medium-sized mixing bowl, then add the sliced apples to that bowl.
The apples and cranberry sauce are together, but the cranberry sauce is still in big soft clumps.
Gently fold the fruit a few times to break up the cranberry sauce enough to spread through the apples without mashing the slices.
That looks better. Do I add both measured dry ingredients at once?
Yes. Sprinkle in the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and the 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, then fold until the apple slices look evenly coated.

Let it chill while you prepare the salad ingredients. It doesn't need to be icy; just cool enough to feel refreshing when it coats the chicken mixture.

Wait until just before serving so the salad stays lively. When you're close to the table, put the chicken, raisins, almonds, and most of the chopped parsley into the large bowl.
We're about ten minutes from eating, and the dressing is still in the fridge. Is that close enough?
Yes. Give the dressing one quick whisk after you take it out, then pour it over the chicken mixture and toss gently until everything is coated.
The raisins and almonds are coated, but I don't want to crush the chicken. How should I toss it?
Use a broad spoon or spatula and lift from the bottom instead of stirring hard. Turn the salad over a few times until the dressing is distributed without breaking up the chicken.
It looks evenly dressed. How should I serve it so it still looks fresh?
Transfer it to the serving dish, scatter the reserved parsley over the top, and serve right away while the dressing is cool and the almonds still have texture.

Measure 1 1/2 cups white sugar and 4 cups all-purpose flour, keeping them separate for the layering.

Add 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda to the flour.

Yes. Combine the flour with the baking powder, baking soda, salt, and nutmeg so the flour layer is evenly seasoned.
The flour mixture looks even. For the wrap-style components, what goes into the jar first?
Use a clean 1 liter wide-mouth glass jar, then add the white sugar as the bottom layer.

Spoon the flour mixture over the sugar, then press it firmly in place so the layers stay distinct.

Seal the jar, then attach a card with the mixing directions for the person who will bake it.

I'm making Date Nut Bars today. Can you guide me through the ingredients and baking so I don't miss anything?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 cups sugar, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need dates, nuts, eggs, butter, and vanilla for the batter.
I've measured the sugar and flour, and I found the baking powder and salt. Should I combine the dry ingredients in one bowl?
Yes, use a large bowl. Add the sugar, flour, baking powder, salt, dates, and nuts, then stir them together so the leavening and mix-ins are evenly distributed.
The dates and nuts are mixed in with the dry ingredients. The bowl looks pretty full—does that sound right?
That sounds right for this recipe. Because the batter ends up very stiff, having everything in a large bowl will make the next mixing step easier.
I'm ready to add the wet ingredients. Do the eggs, butter, and vanilla go in together?
Yes. Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla to the bowl, then stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened. Don't worry if it feels thick—the batter is supposed to be very stiff.
It's definitely stiff, but I don't see dry flour pockets anymore. What pan should I use?
Grease a 15-in pan, then spread the batter into it as evenly as you can. A spatula can help press it out to the corners since it won't pour like a loose batter.
The batter is spread in the greased pan. What oven temperature and time should I use?
Bake the bars at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes. Start checking near 20 minutes and look for a golden brown top.
If they look golden at 22 minutes, should I pull them out or wait the full 25?
If they're golden brown at 22 minutes, you can take them out rather than waiting the full 25. Let the pan cool before cutting so the Date Nut Bars set up neatly.
Can you help me cook Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken? I've got the chicken out but haven't started seasoning yet.
Absolutely. You'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, plus salt and pepper for seasoning. Pat the chicken dry if it's damp so it browns better in the skillet.
Chicken is patted dry. Before I touch the stove, what else should be on the counter?
Set out 2 teaspoons olive oil and 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions. Keep the can nearby for later, but don't add it during the browning step.

Yes. Sprinkle salt and pepper on both sides of each chicken breast, making sure the seasoning is fairly even across the surface.
They're seasoned. How hot should the pan be before the chicken goes in?
Put the skillet over medium-high heat and add the olive oil. Let the oil heat until it looks loose and shimmery, but don't let it smoke.
The oil is shimmering. Should I crowd all 4 pieces in there if they fit tightly?
Place the chicken in the skillet in a single layer. If the pieces are too tight to brown well, work in batches, but the key step is to cook them and turn once so each side browns.
One side has color now. Am I looking for fully cooked chicken at this point or just browning?
For this part, focus on browning both sides. Turn each breast once, let the second side take on color, and avoid moving them around too much so the crust can form.
Both sides are browned and there are browned bits in the pan. What should I do with the chicken now?
Lift the chicken out of the skillet and set it aside on a clean plate. Leave the pan as is for the next stage, since those browned bits will add flavor.

Absolutely. Get 4 large carrots cut into 1 inch pieces, and chop 1/4 large onion. Those can go straight into a large saucepan once they're ready.

You'll need 1 quart vegetable broth and 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro. Keep both close because they go into the saucepan with the carrots and onion.

Yes. Add the carrots, chopped onion, vegetable broth, and fresh cilantro to the large saucepan before turning up the heat.

Bring the soup to a boil, then let it cook until the carrots are tender. That should take about 10 minutes.

They should be soft enough that a fork slides into a carrot piece easily. Since they're 1 inch pieces, start checking around the 10 minute mark.

Take the saucepan off the heat first and let the soup cool slightly. That makes it safer and easier to puree.

Use either the blender or food processor to puree the soup until smooth, working carefully if it's still warm. Once it's silky with no large carrot pieces left, it's ready to serve.
I'm making Best Macaroni Salad and want to stay organized. What should I set out before I start boiling anything?

Set out 1 (16 ounce) package of macaroni, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup cucumber that's peeled, seeded, and chopped, and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. You'll also want a large pot for the pasta, a colander, and a large mixing bowl.
I've got the macaroni and mayo measured. The cucumber still needs prep—how should it be cut for this?
Peel the cucumber, scoop out the seeds, then chop it into small pieces so it mixes evenly through the salad instead of leaving big watery chunks.
The cucumber is chopped, and I have the dried minced onion ready. How salty should the pasta water be?
Use a large pot of boiling water and salt it well enough to season the macaroni as it cooks. Add the macaroni and cook it until it's al dente, so it still has a little firmness.
The pasta is cooked. Do I drain it hot or cool it down first?
Drain it, then rinse the macaroni under cold water. Let it drain well after rinsing so the salad doesn't turn watery.
It's cooled and drained. Should I add the vegetables right away or start with the dressing?
Start with the pasta and mayonnaise in the large bowl. Combine the cooled macaroni with the 1/2 cup mayonnaise and mix well so the pasta gets evenly coated.
The mayo is mixed in and the pasta looks coated. Where do the cucumber and onion go in?
Stir in the chopped cucumber and the 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. The recipe also calls for stirring in ham and cheese at this point, so add those now if you have them prepared.
Everything is in the bowl. How do I know when it's finished?
Give it a thorough final mix so the cucumber, onion, ham, cheese, and coated macaroni are evenly distributed. Once it looks well combined, the Best Macaroni Salad is ready to serve or chill.

Rub the chicken evenly with 1/2 of the fajita seasoning, coating both sides so the flavor is spread across the pieces.

Cook the chicken for 8 minutes on each side, or until the juices run clear. Once it's cooked through, move it to a plate and set it aside.

Take 1 15 ounce can of black beans, rinse and drain them, then add them to a large saucepan.

Stir in the corn, salsa, and the other 1/2 of the fajita seasoning. Mix everything well so the seasoning coats the beans and vegetables.
How do I warm that mixture without overdoing it?
Keep the saucepan over medium heat and stir occasionally until the mixture is warm. Then serve it with the cooked chicken for the Chicken Fiesta Salad.

Can you talk me through making English Walnut Pie? I've got my mixing bowl out and want to start with the ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 3 eggs, 1/4 teaspoon salt, 3/4 cup white sugar, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract. You'll also need the syrup and butter or margarine for the filling mixture.
I found the eggs, sugar, salt, and vanilla. Should I get the oven going before I crack the eggs?
Yes, heat the oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C), so it's hot by the time the filling is ready.

Use the 3 eggs whole. Crack them into a large bowl and beat them until the yolks and whites are fully blended.
They're beaten and a little foamy. What should go into that bowl next?
Mix in the 3/4 cup white sugar, the 1/4 teaspoon salt, the 2 teaspoons vanilla extract, and the syrup. Stir until the mixture looks even and the sugar is worked in.

Whisk or stir steadily, just enough to combine everything smoothly. You don't need to whip in a lot of air; you're aiming for a uniform pie filling base.
The filling base looks smooth. What about the butter or margarine?
Melt the butter or margarine, then pour it into the egg mixture. Add it gradually while stirring so the warm fat blends in evenly.
It's all mixed together. Anything I should check before I move on to the pie shell?

Give the bowl a final scrape around the sides and bottom, making sure no sugar or salt is sitting unmixed. Once it looks consistent, the English Walnut Pie filling mixture is ready for the next part of your pie assembly.
Help me stay organized for Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles. What comes first? I'm setting up the counter and want to know what to pull out first.
Absolutely. Start by gathering 2 teaspoons olive oil and 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves. You'll also want a heavy skillet, or a nonstick frying pan if you'd rather use cooking spray.

Have 1 (10 ounce) can of refrigerated large crescent roll dough ready, along with 8 ounces Brie cheese. Keep the dough chilled until you're close to using it so it stays easier to handle.

Sauté the chicken breasts until they're no longer pink and the juices run clear. Once they're cooked through, move them to a plate and set them aside.

The oven should be at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) before Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles goes in.

Go ahead and open it when you're ready to assemble. Unroll 4 large crescent rolls on your work surface, keeping them intact as much as you can.
The 4 crescent pieces are unrolled. Anything I should watch for with the Brie before I continue?

Keep the 8 ounces Brie nearby and work gently with the dough so it doesn't tear. The recipe guidance provided gets you through cooking the chicken, preheating the oven, and unrolling the crescent rolls for the bundles.
I'm making Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup and have the slow cooker on the counter. Can you guide me without rushing?

Stir in the chopped onion and the full 28 ounce can of crushed tomatoes.

Everything is in the crock now, but the top looks a little uneven. Should I mix it more or leave it layered?
Give it a gentle stir so the beef, potatoes, mixed vegetables, onion, and tomatoes are evenly combined, while keeping the contents inside the cooker.
Okay, it looks evenly mixed. What seasonings go in before I put the lid on?
Season the soup with bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil. Once those are added, put the lid on the slow cooker and let it cook according to your slow cooker setting.

messages.content: I'm making Chicken and Herbs in White Wine. Can you guide me through the setup before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 chicken cut into pieces—about 4 pounds—garlic powder to taste, and 1/2 pound fresh mushrooms, sliced.
I've got the chicken pieces and mushrooms ready. What pan should I use for this?
Use a large Dutch oven so the chicken has room to brown and the pan can go back on the stove after you remove the pieces.
The Dutch oven is on the burner. Do I add the oil right away?

Sprinkle the chicken pieces with garlic powder to taste while the oil heats.

Take the pot off the heat and let the broth cool overnight with the meat still in it. Once it's safe to handle, chill it covered.

Lift the meat out of the cooled broth, trim off any gristle, and cut the meat into medium sized pieces; set it aside. Keep the onions, carrots, and reserved fresh herb garnish ready for when you continue the broth.

messages.content: I'm starting Baked Apple Oatmeal and I'd like to avoid scrambling once the stove is on. What should I have ready first?

For the serving sauce, draw two narrow lines over each portion and keep the rest in a small dish on the side. Set out a saucepan, a greased 2-qt. casserole, and the measured base ingredients: 4 cups milk, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, 2 teaspoons butter or margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
The casserole is greased and the saucepan is on the burner, but I haven't turned it on yet. Should I preheat now?
Yes, start the oven at 350 degrees F now. That way it will be ready when the oatmeal mixture is spooned into the casserole.

Yes. Put the milk, brown sugar, butter or margarine, salt, and cinnamon into the saucepan together, then heat them gently while stirring.
I like the two narrow lines for serving; that's exactly what I wanted for this dish. The milk is getting steamy and the butter is almost gone—how hot should I let it get?
Let it get hot enough that the butter melts fully and the brown sugar dissolves into the milk. Keep it below a hard boil so the milk doesn't scorch.
It's smooth now, and I don't see sugar on the bottom when I stir. Am I ready for the oats and apple mixture?
Yes, add the remaining ingredients now. Mix gently, using a folding motion so the oats and apple pieces are evenly coated without making the mixture heavy.

No, stop once everything is evenly combined. The oats will absorb the liquid as it bakes, so it should still look fairly loose before going into the oven.
Okay, I'm transferring it. Do I pack it down in the casserole or leave it lighter?
Spoon it into the greased 2-qt. casserole and spread the top level, but don't press it down firmly. A light, even layer will bake more pleasantly.
The dish is filled and leveled. Should I cover it with foil before baking?
Cover the casserole before it goes into the oven. Bake it at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes.
While it's baking, I'm setting up bowls and the sauce. Any serving details I should plan for?

Keep the extra sauce in a small dish and stir it before serving. When the oatmeal is done, portion it into bowls, add the two thin lines over each serving, and let people spoon on more sauce if they want it.

Absolutely. Get out a blender and measure 1 cup sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, and 1/3 cup hot salsa.

Yes, add the cottage cheese as-is. The blender will smooth it out once everything is combined.
Okay, cottage cheese is in. I'm adding the hot salsa now—does it all get blended together?
Yes. Add the hot salsa to the blender with the sour cream, mayonnaise, and cottage cheese.
I see the recipe also mentions cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt, but I don't have amounts listed. How should I handle that?

Use the recipe's listed ingredients as the measured base, and if you have cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt on hand, add them lightly to the blender so they blend into the sauce without overpowering it.
Everything is in the blender. What texture am I aiming for?
Puree until the sauce looks smooth and uniform, with no visible cottage cheese curds remaining.
It's blended smooth now. Should I taste it before chilling?
Yes, give it a quick taste so you know the flavor is balanced, then transfer it to a covered bowl or container.
It tastes good and it's in a small bowl. Do I serve it right away or hold it?
Chill it before serving. Keep it covered in the refrigerator, then spoon or dollop it alongside the crab cakes when you're ready to eat.
I'm making Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic. Can you stay with me while I get the prep started?
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup olive oil, 8 cloves garlic minced, 2 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper. You'll also need the cumin and oregano for the paste, plus the butterflied leg of lamb.
I've got the oil, garlic, salt, and pepper measured. Should I mix the seasoning paste in a bowl?
Yes, use a small bowl. Stir together the olive oil, minced garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano until it looks like a spreadable paste.
The paste is mixed. The lamb is butterflied on my board, and I'm not sure which side to coat first.
Coat one side generously, then flip the lamb and spread the paste over the other side too. Try to cover the full surface so the garlic and spices are evenly distributed.
Both sides are covered. Do I put it straight under the broiler now or let it sit?
Let it stand for an hour so the meat can come to room temperature before broiling.
It's been resting, and I'm setting up the oven. Where should the rack go for this cut?
Move the oven rack to the upper or upper-middle position, depending on the lamb's thickness, then preheat the broiler on high for at least 10 minutes.
I have a roasting pan and a wire rack. Should I line the pan before the lamb goes on?
Line the roasting pan with foil for easier cleanup, set the large wire rack over it, and place the lamb on the rack cut side up.
The broiler is hot and the lamb is cut side up on the rack. How do I manage the browning?
Broil it for about 8 minutes, moving the pan as needed so the entire surface browns evenly. Keep an eye on the garlic paste so it browns without scorching.

messages.content: I'm making Dads Best Burgers and have a mixing bowl out. Can you guide me from the ingredient prep through grilling?

Absolutely. Set out the 1 (3 ounce) package of softened cream cheese, 1 egg, 1 medium onion finely chopped, and 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs. The recipe also calls for beef and sausage to be crumbled in after the initial mixture is combined.
The cream cheese is soft, but the onion still needs chopping. How fine should I make it for the patties?
Chop the medium onion finely so it blends into the burger mixture instead of leaving big pieces that can make the patties break apart. Once it's chopped, keep the bread crumbs nearby for mixing.
Onion is chopped, and I've got the egg cracked into the bowl with the cream cheese. Do the crumbs go in now too?
Yes, add the 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs and the finely chopped onion to that bowl. Combine the first ingredients in the bowl until the egg, cream cheese, onion, and crumbs are evenly worked together.
It's coming together, but the cream cheese is a little streaky. Should I keep mixing before adding the meat?

Mix a bit more so the cream cheese is distributed through the base. It doesn't have to be perfectly smooth, but you want it even enough that the beef and sausage can pick it up throughout the mixture.
Okay, the base looks even. I have the beef and sausage ready on a plate.
Crumble the beef and sausage over the mixture in the bowl, then mix well. Use a gentle hand so it's combined without packing the meat too tightly.
The meat mixture is combined. I'd like the patties to cook evenly on the grill—how should I portion them?
Shape the mixture into eight patties. Try to make them similar in thickness, and press them just firmly enough to hold together without making them dense.
The grill is hot and the patties are shaped. What timing should I use, and how do I know they're done?
Grill the patties uncovered over medium-hot heat for 4-6 minutes on each side. They're ready when they're no longer pink in the center.

Yes. Keep stirring until those last pieces melt completely and the butter-water mixture reaches a boil.

memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For tonight I'm turning Coconut Ambrosia Salad into a casserole-style dish with a little dressing or drizzle involved. Where should that saucy part go?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Mix a small amount of sauce into the center and leave the edges mostly plain.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Coconut Ambrosia Salad as a skillet or casserole serving with a sauce, dressing, glaze, drizzle, topping, or finishing condiment. How should I handle the sauce?

messages.content: For tonight I'm turning Coconut Ambrosia Salad into a casserole-style dish with a little dressing or drizzle involved. Where should that saucy part go?
For this serving, work a small spoonful of the sauce through the middle of the salad, and keep the outer edges mostly undressed and plain.
Perfect, that's the approach for this batch. I've got a large bowl out—what fruit should I open and drain first?
Open and drain 1 (11 ounce) can of mandarin oranges and 1 (8 ounce) can of crushed pineapple. Let them drain well so the salad doesn't turn watery.
The fruit is draining in a colander. What cold ingredients do I need from the fridge or freezer?
You'll need 3 1/2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, plus 2 cups shredded coconut. If the whipped topping is still firm, give it a few minutes so it folds in smoothly.
I have the whipped topping softened and the coconut measured. The instructions mention a couple more add-ins—do those go in the bowl too?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine the drained mandarin oranges, drained crushed pineapple, thawed whipped topping, shredded coconut, marshmallows, and milk.
Should I stir hard to break it up, or keep it gentle so the oranges stay intact?
Keep it gentle. Fold everything together with a spatula until the whipped topping coats the fruit, coconut, marshmallows, and milk evenly without crushing the mandarin orange segments.
It looks evenly mixed now. Since I'm serving it casserole-style, do I add the center sauce before or after chilling?
Chill the mixed salad first for 1 hour before serving. After it has set, add that small amount of sauce through the center so the edges stay mostly plain.
Good to know. Should the dish be covered while it chills?
Yes, cover the bowl or casserole dish before refrigerating so it stays fresh and doesn't pick up other flavors while it chills for that 1 hour.
It's chilled and I've added the sauce only through the center. What's the last touch before it goes out?
Garnish with cherries just before serving. Keep them on top so the Coconut Ambrosia Salad looks bright and the creamy mixture stays light.
Let's work through Blackened Tuna today. Where should I begin? I've got fresh tuna steaks and want to get the pan work right.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 1/2 pounds of fresh tuna steaks, about 1 inch thick, plus 2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 tablespoons butter.
The tuna steaks are about 1 inch thick. Should I season them before the skillet is hot?
Yes. Generously coat the tuna all over with the Cajun seasoning so the surface is well covered before it hits the pan.
They're coated now. I'm using a large skillet—what goes in it?
Add the 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter to the large skillet, then set it over high heat.
The butter is melting quickly. How hot should I let the oil and butter get?
Let the mixture get very hot, almost to the smoking point. That high heat is what helps blacken the seasoned tuna.
It's nearly smoking now. Do I lower the heat before adding the steaks?
Keep it on high heat and carefully place the tuna steaks in the pan once the oil is nearly smoking.
The steaks are in and sizzling hard. Should I move them around?
Leave them in place so the coating can blacken properly. Cook on one side for 3 to 4 minutes, or until that side is blackened.
After 3 minutes the underside looks dark and crusted at the edges. Is that the texture I'm aiming for?
Yes, that dark, crusted surface is the blackened finish you want. If it needs a little more color, let it go closer to 4 minutes on that side.
I'm making Fresh Apple Walnut Cake and want to set myself up before I start mixing. Can you walk me through it?

Absolutely. Put your oven rack in a good center position and gather the dry ingredients you'll need: 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I've got the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt on the counter. Should I start with the pan or the oven?
Start the oven heating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the batter is prepared.
The oven is set. I'm using a 9x13 inch pan—what should I do to it?
Grease the 9x13 inch pan well, then dust it with flour. Tap the pan around so the flour coats the greased surface, and shake out any excess.
Pan is coated. For the dry mix, do I just whisk everything together?
For this cake, sift the dry ingredients together: the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. Sifting helps blend them evenly and breaks up any clumps.
I'm sifting now. The cinnamon is mixed through and the flour looks lighter.
That's just what you want. Once the dry mixture is sifted, keep it nearby while you handle the apple mixture.
I have the apples ready. What happens with the sugar at this point?
Combine the apples with the white sugar, stirring so the apples are evenly coated, then set that mixture aside.
Should the apples sit in a bowl while I clean up the flour on the counter?

Yes, let the apple and white sugar mixture sit in the bowl while you tidy up. You've got the oven preheating, the 9x13 inch pan greased and floured, the dry ingredients sifted, and the apples with sugar set aside.
I'm making Artichoke Hummus. Can you guide me through it from the ingredient prep?
Absolutely. Start by setting up your food processor, then drain 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, also called garbanzo beans. You'll also need 1 clove of garlic ready to go in.
The chickpeas are drained and the garlic is peeled. What should I measure next?
Measure 1/2 cup of drained marinated artichoke hearts and 2 tablespoons of lemon juice. Keep everything close to the food processor bowl.
I have the artichokes and lemon juice measured. Do I chop the garlic or artichokes first?
No chopping is needed if your food processor can handle them. Add the drained chickpeas, garlic clove, drained marinated artichoke hearts, and lemon juice to the work bowl.
I noticed the directions mention parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks, but I don't have those out. Should they go in too?
For the blending part, combine all ingredients except parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks in the food processor work bowl, so leave those out of the processor.
Everything for the hummus is in the processor bowl. How long should I run it?
Pulse it in short bursts until the mixture turns smooth. Scrape down the sides if needed so the chickpeas and artichokes blend evenly.
It's mostly smooth now, with just a little texture from the artichokes. Is that okay?
Yes, that sounds right for artichoke hummus. Once it's as smooth as you want it, transfer it into a serving bowl.
It's in the bowl. I'm not serving it for a while—what should I do with it?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the Artichoke Hummus until you're ready to serve.
I'm making Grandmas Gingersnaps and want to stay organized. What should I pull out before mixing?
Set out 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. You'll also need a medium mixing bowl, measuring cups, and whatever you'll use to stir or beat the dough.
I've got the margarine, sugar, egg, and molasses on the counter. Should I start with the oven or the bowl?
Get the oven going first so it has time to heat: preheat it to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is set to 350. For the margarine and sugar, am I melting anything?
No melting needed. Put the 3/4 cup margarine and 1 cup white sugar in a medium bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's looking pale and smooth now. Do the egg and molasses go in together?
Yes. Beat in the 1 egg and the 1/4 cup molasses until everything is well blended and the mixture looks even.
The wet mixture is combined. I don't want to overwork it—what dry ingredients go in?
Combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt separately if you can, then stir that dry mixture into the molasses mixture.
Should I stir gently at this point, or keep beating it like before?
Switch to stirring. Mix just until the dry ingredients disappear and it comes together into a dough.
The dough has formed and there are no dry streaks. Is that the stopping point for this part?

Yes, that completes the dough stage for Grandmas Gingersnaps: oven preheated to 350 degrees F/175 degrees C, margarine and sugar creamed, egg and molasses blended in, and the flour-spice mixture stirred in to form the dough.
I'm making Butterscotch Brownies in a Jar. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. For the dry mix, make sure you have 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 tablespoons baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup flaked coconut ready.
I've got the flour and coconut measured. Should I deal with the oven or the pan next?
Go ahead and heat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it can heat while you prep the pan and batter.
The oven is on. I'm using a 9x13 pan—does it need parchment or just grease?
The recipe calls for greasing a 9x13 inch baking pan. Coat the bottom and corners well so the brownies release cleanly.
Pan is greased. The jar mix looks a little clumpy when I pour it out—is that okay?
Yes, that can happen. Empty the jar of brownie mix into a large mixing bowl, then stir through it to break up the lumps before adding the wet ingredients.
The dry mix is loosened up now. What wet ingredients go in?
For this batch of Butterscotch Brownies in a Jar, add 3/4 cup softened butter, 2 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract to the bowl.
Should the butter be melted completely, or just soft enough to stir in?
Use softened butter, not fully melted. It should be easy to press and blend into the mix without being liquid.
Everything is in the bowl. What should the batter look like before I put it in the pan?
Mix until it's well blended, with no dry pockets of floury mix left. Once it looks evenly combined, spread it into the greased 9x13 inch pan.
I'm making Alaskan Halibut Lasagna, and I've got the skillet out. Can you help me start with the fish portion?
Absolutely. For this part, have 6 tablespoons butter or margarine available, but keep it divided because you'll only use 2 tablespoons in the skillet at the start.
Got it. The butter is measured. How should I prep the halibut before it hits the pan?
Use 1 1/2 pounds halibut steaks with the bones removed, then cut the fish into 1 inch cubes so the pieces cook evenly.
The halibut is cubed. I also have garlic on the board—how much goes in?
Mince 2 garlic cloves. You'll also need 3/4 teaspoon dried thyme ready to add with the fish.
Everything is prepped. Should I put the butter in the skillet before adding the fish?
Yes. Set the large skillet over medium heat and melt 2 tablespoons of the butter or margarine in it.
The butter has melted and is coating the pan. What goes in next?
Add the cubed halibut, the minced garlic, and the dried thyme to the skillet together, spreading the fish out so it cooks evenly.
The fish is in the pan with the garlic and thyme. How long should I cook it?
Cook it until the halibut flakes easily with a fork, which should take about 10 minutes. Keep the heat at medium and turn the pieces gently as needed.
It's starting to look opaque. How do I know it's ready to come out?
Check a thicker cube with a fork; if it separates into flakes easily, remove the halibut mixture from the skillet and set it aside for the next part of the lasagna.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Let the pan liquid cook down until it's a little thicker, then ladle it beneath the starches so the bowl stays glossy instead of soupy.
