original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Glazed Ham as a wide shallow bowl with noodles, pasta, rice, or grains. How should I manage the liquid?

messages.content: Today I'm turning Glazed Ham into a broad, low bowl over noodles, pasta, rice, or grains; what should I do with the liquid so it sits right?
Let the pan liquid cook down until it's a little thicker, then ladle it beneath the starches so the bowl stays glossy instead of soupy.
That's the serving style I'm going with. Before I start, what needs to be on the counter?
Set out 1 (8 pound) bone-in shank ham, 4 cups water, or as needed, plus 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup brown sugar.
I've got the ham, water, honey, and brown sugar. What pan setup should I use?
Use a roasting pan large enough to hold the ham comfortably, and make sure you have a tight fitting lid ready for it.
The roasting pan and lid are out. What oven temperature am I aiming for?
Heat the oven to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C.
While that warms, should the ham go in flat-side down or just into the pan as it fits?
Place the bone-in shank ham in the roasting pan so it sits steady and the lid can close tightly.
It's in the pan and stable. How much water do I add before covering?
Pour in water until it reaches a 2 inch depth in the roasting pan; use the 4 cups as your guide, adding only as needed to hit that level.
The water is at 2 inches. Do the honey and brown sugar go in right now?
Keep the 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup brown sugar measured and ready for the glaze; for this covered start, the recipe has you cover the ham with the water in the pan.
Okay, I want to get it into the oven without losing moisture. What's the last move here?
Put the tight fitting lid on the roasting pan, then transfer it to the 275 degrees F oven.
I'm making Fresh Apple Cake and want to get set up before I start mixing. What should I pull onto the counter?
Set out 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil, 2 cups white sugar, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract. You'll also need a 10 inch tube pan ready for the batter.
I've got the oil, sugar, eggs, and vanilla measured. Should I handle the pan or the oven first?
Start the oven now so it has time to heat: preheat it to 325 degrees F, or 165 degrees C. While it warms, grease the 10 inch tube pan thoroughly, including the center tube.
The oven is set to 325, and I'm greasing the tube pan. For the wet mixture, do the eggs go in with the oil?
Yes. Beat together the vegetable oil, beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white sugar until the sugar is evenly moistened and the mixture looks unified.
The wet mixture is glossy and smooth. I see flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg in the next part—do I just stir those in?
Before adding them to the wet ingredients, sift together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Sifting helps distribute the leavening and spices evenly.
I don't want pockets of spice. Should I sift once into a separate bowl?
That's a good approach: sift the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg into a separate bowl, then give it a light whisk if you want extra even distribution.
The dry bowl is sifted. Is there anything else from the recipe I should confirm before I combine things?
You've covered the listed setup: oven at 325 degrees F or 165 degrees C, one greased 10 inch tube pan, wet ingredients beaten together, and the dry ingredients sifted together.
Great. I'm going to scrape down the wet bowl and keep the pan nearby.
Perfect. Keep the greased tube pan within reach, and when you bring the mixtures together, scrape the bowl well so the oil, eggs, vanilla, and sugar stay evenly incorporated.
Crustless Spinach Quiche 2 is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got the quiche pan out but want to make sure I start in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 3 ounces reduced fat cream cheese and let it be softened before mixing. You'll also need 1 cup fat-free milk, 1 cup egg substitute, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
The cream cheese is soft enough to press with a spoon. Should I spray the pan now or wait?
You can coat the quiche pan with nonstick cooking spray now so it's ready when the filling is mixed.
Pan is sprayed. What bowl should I use for the filling?
Use a small mixing bowl. Put the softened reduced fat cream cheese in it and beat it until it loosens up and looks creamy.
It's smoothing out, but there are still a few little lumps. Is that okay before adding the liquid?
A few small bits are fine, but give it another brief beating so the milk and egg substitute blend in more easily.
Okay, it looks creamier now. Do I pour in the milk first?
Add the 1 cup fat-free milk, the 1 cup egg substitute, and the 1/4 teaspoon pepper to the bowl, then beat everything together until the mixture is smooth.
The mixture is smooth and pourable. Where does the spinach part come in?
Stir in the remaining ingredients from your recipe at this point, including the spinach if that's part of what you have prepared. Fold them through so they're evenly distributed.
Everything is mixed together and the pan is waiting. How do I transfer it without making a mess?
Pour or scrape the mixture into the prepared quiche pan coated with nonstick cooking spray, spreading it gently so the filling sits evenly in the pan.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Keep the topping separate so it stays crunchy, then scatter it over the dish right before you reheat it or serve it.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, I'm prepping it ahead and adding a crumbly crisp topping just this time. At what point should that topping go on?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Hold the topping separately and add it just before reheating or serving.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style as a make-ahead dish with crumbs, streusel, or a crisp topping. When should I add the topping?

messages.content: For this Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, I'm prepping it ahead and adding a crumbly crisp topping just this time. At what point should that topping go on?
Keep the topping separate so it stays crunchy, then scatter it over the dish right before you reheat it or serve it.
Perfect, that's exactly how I want to handle this pan. Can you help me set up the squash part first?
Yes. Put the oven on to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), and have a baking sheet ready to coat lightly with cooking spray.
The sheet pan is out. What ingredients should I pull together before I cut anything?
You'll need 1 spaghetti squash, 1 onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 (14 ounce) cans stewed tomatoes.
I have the cans, onion, and garlic out. How should the squash be prepped for the pan?
Halve the spaghetti squash lengthwise and scrape out the seeds. Once the baking sheet has a thin layer of cooking spray, set the squash halves on it cut side down.
The squash is seeded and face-down. Does the onion get chopped now too?
Go ahead and chop the onion now so it's ready for the lasagna-style filling later; keep the minced garlic and stewed tomatoes nearby as well.
The oven just reached temperature, and the squash is on the sprayed sheet. How long am I baking it?
Bake the squash for 35 minutes in the preheated oven.
What should I check at 35 minutes so I don't overdo it?
Slide a knife into the squash; it should go in easily. If it still resists, give it a little more time and check again.
Once it's tender, I'll cool it and assemble later. Just to be sure, the crisp topping still waits, right?
Right—keep that topping off during make-ahead storage, then add it just before reheating or serving.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Keep the extra liquid in its own container, then stir it in once you open the thermos so the noodles, pasta, rice, or grains don't soak it all up too early.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this BBQ Chuck Roast, I'm turning it into a thermos lunch over noodles, pasta, rice, or grains, so I need the brothier part handled differently today. What should I do with the liquid?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Pack the extra liquid separately and add it after opening the thermos.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making BBQ Chuck Roast as a thermos lunch with noodles, pasta, rice, or grains. How should I manage the liquid?

messages.content: For this BBQ Chuck Roast, I'm turning it into a thermos lunch over noodles, pasta, rice, or grains, so I need the brothier part handled differently today. What should I do with the liquid?
Keep the extra liquid in its own container, then stir it in once you open the thermos so the noodles, pasta, rice, or grains don't soak it all up too early.
Perfect, that's the lunch setup I want for this batch. What should I pull out before I start?
Get the main items on the counter: 1 (5 pound) chuck roast, 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer.
The roast is out, and I've got the sauces and beer nearby. Do I need a particular bowl?
Use a large bowl with enough room for the roast and marinade. In it, combine the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt.
I've mixed the marinade; it smells strong and savory. Does the roast go straight in?
Yes. Place the chuck roast into the marinade, turn it so it's coated, cover the bowl, and refrigerate it for six hours.
During those six hours, should I leave it alone or keep checking it?
Turn it often while it marinates so different sides stay in contact with the sauce mixture.
It's been chilling, and I'm thinking ahead to cooking. What should I set up outside?
Preheat an outdoor grill for indirect heat, so the roast can cook away from direct flames.
The grill is set for indirect heat. What happens to the marinade when I lift the meat out?
Remove the roast from the marinade, and pour the marinade into a saucepan.
Since I'm packing this with grains later, should that saucepan liquid be the part I keep separate?
Yes, use that extra liquid as the separate add-in for the thermos lunch, then pour it in after opening so the grains stay in better shape.
I'm making Garden Potato Salad. Can you help me organize the prep before I start assembling it?
Absolutely. Have your 6 large potatoes already cooked, peeled, and cubed, and slice 4 hard-cooked eggs. Those will form the base of the salad.
The potatoes are cubed and the eggs are sliced. What vegetables should I prep with them?
Slice 2 celery ribs and 6 green onions with their tops. The recipe also has you combine radishes, salt, and pepper with the potato mixture, so keep those ready too.
I've got a large bowl out. Should the potatoes and eggs go in together?
Yes. Add the potatoes, sliced hard-cooked eggs, celery, green onions, radishes, salt, and pepper to the large bowl, then gently combine so the potatoes don't break up too much.
That's mixed. Do I chill it now, or make the dressing first?
Set the bowl aside for the moment and make the dressing. In a saucepan, combine eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt.
What heat should I use for the saucepan?
Use medium heat, and stir the dressing as it cooks. Keep stirring until it thickens.
How will I know it's thick enough?
It should look noticeably thicker and coat the spoon rather than running off like a thin liquid. Once it reaches that point, take it off the heat.
The dressing has thickened. What's the last thing I need to do before combining or serving?
Let the dressing cool before you proceed with the salad. Cooling is the final instruction for this Garden Potato Salad stage.
I'm making Cookie Jar Gingersnaps and have a large mixing bowl out. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start?
Absolutely. For the wet mixture, set out 3/4 cup shortening, 1 cup sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. You'll also need flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt ready for the dry mixture.
The shortening, sugar, egg, and molasses are on the counter. Should the shortening go in the bowl by itself first?
Put the shortening in the large mixing bowl with the sugar, then cream them together until they look well blended and a bit lighter in texture.
It's starting to look smooth, but there are still a few streaks of shortening. Is that okay?
Keep mixing a little longer so the shortening and sugar are evenly creamed. You don't need it fluffy like frosting, just combined enough that there aren't obvious clumps.
Okay, the mixture looks even now. Do I crack the egg straight in with the molasses?
Yes. Beat in the egg, then add the molasses and mix until the dough base is uniform and glossy.
The molasses is mixed in and the bowl looks dark and sticky. What should I do with the dry ingredients?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt. Stir them together so the spices and leavening are spread evenly.
Dry ingredients are mixed. Should I dump them all into the sticky mixture?
Add the dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture, mixing as you go. Stop once the dough comes together and there are no dry pockets.
The dough is together and a little tacky. How do I shape the cookies for the tray?
Scoop teaspoonfuls of dough and roll each one into a ball. Set the balls on your prepared baking sheet, leaving space between them so they have room as they bake.
Before I get moving on California Chicken, what should I have ready? I've got 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts on the counter and want to keep the timing straight.

Absolutely. Set out the chicken breasts, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and a pinch of salt. You'll also want a skillet ready, plus salt and pepper for seasoning to taste at the end.
The skillet is on the stove. Do I need the oven involved before I start browning the chicken?
Yes—set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready while you work on the stovetop.
The oven is set. Should I put the oil in while the pan is still warming?
Go ahead and warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in the skillet over the heat. Once the oil is warm, add the chicken breasts.
The chicken is in the pan. Where does the onion powder fit in?
Sprinkle the 1/2 teaspoon onion powder over the chicken as it cooks, along with that pinch of salt. Keep the chicken in contact with the skillet so it can brown.
It's starting to sizzle. How long should I leave it before I worry about doneness?
Cook it for about 15 minutes, or until the chicken is browned and just about done. Turn the pieces as needed so they brown evenly rather than scorching in one spot.
The outside is browned now, but I'm checking the thicker pieces. What texture should I be looking for?
They should look firm and nearly cooked through, with no raw-looking exterior areas. Since the recipe says browned and just about done, don't keep pushing them far past that point in the skillet.
Okay, they look nearly done. How do I season before serving?
Add salt and pepper to taste while the chicken is still hot. Give the pieces a brief turn in the skillet so the seasoning lands evenly, then serve the California Chicken warm.
I'm making Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms today. Can you talk me through the setup before I start?

Absolutely. Have ready 3/4 cup melted butter, divided, plus 1 pound fresh mushrooms with the stems removed. You'll also need 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons and 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, along with the crabmeat, lobster, and garlic for the stuffing.
The mushrooms are cleaned and the stems are out. Should I prep the oven or the pan first?
Get the oven heating to 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the mushrooms are stuffed.
The oven is set. I have a large baking sheet out—how much butter goes on it?
Brush the baking sheet with about 1/4 cup of the melted butter. Try to cover the surface where the mushroom caps will sit so they pick up some richness and don't stick.
The sheet is buttered. Do the caps go open side up?
Yes, arrange the mushroom caps in a single layer on the baking sheet, open side up, with a little space between them so they're easy to fill.
They're lined up. I've got the croutons crushed—what goes into the filling bowl?
In a medium bowl, combine the 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons with the remaining 1/2 cup melted butter, the 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic.
Should I stir that gently or really mash it together?

Stir it until the butter coats the croutons and the seafood, garlic, and mozzarella are evenly distributed. It should hold together enough to spoon into the caps, but it doesn't need to be mashed smooth.
The mixture looks evenly combined. Is there anything else I should check before filling them?

Just make sure the caps are still in a single layer and the stuffing is well mixed. Spoon the crab and lobster mixture into the mushroom caps, keeping the baking sheet level so the butter stays under them.
I'm making Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf and want to get the bacon-and-vegetable prep started. Can you guide me through it?

Absolutely. Set out 12 ounces chopped raw bacon, 1 small white onion chopped, 5 button mushrooms chopped, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef. You'll also want a skillet, a slotted spoon, and paper towels nearby.
I have the skillet out, but the oven is still off. Should I heat it before I start the bacon?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the meatloaf prep catches up.
The oven is set. My bacon is already chopped; do I need oil in the pan?
No oil needed. Put the chopped raw bacon into the skillet and cook it over medium heat. Stir it occasionally and let the pieces brown as their fat renders.
It's starting to sizzle, and there's a good amount of grease in the pan. How browned should the bacon pieces be?
Cook them until the pieces look browned rather than pale or soft. They don't need to be burned or extra crisp; just browned enough to give flavor and texture.
The bacon looks browned now. I'm trying not to drag too much grease with it—what's the cleanest way to move it?
Use a slotted spoon to lift the bacon out of the skillet, letting the grease drain back into the pan. Transfer the bacon to paper towels so it can drain further.
The bacon is on paper towels. The skillet still has a lot of fat in it—how much am I supposed to keep?
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon grease from the skillet. Keep that small amount in the pan for the next part of the meatloaf prep.
Got it. I've got the chopped onion, chopped mushrooms, and extra-lean ground beef waiting. Anything I should avoid doing right now?

Don't add the ground beef to the hot skillet at this point. For the steps we've covered, the key is that the oven is at 350 degrees F, the bacon is browned and drained, and only 1 tablespoon of bacon grease remains in the skillet.
I'm making Chicken Tacos and have a large skillet out. Can you guide me through the prep before I turn on the heat?
Absolutely. Cut 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite-size pieces, and set out 1 cup lemonade, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 1 tablespoon lime juice.
The chicken is cut up. I also have the lemonade, olive oil, and lime juice measured. Anything else needs to be nearby?
Yes—keep Worcestershire sauce close for the skillet, plus garlic powder, onion powder, and a bay leaf for seasoning. You'll also need tortillas ready to warm later.
Got it. Should the skillet be on medium before I add the chicken?
Yes, set the large skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken pieces, lemonade, olive oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce to the skillet together.
Everything is in the pan now, and the liquid is starting to heat around the chicken.
Good. Sprinkle in the garlic powder and onion powder, then add the bay leaf. Stir so the chicken gets coated evenly in the seasoned liquid.
The seasonings are mixed in. Do I keep stirring constantly or let it cook?
Let it simmer, stirring occasionally so the pieces cook evenly. Keep it going until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear, about 15 to 20 minutes.
It's been around 15 minutes. Some pieces look done, but I want to be sure before serving.

Check a thicker piece by cutting into it: there should be no pink in the center, and the juices should run clear. If any pieces still look underdone, simmer a few more minutes, up to the 20-minute mark.
The chicken looks cooked through now. How should I handle the tortillas?
Warm the tortillas until soft, either in the oven or in the microwave. Once they're pliable, spoon in the simmered chicken and serve the tacos while everything is warm.
Let's work through Garden Party Salad today. Where should I begin?
Absolutely. Start by setting out a small bowl for the dressing and a large bowl for assembling the salad. For the dressing ingredients you'll need 1/4 cup vegetable oil and 1/4 cup orange marmalade.
I've got the oil and marmalade on the counter. What else goes into the dressing?
Add 3 tablespoons cider vinegar and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise to your setup as well. Those will get whisked with the other dressing ingredients until the mixture is smooth.
Should I whisk it by hand, or do I need a blender?
A whisk is fine here. Use the small bowl and whisk the dressing ingredients until the marmalade and mayonnaise smooth out into the oil and vinegar.
The dressing looks mostly smooth but still a little glossy. Is that okay?
Yes, that's okay. Once it's smooth and combined, put the dressing in the refrigerator to chill while you get the salad ingredients ready.
While it chills, what should I put in the large bowl?
Just before serving, combine the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley in the large bowl. Keep the dressing separate until you're ready to toss so the salad stays fresh.
The chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley are together. Do I pour in all the dressing?
Yes, add the chilled dressing to the large bowl, then toss gently until everything is lightly coated.
It's coated now. Any serving tip before I bring it out?
Serve it right away after tossing. Give the bowl one last gentle turn so the dressing is evenly distributed, then transfer it to your serving dish if you're using one.
I want to make Grandmas Gingersnaps. Can you guide me while I get the ingredients out?
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. You'll also need the dry ingredients mentioned for the dough: flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt.
I've got the margarine and sugar measured. Should I turn on the oven before mixing?
Yes, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready by the time the dough comes together.
The oven is on, and I have a medium bowl ready. What goes in it first?
Put the 3/4 cup margarine and the 1 cup white sugar into the medium bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's mostly smooth but a little soft. Is that okay before I add anything else?
That's fine for this dough. Add the 1 egg and the 1/4 cup molasses, then beat everything until the mixture is well blended and evenly dark.
The molasses is mixed in now. Do the spices go straight into this bowl?
Combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt separately first, then stir that dry mixture into the molasses mixture.
I'm adding the dry ingredients in. How do I know when to stop stirring?
Stop once it has formed a dough and you no longer see dry streaks of flour. Try not to keep mixing after it comes together.
The dough has come together in the bowl. Anything I should check before moving on?
Check that the oven is still at 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, and that the dough looks evenly mixed with the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt fully incorporated.
I'm making Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men. Can you help me start with the ingredients I'll need on the counter?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup margarine, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup molasses, and 1 egg yolk. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready.
I've got the margarine and sugar measured, and the molasses jar is open. Should the margarine be mixed with anything first?
Yes. Put the margarine and sugar into the large bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's smoothing out now, but I still see a few little streaks of margarine. Is that okay?
Keep mixing a bit longer so the margarine and sugar look evenly combined and smooth before adding the next ingredients.
Okay, the bowl looks much more even. What goes in with that mixture?
Stir in the 1/2 cup molasses, then add the egg yolk. Mix until the molasses and yolk are worked through the creamed margarine and sugar.
The molasses made it darker and a little sticky. Do I add the dry ingredients straight into this bowl?
Combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg, then blend that dry mixture into the molasses mixture until the dough is smooth.
I'm folding in the dry ingredients now. What texture should I look for before I stop?
Stop once there are no dry patches left and the dough looks smooth throughout. It may be thick and spiced, but it should be evenly blended.
The dough is smooth and ready. What do I do before shaping the gingerbread men?
Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour. That rest will firm it up so it's easier to handle later.
I'm ready to cook Blackened Tuna. What should be ready before I begin? I've got fresh tuna steaks and want to do it in a skillet.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 1/2 pounds fresh tuna steaks, about 1 inch thick, plus 2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning for the coating.
The tuna is on a plate now. Should the seasoning go on lightly or be pretty heavy?
Use a generous coating of the Cajun seasoning on the tuna so the surface can blacken well in the hot pan.
Okay, the steaks are coated. What fat am I cooking them in?
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter together in a large skillet over high heat.
I'm using my biggest skillet. How hot should I let the oil and butter get before the tuna goes in?
Let the skillet get very hot, until the oil is nearly smoking, then place the tuna steaks in the pan.
The pan is hot and I'm ready to lay them in. Do I need to crowd them close together?
Give the steaks room if you can, so each piece sits flat against the skillet and gets a good blackened surface.
They're in the pan now. How long should I leave the first side alone?
Cook that side for 3 to 4 minutes, or until it looks blackened.
I can see the crust forming around the edges. Should I move them while that happens?
Try not to move them much during those 3 to 4 minutes; steady contact with the hot skillet helps build the blackened crust.
I'm making Broccoli Chicken Roli and want to get my prep organized. What should I put on the counter first?
Set out 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat and 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli. Use a large mixing bowl, since everything will be combined there.
Chicken and broccoli are ready. I'm chopping the vegetables now—what amounts do I need?
You'll need 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper. Keep the pieces fairly small so they mix evenly with the chicken and broccoli.
Got it. Does the oven need to be on before I mix the filling?
Yes, go ahead and heat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), so it's ready when the mixture is prepared.
The oven is set. I have the large bowl out—what goes into it?
Add the chopped cooked chicken, fresh chopped broccoli, chopped onion, chopped green bell pepper, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic to the large bowl.
All the filling ingredients are in. Should I stir gently or really work it together?
Mix everything together until the chicken, vegetables, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, and seasonings are evenly distributed. You don't need to mash it—just combine it well.
The mixture looks evenly coated. What pan setup do I need before it goes any further?
Cover a cookie sheet with aluminum foil. Smooth the foil over the surface so the sheet is ready for the prepared mixture.
Foil is on the cookie sheet. Anything I should double-check before I continue?
Make sure the oven is holding at 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, and that the filling is fully mixed with no dry pockets of seasoning or unmixed mayonnaise and mustard.
I'm setting up for Fresh Apple Cake; what should happen before the heat goes on? I'm setting things out and want to be sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Put 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil and 2 cups white sugar on the counter, and grab a mixing bowl large enough to beat them with the eggs and vanilla.
Oil and sugar are out. I also have eggs nearby—how many should I crack?
You'll need 3 eggs, beaten. Crack them into a small bowl first, beat them, and keep 2 teaspoons vanilla extract ready too.
The eggs are beaten and the vanilla is measured. Should I get the pan and oven ready before mixing?
Yes. set the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), so it can heat while you prep the batter.
Oven is on. What pan am I using for this cake?
Use one 10 inch tube pan. Grease it well, making sure the center tube and the bottom are coated so the cake releases cleanly.
The tube pan is greased. Do I combine the wet ingredients now?
Yes—beat together the vegetable oil, beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white sugar until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
It looks glossy and the sugar is mostly worked in. What dry ingredients should I prepare?
Sift together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a separate bowl. Sifting helps break up lumps and distributes the spices evenly.
The dry mixture is sifted. Anything I should check before I move on?
Make sure the oven is still holding at 325 degrees F, the 10 inch tube pan is greased, and your wet mixture of oil, eggs, vanilla, and sugar is ready beside the sifted dry ingredients.
I'm making Coq au Vin alla Italiana, and I've got a large skillet out. Can you talk me through the prep before I turn on the burner?

Absolutely. Set out 4 pounds of dark meat chicken pieces, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 5 cloves crushed garlic, and 1/2 cup all-purpose flour. Keep the flour in a shallow dish so it's easy to coat the chicken.
The chicken is on a tray, and the flour is in a dish. Should the garlic all go in with the oil?
Not all of it. Once the oil is heating in the large skillet, add 1/2 of the crushed garlic and let it flavor the oil briefly before the chicken goes in.
Okay, I'll save half the garlic. How hot should the skillet be before I start?
Use medium to medium-high heat. Add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, and when it looks glossy and moves easily across the pan, stir in that first half of the garlic.
The oil is glossy and the garlic is starting to smell good. What do I do with the flour?
Season the 1/2 cup all-purpose flour with poultry seasoning, then mix it so the seasoning is evenly distributed.
Do I coat every piece heavily, or just dust the chicken?
Dredge the chicken parts in the seasoned flour so each piece gets an even coating. Shake off loose excess flour before setting the pieces in the skillet.
The pan looks crowded with all the chicken. Is that a problem for browning?
If the pieces are packed tightly, brown them in batches. Give each piece contact with the skillet so the coating can brown instead of steaming.
How long should each batch stay in the skillet, and what color am I looking for?
Brown the flour-coated chicken in the skillet for 4 or 5 minutes, aiming for a golden surface on the outside. Turn the pieces as needed so they brown evenly.
I'm making Apple Cranberry Crisp 2 and have an 8 inch square baking dish ready. Can you talk me through it while I prep?
Absolutely. Set your oven to 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, and butter that 8 inch square baking dish so the fruit won't stick.
Dish is buttered. For the fruit, I have Granny Smith apples, but I want to confirm the amount before I slice them.
Use 2 pounds of Granny Smith apples. Peel them, core them, and slice them thinly so they soften evenly in the crisp.
The apples are sliced. I also have cranberries on the counter—how much goes in?
Add 3/4 cup cranberries to a large bowl with the sliced apples.
Fruit is in the bowl. What sweetener and spice should I add before it goes into the pan?
Mix in 1/4 cup white sugar and 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon. The recipe also has you mix in nutmeg at this stage, so add it with the cinnamon if you have it measured.
I've stirred the apples, cranberries, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg together. Should it look fully coated?
Yes, aim for the apple slices and cranberries to be evenly coated with the sugar and spices. Once they look glossy and speckled throughout, they're ready for the baking dish.
The fruit mixture is coated. How do I move it into the dish without leaving gaps?
Tip the mixture into the buttered dish and spread it evenly into the corners, keeping the fruit in a fairly level layer.
Fruit is leveled out. What do I do with the bowl now for the topping ingredients?
Use that same bowl and combine the oats, flour, and brown sugar. Stir them together well so the topping mixture is evenly blended before you continue.
I'm setting up for Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got a large mixing bowl ready.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1/2 cup margarine and 1/2 cup sugar, since those will go into the bowl together.
They're measured out. Should the margarine and sugar be mixed by hand or beaten?
Either works, but beat or stir them well enough that they cream together into a smooth mixture in the large bowl.
The mixture looks smooth now. What do I add from the wet ingredients?
Add 1/2 cup molasses and 1 egg yolk, then stir until they're fully worked into the margarine-sugar mixture.
The molasses made it darker and glossy. Do the dry ingredients go in next?
Yes. Combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg before adding them to the molasses mixture.
I have the spices and leaveners together with the flour. Should I dump it in all at once?
Add the dry mixture into the molasses mixture and blend until the dough is smooth. If it feels easier to control, you can stir it in gradually.
It's coming together as a thick dough. How smooth should it be before I stop?
Stop once you don't see dry streaks and the dough looks evenly mixed throughout; it should be cohesive rather than crumbly.
The dough looks even now. What should I do with the bowl before shaping the cookies?
Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour before you try to roll or shape the gingerbread men.
Can you help me mix a Bahama Mama II? I've got a glass and ice ready, but I want the proportions right.
Absolutely. For one drink, measure out 1 fluid ounce dark rum and 1/2 fluid ounce apricot brandy. A jigger or small measuring cup will help keep it balanced.
Dark rum and apricot brandy are measured. What should I add for the fruity part?
Add 3 1/2 fluid ounces fruit punch, then measure in 1/2 fluid ounce pina colada mix. Those go with the rum and brandy in a mixing glass.
Should I pour everything straight into the serving glass over the ice?
Use the mixing glass first if you have one. Combine the dark rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and pina colada mix there so the drink blends evenly before it hits the ice.
All four ingredients are in the mixing glass. Do I shake it or just stir?
Just stir it to blend. Give it a steady stir until the pina colada mix is fully worked into the fruit punch and the color looks even.
It looks smooth now. My serving glass already has ice in it—okay to pour?
Yes, pour the blended drink over the ice in your serving glass. Try not to overfill so it stays easy to carry and sip.
There's a little foam from stirring. Is that a problem?
No problem. A little foam is fine; it should settle quickly. The main thing is that the drink is blended and chilled by the ice.
Any last check before I serve it?
You're set: 1 fluid ounce dark rum, 1/2 fluid ounce apricot brandy, 3 1/2 fluid ounces fruit punch, and 1/2 fluid ounce pina colada mix, stirred together and served over ice.
I want to make Bakers Secret Pie Crust. Can you help me set up before I start mixing?

Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup cake flour and 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, plus 1 teaspoon white sugar and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need butter, shortening, baking powder, a plate, and a food processor.
I've got the flours measured. Should the butter and shortening be cold right away?
Yes. Measure the butter and shortening onto a plate and put the plate in the freezer for about 20 minutes so the fats get firm before they go into the flour.
While that chills, can I load the food processor bowl?
Go ahead. Add the cake flour, all-purpose flour, white sugar, salt, and baking powder to the bowl of the food processor.
The dry ingredients are in. Do I need to run it long?
Just pulse for a few seconds to mix them evenly. You're not trying to work the flour much yet.
The butter and shortening have been in the freezer close to 20 minutes. What texture am I looking for?
They should feel cold and firm, not soft or melty. Take 1/2 of the cold butter and 1/2 of the cold shortening and add them to the processor with the dry ingredients.
Both halves are in with the flour mixture. Should I hold the pulse button continuously?
Use short on-and-off pulses for about 1 minute. That keeps the fat from warming too quickly while it cuts into the dry ingredients.
It's starting to look crumbly. Is that the right stopping point for this part?
Yes, crumbly is what you want after pulsing the cold butter and shortening with the dry mixture. Stop there so the fat stays cold for the next stage of the crust.
I'm making Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats and already have the baked potatoes on the counter. Can you guide me without rushing?

Absolutely. You'll want 4 medium baked potatoes, quartered lengthwise, plus 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing, 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, and sliced green onions if you want a garnish.
The potatoes are baked and cool enough to handle. Should I start heating the oven now?
Yes, set the oven to 375 degrees F so it can preheat while you assemble the potato boats.
I've quartered the potatoes lengthwise. How much potato should I scoop out of each skin?
Scoop the potato flesh out of the skins carefully, leaving the skins intact enough to hold their shape as boats.
The skins are holding together. Where does the Ranch go?
Coat the inside of the potato skins with the 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing, spreading it across the hollowed centers.
I have the scooped potato sitting in a bowl. Does it go back in after the Ranch?
Yes. Once the insides of the skins are coated with Ranch, place the scooped potato back into the skins.
They're filled again. I want them cheesy but not messy—what's the topping step?
Sprinkle the 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese over the potato boats, aiming for an even layer so each piece gets some cheese.
I also sliced a few green onions. Should those go on before serving?

Yes, use the sliced green onions as an optional topping. Once the potato boats are assembled with Ranch, potato, Cheddar, and the optional onions, they're ready to serve or warm through in the preheated oven.
I'm about to start Corned Beef Hash. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a large deep skillet ready.
Absolutely. Peel and dice 6 large potatoes, cut 1 (12 ounce) can of corned beef into chunks, and chop 1 medium onion. You'll also need 1 cup beef broth nearby.
The potatoes are peeled and diced, and the onion is chopped. Should the corned beef go in cold from the can?
Yes, that's fine. Just break or cut it into chunks so it can mix through the potatoes as it heats.
Everything is prepped. Do I heat the skillet before adding the ingredients?
Set the large deep skillet over medium heat, then add the diced potatoes, corned beef chunks, chopped onion, and the beef broth all together.
They're all in the skillet now. The broth is sitting mostly around the potatoes.
That's right. Give everything a gentle stir so the onion and corned beef are distributed, then cover the skillet.
Covered. How do I know when it has simmered long enough?
Let it simmer over medium heat until the potatoes are soft enough to mash and the liquid is almost gone. If you press a potato piece with a spoon, it should give way easily.
The potatoes are getting soft, but there's still some broth at the bottom.
Keep it covered a little longer, checking occasionally. You're aiming for very tender potatoes with only a small amount of liquid left in the pan.
Okay, the liquid is nearly gone and the potatoes mash when I press them. What's the last move?
Mix everything well in the skillet so the potatoes, corned beef, and onion come together into a hash, then serve it hot.
I'd like to make Chicken Stuffed Buns. Can you guide me without rushing? I've got a baking sheet out.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you prep the buns and filling.
Oven is heating. Before I start cutting, can you confirm the main ingredients I should have on the counter?
You'll need 6 large sourdough buns, 2 cups cooked and diced boneless chicken breast halves, 1 softened 8 ounce package of cream cheese, and 1 cup shredded Pepper Jack cheese.
I have the buns and chicken ready. The cream cheese is soft, and the Pepper Jack is shredded. What should I do with the buns?
Slice the top off each sourdough bun, but keep those tops nearby. Try to cut them like little lids so they can go back on neatly later.
The tops are off and saved. Should I scoop out a lot of bread or leave them sturdy?
Hollow out each bun enough to make room for the chicken filling, but leave a firm shell so the buns don't collapse or leak.
The shells look good. I've got a pile of bread pieces on the side. How do I mix the filling?

In a medium bowl, combine the diced chicken, softened cream cheese, shredded Pepper Jack cheese, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and spinach. Mix until the cream cheese coats the chicken and everything is evenly distributed.
The mixture is thick but spreadable. Should I pack it tightly into the buns?
Spoon it into the hollowed buns and press gently so each one is filled, but don't mash it down hard. You want the filling snug, with the saved tops ready to sit back on.
They're filled and the tops are back on. Any last check before they go into the oven?

Place the stuffed buns on your baking sheet and bake them in the preheated 350 degrees F oven until the buns are warm and the cheese filling is heated through and melty. Let them sit briefly before serving so the filling isn't too hot.
I'm getting ready for Awesome Turkey Sandwich. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got a cutting board out and can toast the bread if needed.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 slices of whole wheat bread; toast them if you want a sturdier, warmer sandwich. You'll also need 1 tablespoon mayonnaise for one slice.
The bread is toasted and the mayo is ready. Should I grab the mustard and turkey now?
Yes—pull out 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard and 3 slices smoked turkey breast. Keep the turkey slices separated so they're easy to layer.
I have those on the counter. Which slice gets which spread?
Spread the mayonnaise evenly over one slice of toast, all the way toward the edges. Spread the Dijon mustard on the other slice so each bite gets some of both.
Done. The mustard slice is a little thinner-coated than the mayo slice—is that okay?
That's fine. Dijon is stronger, so a lighter layer works well. Place the smoked turkey on one side, folding or overlapping the slices so the bread is covered.
The turkey is on the mayo side. I also see guacamole in the instructions—where does that go?
Spread the guacamole directly over the turkey. Use a gentle hand so the turkey stays in place, and make the layer even enough to help hold the toppings.
Guacamole is on. I'm trying not to make the sandwich too messy—what toppings go next?
Pile on the salad greens, bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese. Keep the greens fairly flat, tuck loose sprouts toward the middle, and place the cheese where it can help weigh everything down.
All layered. Should I close it with the mustard slice and cut it right away?
Yes. Set the mustard-coated slice on top, press lightly with your palm, then slice the sandwich in half if you like. Serve it right away so the toast stays crisp.
I pulled up Crustless Spinach Quiche. Can you guide the first few moves? I want to get everything set out before I turn on the stove.
Absolutely. Pull out 1 tablespoon vegetable oil and 1 onion, chopped. You'll also need a large skillet and a 9 inch pie pan.
The onion is chopped, and I found the pie pan. What else should be on the counter?
Get 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and well drained, plus 5 eggs, beaten. Try to press extra moisture out of the spinach so the quiche doesn't turn watery.
The spinach is thawed and squeezed out, and the eggs are beaten in a bowl. Should the oven be heating yet?
Yes, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) while you finish the stovetop prep.
Oven is heating. Do I need to do anything to the pie pan before filling it?
Lightly grease the 9 inch pie pan, including the sides, so the crustless quiche releases cleanly later.
Pan is greased. I'm ready at the stove with the skillet—how hot should it be?
Set the large skillet over medium-high heat and add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil. Let it warm until the oil looks glossy.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do the onions go in by themselves?
Yes, add the chopped onion to the skillet. Cook it while stirring occasionally, keeping the heat at medium-high.
What texture am I looking for before I stop cooking the onion?
Cook until the onions are soft. Once they've softened, you're ready for the next part of assembling the quiche with the spinach and beaten eggs.
I'm making Armadillo Eggs today. Can you guide me without rushing through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 24 jalapeno peppers, 1 pound sausage, 2 cups all-purpose baking mix, and 1 (16 ounce) package of shredded Cheddar cheese so everything is within reach.
The peppers and sausage are on the counter, and I found the Cheddar. What should I do about the oven?
get the oven warming to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) so it has time to come up to temperature while you work on the peppers.
Oven is heating. I also have a medium baking sheet—does it need anything before the peppers go on it?
Yes, lightly grease the medium baking sheet. A thin coating is enough to help prevent sticking later.
Done. For the jalapenos, should I cut them all the way open or just make an opening?
Cut a slit in each jalapeno pepper rather than slicing them completely apart. You want an opening you can work through while keeping the pepper mostly intact.
I've slit a few. The seeds are still inside and my hands are getting messy—what's the cleanest way to handle that part?
Use a small spoon or the tip of a knife to remove the seeds and pulp from each pepper, then discard them. If you have gloves, they can make this part more comfortable.
Good call on the gloves. Should I be saving any of the pulp for the filling?
No, discard the seeds and pulp for this recipe. Keep the cleaned jalapeno shells ready with the sausage, baking mix, and shredded Cheddar nearby.
All the peppers are cleaned out now. Can I pause here for a minute before mixing anything?

Yes. Leave the prepped peppers on the greased baking sheet or a clean plate, keep the oven at 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), and make sure the 1 pound sausage, 2 cups baking mix, and 16 ounce package of shredded Cheddar are still ready for the next stage.
I want to make Drunken Fruit Salsa. Can you talk me through the prep so I don't miss anything?
Absolutely. Set out a glass bowl, a cutting board, and a sharp knife. You'll need 1 medium mango peeled and finely diced, plus 3/4 cup chopped fresh strawberries.
The mango is diced and I measured the strawberries. Should the pieces be pretty small?
Yes, keep them finely diced or chopped so the salsa scoops easily and the fruit mixes evenly. Add those to the glass bowl when they're ready.
They're in the bowl. I also have a kiwi and a jalapeno on the counter.
Great. Peel and finely dice 1 kiwi, then seed the jalapeno pepper and finely chop it. Removing the seeds keeps the heat more controlled.
Kiwi is diced. For the jalapeno, should I add all of it?
Use the 1 seeded, finely chopped jalapeno from the recipe. Stir it in with the mango, strawberries, and kiwi.
Everything is in the glass bowl except the mint and rum mentioned in the directions.
Add the mint and rum to the glass bowl, then stir everything together gently so the fruit stays intact but the flavors are evenly distributed.
It's mixed. The fruit looks glossy, and there's a little liquid at the bottom.
That's fine. Cover the bowl and refrigerate the salsa for 1 to 3 hours. During that time, stir it once or twice so the fruit keeps soaking evenly.
After it chills, do I need to drain it or do anything before serving?
Give it one final gentle stir. If there's more liquid than you want, you can serve it with a slotted spoon, but don't rinse or press the fruit. Serve it chilled.
I want to make Campagnard Sauce today. Can you talk me through it while I prep?
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl, a spoon or spatula, and something to blend with later. For the ingredients, you'll need 2 cloves garlic, minced, and 1/2 cup goat cheese.
The garlic is minced and the goat cheese is measured. What should I prep next?
Mince 1 celery stalk, then measure 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar. Keep olive oil nearby too, since it gets stirred in with the sauce ingredients.
Celery is minced, vinegar is measured, and I've got the olive oil out. Do I add everything straight to the bowl?
Yes. Add the minced garlic, goat cheese, minced celery, balsamic vinegar, and olive oil to the bowl. Stir them together until the goat cheese starts loosening into the mixture.
It's mixed, but the goat cheese is still a little chunky. Is that okay at this point?
That's fine for now. Give it a good stir so the garlic, celery, vinegar, and olive oil are evenly distributed before you season it.
Okay, it smells good. How much salt and pepper should I use?
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Start lightly, stir, taste a small bit, and adjust only if it needs more brightness or bite.
The seasoning tastes balanced. Should I keep stirring by hand or use the blender now?
Use the blender now, or an immersion blender if that's what you have. Blend well until the sauce is smooth.
It's smooth now. I'm not serving it right away—what's the best way to store it?
Transfer it to a covered container, cover it tightly, and refrigerate. Give it a quick stir before serving if it settles.
I'm making Atomic Canuck Chili and I've got the slow cooker out. Can you guide me through what to prep before the heat goes on?
Absolutely. Set out 2 pounds lean ground beef and dice 1/2 large onion. You'll also want 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper and 3 tablespoons garlic powder ready by the skillet.
The beef is thawed, and the onion is diced. Should I measure the spices before browning?
Yes, measure them now so the skillet step moves smoothly: keep the crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper close by.
I'm at the stove with a large skillet. What heat should I use?
Put the skillet over medium heat. Add the ground beef, diced onion, crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper, then cook while breaking up the beef until it's browned.
The beef is browned and the onions have softened. There's some fat in the pan.
Drain off the fat carefully, then transfer the beef and onion mixture into the slow cooker.
Mixture is in the slow cooker. I see mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce on the counter.
Great—stir all of those into the slow cooker. Add the kidney beans with their liquid, then mix everything well so the tomato paste and barbeque sauce spread through the chili.
It's thick but mixed. Should the vegetables be fully buried in the sauce?
Try to fold the carrots, celery, peppers, and mushrooms down into the bean-and-beef mixture so they cook evenly in the slow cooker.
Before I put the lid on, how do I adjust the heat level?
Season it with hot sauce and more crushed red pepper to taste, then stir once more before covering the slow cooker.

messages.content: I'm making Easiest Salad Dressing for a green salad tonight. Can you help me get organized?

Keep the crunchy salad topping in a narrow stripe of small uneven pieces instead of spreading it across the whole bowl. For the dressing, set out a jar with a tight-fitting lid, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 3 teaspoons milk, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1 pinch ground black pepper.
I found a small jar with a lid. Should I measure everything straight into it?
Yes. Add the 1/2 cup mayonnaise to the jar first so the thinner ingredients can loosen it up when you shake.
The mayonnaise is in. The milk is measured too—does all 3 teaspoons go in now?
Pour in all 3 teaspoons milk, then add the 1/4 teaspoon salt and the pinch of ground black pepper.
I like that crunchy strip for the salad; it works better for this. The salt and pepper are in the jar now.
Great. Put the lid on tightly and make sure it is seated well, since this dressing needs a vigorous shake.
Lid is on. How long should I shake it?
Shake it hard until the mayonnaise, milk, salt, and pepper look fully combined and the dressing is smooth enough to pour.
It looks mixed, but there are a couple thicker streaks on the side of the jar.
Scrape or tap the sides if needed, close the lid again, and give it another brisk shake to pull those streaks into the dressing.
Now it looks creamy and even. Should I dress the salad right away?
Yes, pour it over the salad when you're ready to serve, then toss lightly so the greens get coated without getting weighed down.
And the crunchy topping goes on after tossing?
Right—dress and toss the salad first, then add the crunchy topping in that narrow strip so it stays distinct and crisp.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip and want to keep it moving smoothly. What should I set out before I turn on the oven?

Set out 1 cup mayonnaise, 8 ounces sour cream, 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, and 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts. Drain and chop the artichoke hearts so they're ready to stir in.
The artichokes are drained and chopped. Do I need a particular dish for mixing and baking?
Use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish. You can mix everything right in that dish, which keeps cleanup simple.
Good. Should the oven be heating while I combine the dip?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) before you start assembling the casserole.
Oven is preheating. I have mayo, sour cream, soup mix, and the chopped artichokes in front of me—what goes in the casserole?
Add the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat to the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish.
Do I need to layer those, or just stir them together?
Just stir everything together until the sour cream and mayonnaise look evenly blended with the soup mix, artichokes, cheese, and crab meat.
It's mixed and looks creamy. Should I cover the dish before it goes in?
Bake it uncovered at 350 degrees F for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, what's the best way to serve it?
Serve the Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip immediately while it's hot and creamy.
I want to make Best Macaroni Salad. Can you help me get set up before I start boiling anything?
Absolutely. Put a large pot of salted water on to boil, and have 1 (16 ounce) package of macaroni ready. You'll also need 1/2 cup mayonnaise for the dressing part.
The pot is heating, and I found the mayo. What vegetables should I prep while I wait?
Prep 1 cup cucumber by peeling it, seeding it, and chopping it. Also measure out 1 tablespoon dried minced onion so it's ready to stir in later.
Should the cucumber pieces be tiny, or is a rough chop okay?
Aim for small bite-size pieces so they mix evenly through the macaroni salad. Since the cucumber is peeled and seeded, it should stay crisp without making the salad too watery.
The water is boiling now. How should I cook the macaroni?
Add the macaroni to the salted boiling water and cook it until al dente. Once it has that tender but slightly firm texture, drain it right away.
After draining, do I let it sit hot, or cool it down?
Rinse the cooked macaroni under cold water, then drain it well. That cools it for the salad and helps keep the mayonnaise from loosening too much.
It's cooled and drained. What bowl should I use for mixing?
Use a large bowl so you have room to fold everything together. Add the pasta and 1/2 cup mayonnaise, then mix well until the macaroni is evenly coated.
The pasta is coated. Do the cucumber and onion go in now, and what about the ham and cheese listed in the directions?
Yes. Stir in the chopped cucumber, the dried minced onion, and the ham and cheese. Mix well so everything is distributed, then it's ready to serve or chill until you want it cold.
I want to make Gelatin Fruit Salad. Can you help me get it started and make sure I don't miss anything?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple with the juice left in.
I've got the applesauce and gelatin on the counter. The pineapple says crushed, and I haven't drained it.
That's right—keep the crushed pineapple undrained. You'll also want a saucepan for the applesauce, something to stir with, and a dish or mold for chilling the salad.
Should I pour the applesauce straight into the saucepan by itself?
Yes. Add the 1 cup applesauce to the saucepan and heat it until it comes to a boil, stirring so it doesn't stick.
It's bubbling now. Do I keep the burner on while adding the gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat before adding the gelatin. Stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin until the powder is fully dissolved.
The mixture looks smooth and red now, with no dry granules that I can see.
Good. Next, slowly pour in the 12 ounce can of lemon-lime soda. Go gradually because it may foam as it hits the warm gelatin mixture.
It foamed a little but settled down. When does the pineapple go in?
Stir in the entire 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple, including the juice. Mix gently until it's evenly distributed.
Everything is mixed. Should I cover it before putting it in the fridge?
Pour it into your serving dish or mold, cover it if you like, and refrigerate it until firm. Once set, it's ready to serve chilled.
I want to make Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style. Can you help me get set up before I turn on the oven?
Absolutely. You'll need 1 spaghetti squash, halved lengthwise and seeded, plus 1 chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 cans of stewed tomatoes, each 14 ounces.
The squash is cut and seeded, and I have the onion, garlic, and tomatoes on the counter. What oven temperature should I use?
heat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). While it heats, keep the squash halves ready with the cut sides exposed.
My baking sheet is out. Do I need parchment, oil, or anything on it?
Use a thin layer of cooking spray on the baking sheet. You just want enough to help prevent sticking, not a heavy coating.
The sheet is sprayed. Which way should the squash sit on it?
Place both squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet so the flesh is against the pan.
They're on the pan cut side down. Should the onion, garlic, or tomatoes go in now?
For this part, keep the onion, the 2 tablespoons of minced garlic, and the 2 14-ounce cans of stewed tomatoes gathered and ready. The baking step is just for the squash halves.
Okay, the oven says it's at 325. How long should I bake the squash?
Bake the squash for 35 minutes in the preheated oven. It's ready when a knife can be inserted easily into the squash.
If the knife still meets resistance at 35 minutes, what should I look for before taking it out?
Check the thickest part of the squash. If the knife doesn't slide in easily yet, leave it in a little longer and recheck until the flesh is tender enough for the knife to go in without much pressure.

messages.content: I'm making Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf tonight. Can you walk me through the setup before I start handling the meat?

Keep the tender topping gathered in the center of the meatloaf, and hold the crisp bacon pieces to one side as a crunchy accent instead of scattering them everywhere. Heat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, and set out a skillet, paper towels, and a slotted spoon.
Oven is on. Which ingredients should I pull out first?
Bring out 12 ounces chopped raw bacon and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef. Keep the beef cold while you start the bacon so it stays easier to shape later.
The beef is still in the fridge for now. What should I chop while the skillet heats?
Chop 1 small white onion and 5 button mushrooms. Aim for fairly even mushroom pieces so they soften at the same rate.
I like that arrangement for the top; that center feature with the crisp side accent works better for this dish than an even sprinkle all over.
Great. Put the chopped raw bacon in the skillet over medium heat and stir it as it cooks so the pieces brown evenly.
The bacon is sizzling, but some pieces are browning faster than others. Should I lower the heat?
Keep it around medium heat and stir more often, nudging the darker pieces away from the hottest spot. You're looking for browned bacon pieces, not burnt edges.
It's browned now and there's a lot of grease in the pan. What's the cleanest way to move it?
Use the slotted spoon to lift the bacon out, letting the extra fat drip back into the skillet. Spread the bacon on paper towels so it drains and stays crisp.
Bacon is draining. Do I pour off all the fat before I deal with the onion and mushrooms?
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon grease. That small amount keeps the bacon flavor without making the meatloaf mixture heavy or greasy.
I've got the chopped onion, mushrooms, bacon, and chilled beef ready. Any texture thing I should watch when I combine everything?
Handle the 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef gently and avoid packing it tightly. Fold the chopped onion and mushrooms in evenly, then shape the loaf with light pressure so it doesn't turn dense.
When I add the toppings later, should the bacon go on while it's still crisp from the towels?
Yes, keep the drained bacon crisp and add it as the side accent after shaping. Put the softer topping in the middle so the loaf has a clear focal point and the crunchy bacon stays distinct.

messages.content: I've got Almond Apricot Bread on the counter, but I want to sort the bowls and ingredients before I start mixing. Where should I begin?

For the briny add-ins, mince the pickle, capers, olives, or pepperoncini very finely and stir them into the creamy glaze so they show as small bright flecks. For the bread batter, set out one large bowl for the dry ingredients and a second bowl for the wet mixture.
The two bowls are out, and I have the flour bag open. How much goes into the big bowl?
Add 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour to the large bowl. Level it off so the bread doesn't turn heavy.
Flour is measured. I've got white sugar and brown sugar next to it.
Stir in 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar with the flour. Break up any brown sugar clumps before you add the leavener.
The sugars are mixed in loosely. The baking powder and salt are still waiting.
Add 3 teaspoons baking powder, then add the salt called for in the recipe. Whisk the dry bowl until the flour, sugars, baking powder, and salt look evenly combined.
I like the tiny briny bits in the glaze; that's exactly what I wanted with a bread this rich.
Great—keep that glaze portion separate for the moment so those bright bits stay distinct instead of getting lost in the batter.
Before I work on the wet bowl, what happens with the baby food?
Spoon out 1 tablespoon baby food and reserve it for the glaze. Put the remaining baby food with the wet ingredients.
Reserved spoonful is set aside. The rest is beside the egg, milk, oil, and extract.
In the second bowl, beat the egg, milk, oil, extract, and remaining baby food together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
The wet bowl is smooth. I'm worried about making the loaf dense when I combine everything.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir gently just until moistened. Stop as soon as the dry flour streaks disappear, even if the batter still looks a little lumpy.
The batter is combined and still looks soft. Should I scrape the bowl more before moving it to the pan?
Give the bowl one careful scrape from the bottom to catch any dry pockets, then stop mixing so the bread stays tender. Keep the reserved 1 tablespoon baby food glaze ready for the top.
Before I get moving on Grandmas Gingersnaps, what should I have ready?
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. You'll also want a medium mixing bowl ready.
I've got the margarine and sugar measured. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready by the time the dough comes together.
Oven is on. I'm using a medium bowl now—what goes in first?
Put the 3/4 cup margarine and the 1 cup white sugar in the bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's getting lighter and smoother, but there are still a few streaks of margarine. Keep mixing?
Yes, keep creaming just until those streaks mostly disappear and the sugar and margarine look evenly combined.
That looks smooth now. Do I add the egg by itself or with the molasses?
Add the 1 egg and the 1/4 cup molasses to the bowl, then beat them in until everything is well blended.
The mixture is glossy and brown. I'm ready for the dry ingredients—what should I combine?
In a separate bowl or off to the side, combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt so they're evenly distributed.
Those dry ingredients are mixed. How do I bring it all together without overdoing it?
Stir the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt mixture into the molasses mixture just until it forms a dough. Stop once no dry streaks remain.
I want to make Cinnamon Crackle Cookies today. Can you stay with me while I get started?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're ready to cream together.
Those are on the counter. The butter is soft but not melted. What sugars should I measure?
Measure 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Pack the brown sugar firmly into the measuring cup, then add both sugars to your mixing bowl with the butter and shortening.
I've got them in the bowl. Should I use a hand mixer or a spoon for the creaming?
A hand mixer will make it easier. Beat the butter, shortening, sugar, and brown sugar together until the mixture looks creamy and well blended.
It looks lighter and smoother now. The bowl sides have a little mixture stuck to them.
Scrape down the sides, then add the egg and extracts. Mix well so they're fully worked into the creamed mixture.
The egg and extracts are mixed in. I have the dry ingredients nearby, but the recipe says the next eight ingredients.
Right—combine those next eight dry ingredients in a separate bowl first. Once they're evenly mixed, add them gradually to the creamed mixture instead of dumping them in all at once.
The dough is coming together. It's thick enough to scoop, but a little sticky.
That's fine for these cookies. Shape the dough into 1-in balls; if it sticks to your hands, work gently and keep the balls roughly even in size.
I've rolled a tray of dough balls. Do they go on a greased pan, and when does the extra sugar come in?
Roll each 1-in ball in sugar, then place them apart on ungreased baking sheets so they have room as they bake.
Aunt Mamies is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese and 1/2 cup butter so both are softened before you begin.
The cream cheese and butter are on the counter. Do I need anything dry measured out too?
Yes, measure 2 cups all-purpose flour and 1 cup white sugar. Keep the flour near your mixing bowl and the sugar aside for the saucepan step later.
I've got a bowl ready. Should the cream cheese and butter go in together?
Yes. Put the softened cream cheese and butter in the bowl, then beat them together until the mixture looks smooth and well blended.
It's blended and creamy. How should I add the flour so it doesn't clump up?
Add the flour gradually if that's easier to manage, mixing well as you go, until it's fully incorporated into the cream cheese and butter mixture.
The dough has come together. What texture am I aiming for before chilling it?
It should hold together well enough to shape. Form it into a ball, cover it, and chill it for 2 hours.
The dough is covered and in the fridge. While it chills, what pan do I need for the sugar part?
Use a saucepan. When you're ready for that part, combine the sugar and milk in it and place it over medium heat.
Once the saucepan is on medium heat, how do I know when that mixture is done?
Stir it occasionally as it heats. It's ready when the milk boils and the sugar has dissolved.
I'm making Broccoli Coleslaw and want to get the dressing started before I chop anything. What should I put on the counter?

Set out 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1 (3 ounce) package chicken flavored ramen noodles. Keep the seasoning packet from the ramen because it goes into the dressing.
Got it. Should I crush the ramen right away, or save that for later?
You can crush the ramen noodles now if you like, but keep the crushed noodles separate for the moment. Open the seasoning packet and add that to a small bowl with the olive oil, vinegar, and sugar.
The oil, vinegar, sugar, and seasoning are in a small bowl. It looks a little separated.

That's fine at this stage. Mix it really well until the sugar and seasoning are distributed through the oil and vinegar. Once mixed, refrigerate the dressing for at least 1 hour before serving, or overnight if you're making it ahead.
I'm aiming to serve it later today, so I'll chill the dressing for 1 hour. What should I prep while it's in the fridge?
Use a large bowl for the vegetables and add the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds. Give them a toss so the sunflower seeds and green onions are spread through the mix.
The vegetables and sunflower seeds are combined. Should the ramen go in before the dressing?
Yes, stir in the crushed ramen noodles with the broccoli mixture. Add them close enough to serving time that they still have some crunch.
The dressing has chilled and the ramen is stirred into the vegetables. Do I just pour it over?
Pour the chilled dressing over the broccoli mixture and toss well so the oil-vinegar dressing coats the broccoli, carrots, green onions, sunflower seeds, and ramen evenly.
It's coated. Any serving tip so it doesn't get soggy?
Serve it soon after the crushed ramen is stirred in if you want the most crunch. If you need to hold it, keep it refrigerated until serving.
