Gather the moistened mixture together, pat it into a round, and wrap it in plastic. Keep it compact, but don't knead it; you just want the tart dough shaped and covered.
Help me stay organized for Black Bean and Corn Quesadillas. What comes first? I've got a large saucepan out.
Absolutely. Set out 2 teaspoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons finely chopped onion, 1 (15.5 ounce) can black beans that are drained and rinsed, and 1 (10 ounce) can whole kernel corn that's drained.
The beans are rinsed, the corn is drained, and the onion is chopped pretty fine. Should the pan be hot before the oil goes in?
Put the olive oil in the large saucepan and heat it over medium heat. Give it a short moment to warm so the onion sizzles gently rather than browning too fast.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do I add all 3 tablespoons of onion at once?
Yes, add all the finely chopped onion and stir it into the oil. Cook it until softened, about 2 minutes, stirring occasionally so it doesn't stick.
It smells good and the onion looks softer, but it hasn't browned much. Is that okay?
That's exactly fine for this recipe. Once the onion is softened, stir in the drained and rinsed black beans and the drained whole kernel corn.
Beans and corn are in the pan. The mixture looks a little dry—what goes in with them?
Add the sugar, salsa, and pepper flakes, then mix everything well so the beans and corn are evenly coated.
I've stirred in the salsa, sugar, and pepper flakes. How long should it cook from here?
Keep it over medium heat until everything is heated through, about 3 minutes. Stir once or twice so the bottom stays clean and the heat spreads evenly.
After 3 minutes it's hot and saucy. Should I keep cooking it down more before using it?
No need to cook it much further unless it seems watery. If it's heated through and well mixed, it's ready to spoon into your quesadillas.
I'm making Cabbage Kielbasa Supper in the slow cooker today. Can you guide me without rushing? I've got cabbage on the counter.
Absolutely. Shred enough cabbage to make 8 cups, then cut 3 medium potatoes into 1/2 inch cubes. Those can go near your 5-qt. slow cooker while you prep the rest.
The cabbage is shredded and the potatoes are cubed. I'm checking the onion and seasoning now—what exactly goes in?
Chop 1 medium onion and measure 1 3/4 teaspoons salt. You'll also want pepper ready, plus broth to pour over everything and the sausage for the top.
My slow cooker is a 5-qt. one, and the vegetables look like they'll fill it pretty high. Is that okay?
Yes, that's expected for this recipe. Put the shredded cabbage, potato cubes, chopped onion, salt, and pepper into the 5-qt. slow cooker and combine them as evenly as you can.
They're mixed, though the cabbage is piled up. Should I press it down or leave it loose?
You can gently tuck it down so the lid will fit, but don't worry if it looks full—the cabbage will cook down as it heats.
I'm ready with the broth. Do I stir it in or pour it over the top?
Pour the broth over all of the vegetables. Let it run down through the cabbage and potatoes; you don't need to fully stir again unless the salt and pepper are sitting in one spot.
Broth is in. Where should the kielbasa go?
Place the sausage on top of the cabbage mixture. Keeping it on top helps it heat through while the vegetables soften underneath.
Lid is on and the cooker is full but closes. What setting and how long should I plan for?
Cook it covered on low for 8-9 hours, until the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through. When it's done, check that the potatoes are soft before serving.
I'm making BBQ Chuck Roast today with a 5 pound chuck roast. Can you guide me without rushing the prep?

Absolutely. Set out the roast, 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 12 fluid ounce can or bottle of beer. You'll also need a large bowl for the marinade, something to cover it, and later a saucepan for the used marinade.
I've got the sauces and beer on the counter. Does the marinade get mixed before the roast goes in?
Yes. In the large bowl, stir together the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt until the mixture looks even.
The bowl is ready, and the marinade smells strong. Should I trim the roast or just put it in?
If there are large loose pieces of surface fat you can tidy them up, but keep the roast intact. Place the chuck roast into the marinade and turn it so the outside is well coated.
It fits in the bowl, but the marinade doesn't completely cover the top. Is that okay for the 6 hours?
That's fine as long as you cover it, refrigerate it for six hours, and turn it often so all sides spend time in the marinade.
I'm putting it in the fridge now. When it's close to done marinating, what should I set up outside?
Before the roast comes out of the refrigerator, preheat your outdoor grill for indirect heat. Arrange it so the roast can cook away from direct flames rather than sitting right over the heat source.
The grill is heating indirectly, and the roast has marinated. Do I throw away the marinade?
Don't discard it yet. Remove the roast from the marinade, then pour the marinade into a saucepan.
Should I keep the roast on a plate while I deal with the saucepan and grill?

Yes, set the roast on a clean plate or tray while the marinade is transferred to the saucepan. Keep raw-meat tools and surfaces separate from anything clean, then you'll be ready to move the roast to the indirect-heat grill.
I want to get Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce right. What should I handle first? I want to get everything set up before I start heating the oven.
Absolutely. For the ingredients, have 1 medium head garlic, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, and 1/2 cup white wine ready on the counter.
I've got the garlic and olive oil out. The chicken breasts and white wine are still in the fridge—should I grab them now too?
Yes, bring out the 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts and measure 1/2 cup white wine so the full recipe is ready when you need it.
Everything is out now. What temperature should I set the oven to for the garlic?
Set the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, and let it preheat fully before the garlic goes in.
The oven is preheating. How much of the garlic top am I supposed to cut off?
Slice just enough off the top of the head of garlic to remove the papery covering there and expose the tops of the cloves.
I can see the clove tops now. Do I peel the whole thing or leave it together?
Leave the head of garlic together. The cloves should stay in their skins while roasting, with only the tops exposed.
I don't have a clay garlic roaster. What should I use instead, and where does the oil go?
Drizzle the exposed garlic with the 1 tablespoon olive oil, then wrap it in aluminum foil and place it in the preheated oven.
It's wrapped and in the oven. How will I know when the garlic is done?
For Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce, roast it for 20 minutes, or until the cloves are soft and slip from their skins when gently pushed.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce

messages.content: Before I get moving on Cucumber Sandwiches, what should I have ready?
In this Cucumber Sandwiches step, set out 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese spread, 2 teaspoons ranch salad dressing mix, 12 slices pumpernickel rye bread, and 2 medium cucumbers.
I've got the bread and cucumbers out. Do I need anything besides a bowl and a knife?
A bowl, a spreading knife, and a cutting board should cover it. Use the bowl to stir the cream cheese spread with the ranch dressing mix until the seasoning is evenly blended.
The cream cheese mixture looks smooth. Should the cucumbers be peeled?
Peeling is up to you. If the skins are tender, you can leave them on; if you want a softer bite or neater look, peel them before slicing.
I'll peel them. How thin should I cut the slices?
Slice the cucumbers thinly so they layer easily and the sandwiches stay tidy when stacked.
Cucumbers are sliced. Should I spread all the bread or just the bottom pieces?
Spread the cream cheese mixture on one side of each of the 12 slices of pumpernickel rye bread.
All 12 slices are spread. How do I divide the cucumber?
Arrange the thin cucumber slices over 6 of the bread slices, keeping them fairly even from edge to edge.
The cucumber-topped slices are ready. What's the best way to close them without making a mess?
Place the remaining 6 bread slices on top, spread-side down, and press gently so the sandwiches hold together without squeezing out the filling.
I want to make Cinnamon Bread I. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Pull out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda to start.
Those are on the counter. Should I heat the oven before mixing anything?
Yes, bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it is ready when the batter is mixed.
The oven is heating. What pan should I use?
Here, use one 9x5 inch loaf pan, and grease it well so the cinnamon bread releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. I have a large mixing bowl ready—what goes into it?
Measure the flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla into the large mixing bowl.
Everything is in the bowl. Do I stir by hand or use a mixer?
Use a mixer if you have one, and beat the batter for 3 minutes. Scrape the sides once if dry flour clings to the bowl.
After 3 minutes, should the batter be perfectly smooth?
It should look evenly combined and fairly smooth, with the dry ingredients fully worked in. Avoid adding extra flour or sugar beyond the recipe amounts.
Okay, the batter looks even. Do I put it straight into the loaf pan now?
Yes. Pour the batter into the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan, spread the top gently, and keep the oven at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for baking.
Today I'm tackling Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms. Can you help me line up the prep? I'm setting up my cutting board now.
Absolutely. Start by getting the vegetables ready: dice 2 cups of Broccoflower, chop 2 cups of assorted wild mushrooms, and chop 1/2 white onion.
The Broccoflower is diced and the mushrooms are chopped. Should I heat the pan before dealing with the butter?
Yes, set a wide pan over medium heat and add 1 tablespoon unsalted butter. Let it melt gently so it coats the bottom without browning too much.
Butter is melted. The onion is ready too—do the vegetables all go in together?

Add the diced Broccoflower, chopped wild mushrooms, chopped onion, and garlic to the pan. Sauté everything for 10 minutes, stirring now and then so the mushrooms soften and the onion turns translucent.
It's been about 10 minutes, and the pan smells good. The vegetables look softened but not mushy.
That sounds right. Scoop the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic out of the pan and set them aside in a bowl for later.
The pan has some browned bits left in it. Should I clean it before starting the rice?

Keep those browned bits in the same pan; they'll add flavor. Add the rice there, then begin cooking it by adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time, stirring until the liquid is well incorporated before adding the next cup.
I'm adding the stock slowly. What texture am I looking for before I put more in?
Wait until the rice has absorbed most of the stock and the mixture looks creamy rather than soupy. Then add the next 1 cup of chicken stock and keep stirring.
The rice is tender now and the stock is absorbed. Do the vegetables go back in before seasoning?
Yes, stir the sautéed vegetables back into the tender rice. Then stir in nutmeg and herbs, and season with salt and pepper. Taste and adjust before serving while it's creamy and warm.
I pulled up California Chicken. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got chicken breasts out but want to stay on track.
Absolutely. You'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1 pinch salt. Keep pepper nearby too, since it's added to taste at the end.
I have a skillet and a baking dish ready. Does the oven need to be on before I start browning the chicken?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready when you need it.
Oven is heating. Should the skillet be hot before the oil goes in?
Warm the skillet, then add the 1 teaspoon olive oil and let it spread across the pan.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do I put all 4 chicken breasts in at once?
Add the 4 chicken breasts to the skillet in a single layer if they fit without crowding. Sprinkle in the 1/2 teaspoon onion powder as they start cooking.
They fit, and the onion powder is on. What texture or color am I watching for?
Cook them for about 15 minutes, turning as needed, until the chicken is browned and just about done.
After 15 minutes the outside is browned, but I'm not sure if it needs more seasoning before the oven.
Add the 1 pinch salt now, then season with pepper to taste. Keep the seasoning light and even across the chicken.
That's done. Anything else before I serve or clean up the skillet?
Once the chicken is browned and just about done, let it finish as needed in the preheated oven, then serve it hot. The skillet can cool slightly before cleanup.
I'm making chicken pot pie ix today. What's the best place to start?
Absolutely. For this recipe, set out 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cubed, plus 1 cup sliced carrots, 1 cup frozen green peas, and 1/2 cup sliced celery.
The chicken is cubed, and I sliced the carrots and celery. Should the oven be on already?
Yes, go ahead and heat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C), so it is ready while you start the saucepan.
For chicken pot pie ix, oven is heating. What size pan should I use for the chicken and vegetables?
Use a saucepan large enough to hold the chicken, carrots, peas, and celery with room for water to cover them.
I've got everything in the saucepan. Do the peas go in frozen?
Yes, add the 1 cup frozen green peas straight in with the cubed chicken, 1 cup sliced carrots, and 1/2 cup sliced celery.
All combined. How much water am I adding?
Pour in just enough water to cover the chicken and vegetables, then bring it to a boil.
It's boiling now. How long should I keep it going?
Boil the mixture for 15 minutes, keeping an eye on the pot so it stays at a steady boil without overflowing.
The 15 minutes are up. What do I do with the liquid?
Remove the saucepan from the heat, drain the chicken and vegetables well, and set the mixture aside for the next part of the pot pie.
Before I get moving on Cabin Hash, what should I have ready? I've got a big skillet ready but want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Set out 12 medium potatoes, already peeled, cooked, and cubed, plus 3 cups of cubed fully cooked ham. Those two make up most of the hash.
Potatoes and ham are on the counter. What else should I pull from the fridge or pantry?
You'll also need 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup butter or margarine. Keep salt and pepper nearby for seasoning later, and sour cream if you want it for serving.
The onion is chopped. Should I melt the butter before adding everything?
Yes. Put the large skillet over the heat and melt the butter or margarine, then add the cubed potatoes, ham, and chopped onion.
Everything is in the skillet now. How active do I need to be with stirring?
Stir frequently so the onion cooks evenly and the potatoes brown without sticking. Keep cooking until the potatoes are lightly browned.
The potatoes are starting to get some color. There's broccoli in the recipe instructions—when does that go in?
Add the broccoli once the potatoes are lightly browned. Stir it into the hash and heat it through.
The broccoli is hot and mixed in. Should I season while it's still in the pan?
Yes, season the hash with salt and pepper while it's warm in the skillet, then give it a final stir and taste.
It tastes good. What's the best way to serve it?
Spoon the Cabin Hash onto plates while it's hot. Add sour cream on the side or on top if desired.
Garlic Chicken Stir Fry is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got a wok out and want to prep everything before heating it.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. You'll also need the chicken ready to add near the end, plus salt for the aromatics.
The garlic is minced, but I noticed the cooking step only uses some of it at the start. How much goes into the hot oil?
When the oil is ready, you'll quickly stir in 2 cloves of the minced garlic with the ginger, green onions, and salt. Keep the rest of the minced garlic aside if you've prepped all 6 cloves.
Got it. Should I heat the wok empty first or add the peanut oil right away?
Add the 2 tablespoons peanut oil to the wok or large skillet, then heat it. Watch closely; this recipe has you wait until the oil begins to smoke before adding the aromatics.
The oil is shimmering and just starting to smoke. My ginger and green onions are beside the stove.
Go ahead and quickly stir in the 2 cloves minced garlic, the 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving so the garlic doesn't sit and scorch.
It smells good, and the green onions are softening. What texture am I looking for before the chicken goes in?
Stir fry the mixture until the onion turns translucent, about 2 minutes. It should look softened and glossy rather than browned.
I'm at about the 2-minute mark, and the onions look translucent. The chicken is cut and ready.
Add the chicken now and stir it through the aromatics. Keep tossing and spreading the pieces against the hot surface so they cook evenly.
How do I know when the chicken part is done?
Cook and stir until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes. Once there's no raw-looking surface left, take it off the heat and serve it while it's hot.
Before I get moving on Delicious Artichoke Dip, what should I have ready? I've got the counter cleared and want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup mayonnaise and 1/2 cup sour cream, since those form the creamy base.
Those are measured. I also have a can of artichokes—what cheese amount am I using?
Use 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and drain 1 (14 ounce) can of artichoke hearts before they go into the dip.
The artichokes are drained. Should I turn the oven on before mixing?
Yes, get the oven warming to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), so it's ready when the dip is mixed.
Oven is heating. What bowl should I use, and what goes in first?
Use a medium-sized mixing bowl. Stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, Parmesan cheese, and onion until the mixture looks evenly combined.
It's creamy now, with the cheese mixed through. Do the artichokes get chopped or added as they are?
If the artichoke hearts are large, roughly chop them so they're easier to scoop, then mix them into the creamy base.
They're mixed in. I see lemon juice, salt, and pepper mentioned—do those go in at this point too?
Yes, add the lemon juice, salt, and pepper now, then stir until everything is evenly distributed.
The texture looks thick and scoopable. What dish should I move it into?
Transfer the mixture into a shallow baking dish and spread it into an even layer so it will heat evenly in the oven.
I'm about to start Cabbage Rolls II. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got the cabbage out, but I want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Set aside 12 cabbage leaves and make sure you have 1 cup cooked white rice ready. You'll also need a beaten egg and 1/4 cup milk for the filling.
The rice is cooked, and I can beat the egg now. Should I start heating water before mixing anything?
Yes, put a large pot of water on to boil. While it heats, you can keep the rice, beaten egg, milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper nearby for the filling.
The pot is coming up to a boil. Do the cabbage leaves go in whole?
Yes, add the cabbage leaves whole once the water is boiling. Boil them for 2 minutes, just long enough to soften them, then drain them well.
They're drained and a little floppy, which seems right. Should I dry them more?
Let them sit briefly in the colander or blot off extra water if they're dripping. They should be soft enough to roll without being soggy.
Okay, the leaves are cooling. What exactly goes into the bowl for the filling?
In a large bowl, combine the 1 cup cooked rice, beaten egg, 1/4 cup milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper. Mix until everything is evenly distributed.
The filling is mixed. How much should I put on each cabbage leaf so they don't burst?
Use about 1/4 cup of the meat mixture for each leaf. Place it in the center, leaving enough room around the edges to fold and roll.
I'm at the rolling part. Do I fold the sides first or roll from the bottom?
Fold the sides in as you roll, tucking in the ends so the filling stays enclosed. Keep each cabbage roll snug, but don't squeeze so hard that the leaf tears.
I'm making Easy Marinated Vegetables today. What's the best place to start? I've got my cutting board out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting aside 1 1/2 cups broccoli florets and 1 1/2 cups cauliflower florets. Try to keep the florets fairly similar in size so they blanch evenly.
The broccoli and cauliflower are measured. What vegetables should I cut before I turn on the stove?
Cut 1 green bell pepper into 1 inch pieces, then peel, seed, and chop 1 cucumber. If your carrot is not already prepared, have it ready too, since it gets mixed in at the end.
Bell pepper is chopped, and the cucumber is peeled and seeded. What pot should I use?
Use a large pot, fill it with enough water to cover the broccoli and cauliflower, salt the water, and bring it to a boil.
The water is boiling now. Do both florets go in together, and how long should they cook?
Yes, add the broccoli and cauliflower florets together. Keep them in the boiling water for 1 minute only, just to briefly blanch them.
It's been 1 minute. They're still bright and a little firm—is that right?
That sounds right. Drain the florets right away, then rinse them to stop the cooking and cool them down.
They're drained and rinsed. Should I dry them before mixing so the dressing isn't watery?
Give them a good shake in the colander, and if they seem very wet, pat them lightly. Then put the broccoli and cauliflower into a medium size mixing bowl.
They're in the bowl with the bell pepper and cucumber. What goes in last?
Add the carrot and Italian salad dressing, then toss everything together until the vegetables are coated. Once mixed, the Easy Marinated Vegetables are ready to serve or chill.
I'm making Country Fried Chicken today. Can you guide me through the coating setup before I start handling the chicken?

Absolutely. Set out a large resealable plastic bag for the dry coating and a shallow bowl for the wet dip. For the dry mix, measure 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika.
I've got the bag open in a bowl so it won't tip over. Do the flour and seasonings all go in together?
Yes, add the flour, garlic salt, pepper, and paprika to the bag together. Seal it with a little air inside and give it a quick shake so the seasoning spreads evenly through the flour.
The dry mix looks even. What should I do with the shallow bowl?
Beat the egg and milk in the shallow bowl until they're blended. You want it loose enough that the chicken can dip in and come back out with a thin, even coating.
The egg mixture is ready. Should I put all the chicken in the flour bag at once?
Add the chicken a few pieces at a time instead. That gives each piece room to move around, so seal the bag and shake until the pieces are coated in the flour mixture.
Some pieces have a light coating now. Do they go straight into the pan after that?
Not yet. Dip the coated pieces into the egg and milk mixture, letting any extra drip back into the bowl so the outside doesn't get clumpy.
Okay, I dipped the first batch. The coating looks a bit wet and thin.
That's right for this point. Return those dipped pieces to the flour mixture in the bag, seal it again, and shake to coat them a second time.
The second coating is sticking much better. Any tip before I repeat that with the rest?

Keep working in small batches: flour shake, egg-and-milk dip, then back to the flour mixture for another shake. If flour builds up on your fingers or tongs, pause and wipe them so the coating stays even on the chicken.
I'm ready to cook Cucumber Sandwiches. What should be ready before I begin?
Absolutely. For this recipe, set out 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese spread, 2 teaspoons ranch salad dressing mix, 12 slices pumpernickel rye bread, and 2 medium cucumbers.
I've got the cream cheese spread and ranch mix on the counter. Should I use a bowl for mixing?
Yes, use a medium bowl. Add the cream cheese spread and the 2 teaspoons ranch salad dressing mix, then stir until the ranch mix is evenly blended into the cream cheese.
The spread looks smooth now. Do I need to prep all the bread before slicing the cucumbers?
That works well. Lay out the 12 slices of pumpernickel rye bread and spread the cream cheese mixture on one side of each slice.
I'm spreading it now. Should the layer be thick or just enough to cover the bread?
Aim for an even layer that covers the surface without piling it too high, so the sandwiches hold together neatly when you add the cucumbers.
Bread is covered. For the 2 cucumbers, do I peel them first?
Peel the cucumbers if you'd like a softer look and texture; leaving the peel on is fine too. Either way, thinly slice the 2 medium cucumbers.
They're thinly sliced. How many bread slices get cucumber?
Place the cucumber slices on six of the bread slices, right over the cream cheese mixture. Try to spread them out evenly so each sandwich has cucumber in every bite.
Six slices are topped with cucumber. What's the easiest way to close and serve them?
Top those cucumber-covered slices with the remaining six bread slices, cream-cheese side down. Press lightly, then arrange the sandwiches on your platter.
A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got my blender out but haven't opened anything yet.
Absolutely. Set up the blender jar and gather the fruit: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen mixed berries and 1 (15 ounce) can sliced peaches, drained.
The berries are still frozen, and I drained the peaches. Is there anything else before I start loading the blender?
Yes, measure out 2 tablespoons honey. That's the only other ingredient for this smoothie.
Should the frozen berries go in first, or does it not matter?
Add the frozen mixed berries to the blender, then pour in the drained sliced peaches. The softer peaches can help the blades catch the frozen fruit.
Both fruits are in. The honey is sticking to the spoon a bit.
Scrape the 2 tablespoons honey into the blender as best you can. It's fine if a little clings to the spoon; the blender will mix the rest in once it gets moving.
Everything is in the jar. Do I need to add liquid?
For this recipe, don't add extra liquid. Just blend the frozen berries, drained peaches, and honey together until the mixture turns smooth.
Here, it's blending, but there are still a few berry chunks near the top.
Stop the blender, scrape down the sides if needed, then blend again until those chunks disappear and the smoothie looks evenly smooth.
It looks thick and smooth now. How should I serve it?
Pour it into glasses right away while it's cold and frosty. Give the blender jar a quick rinse soon after serving so the honey and fruit don't dry onto it.

original_cues.support_assistant_cue: Yes. I'll keep that texture in mind for this cheesecake: let the cheese lose some of its chill before you need it, and near serving, break it into uneven hand-crumbled pieces so it stays rustic rather than uniform.
original_cues.support_feedback_cue: Yes, that crumbly cheese style is exactly what I mean for this one. While the oven heats, do I grease the springform?
original_cues.support_user_cue: When we make Chocolate Cheesecake II, can we do the cheese the way I usually like it—softened a bit, then broken up by hand instead of made perfectly smooth?

memory_annotations.support_assistant_cue: For the cheese later, let it warm just enough to lose its chill, then break it by hand into uneven crumbles near serving. Stop stirring now, and do not shake the pan. Let it cook undisturbed from this point so the candy stays smooth instead of turning grainy.

Peel them over a bowl or scrap container to keep the skins contained. Once peeled, move the potatoes onto the lightly floured surface.

Use the rolling pin as a masher, not like you're rolling pastry. Press and roll gently over the potatoes until they break down into an even, fluffy mash.

Sprinkle the 1/2 cup all-purpose flour over the potatoes, add the 1 egg, and bring the mixture together gently. Fold in most of the finely chopped parsley as you mix so it stays evenly distributed.

Add the aromatics immediately, then stir right away. Keep them moving across the hot surface so the garlic perfumes the oil without sitting in one spot.

Keep stir frying until the onion becomes translucent, about 2 minutes total. You're looking for softened, glossy pieces rather than browned ones.

Yes, add the chicken now and stir it through the garlic, ginger, and green onions. Keep tossing until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes.

Make sure the chicken looks opaque throughout and no raw-looking spots remain. When it's cooked through, take the wok off the heat and serve the stir fry right away with the fruit on the side.
I want to get Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup right. What should I handle first? I'm getting my pot and cutting board out now.

Yes. Add the vegetable oil to the large pot and warm it over medium heat while you keep the vegetables nearby.

They do. Stir in the onion, green bell pepper, carrot, and garlic, then cook them for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they're tender.

They should soften around the edges and bend a little when you press them with the spoon, while the onion and bell pepper look tender rather than raw.

Mix 1 can of black beans into the pot along with the chicken broth, stirring so the softened vegetables are evenly distributed.

Exactly. Put the remaining can of beans in a blender and puree it until smooth so it can give the soup a thicker, creamier body.

Yes, stir the smooth puree into the pot until it blends with the broth, beans, and vegetables. Keep the heat at medium and scrape the blender well so you don't leave that thickened bean mixture behind.

messages.content: Chicken Fiesta Salad is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got the chicken out and want to make sure I'm not missing anything before I start.
Absolutely. For the chicken part, have 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves ready, plus 1 packet of dry fajita seasoning—the 1.27 ounce size. You'll divide that seasoning in half.
I found the fajita packet. What should I set by the stove with the skillet?
Put 1 tablespoon vegetable oil near the skillet. You'll also want a large saucepan for the bean mixture, plus 1 can of black beans, 15 ounces, rinsed and drained.
Beans are drained. The recipe mentions the warm mixture too—what else goes in there?
In the saucepan later, you'll combine the black beans with corn, salsa, and the remaining 1/2 of the fajita seasoning. Keep those close so you don't have to hunt for them while the chicken cooks.
Okay, chicken is on a plate. Do I season it before heating the pan?
Yes. Rub the chicken evenly with 1/2 of the fajita seasoning, coating both sides as evenly as you can.
It's coated. Should the skillet be really hot or more moderate?
Use medium heat. Warm the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in the skillet, then add the chicken.
Chicken is in the skillet. How long should I let it go before flipping?
Cook it for 8 minutes on the first side, then flip and cook another 8 minutes on the other side, or until the juices run clear. After that, set the chicken aside.
The chicken is set aside and the saucepan is ready. How do I finish the beans?

Add the rinsed and drained black beans to the large saucepan with the corn, salsa, and the other 1/2 of the fajita seasoning. Heat it over medium heat until everything is warm, then serve it with the chicken for the Chicken Fiesta Salad.
I pulled up Cosmopolitan. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got a shaker out but I want to measure it properly.
Absolutely. For one drink, measure 1 jigger vodka, which is 1.5 fluid ounces, plus 1/2 fluid ounce cointreau.
Vodka and cointreau are measured. What juices should I add before I put ice in?
Add 1 teaspoon fresh lime juice and 1 1/2 fluid ounces cranberry juice to the shaker with the spirits.
Should the ice go in after everything is poured, or should I chill the shaker first?
Once all the ingredients are in the shaker, fill it with lots of ice so the drink gets cold quickly when you shake it.
The shaker is full of ice and liquid. How hard am I shaking this?
Shake it vigorously for several seconds. You want the outside of the shaker to feel very cold, but the recipe just calls for a short, strong shake rather than a long one.
I've shaken it and the tin is frosty. Do I pour everything, ice included, into the glass?
Strain it into a cocktail glass so the ice stays behind in the shaker and the drink goes in smooth.
It's strained into the glass. I have a lime—what kind of garnish should I make?
Use a lime twist. Cut or peel a small strip of lime zest, twist it over the drink if you like, then place it on the rim or drop it in.
Looks good. Anything else before serving it?
That's it: vodka, cointreau, fresh lime juice, and cranberry juice shaken with plenty of ice, strained into a cocktail glass, and garnished with the lime twist. Serve it right away while it's cold.
I'm about to start Caramelized Apple Bites. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got apples on the counter but haven't started prepping them yet.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 individually wrapped caramels, unwrapped and chopped, plus 2 tablespoons of light corn syrup. Set those beside a medium microwave-safe bowl.

Yes, chop the caramels into smaller pieces so they melt more evenly. Put the chopped caramels into the microwave-safe bowl with the light corn syrup.
Done. For the apples, do they need to be peeled and diced before I melt the caramel?
Yes. Peel, core, and dice 2 apples before you melt the caramel mixture, so they're ready to toss as soon as it's smooth.
The apples are diced now. How long should the bowl go in the microwave?
Microwave the caramels and light corn syrup on high for about 30 seconds, just until the mixture is melted.
It's mostly melted but I see one small lump of caramel. Should I stir it?
Give it a careful stir; the heat in the bowl may smooth out that last bit. If it's melted enough to coat the apples, you're ready to continue.
The caramel mixture is smooth now. Do the apples go straight into that same bowl?
Yes, add the diced apples to the bowl and toss them until they're coated with the caramel and light corn syrup mixture.
They're coated and look glossy. Can I serve them right away, or should they sit for a bit?
Let the Caramelized Apple Bites cool before serving so the coating settles and they're easier to eat.

I'm starting 1 Pot 3 Bean Chicken Stew; can you walk me through the setup? I'm starting with the chicken and vegetables on the counter.

Chop 1 large yellow onion and slice 1 cup celery. The onion goes in after the chicken is browned, and the celery gets added with the stew ingredients for the long simmer.

Add the canola oil to the large pot and heat it, then brown the chicken chunks in the oil. Give the pieces some space so they brown instead of steaming.

Add the chopped yellow onion to the same pot and sauté it until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir occasionally and let it pick up those browned bits for flavor.

Add the broth, beans, tomatoes, sliced celery, carrots, wine, bay leaf, herbs, and all of the browned chicken back into the pot. Stir everything together so the chicken is nestled into the liquid.

Cover the pot and let the stew simmer for 40 minutes. Keep it at a gentle simmer, not a hard boil, and stir once or twice so nothing sticks to the bottom.

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need a clean wide-mouth 1 liter glass jar for layering the mix.
The jar is clean and dry. Do I mix the sugar in with the flour right away?

Keep the sugar separate for the moment. In a bowl, combine the 4 cups all-purpose flour with the 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda, along with the salt and nutmeg called for in the instructions.
The flour mixture is blended. It looks a little fluffy—should I pack it before it goes into the jar?
Not yet. Add the 1 1/2 cups white sugar to the bottom of the wide-mouth 1 liter jar first, keeping it as an even layer.
Sugar layer is in, but some stuck to the side of the glass. Is that a problem?
That's fine. Gently tap the jar on the counter to level the sugar, then spoon the flour mixture on top so the two layers stay distinct.
The flour mixture is in the jar now, but it's mounded close to the rim.
Press the contents firmly in place so the mix settles and the lid can close securely. Once it's compacted, seal the jar.
It sealed. What should I write on the card for whoever bakes them?
Write that they should place the mix in a large bowl, then beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy before continuing with the cookie preparation.
Should the card mention anything about the jar layers, or just the egg and butter part?

Keep the card focused on the baking instructions: use the jarred mix, and in a large bowl beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy. Then attach the card to the sealed jar.
I want to make Caraway Rye Muffins. Can you guide me while I get set up?

Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and gather 1 cup rye flour, 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup sugar, and 2 1/2 teaspoons baking powder. You'll also need salt, caraway seeds, cheese, an egg, milk, oil, and greased or paper-lined muffin cups.
The flours, sugar, and baking powder are measured. Should the dry ingredients all go in together?

Yes. In the large bowl, combine the rye flour, all-purpose flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and caraway seeds. Mix them well enough that the baking powder and seeds are evenly spread through the flour.
I can see the caraway seeds throughout the bowl now. Where does the cheese come in?
Stir the cheese into that dry mixture. Use a light hand so it gets coated with the flour mixture instead of clumping together.
The cheese is mixed in, but I haven't touched the wet ingredients yet. What should I combine?
In a separate bowl or measuring cup, combine the egg, milk, and oil. Beat or stir them together until the egg is broken up and the mixture looks mostly uniform.
The wet mixture is ready. I'm worried about making the muffins tough when I add it.
Pour the egg, milk, and oil mixture into the dry ingredients, then stir just until moistened. Stop as soon as you no longer see dry patches; a few lumps are fine.
The batter looks a little lumpy but there aren't dry streaks. How full should the muffin cups be?
That texture sounds right. Fill the greased or paper-lined muffin cups two-thirds full so the muffins have room to rise.
I've filled the cups about two-thirds full. Anything to tidy up before they bake?

Wipe any batter off the top of the muffin pan so it doesn't bake on, and make sure each cup is filled fairly evenly. The recipe guidance you have ends with the cups filled two-thirds full, so they're ready for the next baking direction you're using.
I want to make Caraway Rye Muffins and I'm setting up the counter. What should I measure out first?
Start with the dry base: measure 1 cup rye flour and 3/4 cup all-purpose flour into a large bowl, or into separate cups if you like to double-check before mixing.
The flours are measured. I still have sugar and baking powder nearby—how much of each goes in?
Add 1/4 cup sugar and 2 1/2 teaspoons baking powder to the bowl with the flours. You'll also be combining salt and caraway seeds with those dry ingredients.
Should I whisk those together, or just dump everything in and leave it?
Give the flours, sugar, baking powder, salt, and caraway seeds a good stir in the large bowl so the leavening and seeds are evenly spread through the mixture.
The dry mixture looks even. I have the cheese ready—does that go in before the wet ingredients?
Yes, stir in the cheese now. Coat it lightly with the flour mixture as you stir so it doesn't clump in one spot.
Cheese is mixed in. For the wet bowl, I'm using an egg, milk, and oil, right?
Right. Combine the egg, milk, and oil in a separate bowl or measuring cup, then pour that into the dry ingredients.
When I mix the wet and dry together, how far should I take it? I don't want dense muffins.
Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened. A few small lumps are fine; stop before the batter gets smooth and overworked.
The batter is ready, and I have paper liners in the muffin pan. How full should each cup be?
Spoon the batter into the greased or paper-lined muffin cups until each one is about two-thirds full. Wipe any big drips from the pan edges before baking.
I'm planning to make BBQ Chuck Roast today. Can you guide me through what to set out before I start?
Absolutely. Put out 1 (5 pound) chuck roast, 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer. You'll also want a large bowl for the marinade.
I have the roast and sauces on the counter. The beer is chilled—does that matter for mixing the marinade?
Chilled beer is fine. Pour the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, and beer into the large bowl, then mix in the garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt until the marinade looks evenly combined.
The marinade is mixed and smells pretty strong. Do I trim the roast before it goes in?
You can leave the roast mostly as it is unless there are very thick, loose pieces of surface fat you want to remove. Set the chuck roast into the marinade so it's well coated.
It's in the bowl now, but the top isn't fully submerged. Is coating it enough?
Yes, coating is fine as long as you cover it and refrigerate it for six hours, turning it often so different sides spend time in the marinade.
I'll turn it during the afternoon. When it's close to cooking time, what should I do with the grill?
Preheat an outdoor grill for indirect heat. Set it up so the roast won't be sitting directly over the heat source.
The grill is heating for indirect cooking. Should I keep the marinade or throw it out when I pull the meat?
Keep it for this recipe step: remove the roast from the marinade, then pour the marinade into a saucepan.
Got it. I've moved the roast out and the marinade is in a pan. Anything I should watch so cleanup is easier?

Wipe any drips from the bowl area and keep the saucepan separate from clean utensils. At this point, you're set up with the marinated roast ready for the grill and the reserved marinade in the saucepan.
I'm starting Babis Bean Salad; can you walk me through the setup? I soaked the black-eyed peas overnight and want to make sure I handle them right.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 1/2 cups dried black-eyed peas that have been soaked overnight, plus 1/3 cup chopped celery with the leaves included.
The peas are drained, and I have celery with some leafy tops. What should I prep before turning on the stove?
Go ahead and prep the remaining vegetables: 1 1/2 cups shredded carrot and 3/4 cup chopped fresh parsley. Keep those aside while the beans cook and cool.
I've got a medium saucepan ready. How much water should I add with the beans?
Put the soaked black-eyed peas in the saucepan, then add enough water to cover them by 1 inch. That gives them room to simmer evenly without drying out.
They're covered by about an inch now. Should I start them on high heat?
Yes, bring them up gently until the water reaches a slow boil. You're looking for steady movement, not a hard rolling boil.
It's bubbling slowly around the edges and through the middle. Do I leave it there?
Turn the heat down to low and let the beans simmer until they're tender but not mushy, about 35 minutes. Check once or twice to make sure they stay covered with water.
What texture am I aiming for when I taste one?
A bean should bite easily without feeling chalky, but it should still hold its shape. If it starts splitting apart or turning creamy, it's going too far for a salad.
They're tender now and still mostly intact. What do I do before adding the celery, carrot, and parsley?
Take the pan off the heat and set the beans aside to cool. Once they're no longer hot, they'll be ready to combine with the chopped celery, shredded carrot, and fresh parsley.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Put the dressing beneath the greens, then keep the surface mostly undressed so the plate stays neat and the top looks fresh.

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Spoon the dressing underneath the greens and leave the top mostly dry.
