messages.content: For this serving of Best Chocolate Chippers, I'm plating it like a salad with a dressing or vinaigrette. What's the best way to dress the plate?
Put the dressing beneath the greens, then keep the surface mostly undressed so the plate stays neat and the top looks fresh.
Perfect, that's the style I want for this one. Before I start mixing, which ingredients should I pull out first?
Get the 1 cup butter and 1 cup vegetable oil onto the counter first, since they'll be creamed together with the sugars.
I've got the butter and oil ready. What sugars do I need beside the bowl?
Set out 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Use a large bowl so you have room to work the butter, oil, and both sugars until smooth.
The large bowl is out, and the sugars are measured. Should I deal with the oven before combining anything?
Yes, turn the oven on to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you mix.
Oven is heating. What texture am I looking for when I mix the butter, oil, and sugars?
Cream the butter, vegetable oil, brown sugar, and white sugar together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended, with no separate streaks of fat or sugar pockets.
It's looking smooth now. I see eggs and vanilla in the directions—do they go in next?
Yes, beat in the eggs and vanilla now. Mix until they're fully incorporated into the creamed mixture.
That's mixed in. I want to keep cleanup easy—can I combine the dry ingredients separately first?
Combine the flour, baking soda, cream of tartar, and salt together, then stir that dry mixture into the creamed mixture.
Once the dry ingredients go in, should I keep beating hard or switch to a gentler stir?
Switch to stirring just until the flour mixture is worked in. That keeps the dough from getting overmixed while still bringing everything together for Best Chocolate Chippers.
British Bread Pudding is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a mixing bowl ready and want to make sure I start in the right order.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it can heat while you prepare the pudding mixture.
Oven is heating. What should I measure out for the bread part?
Measure 6 1/4 cups of cubed whole wheat bread and put it into a large bowl. Pour 1 1/4 cups milk over the bread.
The bread and milk are in the bowl. Do I stir it right away or let it sit?
Give it a light turn so the bread is moistened, then set the bowl aside for 5 minutes so the cubes can soak up the milk.
While it soaks, what else needs to be ready on the counter?
Have 1 beaten egg ready, along with 1/3 cup softened butter. You'll also need the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon for the next mixing stage.
The bread has softened. Should the egg and butter go in before the fruit and spices?
Yes. Stir in the beaten egg and the softened butter, then add the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon to the same bowl.
It's looking a little uneven with pockets of butter. How much mixing should I do?
Mix well, scraping around the sides and folding through the center, until the butter, egg, fruit, sugar, and spices are evenly worked into the soaked bread.
So at this point the mixture should be fully combined before I do anything else?
That's right. Once it's evenly mixed and the bread is well coated, you've completed the prep covered here for the British Bread Pudding.
Easy Punch is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I'm setting out a large punch bowl now.
Absolutely. Put the large punch bowl on a steady surface, and gather 4 packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder, each 0.13 ounce.
The drink mix packets are out. I also see pineapple juice in the pantry—how much goes in?
You'll need 2 cans of pineapple juice, 46 fluid ounces each. Open both so they're ready to pour into the bowl.
Both cans are open. What else should I measure before I start combining everything?
Measure 3 cups of white sugar and 4 quarts of water. Those go in with the drink mix and pineapple juice.
I've got the sugar measured and the water ready. Do I pour it all into the punch bowl together?
For this batch of Easy Punch, add the strawberry drink mix powder, pineapple juice, white sugar, and water to the large punch bowl.
Everything is in the bowl, but I can still see sugar and powder settling near the bottom.
Stir steadily, scraping along the bottom and sides of the bowl, until the sugar and drink mix are fully dissolved.
It looks smooth now and I don't feel grit on the spoon. The bowl is pretty full—what about the ginger ale?
Gently stir in the ginger ale so it mixes through without losing too much fizz.
The punch is mixed and bubbly. Should I serve it right away or do anything else first?
It's ready to serve once the ginger ale is stirred in. Give it a light final stir before ladling or pouring into cups.
I have Caraway Rye Muffins planned for today. What should I set up first? I'm starting with an empty counter and want to measure things as we go.
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl, a smaller bowl or measuring cup for the wet ingredients, and a muffin tin with greased cups or paper liners.
The bowl and muffin tin are ready. Which dry ingredients should I measure first?
Measure 1 cup rye flour and 3/4 cup all-purpose flour into the large bowl.
Both flours are in. I have sugar and baking powder next to me.
Add 1/4 cup sugar and 2 1/2 teaspoons baking powder to the same bowl, then include the salt and caraway seeds from the recipe.
The dry mixture is together. Should I whisk it or just leave it layered?
Give it a good stir so the flours, sugar, baking powder, salt, and caraway seeds are evenly combined before adding anything heavier.
It looks evenly mixed. I've got the cheese out now—does that go in before the liquids?
Yes, stir in the cheese at this point so it gets coated with the dry mixture.
Cheese is mixed in. I'm ready for the egg, milk, and oil, but I don't want to overwork the batter.
Combine the egg, milk, and oil separately, then pour that into the dry ingredients. Stir only until everything is just moistened; a few small lumps are fine.
The batter is thick and a little lumpy, not dry. How full should I make the muffin cups?
Spoon the batter into the greased or paper-lined muffin cups until each one is about two-thirds full, then they'll be ready for baking according to your recipe's baking directions.
I'm getting ready for Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing. Can you help me sequence the steps? I'm starting with the rotisserie chicken and want to set up the bowls correctly.
Absolutely. Put a medium bowl on your work surface for the salad. You'll need 4 cups rotisserie chicken, skinned and boned, with the meat shredded into bite-sized pieces.
The chicken is shredded. I also have celery, green onions, and peanuts—how should I prep those before they go in?
Cut 2 medium celery ribs into small dice, slice 2 medium green onions thin, and chop 1/4 cup honey-roasted peanuts. Add all of those to the medium bowl with the chicken.
Everything is in the medium bowl. Should I stir it a lot or just combine it lightly?
Give it a gentle mix so the chicken, celery, green onions, and peanuts are evenly distributed without crushing the peanuts too much.
I'm ready for the dressing. What goes into the small bowl?
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, sugar, red pepper, cilantro, mint, and 2 Tbs. water until the sugar starts to dissolve and the herbs are spread through the dressing.
The dressing smells bright and a little salty. Do I pour all of it over the chicken at once?
Yes, toss the dressing with the chicken mixture. Use a folding motion so everything gets coated while the shredded chicken stays in bite-sized pieces.
It's coated now. What texture should I be looking for before serving?
It should look lightly dressed rather than soupy, with the celery still crisp and the peanuts adding little crunchy bits throughout.
I have Boston lettuce washed and dried. How do I plate it?
Arrange the chicken salad on a bed of Boston lettuce and serve it with the suggested accompaniments. If any dressing has settled in the bowl, spoon a little over the top just before serving.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing

messages.content: I want to make Basil Burgers on the grill today. Can you guide me from setup through cooking?

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil, or more to taste, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt. You'll also want pepper, a mixing bowl, a plate or tray for the patties, and oil for the grill grate.
I've got the beef and seasonings out. Should I start heating the grill before mixing?
Yes, preheat an outdoor grill to high heat while you make the patties. That way the grate is hot when the burgers are ready to go on.
The grill is warming up. How should I combine everything without overworking the meat?

Put the ground beef in a bowl, then add the Worcestershire sauce, dried basil, garlic salt, and pepper. Mix gently with your hands or a fork just until the seasonings are evenly distributed; stop once it looks combined.
The mixture smells good. How many patties am I shaping, and how thick should they be?
Form the mixture into 4 burger patties. Try to make them even in size so they cook at the same pace, and press a shallow dimple in the center of each one to help them stay flatter on the grill.
They're shaped and on a tray. Do I need to oil the grill now?
Yes. Lightly oil the grill grate right before cooking so the patties release more easily. Use tongs and an oiled paper towel, and be careful around the high heat.
The grate is oiled. How long do the burgers need, and when do I flip them?

Place the patties on the hot grate and cook them about 6 minutes total, turning once during cooking. Keep the lid down between checks if your grill has one, and avoid pressing on the burgers so the juices stay inside.
I have a thermometer ready. What temperature should I look for before serving?

Check the center of each burger and cook to an internal temperature of 160 degrees F, which is 70 degrees C, or to your desired doneness. Once they're there, move them off the grill and let them rest briefly before serving.
Basic Syrup for Sunset Cooler is on deck today. What should I do first? I'm setting out the saucepan and ingredients now.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 cup white sugar, 1 cup water, and 2 pandan leaves. Use a deep saucepan so the syrup has room as it comes to a boil.
I've measured the sugar and water. Should the pandan leaves go in whole?
Yes, add the pandan leaves whole with the sugar and water. Put all three into the deep saucepan together before heating.
Everything is in the pan. What heat should I use to start?
Set the pan over heat and bring the mixture to a boil. Give it a gentle stir if needed so the sugar starts dissolving.
It's starting to bubble, and I can still see a little sugar at the bottom.
Once it reaches a boil, lower the heat and let it simmer until the sugar is completely dissolved. The liquid should look clear rather than grainy.
The syrup looks clear now. Do I keep simmering it for longer?
No extra simmering is needed once the sugar has dissolved. Take it off the heat and remove the pandan leaves.
I pulled out the leaves. There are a few tiny bits in the liquid—should I strain it?
Yes, strain the syrup to catch any pandan pieces or residue. Pour it through a fine strainer into a clean container.
It's strained and still warm. Can I use it in the drink right away?
Let it cool first, then it's ready to use as the basic syrup for the Sunset Cooler.
I'm setting up for Gingered Mango Salsa; what should happen before the heat goes on? I'm getting the ingredients onto the counter now.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 cup chopped peeled mango, 1/4 cup chopped red onion, 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro, and 1/4 cup lime juice.
I've got the mango peeled and chopped. Should the onion and cilantro be chopped pretty small?
Yes, keep the red onion chopped small so it blends through the salsa, and mince the fresh cilantro. Measure out 1/4 cup of each.
Done. I also measured the lime juice into a small cup. What bowl should I use?
Use a medium mixing bowl with enough room to toss everything together without spilling.
The mango is in the bowl. Do I add the onion next or the lime juice?
Either order is fine. Add the chopped red onion, minced cilantro, and lime juice to the bowl with the mango.
Everything is in there now. Should I mash it at all or just mix?
Just stir it together gently. You want the mango pieces to stay intact while the lime juice coats everything.
It's mixed and looks bright. Is it ready to serve right away?
Let it stand for 30 minutes before serving so the flavors have time to blend.
Should I cover it while it sits, or leave it uncovered on the counter?
Cover the bowl while it stands. After 30 minutes, give the salsa one more gentle stir and serve it fresh.
I want to make Chocolate Hazelnut Fruit Crepes. Can you talk me through getting everything ready?
Absolutely. Set out 4 crepes, 1 cup chocolate hazelnut spread, 4 sliced bananas, and 1 (7 ounce) can of pressurized whipped cream. A skillet and a spatula will help for warming them.
The crepes are on a plate and the bananas are sliced. Should I divide the spread before I start filling?
Yes, that will make it easier: use 1/4 cup of chocolate hazelnut spread for each crepe, spreading it across the surface while leaving a little room near the edges.
I've spread the chocolate hazelnut on all 4. How should the banana go in so they roll neatly?
Arrange 1 sliced banana down the center of each crepe in a fairly even line. Try not to pile it too high, so the crepes can roll without tearing.
They're filled, but the ends look a little loose. Do I tuck them or just roll straight across?
Roll each crepe up gently around the banana filling. You can keep the seam side down after rolling so they hold together better.
My skillet is on the stove. How warm should it be before the crepes go in?
Use a warm skillet over medium heat. Once it feels gently heated, place the rolled crepes in seam side down so they can warm without scorching the spread.
They're in the skillet now. How long do I leave them there?
Let them warm for about 90 seconds. You're just taking the chill off and softening the filling, not trying to brown them deeply.
They're warmed through and still soft. When does the whipped cream come in?
Move the crepes to serving plates, then add the pressurized whipped cream on top or alongside right before serving so it stays fluffy.
I have Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got the squash on the counter but haven't cut it yet.

Absolutely. You'll need 1 spaghetti squash, halved lengthwise and seeded, plus 1 chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 (14 ounce) cans stewed tomatoes. Go ahead and cut the squash lengthwise and scoop out the seeds.
The squash is halved and seeded. Should I prep the onion and garlic now too?
Yes, chop the onion and measure out the minced garlic while the oven comes up to temperature. Set the tomatoes nearby too, so everything is ready for the lasagna-style filling later.
What temperature should I set the oven to for the squash?
Yes, get the oven warming to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C, for Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style.
Oven is heating. What pan setup works best for the squash halves?
Use a baking sheet and coat it with a thin layer of cooking spray so the squash doesn't stick while it bakes.
I sprayed the baking sheet. Do the halves go open-side up or down?
Place the spaghetti squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.
They're on the sheet cut side down. How long should I bake them?
Here, bake the squash for 35 minutes in the preheated oven.
How do I know if it's done if my squash is a little larger?
Check it with a knife: it's ready when the knife can be easily inserted into the squash. If it still feels firm, give it a few more minutes and check again.
I want to make Garlic Butter for bread tonight. Can you guide me through what to set out?

Absolutely. Put a small mixing bowl and a fork or flexible spatula on the counter. You'll need 1 cup butter, softened; 1 tablespoon minced garlic; 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese; and 1 tablespoon garlic salt.
The butter is soft enough to press with a spoon. Should I add everything to the bowl at once?

Start with the softened butter in the small bowl, then add the 1 tablespoon minced garlic and the 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese. Mash and fold them together until the garlic and cheese are evenly worked through the butter.
It's mixed, but I can still see little Parmesan flecks. Is that fine?
Yes, Parmesan flecks are expected. The mixture should look creamy overall, with the garlic and cheese distributed throughout rather than completely smooth.
I'm ready to season it. The garlic salt is measured—do I put in the whole amount?
Add the 1 tablespoon garlic salt and stir it in well. Then season with Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika, mixing after each addition so the flavor spreads evenly.
The paprika made it a little speckled and the smell is strong in a good way. Should I keep mixing?
Give it a few more folds, scraping the sides of the bowl so there aren't plain streaks of butter left. Once the color and seasonings look evenly dispersed, you can stop.
I'm going to spread it on sliced bread. Should I chill it first or use it soft?
For spreading on bread right away, use it soft. If you want a firmer garlic butter for later, shape it or spoon it into a container and chill it after mixing.
Before I serve it, is there anything else the recipe needs?
No additional recipe step is needed after the seasoning is mixed in. Taste a tiny bit if you like, then spread it on the bread or store the finished Garlic Butter for later.
I pulled up BBQ Chuck Roast. Can you guide the first few moves? I'm getting the meat and sauces out now.

Absolutely. You'll need 1 (5 pound) chuck roast, 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer. Also have garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt ready for the marinade.
I've got the 5 pound roast, the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, and a 12 fluid ounce beer. What kind of bowl should I use?

Use a large bowl with enough room to stir the marinade and later hold the roast. Pour in the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, and beer, then mix in the garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt until everything is evenly combined.
The marinade is mixed and smells pretty strong. Do I put the roast straight into that bowl?
Yes. Place the chuck roast into the marinade, turn it so the surface gets coated, then cover the bowl and refrigerate it for six hours.
During those six hours, should I leave it alone or move it around?
Turn it often while it marinates so different sides spend time in the sauce. Keep it covered and refrigerated the whole time.
It's been marinating for six hours, and I'm ready to cook outside. What should I do with the grill?
Preheat your outdoor grill for indirect heat. Set it up so the roast can cook away from direct flame rather than sitting right over the hottest area.
The grill is set for indirect heat. Should I carry the whole bowl outside?
Bring the roast and marinade out carefully, but keep them separate once you remove the meat. Lift the roast out of the marinade and let the excess drip back into the bowl.
The roast is out. I still have a lot of marinade in the bowl—do I toss it?
Don't toss it yet. Pour the marinade into a saucepan as the recipe directs, then you'll be set up for the next part of cooking the BBQ chuck roast.
I want to get Banana Chip Muffins I right. What should I handle first? I'm setting a large mixing bowl on the counter.
Absolutely. For the dry ingredients, measure 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour into the large bowl, then add 1/2 cup white sugar.
Flour and sugar are in. I'm checking the leavening and salt next—how much should I use?
Here, add 1 tablespoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt to that same bowl.
Those are measured in. The recipe mentions chocolate chips too—do they go with the dry ingredients?
For this batch of Banana Chip Muffins I, yes, measure the chocolate chips into the large bowl along with the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Everything dry is in the bowl. Do I just stir it, or should I be careful with the texture?
Mix the dry ingredients thoroughly so the baking powder and salt are evenly distributed, then make a well in the center of the mixture.
I made the well. I've got a small bowl ready for the egg—what should it look like before I add anything else?
Beat the egg in the small bowl until it looks frothy, with bubbles on the surface and a loosened texture.
The egg is frothy now. I have cooking oil, milk, and bananas nearby.
Mix the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the beaten egg mixture.
The wet mixture is combined, and the dry bowl still has the well in the center. Is that the point I should be at?
Yes, that matches the recipe flow: the dry ingredients and chocolate chips are mixed with a well in the center, and the egg has been beaten frothy before mixing in the cooking oil, milk, and bananas.
I have French Spring Soup planned for today. What should I set up first? I'm putting a large pot on the stove and want to check what to prep first.
Absolutely. Have 1/4 cup butter ready, plus 1 pound leeks, chopped. You'll also need 1 chopped onion and 2 quarts water for the base.
The leeks are chopped, but they look a little sandy. Should I rinse them before they go in?
Yes, rinse the chopped leeks well and drain them so grit doesn't end up in the soup. Once they're clean, keep the chopped onion nearby too.
Everything is rinsed and drained. Do I start with the butter in the pot?
Yes. Melt the butter in the large pot over medium heat, letting it coat the bottom without browning.
The butter has melted and is foaming lightly. Should I add both vegetables at once?
Add the leeks and onion together, then stir them through the butter. Cook them until they're tender, stirring now and then so they soften evenly.
They're soft and smell sweet. There are a few bits stuck to the bottom of the pot.
That's fine. Pour in the 2 quarts water and stir across the bottom of the pot to loosen those bits into the soup.
Water is in. I also have potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice ready on the counter.
Great. Mix in the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice, making sure the rice is distributed instead of clumping in one spot.
It's all stirred together. Should I keep the heat at medium for now?
Keep it heating steadily so the soup can come together, stirring occasionally to keep the rice from settling on the bottom.
I pulled up Dads BBQ Roast. Can you guide the first few moves? I have the counter cleared and want to make sure I set everything out correctly.

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 envelopes of dry onion soup mix, and the 5 pound beef rump roast. You'll also need a small bowl, something to stir with, paper towels for drying the roast, and two long sheets of aluminum foil.
I found the mustard and the onion soup mix. Each envelope is 1 ounce—does that match what I need?
Yes, that's right: use 2 of those 1 ounce envelopes. Stir both envelopes into the 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard in the small bowl until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The mustard mixture is thick and speckled from the soup mix. Should I thin it out at all?
No need to thin it. A thick mixture is useful here because it will cling to the roast when you coat it.
I've got the roast still in its packaging. What should I do before it touches the foil?
Unwrap the 5 pound beef rump roast and pat it dry well with paper towels. Drying the surface helps the mustard-onion mixture spread and stay on the meat.
For the foil, do the two sheets go side by side or stacked?
Lay out two long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise, like a plus sign. That gives you enough coverage under the roast and around the sides.
The foil is crossed on the counter. Where should the roast sit?
Place the patted-dry roast right in the center where the two foil sheets overlap, so it's supported from underneath.
Okay, the roast is centered. How heavy should I go with the coating?
Coat it generously with the mustard and onion soup mixture, spreading it over the exposed surfaces so the roast is well covered before you wrap or continue with the rest of your cooking plan.
I have Babis Bean Salad planned for today. What should I set up first? My black-eyed peas soaked overnight, and I'm ready to start.
Absolutely. Check that you have 1 1/2 cups dried black-eyed peas that have soaked overnight, plus a saucepan large enough to hold them with water above the beans.
The peas are drained and in the saucepan. How much water should I add?
Add enough water to cover the beans by 1 inch. Once they're covered, put the pan on the stove.
Done. While that heats, what fresh ingredients should I prep for the salad?
Prep 1/3 cup chopped celery, including the leaves, 1 1/2 cups shredded carrot, and 3/4 cup chopped fresh parsley.
I've got the celery, carrot, and parsley ready. The pot is starting to bubble gently.
Let the beans come to a slow boil rather than a hard, rolling boil. Keep an eye on the water level so the beans stay covered.
It's at a slow boil now. Should I turn it down right away?
Yes. Reduce the heat to low and let the beans simmer until they're tender but not mushy, about 35 minutes.
What texture am I looking for when I check them after 35 minutes?
They should bite easily and feel creamy inside, but still hold their shape. If they're collapsing or splitting a lot, they've gone past the ideal texture for this salad.
They're tender and still holding together. Do I mix in the vegetables now?
Take the saucepan off the heat and set the beans aside to cool first. Once they've cooled, they'll be ready to combine with the chopped celery, shredded carrot, and parsley.
Let's work through Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce today. Where should I begin? I'm starting with an empty counter.
Absolutely. Set out 1 medium head of garlic, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, and 1/2 cup white wine so everything is within reach.
I've got the garlic and olive oil out, and the chicken breasts are still in the fridge. Should I turn on the oven now?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it's ready for roasting the garlic.
Oven is heating. For the garlic, am I peeling the whole head or leaving it together?
Leave the head together. Slice just the top off the garlic head—only enough to remove some papery covering and expose the tops of the cloves.
The clove tops are exposed, but the head is still intact. How much oil goes on it?
Drizzle the garlic with 1 tablespoon olive oil, letting it run over the exposed cloves.
I don't have a clay garlic roaster. What should I use instead?
Wrap the oiled garlic head in aluminum foil; that works for roasting it in the preheated oven.
It's wrapped in foil and ready. How long should it roast?
Put it in the 400 degrees F oven and roast for 20 minutes, then check whether the cloves are soft.
What should the garlic feel like when it's done, and when do the chicken and wine come in?

The roasted cloves should be soft enough to slip from their skins when pushed. Keep the 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts and the 1/2 cup white wine ready for the sauce stage after the garlic is roasted.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce

messages.content: I'm making Easy Punch for a group today. Can you help me get the amounts straight before I start?
For Easy Punch, set out 4 packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder, each 0.13 ounce, plus 2 cans of pineapple juice, 46 fluid ounces each.
Those are on the counter. I've also got a big punch bowl ready—what else goes in?
You'll also need 3 cups white sugar and 4 quarts water. Since this is mixed all at once, make sure the bowl is large enough to hold everything with room to stir.
The bowl is large, and I measured the sugar. Should the water go in before or after the juice?

Add the drink mix powder, pineapple juice, white sugar, and water to the punch bowl together. The order isn't critical, but pouring in some liquid before stirring can help the powder and sugar dissolve more easily.
I added the pineapple juice and water, then poured in the powder and sugar. It's looking a little cloudy.
That's expected at this point. Stir steadily, scraping around the bottom and sides of the bowl, until the drink mix and sugar are fully dissolved.
I can still feel a bit of sugar at the bottom with the spoon. Should I keep going?
Yes, keep stirring until the bottom feels smooth and you don't see undissolved powder floating on top. The punch should look evenly colored.
Okay, it's smooth now and the color is even. I see the recipe mentions ginger ale—when should I add that?
Stir in the ginger ale after everything else has dissolved. Add it gently so you keep some of the fizz instead of stirring it flat.
The ginger ale is in. Any serving tip so it stays nice for guests?
Serve it cold soon after adding the ginger ale, or keep it chilled and give it a light stir before ladling if it sits for a while.
I'm setting up for Easy Alfredo Sauce I; what should happen before the heat goes on? I want to get everything measured before I turn on the stove.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pint heavy whipping cream, 1/2 cup butter, and 1 1/2 cups grated Parmesan cheese. You'll also want a medium saucepan and something to stir with.
I have the cream and Parmesan measured, but the butter is still in one stick. Is 1/2 cup right?
Yes, 1/2 cup butter is the amount for this sauce. Put the cream, butter, and grated Parmesan into the medium saucepan together.
All three are in the pan. Should I melt the butter first or just heat it all together?
Heat it all together over medium-low heat. Stir as it warms so the butter melts into the cream and the Parmesan starts blending in.
It's warming up, and I'm seeing some little cheese specks. Is that okay?
That's fine at this point. Keep the heat at medium-low and continue stirring until the sauce looks smooth.
The butter seems fully melted now, but the sauce is still a bit loose.
That's expected. Once it's smooth, take the saucepan off the heat; the sauce will thicken as it stands.
It looks smooth now. I'm removing it from the burner.
Great. Let it sit briefly in the warm pan. As it rests, it should thicken without needing extra ingredients.
Should I serve it right away over pasta, or wait until it thickens more?
Give it a short stand so it can thicken, then spoon or toss it with your pasta while it's still warm and creamy.
I want to make Fire Side Coffee. Before I start, what should I pull out and measure?

Get a mixing bowl, a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, a spoon, and a jar with a tight lid. Measure 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
I've got the creamer and hot chocolate mix measured. Should the coffee granules go in with those right away?
Yes. Add the 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules to the same bowl with the creamer and hot chocolate mix, then add the 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
The recipe line I'm looking at mentions nutmeg too, but I don't see an amount. How should I handle that?

Sift together the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, cinnamon, and the nutmeg if your recipe source includes it, but don't guess a quantity if none is given. Keep the measured ingredients exactly as listed.
Everything is in the sifter. Do I need to sift until it looks completely even?
Sift it into the bowl until the powders are blended and any small clumps from the creamer, cocoa mix, or coffee are broken up. A uniform, speckled dry mix is what you want.
The mix looks even now. What's the best way to store it?
Spoon or pour the dry mixture into a clean jar, then seal it with a lid so it stays dry and easy to scoop.
I'm ready to make one cup. How much mix goes into the mug?
Use 3 teaspoons of the mixture for 1 cup of hot water. Stir well so the coffee granules and hot chocolate mix dissolve.
If it tastes a little weak or too strong, what should I adjust?
Adjust to taste: add a bit more dry mix for a stronger, sweeter cup, or add more hot water to mellow it out. Reseal the jar when you're done.
Can you stay with me while I make Flavorful Rice Dressing 2? I'm clearing counter space and want to get the bread part right.
Absolutely. Set out a large bowl, a skillet, and a spoon or spatula for tossing and stirring. For the bread base, you'll need 7 slices of day-old bread, torn, plus 1 cup torn corn bread.
The breads are torn and in separate piles. Do they both go into the large bowl together?
Yes, put the torn day-old bread and the torn corn bread into the large bowl together. Keep the texture loose rather than packed down.
Got it. I also see hot water and celery on the ingredient list—how much should I measure?
Measure 2/3 cup hot water and 1/2 cup thinly sliced celery. The water will go with the bread first; the celery gets cooked in the skillet with the other vegetables.
The hot water is ready. Should I pour it all over the bread at once or add it slowly?
Add the 2/3 cup hot water to the bread in the large bowl and lightly toss as you go. You're moistening the bread, not mashing it into a paste.
The bread is damp and still a little chunky. I've got the skillet ready for the celery.
Good texture. In the skillet, sauté the thinly sliced celery with the onion and mushrooms in oil until the vegetables are tender, stirring constantly so they soften evenly.
The celery, onion, and mushrooms look tender now, and there's a little oil still coating them.
That's fine. Stir the sautéed vegetable mixture into the moistened bread mixture, folding it through so the vegetables are distributed without crushing the bread.
Everything is combined in the bowl. What should I do with the rest before serving or moving it on?

Add the remaining ingredients called for by your recipe and mix well. Once it looks evenly combined, the rice dressing mixture is ready for whatever final cooking or serving step your full recipe uses.
Before I get moving on Chicken Fried Chops 2, what should I have ready? I've got pork chops out and want to set up the coating correctly.
Absolutely. Put a shallow bowl near your chops and add 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground mustard, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder.
Everything is measured into the bowl. Should I mix it before the chops go in?
Yes, stir the dry mixture so the salt, mustard, and garlic powder are evenly worked through the flour. Then dredge each pork chop in it, coating both sides.
The chops are coated, and there's a little flour mixture left in the bowl. What pan should I use next?
Use a skillet large enough to hold the chops without crowding, or brown them in batches. Add oil to the skillet and heat it before the chops go in.
How browned do they need to be before I move them?
Brown the chops on both sides in the oil. You're looking for color on the outside, not cooking them all the way through at this point.
They have a nice crust on both sides. Do I drain them or transfer them straight over?
Lift them from the skillet and place the browned chops in the slow cooker. Try to keep them in an even layer if your cooker size allows.
The slow cooker is loaded. I see the soup and water mentioned, but I'm not sure how to add them.
Combine the soup and water in a separate bowl or measuring cup until smooth enough to pour, then pour that mixture over the chops in the slow cooker.
Should the liquid cover every chop completely?
It doesn't have to fully submerge them; just pour it evenly over the top so the chops are coated and the liquid settles around them in the slow cooker.
Can you talk me through making Butterscotch Basketball Cookies? I'm setting up my mixing bowl and microwave-safe bowl now.
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup softened butter, making sure it's real butter with no substitutes.
The chips are in a microwave-safe bowl, and the butter is softened on the counter. What sugars do I need?
Measure 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them near the butter because they'll get creamed together.
Both sugars are measured. Do I melt the butterscotch before mixing anything else?
Yes. Melt the butterscotch chips in the microwave, then let the melted chips cool for 10 minutes so they don't hit the dough too hot.
They're melted and cooling. While I wait, should I start the butter mixture?
Go ahead. In the mixing bowl, cream the softened butter with the sugar and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks blended and fluffy.
The butter and sugars look smooth and lighter. What gets mixed in before the melted chips?
For this batch of Butterscotch Basketball Cookies, add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so everything is evenly combined.
The wet ingredients are mixed in, and the butterscotch has cooled for the full 10 minutes.
Great. Beat the melted butterscotch chips into the dough, scraping the bowl as needed so the butterscotch is fully incorporated.
The dough looks evenly butterscotch-colored. Is there anything I should check before moving on?
Check that there are no streaks of plain butter-sugar mixture and no pools of melted chips at the bottom. Once it's uniform, you're ready for the next part of the cookie recipe.
I pulled up British Bread Pudding. Can you guide the first few moves? I'm getting the bowl and baking dish out now.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) so it can heat while you prepare the pudding.
Oven is heating. What should I measure for the bread and milk mixture?
Put 6 1/4 cups cubed whole wheat bread into a large bowl, then pour in 1 1/4 cups milk.
The bread cubes are in the bowl with the milk. Should I stir it or just leave it?
Give it a gentle turn so the bread is evenly moistened, then let it soak for 5 minutes.
While that soaks, what else needs to be ready on the counter?
Have 1 beaten egg and 1/3 cup softened butter ready. You'll also need raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon for the next mix-in.
The bread has soaked and looks soft, with a little milk still visible at the bottom.
That's fine. Stir in the beaten egg and softened butter first so they distribute through the bread.
Egg and butter are mixed through. Do the fruit and spices go in together?
Yes, add the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon, then fold everything together thoroughly.
It's combined but a few bread pieces are still holding their shape. Is that okay before baking?
Yes. Just make sure the mixture is well mixed and evenly coated; the bread can still have some texture in British Bread Pudding.
Today I'm tackling Gingered Mango Salsa. Can you help me line up the prep? I've got a cutting board out and want to make sure I set up the ingredients correctly.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup chopped peeled mango, 1/4 cup chopped red onion, 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro, and 1/4 cup lime juice. You'll also want a mixing bowl and a spoon for folding everything together.
The mango is peeled and chopped, but I haven't measured it yet. Should it be a full packed cup?
Measure 1 cup of chopped peeled mango, but don't pack it down hard. Just fill the cup evenly so the pieces sit naturally.
Okay, I have 1 cup of mango in the bowl. The red onion is chopped pretty small—does that work?
Yes, small pieces are good here. Add 1/4 cup chopped red onion to the bowl with the mango so it spreads evenly through the salsa.
I added the onion. I'm mincing the cilantro now; should I include the stems?
Use the tender parts if you like, but keep it finely minced. Measure 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro and add it to the bowl.
Cilantro is in. I have bottled lime juice—do I just measure the same amount?
Yes. Measure 1/4 cup lime juice and pour it over the mango, onion, and cilantro.
Everything is in the bowl. How much should I stir it?
Gently combine all the ingredients until the mango, red onion, cilantro, and lime juice are evenly mixed. Try not to mash the mango pieces.
It looks mixed and juicy. Can I serve it right away, or does it need time?
Let it stand for 30 minutes before serving. That gives the lime juice time to mingle with the mango, onion, and cilantro so the salsa tastes more balanced.
Let's work through Caramel Chocolate Corn today. Where should I begin? I'm trying to get the popcorn mixture set up without making a mess.
Absolutely. Start by making sure you have 16 cups of popped popcorn and 1 cup of roasted peanuts ready. Since the volume is large, keep your biggest workspace clear.
I've got the popcorn in a big bowl and the peanuts nearby. What else should I pull out before I start?
You'll also need 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter for the caramel mixture. Have cookie sheets ready too, because they'll need to be greased before the coated popcorn goes on them.
For the cookie sheets, should I grease them now or wait until the caramel is made?
Grease the cookie sheets now. It's easier to do before the caramel mixture is hot and you're trying to move quickly.
Done. The popcorn is still in the bowl—does the recipe need it somewhere else?
Yes, transfer the popped popcorn and the roasted peanuts into a paper bag. That gives you room to toss everything together later.
A paper grocery bag is ready. Should the peanuts go in with the popcorn all at once?
They can go in together. Add the 16 cups popped popcorn and the 1 cup roasted peanuts to the bag, then leave the bag open for now.
Okay, popcorn and peanuts are in the bag. Do I set that aside while I make the coating?
Exactly—set the bag aside where it won't tip over. Next, use a microwave-safe bowl for the caramel ingredients.
Before I continue with Caramel Chocolate Corn, i have a microwave-safe bowl out. What goes into it?
Combine the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt in the microwave-safe bowl. That's the mixture you'll heat for the coating.
I have Aunt Mamies planned for today. What should I set up first? I'm setting out the ingredients and want to avoid missing anything.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 softened 8 ounce package of cream cheese and 1/2 cup softened butter. You'll also need 2 cups all-purpose flour and 1 cup white sugar.
Cream cheese and butter are on the counter softening. Should I use a bowl or the saucepan right away?
Use a mixing bowl for the dough part. Beat the softened cream cheese and butter together until they look smooth and well blended.
The mixture is creamy now, but a little thick. Is that okay before I add flour?
Yes, that's fine. Add the 2 cups of all-purpose flour and mix until it's worked in evenly; the dough should come together rather than stay loose.
It's starting to form a dough. Do I need to knead it or just gather it up?
Just gather it into a ball. Once it holds together, cover it and chill it for 2 hours.
Covered and in the fridge. While it chills, should I clean the bowl or keep anything out?
You can clean the mixing bowl and beaters. Keep the white sugar handy, and have a saucepan ready for the later sugar-and-milk mixture.
The 2 hours are up. For the saucepan part, what heat should I use?
Set the saucepan over medium heat. Add the 1 cup white sugar with the milk, then cook while stirring occasionally.
What am I watching for so I know the sugar mixture is done?
Keep it on medium heat until the milk boils and the sugar has dissolved. Stir occasionally so the mixture heats evenly and the sugar doesn't sit on the bottom.
Before I get moving on Carrot Pineapple Cake I, what should I have ready? I want to get the dry ingredients and pan ready before I start mixing.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cups all-purpose flour and 2 teaspoons baking soda to start, and keep your measuring spoons nearby.
Flour and baking soda are on the counter. What other dry ingredients should I measure?
Measure 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1 teaspoon salt. The recipe also has you mix cinnamon with the dry ingredients, so have that ready too.
Got it. Should I turn on the oven now, or wait until the batter is closer?
Turn it on now so it has time to heat: bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
The oven is heating. I have a 9x13 inch pan—what should I do to prep it?
Grease the 9x13 inch pan well, then dust it with flour so the cake releases more easily after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. For the bowl, do I just dump all the dry stuff together?
Yes. In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon, then stir until they look evenly distributed.
The dry mixture looks even. How do I add the wet ingredients without making a mess?
Use a spoon or spatula to make a well in the center of the dry mixture. Add the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla into that well.
Everything is in the well. Should I scrape the bowl as I mix?
Yes, scrape around the sides and bottom as you bring the dry ingredients into the center, mixing until the ingredients are incorporated and no obvious dry pockets remain.
I'm getting ready for Atomic Canuck Chili. Can you help me sequence the steps? I'm setting up the counter now.
Absolutely. Start by pulling out 2 pounds lean ground beef and 1/2 large onion, diced. You'll also want a large skillet and a slow cooker ready.
Beef and onion are out, and the slow cooker is on the counter. What seasonings should I measure before the pan gets hot?
Measure 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper and 3 tablespoons garlic powder. The skillet step also uses seasoned pepper, so keep that nearby too.
Got it. Should I add everything to the skillet at once or brown the beef first?
Put the ground beef, diced onion, crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper into the large skillet together over medium heat. Cook until the beef is browned and the onion has softened.
The beef is browned, but there's a fair amount of liquid and fat in the pan. What should I do with it?
Drain off the fat from the skillet, then transfer the browned beef and onion mixture into the slow cooker.
The meat mixture is in the slow cooker. I'm clearing space for the add-ins—what goes in next?

Here, stir in the mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans with their liquid, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce. Mix well so the tomato paste and sauce spread through the chili.
Everything is mixed in. The pot looks thick in some spots and looser around the beans.
Give it a few slow, thorough stirs from the bottom and sides of the slow cooker. That should even out the beans, vegetables, sauce, and beef without mashing everything.
Looks more even now. How should I season it before I let it cook?

Season it with hot sauce and more crushed red pepper, adding them gradually so you can control the heat. Once it's seasoned, cover the slow cooker and let the chili continue cooking according to your slow cooker plan.
Let's work through Fresh Apple Salsa today. Where should I begin? I've got a cutting board out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by gathering 2 tart apples, 4 tablespoons lime juice, 1 fresh jalapeno pepper, and 1 fresh Anaheim chile. You'll also want a large bowl for mixing.
The apples are ready. Should I peel them, or just core and cube them?
Keep the prep simple: core the 2 tart apples and cube them. The recipe doesn't call for peeling, so you can leave the skins on if you like the texture.
They're cubed. I'm worried they'll brown while I slice the peppers.
Put the apple cubes into the large bowl and stir them with the 4 tablespoons lime juice right away. That coats them and keeps the salsa bright.
Done. For the jalapeno and Anaheim chile, do both need the seeds removed?
Yes. Seed and slice 1 fresh jalapeno pepper and 1 fresh Anaheim chile, then stir those slices into the lime-coated apples.
The chile slices are mixed in. The bowl looks pretty colorful already.
Great. Add the onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt to the same bowl. Scatter them around a bit so they're easier to combine evenly.
I added those. Should I mash anything, or keep it chunky?
Keep it chunky. Just mix thoroughly, folding everything together until the apples, chiles, onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt are evenly distributed.
It's mixed. Any serving tip before I bring it to the table?
Give it one final stir from the bottom of the bowl so the lime juice is spread through the salsa, then serve it fresh while the apples still have their crisp texture.
I'd like to make Buffalo Chicken Wings I. Can you guide me while I cook?

For Buffalo Chicken Wings I, set out 24 chicken wings and 2 quarts vegetable oil for deep frying. You'll also need 4 tablespoons butter, 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar, hot sauce, plus salt and pepper to taste.
The wings are ready, and I have a deep fryer. Should I heat all the oil before adding them?
Yes. Heat the vegetable oil in the deep fryer or a large skillet, then carefully add the chicken wings. Fry them until done, about 10 minutes.
They're frying now. What should I look for so I don't pull them too early?
They should be cooked through and look well fried on the outside. Since the recipe gives about 10 minutes, use that timing as your main guide and make sure the wings are done before removing them.
Okay, the wings are done and I need to clear the fryer area. What happens with the oil?
Carefully remove the chicken, then drain the oil from the skillet or fryer. Reserve the cooked wings while you make the sauce.
I have the wings resting. Do I use the same skillet for the sauce?
Yes, once the oil is drained, melt 4 tablespoons butter in the skillet.
While working on Buffalo Chicken Wings I, the butter is melted. When do the vinegar and hot sauce go in?
Add 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar and the hot sauce to the melted butter, then stir the sauce together in the skillet.
For Buffalo Chicken Wings I, the sauce is mixed. How should I season and serve the wings?
Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste, then coat or toss the reserved wings with it and serve them hot.
I'm making BBQ Chicken Wings and want to get the marinade started. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Set out a large bowl and gather the sauce base: 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce, 1 cup oyster sauce, 1/4 cup soy sauce, and 1/4 cup ketchup.
I've got those measured. The bowl is big enough for the wings too—what else goes into the sauce?
Add the garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar to that same bowl, then stir everything until the ketchup and sauces are fully blended.
The marinade looks smooth and smells smoky. Should the chicken go in right away?
Yes. Place the chicken wings into the bowl and turn them so they're well coated in the marinade.
They're coated. I'm trying to plan dinner timing—how long do they need in the fridge?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the wings for 8 hours or overnight so the flavor has time to soak in.
I'll leave them overnight. When I'm ready to cook, what should I do before putting them on the grill?
Preheat the grill for low heat. Give it time to settle there rather than starting hot.
The grill is heating on low. Do I need to prep the grate while I wait?
Yes, lightly oil the grill grate so the marinated wings are less likely to stick when you place them on.
Got it. So the flow is mix, marinate, low grill, then oil the grate?
That's the right order: mix the marinade, coat and cover the wings, refrigerate them for 8 hours or overnight, preheat the grill on low, and lightly oil the grate before grilling.
I'm getting ready for Eggplant Mixed Grill. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got the vegetables out, but I want to get the marinade organized before I start cutting everything.
Absolutely. For the herb-oil base, measure 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil.
Those are on the counter. What should I mix them in, and what else goes into that bag?
Use a large resealable plastic bag. Add the olive oil, parsley, oregano, basil, vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic, then gently shake or massage the bag so the marinade is evenly combined.
The marinade is mixed. I have onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and both red and yellow bell peppers ready to go.

Great. Put the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper into the bag with the marinade. Try to spread them out a bit so everything gets coated instead of clumping in one corner.
The bag is pretty full. Should I press the air out before refrigerating it?

Yes, press out excess air, seal the bag well, and turn it a few times to coat the vegetables. Set it in the refrigerator to marinate for 2 hours, turning occasionally so the marinade reaches all the pieces.
It's in the fridge now. When should I deal with the grill?
Near the end of the marinating time, preheat the grill for high heat so it's hot when the vegetables come out of the refrigerator.
The 2 hours are almost up, and the grill is heating. Anything I should do to keep the vegetables from sticking?
Lightly oil the grill grate before the vegetables go on. That helps the eggplant, peppers, mushrooms, asparagus, and onion release cleanly as they cook.
Should I drain the vegetables or just take them straight from the bag to the grill?

Lift them from the marinade and let extra liquid drip back into the bag before placing them on the lightly oiled grate. Keep the grill on high heat and arrange the vegetables in a single layer as much as you can.
I pulled up Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got a mixing bowl out but want to go step by step.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1/2 cup margarine and 1/2 cup sugar, since those get creamed together in the large bowl.
Those are measured. Should the molasses and egg be ready now too?
Yes, have 1/2 cup molasses ready, and separate 1 egg so you're using just the yolk.
The yolk is separated. Do I add everything to the bowl at once?
Not yet. Put the margarine and sugar in the large bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's smooth and lighter-looking. Is the molasses next?
Yes. Stir the molasses into that creamed mixture, then add the egg yolk and mix until it's evenly combined.
The bowl looks glossy and dark now. What should I do with the dry ingredients?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg so the leavening and spices are evenly distributed.
Dry mix is combined. Should I dump it all in or add it gradually?
Blend the dry mixture into the molasses mixture until the dough is smooth. If adding it gradually helps you avoid flour pockets, that's fine.
The dough is smooth now, but it feels soft. Do I shape the cookies immediately?
Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour before shaping or cutting the gingerbread men.
I'm setting up for Adriennes Tom Ka Gai; what should happen before the heat goes on? I'm at the counter and want to prep before heating anything.
Absolutely. Set out 2 teaspoons peanut oil and slice 2 cloves of garlic thinly. You'll also want a large saucepan ready for cooking over medium heat.
Garlic is sliced and the saucepan is out. What aromatics should I prep next?
Grate 2 tablespoons fresh ginger root and chop 1/4 cup lemon grass. Keep them close by with the garlic since they'll go into the hot oil together with the spices.
The ginger and lemon grass are ready. Should I start the pan now?
Yes. Put the large saucepan over medium heat and warm the 2 teaspoons peanut oil until it looks loose and shimmery.

Help me stay organized for Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth. What comes first? I've got a large pot out but want to be sure I start in the right order.
Absolutely. Add 2 quarts water to the large pot and set it over heat so it can come to a boil. While it heats, keep 12 ounces beef shank nearby.

Prep 2 large onions, chopped, and 2 large carrots, sliced. Have them ready, even though the beef goes into the boiling water before the later handling.

Yes, place the beef shank into the boiling water. Once it's in, lower the heat enough to keep a steady simmer rather than a hard boil.

Let the beef shank simmer for 1 1/2 hours. Check occasionally that the liquid stays at a calm simmer.

After the 1 1/2 hours, take the pot off the heat and let everything cool overnight. That cooling step is part of the recipe before trimming the meat.

Lift the meat out of the broth. Trim off any gristle, then cut the meat into medium sized pieces.

For this stage, set the medium sized pieces aside after cutting. You've completed the listed prep: boiled 2 quarts water, simmered the 12 ounces beef shank for 1 1/2 hours, cooled it overnight, then trimmed and cut the meat.

Stop once there are no obvious streaks of the cream cheese mixture and the sausage and beef look evenly combined. The mixture should hold together, but it doesn't need to be kneaded smooth.

Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions and shape each into a patty with an even thickness. Press a shallow dimple in the center of each one so they don't dome too much on the grill.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 2 skinless chicken leg quarters, 1/2 cup chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need chicken bouillon for the broth step.

Stir the chopped onion into the pot around the chicken and cook it for 2 minutes more, just to soften it and pick up some of the browned flavor.

Simmer the soup for 45 minutes. Keep the heat low enough that it bubbles gently; you can use the lid if you like, leaving it slightly ajar if the simmer gets too vigorous.

Yes. In that same skillet, melt the 1/2 cup butter. Once it's melted, add the 2 pounds of cleaned crawfish.

Sauté the crawfish for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally so they heat evenly in the butter.

Set the sautéed crawfish aside, just like you did with the green onions. That completes the skillet prep for this Crawfish Chowder.

Yes, give the sides and bottom a scrape, then pour the batter into the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan and spread it evenly before baking.

messages.content: I want to put together Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies as a jar mix. Can you guide me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need a clean wide-mouth glass jar that holds 1 liter.

Keep it as a layer. Spoon the white sugar into the bottom of the clean 1 liter wide-mouth jar first, then add the flour mixture on top of the sugar.

Press the layers firmly in place so the contents are compact and don't shift around too much. Once it's snug, seal the jar tightly.

Write that the recipient should place the mix in a large bowl, then beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy before continuing with the cookie dough.
Should the card mention that the butter needs to be softened?
Yes, include softened butter or margarine exactly, because that texture helps it beat smoothly with the egg and become light and fluffy.
Anything else I should check before I decorate the jar?
Make sure the lid is secure, the layers are pressed down firmly, and the card is attached clearly with the egg and 1 cup softened butter or margarine instruction visible.

Before I get moving on Best Ever Tuna Salad, what should I have ready? I'm setting out a saucepan and a mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Pull together 2 eggs, 1 (12 ounce) can white tuna, 1 (6 ounce) can shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise.
I found the tuna and mayo. The crabmeat is a 6 ounce can, and I have two eggs ready—do the eggs get cooked before mixing?
Yes, cook the eggs first. Put the eggs in the saucepan and cover them with cold water.
How much water should be over the eggs? I don't want them half exposed.
Use enough cold water to fully cover the eggs so they're submerged while the water heats.
They're covered and on the stove. Should I keep them boiling for a while?
Bring the water to a boil, then immediately remove the saucepan from the heat.
Okay, the pot is off the burner. Do I drain them right away or let them sit?
Cover the saucepan and let the eggs stand in the hot water for 10 to 12 minutes.

Yes, you can open the white tuna and shredded crabmeat while you wait, and drain off extra liquid before they go into the bowl.

Remove the eggs from the hot water, cool them, peel them, and chop them finely. Then combine the chopped eggs with the tuna, shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise in your mixing bowl.
Help me stay organized for Cabbage Rolls II. What comes first? I've got the cabbage out, but I want to make sure I prep it in the right order.

If a rib feels bulky, just press it gently or trim a little from the thickest part so the leaf rolls more easily. Keep the leaves intact so they can hold the filling.

In a large bowl, combine the 1 cup cooked white rice, the beaten egg, 1/4 cup milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper. Mix until everything is evenly distributed without overworking the meat.

Fold the sides in over the filling, then roll the cabbage leaf up snugly, tucking in the ends as you go. Set each roll seam-side down so it holds its shape.
Chicken and Black Bean Chili is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I'm starting with the chicken still on the cutting board.

The spices are stirred in and it smells good. Should the vegetables go in right away?
Yes. Mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper, scraping the bottom of the pot as you stir so the seasonings get distributed through the vegetables.
The peppers and onion are in. What texture am I looking for at this point?
You want the onion and both bell peppers mixed evenly with the seasoned chicken and starting to soften in the pot. Keep stirring occasionally so nothing sticks while the chili base comes together.

messages.content: I'm getting ready to prep Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken, and I'd like help pacing the marinade and side salad before I handle the raw chicken.

Dress the salad lightly and add a thin swipe of extra dressing along one side of the plate. For the chicken, put a medium mixing bowl near your measuring spoons and lightly oil a 9x13 inch baking dish.
The dish is oiled, and I've got a clean cutting board area set up for the chicken. What should go into the glaze bowl?

Measure 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum into the medium bowl. If your recipe includes mustard and garlic, add those to the same bowl too.
I added the ketchup, juice, molasses, rum, mustard, and garlic. The molasses is clinging to the spoon a bit—should I scrape it all in?

Yes, scrape in as much of the molasses as you can so the glaze keeps its full sweetness and body. Stir slowly at first, then more firmly once the ketchup starts loosening into the pineapple juice and rum.
I like that move with the salad—the thin extra streak works better than coating the whole thing heavily.
That should give you a fresher plate alongside the sticky glaze. Keep stirring the glaze until it looks glossy and evenly blended, with no thick molasses streaks left at the bottom of the bowl.
It's glossy now, but I haven't seasoned it yet. When do the salt and pepper go in?
Add salt and pepper to taste now, then mix well again so the seasoning is spread through the whole glaze rather than sitting on top.
Seasoning is mixed in. Before I put the chicken in the dish, should I pat it dry or just start brushing?
If the chicken pieces are very wet, pat them lightly so the glaze can cling. Arrange them in the lightly oiled 9x13 inch baking dish in a single layer.
The chicken is arranged with a little space between pieces. Do I pour the glaze on or brush it?
Brush it on so you can coat both sides evenly. Use about 1/2 of the prepared glaze for this stage and keep the remaining glaze separate.
Both sides are coated, and I kept the extra glaze in another container. Should I cover it tightly?
Cover the baking dish before refrigerating so the chicken can marinate without drying out or picking up fridge odors.
How long should I let it sit before cooking, and is overnight okay if dinner shifts?
Refrigerate the covered chicken for at least 2 hours, or leave it overnight if that timing works better. That rest lets the glaze soak into the chicken before it goes to the oven.

messages.content: I'm making Absolutely Awesome BBQ Sauce and I've got the saucepan out. What should I line up before I start heating it?

Keep the sauce loose as it cooks: if it thickens past a light ribbon, stir in a small splash of water, broth, citrus juice, vinegar, milk, or cooking water until it pours narrowly from a spoon. For the main measured ingredients, set out 1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup chile sauce, 1/2 cup rum, and 1/4 cup soy sauce, plus the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, dry mustard, and pepper.
The chile sauce and rum are measured, but the brown sugar has a few hard bits. Is that going to be a problem?
Break up the bigger brown sugar clumps before they go in so they dissolve evenly. A spoon against the side of the measuring cup works fine.
Okay, it's loosened up. Do all the sauces and seasonings go into the pan together, or should I build it in stages?

Add them together over low heat: brown sugar, chile sauce, rum, soy sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, dry mustard, and pepper. Stir slowly as it warms so the sugar starts melting into the liquids instead of settling on the bottom.
I like that lighter ribbon texture here; that's exactly what I wanted, and it works better for this sauce than making it heavy.

That texture will be easiest to keep if the heat stays gentle. Once the mixture looks smooth, lift the spoon now and then; if it starts coating too thickly, loosen it with just a tiny splash and stir before adding more.
The garlic is in, and the smell is pretty strong from the rum and Worcestershire. Should I let it bubble much?
Keep it at a low simmer rather than a hard boil. You want small, steady bubbles so the sauce cooks down without scorching or turning syrupy too fast.
When do I start counting the cook time—right when it hits those little bubbles?
Yes, once it reaches that low simmer, let it go for 30 minutes. Stir occasionally, making sure the spoon drags across the bottom of the saucepan.
Some sauce is sticking higher up on the sides of the pan. Should I leave it alone or scrape it back in?
Scrape the sides down when you stir. That keeps the brown sugar and seasonings from drying onto the pan and helps the sauce stay even.
It has simmered for the full 30 minutes and looks glossy, but the spoon trail is a little thicker than I want.

Take the pan off the heat first, then adjust while the sauce is still warm. Add one small splash of your chosen liquid, stir thoroughly, and check the spoon again before deciding whether it needs another.
I'm cooking it ahead for later tonight. How should I store it after I get the texture right?

Let the sauce cool, then move it into a covered container and refrigerate it until you're ready to use it. Before serving, give it a good stir and loosen it with another small splash if chilling makes it thicken up.

Keep the Brie coating light; if it starts feeling dense or pasty, loosen the cheesy smear with tiny splashes of milk or water until it drapes in a thin ribbon. Set out 2 teaspoons olive oil, 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves, 1 10 ounce can refrigerated large crescent roll dough, and 8 ounces Brie cheese.
I have a heavy skillet and a nonstick pan. Which one makes more sense for cooking the chicken?
Either works for this recipe. Heat the 2 teaspoons olive oil in the heavy skillet, or spray the nonstick frying pan with cooking spray if you want to skip the oil in the pan.
I'll use the skillet with the olive oil. Should the oven be on already, or should I wait?
You can turn it on now so it's ready later. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, while you sauté the chicken.
That light Brie coating is exactly what I wanted for these; I like it much better when the bundles don't turn rich and heavy.
Great, we'll keep the filling tidy. Warm the oil, add the chicken breast halves, and sauté them until they're no longer pink and the juices run clear.
The chicken is in the skillet now. Should I move it around a lot or let it sit?
Let each piece get steady contact with the pan, then turn as needed so it cooks through evenly. Watch for clear juices and no pink in the center before you set the chicken aside.
The oven is heating, and the chicken looks cooked through. I put it on a clean plate.
Good call using a clean plate. Keep anything that touched the raw chicken away from the cooked pieces, then open the refrigerated crescent roll dough.
The can is open. It says large crescent rolls; how many do I unroll?
Unroll 4 large crescent rolls onto your work surface. Try to keep the dough relaxed rather than stretched thin, so it can wrap around the chicken and Brie.
The dough is laid out, and the Brie is soft enough to cut. Should I slice it or spread it?
Cut the 8 ounces Brie into manageable portions instead of spreading it thickly. Place it where it can sit neatly with the chicken inside each crescent roll.
Before I assemble, anything I should wipe down or move out of the way?

Clear the raw-chicken utensils, wipe the board if it touched raw poultry, and keep the cooked chicken separate. With the 4 crescent rolls unrolled, the chicken cooked, and the Brie portioned lightly, you're ready to build the bundles.

Put the extra cooking liquid in a separate small container, and mix it in only after you open the thermos to eat.
Great, that is exactly what I want for today's lunch. I have the skillet out; what should I prep first?
Cut 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite size pieces, and measure 1 cup of lemonade so both are ready to go into the skillet.
The chicken is cut and the lemonade is measured. What liquids should I keep next to the stove?
Have 2 tablespoons olive oil and 1 tablespoon lime juice ready. You will also need Worcestershire sauce when everything goes into the skillet.
I found the Worcestershire sauce too. Should the pan be hot before I add the chicken?
Yes. Set a large skillet over medium heat, then add the chicken, lemonade, olive oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce together.
Everything is in the skillet and starting to bubble lightly. What seasonings go in?
Season the mixture with garlic powder, onion powder, and a bay leaf, then stir so the chicken pieces are coated in the liquid and seasoning.
The seasonings are stirred in. How long should I let it cook, and what should I look for?
Let it simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear.
While that simmers, I want the tortillas soft for serving. What's the easiest way?
Warm the tortillas in the oven or microwave until they are soft and flexible.
The chicken looks cooked through, and I have some liquid left in the pan. For the thermos, should I put all of that in with the rice now?
For this thermos lunch, spoon the chicken over the rice with only enough liquid to keep it moist, and keep the extra liquid separate so you can add it after opening.
