messages.content: I'm making Apple Butter V today; can you help me get organized before I start coring the apples?

For serving, choose one flavor garnish and one texture garnish, and leave off the rest of the decorative toppings. For the apple butter, start with a Dutch oven, a food mill, 6 pounds of tart apples, and 6 cups of apple cider.
The Dutch oven is on the stove. Should the apples be peeled, or just cored and sliced?
Use the recipe direction as written: core and slice the 6 pounds of tart apples. Once they're sliced, pile them into the Dutch oven.
They're sliced now. What else should I measure before turning on the heat?
Measure 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon so they're ready. Keep the apple cider close too, because it goes in with the apples right away.
I like that serving plan; it works better for this apple butter and keeps the finish from looking overdone. What goes into the pot first?
Put all of the sliced tart apples into the Dutch oven first, spreading them out enough that they settle evenly.
The pot is full of apples. How much cider am I adding?
Pour in the 6 cups of apple cider over the apples. It should help them soften as the pot heats.
Cider is in. Do I go straight to a boil?
Yes. Bring the apples and cider to a boil, then cook on medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
Should I stir in the sugar and cinnamon while it cooks down?
Keep the 3 cups of sugar and 2 teaspoons of cinnamon measured and ready, but for the step you're on, focus on cooking the apples in cider until they're soft enough to mill.
The apples are very soft now. How do I get the texture right?
Press the softened apple mixture through a food mill. Work in batches if needed, and scrape the underside of the mill so you keep the smooth apple base.
I want to make Eclairs II, and I'm setting up the counter. Can you guide me through the start?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup water, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1/4 teaspoon salt so everything is ready before the pan goes on the heat.
I've got the butter and water measured. Should the oven be heating already?
For Eclairs II, set the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
The oven is on. What pan or tray should I prepare while it heats?
Grease a cookie sheet so it's ready when the dough is prepared.
Cookie sheet is greased. I have a medium saucepan out—what goes in it?
Here, put the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water into the medium saucepan together.
They're in the pan. Should I stir right away or wait until it heats?
Start heating the saucepan and stir as it comes up to temperature so the butter melts evenly into the water.
The butter is mostly melted, but there are a few pieces left. Do I keep it on the heat?
Keep it on the heat and bring the mixture to a boil, stirring until the butter melts completely.
Once it's boiling and fully melted, am I ready for the flour and salt nearby?
Yes. Have the 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt close by; the mixture should be boiling with the butter fully melted before you move on.

Keep the finishing touches to one flavor accent and one crunchy or textured accent, and skip anything extra. For the crust prep, measure the butter and shortening onto the plate so they can go into the freezer for about 20 minutes.
Before I put anything in the freezer, I want the dry side ready. Which ingredients should I measure?
Measure 3/4 cup cake flour, 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon white sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Also have the baking powder from the recipe ready for the food processor bowl.
Okay, the flours, sugar, salt, and baking powder are out. Do they go into the processor now or after the fats chill?
You can put them in the food processor bowl now. Once they're in, just leave the machine off until you're ready to pulse the dry mix.
I like that approach for serving too—useful flavor and texture, not extra decoration. That works better for this crust.
Exactly. This crust is better when the texture does the talking, so while the butter and shortening are getting cold, keep the dry bowl simple and ready.
The butter and shortening are measured on the plate. Is the freezer time really necessary if they already feel cold?
Yes, give them about 20 minutes in the freezer. Very cold fat helps the processor cut it into the flour instead of smearing it.
The dry ingredients are in the processor bowl now. How much should I mix them before adding the fat?
Pulse for just a few seconds to combine the cake flour, all-purpose flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder evenly. Stop before it starts looking packed down.
The fats are firm now. Should I add the whole plate at once?
Add only 1/2 of the cold butter and 1/2 of the cold shortening to the processor with the dry ingredients. Keep the remaining cold fat aside for later in the recipe.
They're in the bowl. Do I hold the button down or pulse in bursts?
Pulse off and on for about 1 minute. You want the fat broken into the flour, but not warmed into a paste.
If I'm serving the baked crust later with a filling, should I plan anything decorative around the edge?
Only if it adds something clear: one small flavor accent and one bit of crunch or texture are enough. Otherwise, let the Bakers Secret Pie Crust stay neat and unfussy.
I'm making Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake and want to get the prep right before I start mixing. Can you guide me?
Absolutely. Pull out 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 6 squares of unsweetened chocolate, 1 ounce each, chopped.
The dry ingredients are on the counter, and I have the chocolate chopped. What equipment should I set up?
You'll need 2 round cake pans, each 9 inches, plus whatever you like for sifting the dry ingredients—a sifter or fine-mesh sieve works well.
Got it. Should the oven be heating while I prep the pans?
Yes, turn the oven on to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you get the pans ready.
The oven is preheating. I'm using metal pans—how should I coat them?
Grease both 9 inch pans well, then dust them with flour. Tap and rotate each pan so the flour coats the greased surface, then shake out any excess.
Both pans are greased and floured. For the dry mix, do I sift everything together at once?
Yes. Sift together the 2 1/4 cups flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt into a bowl so they're evenly combined.
The mixture looks lighter after sifting, but there are a few tiny flour clumps left in the sieve. Is that okay?
That's fine. Press any soft clumps through if they break up easily; discard anything hard or gritty. The goal is an even flour, baking soda, and salt mixture.
Dry ingredients are sifted and the chocolate is still chopped on the board. What should I do with the bowl now?
Set the sifted dry ingredients aside for the next stage of the cake, keeping the chopped unsweetened chocolate ready nearby.

I want to make Crab Quiche today. Can you guide me through it while I cook?
Absolutely. Pull out a 1 (9 inch) deep dish frozen pie crust, 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. The filling step also uses pepper and hot sauce, so keep those nearby too.
The crust is still frozen, and I've set the eggs and cream on the counter. Should I start heating the oven?

It's been close to 10 minutes. The edges are getting a little color, but the center still looks pale.

Yes, whisk the eggs, cream, salt, pepper, and hot sauce together in the large bowl until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
The filling is whisked and the crust has cooled a bit. Is it ready to assemble?
Yes. With the crust cooled from the prebake and the egg mixture whisked smooth, you're ready to pour the filling into the crust and continue with the quiche.

Measure 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Those all go into the large bowl together.

Buffalo Chicken Wings I is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got the wings out and want to cook along.

Melt the butter in the skillet over gentle heat. Once it's melted, stir in the distilled white vinegar and hot sauce so the sauce comes together.
The sauce is smooth. Do the wings go back into the skillet now?

messages.content: Cabbage Rolls II is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got the cabbage out but want to make sure I prep it right.
Absolutely. You'll need 12 cabbage leaves, 1 cup cooked white rice, 1 beaten egg, and 1/4 cup milk. The filling also uses onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper, so set those within reach too.
The rice is already cooked, and I have the egg and milk measured. Should I start with the cabbage leaves?
Yes. Put a large pot of water on the stove and bring it to a boil so the leaves can soften enough to roll.
The pot is heating now. Do the leaves go in whole, or should I cut them smaller first?
Keep the cabbage leaves whole. Once the water is boiling, add the leaves and boil them for 2 minutes, then drain them well.
They're drained and flexible. A few are still a little wet—does that matter?
A little moisture is fine, but shake off or pat away excess water so the filling doesn't get watery and the rolls are easier to handle.
Okay, I'm ready to mix the filling. What goes in the bowl?
In a large bowl, combine the 1 cup cooked white rice, beaten egg, 1/4 cup milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper. Mix until everything is evenly distributed.
The filling is mixed. How much should I put on each leaf so they don't burst?
Use about 1/4 cup of the meat mixture for each cabbage leaf, placing it in the center rather than too close to the edges.
I've portioned the filling onto the leaves. What's the best way to roll them neatly?
Fold the sides inward, then roll each cabbage leaf up around the filling, tucking in the ends as you go so the rolls stay closed.

messages.content: I'm making Fig Bars II today. Can you walk me through the setup before I start mixing?

For the fig bars, let one side take on deeper color in the pan, then finish the bake more gently so the browning stays uneven on purpose. Set up a 9x13 inch baking pan, a large mixing bowl, and a sifter if you have one.
I have the pan and bowl out. Should I heat the oven now or prep the pan first?
Do both before mixing: heat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), then grease and flour the 9x13 inch baking pan so the batter can go in as soon as it's ready.
The pan is greased and floured. What ingredients should be on the counter?

Set out 1 cup white sugar, 3 eggs, 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking powder. The directions also call for salt, cloves, cinnamon, allspice, and vanilla when you combine the dry ingredients and flavor the batter.
I like that uneven browning plan for these bars; that's exactly what I wanted here. How do I start the batter?
Crack the 3 eggs into a large bowl, add the 1 cup white sugar, and beat them together until the mixture looks thick and pale.
I'm whisking by hand. What should I look for before I stop?
Look for the color to lighten and the mixture to fall from the whisk in a slightly thicker ribbon instead of running off thinly. It doesn't have to be stiff, just noticeably fuller and paler.
That looks right. I've got the flour and baking powder measured—when do the spices go in?
Sift the 7/8 cup all-purpose flour with the 1 teaspoon baking powder, plus the salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice called for in the directions.
Do I add the vanilla with the dry mix or after it's folded in?
Blend the sifted dry mixture into the egg-and-sugar mixture along with the vanilla. Stir just until everything is combined so the batter stays tender.
The batter is in the prepared pan. How should I handle the oven so the color comes out right?

Bake it at 325 degrees F, watching for the bars to set while allowing that one side to deepen a bit more than the rest. Once the contrast is there, keep the heat gentle and avoid overbaking so the paler areas stay soft-looking rather than drying out.
Can you talk me through making Feta Chicken Salad for lunch?
Absolutely. Start by getting the main chopped ingredients ready: 3 cups diced cooked chicken, 2 large stalks celery diced, 1 red bell pepper seeded and diced, and 1/2 red onion diced.
The chicken is already cooked and diced. Should I use a serving bowl right away?
Yes, use a serving bowl big enough to toss everything comfortably. Add the diced chicken, celery, and red onion to it.
Got those in the bowl. Does the red bell pepper go in with them too?
Add the seeded, diced red bell pepper now as well so the vegetables are evenly distributed before the dressing goes on.
The bowl looks colorful. What do I mix the creamy part in?
Use a separate small or medium bowl. Stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the mixture looks fairly even.
The feta is still a little crumbly in the dressing. Is that okay?
That's fine for this salad. It does not need to be perfectly smooth; just make sure the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta, and dill are combined enough to spoon or pour over the chicken mixture.
Okay, I'm ready to combine it. Should I dump it all in?
Pour the dressing over the chicken and vegetable mixture, then stir gently until everything is coated and blended.
It's mixed. What's the last adjustment before serving?
Taste the salad, then season with salt and pepper as needed. Once the seasoning tastes balanced, it's ready to serve.

messages.content: I'm getting started on the Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart and have my mixing bowl, sifter, and plastic wrap out. Can you keep me on track through the dough prep?

Keep the glaze or sweet finishing layer on the outer rim of the tart so the center fruit stays more visible and lightly coated. For the dough, sift the dry ingredients together in the bowl before adding any butter.
Got it. I'm ready to measure the dry ingredients—what goes into the sifter?
Add 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon light brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/8 teaspoon salt to the sifter.
Those are measured. Should I sift once, or keep going until it looks extra fine?
Sift once into the bowl, then give the mixture a quick look for any brown sugar clumps. If you see a few, press them through or break them up so the dry mix is even.
That outer-rim shine is exactly what I wanted for this tart; I like the fruit showing more in the middle. The sifted mixture looks even now—what happens with the butter?
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. A pastry cutter, two knives, or cool fingertips will work; stop while it still looks crumbly rather than smooth.
I'm using my fingertips, and there are some tiny flakes plus a few pea-size pieces. Is that close enough?
Yes, that texture is right. You want a rough crumb mixture, not a paste, so leave those small uneven bits in place.
The ice water is beside me, but the recipe doesn't list a specific amount. How cautious should I be?
Sprinkle in the ice water gradually while tossing with a fork. Add just enough for the crumbs to become evenly moistened, without making the dough wet or sticky.
Should I press it together with the fork, or just keep lifting and tossing?
Keep it light with the fork—lift, toss, and turn the crumbs so the water spreads evenly. Avoid hard stirring, which can overwork the dough.
When I squeeze a small bit, it holds together, but the bowl still looks loose. Do I dump it out now?
Yes, gather the moistened crumbs together and pat them into a round. Use gentle, even pressure so it holds without becoming dense.
The round is formed and not too sticky. Should I wrap it, and do I need anything else out for the fruit finish?
Wrap the dough round in plastic now. You can leave the glaze items aside until later, when the sweet finish can be brushed mainly around the tart's outer edge.
I want to get started on these Empanadas, but I know the dough needs chilling. Can you guide me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1 (3 ounce) package cream cheese so they're easy to blend. You'll also need 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour and 1 cup fruit preserves for the recipe.
The butter is soft and the cream cheese is open. Should I use a mixer or do this by hand?
Either works, but a mixer will make it easier. Cream the butter and cream cheese together until the mixture looks smooth and fully blended, with no obvious streaks of either one.
It's looking creamy now. I sifted the flour into a small bowl—do I add it all at once?
Yes, beat in the 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour. Mix just until it becomes a cohesive dough rather than continuing to whip it.
The dough has come together, but it's pretty soft. Is that okay before chilling?
That's okay. Gather it gently and shape it into a smooth ball. The overnight rest will firm it up and make it easier to handle.
I've formed the ball. What should I wrap it with so it doesn't dry out in the fridge?
Wrap the dough well in foil or cling wrap, making sure the surface is covered. Then refrigerate it overnight; it can stay chilled for up to a week.
Good to know. I'm planning to bake tomorrow, and the fruit preserves are still sealed.
That's fine. Keep the 1 cup fruit preserves ready for when you assemble them; tonight's main job is getting the dough chilled properly.
Tomorrow, do I use the dough straight from the refrigerator or let it sit out first?
At baking time, remove the dough from the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it so it softens enough to roll and shape.
Can you talk me through making Chocolate Chews? I'm setting out the ingredients now.
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. You'll also want a heavy saucepan for melting the chocolate.
The chocolate chips and saucepan are ready. Should the heat be high enough to speed this up?
Keep it very low. Add the semisweet chocolate chips to the heavy saucepan and let them melt gently so they don't scorch.
On Chocolate Chews, they're starting to soften around the edges. Do I leave them alone or stir?
Stir them as they melt so the chocolate becomes smooth and evenly melted. Slow, steady stirring is best here.
The chocolate is smooth now. I've got the softened butter in a bowl with both sugars measured.
Great. Cream the 1/2 cup softened butter with the 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar until the mixture looks lighter and softer.
It's getting fluffy, but there are still a few darker streaks from the brown sugar.
Keep creaming a little longer until the sugars are well blended into the butter and the mixture looks light rather than streaky.
Okay, the butter and sugars look light now. What happens with the eggs?
Beat in the eggs one at a time. Let the first egg mix in fully before adding the next so the batter stays smooth.
The first egg is mixed in and the bowl sides are a bit messy. Should I scrape before adding another?
Yes, scrape down the sides, then beat in the next egg until it's fully incorporated. After that, you'll have the melted chocolate and creamed mixture ready for the remaining recipe steps.
Before I get moving on E Z Cheezy Pie, what should I have ready? I've got the counter cleared and want to make sure I'm starting with the right things.
Absolutely. Set out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells and 3 packages of softened cream cheese, 8 ounces each. Softened cream cheese will whip much more smoothly.
The pie shells are already baked, and the cream cheese has been sitting out. What else should I put beside the bowl?
You'll also need 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. A medium mixing bowl and a hand mixer or sturdy whisk will help with the filling.
I have a medium bowl and mixer ready. Should I turn the oven on even though the shells are baked?
Yes, follow the recipe and get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, you can start the cream cheese mixture.
The oven is heating. The cream cheese feels soft but still holds its shape—does that work?
That should be fine. Put the softened cream cheese into the medium mixing bowl and whip it until it looks fluffy, with fewer dense lumps.
It's getting lighter and fluffier, but there are a couple small streaks left on the sides of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides of the bowl, then whip briefly again so the cream cheese is evenly fluffy before adding the sweetener.
The texture looks even now. Do I add the sugar and vanilla together?
Yes. Add the 1/2 cup white sugar and the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the whipped cream cheese.
They're in the bowl. How smooth should the filling be before I use it with the pie shells?
Mix until the filling is smooth, creamy, and evenly blended with no visible sugar pockets or vanilla streaks. Then it's ready for the baked pie shells.

Set out 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter. You'll also need the corn syrup, vanilla, and salt for the microwave-safe bowl when you make the coating.

Prep them now: grease your cookie sheets before the caramel mixture is hot, so you can spread the coated corn right away later.

Leave the bag set aside for the moment. That keeps the dry mix ready while you combine the caramel ingredients.

Use a microwave-safe bowl and combine the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt in it.

Keep that reserved bit separate until the coated mixture is spread on the greased cookie sheets, then add it across the top so the finished Caramel Chocolate Corn still reads like a mixed platter.
I'm making Easy Pot Roast and have a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast on the counter. Can you help me get it started?
Absolutely. Set your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it can heat while you prep the roast.
The oven is heating. I also have an oven bag—should the roast go in whole?
Yes. Score the roast across the top and along the sides, then place it in a medium sized oven bag.
Scored and bagged. I see the recipe uses water and soup mix—what amounts should I measure?
Measure 2 cups water and open 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix.
Got those measured. Does the Worcestershire go in with that mixture?
It does. Stir the 2 cups water, the dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce together.
The liquid is mixed. Should I pour it over the meat or around it in the bag?
Pour the mixture directly over the roast in the oven bag so the seasoning coats the meat.
I'm adding vegetables too. Where should they sit?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag, keeping the roast centered.
Everything is in the bag now. Before it goes in, can you recap what should be in there?

You should have the 4 pounds boneless chuck roast, the mixture of 2 cups water with 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce, plus the vegetables arranged around the meat. The oven should be at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Black Forest Dump Cake II is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I'm setting up the counter and want to be sure I have the right cans out.

Absolutely. For the fruit layer, you'll need 1 (21 ounce) can cherry pie filling and 1 (16.5 ounce) can pitted dark sweet cherries. Keep the juice with the dark sweet cherries; it goes into the baking dish too.
I found both cans, and the cherries are still in their juice. What pantry items should I pull next?
Grab 1 (18.25 ounce) package chocolate cake mix and 1 cup chopped walnuts. You'll also want cooking spray and a 9x13 baking dish nearby.
The 9x13 dish is out. Should I do anything to the oven before opening the cans?
Yes, heat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's heating while you assemble the cake.
Oven is preheating. I'm worried about the fruit sticking around the edges of the pan.
Coat the 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray, including the corners and sides. That will help the fruit layer release more cleanly.
The dish is sprayed. Do I drain the cherry pie filling or just spoon it in as-is?
Use the cherry pie filling as-is. Dump the whole 21 ounce can into the sprayed dish, then spread it evenly across the bottom.
It's spread out in an even layer. For the pitted dark sweet cherries, should the juice go in too?
Yes. Add the 16.5 ounce can of pitted dark sweet cherries including the juice, and spread them over the cherry pie filling.
The two cherry layers are in the pan. I also have the chocolate cake mix and walnuts ready beside it.

Great. At this point, the recipe's listed prep has the dish sprayed, the cherry pie filling spread evenly, and the dark sweet cherries added with their juice, with the 18.25 ounce chocolate cake mix and 1 cup chopped walnuts ready for the remaining assembly.

Start with 12 ounces dry fettuccine pasta and 1 pound lean ground beef, if you're using the beef.

Set out 1 cup chopped onion and 1 cup chopped red bell pepper so they're ready when the skillet is hot.

Yes. Fill a large pot, salt it lightly, and bring it to a boil.

Cook the pasta for 8 to 10 minutes, just until al dente, then drain it well.

In this Baked Fettuccine Lasagna step, put the lean ground beef in the large skillet and brown it over medium heat, breaking it up as it cooks.

I'm making Cornbread Dressing I today. What's the best place to start? I've got the oven area cleared and want to start with the baking parts.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 (12 ounce) package refrigerated biscuit dough and 1 (8 ounce) package corn bread mix for the base of the dressing.
I found both packages. Should I be looking for anything to chop before I open them?
Yes—dice 1 cup onion and 1 cup celery. Keep them nearby because they'll get combined later with margarine and chicken broth in a small pot.
The onion and celery are diced. Do the biscuits and cornbread bake separately?

Yes. Prepare the biscuits according to the package directions, making enough so you'll have 4 cups once they're crumbled. Also prepare one 8x8 inch pan of cornbread according to the corn bread mix directions.
The biscuit package is going in first, and I'll do the cornbread in the square pan. Do I need to season anything yet?
Not at this stage. Just follow the package directions for the biscuits and the 8x8 inch cornbread pan, then let both bake through before you handle them for crumbling.
They're both baked now and pretty hot. Should I crumble them right away or wait?
Let them cool first so they're easier and safer to handle. Once cooled, crumble the biscuits and cornbread; the biscuits should give you about 4 cups crumbled.
The crumbs are in a big bowl. What oven setting do I need for the dressing part?
get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). That gets it ready for the next stage of the dressing.
Oven is set to 350. I have a small pot out—what goes in it?
In that small pot, combine the diced onion, diced celery, margarine, and chicken broth. Stir them together as they heat so the vegetables start softening and the broth and margarine come together.

I want to make Black Bean Lasagna Rolls. Can you help me get set up without skipping anything?
Absolutely. Put a pot of water on for the lasagna noodles and gather 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese, and a 15 ounce container of part-skim ricotta cheese.
The noodles, Monterey Jack, and ricotta are out. I also see a small can of chiles in the pantry—do those go in?
Yes. You'll need 1 can of chopped green chiles, 4.5 ounces, drained before mixing them in.
Got it. Should I salt the noodle water or add oil so they don't stick?
For this recipe, cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions while omitting salt and fat. Once they're tender, drain them well.
The noodles are cooked and draining. They're a little slippery—what should I work on while they cool?
Make the filling: combine the cheeses and the next 3 ingredients, then stir well so the ricotta, Monterey Jack, drained chiles, and remaining filling ingredients are evenly mixed.
The cheese mixture looks smooth with the chiles mixed through. Do I lay the noodles flat?
Yes. Lay each noodle flat in a single layer, then spread the cheese mixture over one side of each noodle.
How thick should the cheese layer be? I don't want the rolls bursting.
Use an even layer across each noodle, leaving it spreadable rather than piled high so the noodles can roll neatly.
The noodles are covered with the cheese mixture. Where do the black beans go?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on each noodle, keeping them distributed so every roll gets some filling.
I'm making Fiery Fish Tacos with Crunchy Corn Salsa. Can you guide me while I get the salsa and seasoning ready?
Absolutely. Set your grill to preheat on high heat so it's ready when you need it, then start gathering the salsa ingredients.
The grill is heating. I have corn and a red onion out—how much of each should go in?
Use 1 cup corn and 1/2 cup diced red onion. Put them into a medium bowl so you have room to toss everything together.
Done. I also bought jicama and a red bell pepper; what amounts am I cutting?
Peel and chop enough jicama for 1 cup, and dice 1/2 cup red bell pepper. Add both to the same bowl with the corn and onion.
The bowl is filling up nicely. Does cilantro go in with those vegetables?
Yes, mix the cilantro into the medium bowl with the corn, red onion, jicama, and red bell pepper until the colors are evenly distributed.
It looks crunchy and colorful. What should I add to brighten it up?
Stir in lime juice and lime zest. Fold gently so the jicama and pepper stay crisp while the citrus coats the salsa.
The salsa smells fresh. Should I make the spicy seasoning separately?
Yes. In a small bowl, combine cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt. Keep it separate so you can season the fish evenly.
The grill is hot and the salsa is ready. Anything I should check before assembling the tacos?

Give the salsa one last stir and make sure the lime is evenly mixed through. Keep the cayenne, black pepper, and salt blend nearby for the fish, then you're set to build the Fiery Fish Tacos with the crunchy corn salsa.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this batch, brush on a light glaze across the whole top, but keep one corner unglazed.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm putting these Empanadas into a dessert gift box with things like fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, and other sweets, so I want them to look platter-ready. What should I do on top for this batch?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a thin full-surface glaze and leave one corner plain.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Empanadas for a gift box or dessert platter with fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, or desserts. How should I finish the top?

messages.content: I'm putting these Empanadas into a dessert gift box with things like fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, and other sweets, so I want them to look platter-ready. What should I do on top for this batch?
For this batch, brush on a light glaze across the whole top, but keep one corner unglazed.
Perfect, that's the look I want today. Before I start mixing, what ingredients should I soften or measure?
Have 1/2 cup butter softened and set out 1 (3 ounce) package cream cheese so they can blend smoothly.
The butter and cream cheese are out. What dry ingredient and filling should I add to the setup?
Measure 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour, and keep 1 cup fruit preserves nearby for the filling.
Everything is measured. Since the dough rests overnight, what bowl-and-tool setup makes sense?
Use a mixing bowl and a sturdy spoon or mixer for the butter and cream cheese, plus foil or cling wrap ready for wrapping the dough once it comes together.
I'm at the bowl now. What texture am I aiming for with the butter and cream cheese?
Cream the softened butter and cream cheese together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
It's smooth and creamy. How do I bring in the flour without overthinking it?
Beat in the sifted all-purpose flour until it's incorporated and the dough starts holding together.
The dough has come together. How should I wrap it so it's ready later?
Shape the dough into a smooth ball, wrap it well in foil or cling wrap, and refrigerate it overnight or for up to a week.
When I'm ready to bake and fill them, how early should I pull the dough out of the refrigerator?
At baking time, take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it so it has time to soften slightly.
I'm making Easy Pot Roast today with a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast. Can you help me get set up?
Absolutely. Set out the chuck roast, 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. You'll also want a medium sized oven bag ready.
I have the roast and oven bag out. Should I start heating the oven before I mix anything?
Yes, bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready by the time the roast is bagged and sauced.
The oven is heating. Do I season the outside of the roast first or cut into it?
Score the roast on the top and sides, making shallow cuts rather than deep slices. Then place it into the medium sized oven bag.
It's in the bag now. The soup mix is dry—do I sprinkle it on or make a liquid?
Make a liquid mixture: combine the 2 cups water, the dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce.
The mixture looks thin but the soup mix is mostly dissolved. Is that okay?
That's fine. Pour the mixture over the roast in the oven bag, letting it run around the meat as well as over the top.
I was planning to add vegetables with it. Where do they go so they cook with the meat?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag, keeping the roast centered and the vegetables nestled along the sides.
Everything is in the bag and the roast is sitting flat. Anything I should check before it goes in?

Check that the roast has been scored on the top and sides, the water-soup mix-Worcestershire mixture is poured over it, and the vegetables are arranged around the meat. Then it's ready for the preheated 350 degrees F oven.
Today I'm tackling Fried Apple Pies. Can you help me line up the prep? Can you help me get set up before I start peeling apples?
Absolutely. For the dough ingredients, set out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup shortening, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup cold water. Keep the water cold until you're ready to mix.
I have the flour, shortening, salt, and cold water measured. Should I start with the apples or mix the dough first?
Start with the apple filling so it has time to soften. Peel the apples, then dice them into small pieces so they cook down evenly.
The apples are peeled and diced. They're in a bowl right now—what should I add before they go on the stove?
Sprinkle in sugar and cinnamon, then stir until the apple pieces are coated. Once they're evenly seasoned, transfer them to a saucepan.
They're coated and in the saucepan. What heat should I use, and do I need to add anything else?
Use low heat. Let the apples cook gently, stirring now and then so the sugar and cinnamon don't catch on the bottom of the pan.
They're starting to release juice and smell good. What texture am I waiting for?
Keep cooking until the apples are soft enough to mash easily with a fork. You're aiming for a thick applesauce texture, not a watery filling.
Some pieces are soft, but a few still hold their shape. Should I mash now or wait longer?
Give them a little more time on low heat, then mash with a fork once the pieces soften. Mash until the mixture looks thick and spoonable.
The filling is thick now. While it cools, can you remind me of the dough amounts so I can clear the counter?
Sure: use 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup shortening, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup cold water. Clear enough space to work the dough, and keep the apple filling nearby once it has cooled slightly.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip. Can you help me get set up before I turn on the oven?
Absolutely. Have a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish ready, and gather 1 cup mayonnaise, 8 ounces sour cream, a 1 ounce package of garlic and mushroom soup mix, and a 14 ounce can of artichoke hearts.
The casserole dish is out. Should the artichokes go in straight from the can?
Drain the artichoke hearts first, then chop them so they'll mix evenly through the dip.
They're drained and chopped. I also have the mayo, sour cream, and soup mix measured.
Great—get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's hot by the time the dip is mixed.
Oven is heating. Do I mix everything in a bowl first or right in the baking dish?

You can mix it right in the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish: add the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat, then stir until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The crab and cheese are folded in, but the mixture looks pretty thick. Is that expected?
Yes, this dip should be thick and creamy before baking. Just make sure there aren't dry pockets of soup mix and that the artichokes and crab are spread throughout.
It's smoothed out in the dish. Should I cover it with foil?
For this batch of Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, leave it uncovered and bake it for 30 minutes.
On Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, after 30 minutes, what should I do for serving?
Take it out carefully and serve it immediately while it's hot and creamy.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Start a little chili in the oil so it blooms early, then don't add more chili as a topping at the end.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Flavorful Rice Dressing 2, I'm treating it more like a saucy, simmered dish and I want some heat from chili or something similar. What's the best way to work that in?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Bloom a small amount of chili in oil at the start and add no extra chili on top.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Flavorful Rice Dressing 2 as simmered beans, sauce, or stew with chili, hot sauce, pepper flakes, spicy oil, jalapeno, or cayenne. How should I handle the chili?

messages.content: For this batch of Flavorful Rice Dressing 2, I'm treating it more like a saucy, simmered dish and I want some heat from chili or something similar. What's the best way to work that in?
Start a little chili in the oil so it blooms early, then don't add more chili as a topping at the end.
Great, that's exactly the special version I want just for this one. I'm clearing space now—what should I pull out first?
Put a large bowl on the counter and tear up 7 slices of day-old bread, along with 1 cup of torn corn bread.
The breads are torn and in front of me. What liquid and vegetable prep do I need before I turn on the stove?
Measure 2/3 cup hot water, and slice enough celery thinly to make 1/2 cup.
I've got the hot water measured. Do I pour it all over the bread at once or work it in slowly?
Add the hot water to the breads in the large bowl and lightly toss everything together, just enough to moisten without packing it down.
The bread mixture is damp and still loose. I'm ready for the skillet—how should I handle the celery and heat?
Warm the oil in the skillet, bloom that small amount of chili in it, then add the celery with the onion and mushrooms. Sauté until tender, stirring constantly.
I'm stirring nonstop. What should the vegetables look like before I take them off the heat?
They should look softened and tender rather than crisp; once they reach that point, scrape the skillet contents into the bread mixture.
The sautéed vegetables are in the bowl with the bread. What comes after that?
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well so the bread, corn bread, celery, onion, mushrooms, oil, and seasonings are evenly combined.
It's mixed and holding together without looking mashed. Anything else before I serve or clean up?
You're at the end of the recipe once everything is mixed well. Give the bowl one last gentle turn-through, then you can serve it and wipe out the skillet while it's still warm.
I'm making Eggplant Mixed Grill and have a resealable bag and grill tools ready. Can you guide me from prep to the grill setup?
Absolutely. Start by measuring 2 tablespoons olive oil into the large resealable plastic bag, then add 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley.
The oil and parsley are in the bag. I also have fresh oregano and basil washed—how much of each goes in?
Add 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil. Then mix in the vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic right in the bag to make the marinade.
The marinade is mixed. It smells pretty herby—what vegetables should go into the bag?
Add the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper to the bag with the marinade.
Everything is in there, but the eggplant pieces are taking up a lot of space. Should I shake it or turn it?
Seal the bag well, then gently turn and massage it so the vegetables get coated without crushing them. Try to spread the marinade around the eggplant and peppers especially.
The vegetables look coated. How long does the bag need to sit, and does it go on the counter or in the fridge?
Marinate it for 2 hours in the refrigerator. Turn the bag occasionally during that time so the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and peppers keep getting coated.
The 2 hours are almost up. When should I start heating the grill?
Go ahead and preheat the grill for high heat while the vegetables finish marinating.
The grill is hot now. Anything I should do to the grate before the vegetables go on?
Here, yes—lightly oil the grill grate before adding the marinated vegetables. That helps reduce sticking, especially with the eggplant and peppers.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this serving, arrange 3 small garnish clusters around the platter so it looks finished without getting crowded.
