Frozen is fine for this smoothie. Add the frozen mixed berries straight to the blender; they'll help make the smoothie thick and cold.

Either order works, but adding the drained sliced peaches after the berries can help the blender catch a little moisture as it starts mixing.

Drizzle in the 2 tablespoons of honey over the fruit so it blends evenly instead of sticking to one spot.
Everything is loaded. Should I pulse it or just let the blender run?
Start with a few short pulses to break up the frozen berries, then blend steadily until the mixture looks smooth.
It's blending, but I can still see a few little berry pieces near the sides.
Stop the blender, scrape down the sides if needed, then blend again until there are no visible chunks and the texture is smooth.
It looks smooth now. Any serving tip before I pour it?
Pour it right away while it's cold and thick. Give the blender jar a quick rinse soon after serving so the honey and fruit don't dry onto it.

Keep the topping to the warm brown sugar-spice mixture with the chopped pecans for crunch, and skip any extra decorative garnish. Set out 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and 1/2 cup chopped pecans, plus a 9x13 inch pan.

Add the apple butter, vanilla, and the wheat germ or bran cereal. Mix those in before you start alternating the dry ingredients and sour cream.

Add some of the sifted dry ingredients, mix well, then add some sour cream and mix again. Continue alternating between the dry mixture and sour cream, mixing well after each addition.

Yes, spread the batter evenly in the prepared 9x13 inch pan. Smooth it into the corners so the cake bakes evenly.

Sprinkle the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and pecan topping evenly over the batter. Let that be the finished surface—warm spice for flavor and pecans for texture, with no extra garnish piled on.
I'm baking apple butter spice cake and want to get organized before I start. What should I pull out for the topping?

For the topping, set out 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and 1/2 cup chopped pecans. Keep a small bowl nearby so you can mix them together once the pan and oven are ready.

Yes. Heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), then spray or grease one 9x13 inch pan. Once that's done, the topping can be stirred together without rushing.

It should look like a loose, sandy nut mixture rather than a smooth paste. Stir the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and chopped pecans until the spices are evenly spread through the sugar and nuts.
That's ready in a bowl. What dry ingredients should I handle next?
Sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Sifting helps the leaveners and salt distribute evenly before they go into the batter.

Begin by blending the butter and sugar together, then add the eggs and beat well. After that, mix in the apple butter, vanilla, and either wheat germ or bran cereal.

Add the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream. Mix well after each addition, but stop once everything is incorporated so the batter stays tender.

Use the prepared brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and pecan topping as the topping for the cake once the batter is ready for the greased 9x13 inch pan. Spread the batter evenly, then distribute the topping evenly over it.
I'm cooking Glazed Ham today with an 8 pound bone-in shank ham. Can you help me get set up?
Absolutely. Put the ham near your roasting pan and make sure you have water ready—about 4 cups, or enough to come up to the right depth in the pan.

Yes, set out 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup brown sugar so they're ready when you need them.

get the oven warming to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). This low temperature is right for gently heating the ham.
The oven is preheating. Should the ham go directly into the roasting pan now?
Yes. Place the bone-in shank ham in the roasting pan, keeping it stable and centered so the water can sit evenly around it.

Pour water into the roasting pan until it reaches a 2 inch depth. Use the 4 cups as your starting amount, then add more if the pan needs it to reach that depth.

Use a tight fitting lid if your roasting pan has one. The key is to cover it snugly so the moisture stays in while it cooks.

You've preheated the oven to 275 degrees F / 135 degrees C, placed the 8 pound bone-in shank ham in the roasting pan, poured in water to a 2 inch depth, and covered it with a tight fitting lid. You also have the 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup brown sugar ready for the glaze.
I'm making Chocolate Chews and have the chocolate chips out. Can you help me pace the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar so everything is within reach.
The butter is soft, and I've measured both sugars. Should I start with the saucepan or the mixing bowl?
Start with the saucepan. Put the semisweet chocolate chips in a heavy saucepan and keep the heat very low so the chocolate melts gently instead of scorching.

Give them gentle, steady stirs as they soften so the chocolate melts evenly throughout.
The chocolate is mostly smooth now, with just a few small bits left. Is that okay?
Yes. Keep it over very low heat and stir until those last bits melt into a smooth, even mixture.
The chocolate is smooth. I've got the butter and sugars in a bowl—what texture am I aiming for?
Cream the softened butter with the white sugar and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks lighter and a bit fluffy.
It's lighter now, but there are still a few sugar granules visible. Should I keep beating?
A little texture from the sugar is fine, but beat a bit longer if the butter still looks streaky. You want the butter and sugars evenly combined and light.
That looks good. The eggs are ready beside the bowl—how do I add them?
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing after each addition before adding the next so the mixture stays smooth.
I want to make Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake. Can you help me get set up before the ice cream starts softening?

Absolutely. Pull out 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies, 1/4 cup melted margarine, 1 cup hot fudge topping, and 2 quarts vanilla ice cream. You'll also want a 9-inch springform pan or a pie plate.
I've got the cookies and margarine ready. Should I open the fudge and ice cream now too?
Yes, have the hot fudge topping nearby, but keep the vanilla ice cream cold for the moment. We'll build the crust and cookie edge before using it.
For the crust, how many cookies am I crushing?
Crush half the package, about 20 small chocolate chip cookies, until they're crumbly enough to press into a crust.
They're mostly fine crumbs with a few small chunks. Is that okay?
That's fine. Mix those crumbs with the 1/4 cup melted margarine until evenly moistened.
The crumbs look damp now. Do I pack them straight into the pan?
Yes. Press the crumb mixture firmly into the bottom of the 9-inch springform pan or pie plate so it forms an even base.
The crust is pressed in. What do I do with the cookies I didn't crush?
Stand the remaining cookies upright around the edge of the pan, with them touching the crust and lining the sides.
The cookie wall is in place. How much fudge goes on the crust before the ice cream?
Spread 3/4 cup of the hot fudge topping over the crust in an even layer. Save the rest of the 1 cup topping for later serving or decorating if you like.

I've got the soy sauce, oil, sherry, and ginger measured. The recipe also mentions garlic in the mixing step—should it go in with the marinade?

Yes. Open the large resealable bag wide, pour in the marinade, and keep the top folded back a little so the seal area stays cleaner.

Slide the swordfish steaks in gently, one at a time if needed, then seal the bag most of the way and press out excess air before closing it fully.

Shake and turn the bag just enough to coat the swordfish steaks all over with the mixture. You can also massage the outside of the bag lightly so the marinade reaches the surfaces evenly.
Everything looks coated. What timing should I follow from here?
Place the sealed bag in the refrigerator and let the swordfish steaks marinate at least 4 hours. Set the bag on a plate or in a shallow dish in case of leaks.

They can go straight in frozen. The boil will handle them; just make sure they're in the 3 quarts of cold water before you turn on the heat.

Set a strainer over a large bowl or pitcher and strain out the cranberries. Then stir the 2 cups orange juice, 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice, lemon juice, and sugar into the cranberry liquid until the sugar dissolves. Chill it if you want it colder before serving.

Cover the outside of the upside-down loaf pan with foil. Smooth the foil over the corners and sides so the cookie bowl has a clean surface to bake against.

Set the foil-covered, upside-down pan onto a cookie sheet. That will make it easier to move in and out of the oven.

Chop enough fresh cilantro to make 1/2 cup. It goes into the saucepan before boiling, along with the carrots, onion, and most of the vegetable broth.
I like having that saved broth for the finish; that works better for this soup when the blender makes it too thick. I've got the cilantro measured now.
Add the carrot pieces, chopped onion, and 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro to a large saucepan. Pour in most of the vegetable broth, leaving that small splash aside in the measuring cup.
The pan is loaded, and I can still see a bit of broth left in the cup. Should I cover it while bringing it up?

You can cover it briefly to help it come to a boil, then uncover or leave it slightly ajar once it is bubbling so you can watch it. Keep the heat high enough to reach a boil without letting it splash over.
It's boiling now, and the carrots are bobbing around. How long should I cook it from here?
Cook it until the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes. Check a piece with a fork; it should pierce easily without much resistance.
After about 10 minutes, the fork goes through the carrot pieces easily. The kitchen smells very cilantro-forward.
That sounds right for this recipe. Take the saucepan off the heat and let the soup cool slightly before pureeing.

Give it a few minutes so it is no longer vigorously steaming. Blend carefully in manageable amounts if needed, and do not seal in too much steam pressure.

Puree the soup until smooth, using the blender or a food processor. You want the carrots, onion, cilantro, and broth fully blended into an even soup.

Yes. Put the water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil into the small saucepan, then set it over medium heat.

Give it a few gentle stirs so the sugar and salt dissolve evenly. Let it heat until the mixture comes to a boil.

Stir the flour in until the mixture pulls together and forms a ball. It should look like a thick dough rather than a loose batter.

Heat oil for frying in a deep-fryer or a deep skillet. Bring it to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, before you cook the churros.
I'm using a deep skillet. Anything to watch while the oil comes up to 375?
Keep the skillet steady and give the oil time to reach 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Once it's at temperature, you'll be ready to fry the churro dough in batches.

Keep the sugar separate for layering. In a bowl, combine the flour with the baking powder, baking soda, salt, and nutmeg.

Spoon the white sugar into the bottom of the wide-mouth jar first, then add the flour mixture on top of it.

Great—set out 1 cup mayonnaise, 8 ounces sour cream, 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, and 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts. Drain and chop the artichoke hearts so they're ready to stir in.
The artichokes are drained and chopped. What dish should I mix this in?
Use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish. You'll mix the dip right in that dish: mayonnaise, sour cream, the garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, plus the cheese and crab meat.
Before I combine it, should I start heating the oven?
Yes, bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, you can finish combining the dip ingredients in the casserole dish.
I've got the mayo and sour cream in the dish with the soup mix. The mixture looks thick.

That's okay for this dip. Fold in the chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat until everything is evenly distributed, scraping the corners of the casserole dish so there aren't dry pockets of soup mix.

Leave it uncovered. Put the casserole in the preheated 350 degrees F oven and bake it for 30 minutes.
While it bakes, what should I watch for so I know it's on track?
After the 30 minutes, it should be hot throughout and ready to serve right away. Since the recipe bakes it uncovered, the top may look a little set around the edges.
The timer just went off and the dip is bubbling lightly at the sides. How do I serve it?
Take it out carefully and serve immediately while it's hot. Give the dish a quick check that the center is heated through, then bring it to the table in the casserole dish.

Get 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute and 1/2 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice. The spice gets divided: 1/4 teaspoon goes with the fruit, and 1/8 teaspoon goes into the flour mixture.
I have the spice measured. Should the fruit go into the bowl right away?
Yes. In the medium bowl, combine the chopped apples, blueberries, sugar substitute, and 1/4 teaspoon apple pie spice. Stir gently so the berries don't get crushed, then set that bowl aside.
The fruit bowl is mixed and sitting off to the side. I'm ready for the dough ingredients.
Use another medium bowl and stir together the whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, and the remaining 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice. Mix just enough to distribute the salt and spice evenly.
The dry mixture looks even. I've got oil and milk nearby—do they go in separately?
Add the oil and milk all at once to the flour mixture. Pour them in together rather than adding one at a time.
They're in the bowl now. What should the mixing motion be like so I don't overwork it?
Stir lightly with a fork, using short, gentle strokes. Stop once the dough comes together; it does not need to look perfectly smooth.
It's starting to clump and there are a few dry-looking bits at the bottom. Should I keep going?
Give it just a few more light fork turns to bring those dry bits into the dough, then stop as soon as it holds together. Keep the fruit mixture nearby for assembling the Apple Blueberry Tarts.
Before I get moving on Cupids Cookies, what should I have ready? I've got a medium mixing bowl out but haven't measured anything yet.
Absolutely. Measure out 1 cup butter and 1 cup white sugar to start. Let the butter be soft enough to cream smoothly with the sugar.

Have 1 egg and 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract ready. You'll also need flour and salt for the dry mixture later.

Yes—cream the butter or margarine with the white sugar in the medium bowl until the mixture looks light and fluffy rather than dense or streaky.
It's paler now and looks fluffy around the beaters. Do I crack the egg straight in?
Go ahead and blend in the egg, then add the vanilla extract. Mix until both are evenly worked into the creamed butter and sugar.
The egg and vanilla are mixed in. I'm noticing the bowl sides need scraping—should I do that before the dry ingredients?
Yes, scrape down the sides so the wet mixture is even. In a separate bowl or onto parchment, sift together the flour and salt.
I sifted the flour and salt together. Do I add all of it at once or work it in gradually?
Add the sifted flour and salt to the creamed mixture, then mix well. If your mixer is kicking up flour, start slowly and increase once it begins to combine.
The dough is coming together but I still see a little flour at the bottom of the bowl. Is that okay?
Keep mixing just until that flour disappears and the dough looks evenly combined. Once it's mixed well, the Cupids Cookies dough is ready for the next part of your baking plan.

messages.content: I'm making Anzac Biscuits I and have a mixing bowl out. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start?

Absolutely. Put 1 cup quick cooking oats, 3/4 cup flaked coconut, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking soda within reach. You'll also need the sugar and, for the stovetop mixture, syrup, butter, and boiling water.
The oats, coconut, flour, and baking soda are measured. Should the dry ingredients all go in the same bowl?
Yes. In the mixing bowl, combine the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut. Stir them together so the coconut and oats are evenly spread through the flour.
The dry mix looks even. I've got a small saucepan ready—what goes in it?
Add the syrup and butter to the small saucepan and keep the heat low. Let them melt together gently, stirring so the butter blends into the syrup without scorching.
The butter has melted into the syrup. I'm not sure how to handle the baking soda part.
Mix the baking soda with the boiling water in a small cup or bowl, then pour that into the melted butter and syrup mixture. It may foam a little, so stir carefully.
It foamed slightly and is combined. Do I pour it straight into the dry bowl?
Yes, add the warm butter mixture to the dry ingredients. Pour it over the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut, then stir until everything is moistened.
Some dry bits are still stuck at the bottom of the bowl. Should I keep folding it?
Keep scraping from the bottom and folding until no loose floury patches remain. The mixture should look evenly coated rather than dusty.
The dough is evenly mixed now. Is there anything else from the recipe before I shape or bake them?

That completes the listed preparation for Anzac Biscuits I: dry ingredients mixed, syrup and butter melted, baking soda mixed with boiling water and added, then the butter mixture stirred into the dry ingredients.
I'm making Chocolate Covered Banana Pie and I've got a 9 x 13 inch pan out. Can you help me set up the crust part?

Absolutely. For the crust mixture, measure 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers, 1/2 cup chopped pecans, and 2/3 cup melted butter. Keep the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips nearby too, since they're part of the recipe.
The wafers are crushed, but the pecans are still in bigger pieces. Should I chop them before mixing?
Yes, chop the pecans so they'll distribute evenly through the crumbs. Then combine the crushed vanilla wafers, chopped pecans, and melted butter in a bowl.
The butter is melted and I'm stirring everything together. How wet should this look?
It should look evenly moistened and crumbly, not like a batter. If you press a small handful, it should mostly hold together from the butter coating the crumbs and pecans.
Okay, the mixture clumps when I squeeze it. Do I grease the pan before pressing it in?
The recipe just says to press the mixture into the 9 x 13 inch pan, so spread it across the bottom and press it firmly into an even layer.
I've pressed it in, but the corners are a little thinner than the middle.
Use your fingertips or the bottom of a measuring cup to push some crumbs toward the corners until the thickness is more even across the pan.
The crust is even now. What oven setting and time should I use?
Bake it at 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, for 5 minutes.
The 5 minutes are up and it smells toasted. Should I take it out right away?
Yes, take the pan out carefully and let the crust cool. Once it's cooled, you'll be ready for the next part of the Chocolate Covered Banana Pie.
I'm making Broccoli Cheese Crepes and want to stay organized. Can you talk me through the batter and the next pan step?
Absolutely. Set out 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt for the crepe batter. You'll also want a blender ready.
Blender is on the counter. Do the eggs and water go in before the flour?
Yes, add the eggs and water to the blender, then add the flour and salt. Combining them all together there will make the batter smooth.
The flour is measured. Should I pulse it or run the blender continuously?
Cover the blender and process the mixture until it looks smooth, with no visible dry flour clumps.
It looks thin and even. Does it need to sit before I cook anything?
Let the batter stand for 15 minutes. That rest helps it settle before you cook the crepes.
While it rests, I can start the filling base. What pan should I use for the onion?
Use a small saucepan. Add the butter, then saute the onion in the butter until the onion is tender.
The onion is softening. How tender should it be before I add anything else?
Look for it to be softened and not crisp; it should stir easily in the butter. Once it's tender, you're ready for the flour.
Okay, onion is tender. How do I add the flour without making lumps?
Sprinkle in the flour and stir it into the onion and butter until everything is blended into an even mixture.
I'm baking Fresh Apple Cake today. Can you help me set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Get out 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil, 2 cups white sugar, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract. You'll also want your oven, a 10 inch tube pan, and a bowl for mixing.
I have the oil, sugar, eggs, and vanilla on the counter. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and heat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), so it has time to come up to temperature while you prep the pan and batter.
The oven is set to 325. I'm pulling out the tube pan now—what should I do to it?
Grease one 10 inch tube pan well, making sure you cover the center tube and the sides so the cake releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. For the wet mixture, do I add the sugar with the eggs or keep it separate?
Beat the oil, beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white sugar together in the same bowl until the mixture looks combined and smooth.
It's glossy and the sugar is mostly mixed in. Is that enough beating?
That sounds right for this stage. You don't need to whip in lots of air; just make sure the 1 1/2 cups oil, 2 cups sugar, 3 eggs, and 2 teaspoons vanilla are evenly blended.

I want to make Cabbage Kielbasa Supper in the slow cooker. Can you help me get the ingredients prepped in a sensible order?

The cabbage is shredded, and I'm cubing the potatoes now. Does the slow cooker really hold all 8 cups?
It will look very full at first, but that's expected. The cabbage cooks down as it heats, so just add it loosely rather than packing it hard.
Potatoes are at about 1/2 inch, and the onion is chopped. What should go into the cooker together?

Add the shredded cabbage, potato cubes, chopped onion, 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, and pepper directly to the 5-qt. slow cooker. Give everything a light toss so the potatoes and onion aren't all sitting in one spot.
That's mixed together. I don't want to wash extra dishes—can I pour the liquid straight in?
Yes, pour the broth right over everything in the slow cooker. Aim to wet the vegetables across the surface so the cabbage and potatoes begin cooking evenly.
Broth is in. Where does the kielbasa go—mixed in or on top?
Place the sausage on top of the cabbage mixture. Don't worry if the cooker seems crowded; the cabbage will shrink as it cooks.
The lid fits, but it's close. Should I press everything down before turning it on?
Only press gently if needed to seat the lid. Keep the sausage on top, cover the slow cooker, and cook on low for 8-9 hours.
How will I know it's ready to serve after that long cook?

It's ready when the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through. Check the potatoes with a fork; if they're soft after the 8-9 hour low cook, you can serve it straight from the slow cooker.

Start the oven now: preheat it to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.

Into a large mixing bowl, measure the flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla.

I want to make Eclairs II, but I'd like someone to pace me through the early steps.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup water, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1/4 teaspoon salt so everything is ready before the pan heats.
I've measured the butter and water. Should I start heating the oven before I deal with the saucepan?

Oven is on. What should I do with the cookie sheet?
Grease a cookie sheet well, especially the spots where the eclairs will sit, so the pastry can release cleanly later.
The sheet is greased, and I have a medium saucepan on the stove. Do the butter and water go in together?
Here, they do. Put the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water into the medium saucepan together.
Should I slice the butter smaller, or is it fine as a half-cup stick?
Either works, but cutting the 1/2 cup butter into a few pieces will help it melt more evenly as the water heats.
I'm turning on the burner now. How active should the stirring be?
Stir steadily while the mixture heats, just enough to keep the butter moving through the water and melting smoothly.
The butter is nearly gone and the liquid is starting to bubble. What am I waiting for exactly?
Bring it all the way to a boil, continuing to stir until the butter melts completely. Keep the 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt nearby for the next part.
Famous Caramel Cookie Bars is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I'm setting up the counter now.

Spoon a thin line of caramel over each cookie. Try to divide it evenly so all 40 cookies get a stripe.

For the listed steps, place the cookies in the refrigerator until the caramel is set. Keep the 4 cups milk chocolate chips ready if you plan to use them after the caramel firms up.
Help me stay organized for Fried Chicken Tenders. What comes first? I've got chicken ready but want to set up the coating station correctly.

In a separate shallow bowl, add 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs. Stir in 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper so the seasoning is spread evenly through the crumbs.

Yes. Use a small bowl for the eggs and water. Beat them together so the chicken can get an even wet coating between the flour and bread crumbs.
So the bowls should be flour, egg mixture, then seasoned bread crumbs?
That's the right order: flour first, then eggs and water, then the bread crumbs mixed with black pepper and cayenne.
I'm about to start dipping. Should I do all the chicken at once or piece by piece?
Work one piece at a time. Coat a piece of chicken in the flour, dip it into the egg-and-water mixture, then press it into the bread crumbs until covered.
Some crumbs are falling off when I move the chicken. Is there a better way to handle it?
After the egg dip, let extra liquid drip off briefly, then press the chicken firmly into the bread crumbs on both sides. Move it gently once coated.
Where should I put the coated pieces while I finish the rest?
Set each coated chicken piece aside in a single layer as you finish it, then continue the same flour, egg, and breadcrumb coating sequence for the remaining tenders.

Set out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a saucepan, a spoon for the early stirring, and a large cookie sheet that's already buttered so it's ready when the candy hits temperature.

Give it a light stir so the sugar and salt dissolve into the water and oil. Once it reaches a boil, take the saucepan off the heat.

Put the diced onion and diced celery into a small pot. Add the margarine and chicken broth there as directed, keeping the mixture together for the dressing base.

A small pot is fine for combining the 1 cup diced onion, 1 cup diced celery, margarine, and chicken broth. Keep the crumbled biscuits and cornbread nearby so you're ready to bring the dressing components together after this mixture is prepared.

Absolutely. You'll need 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies, 1/4 cup melted margarine, 1 cup hot fudge topping, and 2 quarts vanilla ice cream. Keep the pan nearby so you can build the crust right in it.

messages.content: I'm cooking Barbecued Shredded Beef today and I've got a large roasting pan ready. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I turn on the oven?

Add 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream directly to the casserole dish.

Yes, use the full 1 ounce package of garlic and mushroom soup mix. Stir it into the mayonnaise and sour cream until it's evenly blended.

Chop the drained artichoke hearts, then fold them into the dip mixture so they're spread throughout.

Yes. Add the cheese and crab meat to the same 1-1/2 quart casserole dish, then stir everything together gently so the crab stays in nice pieces.
Everything is combined and leveled out. Do I need to cover the casserole?
Leave it uncovered and bake it in the 350 degrees F oven for 30 minutes.
It's been 30 minutes and it looks hot around the edges. What's the serving move?
Take it out carefully and serve immediately while the dip is warm and creamy.
I'm making Broccoli Chicken Roli and I've got a cutting board out. Can you help me start with the prep?
Yes. Set up a large bowl, then measure out 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat and 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli. Those can go nearby while you finish the rest of the vegetables.
The chicken is already cooked and chopped, and the broccoli is chopped too. What vegetables should I add next?
Chop enough onion for 1/2 cup and enough green bell pepper for 1/2 cup. Keep the pieces fairly small so they mix evenly with the chicken and broccoli.
I've got the onion and green bell pepper measured. Should everything go straight into the bowl?
Yes. Put the chicken, broccoli, onion, and green bell pepper into the large bowl. Then add the cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic called for in the recipe.
All of that is in the bowl now. How thoroughly should I combine it?
Mix it until the chicken, broccoli, vegetables, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, and seasonings are evenly distributed. You're looking for the mixture to hold together without leaving dry pockets.
The mixture looks evenly coated. Should I heat the oven before I shape or arrange anything?
Go ahead and get the oven warming to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). That way it can come up to temperature while you prepare the pan.
Oven is set to 400. What pan setup do I need?
Use a cookie sheet and cover it with aluminum foil. Press the foil down so it sits flat and gives you an easy surface for arranging the roli.
The foil is on the cookie sheet. Anything I should check before moving the filling over?

Give the filling one last stir and make sure the bowl has no unmixed streaks of mayonnaise, mustard, or seasoning. Once the oven reaches 400 degrees F, the foil-lined cookie sheet will be ready for the next part.
I'm cooking Black Bean Chili today. Can you help me get everything started without jumping too far ahead?
Absolutely. Set out a large saucepan and gather 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 chopped onion, 2 red bell peppers that are seeded and chopped, and 1 jalapeno pepper that's seeded and minced.
I've got the saucepan out, and the onion and peppers are prepped. Should I heat the pan before adding anything?
Yes. Put the saucepan over medium-high heat, then add the olive oil and let it warm until it looks glossy.
The oil is glossy now. Do the onion and peppers all go in together?
They do. Add the onion, red bell peppers, and jalapeno, along with the mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn. Stir them through the oil so the vegetables start cooking evenly.
They're in the pan. How long should I let the vegetables cook down?
Sautee them for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, or until the onions turn translucent and the peppers soften.
The onions are starting to look translucent, and there's some moisture in the pan. Is that okay?
That's fine for chili. Keep the heat at medium-high and stir so the vegetables don't stick while the moisture cooks into the mixture.
The vegetables look softened now. When do the seasonings go in?
Add the black pepper, cumin, and chili powder now. Stir well so the spices coat the vegetables and warm in the pan.
The spices smell good. What do I add to turn it into the chili base?
Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt. Mix everything together, scraping the bottom of the saucepan so the seasoned vegetables blend into the broth.
I'm making Chicken Marsala with Portobello Mushrooms, and I'd like to cook along without getting ahead of myself.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 3/4 cup butter, divided, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided, so the measured portions are ready when the skillet is hot.
I've got the butter and oil measured. Should I prep the mushrooms before I turn anything on?
Yes. Slice 4 portobello mushroom caps, and chop 1 clove garlic so it's ready beside the stove.
The mushrooms are sliced and the garlic is chopped. Do I need the oven for this part?
Bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for Chicken Marsala with Portobello Mushrooms.
The oven is heating. I have a skillet on the stove; what goes in first?
Put the skillet over medium heat, then melt 1/2 cup butter with 1 tablespoon vegetable oil.
The butter has melted into the oil and it's gently bubbling. Should the mushrooms go in now?
Yes, add the sliced portobello mushrooms to the skillet and stir them through the butter and oil.
They're in the pan. How do I know when they're cooked enough?
Keep cooking and stirring until the mushroom slices are tender; they should soften and look glossy rather than firm or dry.
The mushrooms feel tender now, and there's still some buttery liquid in the skillet. What should I do with them while I keep cooking?
Take the skillet off the heat, cover the mushrooms to keep them warm, and set them aside.
I'm putting together Double Fudge Brownie Mix in a jar. Can you help me organize the ingredients before I start layering?
Absolutely. Set out a 1 quart or 1 liter jar, then measure 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.
The jar is clean and dry. Does the order matter, or can I just pour everything in?
Use the listed order so the layers look neat: white sugar on the bottom, then unsweetened cocoa powder, then all-purpose flour, with chopped pecans on top.
The sugar is in, but the cocoa is making a dusty layer. Should I pack it down?
You can gently tap the jar on the counter to settle it, but don't press hard. A light leveling helps keep the cocoa layer even without compacting everything too much.
Okay, cocoa is leveled. I'm adding the flour now—anything I should watch for?
Spoon or pour the flour in slowly so it doesn't punch through the cocoa layer. If it mounds up, tilt the jar slightly or tap it gently to even it out.
The flour layer looks fine. I've got the 1 cup chopped pecans ready for the top.
Add the pecans last and spread them across the top of the flour. Once they're in, close the jar securely so the layers stay in place.
Jar is closed. What needs to go on the tag?
Write the mix name and include this baking instruction on the tag: set the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Should I include anything else from this recipe before I tie the tag on?

For the recipe details you have, that's the full set: the layered jar ingredients and the tag instruction to get the oven warming to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Tie the tag on and store the jar upright.
I'm making Chicken Vegetable Stew and I've already cleared space near the stove. Can you help me organize what goes into the pot?
Absolutely. For the main stew base, have ready 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into bite-size pieces, 1 chopped onion, 1/2 pound baby carrots, and 4 potatoes.
The chicken is cut up, the onion is chopped, and the carrots are still whole baby carrots. Should the potatoes be prepped before I start loading the pot?
Yes, get the potatoes ready before the pot fills up so everything can go in together. Once they're prepped, place the chopped onion, chicken breast meat, baby carrots, and potatoes into a large pot.
I have a large pot on the counter, not on heat yet. Is it okay if the onion goes in with the raw chicken instead of being cooked separately?
For this recipe, yes. The onion, bite-size chicken pieces, carrots, and potatoes all go into the large pot together rather than sautéing the onion separately.
Everything is in the pot now. I see salt and turmeric in the ingredient area, but there aren't amounts listed. What should I do next without overdoing it?
Add the salt and turmeric next. Since the recipe doesn't give exact amounts, season modestly at this stage; you can adjust later after the stew has come together.
The turmeric is in and the color is starting to spread over the chicken and vegetables. What happens with the tomato paste?
Dissolve the tomato paste in water before adding it. Stir it until it loosens into the water, then pour that mixture into the pot so it distributes more evenly.
Should I pour the tomato mixture over one spot or move it around while adding it?
Pour it around the pot rather than dumping it all in one place, then gently stir so the tomato-water mixture coats the chicken, potatoes, carrots, and onion.
I'd like a little more seasoning, but I don't want to cover up the stew flavor. What are the optional add-ins?

If you want a bit more seasoning, add garlic powder and ground black pepper to taste. Stir them in gently, then check that the chicken, onion, carrots, potatoes, salt, turmeric, and tomato paste mixture are all evenly combined.
I'm making Escargots Vol au Vent and have the snails on the counter. Can you coach me through the prep?
Absolutely. Check that you have 12 helix snails without shells, plus 1/2 cup softened butter ready to turn into the seasoned mixture.
The butter is soft, and the snails are out of their container. What aromatics should I prep before I start?
Finely chop 2 cloves of garlic and 1 green onion. Keep them close to the mixing bowl so they can go straight into the butter.
Garlic and green onion are chopped. Should I heat the oven before handling the escargots?
Yes, set the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it can heat while you get the escargots and butter mixture ready.
The oven is heating. The snails look packed in liquid—what should I do with them?
Drain the escargots, rinse them under cold water, then drain them again well so extra liquid doesn't loosen the butter mixture.
They're rinsed and draining in a small sieve. What goes into the bowl with the butter?
Add the softened butter to the mixing bowl with the chopped garlic, chopped green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine.
I've added everything to the bowl, but the butter is still a little streaky. How much should I work it?
Mix it thoroughly until the garlic, green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine are evenly distributed through the butter.
That looks even now. Should the escargots be completely dry before I combine or arrange anything?
They don't need to be bone-dry, but they should be well drained after the cold-water rinse. Pat lightly if needed, then keep them ready for assembling the vol-au-vent.
I'm making Apple Cranberry Crisp 2 and I've got a pile of Granny Smith apples on the counter. Can you guide me through the prep?
Absolutely. Peel, core, and thinly slice 2 pounds of Granny Smith apples, then measure out 3/4 cup cranberries so the fruit is ready to mix.
The apples are sliced thin, and the cranberries are measured. Which sweetener and spice should I put nearby?
Set out 1/4 cup white sugar and 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon. The directions also mention nutmeg when mixing the fruit, though the amount isn't listed in the ingredients.
Thanks for flagging that. I have an 8 inch square dish—should I prep the oven and pan before mixing the fruit?
Yes. Heat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, and butter the 8 inch square baking dish so the crisp won't stick.
The oven is heating and the dish is buttered. I'm using a large mixing bowl; what goes in together?
Add the sliced apples and cranberries to the large bowl, then sprinkle in the white sugar, cinnamon, and the nutmeg called for in the directions.
The fruit is coated, but some apple slices are clumping together. Does it need to be perfectly mixed?
It doesn't need to be perfect, but toss until the sugar and spices are spread through the apples and cranberries fairly evenly.
That looks evenly coated now. How should I move it into the baking dish without making one side too full?
Tip the fruit mixture into the buttered dish and spread it into an even layer, making sure the corners get filled too.
The fruit is in the dish. I still have the same bowl out—what should I combine for the topping base?
Use that same bowl to combine the oats, flour, and brown sugar. The recipe doesn't give amounts for those topping ingredients here, so follow your recipe source if you have the remaining quantities.
I want to make Broccoli Coleslaw. Can you help me get the dressing started and keep me on track?

Absolutely. For the dressing, set out 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1 chicken-flavored ramen package that is 3 ounces. Keep the seasoning packet aside because it goes into the dressing.
I've got the oil, vinegar, and sugar measured. Should I crush the ramen before opening the seasoning packet?
You can crush the noodles while they're still in the package, then open it carefully and remove the seasoning packet. Put the crushed noodles aside for later so they stay crisp.
What bowl should I use for the dressing?
Use a small bowl. Add the olive oil, distilled white vinegar, white sugar, and the reserved ramen seasoning packet to it.
The sugar is sitting at the bottom a bit. Do I whisk it or just stir?
Whisk or stir it well until the seasoning is evenly mixed and the sugar starts to dissolve into the oil and vinegar.
How long does that dressing need to chill before I put everything together?
Refrigerate the mixed dressing for at least 1 hour before serving. If you have time, letting it sit overnight is also fine.
While that chills, I'm using a big salad bowl. What goes in there besides the noodles?
In the large bowl, combine the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds. Toss them lightly so everything is distributed before the ramen goes in.
The vegetables are mixed. Do the crushed ramen noodles go in right before serving?
Yes. Stir in the crushed ramen noodles near the end so they keep some crunch, then add the chilled dressing when you're ready to serve and toss the coleslaw well.
I'm about to start Best Macaroni Salad. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a big pot and a mixing bowl ready.
Absolutely. Set up your ingredients: 1 (16 ounce) package macaroni, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup cucumber that's peeled, seeded, and chopped, and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion.
The cucumber is prepped, and I found the dried minced onion. Should I start the pasta water now?
Yes. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, then add the macaroni and cook it until al dente.
How firm should the macaroni be before I drain it?
It should be tender but still have a little bite, since it will be mixed into the salad instead of cooked further.
The pasta is al dente. Do I drain it hot or cool it down?
Drain it, rinse it under cold water, and let it drain well so the salad doesn't turn watery.
The macaroni is cold and drained. I'm using the large bowl now.
Add the pasta to the bowl with the mayonnaise, then mix well so the macaroni is evenly coated.
It's coated. When do the cucumber and onion go in?
Stir in the chopped cucumber and dried minced onion, along with the ham and cheese, distributing everything through the pasta.
Everything is in the bowl. What's the last thing I should check before serving?
Give the salad one final thorough mix so the mayonnaise, cucumber, onion, ham, and cheese are evenly combined, then it's ready to serve.
Let's work through Cabbage Kielbasa Supper today. Where should I begin? I've got a 5-qt. cooker out.
Absolutely. Start by prepping the vegetables: you'll need 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2 inch cubes, and 1 medium onion chopped.
The cabbage is shredded, and I'm cubing the potatoes now. Should the potato pieces stay pretty small?
Yes, keep them around 1/2 inch so they get tender during the long slow-cook time. Once the potatoes and onion are ready, add the cabbage, potatoes, and onion to the slow cooker.
They're in the cooker, but it's already looking very full. Is that okay?
That's expected for this recipe. The cabbage will cook down quite a bit, so it's fine if the slow cooker looks full at the start.
What seasoning goes in before I add the liquid?
Sprinkle in 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, plus pepper as directed in the recipe, over the cabbage, potatoes, and onion.
Seasoning is in. Do I stir it all together before adding broth?
A light mix is helpful to distribute the salt and pepper, but you don't need to pack it down. After that, pour the broth over everything in the slow cooker.
Broth is poured in. Where does the kielbasa go?
Place the sausage on top of the cabbage mixture. It should sit above the vegetables and heat through as the cabbage and potatoes cook underneath.
All set. How long should I cook it, and what am I checking for at the end?
Cover the slow cooker and cook on low for 8-9 hours. It's done when the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through.
I want to make Beet and Pear Puree. Can you guide me through the prep without rushing?
Absolutely. Set out 8 medium beets, 1 pound unsalted butter, 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions, and 4 Bosc pears. The pears should be peeled, cored, and minced.
I've got the beets and butter on the counter. Should I deal with the oven before chopping anything?
Yes. heat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), so it's ready when the beets are washed.
Oven is heating. What pan should I use for the beets?
Use a roasting pan. Wash the 8 medium beets well, then place them in the roasting pan.
The beets are washed and in the pan. How long am I roasting them?
Bake them for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until they're tender. After that, set them aside to cool before handling.
While they roast, I can prep the pears and onions. Can you confirm the amounts?
Yes: mince 1 1/2 cups Vidalia onions, and prepare 4 Bosc pears by peeling, coring, and mincing them.
The beets are tender now and cooling. What should I get ready on the stovetop?
Place a large skillet on the stove and add the 1 pound unsalted butter.
Skillet is ready with the butter in it. What heat should I use?
Melt the butter in the large skillet over medium heat.
I'm starting French Apple Cream Pie; can you walk me through the setup? I've got a 9 inch pie pan out and want to stay on track.
Absolutely. You'll need pastry for a 9 inch double crust pie, a 21 ounce can of apple pie filling, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg.
The pastry is thawed and the apple filling can is open. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes—set the oven to 425 degrees F, which is 220 degrees C, so it can heat while you work with the crust.
Oven is on. I'm about to roll the pastry; should I put both crusts in the pan right away?
Roll out the pastry shell, then let it rest in the refrigerator for a bit before lining the pan. Keep the second crust ready since this is for a double crust pie.
The dough has rested and feels cool. How should I fit it into the pie pan without tearing it?
Lay one rolled out pastry crust into the 9 inch pie pan, easing it down into the corners rather than stretching it. If it wrinkles, lift and settle it gently.
The bottom crust is in place. Do I mix the spices straight into the can of filling or use a bowl?
Use a medium mixing bowl. Add the apple pie filling, then stir in the 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg so the spices spread evenly.
I see lemon rind mentioned in my notes too. Does that go in with the filling mixture?
Yes, combine the lemon rind in the same bowl with the pie filling, cinnamon, and nutmeg, then stir until everything looks evenly mixed.
The filling is mixed and smells good. Should I pour it into the crust now?
Yes. Spoon or pour the spiced apple filling into the pastry-lined 9 inch pan, spread it evenly, and keep the remaining rolled pastry ready for the top crust.
I'm ready to cook A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie. What should be ready before I begin? I've got my blender out but haven't opened anything yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 (10 ounce) package of frozen mixed berries, 1 (15 ounce) can of sliced peaches that you'll drain, and 2 tablespoons of honey.
Before I continue with A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie, the berries are still frozen solid. Is that okay, or should I thaw them first?
Frozen is fine for this smoothie. They'll help make it thick and cold; just make sure your blender can handle frozen fruit.
I drained the peaches. Should the peach slices go in before the berries?
Yes, add the drained sliced peaches to the blender first if you'd like easier blending, then add the frozen mixed berries on top.
Where does the honey fit in? I don't want it stuck to the lid.
Drizzle the 2 tablespoons honey directly over the fruit in the blender jar so it gets pulled into the mixture as it blends.
Everything is in the blender now. Do I need any liquid?
The recipe only calls for the frozen mixed berries, drained peaches, and honey, so start without extra liquid. If your blender struggles, pause and scrape down the sides, then blend again.
It's blending but still has a few berry pieces. What texture am I aiming for?
Keep blending until the smoothie is completely smooth, with no big fruit chunks left.
It looks smooth now. Should I serve it right away or chill it?
Serve it right away while it's cold and thick. Pour it into glasses, then rinse the blender jar soon so the honey and fruit don't dry onto it.
I want to make Frosted Shortbread today. Can you guide me without rushing? I've got my mixing bowl out.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 cup softened butter with no substitutes and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Those need to be ready for creaming together.
The butter is soft and the brown sugar is packed. Do I need anything else at the bowl before I start mixing?
Yes—keep 1 egg yolk and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract nearby. You'll add those after the butter and brown sugar are creamed.
Got it. Should the pan be ready now too, or can that wait?
Go ahead and grease a 15-in pan now if it's convenient. That way the dough can go straight in once it's mixed.
Pan is greased. I'm ready to start the dough; what texture am I aiming for with the butter and sugar?
Cream the softened butter and packed brown sugar in the mixing bowl until they look evenly blended and a bit lighter. Scrape the bowl as needed so there aren't streaks of butter.
That's mixed and looks smooth. I separated the egg already—just the yolk goes in, right?
Right, add only the egg yolk along with the vanilla extract, then mix well until everything is fully incorporated.
The yolk and vanilla are mixed in. The bowl smells great. What happens with the dry ingredients?
Combine the flour and salt separately, then add that mixture to the creamed mixture. Mix just until the dough comes together evenly.
The dough is together. It's soft but holds when I press it—how should I get it into the pan?
Press the dough evenly into the greased 15-in pan, working it out to the edges and smoothing the surface as best you can.
Can you help me put together Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies? I'm making the jar mix, not baking them right this second.

For this batch of Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies, set out 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need a clean wide-mouth 1 liter glass jar for layering.
I've got the jar washed and dried. Should the dry ingredients be mixed before they go in?
Yes. In a bowl, combine the flour with the baking powder, baking soda, salt, and nutmeg. Stir it well so the leavening is evenly distributed through the flour mixture.
The flour mixture looks even. Do I put that in the jar first?
Put the white sugar in first as the bottom layer, then spoon the flour mixture on top of it in the wide-mouth jar. Try to keep the layers distinct as you add them.
The flour is making a mound near the top. Should I shake the jar down?
A light tap on the counter is fine, but don't shake hard enough to blur the layers. Press the mixture firmly in place so everything fits neatly.
It's packed down now and the lid fits. Is sealing it enough?
Yes, seal the jar tightly once the layers are firmly packed. Wipe the rim first if any flour is caught there so the lid closes cleanly.
I want to add the instruction card. What exactly should it say for the person baking later?
Write that they should use a large bowl and beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy.
Should I attach that card to the lid or hang it around the neck of the jar?

Either works. Tie it around the neck if you want it visible as a gift, or tape it to the lid if the jar will be stored in a pantry. The important part is that the card stays with the Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies mix.
I want to make Cheddar Artichoke Quiche Cups. Can you guide me while I prep the artichokes and eggs?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (7.5 ounce) jar of marinated artichoke hearts, 1 small finely chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 4 beaten eggs. Keep a skillet and a large mixing bowl nearby.
The jar is open, and I have the onion chopped. Should I pour off all the artichoke marinade?
Drain the artichokes, but save half of the marinade. You'll use that reserved marinade to cook the onion and garlic.
I saved about half. The artichoke hearts are still whole pieces—how small should they be?
Chop the artichoke hearts into small bite-size pieces, then set them aside so they're ready to fold in later.
Done. I have the skillet out—does the onion go in with oil or with the marinade?
Use the reserved marinade in the skillet. Add the finely chopped onion and minced garlic, then sauté them until they're tender.
The onion is soft and the garlic smells good. Should I leave that mixture in the pan?
Take the skillet off the heat and set the onion-garlic mixture aside. That keeps it from overcooking while you mix the egg base.
I've got the large bowl ready with the beaten eggs. What gets mixed into them?
In this Cheddar Artichoke Quiche Cups step, in the large bowl, combine the beaten egg with bread crumbs, mustard, oregano, pepper, and hot pepper sauce. Stir until the mixture looks evenly blended.
The bowl mixture is smooth with the seasonings mixed in. Do the artichokes and sautéed onion mixture wait off to the side for now?
Yes. Keep the chopped artichokes and the sautéed onion-garlic mixture nearby so they're ready for the next stage of assembling the Cheddar Artichoke Quiche Cups.
Today I'm tackling Asparagus Sandwiches. Can you help me line up the prep? I've got the canned asparagus but want to keep the rolls from getting soggy.
Absolutely. Start by draining 1 (10 ounce) can of asparagus tips well, then lay the spears on paper towels so they can give off extra liquid before you roll them.
They're on paper towels now. Should I press them, or just let them sit while I mix the spread?
Just let them sit and blot gently if needed; pressing can break the tips. While they drain, put 1/2 cup mayonnaise into a small bowl.
Mayonnaise is in the bowl. I have an onion here—how fine should I chop it?
Chop it finely so it blends smoothly into the spread, then add 2 tablespoons finely chopped onion to the mayonnaise.
Added the onion. The seasoning salt is pretty strong, so I don't want to overdo it.
Use just 1 pinch seasoning salt, then stir the mayonnaise, onion, and seasoning salt together until the mixture looks even.
The spread is mixed. I'm using soft sandwich bread—do I trim it before spreading?
Yes, remove the crusts from the bread slices before you add the filling. That helps them roll more neatly.
Crusts are off. How much of the mayonnaise mixture should go on each slice?
Spread the mayonnaise mixture thinly on each slice, just enough to coat the surface without making the bread heavy or wet.
The slices are spread and the asparagus looks drained. What's the best way to assemble them?
Place one asparagus spear onto each prepared slice, then roll the bread up around it. Set the rolls seam-side down on the tray so they hold their shape.
I have Churros planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a small saucepan out, but I want to make sure I'm measuring everything right.
Absolutely. Measure 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. Keep flour nearby too, since you'll stir it in after the liquid comes off the heat.
The water, sugar, salt, and oil are measured. Should they all go into the saucepan together?
Yes. Put the 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil into the small saucepan, then set it over medium heat.
It's on medium now. Am I just warming it, or should I wait for a real boil?
Let it come to a full boil. Once it reaches that point, take the saucepan off the heat right away.
It boiled and I moved it off the burner. The pan is still hot—do I add the flour immediately?
Yes, stir in the flour while the mixture is hot. Keep stirring until it pulls together and forms a ball.
It's starting to clump but there are still a few streaks. Should I keep mixing?
Keep stirring until the dough looks unified and ball-like. It should come together rather than stay loose or streaky.
The dough has formed a ball. What frying setup should I use if I don't have a deep-fryer?
Use a deep skillet instead. Heat the frying oil in the deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
Got it. I'll use the deep skillet and check the temperature. Anything I should watch before frying?
Make sure the oil is steady at 375 degrees F or 190 degrees C before you add any dough, and keep the pan area clear so you can work safely with the hot oil.
I pulled up Gelatin Fruit Salad. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got a saucepan out, but I want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup applesauce and 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin for the base of the salad.
Those are on the counter. The applesauce is measured—what else should I pull from the pantry or fridge?
You'll also need 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple. Keep the pineapple undrained, since the liquid goes in too.
Good to know about the pineapple juice. Should I open the cans before heating the applesauce?
Yes, that will make things smoother. Open the soda and pineapple, then pour the applesauce into the saucepan.
The applesauce is in the pan. How hot should I take it?
Heat it until the applesauce comes to a boil, stirring occasionally so it warms evenly and doesn't stick.
It's bubbling now. Do I leave it on the burner while adding the gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat, then stir in both packages of cherry gelatin until the powder is completely dissolved.
The gelatin looks dissolved and smooth. Is the soda supposed to go in all at once?
Add the lemon-lime soda slowly so it doesn't foam over, then stir in the undrained crushed pineapple.
Everything is mixed. What kind of dish should I put it in before chilling?
Pour it into your serving bowl or mold, then refrigerate it until firm. Once it's fully set, it's ready to serve cold.
Let's work through Atomic Canuck Chili today. Where should I begin? I'm setting up the counter now and want to make sure I start with the right pan.

Yes. Set out a large skillet for the stovetop and a slow cooker for after the beef is browned. You'll need 2 pounds lean ground beef, 1/2 large onion diced, 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper, and 3 tablespoons garlic powder.
The beef is thawed, and I've diced the onion. Should the skillet be hot before I add everything?

Put the skillet over medium heat, then add the ground beef with the diced onion, crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper. Cook it together until the beef is browned and the onion has softened.
It's starting to brown, but there's a lot of liquid and fat in the pan. Do I keep cooking it off?
Once the beef is browned, drain off the fat rather than cooking it all into the chili. After draining, transfer the beef and onion mixture into the slow cooker.
The slow cooker is ready. Do the beans go in drained or with liquid?
Add the kidney beans with their liquid. Stir them into the slow cooker along with the baked beans, mushrooms, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce.
That's a lot in the crock. Should I fold it gently or really mix everything together?
Give it a thorough stir so the tomato paste, beans, vegetables, beer, barbeque sauce, and beef mixture are evenly combined, but don't mash the beans while you mix.
The chili base is mixed. When do I adjust the heat level?
Season it now with hot sauce and more crushed red pepper. Start with a moderate amount, stir, and taste later once the flavors have had time to blend.
Any cleanup or texture check before I put the lid on and let the slow cooker take over?

Scrape down the sides of the slow cooker so nothing dries out above the chili line, make sure the mixture looks evenly saucy and chunky, then cover it. The core recipe steps are done; from here, let the slow cooker handle the chili until it's heated through and the vegetables are tender.

Hold the sealed bag over the bowl and gently shake or turn it until the swordfish steaks are coated on all sides with the marinade.

Heat the 2 tablespoons olive oil in the skillet over medium heat.

Set out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells, 3 softened 8 ounce packages of cream cheese, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The cream cheese is out of the fridge and softening more on the counter. Do I need a specific bowl for this?
Use a medium mixing bowl with enough room for whipping. A hand mixer will make the 3 packages of cream cheese much easier to get fluffy, but a sturdy whisk can work if the cheese is fully softened.
Got it. The shells are already baked, and one has a few crumbly spots. Is that a problem for serving this way?
No problem. Keep the larger crust pieces for the neat edges of the path, and save the crumbs to sprinkle where you want a little extra crunch near the crust side.
I like that center-meet plating; it works better for this dish because the textures don't blur together too soon. When should I turn on the oven?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, while you get the filling ready. Even with baked shells, that is the recipe temperature to have set.
The oven is set, and I've got the bowl ready. Should the sugar and vanilla wait until after the cream cheese is whipped?
Yes. Put only the softened cream cheese in the bowl first, then whip it until it looks lighter, smoother, and fluffy, with no cold dense lumps.
It's starting to loosen up, but the mixer is leaving ridges. Is that still too thick?
A few ridges are fine, but keep whipping until the cream cheese looks airy and spreadable rather than heavy. Scrape the bowl once so the bottom and sides catch up.
Now it looks fluffy. I have the 1/2 cup sugar measured and the vanilla bottle open.
Add the 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the whipped cream cheese. Mix again until the sugar and vanilla are evenly blended through the filling.
The filling smells sweet and smooth, but I can see a couple streaks along the bowl.
Scrape down the sides and mix a little longer until the filling is completely smooth. You should not see streaks of plain cream cheese or pockets of sugar.
It's smooth now. How should I portion the crust and filling on the plate without making a mess?

Arrange the baked 9 inch pie-shell pieces into slim lanes, then spoon the smooth cream-cheese filling beside them in matching lanes. Let the two paths meet only at the center, clean up the edges with the back of the spoon, and serve when the filling looks even and ready.

Set the cheese out early so it loses some of its chill, then crumble it by hand into uneven pieces right before serving. For the smoothie, get the blender ready and tuck a large glass into the freezer or fridge to chill.
The glass is chilling, and the blender jar is on the base. Should I start with the dairy ingredients?
Yes. Measure 1 1/2 scoops vanilla ice cream and pour 1 1/2 cups milk so they can go in together as the cold base.
I measured the milk and scooped the ice cream. The ice cream is softening a little—problem?
A little softening is fine, especially since it will blend more easily. Just don't let it melt completely before it goes into the blender.

Use 1/4 cup whipped cream and 2 tablespoons instant hot chocolate mix. If you're including the crushed cookies mentioned in the blending step, keep them beside the blender too.

They can all go in now: vanilla ice cream, milk, whipped cream, instant hot chocolate mix, and the crushed cookies if you're using them.
Everything is in the jar. The hot chocolate mix is sitting on top—should I stir it down first?
No need to stir by hand. Put the lid on firmly and blend until the drink looks smooth, with no dry cocoa streaks or big cookie bits.
It's blending smoothly now, but it's thick enough that it moves slowly around the blade.
That's okay for this smoothie. If it still pours, leave it thick and creamy; only thin it with a small splash of milk if it gets too stiff to come out of the jar.
It pours, so I'm stopping there. Should I grab the chilled glass before I pour?
Yes, use the chilled glass now. Pour the smoothie in right away so it stays cold and frosty.
The smoothie is in the glass and the top looks creamy. Anything else before I serve it?
Serve it immediately while it's very cold. If you're adding the cheese, scatter the hand-crumbled pieces near serving so they keep that uneven texture.

For Gerrys Chicken Enchiladas, start with 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 1 chopped onion, and 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers.
I've got the chicken, oil, onion, and the 10 ounce can on the counter. What should I do with the chicken first?
Cut the chicken breasts into 1 inch strips so they'll cook evenly and fit well into the wrap.
Before I continue with Gerrys Chicken Enchiladas, the strips are cut. Do they go straight into the skillet, or is there a wait?
For this batch of Gerrys Chicken Enchiladas, put the chicken strips in a medium bowl with your desired marinade, then refrigerate them for at least 30 minutes.

Yes. Keep the onion chopped and ready, and open the diced tomatoes with green chile peppers so everything is close by when the chicken comes out.

Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Use a large skillet, since it gives the chicken strips enough room and will also leave space for the onion and tomatoes later.

Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in the large skillet over medium heat; that's enough to get the cooking started without overloading the filling.

messages.content: I'm making Absolutely Awesome BBQ Sauce and I've got a small saucepan ready. What should I sort out before I turn on the heat?

For the garlic in this sauce, slice it very thin and soften it gently over low heat before adding the liquids. Then set out 1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup chile sauce, 1/2 cup rum, and 1/4 cup soy sauce, plus the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, dry mustard, and pepper.
The measured ingredients are on the counter. Should I start with the garlic alone, or wait until the sauce is mixed?
Start with the garlic alone in the saucepan on low heat. Let it turn fragrant and soft without browning, then you can build the sauce around it.
I sliced the garlic very thin, and the pan is barely warm. About how long should I give it before adding everything else?
Give it just a short gentle start, enough that it smells mellow and no longer sharp. Keep stirring so the thin pieces do not catch on the bottom.
That thin slicing and gentle head start is exactly what I wanted for this sauce; I like how it starts smoother. I'm ready to pour in the rest.

Add the brown sugar first and stir it around the softened garlic, then pour in the chile sauce, rum, soy sauce, ketchup, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir in the dry mustard and pepper until the mixture looks even.
The brown sugar is making it look a little sandy in the pan. Did I add it too early?
No, that is normal. As the sauce warms, the brown sugar will dissolve into the chile sauce, rum, soy sauce, ketchup, and Worcestershire sauce; just keep the heat low and stir along the bottom.
The rum smell is pretty noticeable right now. Should I raise the heat to cook it off faster?
Keep it low rather than rushing it. Once the sauce reaches a gentle simmer, the aroma will soften during the 30 minutes of cooking.
I'm seeing small bubbles around the edges now. Do I cover the saucepan or leave it open?
Leave it uncovered and let it simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Scrape the corners of the saucepan so the sugar and sauce do not scorch.
Halfway through, it's glossy but still thinner than bottled barbecue sauce. Is that okay?
Yes, halfway through it can still be loose. By the end of the 30 minutes, it should look more unified and a bit thicker, with the garlic softened into the sauce.
The 30 minutes are done, and the sauce smells balanced. What should I do before putting it away?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the BBQ sauce cool. Once it has cooled, refrigerate it until you are ready to use it, and stir it before serving if it settles.

Use the 1/2 cup warm water with the yeast in the small bowl. Keep the 1 1/4 cups cold water nearby for when the flour is ready.

Measure 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast. Pour the warm water into the small bowl, then sprinkle the yeast over the top so it can hydrate on the surface.
I like that garnish setup with the soft part centered and the crisp pieces off to the side; that's exactly what I wanted for serving. Now, after sprinkling the yeast, am I waiting or stirring?
Let it stand until the yeast dissolves and turns foamy, about 15 minutes. You do not need to stir unless a few dry bits stick stubbornly to the side of the bowl.
The timer is on. While it foams, should I measure the bread flour now?
Yes, measure 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour into the large bowl. Leave the flour loose rather than packing it down.
The flour is in the big bowl and the center is still flat. Do I make the well now or wait for the yeast?
You can make the well now. Press a hollow into the center of the flour that is wide enough to hold the yeast mixture and the cold water without immediately spilling over the edges.
The yeast looks foamy and smells active. What exactly goes into the well first?
Pour the foamy yeast mixture into the well first. Then add the 1 1/4 cups cold water into the same well so the liquids stay contained in the flour.
Some flour slid down the sides of the well, but the liquid is mostly in the middle. Is that fine?
That is fine. The recipe's listed steps are complete once the yeast mixture and cold water are in the flour well; just keep the bowl steady so the liquid does not run to the rim.
Before I move on, is there anything to tidy or double-check for the soup service later?

Wipe stray flour from the bowl rim and make sure you have used the full 3 1/2 cups flour, 3/4 teaspoon yeast, 1/2 cup warm water, and 1 1/4 cups cold water. When you serve it with soup, keep that soft garnish gathered in the center with the crunchy pieces curved along one side.
I'm ready to cook Cold Cocoa Smoothie. What should be ready before I begin? I've got the blender out and want to keep it simple.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 scoops vanilla ice cream, 1 1/2 cups milk, 1/4 cup whipped cream, and 2 tablespoons instant hot chocolate mix. You'll also want a large glass chilled for serving.
The glass is in the freezer. Should the ice cream go into the blender before the milk?
Yes, add the vanilla ice cream to the blender first, then pour in the milk so the blades have enough liquid to catch everything smoothly.
Okay, the ice cream and milk are in. I'm measuring the whipped cream now—does it go straight in too?
It does. Add the 1/4 cup whipped cream right into the blender, then sprinkle in the 2 tablespoons instant hot chocolate mix.
The cocoa mix is clumping a little on top. Is that a problem?
No problem. Once you blend, it should dissolve into the milk and ice cream. If you have crushed cookies for this smoothie, add them to the blender now as well.
I added the crushed cookies. How long should I blend it?
Blend until the mixture looks smooth and evenly cocoa-colored. Stop once there are no obvious dry streaks of hot chocolate mix or large cookie pieces moving around.
It looks creamy, but there are a few tiny cookie flecks. Should I keep going?
Tiny flecks are fine, especially from the crushed cookies. If the drink is pourable and smooth overall, you can stop blending.
The chilled glass is ready. Do I just pour it in and serve?
Yes. Pour the Cold Cocoa Smoothie into the large chilled glass and serve it right away while it's cold and creamy.
I'd like to make Baked Aloha Chicken. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing anything?

Absolutely. Measure out 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup light corn syrup, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, and 1 teaspoon salt. You'll also need ginger, corn oil, crushed pineapple with its liquid, chicken legs, a mixing bowl, and an ovenproof glass baking dish.
I've got the bowl and the glass baking dish out. Should the chicken go in the dish right away or do I make the sauce first?
Make the sauce first, and get the oven heating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the chicken is assembled.
The oven is set to 350, and I'm measuring the lemon juice and corn syrup now. Do those go in together?
Yes. Add the lemon juice and light corn syrup to the bowl, then stir in the soy sauce, salt, ginger, and corn oil. Mix until the sauce looks smooth.
The sauce is mostly smooth, but the corn syrup took a bit of stirring to blend in. Is that okay?
That's fine. As long as the lemon juice, corn syrup, soy sauce, salt, ginger, and corn oil are evenly combined, you're ready for the pineapple.
I opened the crushed pineapple. Do I drain it before adding it?
Don't drain it. Stir in the crushed pineapple with its liquid so the sauce keeps that sweet, fruity base.
The pineapple is mixed in. The sauce looks loose rather than thick—is that expected?
Yes, it should be pourable. Place the chicken legs in the ovenproof glass baking dish, then pour the pineapple sauce over the top.
The chicken legs are in the dish and covered with sauce. Anything I should check before putting it in the oven?
Make sure the chicken legs are sitting in a single layer and the sauce is distributed over them. Once the oven is at 350 degrees F, the dish is ready to go in.

Add 1/4 cup soy sauce and 1/4 cup ketchup. Stir them in with the teriyaki and oyster sauce so the base starts to look even.

Yes, add the garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar to the same bowl, then whisk until the ketchup streaks disappear and the seasonings are evenly distributed.
Would you thin it before or after the garlic powder and sugar dissolve?
After they dissolve is easier. Whisk first, then judge the sauce; if it drops heavily from the whisk, loosen it a splash at a time until it ribbons instead of clumping.
I like that lighter ribbon texture here—that's exactly what I wanted for these saucy wings.
Great. Once it has that smooth pour, scrape down the sides of the bowl so the marinade is collected at the bottom and ready for the chicken.

Yes, add the chicken wings to the bowl and turn them through the marinade until every piece is coated. Try not to leave any dry spots tucked between the wings.

Any tight cover works—plastic wrap, a fitted lid, or foil pressed snugly over the bowl. Put the covered wings in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight.

Keep the grill on low heat and give it a few minutes to preheat there. The sweet sauce can scorch if the grate is too hot right away.

Lightly oil the grill grate before adding the wings. Let excess marinade drip back into the bowl so the wings glaze on the grill rather than landing with thick pools of sauce.
I want to make Cranberry Apple Pie II today. Can you guide me through it while I set up?
Absolutely. Put your oven rack in a comfortable middle position if needed, and gather the main filling ingredients: 6 apples and 1 (16 ounce) can of whole cranberry sauce.

Yes, you'll also need 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour. Measure those now so the filling comes together smoothly.
Measured. I also have a pie plate ready, but I'm not sure when to start heating the oven.
Go ahead and bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Let it heat while you work on the crust and apples.
Oven is on. Should the pastry go in the pie plate before I deal with the fruit?
Yes. Line the pie plate with pastry, pressing it gently into the bottom and sides so there aren't big air pockets.
The pastry is in place. For the apples, do I leave the skins on or slice them a certain way?
Peel, core, and slice the apples. Try to keep the slices fairly even so they'll bake more consistently in the pie.
I've got a bowl of sliced apples now. Do I mix the cranberries in right away?
Yes. Combine the sliced apples with the whole cranberry sauce in a medium-sized mixing bowl, folding gently so the apples get coated without breaking up too much.
The fruit mixture looks glossy and red. What should I keep nearby before I fill the crust?
Keep the lined pie plate close, along with the measured 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, so everything from the recipe is ready as you continue assembling the pie.

Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a saucepan, a spoon, a candy thermometer if you have one, and a large cookie sheet buttered and ready.
The cookie sheet is buttered. Should the saucepan be on low before I add anything?
Yes, put the saucepan over low heat, then add the butter, white sugar, and the 1 cup chopped almonds.
They're in the pan now. The butter is starting to melt around the sugar and almonds.
Keep stirring constantly while it heats. Stay with it until the mixture comes to a boil.
It's bubbling now. Do I keep stirring so it doesn't stick?
Once it boils, stop stirring, and don't shake the pan. Let it continue heating undisturbed.

Heat it to 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. That's the hard-crack stage for this candy.
If I'm not sure about the thermometer, is there a texture check I can use?
Yes. Drop a small amount of the syrup into cold water; it should form hard, brittle threads.
It reached temperature and the cold-water drop snapped into brittle threads. What do I do right away?
Carefully pour the hot mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet. Tilt or spread it gently if needed, then let it cool on the sheet.
