No—take the pot off the heat, then add the almonds to the hot water. This softens the skins without continuing a hard boil.
They're in the hot water now. How long should they sit before I drain them?
Let the almonds soak for about 5 minutes. After that, drain them well and peel off the loosened skins.
Peeling is going fine, but the almonds are still damp. Is that okay before baking?
A little surface moisture is expected after peeling. Spread the almonds out on baking sheets in a single layer so they can dry evenly in the oven.
What temperature should I use, and am I looking for color or just dryness?
Bake them at 200 degrees F, which is 95 degrees C, until they're completely dry and toasted. Watch for a gently toasted look and a dry feel rather than deep browning.
Once they're dry and toasted, should I let them cool before handling them more?

Yes, let them cool on the baking sheets so they firm up and are easier to handle. Keep the measured 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons orange flower water nearby for the next part of the tart preparation.
I pulled up Corn Bread Sloppy Joes. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got the skillet out and want to make sure I set up the corn bread part correctly.

Absolutely. Put your 1 (8.5 ounce) package corn bread/muffin mix on the counter with 1 egg and 1/3 cup milk. You'll prepare and bake the corn bread according to the package directions using those two add-ins.
The mix, egg, and milk are ready. Should I get the meat started while the corn bread bakes?
Yes. While the corn bread is baking, place a large skillet over medium heat and add the 2 pounds ground beef with the onion.
I don't see onion in my ingredient list, but the directions mention it. How should I handle that?
Use onion if you have it, since the cooking step calls for beef and onion together. Cook them over medium heat until the beef is no longer pink, then drain off the excess fat.
The beef is browned and drained, and the corn bread is still in the oven. What should go into the skillet now?
Stir in the spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix with the cooked beef and onion. Mix until everything is evenly combined.
The sauce looks mixed in, but it's still just warming through. Do I need it bubbling?
Bring the mixture to a boil. Stir occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't stick to the bottom of the skillet.
It's starting to bubble around the edges. Should I wait for a stronger boil?
Let it reach a clear boil across the mixture, then you can reduce the heat if you need to hold it while the corn bread finishes baking.
The corn bread is baked now. How do I serve the sloppy joe mixture with it?
Spoon the hot sloppy joe mixture over portions of the baked corn bread, or split the corn bread and serve the beef mixture on top. Keep it warm and saucy when serving.
I want to make Corn Bread Sloppy Joes. Can you help me get set up before I start cooking?
Absolutely. Put the 1 (8.5 ounce) package corn bread/muffin mix on the counter along with 1 egg and 1/3 cup milk for the corn bread. You'll also need 2 pounds ground beef for the sloppy joe filling.
I've got the mix, egg, milk, and beef out. Do I start with the corn bread or the skillet?
Start with the corn bread so it can bake while you make the filling. Prepare the corn bread according to the package directions, using the egg and milk.
The batter is mixed. Should I bake it exactly the way the box says?
Yes, follow the package baking directions for that corn bread/muffin mix. Once it's in the oven, you can move to the beef mixture.
The corn bread is baking now, and I have a large skillet ready. What goes in there?
Add the ground beef and onion to the large skillet. Cook them over medium heat until the meat is no longer pink.
The beef has browned, and there's some grease in the pan. Should I leave it?
Drain the beef and onion mixture before adding the sauce ingredients, so the filling doesn't turn greasy.
Drained. I also have spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix nearby. Do they all go in together?
Yes. Stir the spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix into the drained beef and onion until everything is evenly combined.
It's mixed together and starting to look saucy. How do I know it's done?
Bring the mixture to a boil. Once it reaches that point, the sloppy joe filling is ready to serve with the baked corn bread.
Let's work through Fancy Brussels Sprouts today. Where should I begin? I've got a saucepan ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup water, 1/4 cup minced fresh parsley, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt so they're ready to go into the pan together.
I measured those. Do they all go in before the sprouts?
Yes. Put the water, parsley, sugar, and salt into the saucepan, then place it over medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil.
The parsley is floating and the water is starting to bubble around the edges. Should I wait for a full boil?
Wait until it's actively boiling, not just lightly bubbling. Once it reaches that point, add the brussels sprouts.
Sprouts are in. Do I leave the pan uncovered?
Cover the saucepan and let the brussels sprouts simmer for 6-8 minutes, just until they're tender.
What should tender feel like when I check them?
They should pierce easily with a fork but still hold their shape. If they feel firm in the center, give them another minute within that 6-8 minute window.
They're tender now. There's still liquid in the pan—do I keep it?
Drain the brussels sprouts so the extra cooking liquid is removed, then return them to the saucepan.
They're drained and back in the pan. How do I finish with the water chestnuts and butter?
Add the water chestnuts and butter to the saucepan with the brussels sprouts. Heat everything through, stirring gently so the sprouts stay intact, then serve while warm.
Carrot Pineapple Cake I is on deck today. What should I do first? I'm setting up the counter and want to start with the dry ingredients.
Absolutely. Put out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 teaspoon salt. You'll also need cinnamon for the dry mix.
I've got the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon out. Should I deal with the pan or the oven before mixing?
Yes—get the oven heating to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready when the batter is assembled.
The oven is heating. I have a 9x13 inch pan; how should I prep it?
Grease the 9x13 inch pan well, then dust it with flour so the cake releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. For the dry bowl, do I just dump everything together?
Add the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon to a mixing bowl, then stir or whisk until they look evenly combined.
The dry ingredients look evenly mixed. Do I need another bowl for the next part?
For this recipe's flow, make a well in the center of the dry mixture right in the same bowl.
I made the well. What goes into it, and should I add it all at once?
Add the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla into that well. Pour them into the center so they're ready to be worked into the dry mixture.
Everything is in the center now. Before I continue, can you recap the setup so I know I haven't missed anything?

You're on track: the oven is preheated to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), the 9x13 inch pan is greased and floured, the flour mixture includes the baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon, and the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla have been added to the well in the center.
I'm making Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon. Can you help me set up so the assembly goes smoothly?
Absolutely. Put out 6 figs, halved, 6 ounces goat cheese, 1/2 cup toasted chopped pecans, and 3 slices bacon cut in half. You'll also want toothpicks ready, since they hold the wrapped figs together.
The figs are halved and the cheese is soft enough to scoop. Should I turn anything on before I start filling them?
In this Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon step, yes, preheat the broiler now so it's ready when the figs are assembled.
Broiler is heating. How much goat cheese should go into each fig half?
Divide the 6 ounces goat cheese among the fig halves, tucking a small scoop into the cut side of each one so it sits securely.
They're filled, but the cheese is a little mounded. Is that okay for the pecans?
That's fine. Press the toasted chopped pecans into the goat cheese so they stick to the surface instead of falling off.
Pecans are pressed in. I have the bacon halves separated—how should I wrap without squeezing out the filling?
Wrap each stuffed fig half with half a slice of bacon, keeping the bacon snug but not so tight that it pushes the cheese out.
Some pieces overlap more than others. Do I need to secure every single one?
Yes, secure each wrapped fig with a toothpick so the bacon stays in place under the broiler.
They're all wrapped and on the pan. Anything I should check before they go under the broiler?
Give them a quick look to make sure each fig half has goat cheese, pecans pressed into the cheese, and a half slice of bacon held with a toothpick. Once that's set, they're ready for the broiler.

source_seed.recipe_title: Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon

messages.content: Baked Fish and Rice 2 is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got the baking dish out but want to make sure I set it up right.
Absolutely. Grease an 11-in. baking dish, and put your oven at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, so it can heat while you measure.
The dish is greased. What should I measure before anything goes in?
Measure 1 1/2 cups boiling chicken broth and 1/2 cup uncooked long grain rice. Keep the broth hot, since it goes straight into the dish with the rice.
I have the broth hot and the rice measured. Are there seasonings in this part too?
Yes. Add 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder to the baking dish along with the boiling broth and rice, then stir so the seasonings are evenly mixed through the liquid.
That's mixed in the dish. Do I cover it tightly or leave it open?
Cover the baking dish before it goes into the oven. Bake it at 375 degrees F, 190 degrees C, for 10 minutes.
The 10 minutes are up. The rice mixture is hot and still a little loose—what goes in before the fish?
Stir in the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, and half of the onions. Spread everything back into an even layer so the fish can sit on top.
Broccoli, Parmesan, and half the onions are in. Should I press the fish down into the rice?
No need to press it in. Lay the fish fillets over the top of the rice mixture, keeping them in a single layer if you can.
The fillets are arranged on top. What's the last seasoning before it bakes again?

Sprinkle the fish with paprika. At this point the dish is assembled according to the recipe: broth, rice, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, then broccoli, Parmesan, half the onions, fish fillets, and paprika on top.
I'd like to make Cinnamon Bread I today. Can you guide me from setup through mixing?

Absolutely. Set out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need the cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla for the bowl in a bit.
I have the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda on the counter. Should I prep the pan or start measuring?
In this Cinnamon Bread I step, get the oven going first so it has time to heat: preheat it to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is set to 350. I'm using a loaf pan—what size should it be?
In this Cinnamon Bread I step, use one 9x5 inch loaf pan, and grease it well so the cinnamon bread releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. For the mixing bowl, do I add the dry ingredients separately first?
For this recipe, measure everything directly into a large mixing bowl: the flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
I want to make sure I don't miss anything—so cinnamon is 1 1/2 teaspoons, right?
Yes, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon goes in with the flour, sugar, leaveners, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
Everything is measured into the large bowl now. Should I stir gently or use a mixer?
Use a mixer or beat it by hand with energy, and beat the mixture for 3 minutes so the batter comes together evenly.
After 3 minutes, should it look completely smooth before it goes into the pan?
It should look evenly mixed and pourable, with no obvious dry pockets. Once it reaches that point, scrape it into the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan for baking.
I'd like to make Basic Chicken Stock. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Put a large soup pot or Dutch oven on your work area, and gather 1 pound chicken parts, 1 large onion, 3 stalks celery with some leaves, and 1 large carrot.
I've got the pot out, and the chicken and vegetables are on the counter. Do I need to peel anything before cutting?
The recipe only calls for the onion to be quartered. For the celery and carrot, scrub them well before chopping; peeling isn't required by the recipe.
The onion is ready. How big should I cut the celery and carrot?
Chop the scrubbed celery and carrot into 1 inch chunks. Include some of the celery leaves if you have them.
Celery leaves are included, and the carrot pieces look about right. What goes into the pot first?
Add the chicken pieces to the large soup pot or Dutch oven, then put in the quartered onion, chopped celery, and chopped carrot.
The chicken and vegetables are in. I noticed the instructions mention seasoning—what should I add with them?
Add the salt and cloves to the pot along with everything else. The recipe doesn't list amounts for those, so use the amounts you have from your source if they're available.
Okay, the salt and cloves are in the pot. How much water should I pour over it?
Pour in 6 cups water, making sure the chicken and vegetables are settled in the pot.
All 6 cups are added. Should I stir it or leave it alone before cooking?

Give it a gentle stir just to distribute the onion, celery, carrot, salt, and cloves around the chicken. Then you're ready to proceed with cooking the stock according to your recipe's next directions.
I'd like to make Carrots and Onions Au Gratin, but I want to get the ingredients set out before I start cutting anything.
Good plan. Put out 1 (16 ounce) package of baby carrots, sliced, plus 2 medium onions, sliced. You'll also need 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter.
The carrots are baby carrots, and I can slice the onions now. Do I need a baking dish right away?
Yes, have a baking dish ready for later. You'll also need a pot large enough to hold the carrots and onions with enough lightly salted water to cover them.
The dish and pot are out. Should I start heating anything while I finish slicing?
Set the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can preheat while you finish the prep.
Oven is set, and the onions are sliced. The carrots and onions are going into the pot next.
Cover them with lightly salted water, just enough so the vegetables are submerged, then bring the pot to a boil.
The water is starting to bubble. How long should they cook once it is boiling?
Cook them for 5 minutes, watching for the carrots and onions to become tender but still firm rather than soft or mushy.
They still hold their shape but a fork goes in pretty easily. Is that the right point to stop?
Yes, that matches tender but firm. Drain the carrots and onions well so extra water does not carry into the baking dish.
They are drained. How should I arrange them in the dish before adding the rest?
Spread 1/2 of the drained carrots and onions evenly across the bottom of the baking dish, then keep the Cheddar cheese and butter nearby for the next layer.
I want to make Cookie Jar Gingersnaps. Can you help me get set up at the counter?
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and measure out 3/4 cup shortening and 1 cup sugar to start the dough.
Shortening and sugar are measured. Should I grab the wet ingredients too?
Yes—have 1 egg and 1/4 cup molasses ready. Those will go in after the shortening and sugar are creamed together.
I've got the egg and molasses. Do I need anything else nearby before mixing?
Keep the dry ingredients within reach too: flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt. You'll combine those separately before adding them to the creamed mixture.
My bowl is ready. How should the shortening and sugar look once I start?
Cream the shortening and sugar in the large mixing bowl until they look evenly blended and a bit lighter, with no obvious streaks of shortening.
That looks smooth now. Do I add the egg straight in?
Yes. Beat in the egg, then add the molasses and keep mixing until the dough base looks uniform.
The molasses is mixed in, and the color is even. What should I do with the dry ingredients?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt. Add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture so it blends in without making a mess.
The dough has thickened up. How do I shape the cookies?
Scoop teaspoonfuls of dough and roll each one into a ball. Set the balls aside on your prepared baking surface, keeping them fairly even in size so they bake consistently.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip for guests. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup mayonnaise, 8 ounces sour cream, 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, and 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts that have been drained and chopped.
I've got the mayo and sour cream measured, and the artichokes are drained. What dish should I use?
Use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish. You'll mix everything right in that dish, so it should be large enough to stir the dip without spilling.
Before I combine it, should the oven be on?
Yes, start preheating the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. Do I add the soup mix straight into the dairy?
Yes. In the casserole dish, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, and the garlic and mushroom soup mix until the mixture looks evenly seasoned.
That's blended. The chopped artichoke hearts are ready beside me.
Fold the drained, chopped artichoke hearts into the mixture, then add the cheese and crab meat and stir until everything is distributed through the dip.
It's all in the casserole dish now. Should I cover it with foil for baking?
Leave it uncovered. Bake it at 350 degrees F for 30 minutes.
After the 30 minutes, what should I do for serving?
Take it out carefully and serve the Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip immediately while it's hot.
I'd like to make Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches. Can you talk me through the prep while I set up my cutting board?
Absolutely. Start by getting the vegetables ready: finely chop 1 small onion, dice 1 medium tomato, chop 1 stalk of celery, and finely chop 1 green bell pepper.
The onion and tomato are cut, and I'm working on the celery and pepper. Should I turn on the oven yet?
Yes, go ahead and preheat your oven's broiler so it's hot by the time the sandwiches are assembled.
Broiler is on. I've got the chopped vegetables in separate little piles; do they all go together?
They do. Put the onion, tomato, celery, and green bell pepper into a medium bowl, then stir in the cheese, chili powder, and salt until everything is evenly combined.
The filling is mixed. It looks a little chunky from the vegetables—is that right?
Yes, that's fine for these sandwiches. You want the mixture combined, with the chopped vegetables distributed through the cheese rather than mashed smooth.
I'm ready with the bread. Should I use a tray or something closer to the broiler?
Arrange the bread slices on a baking sheet or a broiling pan, whichever you have handy and is safe for the broiler.
Bread is on the pan. How much filling should I put on each slice so they cook evenly?
Spoon 1/4 of the mixture onto each slice of bread, then spread it all the way out to the edges so the topping is even.
All the slices are topped to the edges. Anything I should check before they go under the broiler?
Make sure the bread slices are in a single layer and the topping isn't piled too high in the center. Once they're arranged neatly on the baking sheet or broiling pan, they're ready to broil.
I'm making BBQ Chuck Roast today. Can you help me set up before I open the sauces?
Absolutely. Put a large bowl on the counter and have the 1 (5 pound) chuck roast nearby. You'll also need 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer.
The roast is still wrapped, and I've got the barbeque sauce, teriyaki, and beer out. Anything else for the marinade?
Yes—grab garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt. The recipe uses those with the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, and beer to make the marinade.
My bowl is ready. Do I add the roast now or mix the liquid ingredients first?
Mix the marinade first. In the large bowl, combine the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt until everything is evenly blended.
It smells good and looks mixed. How should I get the chuck roast into it without making a mess?
Lower the roast into the bowl slowly, then turn it so the marinade coats the outside. Cover the bowl tightly before it goes into the refrigerator.
Covered and in the fridge. How long does it need, and do I just leave it alone?
Refrigerate it for six hours. Turn the roast often during that time so different sides sit in the marinade and the coating stays even.
The six hours are almost up. Should I start heating the grill before I take the meat out?
Yes, preheat an outdoor grill for indirect heat so it's ready when the roast comes out of the marinade.
The grill is heating for indirect heat. What do I do with the marinade when I pull out the roast?
Remove the roast from the marinade, then pour the marinade into a saucepan. Keep it separate from the roast as you move into the grilling stage.
I'm making Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts today. Can you talk me through the setup before I start blanching the almonds?

Absolutely. For the syrup flavoring, set out 1 cup white sugar, 1 cup water, 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons orange flower water. For the almond prep, you'll also want a pot, a strainer, baking sheets, and an oven that can hold 200 degrees F, or 95 degrees C.
I've got the sugar, water, lemon juice, orange flower water, and my almonds near the stove. How much water goes in the pot for the blanching part?
Use 6 cups of water in the pot and bring it to a full boil. Keep the almonds nearby so you can add them as soon as the pot comes off the heat.
The water is boiling now. Do I keep the burner on when the almonds go in?
No—take the pot off the heat first, then add the almonds to the hot water. That gives them a short soak without continuing to boil them hard.
They're in the hot water. Should I set a timer, and what am I looking for?
Set a timer for about 5 minutes. The skins should loosen so they'll slip off more easily when you drain them.
The timer's almost done. Do I rinse them, or just drain and peel?
Drain them, then peel the almonds once they're cool enough to handle. Pinch each almond so the skin slides off, and keep a bowl nearby for the skins.
The peeled almonds are a little damp. What should I do before they go in the oven?
Spread the almonds out on baking sheets in a single layer so moisture can escape. If they're very wet, you can blot them gently, but the recipe's drying step happens in the oven.
They're spread out. What temperature and endpoint should I use?
Bake them at 200 degrees F, which is 95 degrees C, until they're completely dry and toasted. Check occasionally and shake the pan if needed so they dry evenly without crowding.
I'm making Curried Winter Squash and already have cooked squash ready. Can you help me set it up?

Absolutely. Put a medium microwave-safe bowl on the counter and measure out 3 cups cooked, mashed winter squash. You'll also need 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder, 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
The squash is mashed and in the bowl. Should I melt the butter before adding it?

You can add the 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine directly if it's soft, since it will melt as the squash heats. If it's very cold, cut it into a few pieces so it blends in more easily.
I've got curry powder and maple syrup measured. Do they both go in with the squash now?

Yes. Stir the 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder and 2 tablespoons maple syrup into the squash, along with the butter or margarine. Mix until the curry powder is evenly worked through and you don't see dry streaks.
It's mixed, but the surface looks a little uneven from the butter pieces. Is that okay before microwaving?
That's fine. Smooth it out a bit if you like, then microwave the bowl on high until the squash is heated through, about 5 minutes.
Should I cover the bowl while it heats?
A loose microwave-safe cover or plate is helpful to prevent splatters. Leave a small gap for steam, and use caution when removing it because the squash will be hot.
It has been 5 minutes and it's steaming. What should I check before serving?
Give it a careful stir so the melted butter or margarine and maple syrup are fully incorporated. Check that it's hot all the way through; if the center is still cool, microwave briefly more.
It's hot and smooth now. The recipe mentions coconut—when would that go on?
If you want it, sprinkle coconut over the warm curried squash just before serving. Otherwise, it's ready to serve as is.
I'm making Aunt Mamies and I've got a mixing bowl out. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start?

Absolutely. Put out 1 (8 ounce) package of softened cream cheese, 1/2 cup softened butter, 2 cups all-purpose flour, and 1 cup white sugar. You'll also need milk for the saucepan step, though the recipe doesn't give a measurement for it.
The cream cheese and butter are softened. Should I use the bowl for those first?
Yes. Beat the softened cream cheese with the butter until they're well blended and smooth-looking, with no big streaks of either one left.
They're combined, but the mixture is still a little thick. Is that okay before adding flour?
That's fine. Add the 2 cups of all-purpose flour and mix it in well. It should come together into a dough rather than stay creamy.
The flour is mixed in and the dough is holding together. Do I knead it or just shape it?
No kneading is needed. Shape the dough into a ball, cover it, and chill it for 2 hours so it firms up.
It's covered and going into the fridge. While it chills, what pan should I use for the sugar part later?
Use a small or medium saucepan. When you're ready, combine the white sugar with the milk in the pan and cook it over medium heat.
After the 2 hours, do I start the saucepan right away or wait until the dough is out?
Once the dough has chilled for the full 2 hours, you can start the saucepan step. Keep the heat at medium and stir occasionally while it warms.
What am I watching for in the saucepan so I don't stop too early?
Cook the sugar and milk until the milk boils and the sugar is dissolved. Stir occasionally as it heats, and once those two things happen, that recipe step is complete.
Help me stay organized for Curried Winter Squash. What comes first? I've got cooked squash, but I want to be sure I measure everything correctly.
Absolutely. For the base, measure 3 cups cooked, mashed winter squash into a medium bowl. You'll also need 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder.
The squash is already mashed and in the bowl. Should the curry powder go straight in?
Yes, add the curry powder directly to the squash so it can be mixed evenly throughout.
Before I stir, what are the remaining ingredients?
Add 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, plus 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
The butter is still cold. Is that okay for microwaving with the squash?
That's fine. Since the mixture will be microwaved, the butter or margarine can soften and melt as it heats. Stir it in with the maple syrup as best you can.
So everything goes together in this same medium bowl?

Right. The recipe says to combine the first six ingredients in a medium bowl; with the ingredients you have listed, mix the squash, curry powder, butter or trans fat-free margarine, and maple syrup together well.
It's mixed, though I can still see a little butter. How long should I microwave it?
Microwave it on high until heated through, about 5 minutes. After heating, give it a careful stir so the melted butter blends into the squash.
It's hot now. Is there anything to add before serving?
If you'd like, sprinkle coconut on top. Then serve the Curried Winter Squash while it's warm.
I'm making Dads Best Burgers and I've got a mixing bowl out. Can you walk me through the prep without getting ahead of me?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 softened 3 ounce package of cream cheese, 1 egg, 1 medium onion finely chopped, and 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs.
Cream cheese and egg are on the counter, and I'm chopping the onion now. Should the cream cheese be really soft before I mix it?
Yes, softened cream cheese will blend more evenly. Once the onion is finely chopped, add the cream cheese, egg, onion, and dry bread crumbs to the bowl and combine them well.
The onion is in, and the crumbs are measured. The mixture looks a little thick with the cream cheese—is that okay?
That's fine for this burger mixture. Keep stirring until the egg is worked through and the onion and bread crumbs are evenly distributed.
The base is mixed. I'm ready for the meat, but I don't want to overwork it.
Crumble the beef and sausage over the mixture, then mix just until everything is combined. Use a light hand so the patties stay tender.
The meat is mixed in and it's holding together. How many patties should I make?
In this Dads Best Burgers step, shape the mixture into eight patties. Try to keep them similar in thickness so they cook at the same pace on the grill.
I've got the patties shaped. What heat should the grill be at?
Set the grill to medium-hot heat. Cook the patties uncovered for 4-6 minutes on each side.
After I flip them, what should I watch for so I know they're done?
Keep grilling until the burgers are no longer pink in the center. Once they're cooked through, take them off the grill and let them sit briefly before serving.
I'm setting up for Baked Aloha Chicken; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got chicken legs out and want to make sure I set everything up right.
Absolutely. Heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and set out an ovenproof glass baking dish for the chicken legs.
The oven is heating. For the sauce, which measured ingredients should I put near the bowl?
Measure 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup light corn syrup, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, and 1 teaspoon salt. You'll also need the ginger and corn oil called for in the sauce step.
I have the lemon juice, corn syrup, soy sauce, and salt measured. Should the sauce be mixed before the pineapple goes in?
Yes. In a bowl, stir together the lemon juice, light corn syrup, soy sauce, salt, ginger, and corn oil until the mixture looks smooth.
It's smooth now, kind of glossy. I have crushed pineapple here—do I drain it?
Don't drain it. Stir in the crushed pineapple with its liquid so the sauce keeps that sweet, tangy Aloha-style flavor.
The pineapple is mixed in. Should I grease the glass dish before adding the chicken legs?
The recipe only specifies placing the chicken legs in an ovenproof glass baking dish, so arrange them there in a single layer if you can.
They're in the dish. Do I spoon the sauce over each piece or just pour it all in?
Pour the sauce over the top of the chicken legs, letting the pineapple mixture spread across and around the pieces.
Sauce is over the chicken. Before I put it in, anything I should double-check?

Check that the oven is at 350 degrees F, the chicken legs are in the ovenproof glass dish, and the sauce includes the lemon juice, corn syrup, soy sauce, salt, ginger, corn oil, and crushed pineapple with its liquid.
I want to get Chicken with Vegetables right. What should I handle first? I've got the cooker out and want to prep things in the right order.

Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms, 4 skinless chicken drumsticks, 4 skinless chicken thighs, and 4 sliced celery ribs. You'll also need zucchini, carrots, onion, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper for the vegetables and seasoning.
The mushrooms are sliced, and the drumsticks and thighs have the skin removed. Should the chicken go in before the celery?

messages.content: I'm starting Black Bean and Corn Quesadillas and have the cans by the sink. Can you walk me through the filling and how to finish them for serving?

Keep the sweet finish around the outer edge of the quesadillas, not spread over the whole top. For the filling, set out 2 teaspoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons finely chopped onion, 1 (15.5 ounce) can black beans that are drained and rinsed, and 1 (10 ounce) can whole kernel corn that is drained.
The beans are rinsed and the corn is draining. Should I use my skillet, or is a saucepan better for this filling?
Use a large saucepan. The beans and corn will be easier to stir without spilling, and the mixture can heat evenly once the salsa goes in.
I've got the saucepan on the stove and the onion chopped fine. Do I warm the oil before adding anything else?
Yes, pour in the 2 teaspoons olive oil and heat it over medium heat until it looks glossy and moves easily across the bottom of the pan.
That edge-only sweet finish is exactly what I wanted for these. The oil is shimmering now; should the onion go in?
Add the 3 tablespoons finely chopped onion and stir it into the oil. Let it cook until softened, about 2 minutes, without trying to brown it deeply.
The onion is soft and smells sweet, but it's not browned. Is that enough before the beans?
That's enough. Stir in the drained, rinsed black beans and the drained whole kernel corn, and fold them through the onion so everything starts heating together.
The beans and corn are in the pan. It looks dry in spots, so I'm guessing the salsa goes in now?
Exactly. Add the sugar, salsa, and pepper flakes now, then mix well so the beans and corn are coated instead of sitting in separate pockets.
How vigorous should I be when stirring? I don't want to mash the beans into paste.
Use a gentle folding motion and scrape along the bottom of the saucepan. You want the beans warmed and coated, but they don't need to be crushed.
It's saucy and starting to bubble a little around the edges. How much longer should I cook it?
Cook it until heated through, about 3 minutes. Stir occasionally so the salsa clings to the beans and corn and there aren't cool spots in the middle.
The filling is hot now and smells ready. When I assemble or serve, how do I keep the sweet part from overwhelming the filling?

Spoon in the hot black bean and corn filling, then keep the sugar, glaze, or sweet topping mainly along the outside rim when you finish the quesadillas. That gives a sweet edge without covering the whole surface.
I'm making Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms and want to prep without missing anything. What should I put on the counter first?
Set out 3/4 cup melted butter, but keep it divided because you'll use part of it on the pan and part in the filling. You'll also need 1 pound fresh mushrooms with the stems removed.
Mushrooms are stemmed, and I've got the butter melted in a measuring cup. What goes into the stuffing mixture?

For the stuffing, have 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons, 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic ready. The croutons should be crushed enough to mix evenly, but they do not need to be powdery.
Before I start mixing, should I heat the oven or prep the sheet pan?
Get the oven heating to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it warms, keep your baking sheet nearby so you can butter it next.
The oven is warming. How much butter goes on the baking sheet?
Brush a large baking sheet with about 1/4 cup of the melted butter. Try to cover the area where the mushrooms will sit so they don't stick and pick up some richness underneath.
The sheet pan is buttered. Should the mushroom caps be packed tightly or spaced out?
Arrange the mushroom caps in a single layer over the baking sheet. They can sit fairly close, but keep them flat and not stacked so each cap is easy to fill.
Caps are lined up. I'm ready to make the filling—what exactly goes in the bowl?
In a medium bowl, mix the crushed seasoned croutons with the remaining 1/2 cup melted butter, then stir in the shredded mozzarella cheese, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic.
How should the filling look before I spoon it into the caps?

It should look moist and cohesive from the butter and cheese, with the seafood and croutons distributed throughout. If you see dry pockets of crouton, fold the mixture a few more times before stuffing the mushroom caps.

messages.content: I'm getting ready to make Cindis Egg Rolls and have the wok out. What should I set on the counter before I start cooking?

For the finished egg rolls, place the crunchy garnish as a narrow stripe down the middle, using small uneven bits so it adds crisp contrast without covering the tops. For the filling, set out 1 pound ground pork, 4 cups shredded cabbage, 1 large shredded carrot, and 1/2 green bell pepper cut into thin strips. You'll also want onion, garlic, ginger, cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses nearby.
I've got the pork on one side and the vegetables on the cutting board. Should any of the vegetables go together before the wok is hot?

Yes, use a large bowl for the vegetables. Mix the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, thin green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger there so the blend is ready when the pork is cooked and drained.
The vegetable bowl is ready. I still have the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses unopened—should I deal with those now or wait?
You can make that mixture now. In a small bowl, stir the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses until smooth, with no dry cornstarch left clinging to the bottom or sides.
I like that narrow middle stripe for the crunchy topping here—that's exactly what I wanted for these. I'm ready to cook the pork now; how hot should the wok be?
Run the wok over medium-high heat. Add the ground pork and cook it through, breaking it up as it browns so it mixes evenly later.
The pork is browning fast, but there's some liquid collecting around it. Should I keep cooking it in that?
Once the pork is cooked through, drain it rather than leaving that liquid in the filling. Set the drained pork aside for a moment so the egg rolls don't turn soggy.

Yes, fold the drained pork into the cabbage, carrot, green bell pepper, onion, garlic, and ginger. Mix gently so the pork gets distributed without smashing the shredded vegetables.
The bowl looks evenly mixed. The sauce mixture is smooth too—am I looking for a certain texture before filling?
Aim for filling that looks moist but not watery, with the pork spread through the vegetables and the smooth cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses mixture ready to coat evenly when you add it.
The green pepper strips look a little long compared with the cabbage. Is that a problem?

They should be thin strips, so if a few pieces feel awkward for rolling, cut them shorter. Keep the 1/2 green bell pepper dispersed through the 4 cups cabbage and the 1 large carrot so each egg roll gets a little of everything.
Everything is mixed and the filling doesn't look wet. When should I add the crunchy topping so it stays crisp?
Add it right before serving, after the egg rolls are ready. Keep it in that narrow center line and scatter the bits lightly so the surface still shows and the crunch stays fresh.

messages.content: I'm making Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style and have the squash, onion, garlic, stewed tomatoes, and some tender herbs on the counter. Can you talk me through it while I set up?

For the herbs, mince the tender leaves very small, stir some in when the tomato mixture is nearly finished, and hold a little back to sprinkle on each serving. Go ahead and preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, or 165 degrees C.
The oven is heating. My spaghetti squash is still whole, so what should I do before it goes anywhere near the pan?
Use 1 spaghetti squash. Cut it in half lengthwise, then scoop out the seeds from both halves so the centers are clean.
Squash is halved and seeded. I still need to get the topping ingredients ready—what quantities am I aiming for?
Chop 1 onion, measure 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and open 2 (14 ounce) cans of stewed tomatoes. Keep those ready as the lasagna-style topping for the squash.
I like that tiny herb cut here; that's exactly what I wanted for this dish. Should I coat the baking sheet before I put the squash on it?
Yes. Spray the baking sheet with a thin layer of cooking spray so the squash releases more easily after baking.
Pan is sprayed. Do the squash halves sit like bowls, or do I flip them over?
Flip them over so both halves are cut side down on the sprayed baking sheet.
They're on the sheet cut side down. Once the oven reaches temperature, how long should I bake them?
Bake the squash for 35 minutes in the preheated 325 degrees F oven, until a knife can be inserted easily.
While that bakes, should I start combining the onion, garlic, and tomatoes?
Yes, you can get them ready together: the chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and the 2 cans of stewed tomatoes make the savory topping for the tender squash.
The timer is close. Where should I check the squash with the knife so I don't underbake it?
Check the thickest part of the squash flesh. If the knife slides in easily, it's ready; if it resists, give it a little more time.
It's tender now. How do I pull the serving together with the tomato mixture and herbs?

Turn the squash cut side up, spoon the onion-garlic-stewed tomato mixture over the tender flesh, then fold in part of the finely minced herbs near the end. Finish each serving with the reserved fresh sprinkle.
I'm starting Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce; can you walk me through the setup? I want to get the garlic started properly before dealing with the chicken.
Absolutely. Set out 1 medium head of garlic, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, and 1/2 cup white wine so everything for the recipe is within reach.
The chicken breasts and white wine are in the fridge, and I have the garlic on the board. Should I heat the oven now?
Yes, get the oven warming to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). The garlic can be trimmed while the oven heats.
I've got a whole head of garlic. How much of the top should I cut off?
Slice off just enough from the top of the head of garlic to remove the papery tips and expose the tops of the cloves. Keep the head intact rather than separating the cloves.
The cloves are exposed, but some loose papery bits are still around the outside. Is that okay?
That's fine. Brush away any loose paper that might burn, then drizzle the exposed garlic with the 1 tablespoon olive oil so it can soak down into the cloves.
On Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce, i don't have a clay garlic roaster. What should I use instead?
Wrap the oiled garlic head in aluminum foil. The recipe allows either a clay garlic roaster or foil, and the foil will hold in enough heat and moisture for roasting.
The oven is at 400 degrees F now, and the garlic is wrapped. Where should it go?
Place the wrapped garlic in the preheated oven and roast it for 20 minutes. Set a timer so you can check the texture right when it reaches that point.
When the timer goes off, what exactly am I looking for before I move on?
Check that the cloves are soft and slip from their skins when pushed. If they do, the roasted garlic is ready for the sauce part of Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce.

messages.content: I'm starting Citrus Infused Guacamole and I've got ripe avocados on the counter. Can you talk me through the order so I don't make it watery?

With the briny add-ins, mince a little pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini and fold it through the mashed avocado mixture instead of using it as a topping. Peel, pit, and mash 2 avocados in a large bowl, and save one pit for later.
The avocados are mashed and the pit is sitting aside. Do the citrus juices go straight in now?
Yes. Stir in 1/2 tablespoon lime juice, 1/2 tablespoon orange juice, and 1/2 tablespoon pineapple juice, using a light hand so the avocado stays creamy.
I see cumin, cilantro, and salt in the instructions too. Should those wait until the end?
Add the cumin, cilantro, and salt with the citrus juices. That helps the seasoning spread evenly before any small add-ins make the dip chunkier.
I like those little pickle-caper bits mixed through the dip; that's exactly what I wanted here, not perched on top. Should I add them before I taste for salt?
Add them after the citrus and seasonings are mixed in, then fold gently. Taste after that, because capers, olives, or pickles can bring extra saltiness on their own.
I minced a few capers and a tiny bit of pickle. The guacamole looks bright but slightly loose from the juices.
Stop stirring once everything is combined. The mashed avocados will hold it together, and too much mixing can make the texture feel pasty instead of fresh.
Would hot pepper sauce clash with the orange and pineapple, or is it okay here?
It's okay if you want heat. Mix in hot pepper sauce a few drops at a time, then taste so it doesn't cover up the lime, orange, and pineapple.
I added just a few drops and it tastes good. What do I do with the saved avocado pit?
Place one avocado pit into the bowl with the guacamole. The recipe uses it to help keep the guacamole fresh while it waits.
We're not eating for about half an hour. Should I leave it out with the pit in, or chill it?
If you're not serving right away, refrigerate it until serving. Keep the pit nestled in the bowl while it chills.
When it comes out of the fridge, should I stir it again before setting it out with chips?
Give it a quick, gentle check and a small fold only if liquid has gathered at the edges. Then serve it immediately with chips or your other dippers.
I'm getting ready for Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake. Can you help me sequence the steps?
Absolutely. You'll need 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate, chopped.
I've got the flour bag open and the baking soda nearby. Should I measure the dry ingredients before turning on the oven?
You can measure them now, and also get the oven heating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the pans are prepared.
Oven is warming up. I have two round cake pans out—are these supposed to be 9 inch pans?
Yes, use 2 (9 inch) pans. Grease them well, then dust them with flour so the cake layers release cleanly later.
I'm greasing the pans now. For the chocolate, do the 6 squares need to be chopped before I start mixing dry ingredients?
Yes, chop the 6 unsweetened chocolate squares and keep them ready. For this part, the dry mixture is handled separately.
The pans are floured and the chocolate is chopped. What should I put through the sifter?
Sift together the 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Some flour is sticking in the sifter. Should I press it through or leave the clumps out?
Gently tap or stir it through so the flour, baking soda, and salt become evenly combined and lighter in texture.
The sifted dry mixture looks even now. Where should I keep it while the oven finishes heating?
Set it aside in the bowl for now, with the prepared 9 inch pans and chopped unsweetened chocolate nearby for the next stage.
I have Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip planned for today. What should I set up first? I'm getting the casserole dish and ingredients out.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream, and use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish so the dip has enough room to bake evenly.
The mayo and sour cream are measured. What should I open and prep before the oven goes on?
You'll need 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, plus 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts. Drain the artichokes well and chop them before mixing.
The artichokes are drained and chopped. Should I heat the oven now?
Start Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip by heating the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C.
Oven is heating, and I have the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish ready. Do I mix everything right in that dish?
Yes. In the casserole dish, combine the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat.
I'm folding it together now. Should the mixture be completely smooth or is some texture okay?
Some texture is fine from the artichoke hearts and crab meat. Just make sure the sour cream, mayonnaise, and soup mix are evenly blended through the dish.
Everything looks evenly mixed in the casserole. Do I cover it with foil for baking?
Bake it uncovered so the top can heat properly. Put it in the 350 degrees F oven for 30 minutes.
The timer is set for 30 minutes. Once it comes out, should it rest or go straight to the table?
Serve it immediately while it's hot and creamy.
I want to make Dads Flat Bread today. Can you guide me from setup through kneading?

Absolutely. Set out 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast, 2 cups warm water at 110 degrees to 115 degrees, 1/3 cup sugar, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also want a large mixing bowl, measuring cups and spoons, and a floured work surface ready for later.
I've got the bowl out. Since the water is divided, how much goes in with the yeast?
Pour 1/2 cup of the warm water into the large mixing bowl and sprinkle in the yeast. Stir gently so the yeast dissolves in that water before you add anything else.
The yeast is dissolved. I see sugar and oil on the counter, but what else joins the bowl at this stage?
Add the 1/3 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining warm water. Beat the mixture until it looks smooth.
I added everything and beat it. It's smooth but still more like a thick batter than dough.
That's the point where you start adding enough of the remaining all-purpose flour to make it a soft dough. Add it gradually so it firms up without becoming stiff or dry.
It's pulling together now. How soft should it feel before I stop adding flour?
Look for a dough that holds together and can be handled, but still feels tender. It should be soft rather than tight; if it's only a little tacky, that's fine.
The dough is workable. Do I knead it right in the bowl or move it?
Move it onto a floured surface. Dust the counter lightly, turn the dough out, and keep a bit of flour nearby in case it starts sticking while you work.
It's on the floured counter and sticking a little to my hands.
Knead it until it becomes smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. Use light flour as needed for sticking, but avoid working in so much that the soft dough turns heavy.
Help me stay organized for Coconut Ambrosia Salad. What comes first? I'm starting by clearing space for a big mixing bowl.
Absolutely. Set out a large bowl and make sure your fruit is drained well: you'll need 1 (11 ounce) can of mandarin oranges, drained, and 1 (8 ounce) can of crushed pineapple, drained.
Both cans are open and draining. Should I press the pineapple or just let it sit?

Let it drain thoroughly, and if it still looks very wet, give it a gentle press so the salad doesn't turn soupy. While that finishes, get 3 1/2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, and 2 cups shredded coconut ready.
The whipped topping is thawed, and I measured the coconut. Do the oranges need to stay whole?
Yes, keep the mandarin orange segments as intact as you can. They're delicate, so you'll fold them in rather than stir hard.
The bowl is ready. What should go in it first?
Add the drained mandarin oranges and drained crushed pineapple to the large bowl, then spoon in the thawed whipped topping.
Fruit and whipped topping are in. The mixture looks soft already—when does the coconut go in?
Add the 2 cups shredded coconut now, along with the marshmallows and milk called for in the recipe instructions. Fold everything together gently until it's evenly combined.
I've folded it together. It looks creamy with coconut throughout, but I don't want to overmix it.
That sounds right. Stop once there are no big streaks of whipped topping and the fruit is distributed. Cover the bowl and chill it for 1 hour before serving.
It's going into the fridge for the hour. How should I serve it when it's chilled?
After the 1 hour chill, give it a gentle spoon-through, transfer it to a serving bowl if you like, and garnish with cherries just before serving.
I'm starting Broccoli Chicken Roli; can you walk me through the setup? I've got cooked chicken ready but want to set things up in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by putting a large mixing bowl on the counter. You'll need 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat and 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli for the main filling.
The chicken is chopped, and I'm cutting the broccoli now. How small should I go with the onion and pepper?
Chop them small enough to mix evenly through the filling. Measure out 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper.
Those are measured. Do I add the vegetables to the bowl with the chicken right away?
Yes. Add the chicken, broccoli, onion, and green bell pepper to the large bowl. Then add the cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic.
Everything is in the bowl, but the mayonnaise and mustard are sitting in clumps. Should I fold it or stir hard?
Stir it thoroughly, scraping from the bottom and turning the mixture over until the chicken and vegetables are evenly coated and everything is mixed together.
The filling looks evenly coated now. Should I prep the oven before I shape or arrange anything?
Yes, get the oven heating now. Preheat it to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
Oven is heating. What pan setup do I need so it doesn't stick or make a mess?
Use a cookie sheet and cover it with aluminum foil. Press the foil flat so the surface is even and easy to work on.
The cookie sheet is lined with foil. Is there anything else I should check before putting the mixture on it?

Make sure the filling is fully combined, with no dry pockets of chicken or unmixed mayonnaise and mustard. Once the oven reaches 400 degrees F, you'll be ready to continue with the prepared foil-covered cookie sheet.

Mix until the sugar is moistened and the mixture looks smooth and glossy. Once it's even, you're ready for the next part of shaping or baking.
I want to get Curried Winter Squash right. What should I handle first? I've got cooked squash ready, but I want to make sure I measure everything right.
Absolutely. Measure out 3 cups of cooked, mashed winter squash into a medium microwave-safe bowl. You'll also need 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder.
The squash is mashed and in the bowl. Should the curry go straight in, or do I mix the sweetener and fat first?
You can add everything to the same bowl before heating: the curry powder, 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
I'm using butter. It's still cold from the fridge—is that okay for the microwave step?
Yes, that's fine. Cut or break the 2 tablespoons butter into smaller pieces so it melts more evenly into the squash as it heats.
All the ingredients are in the bowl now. How thoroughly should I stir before microwaving?
Stir until the curry powder is mostly worked through the squash and the maple syrup is distributed. It doesn't have to be perfectly smooth yet because you can stir again after heating.
The bowl is ready for the microwave. How long should I set it for?
Microwave it on high until heated through, about 5 minutes. If your microwave runs hot, you can pause partway through and give it a stir.
It's hot now, and the butter has melted in. The top looks a little uneven from stirring.
Give it one more good stir so the curry, butter, and maple syrup are evenly blended into the 3 cups of squash. Smooth the surface if you want it to look nicer for serving.
I remember there was something optional at the end. Do I need to add it?
If you'd like, sprinkle coconut over the warm squash just before serving. If not, you can simply serve it as is.
I'm making Cinnamon Chocolate Cake 2 today. What's the best place to start? I want to get my bowl and ingredients set up correctly.
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl for the dry ingredients. Measure in 2 cups all-purpose flour and 2 cups sugar.
The flour and sugar are in the bowl. I'm checking the spice and salt next—how much of each goes in?
Add 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon salt to that same bowl, then stir those first four ingredients together so they're evenly combined.
The dry mix looks even. Should I start something on the stove now?
Yes. In a saucepan, combine the water, oil, butter, and cocoa. Put it over medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil.
It's heating now. Do I need to whisk it while the butter melts?
Give it an occasional stir so the cocoa blends in and the butter melts smoothly. Once it reaches a boil, take it to the dry ingredients.
The cocoa mixture just boiled. I've got the bowl of dry ingredients beside me—what's the safest way to add it?
Carefully pour the hot saucepan mixture over the dry ingredients in the bowl, then mix well until the batter looks smooth and no dry pockets remain.
The batter is smooth and warm. I still have eggs, buttermilk, vanilla, and baking soda waiting.
Add the eggs, buttermilk, vanilla, and baking soda to the bowl. Mix well again so everything is fully incorporated.
It's mixed together now. What should the batter look like before I move on?
It should look evenly blended, chocolatey, and pourable, with the cinnamon and salt already mixed through from the dry bowl. Scrape the sides and bottom once more to catch anything unmixed.

For the briny add-ins, chop any pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini very fine and stir them into the sauce as small bright flecks. Grease a 13-in baking dish, then keep a saucepan handy for the sauce.
The dish is greased. Should the burritos thaw first, or do they go in as they are?
Use them straight from frozen. Arrange all 6 frozen prepared bean and cheese burritos in the greased baking dish, then set the dish aside while you work on the sauce.
They're lined up snugly in the dish. I've got the saucepan on the burner—am I starting with butter or margarine?
Yes, start with 2 tablespoons butter or margarine in the saucepan over medium heat. Let it melt gently, stirring just enough to keep it from browning.
The butter is melted and a little foamy. Is the flour next?
Stir in 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour. Keep stirring until there are no dry patches and the mixture looks like a smooth, soft paste.
I like the little briny bits running through the sauce—that's exactly what I wanted. The paste is thick now; how do I add the water without making lumps?
Add the 1 3/4 cups water gradually, stirring the whole time. A slow pour lets the flour mixture loosen evenly instead of clumping.
I've added about half the water, and it's smoothing out but still feels tight. Keep going the same way?
Keep adding the remaining water a little at a time while stirring. Scrape around the bottom and corners of the pan so the sauce stays even.
All the water is in now, and the sauce looks thin and pale. Should I turn the heat up?
Bring it to a boil while stirring. Once it's bubbling, cook and stir for 2 minutes, or until the sauce thickens.
It thickened after the 2 minutes and coats the spoon. Does it go straight over the burritos?
Yes, pour the thickened sauce evenly over the burritos in the 13-in dish. Try to cover the tops and let some run down between the burritos.
I'm serving them shortly. Anything I should check before they hit the plates?
Make sure the sauce is smooth, glossy, and coating the burritos well. Let the dish sit for a minute so the sauce settles, then serve while everything is hot.

messages.content: I'm starting Apple Blueberry Tarts and have two medium bowls on the counter. Can you talk me through the setup?

For the briny add-in, mince the caper or pepperoncini very finely, then fold it into the fruit filling so it comes through as tiny pops rather than chunks. For the tart filling, gather 2 medium cooking apples, 2/3 cup fresh or frozen blueberries, 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute, and 1/2 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice.
The apples are peeled, cored, and chopped. My blueberries are frozen but loose, not stuck together.
Loose frozen berries can go straight in. Add the chopped apples and the 2/3 cup blueberries to one medium bowl, and keep the other bowl dry for the pastry mixture.
I like that little briny pop worked into the filling; that's exactly what I wanted for these tarts. The fruit is sitting in the first bowl now.

Sprinkle the fruit with 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute and 1/4 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice. Toss gently so the apples and blueberries are coated without crushing the berries, then set that bowl aside.
The filling is mixed and resting. I'm ready to deal with the dry ingredients in the second bowl.
Add the whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice to the second medium bowl. Stir until the salt and spice look evenly dispersed through the flour.
The flour mixture looks even. I'm not sure whether to pack it down or leave it fluffy before adding liquids.
Leave it fluffy. If there are any compacted spots, break them up with the fork so the oil and milk can moisten the flour evenly.
Okay, the dry bowl is loosened up. Should the oil and milk go in separately?
Add the oil and milk all at once to the flour mixture. Pour them over the surface rather than into one tight spot, then use a fork to start bringing the dough together.
It's starting to clump, but the edges still look shaggy and there's flour showing at the bottom.
Keep using the fork and stir lightly. Scrape from the bottom, lift, and fold toward the center just until the dough comes together.
The dough is mostly holding, but I'm tempted to knead it a little so it looks smoother.
Skip kneading here. A slightly rough dough is fine; stop once it holds together so the tart pastry stays tender instead of getting tough.
Got it. The dough is together, the fruit bowl is off to the side, and I need to pause before shaping.
Keep the filling and dough in separate bowls, scrape off the fork, and clear loose flour from the work area. When you come back, you'll be set up cleanly for shaping the Apple Blueberry Tarts.
I want to get Asparagus Sandwiches right. What should I handle first? I've got the canned asparagus out, but I'm not sure how dry it needs to be.
Absolutely. You'll want 1 (10 ounce) can of asparagus tips, drained. Lay the spears on paper towels for a few minutes so the extra liquid is absorbed; that keeps the sandwiches from getting soggy.
They're draining now. While that sits, what should I mix for the spread?
In a small bowl, stir together 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons finely chopped onion, and 1 pinch seasoning salt until the onion is evenly mixed through.
Should the onion be almost minced, or is a rough chop fine here?
Go fairly fine with it. Since the spread goes on thinly, small pieces of onion will roll up more neatly and won't tear the bread.
The spread is mixed. Do I need to toast the bread or leave it soft?
Leave the bread soft for this recipe. Trim off the crusts from the bread slices so they'll roll more easily.
While working on Asparagus Sandwiches, crusts are off. How much of the mayonnaise mixture should go on each slice?
Spread it thinly over each slice—just enough to coat the surface. Too much filling can squeeze out when you roll the sandwiches.
The asparagus tips look a little fragile. How should I place them without breaking them?
Set one asparagus spear onto a prepared bread slice gently, keeping it near one edge so you can roll the bread around it without pressing too hard.
I've rolled a couple. Any serving or cleanup tip before I finish the rest?
Keep rolling each slice around a spear, then place the rolls seam-side down on a serving plate. Wipe up any extra moisture from the paper towels and bowl area so the sandwiches stay tidy and dry.

messages.content: Today I'm turning Gelatin Fruit Salad toward a breakfast-style muffin or quick bread with fruit and warm spices. Which spices should go in?
Go with cinnamon and ginger; skip the cardamom.
Perfect for today. Before I heat anything, what needs to be on the counter and opened?
Set out 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple, undrained.
I've got the saucepan out and the applesauce measured. Does the pineapple get drained?
Keep the pineapple undrained. Pour the 1 cup applesauce into the saucepan and bring it to a boil.
The applesauce is bubbling. Should I keep the burner on while adding the gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat, then stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin until the granules are fully dissolved.
It's smooth and glossy now. I'm worried the soda will foam up if I pour too fast.
Add the lemon-lime soda slowly from the 12 ounce can, stirring gently so the mixture stays under control.
The soda is in. When do I add the crushed pineapple?
Stir in the whole 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple, including its juice, until it's evenly spread through the gelatin mixture.
What dish should I use for chilling, and do I cover it right away?
Pour the mixture into your serving dish or mold, let the surface settle for a moment, then cover it and refrigerate it.
How do I know it's ready to serve with the breakfast spread?
It's ready when the gelatin is firm all the way through. Keep it refrigerated until serving.
Can you help me get started on Date Loaf Cake? I want to make sure I have everything measured before I turn on the oven.
Absolutely. For this Date Loaf Cake, measure out 1 cup dates, pitted and chopped, and 1 cup dark brown sugar. Keep them near a large mixing bowl.
Dates are chopped and the brown sugar is ready. What else should be on the counter?
You'll also need 1/4 cup margarine and 1 cup boiling water. Since the water needs to be boiling, you can start a kettle or small pot now.
The kettle is on, and I have a 9x5 inch loaf pan. Should I heat the oven yet?
Start Date Loaf Cake by heating the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C.
Oven is heating. Do I need to prep the pan before mixing the dates?
Go ahead and grease and flour the 9x5 inch loaf pan so it's ready when the mixture is done standing.
The pan is greased and floured. My water just boiled—what goes into the bowl?
In the large bowl, combine the chopped dates, dark brown sugar, margarine, and the 1 cup boiling water. Stir just enough to bring everything together and help the margarine start melting.
It's mixed, and the margarine is melting into the hot water. Is it supposed to sit before anything else happens?
Yes. Let the mixture stand for 15 minutes. That gives the dates time to soften in the hot liquid.
While it stands, should I be watching for a particular texture or just the timer?
Use the 15-minute timer as your guide. By the end, the dates should look plumper and the mixture should be warm rather than freshly boiling.
I pulled up Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got my skillet out and want to prep things in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 12 ounces chopped raw bacon, 1 small white onion chopped, 5 button mushrooms chopped, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef.
The bacon is chopped already, and I'm dicing the onion now. Should I turn the oven on before I start the skillet?
Yes, go ahead and heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready when the meatloaf needs to go in.
Oven is heating. For the bacon, should I use medium heat or start hotter to crisp it faster?
Use medium heat. Put the chopped raw bacon in the skillet and cook it until the pieces are browned, stirring as needed so they brown evenly.
The bacon is sizzling and giving off a lot of grease. What texture am I looking for before I pull it out?
Look for browned pieces rather than pale or soft ones. Once the bacon is browned, lift it out with a slotted spoon and transfer it to paper towels.
I have a plate lined with paper towels ready. Do I leave the skillet on the heat while I remove the bacon?
You can keep it on medium briefly while you scoop carefully, but if it's sputtering a lot, lower the heat or slide the pan off the burner while you transfer the bacon.
Bacon is draining now, and the skillet has a deep layer of fat. How much should stay in the pan?
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon grease. Keep just that small amount in the skillet for the next cooking stage.
Got it. I'll measure off about 1 tablespoon and clear the rest. Should the onion, mushrooms, and beef stay nearby?
Yes, keep the chopped onion, chopped button mushrooms, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef close by so you're ready to continue once the skillet is set.
Can you help me put together Easy Punch for a group? I'm setting out a large punch bowl now.
Absolutely. For the base, have ready 4 packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder, each 0.13 ounce, plus 2 cans of pineapple juice, 46 fluid ounces each.
The drink mix and pineapple juice are on the counter. What else should I measure before I start pouring?
Measure out 3 cups of white sugar and 4 quarts of water. Once those are ready, you'll have the main mixture covered.
I've got the sugar measured and the water in a pitcher. Should everything go straight into the punch bowl?
For this batch of Easy Punch, add the strawberry drink mix powder, pineapple juice, white sugar, and water to the large punch bowl.
The powder is floating a bit on top. Do I need to worry about the order, or just stir it in?
Just stir thoroughly. Keep going until the drink mix and sugar are dissolved so the punch looks evenly blended with no gritty sugar at the bottom.
It's turning a uniform pink-red now, but I can still feel a little sugar when I drag the spoon along the bowl.
Give it another minute of steady stirring, scraping across the bottom and around the sides of the bowl to help the last sugar dissolve.
That smoothed out. The recipe mentions ginger ale—when should I add it?
Here, stir in the ginger ale after the sugar and drink mix have dissolved. Pour it in gently so you keep some of the fizz.
Should I serve it right away, or can it sit while guests arrive?
You can serve it right away once the ginger ale is mixed in. If it needs to wait, keep it chilled and give it a light stir before serving.

Perfect. Before I heat the pot, tell me what needs to be on the counter.
Set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 2 skinless chicken leg quarters, 1/2 cup chopped onion, 2 quarts water, and the chicken bouillon.
I've got the large pot out, plus the oil and chicken. How hot should I start it?
Put the pot over medium heat, add the vegetable oil, then cook the chicken pieces until they're browned on both sides.
The chicken is browning now. Does the onion wait until after both sides have color?
Yes. Once both sides are browned, stir in the 1/2 cup chopped onion and let it cook with the chicken for 2 minutes more.
The onion has softened a bit and the pot smells good. What liquid goes in?
Pour in the 2 quarts water along with the chicken bouillon, then bring the pot up to a boil.
Once it boils, am I keeping it rolling hard or backing it down?
Back the heat down and let it simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Since I'm serving it as a wrap filling, should I add the crunchy center layer while the soup is simmering?
No—keep the crunchy topping dry until assembly, then add those larger pieces in the center layer of each wrap or taco.
After the 45 minutes, what's the best way to keep the filling from making the wrap soggy?
Use the cooked chicken and onion as the main filling, letting excess broth drain off before wrapping, then add the crunchy middle layer right before serving.

I want to make Fire Side Coffee mix for a jar. Can you guide me while I measure everything?
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl, a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, and a clean jar with a lid. Measure 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer and 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix into your prep area.
Those two are measured. The creamer is a little clumpy—does that matter?
A few clumps are fine because you'll sift the dry ingredients together. Before that, add 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon to the lineup.
Coffee and cinnamon are ready. Should I sift into the bowl all at once or in batches?

Sift them into the bowl in batches if your strainer is small: creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, cinnamon, and nutmeg if you're including it from the recipe directions. Tap the strainer gently so the mixture turns evenly powdery.
I've sifted it, and the color looks pretty even. Do I need to stir after sifting?
Yes, give it a brief stir with a spoon or whisk to make sure the coffee granules and cinnamon are evenly distributed through the lighter powders.
The dry mix looks blended now. I have a quart jar—can I transfer it?
Go ahead and pour the mixture into the jar. Use a funnel or folded parchment if you want less mess, then seal it tightly with the lid so the powder stays dry.
The jar is sealed. How do I make one mug from it?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Mix until it dissolves as much as possible and the drink looks smooth.
I stirred 3 teaspoons into my mug, and it smells good. What if I want it stronger or creamier?
Adjust to taste: add a little more mix for a stronger, sweeter cup, or dilute with extra hot water if it's too intense. Keep the remaining mix sealed in the jar between servings.

Keep the 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour in the large bowl and make sure there's enough room in the center for the liquids.

Make a well in the center of the flour, then pour in the foamy yeast mixture and the 1 1/4 cups cold water.
Got it. And for the skillet part later, I'm still leaving out the chopped briny pieces, right?
Right—when you warm the skillet version, use just that spoonful of brine in the pan and leave the solid briny bits out.

messages.content: I'm setting up outside for Deep Fried Turkey and want to get the gear and ingredients organized before anything gets hot.

Keep the sweet finishing glaze or topping in a narrow ring around the outside of the turkey instead of coating the whole bird. For the setup, have a large stockpot or turkey fryer, peanut oil, the 12 pound turkey, Creole seasoning, 1 white onion, paper towels, and a large platter ready.
That helps. How much oil should I plan for, and what size turkey is this recipe built around?
Plan on 3 gallons of peanut oil for frying, or the amount your fryer safely needs, and use 1 whole turkey, about 12 pounds, with the neck and giblets removed.
I've got the fryer on a level spot outside. Before I unwrap the bird, what should I put within reach?
Set out 1/4 cup Creole seasoning and 1 white onion, then keep a big stack of paper towels close by. The turkey has to be rinsed and patted very dry before it gets near the oil.
I like having that sweet finish only around the outside edge; that's exactly what I wanted for this turkey. Do I start heating the peanut oil now?
Yes. Pour the peanut oil into the turkey fryer or large stockpot, making sure you leave room for the turkey, then heat it to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C.
The thermometer is clipped on. How cautious should I be about the oil level while it heats?
Be very cautious: the pot needs enough empty space for the 12 pound turkey to displace the oil. If it's filled too high, the oil can spill over when the turkey goes in.
While the oil is coming up, I want the landing area ready. What should I use for the platter?
Line a large platter with food-safe paper bags so the turkey has a safe place to land after frying.
The platter is lined, and the turkey is unwrapped. What do I check inside before rinsing it?
Check the cavity and remove the neck and giblets if they are still there. After that, rinse the turkey.
It's rinsed. The skin still feels damp in a few spots near the wings and cavity.
Pat it thoroughly dry with paper towels, taking extra time around the wings, legs, skin folds, and inside the cavity. Dry skin is especially important for deep frying.
The turkey is dry now, and I have the Creole seasoning and onion beside it. Anything else before I move it toward the fryer?

Keep the 1/4 cup Creole seasoning and the 1 white onion with the turkey for the final prep, then do a safety check: oil at 400 degrees F or 200 degrees C, platter lined, fryer not overfilled, and the turkey completely dry.
