Measure 2 cups sugar and 2 cups all-purpose flour into the dry-base area. Add 2 teaspoons baking powder and 1/4 teaspoon salt with them, but don't stir in the dates and nuts yet unless they're already chopped and ready.

Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla to the bowl now. Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened; the batter is supposed to be very stiff, so stop once there are no obvious dry pockets.

A normal greased 15-in pan is fine. Scrape the batter in, then press and spread it evenly toward the edges and corners rather than trying to make it perfectly glossy.

Small ridges are fine. Aim for an even thickness across the pan so the bars bake at the same pace and the top can turn golden brown.

Bake the Date Nut Bars at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes, until they're golden brown. Let them settle briefly after baking before cutting so the stiff batter sets into clean bars.
I'm making Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts today. Can you help me set up the syrup ingredients before I start on the almonds?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup water for the syrup base, and keep a small saucepan handy.

Yes—measure 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice and 2 tablespoons orange flower water. Those will give the syrup brightness and its floral note.
Great. I've got a pot ready for the almonds too. How much water should I heat?
Bring 6 cups of water to a full boil. Use a pot with enough room so the almonds can go in without splashing.
The water is boiling. Do I keep it on the burner when I add the almonds?
Take the pot off the heat first, then add the almonds to the hot water.

Let the almonds soak for about 5 minutes. After soaking, drain them, then peel off the skins while they're still manageable to handle.
I'm peeling them now. Should I prep the oven and baking sheets while I finish?
Yes. Spread the peeled almonds on baking sheets in a single layer, and set the oven to 200 degrees F, which is 95 degrees C.
Once they're on the sheets, how do I know when to pull them out?
Bake them at 200 degrees F or 95 degrees C until they are completely dry and toasted. Check occasionally and shake the pan gently so they dry evenly.

Drain off the fat from the skillet, then transfer the beef and onion mixture into the slow cooker.
It's in the slow cooker. I'm looking at the rest of the ingredients—what all gets stirred in now?

Stir in the mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans with their liquid, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce. Mix well so the tomato paste and barbeque sauce spread through the chili.
Should the kidney bean liquid really stay in? I don't want it too dry.
Yes, keep the kidney beans with liquid as written. That liquid helps loosen the chili base, especially with the tomato paste and beans in the slow cooker.
Everything is mixed in. How do I adjust the heat at the end?

Season it with hot sauce and more crushed red pepper, adding a little at a time and tasting as you go. Once the heat level tastes right, let the slow cooker carry the chili until the vegetables are tender and the flavors come together.
I want to make Cinnamon Crackle Cookies. Can you talk me through the setup without racing ahead?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're easy to cream together.
Those are on the counter. Which sugars go into the bowl with them?
Use 1 cup sugar plus 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Add both to the mixing bowl with the butter and shortening.
I've got a mixing bowl ready. Do I just stir, or should this be beaten?
Beat or cream the butter, shortening, and both sugars together until the mixture looks well blended and a bit lighter.
It's combined and looks creamy. What should I add from here?
In this Cinnamon Crackle Cookies step, add the egg and the extracts, then mix well so they're fully worked into the creamed mixture.
That's mixed in. I see the dry ingredients waiting—how should I handle them?
Combine the next eight ingredients separately, then add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture rather than dumping it in all at once.
The dough is coming together. Should I keep mixing until it's completely smooth?
Mix just until the dry ingredients are incorporated and the dough holds together; you don't need to keep beating it after that.
Ready to shape them. What size should the cookies be, and do I grease the pans?
Shape the dough into 1-in balls, roll each one in sugar, and arrange them spaced apart on ungreased baking sheets.
I want to make Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup. Can you stay with me while I prep and cook it?
For Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup, set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 medium onion chopped, 1 green bell pepper chopped, and 1 large carrot peeled and thinly sliced.
The onion and pepper are chopped, and the carrot is sliced. Do I need a big pot for this?
Yes, use a large pot. Pour in the vegetable oil and warm it over medium heat.
The oil is heating. Should it be shimmering before I add the vegetables?
A light shimmer is perfect. Add the onion, green bell pepper, carrot, and garlic, then stir so everything gets coated in the oil.
They're in the pot. How long should I cook them before adding beans?
Cook the vegetables for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they look tender and the onion has softened.
The vegetables are softer now and smell good. Which beans go in whole?
Stir in 1 can of black beans along with the chicken broth, keeping the heat at medium so the soup starts coming together.
That's mixed in. I still have another can of black beans—what should I do with it?
Put the remaining can of beans in a blender and puree it until smooth. That puree will help thicken the soup.
The puree is smooth. Should I add it back to the pot right away?
Yes, scrape the smooth bean puree into the pot and stir it in well. Let the soup heat through, then taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.

Have 6 beaten eggs ready, along with 2 1/4 cups milk.

Measure out 1/3 cup white sugar and keep 1 teaspoon vanilla extract nearby for the batch.

Start by putting the beaten eggs, the milk, and the 1/3 cup sugar into a large saucepan. Hold the vanilla for later since the cooking step uses those three together.

Use medium heat and stir steadily so the egg mixture warms evenly instead of scrambling.

Keep cooking and stirring until the mixture coats a metal spoon; that's the sign to stop heating.

For Eggnog II, take the saucepan off the heat right away.

Set the pan in the sink or a bowl of ice water and stir for 1 to 2 minutes so it cools quickly, then portion it into the small bowls.
I'm about to start Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Have 1 pound fresh mushrooms ready with the stems removed, and keep 3/4 cup melted butter nearby because it gets divided during prep.
The caps are cleaned and the stems are out. How should I set up the pan?
bring the oven up to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), then grab a large baking sheet for the mushroom caps.
Oven is heating, and the baking sheet is on the counter. Do I butter it before the mushrooms go on?
Yes. Brush the large baking sheet with about 1/4 cup of the melted butter so the caps have a rich base and do not stick.
The pan is buttered. Should the mushrooms be crowded together or spaced out?
Arrange the mushroom caps in a single layer over the baking sheet. They can sit close, but keep them from stacking so each cap can hold filling evenly.
They're in one layer. What goes into the stuffing bowl?
In a medium bowl, add 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons, 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, the remaining 1/2 cup melted butter, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic.
While working on Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms, should I stir that gently or really mash it together?
Mix it until the croutons are moistened with butter and the mozzarella, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic are evenly distributed. Try not to crush it into a paste.
The filling looks combined and still a little chunky. Is that the right point to start stuffing the caps?
Yes, that texture is right for stuffing. Spoon the mixture into the prepared mushroom caps on the buttered baking sheet, keeping the filling tucked into each cap so they're ready for the oven.
I'm getting ready for Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers. Can you help me sequence the steps?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, 1 small chopped onion, and 1 egg so the filling mixture is ready to come together.
Cheddar, Parmesan, onion, and the egg are on the counter. Should I get the grill going before mixing?
Yes, preheat the grill for high heat now. While it heats, grab a large bowl for the burger mixture.
The grill is heating and I have a large bowl out. What goes into it first?
Add the Cheddar cheese, Parmesan cheese, chopped onion, egg, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper to the bowl, then mix until everything is evenly combined.
That mixture is stirred together. The onion pieces are spread through it pretty well.
Good. Crumble the ground beef into the bowl so it breaks up easily instead of landing in one dense piece.
The beef is crumbled in. Should I use a spoon, or is hands better here?
Use your hands for this part and mix just until the beef and seasoned cheese mixture are combined. Try not to overwork it, so the burgers stay tender.
It looks evenly mixed and still a little loose. How many patties am I shaping?
Shape the mixture into 6 patties, making them as even as you can so they grill at the same pace.
I have 6 patties formed. Where does the bacon come in?
Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty, securing it snugly so it stays in place on the hot grill. Once all 6 are wrapped, they're ready to cook.
Barbecued Shredded Beef is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I want to get the setup right before anything goes in the oven.

Absolutely. You'll need a 3 pounds beef roast, 2 chopped onions, 2 cans or bottles of beer that are 12 fluid ounces each, and 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce. Have a large roasting pan and a large bowl ready too.
I have the roast and onions out. Should I prep the oven before I open the beer and sauce?
Yes, get the oven heating to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C. That low heat is right for gently cooking the beef.
The oven is preheating. Do I need to brown the roast first, or does it go straight into the pan?
For this recipe, place the roast straight into a large roasting pan. Scatter the chopped onions over the top and around it.
Roast is in the pan with the onions. What should I mix in the bowl?
In the large bowl, combine the Worcestershire sauce with liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir those together so the seasonings are evenly mixed.
I've mixed that seasoning base. Do the 2 beers go into the bowl or directly over the meat?
Pour the beer into the bowl with the Worcestershire mixture, stir it together, then add that liquid to the roasting pan.
When I pour it in, should I aim over the onions and roast, or just around the sides?
Pour it into the pan so it reaches the roast and onions, but don't worry about coating every spot perfectly. The beer and seasoning mixture will surround the beef as it cooks.
Everything is in the roasting pan now. Anything I should check before it goes into the 275 degree oven?

Make sure the roast is settled in the large roasting pan, the chopped onions are scattered over it, and the beer mixture has been added. Once that's set, put the pan in the preheated 275 degrees F oven.
I want to put together the Double Fudge Brownie Mix. Can you help me set up the ingredients and jar?
In this Double Fudge Brownie Mix step, set out a clean 1 quart or 1 liter jar, then measure 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.
The jar is clean and dry. Should I combine everything in a bowl first or keep the layers separate?
Keep them separate for this mix. Layer the ingredients in the jar in the order listed: white sugar, unsweetened cocoa powder, all-purpose flour, then chopped pecans.
The sugar is in, but the cocoa is making the side of the jar dusty. Is that okay?
Yes, that is fine. If you want neater layers, tap the jar gently on the counter after adding the cocoa powder so it settles before you add the flour.
I've added the cocoa and flour. The jar is getting close to full; do the pecans still go on top?
Yes, add the 1 cup chopped pecans on top as the final layer. If needed, spoon them in slowly and lightly level them without packing everything down too hard.
The layers are done. What should I write for the tag?
Attach a tag that says: bring the oven up to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Is that the only baking direction included with this mix recipe?
Yes. The recipe you're using gives the jar-layering directions and that preheat instruction for the attached tag; it does not provide additional mixing or baking details.
Got it. How should I close it up so it's ready to give away?
Seal the jar tightly, keep the tag attached where it is easy to read, and store the brownie mix in a cool, dry spot until you are ready to gift or use it.

messages.content: I'm serving Coconut Ambrosia Salad as a plated dinner tonight, with garnishes or little finishing touches available. What's the cleanest way to finish the plate?
Choose a single garnish and set it a little off-center.
That works for tonight. I've drained a 1 (11 ounce) can of mandarin oranges and a 1 (8 ounce) can of crushed pineapple—should anything else be measured before I mix?
Yes. Have 3 1/2 cups thawed frozen whipped topping and 2 cups shredded coconut ready, plus the marshmallows and milk called for when everything gets combined.
The whipped topping is thawed, and the coconut is measured. Do I need a particular bowl for this?
Use a large bowl so the fruit, whipped topping, coconut, marshmallows, and milk can fold together without crushing the oranges.
I've got the large bowl out. Should the oranges and pineapple go in before the whipped topping?
Add the drained mandarin oranges and drained crushed pineapple to the bowl first, then spoon in the thawed whipped topping.
They're in the bowl. I'm worried about making it soupy—how should I mix?
Fold gently rather than stirring hard, then add the shredded coconut, marshmallows, and milk and keep folding until everything is evenly coated.
It looks combined now, with the fruit still mostly intact. Is it ready to plate?
Chill it for 1 hour before serving so the mixture firms up and the flavors settle.
While it chills, should I prep the cherries or wait until serving?
Prep the cherries now, but don't place them until you're ready to serve so the finish stays neat.
It has chilled for 1 hour, and I'm plating individual portions. How do I apply the finish?
Spoon the salad onto each plate, then garnish with cherries—keep to one cherry per plate and place it off-center.
I'm ready to cook Chicken Tortilla Soup IV. What should be ready before I begin? I'm setting out the pot and ingredients now.

Absolutely. For this recipe, have 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil, 6 corn tortillas that are 6 inches each, 3 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready. Cut the tortillas into 1/2 inch strips before you start heating anything.
The tortillas are sliced into strips. Should I put all the oil in the pot at once?
Not all at once. Pour 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil into a large pot and warm it over medium heat. Keep the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of oil nearby for the second batch of tortilla strips.
The oil is heating in the large pot. How do I know when to add the strips?
Once the oil looks hot and loose in the pot, add only half of the tortilla strips. Stir them often so they crisp evenly instead of sitting in one spot.
I added half, and they're starting to firm up. Am I looking for browned edges or just crispness?
Go for crisp tortilla strips; light browning is fine, but don't let them scorch. Keep stirring often until they feel crisp enough to hold their shape.
They look crisp now. Where should I put them so they don't get oily?
Lift them out of the pot and drain them on paper towels. Spread them out a bit so they stay crisp while you cook the remaining strips.
The first batch is draining. There's not much oil left in the pot.
That's when you use the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of vegetable oil. Add it to the pot over medium heat, then cook the remaining tortilla strips the same way, stirring often until crisp.
Second batch is crisp too. Do I mix these into the broth and cumin yet?

For the steps you're on, set the crisp tortilla strips aside after draining them. Keep the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready for the soup, but the tortilla-strip prep is complete.
I'm ready to cook Aaahh Potato Soup. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a pot out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 2 Yukon Gold potatoes, cubed, plus 1 (5.5 ounce) package of au gratin instant potato mix. Those will be the base of the soup.
The potatoes are cubed and the au gratin mix is open. What liquids should I have ready?
You'll need 1 (10.5 ounce) can of condensed chicken broth and 1 1/2 cups water. Keep a little extra water nearby in case the potatoes aren't fully covered once everything is in the pot.
Should I add the potato mix dry, or prepare it separately like the package says?
Add it dry right into the large saucepan or pot with the cubed potatoes, condensed chicken broth, and measured water. Stir it together so the mix starts dispersing into the liquid.
It looks a bit thick already. The potatoes are not quite covered in the pot.
Pour in just enough additional water to cover the potatoes if necessary. Don't flood it; you only need enough so the potatoes can simmer evenly.
What heat should I use, and do I need to stand there stirring the whole time?
Cook it over medium heat, stirring occasionally. Let it go until the potato cubes are tender, which should take about 40 minutes.
How do I check that the potatoes are tender without overcooking the soup?

Pierce a potato cube with a fork; it should slide in easily without the cube feeling hard in the center. If the soup thickens too much before they're tender, stir in a splash of water and keep it at medium heat.
The potatoes are soft now. What's the last thing to do before serving?
Stir in the cream and heat the soup through gently. Once it's hot and evenly creamy, give it a final stir and serve it warm.

messages.content: For Easy Punch today, I want to serve it more like a mixed platter with separate-looking parts instead of one totally uniform bowl. How should I arrange it for this batch?
For this one, bring the punch together with a light hand, and hold back one colorful part so you can lay it over the top in a clean visible stripe right before serving.
Great, I only want that look for this serving. What should I pull out first?

Start with the main flavor base: 4 (0.13 ounce) packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder and 2 (46 fluid ounce) cans of pineapple juice. Use a large punch bowl and a long spoon so you can stir without splashing.
I've got the punch bowl and the pineapple juice open. What else belongs on the counter?
Set out 3 cups white sugar and 4 quarts water. Also keep the ginger ale chilled nearby, because it gets stirred in after the base is dissolved.
Since I'm trying to keep it from looking muddy, should I add everything at once?

Combine the drink mix, pineapple juice, sugar, and water in the large punch bowl, but pour gently and stir from the bottom with slow sweeps. That gives you the recipe mixture while keeping the presentation from looking overworked.
The sugar is settling at the bottom. What texture or look tells me it is ready?
Keep stirring until the sugar and drink mix are dissolved. You should not feel gritty sugar under the spoon, and the liquid should look evenly colored before you move on.
Where does the reserved stripe fit in with the ginger ale?
Once the base is dissolved, keep the reserved colorful portion aside for the topping. Stir in the ginger ale gently at the end so the bubbles stay lively.
I'm using a shallow serving bowl, so I'm worried the top stripe will disappear when people ladle it.
After the ginger ale is in, stop stirring. Pour or spoon the reserved stripe across the surface in one band, then leave it alone so it stays distinct for the first presentation.
Any last serving tip before I bring it out?
Serve it right away while the ginger ale is still fizzy. Place the ladle at the side of the bowl rather than through the stripe, so the top stays neat until guests start serving themselves.

Perfect, that's exactly how I want to handle this one. I've got my cutting board out—what potato prep comes first?
Peel and cube 6 Yukon Gold potatoes, then peel and cube 2 sweet potatoes. Keep the pieces fairly even so they cook at the same pace.

For Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds, yes, put the Yukon Gold potatoes and sweet potatoes into the large pot together, then add enough water to cover them.

Set the burner high and bring the water to a boil. Keep an eye on it so it doesn't foam over once it gets active.
It's starting to bubble hard around the edges and center.
Once it reaches a full boil, remove the pot from the heat and drain the potatoes and sweet potatoes in the colander.
They're drained and steaming. Do I use the butter and cream now or wait?
Keep the butter and heavy cream ready for combining with the hot potatoes, but stay with the recipe's next listed move before the broiler step.
All right, I'm near the oven. What's the last thing I need to do from the recipe?
Preheat the oven broiler so it's ready for the finishing stage.
I'm making Fire Side Coffee today. What's the best place to start? I'm setting out the dry ingredients now.

Absolutely. Put out a large mixing bowl, a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, and a clean jar with a tight lid. For the mix, you'll need 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
I've got the creamer and hot chocolate mix measured. Should the coffee granules go in whole, or do they need crushing first?
Use the instant coffee granules as they are. Add the 1 1/2 cups to the bowl with the creamer and hot chocolate mix, then add the 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
Everything is in the bowl. It looks a little clumpy from the creamer.
That's fine for this kind of mix. Sift the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, cinnamon, and nutmeg together so the powder becomes more even and the larger clumps break up.
I'm sifting it now. Some coffee granules are staying in the strainer—should I force them through?
Gently press them through with the back of a spoon if they'll break down easily. If a few bits remain, stir them back into the sifted mixture so the coffee flavor stays in the batch.
The mixture is blended and smells like mocha cinnamon. What kind of container should I use?
Pour the dry mix into a clean, dry jar, then seal it with a lid. A tight seal helps keep moisture out so the powder stays scoopable.
Jar is filled. I want to make one mug now—how much mix goes into the water?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Stir well so the creamer, cocoa, and coffee dissolve evenly.
I mixed a cup, but I might want it a little stronger. Is that okay?
Yes. Taste it and adjust to taste—add a bit more mix for a stronger, sweeter cup, or add more hot water if you want it lighter.
I want to make German Sweet Chocolate Pie. Can you help me set up without jumping too far ahead?
Absolutely. Put a large microwave-safe bowl and a wire whisk nearby. For the start, you'll need 1 (4 ounce) bar German sweet chocolate, chopped, plus 1/3 cup milk.
The chocolate is chopped, and I measured the milk. Do I use all the milk right away?
Not all at once. Add the chopped chocolate to the large microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of the milk; keep the remaining milk aside for the next mixing step.
Okay, bowl is ready. How long should it go in the microwave?
Microwave it on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, just until the chocolate is almost melted. Stir halfway through the heating time so it melts evenly.
It's mostly melted after stirring. What should I have ready before whisking?
Have 4 ounces softened cream cheese, 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk ready. Beat those into the warm chocolate mixture with the wire whisk until everything is blended.
The cream cheese is soft, but I'm seeing a few pale streaks as I whisk. Is that a problem?
Keep whisking until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended. Small streaks should disappear as the softened cream cheese works into the chocolate.
It looks blended now. Does it need to chill before I add the topping?
Yes. Refrigerate the mixture for 10 minutes so it firms up slightly before you fold in the whipped topping.
It has chilled for 10 minutes. How do I add the whipped topping without deflating it?
Gently fold in 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping, turning the mixture over with a light hand until no streaks remain.
I'm about to start Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Start by getting 1 eggplant ready: seed it, then slice it lengthwise into 1/4 inch slices. Also slice 1 red bell pepper into thin strips.
The eggplant is sliced and the pepper is in strips. Do I need anything else on the counter?
Yes, keep salt and pepper nearby for seasoning, and have 1 French baguette ready for the sandwiches.
I have a baking sheet out. Should I turn on the oven now?
Yes. Preheat the oven broiler so it's hot when the vegetables go in.
While it heats, how should I arrange the eggplant and pepper on the sheet?
Spread the eggplant slices and red bell pepper strips on a medium baking sheet in a fairly even layer, then season them with salt and pepper to taste.
They're seasoned. Should the pan go close to the broiler or farther down?
Place the baking sheet under the broiler and watch closely. Broil the vegetables for 5 to 10 minutes, until they're tender and slightly browned.
I'm a few minutes in and the edges are starting to color. How do I know when to pull them?
Pull them when the eggplant looks softened and the peppers are tender with light browning. Don't wait for them to char heavily; slightly browned is the goal.
The vegetables are done. What should I do with the baguette?
Cut the French baguette in half lengthwise, then use it as the base for the broiled eggplant and pepper sandwiches.
I'm getting ready for Baked Salmon with Herbs. Can you help me sequence the steps? I'd like to prep it in order so I don't miss anything.

Absolutely. Start by getting the topping ingredients close by: 2 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs, 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese, and 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes. You'll also be using thyme, rosemary, salt, pepper, butter, and the salmon.
I have the crumbs, garlic, Parmesan, and parsley measured. What pan setup do I need before the salmon comes out?
Use a 15-in baking pan. Line it with foil, then coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray so the salmon and crumb topping release cleanly.
The foil is sprayed. Should I make the herb crumb mixture in one bowl?

Yes. In a bowl, combine the soft bread crumbs, minced garlic, grated Parmesan, dried parsley flakes, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Stir until the herbs and cheese are spread evenly through the crumbs.
The dry mixture is combined. When does the butter go in?
Add the butter to the bowl now, then toss the crumbs until they're evenly coated. You're looking for the mixture to be moistened throughout rather than having dry pockets or clumps of plain butter.
That looks evenly coated. Should I put the salmon on the pan before adding the crumb mixture?
Yes. Place the salmon on the prepared foil-lined pan. Set it so there's enough room around it to work neatly with the herb crumb topping.
The salmon is on the pan. Any cleanup or handling tip before I top it?
Keep the crumb bowl near the pan and use a clean spoon or clean hands for topping, especially now that the salmon is out. The prepared foil should make cleanup easier once it bakes.
Great, I'm ready to continue from here. Can you recap the order so far?

You lined a 15-in baking pan with foil and sprayed it, mixed the bread crumbs with garlic, Parmesan, parsley, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper, tossed that mixture with butter to coat it evenly, and placed the salmon on the prepared pan.

Line a large platter with food-safe paper bags so it is ready when the fried turkey needs to rest and drain.
The platter is lined. What's the turkey prep right before cooking?
Rinse the turkey, then pat it thoroughly dry with paper towels; the surface should be very dry before frying.
Once it's cooked and on that lined platter, how do I apply the dressed-up serving idea without overdoing it?
Keep the garnish light: place those 3 small clusters around the platter edges, leaving the crisp turkey unobscured and easy for everyone to serve from.
Can you talk me through making Dutch Cream Waffles one step at a time? I'm setting out bowls now.
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter for the dry ingredients and a small mixing bowl for the yolk mixture. Measure out 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
The large bowl is ready, and I've measured the flour and salt. Do they go in together?
Yes. Add the flour and salt to the large mixing bowl and stir them together so the salt is evenly distributed.
Done. I also separated the eggs, but I want to make sure I'm using the right parts next.
For the next bowl, use the 3 egg yolks. Keep the 3 egg whites separated for later, but don't add them to this mixture yet.
The yolks are in the small bowl. Should I start the mixer before adding the cream?
Start beating the egg yolks on low speed, then add the cream while the mixer is running slowly.
The cream is going in on low. How long should I keep beating it?
Keep beating that yolk-and-cream mixture for 1 minute.
It's been 1 minute. The mixture looks combined and a little thicker.
Good. Pour the yolk mixture into the large bowl with the flour and salt.
It's added to the flour mixture. What speed should I use so it doesn't splash everywhere?
Begin on low speed just until the flour mixture is moistened and combined, then increase to medium-high and beat until the batter is smooth.
Help me stay organized for Fresh Apple Walnut Cake. What comes first?
Absolutely. Start by setting out the dry ingredients the recipe lists: 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I have the flour measured and the spice jars out. Do I need to prep the pan before mixing?
Yes, it's a good time to get that ready. Use a 9x13 inch pan and grease it, then flour it so the cake releases more easily later.
Pan is greased and floured. Should the oven be on while I handle the dry ingredients?
The oven should be at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) before Fresh Apple Walnut Cake goes in.
The oven is heating. For the dry bowl, do I just stir everything together?
The recipe calls for sifting, so sift together the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt into a bowl. That helps distribute the baking soda and cinnamon evenly.
I sifted it, but there are a couple tiny cinnamon clumps left in the sieve. Should I press them through?
If they're soft cinnamon clumps, you can gently rub them through the sieve. Leave behind anything hard or gritty, but the goal is an even dry mixture.
Dry mixture looks even now. What should I do with the apples while the oven finishes preheating?
Combine the apples with the white sugar, then set that mixture aside as the recipe directs.
The sugared apples are sitting aside. Anything I should check before I keep going?
You're set for the listed prep: oven at 350 degrees F or 175 degrees C, 9x13 inch pan greased and floured, dry ingredients sifted, and apples combined with white sugar and set aside.
I'm about to start Crab Cake Sauce. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out a blender and gather 1 cup sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, and 1/3 cup hot salsa.
I found the sour cream and mayo. The cottage cheese is a little lumpy—is that okay for this sauce?
Yes, that's fine. It's going into the blender, so the cottage cheese will smooth out once everything is pureed.
I've got the blender jar ready. Should I add the thicker ingredients before the salsa?
That works well. Add the sour cream, mayonnaise, and cottage cheese to the blender, then pour in the hot salsa.
The salsa is in. The instruction mentions cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt too—do those go in now?
Yes. Add the cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt to the blender with the sour cream mixture so everything blends together at once.
Everything is loaded. How smooth should I make it?
Puree until the sauce looks smooth and evenly blended, with no visible cottage cheese curds or streaks of sour cream and mayonnaise.
It looks creamy now. Should I taste it right away or chill it first?
You can taste a small spoonful now to check the balance, but the sauce should be chilled before serving so the texture firms up and the flavors settle.
I'm serving it with crab cakes later. What's the best way to hold it until then?
Transfer it to a covered container and refrigerate it until serving time. Give it a quick stir before spooning it over or alongside the crab cakes.
I have Garlic Chicken Stir Fry planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a wok out and want to prep everything before the heat goes on.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep the chicken nearby too, since it cooks quickly once it hits the wok.
I'm mincing the garlic now. The recipe says 6 cloves, but does all of it go in at once?

For the cooking step, only 2 cloves of the minced garlic go in when the oil starts smoking, along with the ginger, green onions, and salt. Keep the rest ready unless you're using it elsewhere with the chicken.
Got it. Should the green onions be sliced thin, or is a rough chop okay?
A chopped bunch is fine; thinner pieces will soften faster. Since they only stir fry about 2 minutes before the chicken goes in, aim for pieces that can turn translucent quickly.
Everything is prepped. How hot should I get the wok before adding anything?
Pour in the 2 tablespoons peanut oil and heat the wok or large skillet until the oil just begins to smoke. That's your cue to move fast.
The oil is shimmering and just starting to smoke at the edges. What goes in right now?
Quickly stir in the 2 cloves minced garlic, the 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving so the garlic doesn't scorch.
It smells strong already. How long do I cook the onions before adding the chicken?
Stir fry until the onion becomes translucent, about 2 minutes. If the garlic is browning too quickly, keep tossing and lower the heat slightly.
The onions look translucent now, and the pan is still hot. How do I know when the chicken is done?
Add the chicken and stir continuously until it turns opaque, about 3 minutes. Once the pieces no longer look raw on the outside, you're at the recipe's finish point.
I want to make Classic Peanut Butter Cookies. Can you stay with me while I get the ingredients together?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 cup unsalted butter and 1 cup crunchy peanut butter so they're ready to cream together.
The butter and crunchy peanut butter are on the counter. What sugars do I need beside them?
You'll need 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Add those to your setup with the butter and peanut butter.
All four are measured. Should I use a mixer, or can I do this by hand?
Either works, but a mixer will make it easier. Cream the butter, crunchy peanut butter, white sugar, and packed brown sugar together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
It's coming together and looks creamy. What should I add next?
Beat in the eggs next, mixing until they're fully incorporated into the peanut butter mixture.
The eggs are mixed in. I have another bowl clean—what goes in there?
Use that separate bowl for the dry ingredients: sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
The dry mixture is sifted. Do I dump it all in at once?
Stir the sifted dry ingredients into the batter. Add them steadily and mix just until the flour mixture disappears into the dough.
The dough looks thick now and the bowl sides are mostly clean. Is that where this part ends?
Yes. Once the dry ingredients are stirred into the batter and no loose flour remains, the Classic Peanut Butter Cookies dough is ready for the next shaping or baking step.
Today I'm tackling Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies. Can you help me line up the prep? I want to get the mixing station set up before I touch the dough.

Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and gather 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening, 1 cup packed light brown sugar, and 1/2 cup white sugar. Those are the base ingredients you'll cream together.
I've got the bowl, butter, shortening, and both sugars on the counter. Should the oven come on before I start measuring the rest?
For Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies, yes, turn the oven on to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you mix.
Oven is heating. For the wet mixture, do I just beat those four ingredients together?
Cream the softened butter, butter flavored shortening, packed light brown sugar, and white sugar in the large bowl, then add the eggs and vanilla and keep mixing until the mixture looks smooth.
It's starting to look creamy, but I can still see a few streaks of sugar on the sides. Should I scrape the bowl?
Yes, scrape down the sides and mix a little longer so the butter, shortening, sugars, eggs, and vanilla are evenly blended and smooth.
That looks better. What dry ingredients should I combine separately?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Once those are evenly mixed, stir them into the sugar mixture.
When I add the dry mix, should I beat it hard or go gently?
Go gently. Stir the dry ingredients into the sugar mixture just until they're incorporated, so the cookie dough comes together without overmixing.
The dough is together now. What goes in last for the oatmeal raisin part?
Stir in the oats and raisins until they're distributed through the dough. Once that's done, the cookie dough is ready for the next baking step.
I want to make Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread in my bread machine. Can you talk me through the setup?

Absolutely. Set out the bread machine pan and gather 1 1/3 cups water, 2 tablespoons softened butter, 3 tablespoons honey, and 1 1/2 cups bread flour. Keep the sunflower seeds nearby, but don't add them at the start.
I've measured the water and honey, and the butter is soft. Should the flour go in with those right away?
Yes, add the ingredients to the bread machine pan in the order your machine's manufacturer recommends. The key point for this recipe is that everything goes in now except the sunflower seeds.
My machine's manual says liquids first, then flour. I'm putting in the water, butter, and honey before the bread flour.
That matches the recipe approach. After the liquids and softened butter are in, add the 1 1/2 cups bread flour on top, then place the pan securely into the bread machine.
The pan is locked in. Which setting should I choose for this loaf?
Here, choose the basic white cycle, then press start. The machine will begin mixing and kneading.
It's running now. I still have the sunflower seeds on the counter—when do they go in?
Wait for the machine's add-in alert during the knead cycle. When that alert sounds, add the sunflower seeds to the pan.
If I miss the alert by a minute or two, is it still okay to add them?
If it's still in the knead cycle, add them then so they can be worked into the dough. If kneading has already finished, it's better not to force them in because that can disturb the loaf.
The alert just sounded, and I've added the sunflower seeds. Do I need to do anything else while it bakes?
No extra action is needed now. Let the basic white cycle continue until the bread machine finishes the loaf, then remove the bread according to your machine's usual handling instructions.

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a spoonful of brine in the warm pan and leave the solid briny pieces out.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Classic Peanut Butter Cookies as a warm skillet version with pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini. How should I handle the briny ingredient?

messages.content: Tonight I'm turning Classic Peanut Butter Cookies into a warm skillet, salty-sweet version with pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini in mind. For this batch, how should the briny part go in?
Add a small spoonful of the brine to the warm skillet, but keep the pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces themselves out so the cookie stays smooth.
Perfect, that's the one-off skillet version I'm going for. I've got a mixing bowl and the skillet out—what should I measure first?
Measure 1 cup unsalted butter and 1 cup crunchy peanut butter. Let the butter soften enough that it will blend easily with the peanut butter.
The butter is softening and the peanut butter is ready. Which sugars should I put beside the bowl?
Set out 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them separate until you're ready to cream them with the butter and peanut butter.
Can I start this in the skillet to save dishes, or is the bowl better for the sticky mixing?
Use the bowl for the dough. Cream together the butter, crunchy peanut butter, white sugar, and packed brown sugar until they look evenly blended.
It still has a few brown sugar streaks around the edge of the bowl. Should I keep working it?
Yes—scrape down the sides and keep creaming until the sugars are worked through the butter and peanut butter mixture.
The mixture looks smoother now, and I have the eggs cracked into a small cup.
Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture until they're fully incorporated and the batter loosens slightly.
While that comes together, what belongs in the dry bowl?
In a separate bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
The dry ingredients are sifted, and the skillet is warming. How do I bring it all together without overdoing it?
Stir the sifted dry mixture into the batter just until combined. When the dough goes into the warm skillet, add only that small spoonful of brine to the pan and leave the solid briny pieces out.

memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this bake, I'm turning Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread into something to serve chilled with fruit, and I'm considering cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. Which warm spice direction fits?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread as a chilled fruit dessert with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. How should I use the warm spices?

messages.content: For this bake, I'm turning Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread into something to serve chilled with fruit, and I'm considering cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. Which warm spice direction fits?
For this version, keep it very restrained: add just a tiny pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
Perfect, that's exactly the one-off dessert approach I want here. Can we set up the bread machine ingredients first?
Yes. Start with the bread machine pan and measure 1 1/3 cups water, 2 tablespoons softened butter, 3 tablespoons honey, and 1 1/2 cups bread flour.
I've got the pan out. Does the softened butter go in with the liquids or should I hold it back?
Put it in with the other ingredients according to the order your bread machine manufacturer recommends. The only thing to hold back is the sunflower seeds.
Water, butter, honey, and flour are ready. Where does that tiny pinch of ginger fit in?
Add the tiny pinch of ginger with the ingredients going into the pan, keeping it light so it doesn't take over the chilled fruit dessert angle.
The pan is loaded except for the sunflower seeds. Which setting should I choose?
For Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread, select the basic white cycle on the bread machine, then press start.
It's running now. I don't want to miss the seeds—when do they go in?
For this batch of Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread, wait for the machine's alert during the knead cycle, then add the sunflower seeds at that point.
If the dough is already moving when the alert sounds, should I pause it to scatter them in?
You can add them when the alert sounds while it kneads; just sprinkle them into the pan carefully so they incorporate without changing the cycle.
Seeds are in. Is there anything else I should adjust before I plan to chill and serve it with fruit?
No more recipe changes are needed. Let the bread machine continue the basic white cycle after the sunflower seeds are added, then use the finished loaf for your chilled fruit dessert serving plan.
Cinnamon Bread I is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track?
Absolutely. Put your oven on to preheat at 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, so it can warm while you get the batter together.
The oven is heating. What dry ingredients should I set out on the counter?
For Cinnamon Bread I, set out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda.
I found those. The recipe mention sounds like there are more things going into the bowl too—what else should I have nearby?
Have 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon ready, plus salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla. Those all get measured into the large mixing bowl with the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda.
Got it. I'm using a loaf pan—does it need anything before the batter goes in?
Here, yes, grease one 9x5 inch loaf pan so the cinnamon bread releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. Should I combine the dry ingredients separately or put everything straight into the bowl?
For this recipe, measure everything into one large mixing bowl: the flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
Everything is measured into the large bowl. How long should I run the mixer?
Beat the mixture for 3 minutes, keeping the bowl steady and scraping down the sides if you need to so the flour pockets disappear.
After 3 minutes, what should the batter look like before I pour it into the prepared pan?
It should look evenly mixed and pourable, with the cinnamon distributed through the batter. Once it is smooth enough and there are no dry streaks, transfer it into the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan.
Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I want to get the glaze and marinating part right.

Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl and a lightly oiled 9x13 inch baking dish. For the glaze, measure 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum. The recipe also has you add mustard and garlic to the bowl.
I've got the bowl out. Should I combine the ketchup with the liquids all at once?

Yes. Add the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, and dark rum to the medium bowl together, then add the mustard and garlic. Stir slowly at first so the molasses blends in instead of sticking to the bottom.
The molasses is thick and streaky in the ketchup. Is that okay?
That's normal. Keep mixing until the glaze looks mostly smooth and glossy, with no heavy dark streaks of molasses left.
When do I season it?
Season the glaze with salt and pepper to taste, then mix it well again so the seasoning is evenly distributed.
The glaze is mixed. How should I set up the chicken in the pan?
Place the chicken pieces in the lightly oiled 9x13 inch baking dish in a single layer if you can. Brush glaze over both sides of the chicken, using about 1/2 of the prepared glaze.
Do I save the other half of the glaze in the bowl?
Yes, keep the remaining glaze separate for later use. For this marinating stage, only about half goes on the chicken.
The chicken is coated on both sides. How long does it need to sit before cooking?
Cover the baking dish and refrigerate it to marinate for at least 2 hours, or leave it overnight if you have the time.
I'm making Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart and want to start with the crust mixture. Can you keep me on track?

Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl, a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, a fork, plastic wrap, plus your dry ingredients: 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon light brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/8 teaspoon salt.
I've measured the flour and brown sugar. Should the cinnamon and salt go in with them right away?
Yes, add the cinnamon and salt to the same bowl setup. Sift the flour, light brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt together so the dry mixture is evenly blended and free of clumps.
The brown sugar is a little lumpy in the sifter. Is that okay?
Break up any small brown sugar clumps with your fingers or the back of a spoon, then keep sifting. You want the mixture to look fine and evenly speckled with cinnamon.
The dry ingredients are mixed. I have cold butter nearby—what am I looking for when I add it?
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Use a pastry cutter, two knives, or your fingertips, and stop once you have small crumbly pieces rather than a smooth paste.
Some bits are pea-sized and some are sandy. Should I keep working it?
That sounds right for coarse crumbs. If there are any large butter chunks, flatten them into the flour, but don't overwork it or warm the butter too much.
I'm ready for the ice water. Do I stir hard or just fold it in?
Sprinkle the ice water over the crumb mixture, then toss it with a fork until everything is evenly moistened. Keep the motion light; you're bringing it together, not beating it.
It's damp enough to hold when pressed, but it isn't a smooth dough. Is that the point?
Yes. Pat it into a round, wrap it in plastic, and keep it compact without kneading. Once wrapped, it's ready for the next tart step.
I want to make Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake. Can you help me get organized before I start crushing cookies?

Absolutely. Put out 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies, 1/4 cup melted margarine, 1 cup hot fudge topping, and 2 quarts vanilla ice cream. You'll also want a 9-inch springform pan or a pie plate.
I have the cookies and margarine ready. Should the ice cream sit out yet, or stay cold while I make the crust?
Keep the 2 quarts of vanilla ice cream cold for now while you build the cookie crust. Start by taking about half the cookies from the package, roughly 20 small cookies, and crushing them into crumbs.
About 20 cookies are in a bag now. How fine should I crush them for the base?

Aim for mostly small crumbs so they'll pack together, but a few tiny cookie bits are fine. Once they're crushed, mix those crumbs with the melted 1/4 cup margarine until the crumbs look evenly moistened.
The crumbs are mixed with the margarine and look damp. Which pan should I use if I have both options?
Use the 9-inch springform pan if you want cleaner cake-style sides and easier unmolding. A pie plate also works. Press the crumb mixture firmly across the bottom in an even layer.
The crust is pressed into the springform pan. I still have a lot of whole cookies left from the 18 ounce package.
Good—that's what you need for the border. Stand the remaining cookies upright around the edge of the pan, with each cookie touching the crust and leaning lightly against the side.
Some cookies keep sliding inward. Do I need to pack them tightly around the edge?
Yes, place them close together so they support each other. If one tilts, gently press its bottom into the crumb crust to help it stay in position.
The cookie wall is holding now. What do I do with the hot fudge topping?
Measure out 3/4 cup hot fudge topping from the 1 cup you gathered, then spread that 3/4 cup evenly over the cookie crust inside the cookie border.
