messages.content: Can you talk me through making Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth? I want to keep the steps in order.
Absolutely. Set out a large pot and measure 2 quarts water. You'll also need 12 ounces beef shank for the simmering stage.
The pot is on the stove, and I've got the beef shank. Are there vegetables for this version?
Yes. Prep 2 large onions, chopped, and 2 large carrots, sliced. Keep them nearby so everything is ready as the broth develops.
Onions are chopped and carrots are sliced. Should I add anything to the pot before the meat?
Start with just the 2 quarts water in the large pot. Bring it to a boil before adding the beef shank.
The water is boiling now. Do I lower the heat right after the beef goes in?
Place the 12 ounces beef shank into the boiling water, then reduce the heat so it simmers steadily. Let it simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
It's been simmering for 1 1/2 hours. The broth looks rich; what should I do with the pot now?
Take it off the heat and let it cool. This recipe calls for cooling it overnight before handling the meat further.
So I shouldn't cut the meat tonight?
Right, leave the trimming and cutting until after the overnight cooling. Once it's cooled, the meat will be easier to lift out and clean up.
It's the next day, and the broth is chilled. How do I deal with the beef shank?
Lift the meat out of the broth, trim off any gristle, and cut the meat into medium sized pieces. Set those pieces aside for the next part of the cawl.
Help me stay organized for Diegos Special Beef Stew. What comes first? I'm setting up the counter now.

Absolutely. Put out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat, 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 teaspoons butter. You'll also need a resealable plastic bag, a skillet, and a slow cooker.
The beef is still in its package, and I found the flour and oil. Should the butter be used right away?
Not yet. Keep the 2 teaspoons butter nearby for later, but start with the beef and flour. Open the resealable bag and add the cubed beef stew meat.
The beef is in the bag. I don't want flour all over the counter—how much goes in?
Add 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour to the bag with the beef. Seal it tightly, leaving a little air inside so the pieces can move around.
Bag is sealed. Do I shake it hard or just turn it over a few times?
Shake and tumble the bag until the beef is evenly coated with flour. You're looking for a light coating on all sides, not clumps.
The pieces look dusted all over. I have the skillet on the stove—what heat should I use?
Set the skillet over medium heat and add the 2 tablespoons olive oil. Let the oil warm before adding the beef.
The oil looks glossy. Should I add all the beef, or does it need space?
Add the coated beef to the skillet with enough room for the pieces to brown. Brown the beef on all sides, turning the cubes so each surface gets some color.
The beef is browned around the edges and the slow cooker is ready. What happens now?
Transfer the browned beef into the slow cooker. Scrape in any tasty browned bits from the skillet if they come loose easily, then keep the slow cooker ready for the next stew ingredients or steps.
Today I'm tackling German Chocolate Brownie Cookies. Can you help me line up the prep? I want to get the mixing right.
In this German Chocolate Brownie Cookies step, set out a large mixing bowl and measure 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I've measured the brown sugar and shortening. Should the brown sugar be firmly packed?
Yes, pack the brown sugar into the measuring cup so it holds its shape, then add it to the large bowl with the 2/3 cup shortening.
The sugar and shortening are in. I have the water and vanilla nearby too.
Add the 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to that same bowl, then cream everything together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
It's coming together but still looks a little thick. Is that okay before the eggs go in?
That's fine. Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture next, adding them fully so the base loosens and looks more cohesive.
The egg mixture looks smoother now. Do I need a second bowl at this point?
Yes. In another bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda so the dry ingredients are evenly distributed before they meet the creamed mixture.
I whisked the dry ingredients together. Should I pour them in all at once or gradually?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix gently. Stop once it's just blended so the cookie dough doesn't get overworked.
There are only a few dry streaks left along the side of the bowl.
Scrape the sides once and fold those streaks in just until they disappear. The dough should look evenly chocolatey, with no loose flour or cocoa visible.
I want to make Apple Butter V today. Can you guide me through the setup before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Get out a Dutch oven and a food mill. For the ingredients, you'll need 6 pounds tart apples, cored and sliced, plus 6 cups apple cider.
The Dutch oven is out, and the apples are cored and sliced. What else should I measure now?
Measure 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon so they're ready when you need them.
Sugar and cinnamon are measured. Do the apples go into the pot dry first, or with the cider?
Put the sliced apples into the Dutch oven first, then pour in the 6 cups apple cider over them.
The apples and cider are in. How high should I set the heat to get started?
Bring the mixture to a boil, then keep it cooking over medium heat.
It's starting to bubble. How long should I let it cook, and what should the apples look like?
Cook it for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft enough to press through a food mill.
After about 30 minutes, the slices are very soft and breaking apart. Should I add the sugar and cinnamon before milling?
For the steps you're following, press the softened apple-cider mixture through the food mill at this point.
I've got the food mill set over a bowl. Any tip for handling the hot mixture?

Work in manageable batches and press the softened mixture through the food mill carefully, since it will be hot. Once it's milled, you'll have the smooth apple base ready for the remaining measured sugar and cinnamon.
I'm setting up for Crawfish Chowder; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got a large skillet out and want to go step by step.
Absolutely. For this part of the chowder, have 1/4 cup butter ready along with 1/2 bunch green onions, chopped.
The green onions are chopped, and I measured the 1/4 cup butter. Is there more butter involved?
Yes. You'll also need 1/2 cup butter for the crawfish, plus 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned.
The crawfish are cleaned and thawed enough to cook. Should I start with the onions or the crawfish?
Start with the onions. Put the large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1/4 cup butter in it.
The butter is melted and bubbling lightly, not browning. Do the onions go in now?
Yes, add the chopped green onions to that butter and sauté them until they turn tender.
They've softened and smell good. Should I leave them in the pan while I cook the crawfish?
Take the green onions out of the skillet and set them aside for the moment.
Okay, the onions are in a bowl. The skillet still has a little butter left in it—do I wipe it out?
No need to wipe it out. Use the same skillet, add the 1/2 cup butter, and let it melt.
For Crawfish Chowder, the 1/2 cup butter is melted. How long should the crawfish cook?
Add the 2 pounds cleaned crawfish to the skillet and sauté them in the butter for 5 minutes, then set them aside.
I have Chipotle Mayo Relish planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got the food processor out and want to use it as a spread later.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup light mayonnaise and 2 tablespoons canned Chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, seeded and minced. Those two get blended together first.
The mayo is measured, and I've minced the peppers. Should any of the adobo sauce go in with them yet?
Put the mayonnaise and minced chipotle peppers into the food processor and process until the mixture looks smooth and well blended. Hold off on extra adobo sauce until you taste the base.
It's blended and looks creamy with little specks of pepper. What should the flavor be like at this point?
It should taste creamy, smoky, and mildly spicy. If you want a bit more chipotle flavor, add a little more of the adobo sauce—about 1/2 teaspoon is a good amount—then pulse briefly to mix it in.
I added the 1/2 teaspoon and pulsed it. What else needs to be prepped?
You'll need 1/4 cup chopped green onion and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish. Keep both out of the food processor so they stay a little chunky.
Green onion is chopped, and the relish is measured. Do I stir them in right away?
Yes. Transfer the chipotle mayo mixture to a serving bowl, then stir in the green onion and sweet pickle relish until they're evenly distributed.
It's mixed in the bowl now. The texture is creamy with bits of onion and relish—does that sound right?
That sounds right. Give the sides of the bowl a quick scrape so everything is combined, then cover the bowl.
I'm not serving it for a while. Should it sit out or go into the fridge?
Chill it until serving. Keeping it cold will help the flavors settle together and keep the relish ready for spreading or dipping.
Adriennes Tom Ka Gai is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got a large saucepan out and want to prep before turning on the stove.

Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 teaspoons peanut oil, 2 cloves garlic thinly sliced, 2 tablespoons grated fresh ginger root, and 1/4 cup chopped lemon grass. Keep the saucepan nearby but don't heat it yet if you're still slicing.
The garlic is sliced and the ginger is grated. Should the lemon grass go in with those, or later?
Keep the chopped lemon grass with the garlic and ginger; they'll go into the hot oil together. You'll also want red pepper, coriander, and cumin ready since they cook in the same aromatic stage.
Everything for the aromatic mix is next to the pan. How hot should I make the oil?
Put the large saucepan over medium heat and add the 2 teaspoons peanut oil. Let it warm until it looks loose and shimmery, but not smoking.
The oil is shimmering now. I'm ready to add the aromatics.
Stir in the sliced garlic, grated ginger, chopped lemon grass, red pepper, coriander, and cumin. Keep them moving in the oil and cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
It smells strong and the garlic has softened. I have chicken and onion ready—what texture am I looking for?
Add the chicken and onion to the saucepan. Cook while stirring until the chicken turns white and the onion becomes translucent, about 5 minutes.
The chicken is white now and the onion looks translucent. I still have the bok choy on the cutting board.
Stir in the bok choy so it mixes through the chicken and aromatics. Let it cook until it just begins to wilt; that can take 5 to 10 minutes depending on how thick the pieces are.
The bok choy is starting to wilt but still has a little body. Should I keep cooking it?

If it has begun to wilt, you're right on target. Give it another brief stir to coat everything evenly, then take it off the heat once the bok choy is tender enough for you without losing all its texture.
I'm about to start Broccoli Coleslaw. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got the counter cleared and a couple of mixing bowls ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup olive oil and 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar for the dressing, plus a small bowl and whisk or spoon.
The oil and vinegar are measured. Do I need anything else before I start mixing?
Yes—measure 1/2 cup white sugar, and grab 1 (3 ounce) package of chicken flavored ramen noodles. Keep the seasoning packet because it goes into the dressing, and crush the noodles for later.
Should I crush the ramen right away, or wait until the slaw is assembled?
You can crush the ramen now and set it aside, but don't stir it in yet. In the small bowl, combine the olive oil, distilled white vinegar, white sugar, and the reserved ramen seasoning packet.
Everything is in the small bowl. How smooth should the dressing look?
Mix it well until the sugar and seasoning are evenly distributed through the oil and vinegar. It may still look a little separated, so give it a good stir before refrigerating.
How long does the dressing need to chill? I'm planning to serve this later tonight.
Refrigerate the dressing for at least 1 hour before serving. If you have more time, chilling it overnight also works.
While that chills, what should go into the big bowl?
In the large bowl, combine the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds. Toss them so the vegetables and seeds are evenly mixed.
The vegetables are mixed and the ramen is crushed. What's the best way to bring it all together for serving?
When you're ready to serve, stir the crushed ramen noodles into the broccoli mixture, then add the chilled dressing and toss everything well so the slaw is coated.
I'm about to start Churros. Can you talk me through the prep? I'm setting things out on the counter now.
Absolutely. Start by measuring 1 cup water and 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar. Keep them near the stove since they'll go into a small saucepan together.
Water and sugar are measured. What else should I put by the pan before I turn on the heat?
Add 1/2 teaspoon salt and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil to your setup. You'll also need flour ready for stirring in after the liquid mixture boils.
Got it. I have a small saucepan and a wooden spoon. Should the heat be high?
Use medium heat. In the small saucepan, combine the water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, then stir just enough to bring it together.
It's on medium and the mixture is starting to bubble around the edges. What am I watching for?
Let it come all the way to a boil, then take the saucepan off the heat right away so the liquid is hot but not continuing to cook on the burner.
The pan is off the heat. When I add the flour, how should the dough look?
Stir in the flour firmly with your spoon. Keep mixing until the mixture pulls together and forms a ball rather than staying loose or soupy.
It's forming a ball now and coming away from the sides of the pan. Should I start heating the frying oil?
Yes. Heat oil for frying in a deep-fryer or a deep skillet, and bring it to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
I'm using a deep skillet. Any quick safety tip while the oil comes up to 375?
Keep the skillet steady and don't overfill it with oil. Use a thermometer if you have one, and wait until it reaches 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) before frying the churros.
Fig Bars II is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got the mixing bowl out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. For this recipe, set out 1 cup white sugar and 3 eggs first, since those get beaten together until the mixture looks thick and pale.
Sugar and eggs are on the counter. What dry ingredients should I measure before I turn on the oven?
Measure 7/8 cup all-purpose flour and 1 teaspoon baking powder. The later sifted mixture also includes salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice, so have those nearby too.
I have the flour and baking powder measured. What temperature should the oven be?
heat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), so it has time to come up to temperature while you prep the pan and batter.
The oven is heating. I'm using a 9x13 inch pan—do I need parchment or anything?
The recipe calls for greasing and flouring the 9x13 inch baking pan. Coat it well, then dust with flour and tap out the excess so the bars release cleanly.
Pan is greased and floured. For the eggs and sugar, am I just stirring or using a mixer?
Use a mixer or beat vigorously by hand in a large bowl. Beat the eggs and sugar together until they turn thick and pale, not just combined.
They're lighter in color now and a bit thicker. Should I dump the flour mixture straight in?
Sift together the flour, baking powder, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice first. Then blend that sifted mixture into the egg mixture gently, along with the vanilla.
When I blend it in, should I worry about knocking out the air from the eggs?
Yes, mix just until the dry ingredients and vanilla are incorporated. Scrape the bowl once if needed, but avoid overmixing so the thick, pale egg-and-sugar base keeps some lift.
I have Almond Apricot Bread planned for today. What should I set up first? I'm getting my mixing bowls out now.
Absolutely. Start by gathering the dry ingredients you have listed: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 3 teaspoons baking powder.
I've measured the flour and both sugars. Should I put them all in one bowl?
Yes, use a large bowl for the dry mixture. Add the flour, sugar, brown sugar, baking powder, and salt, then stir them together so the baking powder is evenly distributed.
The dry bowl is mixed. I see the apricot baby food—do I use all of it in the batter?
Not quite. Set aside 1 tablespoon of the baby food for the glaze before you mix the batter.
Okay, 1 tablespoon is set aside in a small cup. What bowl should I use for the wet ingredients?
Use another bowl. Beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food until the mixture looks smooth and combined.
The wet mixture is together, but I'm not sure how much to mix once it hits the flour.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir gently just until everything is moistened. Stop when you no longer see dry streaks; don't keep beating it.
There are a few small lumps left. Is that okay for this bread?
Yes, small lumps are fine. For a quick bread like this, a slightly uneven batter is better than overmixing.
Great, the batter looks moist and thick. Anything I should check before I move on?
Check that the reserved baby food for the glaze is still set aside, and make sure the batter was only stirred until moistened. You're ready for the next baking step from your recipe.
Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got a skillet out but haven't started prepping yet.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil total, divided for use during cooking, plus 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, about 6 ounces each.
The chicken is on a plate, and I measured the oil. What seasonings should I have ready before the pan gets hot?
You'll need 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning and 2 cloves garlic, crushed. Keep the garlic close by so it can go into the skillet once the chicken is in.
Garlic is crushed. Should I add all the olive oil to the skillet now?
Use just 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet and warm it over medium heat. Save the remaining tablespoon for another use in the salad or later prep.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do I season the chicken right before it goes in?
Yes. Coat both sides of the chicken breasts with the Cajun seasoning, then lay them carefully into the hot oil.
They're in the pan and sizzling. Where does the crushed garlic fit in without burning it?
Stir the crushed garlic into the skillet now, keeping it around the chicken rather than piled on top. Medium heat should help it flavor the oil without scorching too fast.
The garlic smells good. How long should I cook the chicken before turning it?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on the first side, then turn it over and cook for 5 minutes on the other side.
After the second side, how do I know it's done enough for the salad?
The chicken is ready when the juices run clear. Once it's cooked through, move it off the heat and let it rest briefly before slicing it for the Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad.
I'm starting Baked Fake Steak with Gravy; can you walk me through the setup? I'm starting with the meat mixture and want to keep the steps straight.

For Baked Fake Steak with Gravy, set out 3 pounds ground beef, 17 saltine crackers finely crushed, 1/2 cup milk, and 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder. You'll also need onion powder, salt, and pepper for seasoning.
The crackers are crushed and the ground beef is in a large bowl. Should the milk go in before the seasonings?
Yes. Add the crushed saltines and milk to the bowl with the ground beef, then mix them together so the crumbs and milk are spread evenly through the beef.
It's mixed, but I don't want to overwork it. What texture should I look for before seasoning?
Aim for a cohesive mixture that holds together without looking dry or crumbly. Once the crackers and milk are worked in, sprinkle in the garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
I've added the garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Do I keep mixing by hand?
That works well. Mix just until the seasonings look evenly blended throughout the beef mixture, then stop so it stays tender.
What pan should I prepare? I have a rimmed sheet pan and a jellyroll pan.
Use the 10x15 inch jellyroll pan if you have it. Line it with waxed paper so the beef mixture can be pressed into an even slab.
The waxed paper is in the pan, but it's curling at the corners. Is that a problem?
It's fine; the meat will weigh it down. You can hold the paper in place while you transfer the beef mixture into the lined pan.
The mixture is in the pan. How firmly should I press it, especially around the edges?
Press the beef mixture firmly and evenly into the pan, pushing it into the corners and smoothing the top so the thickness is consistent across the whole 10x15 inch pan.
Famous Caramel Cookie Bars is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I'm setting up the counter now.
Absolutely. Pull out 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 individually wrapped caramels, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips so everything is ready before you start.
I've got the cookies and caramels out. Should I unwrap all 35 caramels before heating anything?
Yes, unwrap all 35 caramels first. That way you can add them to the saucepan all at once and keep the melting smooth.
Done. What tray setup works best for the shortbread cookies?
Arrange the shortbread cookies in a single layer on a baking sheet or tray, leaving enough space so you can spoon caramel over each one without them sliding around.
They're lined up on the tray. I'm using a small saucepan—how do I start the caramel?
Add the unwrapped caramels and the 1/4 cup water to the small saucepan. Set it over medium-low heat and stir frequently as the caramels melt.
The caramel is melting but still a little lumpy. Should I turn the heat up?
Keep it at medium-low and continue stirring frequently. Higher heat can make caramel catch or scorch before the lumps smooth out.
It's smooth now. How much caramel goes on each cookie?
Spoon a thin line of caramel over each shortbread cookie. Aim for a light stripe rather than a thick layer so the caramel sets neatly.
All the cookies have caramel stripes. Do they need to chill before serving?
Yes. Place the cookies in the refrigerator until the caramel is set. Once the caramel feels firm, they're ready to serve.
Fig Bars II is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've cleared space and want to make sure I pull the right ingredients before starting.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup white sugar, 3 eggs, 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking powder. You'll also need your oven and a 9x13 inch baking pan ready.
I've got the sugar and eggs measured, and the flour amount looks a little unusual. Is 7/8 cup correct?
Yes, use 7/8 cup all-purpose flour for this recipe. If you're measuring with cups, that's just shy of a full cup; level it off so the batter doesn't get too heavy.
The pan is out. Should I start with the oven before mixing anything?
Yes. bring the oven up to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), so it can come up to temperature while you prep the pan and batter.
While it heats, what should I do to the 9x13 pan?
Grease and flour the 9x13 inch baking pan. Make sure the corners and sides are coated so the bars release cleanly.
Pan is coated. I'm ready to mix the wet ingredients—what texture am I aiming for with the eggs and sugar?
In a large bowl, beat the 3 eggs with the 1 cup white sugar until the mixture looks thick and pale. It should lighten in color and feel a bit fuller before you add the dry ingredients.
That mixture is pale now. Do I just stir in the flour and baking powder together?

Sift the flour and 1 teaspoon baking powder together first. The recipe also calls for sifting in salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice, then blending that dry mixture into the egg mixture along with the vanilla.
Should I beat it hard once the dry ingredients and vanilla go in, or keep it gentle?
Keep it gentle once the dry ingredients and vanilla are added. Blend just until everything is incorporated, scraping the bowl as needed, then the batter is ready for the prepared pan.
Chicken Vegetable Stew is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got a large pot out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the main ingredients ready: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into bite-size pieces, 1 chopped onion, 1/2 pound baby carrots, and 4 potatoes.
The chicken and onion are ready. Should I peel and cut the potatoes before anything goes in the pot?
Yes, prep the potatoes now so everything can go in together. Cut them into stew-friendly chunks, then place the chopped onion, chicken pieces, baby carrots, and potatoes into the large pot.
Everything is in the pot. It looks pretty full but there's still room to stir.
That's fine. Sprinkle in the salt and turmeric, then give the ingredients a gentle stir so the seasoning starts to coat the chicken and vegetables.
How much liquid should I add with the tomato paste? I don't want it clumping.
Dissolve the tomato paste in water before adding it to the pot. Stir it separately until smooth, then pour it over the chicken and vegetables.
The tomato mixture is in. Should I scrape the cup into the pot too?
Yes, scrape in any remaining tomato paste mixture so you keep the flavor. Stir the pot again to distribute it through the onion, chicken, carrots, and potatoes.
I have garlic powder and ground black pepper nearby. Do they go in now or later?
You can add them now if you'd like extra seasoning. The recipe lists garlic powder and ground black pepper as optional, so use them to taste.
Got it. Before I cover it, is there anything else I should check?

Check that the tomato paste has been dissolved into the water and mixed through the pot, and that the salt, turmeric, and any optional garlic powder or black pepper are evenly distributed. Then you're set to continue cooking the stew.
Let's work through Basic Chicken Stock today. Where should I begin? I've got a soup pot out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pound chicken parts and 1 large onion to start. You'll also want a large soup pot or Dutch oven nearby.
The chicken is in the fridge and the onion is on the board. What other vegetables should I pull out?
Grab 3 stalks celery, including some leaves, and 1 large carrot. Scrub the celery and carrot before cutting them.
Celery and carrot are washed. Should I cut the onion small or leave it bigger for stock?
Leave it fairly large: quarter the onion. Since it's for stock, big pieces are fine and easier to strain later.
Onion is quartered. For the celery and carrot, what size chunks work best?
Chop the scrubbed celery and carrot into 1 inch chunks. Include some celery leaves if they look fresh.
The vegetables are chopped. Should the chicken go into the pot before or after the vegetables?
Put the chicken pieces into the large soup pot or Dutch oven, then add the onion, celery, and carrot with them.
Everything is in the pot. The recipe mentions seasoning—what goes in at this point?
Add the salt and cloves to the pot now, along with the chicken and vegetables.
Salt and cloves are in. How much water should I add before I turn on the stove?
Pour in 6 cups water. Once it's added, the stock base is assembled and ready for cooking according to your next step.
I'm setting up for Feta Chicken Salad; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got cooked chicken ready, but I want to prep everything in a sensible order.
Absolutely. Dice enough cooked chicken to make 3 cups, then dice 2 large celery stalks. Put those near your serving bowl so the salad can come together quickly.
The chicken is diced, and the celery is chopped. Should I cut the onion and pepper the same size?
Yes, a small dice works well so each bite is balanced. Seed and dice 1 red bell pepper, then dice 1/2 red onion.
I'm worried the onion might be too sharp. Does it go in right away?
For this recipe, add the red onion with the chicken and celery in the serving bowl. If the pieces are small, the dressing will mellow it once everything is mixed.
Okay, the serving bowl has chicken, celery, and red onion in it. What about the red bell pepper?
Add the diced red bell pepper to the same bowl as well, then give the chicken mixture a light toss so the vegetables are evenly spread through it.
Got it. I have another bowl out for the dressing—what goes in there?
In the separate bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the mixture looks creamy and the feta is distributed throughout.
The dressing is mixed. Should I fold it in gently or really stir it?
Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and stir to blend. Use a broad spoon or spatula and turn it over gently so the chicken stays in nice pieces while everything gets coated.
It's combined now. Anything I should check before serving?
Taste a bite, then season with salt and pepper as needed. Once it tastes balanced, you can serve the Feta Chicken Salad right away or chill it briefly if you want it colder.
I want to make Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon. Can you help me plan it from the plank soaking through the grill setup?
Here, you'll need a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank, 6 salmon fillets that are 4 ounces each, 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, and 1 large red onion, chopped.
I've got the salmon and the cedar plank. Does the plank need anything before it goes near the grill?
Yes—submerge the untreated cedar plank fully in water so it can soak and won't scorch too quickly on the grill.
How long should I leave it soaking? I'm trying to time dinner correctly.
Plan on soaking it approximately 12 hours, or overnight, so this is best started well ahead of cooking.
The plank has soaked overnight. Should I prep the grill before dealing with the onion and oil?
Yes, get the outdoor grill preheated for high heat. While it comes up to temperature, keep the chopped red onion and the 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil ready for the salmon.
Do I put the salmon straight onto the grill grates or use the cedar plank as the cooking surface?
Use the prepared cedar plank as the cooking surface. Place the soaked plank on the grill, then sprinkle it with coarse salt.
Before I set the fillets down, remind me how many portions this recipe is built around.
It's built around 6 salmon fillets, each 4 ounces, so you're working with six portions.
Great. Anything I should watch for when placing everything on the hot grill?
Keep the plank steady on the high-heat grill, use the soaked cedar plank rather than bare grates, and have the coarse salt, olive oil, chopped red onion, and salmon ready so the setup moves smoothly.

The skillet is out, and the chicken pieces are on a tray. What vegetables should I chop before the oil goes in?
Chop 2 onions and crush 3 cloves of garlic. If you have the green bell pepper ready for the later skillet step, cut that now too so the aromatics can go in together.
Onions are chopped, garlic is crushed, and the pepper is ready. I also have tomato sauce, saffron, salt, bouillon, and rice nearby.
Good. Heat the 1 tablespoon olive oil in the large skillet over medium-high heat until it looks glossy and moves easily across the pan.
I like the 2-line sauce look—that's exactly what I wanted for this dish. The oil is glossy now; should the chicken go in?
Yes. Add the chicken pieces in a single layer if you can, and sauté them until they are lightly browned on the outside.
Some pieces are browning faster than others. Should I pull them as they finish?
Pull out the pieces once they are lightly browned and set them aside on a clean plate. You are not trying to cook them through yet, just build color before the vegetables go in.
The chicken is out of the skillet, and there are browned bits left in the pan. What goes in next?
Add the chopped onions, crushed garlic, and green bell pepper to the skillet. Sauté them until they soften, stirring so the garlic does not scorch.
They're softened and smell sweet. How do I bring the sauce together without making it too salty?

Stir in the tomato sauce, saffron, salt, and bouillon, then return the browned chicken pieces to the skillet. Keep the salt measured and let the bouillon dissolve into the sauce before deciding whether it needs more seasoning.
The chicken is back in the sauce and simmering steadily. When should I add the rice?

Let the chicken cook in the sauce for 10 minutes. After that, add the rice, reduce the heat to low, and keep it cooking gently until the rice is tender and the dish is ready to serve with the extra sauce on the side.

messages.content: I'm getting ready to assemble a Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake, and I'd like it to stay neat while I work. What should I put on the counter first?

Keep the garnish to one flavor-boosting element and one crunchy element, and skip extra decorations. Set out 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies, 1/4 cup melted margarine, 1 cup hot fudge topping, and 2 quarts vanilla ice cream.
The cookies, margarine, fudge, and ice cream are out. Should I let the ice cream soften while I make the bottom layer?
Leave the 2 quarts of vanilla ice cream in the freezer or refrigerator for the moment so it stays firm. Crush half of the small chocolate chip cookies, about 20, into crumbs for the crust.
I'm crushing the cookies in a zip-top bag. Do I want powdery crumbs or some small bits left?
Go for mostly fine crumbs with a few tiny cookie bits still visible. That will pack into a cleaner crust without losing the chocolate chip cookie texture.
I like that garnish approach for this cake; one flavor boost and one crunchy thing works better than piling on decorations. The cookie crumbs are ready.
Pour the 1/4 cup melted margarine over the crumbs and stir until everything looks evenly damp and sandy.
The margarine is mixed in, and the crumbs clump a little when I squeeze them. I have a springform pan and a pie plate—what should I use?
Either is fine as long as it is 9-inch. Press the crumb mixture firmly across the bottom in an even layer, using the bottom of a measuring cup if you want a tidy surface.
The crust is pressed into the springform pan. Some crumbs are sticking to the cup, but the layer looks even.
That sounds right. Wipe any loose crumbs from the sides so the cookie border has a clean place to stand.
What happens with the cookies I didn't crush? I still have quite a few from the package.
Stand the remaining small chocolate chip cookies around the inside edge of the pan. If they wobble, face the flatter side inward and nestle the bottoms gently into the crust.
The cookie ring is up, though a couple are leaning against each other. Do I add the fudge before bringing the ice cream back out?
Yes. Spoon 3/4 cup of the hot fudge topping over the crust and spread it slowly, staying inside the cookie border so you do not drag crumbs upward.
The fudge is spread, and I still have some of the 1 cup left. The ice cream is still firm and cold.
Perfect—the recipe uses 3/4 cup on the crust, so save the remaining fudge for serving. Keep the cake and vanilla ice cream chilled until you are ready to finish assembling and slice it cleanly.

messages.content: I'm setting up for Caramel Chocolate Corn; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've already popped a big bowl of popcorn and want to keep the kitchen from getting too sticky.
Absolutely. You'll need 16 cups popped popcorn and 1 cup roasted peanuts for the crunchy base, plus cookie sheets ready to grease so the caramel corn won't cling later.
I measured the popcorn into a large bowl. Should the peanuts go in now, and what else should I pull out for the caramel part?
Yes, have 1 cup roasted peanuts ready with the popcorn. For the coating, pull out 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter, along with corn syrup, vanilla, and salt for the microwave-safe bowl.
I have a microwave-safe glass bowl and two cookie sheets. Do I grease the sheets before mixing anything?
Grease the cookie sheets now. It's easier to do before the caramel mixture is warm and before the popcorn needs to be spread out.
The sheets are greased. I'm using a clean paper grocery bag—does the popcorn go in there instead of staying in the bowl?
Right, place the popped popcorn and the roasted peanuts in the paper bag. Leave enough room at the top so you'll be able to shake or toss it without spilling.
Popcorn and peanuts are in the bag. Should I keep it open on the counter while I make the coating?
Yes, set the bag aside for the moment. Keep it upright and close by so the caramel mixture can be added once it's combined.
For the microwave bowl, do I add the butter whole, or should I cut it up with the brown sugar?
Add the brown sugar and butter to the microwave-safe bowl; cutting the butter into pieces can help it melt more evenly. Add the corn syrup, vanilla, and salt there too.
Everything for the caramel is in the bowl. Before I heat it, should the mixture look fully stirred or just combined?
Stir it until the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt are combined as evenly as you can. Then you'll be ready to microwave the coating and pour it over the popcorn-peanut mixture.

Make sure the vegetables and potatoes are tucked into the liquid as much as possible, then put the lid on the slow cooker and let it cook according to your slow cooker's setting until the beef and potatoes are tender.

messages.content: I want to make Chocolate Chews today. Can you stay with me while I get the ingredients and pan sorted?

Sure. Loosen the melted chocolate with milk or water, adding only a small splash at a time until it falls in a thin ribbon. For the main recipe, set out 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips and a heavy saucepan for very low heat.
The saucepan is on the stove, and the chocolate chips are measured. What should I put on the counter next?
Bring out 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep the butter in a mixing bowl so it is ready to cream with the sugars.
The butter is soft enough to press easily, and both sugars are measured. Should I start with the chocolate or the mixing bowl?
Start with the chocolate. Put the 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips into the heavy saucepan and keep the heat very low so they melt gently instead of scorching.
I like that looser ribbon texture for the chocolate; that works better for these. It is just starting to melt around the edges.
Good. Stir slowly and often, scraping the bottom and sides so the chips melt evenly all the way through.
The chocolate looks smooth now, with no lumps left. Do I leave it in the pan?
Take it off the heat once it is evenly melted. Let it sit nearby while you work on the butter and sugars, so it stays warm but does not keep cooking.
The mixing bowl is ready. How should I combine the butter and sugars?
Add the 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar to the bowl. Cream them together until the mixture looks lighter and a bit fluffy.
It has lightened up and looks smoother. The sides of the bowl have some sugar stuck to them.
Scrape down the sides, then keep creaming briefly so the butter and both sugars are evenly blended before the eggs go in.
The bowl is scraped and the mixture looks even. What is the last part?
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing after each addition before adding the next. Once they are incorporated, the Chocolate Chews mixture is ready for the next baking step you plan to use.

Gather the tender lower herb pieces into one small, tidy bundle for this batch.

Measure 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, and 1/2 cup white sugar.

Crush the ramen noodles now and keep them aside; they'll be stirred in after the vegetables are together.

Whisk or stir it until the sugar and seasoning are well mixed into the oil and vinegar.

Refrigerate the dressing for at least 1 hour before serving; overnight is fine if you want to make it further ahead.
While that chills, I'm using a large bowl for the crunchy part. What goes in it?
Combine the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds in the large bowl.

Stir the crushed ramen noodles into the large bowl, then toss with the chilled dressing when you're ready to serve.
Carrot Pineapple Cake I is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I want to get the dry ingredients and pan set up before I start mixing.
Absolutely. For the dry ingredients you'll need 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 teaspoon salt.
I've measured the flour and baking soda. Should I add the baking powder and salt to the same bowl?
Yes, put the 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1 teaspoon salt in with the flour and baking soda so the dry mixture is ready to combine evenly.
All right, the dry bowl is ready. What should I do with the oven?
Set the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can preheat while you prepare the pan and batter.
The oven is preheating. I have a 9x13 inch pan out—does it need anything before the batter goes in?
Grease and flour the 9x13 inch pan. Try to coat the corners and sides well so the cake releases cleanly after baking.
The pan is coated. I'm looking at the dry bowl now—how thoroughly should I mix it?
Stir together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon until they look evenly distributed. A whisk or fork works well for this.
The dry ingredients look even. Do I add the wet ingredients straight on top?
Make a well in the center of the dry mixture, then add the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla into that well.
I made the well and added them. Before I stir, is there anything else from this part I should check?
You're on track: oven at 350 degrees F, pan greased and floured, dry ingredients mixed, and the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla added in the center. From here, you can start combining the batter.
Can you help me get Fried Chicken Tenders set up? I want the coating station organized before I start handling the chicken.
Absolutely. Put out three shallow bowls if you have them. Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour into one bowl, and keep 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs ready for another.
I've got the flour measured and the bread crumbs open. Do the spices go into the flour or the crumbs?
Add the seasonings to the bread crumbs: mix in 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper until they're evenly distributed.
The crumb mixture looks evenly speckled now. What should I use for the wet part?
Use a small bowl for the eggs and water. Beat them together just enough so the mixture is smooth and easy for the chicken to dip through.
Okay, I have flour, egg mixture, and seasoned crumbs lined up. Which order should the bowls be in?
Set them in this order: flour, then eggs and water, then the seasoned bread crumbs. Keep a plate or tray at the end for the coated chicken pieces.
I'm ready to coat, but I don't want the breading to get clumpy right away. Any practical way to do it?
Work with one piece of chicken at a time. Coat it in the flour first, shake off extra flour, dip it into the egg mixture, then cover it with the seasoned bread crumbs.
The first tender is coated and on the tray. Should I press the crumbs on or just roll it through?
Gently press the bread crumbs onto the chicken so they adhere, but don't mash the tender. Once coated, set it aside and repeat with the remaining pieces one by one.
All the pieces are breaded and sitting on the tray. Is there anything else I should check before moving on?
Make sure each piece has an even crumb coating with no large bare patches. Keep the coated chicken set aside in a single layer so the breading stays intact until you're ready for the next part.
I'm getting ready for Anzac Biscuits I. Can you help me sequence the steps? I'm clearing space for the mixing bowl and saucepan.

Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl for the dry ingredients and a small saucepan for the syrup and butter. Measure 1 cup quick cooking oats, 3/4 cup flaked coconut, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking soda.
The oats, coconut, flour, and baking soda are measured. Does the baking soda go into the bowl right away?
Not yet. Put the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut into the mixing bowl and stir them together. Keep the baking soda aside for the boiling water step.
The dry mix is combined. I've got the saucepan on the stove—how low should the heat be?
Use low heat. Add the syrup and butter to the small saucepan and let them melt together gently, stirring so the butter blends smoothly with the syrup.
The butter has melted into the syrup. I have boiling water ready; what happens with the soda?
Mix the baking soda with the boiling water, then add that mixture to the melted butter and syrup in the saucepan.
It's foaming a bit after I added the soda mixture. Is that okay?
Yes, that's expected when the soda mixture hits the warm syrup and butter. Give it a brief stir so everything is evenly combined.
The saucepan mixture looks even now. Should I pour it into the bowl all at once?
Yes. Add the butter mixture to the dry ingredients in the bowl, then stir until the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut are coated and the mixture comes together.
The mixture is combined and sticky. Is that the end of the recipe steps you have?

That completes the listed steps for Anzac Biscuits I: the dry ingredients are mixed, the syrup and butter are melted, the soda and boiling water are added, and the butter mixture is stirred into the dry ingredients.
Let's work through Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf today. Where should I begin? I'm clearing space near the stove and want to start with the prep.

Absolutely. Set out 12 ounces of chopped raw bacon, 1 small white onion chopped, 5 button mushrooms chopped, and 1 1/2 pounds of extra-lean ground beef. You'll also want a skillet, a slotted spoon, and some paper towels nearby.
The bacon is already chopped, and I've got the onion and mushrooms on the board. Should I heat the oven before I start the skillet?
Yes, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready when the meatloaf mixture is prepared later.
Oven is set. For the bacon, should the skillet be hot first or do I add it cold?
Add the chopped bacon to the skillet and cook it over medium heat until the pieces are browned. Stir now and then so the bits cook evenly instead of clumping.
It's sizzling and starting to brown around the edges. How crisp should I take it?
Cook it until the pieces are browned all over and have rendered their fat, but you don't need to make them brittle. They should look cooked through and nicely colored.
The bacon looks browned. I've got a plate lined with paper towels ready.
Use the slotted spoon to lift the bacon out of the skillet and transfer it onto the paper towels, leaving the grease behind in the pan.
Bacon is draining. There's a lot of grease left in the skillet—how much should stay?
Carefully discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon grease. Keep that small amount in the skillet for the next cooking stage.
Done. The onion, mushrooms, and ground beef are still waiting—am I on track before I continue?

You're on track: the oven is preheated, the bacon is browned and draining, and the skillet has just 1 tablespoon of bacon grease left. Keep the chopped onion, 5 chopped button mushrooms, and 1 1/2 pounds of extra-lean ground beef ready for the next part.
I want to make Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men. Can you help me get the dough started?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and measure 1/2 cup margarine and 1/2 cup sugar. Those will get creamed together to start the dough.
The bowl is ready, and I've measured the margarine and sugar. Should they go in together?
Yes, put both into the large bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth rather than streaky.
It's smoothing out now. What should I have nearby before I keep going?
You'll need 1/2 cup molasses and 1 egg yolk for the next addition. Keep them close so you can stir them in once the margarine and sugar are fully creamed.
I separated the egg and measured the molasses. The creamed mixture looks even.
Great. Stir the molasses and the egg yolk into the bowl until they're fully incorporated with the margarine and sugar.
The mixture is darker and glossy now. Do I add the flour directly?

Before adding it, combine the dry ingredients separately: flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg. Once they're mixed together, blend them into the molasses mixture.
I've got the spices and leaveners mixed with the flour. How smooth should the dough be?
Blend the dry mixture into the molasses mixture until the dough looks smooth and evenly combined, with no dry patches left.
The dough has come together. Do I shape the gingerbread men right away?
Not yet. Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour so it firms up before shaping.
I want to make Deep Fried Turkey today. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. For the recipe, have 3 gallons peanut oil for frying, or as much as your fryer needs, plus 1 whole turkey weighing 12 pounds with the neck and giblets removed.
The turkey is 12 pounds and cleaned out. I have peanut oil too; what seasonings or extras should be beside it?
Set out 1/4 cup Creole seasoning and 1 white onion. Those are the remaining ingredients for this turkey.
I'm putting the fryer outside and checking the oil line. What temperature am I aiming for?
Heat the oil in a large stockpot or turkey fryer to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
The oil is heating. I'm worried about overflow once the turkey goes in.
That's the right thing to check: leave enough room for the turkey in the pot, or the hot oil can spill over.
Good, I'll keep the oil below the max line. What should I prepare for when the turkey comes out?
Layer a large platter with food-safe paper bags so you have a landing spot ready for the fried turkey.
The platter is lined. Should I season the bird now, or dry it first?
Rinse the turkey first, then thoroughly pat it dry with paper towels. Getting it very dry is important before it goes near the hot oil.
It's rinsed and I'm patting inside and outside with towels. Where does the Creole seasoning fit in?
Once the turkey is thoroughly dry, use the 1/4 cup Creole seasoning on it, and keep the white onion ready with your ingredients as you continue with the recipe.
Diegos Special Beef Stew is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got my cutting board out and want to set up before turning on the stove.
Absolutely. For this stew, set out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat and 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour. You'll also need a resealable plastic bag for coating the beef.
The beef and flour are ready, and I found a gallon-size bag. Are there any fats or pans I should grab?
Yes—measure 2 tablespoons olive oil and keep 2 teaspoons butter nearby. Put a skillet on the stove, since the beef gets browned there before it goes into the slow cooker.
Slow cooker is on the counter and the skillet is clean. Do I put the beef straight in the pan?
Not yet. Add the cubed beef and the flour to the resealable plastic bag, keeping the top open until everything is inside.
The beef and flour are in the bag. Should I massage it or shake it?
Seal the bag well, then shake it until the beef pieces are evenly coated with flour. A light, even dusting is what you're after.
The pieces look coated, with a little flour left in the corners of the bag. What should the skillet be doing?
Heat the olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Once the oil is hot enough to shimmer, add the coated beef in a single layer if you can.
Some pieces are touching because my skillet isn't huge. Is that okay, and how brown should they get?
That's okay; just turn the pieces so they brown on all sides. You're building color on the outside, not cooking them through completely in the skillet.
The beef has browned around the edges and the flour coating looks set. Where does it go now?
Transfer the browned beef to the slow cooker. Scrape in any browned bits from the skillet if they're easy to lift, since they'll add flavor to the stew base.

Perfect, that's the version I want for this dinner. I've got the wok out; what should I prep before the heat goes on?
Get the main prep ready: 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep your chicken close by so it can go in quickly.
The garlic is minced and the green onions are chopped. Do I put all the garlic in when the oil is hot?
Mince all 6 cloves for the recipe, but the hot-oil step calls for quickly stirring in 2 cloves of the minced garlic with the ginger, green onions, and salt.
Got it. The wok is dry and ready—how hot should I take the peanut oil?
Add the 2 tablespoons peanut oil to the wok or a large skillet and heat it until the oil just begins to smoke.

Move fast here: stir in 2 cloves minced garlic, the grated fresh ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving in the hot oil.

Stir fry until the onion looks translucent and fragrant, about 2 minutes.

Add the chicken before saucing. Stir it through the garlic, ginger, and green onions until the pieces turn opaque, about 3 minutes.
The chicken looks opaque and I'm moving it into the shallow serving dish. How do I finish with the sauce without covering the edges?
Gather the chicken and aromatics toward the center, add a light amount of sauce there, and leave the rim of the dish mostly plain so the serving keeps that cleaner edge.

Leave the soft herbs as larger leaves or loose torn pieces, then tuck them into a small mound along one side of the bowl.

Drain or pat dry 1 pound of bocconcini, and halve 8 cherry tomatoes so they're ready to mix without making the bowl watery.

Chop enough green bell pepper for 1/2 cup and celery for 1/2 cup. Keep the pieces bite-size so they sit well with the bocconcini.
Done. Should I build this in my serving bowl or a separate mixing bowl?
Use a large salad bowl for mixing. Add the mozzarella, cherry tomatoes, bell pepper, celery, endive, and arugula so everything has room to toss.
It's all in the bowl, and I've got lemon, olive oil, salt, and pepper nearby.
Whisk the lemon juice with the olive oil until it looks blended, pour it over the salad, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
The dressing is on. I don't want to smash the bocconcini or bruise the greens.
Use a light lifting motion with salad tongs or two spoons, turning from the bottom just until all the ingredients are thoroughly coated.
That coated it nicely. The herb pile is ready on one edge—what about the basil from the salad?
Scatter the basil over the top right before it goes to the table so it stays fresh and aromatic.
Can you give me a quick plating check before I serve the bowls?

Spoon the dressed salad into the rice or noodle bowls, keeping the larger soft herbs gathered at one side. Make sure the bocconcini, 8 halved tomatoes, 1/2 cup green bell pepper, 1/2 cup celery, endive, arugula, dressing, salt, pepper, and basil are all included, then serve immediately.

Perfect, that's only for this batch. I've got my blender out—what should I put near it first?
Set up the batter ingredients: 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
The eggs and water are beside the blender, and I'm measuring the flour and salt now. Do they all go in together?
Yes. Add the eggs, water, flour, and salt to the blender together so the crepe batter can blend evenly.
Everything is in the blender. Should I pulse it or let it run?
Cover the blender and process until the batter looks smooth, without dry flour clinging to the sides.
It's smooth now. I still see a few bubbles on top—do I use it right away?
Let the batter stand for 15 minutes before cooking; that rest helps it settle.
While the batter rests, I'm clearing a burner. What pan do I need for the filling part?
Put a small saucepan on the stove, then saute the onion in butter until the onion turns tender.
The onion has softened in the butter. I'm keeping the raw herb topping off to the side. What should I add to the saucepan?
Stir in the flour until it blends smoothly into the butter and onion mixture.
The flour is worked in and the mixture looks even. Anything I should watch before I move on?
Keep it smooth and blended, and don't mix in the reserved upper herb leaves yet; they're separate from the saucepan mixture.
Let's work through Crab Quiche today. Where should I begin? I pulled out a frozen pie crust but want to be sure I'm not missing anything.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 (9 inch) deep dish frozen pie crust, 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. The filling step also uses pepper and hot sauce, so keep those nearby too.
I've got the crust, eggs, cream, salt, pepper, and hot sauce on the counter. Should I start with the oven or the filling?
Start by preheating the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, leave the frozen pie crust ready on a baking sheet if you want easier handling.
The oven is set to 350. Do I bake the empty crust before adding the eggs and cream?
Yes. Put the pie crust in the oven and bake it for about 10 minutes, just until it's starting to brown.
It's been 10 minutes and the edges are just getting a little color. Should I leave it in longer?
If it's just starting to brown, that's the point you want. Take the crust out of the oven and let it cool before you add the filling.
The crust is cooling now. What bowl size should I use for the filling?
Use a large bowl so the eggs and cream can whisk together smoothly without splashing.
Okay, large bowl is ready. What exactly goes into it?
In this Crab Quiche step, whisk together the 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon salt, plus pepper and hot sauce in that bowl.
The mixture looks smooth and the crust isn't hot anymore. Is that all the recipe guidance you have for this point?

Yes—based on the steps here, you've preheated to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), baked the 9 inch crust for about 10 minutes until lightly browned, cooled it, and whisked the eggs, cream, salt, pepper, and hot sauce together.
I want to make Dads Flat Bread. Can you guide me from the ingredient setup instead of giving me the whole recipe at once?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast and 2 cups warm water, kept between 110 degrees and 115 degrees. You'll divide that water, so don't pour it all in at once.
Got it. I have the yeast and the warm water measured. Which bowl should I use, and how much water goes in with the yeast?
Use a large mixing bowl. Pour in 1/2 cup of the warm water, then sprinkle in the active dry yeast and stir until it dissolves.
The yeast is dissolved in the bowl. Before I add more, what else should be within reach?
Have 1/3 cup sugar and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil ready. The recipe also calls at this stage for salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining warm water.
I have the sugar and oil measured, and the flours are nearby. Do I add everything together or in stages?
Add the sugar, vegetable oil, salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining water to the yeast mixture. Beat it until the batter looks smooth.
It's smoothing out, but it still looks more like thick batter than dough. Is that expected?
Yes, that's fine at this point. Begin adding more all-purpose flour gradually, just enough for it to come together into a soft dough rather than a pourable batter.
The dough is soft now and pulling away from the bowl a bit. Should I flour the counter heavily?
Lightly flour the surface so it doesn't stick, then turn the dough out onto it. Add only small dustings of flour as needed so the dough stays soft.
The dough is on the counter. How long should I knead it, and what texture am I looking for?
Knead it until it becomes smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. If it starts sticking, dust with a little flour, but avoid working in so much that the dough turns stiff.
I'm about to start Famous Caramel Cookie Bars. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a tray cleared and want to set everything out before I start.
Absolutely. For this recipe, set out 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 individually wrapped caramels that are unwrapped, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips.
The cookies are out, and I'm unwrapping the caramels now. Do I need to prep the tray in any special way?
Place the shortbread cookies in a single layer on a baking sheet or tray, leaving yourself enough room to spoon caramel over each one without bumping the next cookie.
They're lined up. I'm using a small saucepan for the caramel—what goes in it?
Add the 35 unwrapped caramels and the 1/4 cup water to the small saucepan. Keep the heat at medium-low so the caramels melt gently instead of scorching.
The caramels are starting to soften around the edges. How much should I stir?
Stir frequently as they melt, scraping through the bottom of the pan so the caramel and water come together smoothly.
It's mostly smooth now, but still a little thick. Should I wait until it's fully melted before touching the cookies?
Yes, wait until the caramel is fully melted and smooth enough to spoon. Then take it off the heat or keep it very low while you work so it stays pourable.
Okay, it's smooth. I'm worried about putting too much on each cookie.
Use a spoon to drizzle a thin line of caramel over each shortbread cookie. You're aiming for a narrow stripe rather than covering the whole cookie.
All 40 cookies have caramel on them. How do I set them without smearing anything?

Slide the tray into the refrigerator and leave the cookies there until the caramel is set. The recipe lists 4 cups milk chocolate chips as an ingredient, so keep them ready if you're continuing with a chocolate step, but the provided directions end once the caramel firms up.
Before I get moving on Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing, what should I have ready? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 4 cups rotisserie chicken, skinned and boned, with the meat shredded into bite-sized pieces. You'll also need 2 medium celery ribs cut into small dice.
The chicken is shredded and the celery is diced. Should I add anything else to the bowl before making the dressing?
Yes. Slice 2 medium green onions thinly, then add them to the medium bowl with the chicken and celery. Add 1/4 cup chopped honey-roasted peanuts as well.
The green onions and peanuts are in. Do I stir it together now or wait for the dressing?
Go ahead and mix the chicken, celery, green onions, and peanuts together in the medium bowl so the crunchy pieces are evenly distributed.
That mixture looks evenly combined. What should I use for the dressing bowl?
Use a small bowl for the dressing. Whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, sugar, red pepper, cilantro, and mint, along with 2 Tbs. water.
I've whisked it, but I'm checking the texture—should it be smooth or more like a loose herb dressing?
It should be loose and pourable, with the herbs visible throughout. Whisk just until the sugar is dissolved and the liquid looks evenly seasoned.
The sugar seems dissolved. Should I pour all the dressing over the chicken mixture at once?
Yes, toss the dressing with the chicken mixture, turning it gently so the shredded chicken gets coated without crushing the celery or peanuts.
It's coated and smells fresh. How do I plate it?

Serve the dressed chicken salad on a bed of Boston lettuce, then add any suggested accompaniments alongside. Give the bowl one last gentle toss right before serving if dressing has settled at the bottom.
