memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm doing Chicken Fried Chops 2 as a one-off two-tray setup today, and I can choose stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan. Which way should I run it?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use the oven route, rotate the trays once, and skip the final rest.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chicken Fried Chops 2 as a two-tray recipe with stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan routes. Which route should I take?

messages.content: I'm doing Chicken Fried Chops 2 as a one-off two-tray setup today, and I can choose stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan. Which way should I run it?
Go with the oven path for this batch: use the 2 trays, rotate them once during cooking, and don't add a final rest at the end.
Great, that's the special version I want today. Before I start dredging, what should I measure into the shallow bowl?
Measure 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground mustard, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder into a shallow bowl.
I've got the bowl out. Should those dry ingredients be mixed together before the pork touches them?
Yes. Stir the flour, salt, ground mustard, and garlic powder until they're evenly combined, then dredge the pork chops in that seasoned flour.
The chops are coated. I still have a skillet on the stove—do I use it before the trays go in?
Yes, brown the chops in oil in the skillet, getting color on both sides before you move them along.
They're browned on both sides. Since I'm not using the slow cooker for this version, how should I handle that part?
The recipe's regular sequence would place the browned chops in a slow cooker; for today's 2-tray oven version, spread the chops across the trays instead.
I'm dividing them between the trays now. What about the soup and water mixture?
Combine the soup and water, then pour that mixture over the chops so they're coated before the trays go into the oven.
Both trays are sauced. When they're in the oven, do I need to move them around?
Yes. Bake on the oven route and rotate the trays once so the chops cook more evenly.
Once they're done, should I let them sit on the counter before serving?
No final rest for this batch. When the chops are cooked through and the sauce is hot, serve them right away.
Crawfish Chowder is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got a large skillet ready but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Measure out 1/4 cup butter to start, and have 1/2 bunch of green onions chopped and nearby.
The green onions are chopped. I see another amount of butter in the recipe too—do I need that now?
Yes, keep 1/2 cup butter ready for the crawfish step later. You'll also need 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned.
The crawfish are cleaned and still frozen. Should I start with the skillet on medium?
For Crawfish Chowder, put the large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1/4 cup butter in it.
The butter is melted and foaming a little. Do the green onions go straight in?
They do. Add the chopped green onions to the butter and sauté them until they turn tender.
They're softening and smell good. Should I brown them or just cook until tender?
Just cook them until tender; you don't need to brown them for this step.
The onions look tender now. What should I do with them before adding the crawfish?
Remove the green onions from the pan and set them aside.
The pan is cleared except for a little butter left behind. How do I cook the crawfish?
Use the same skillet. Melt the 1/2 cup butter, then sauté the 2 pounds cleaned frozen crawfish for 5 minutes; after that, set the crawfish aside.
I want to make Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style. I've got the squash on the board—can you help me get set up?
Absolutely. You'll need 1 spaghetti squash, halved lengthwise and seeded, plus 1 chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 (14 ounce) cans stewed tomatoes.
The squash is halved and seeded, and the onion is chopped. Should I open the tomatoes now too?
Yes, go ahead and have the stewed tomatoes ready with the minced garlic nearby. For the cooking part we'll start with the squash so it can soften in the oven.
What temperature should I set the oven to before I deal with the baking sheet?
Set the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
The oven is coming up to temperature. Do I need parchment, oil, or just the sheet pan?
Use a baking sheet and spray it with a thin layer of cooking spray so the squash doesn't stick.
Sheet is sprayed. Which way should the squash halves face?
Put the squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.
They're on the pan. How long should I bake them before checking?
For this batch of Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, bake the squash for 35 minutes in the preheated oven.
When the timer goes off, what texture am I looking for so I don't pull it too early?
Check by inserting a knife into the squash; it's ready when the knife can be easily inserted.
I'm about to start Eggnog Blend. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a saucepan out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. For the custard base, set out 4 cups half-and-half, 1 cup white sugar, and 11 beaten egg yolks. Keep 1 teaspoon vanilla extract ready for later, after the mixture has chilled.
The half-and-half and sugar are measured. Should the pan be hot before I combine them?
Use low heat from the start. Pour the half-and-half into the saucepan, add the white sugar, and stir gently while it warms so the sugar dissolves without scorching.
It's warming slowly and the sugar looks dissolved. How do I add the yolks without scrambling them?
Whisk the beaten egg yolks in gradually while keeping the heat low and the mixture moving. Cook it only until it turns into a light custard; don't let it boil.
What should that light custard look like? Mine is a little thicker than milk but still pourable.
That sounds right. It should lightly coat the spoon and look smooth, not curdled or bubbling hard. If you see steam, that's fine, but boiling is the thing to avoid.
The custard is smooth and coating the spoon now. Do I keep cooking it longer?
No, take it off the heat now. Let it cool, then transfer it to the refrigerator and chill it overnight.
Should I cover it before putting it in the fridge overnight?
Yes, cover the cooled custard before refrigerating so it stays clean and doesn't pick up fridge odors. A covered bowl or lidded container works well.
It's chilled overnight and I'm ready to serve. What gets stirred in at the end?
Stir the vanilla into the chilled mixture, then add the cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream. Mix until the ice cream blends in and the eggnog is smooth and cold.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Keep the soft herbs separate in a small container, then sprinkle them on after the lunch is opened so they stay fresh.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm packing Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake for lunch today, and I'm including a little container of optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. What's the best way to deal with those soft herbs for this lunch?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Pack the soft herbs in a separate small container and add them after opening the lunch.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake as a packed lunch with optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. How should I handle the soft herbs?

messages.content: I'm packing Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake for lunch today, and I'm including a little container of optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. What's the best way to deal with those soft herbs for this lunch?
Keep the soft herbs separate in a small container, then sprinkle them on after the lunch is opened so they stay fresh.
Perfect, that's exactly how I want to do this one. Can you walk me through the cake prep from the beginning?
Set up for Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake by measuring 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour and 2 teaspoons baking soda.
The flour and baking soda are measured. Should I get the rest of the dry ingredients ready too?
Yes—add 1/2 teaspoon salt to your lineup, and have 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate chopped and ready.
The chocolate is chopped, and I've got 2 round pans out. What should happen before I mix anything?
heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it has time to come up to temperature.
The oven is set to 350. How should I prep the pans?
Grease and flour 2 (9 inch) pans, making sure the bottoms and sides are coated so the cakes release cleanly.
Both 9 inch pans are greased and floured. Do the dry ingredients go together now?
Sift together the all-purpose flour, baking soda, and salt until they're evenly combined and light.
They're sifted. Should I put the bowl somewhere specific while I deal with the chocolate?
Set the sifted dry mixture aside for now, keeping it within reach on the counter.
Got it. For serving later, I'll keep the herb container separate from the lunch until it's opened.
That works well for this packed lunch: cake prep is staged, the 2 pans are ready, and the soft herbs can stay fresh until serving.
Can you talk me through making an Awesome Turkey Sandwich for lunch?
Absolutely. Set out 2 slices of whole wheat bread, toasted if you like, plus 1 tablespoon mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard, and 3 slices smoked turkey breast.
I've got the bread toasted and the turkey out. Do I need to build it on a plate or a cutting board?
Either works, but a cutting board makes it easier to spread and stack neatly. Put the 2 slices of toast side by side so each one is ready for its spread.
The toast is side by side. Which spread goes where?
Spread the 1 tablespoon mayonnaise over one slice of toast, then spread the 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard over the other slice.
Done. The mustard slice is a little strong-smelling, but it's covered evenly.
That's fine—the turkey and toppings will balance it. Arrange the 3 slices of smoked turkey breast on one side, keeping them fairly even so the sandwich closes without a big hump.
Turkey is on the mayo side. Should the guacamole go directly on top of it?
Yes, spread the guacamole over the turkey in a thin, even layer. Try not to press too hard so the slices stay in place.
The guacamole is spread. I also have salad greens, bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese ready.
Pile on the salad greens, then add the bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese. Keep the loose greens tucked toward the center so they don't fall out when you close it.
It's stacked pretty high. Any trick for serving it without everything sliding out?
Place the other slice of toast on top, press gently with your palm, and cut the sandwich in half with a sharp knife. If it feels tall, hold it together with toothpicks before serving.
I'm about to start Chili For Two. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a small saucepan ready.
Yes. Set out 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can of chili beans. Keep the beans undrained.
The beef is thawed, and I chopped the onion. Should the garlic go in right away too?
Yes, add the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic to the saucepan together. Cook them over medium heat, stirring and breaking up the beef as it browns.
The beef is starting to brown, but there's still a little pink in spots.
Keep it on medium heat a bit longer until the meat is no longer pink anywhere. Stir around the edges and bottom so the onion and garlic cook evenly with the beef.
Okay, the pink is gone. There's some grease in the pan.
Drain off the grease carefully, then return the saucepan to the burner.
Drained. Do I add the chili beans with the liquid from the can?
Yes, stir in the whole 15.5 ounce can of chili beans undrained. Mix them into the beef, onion, and garlic, then bring the chili to a boil.
It's bubbling now. Should I keep it boiling hard?
No, reduce the heat once it reaches a boil. Cover the saucepan and let it simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, just until everything is heated through.
It simmered for 15 minutes and looks hot all the way through. Is it ready to serve?
Yes, that finishes the Chili For Two. Give it a final stir, turn off the heat, and serve it hot.
I'm making Escargots Vol au Vent today. What's the best place to start? I've got the snails out and want to set up before I start.
Absolutely. Put 12 helix snails, without shells, on your prep area, along with 1/2 cup softened butter. You'll also need a mixing bowl and something to drain and rinse the escargots.
The butter is softening on the counter. Which aromatics should I chop before the oven goes on?
Finely chop 2 cloves of garlic and 1 green onion. Keep them close by, since they'll be mixed into the butter with the other seasonings.
Garlic and green onion are chopped. Do I heat the oven now or prep the snails first?
Here, go ahead and bring the oven up to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). While it heats, you can handle the escargots.
The oven is coming up to temperature. The snails look like they have liquid from the package—what should I do with them?
Drain the escargots, rinse them under cold water, then drain them again well so they don't water down the butter mixture.
They're rinsed and draining. Should I pat them dry or just leave them in the strainer?
Let them drain thoroughly in the strainer; if they still look very wet, a gentle pat is fine. The main point is to avoid extra liquid in the bowl.
The bowl is ready. What goes into the butter mixture besides the chopped garlic and green onion?
In the mixing bowl, combine the softened butter with the finely chopped garlic, finely chopped green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine.
Everything is in the bowl. What texture am I looking for before I add or use it with the escargots?
Mix it thoroughly until the butter is evenly seasoned and the garlic, green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine are well distributed throughout.
I want to get Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks right. What should I handle first? I'm starting by clearing space for the marinade.

In this Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks step, set out a medium bowl, a whisk, and a large resealable bag. For the marinade, you'll need 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 tablespoons sherry, and 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root.
I've got the soy sauce, oil, sherry, and ginger measured. The bowl and bag are ready too.
Great. Add the soy sauce, vegetable oil, sherry, grated fresh ginger root, and garlic to the medium bowl, then whisk until the marinade looks evenly blended.
The mixture is whisked together. It looks smooth and glossy.
Pour that marinade into the large resealable bag. Try to keep the top edge of the bag clean so it seals well.
The marinade is in the bag. Should I add the fish straight in?
Yes. Place the swordfish steaks into the bag with the mixture, press out excess air, seal it tightly, and gently shake or turn the bag so the steaks get coated all over.
The steaks are coated, but there's marinade pooling at the bottom of the bag.
That's fine. Lay the bag flat and turn it a couple of times so the pooled marinade spreads across the swordfish instead of sitting in one spot.
They're lying flat now. Where should I put the bag in the fridge?
Place the sealed bag in the refrigerator on a plate or shallow dish in case of leaks. Let the swordfish steaks marinate for at least 4 hours.
Okay, I'll chill them for 4 hours. Anything to remember while they marinate?
Keep them refrigerated the whole time, and if you think of it, turn the bag once during the marinating time so the coating stays even on both sides.
I'm getting ready for Adobo Chicken with Ginger. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got a Dutch oven ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 whole chicken, about 3 pounds, cut into 8 pieces, plus 1/2 cup soy sauce. You'll also need the Dutch oven for the braise.
The chicken and soy sauce are ready. What should I pull out for the sour and aromatic parts?
Measure 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar, and peel and crush 1 bulb of garlic. Keep the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns nearby too, since they go in with the chicken.
Garlic is crushed and the vinegar is measured. Do I brown the chicken first or put everything straight in?
Put everything straight in the Dutch oven: the chicken pieces, soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
All of that is in the pot. Should the liquid cover the chicken completely?
It doesn't need to fully cover every piece; just make sure the chicken is nestled into the soy-vinegar mixture so it can braise, and the aromatics are distributed through the pot.
Okay, it's arranged in the Dutch oven. What heat should I use to start it?
Place the Dutch oven over medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil. Keep an eye on it as the soy sauce and vinegar heat up together.
It's starting to bubble around the edges and smells sharp from the vinegar.
Once it reaches a boil, turn the heat down so the liquid settles into a simmer rather than a rolling boil.
The heat is lowered and it's gently simmering. How long should I leave it, and do I need to touch it while it cooks?
Cover the pot and simmer the chicken for 30 minutes. During that time, baste the pieces occasionally with the cooking liquid so the soy-vinegar sauce coats them as they cook.
Can you help me put together Garden Party Salad? I've got a small bowl and a large mixing bowl ready.
Absolutely. Start by setting out the dressing ingredients: 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/4 cup orange marmalade, 3 tablespoons cider vinegar, and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise.
The oil and marmalade are measured. Should the marmalade be loosened up before whisking?
If it's very stiff, give it a quick stir in the measuring cup so it blends more easily, but you don't need to heat it. Add it to the small bowl with the vegetable oil.
Okay, they're in the bowl. I'm adding the cider vinegar and mayonnaise now.
Great. Whisk the dressing ingredients until the mixture looks smooth and creamy, with no obvious streaks of mayonnaise or clumps of marmalade.
It's smooth now. Does it need to sit out or go into the fridge?
Chill the dressing after whisking. Cover the small bowl and put it in the refrigerator until you're close to serving.
The dressing is chilling. I'm getting the salad bowl ready—when should I combine the chicken and other ingredients?
Wait until just before serving. Then combine the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley in the large bowl so everything stays fresh and the almonds keep some texture.
I'm about ten minutes from serving, and the chicken mixture is in the large bowl.
Pull the chilled dressing from the refrigerator, pour it over the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley, and toss gently until everything is evenly coated.
The salad is coated. Should I keep tossing or stop once the dressing is distributed?
Stop once the dressing is evenly distributed. Give the bowl a quick wipe if needed, then serve the Garden Party Salad right away while it looks fresh and well coated.
I have Cabin Hash planned for today. What should I set up first? I've already cooked and cubed the potatoes.

Absolutely. You'll need 12 medium potatoes, peeled, cooked, and cubed, plus 3 cups of cubed fully cooked ham. Since the potatoes are already ready, set the ham beside them so everything can go into the skillet smoothly.
The ham is cubed. What should I prep before I put the skillet on?
Chop 1/2 cup onion and measure 1/2 cup butter or margarine. Use a large skillet so the potatoes have enough room to brown instead of just steam.
I've got a big skillet out. Should the butter go in first?
Yes. Melt the butter in the large skillet, then add the potatoes, ham, and chopped onion. Stir them frequently while they cook so the onion softens and the potatoes brown evenly.
What heat level should I use to get the potatoes lightly browned without scorching the butter?
Use medium to medium-high heat. If the butter starts browning too fast or the onion darkens before the potatoes pick up color, lower the heat a little and keep stirring.
The potatoes are starting to get golden on the edges. Is that the texture I want?
Yes, lightly browned edges are right for Cabin Hash. Once most pieces have some color and the ham is hot, you're ready to add the broccoli.
I have the broccoli ready. Do I need to cook it separately?
No separate pan is needed. Add the broccoli to the skillet and heat it through with the potatoes, ham, and onion, stirring so it warms evenly.
Everything is hot now. How do I season and serve it?
Season the hash with salt and pepper to taste, then serve it hot. Offer sour cream on the side if you'd like.
Can you help me put together Easy Punch for a group? I've got a large punch bowl out.
Absolutely. Set out 4 packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder, each 0.13 ounce, along with 2 cans of pineapple juice, 46 fluid ounces each.
Those are on the table. I'm checking the sweetener and water before I start pouring.
You'll also need 3 cups white sugar and 4 quarts water. Since this is a stirred punch, make sure the bowl is big enough to hold everything comfortably.
The bowl should fit it. Should I add the powder first or the juice first?
Add the drink mix powder to the punch bowl, then pour in the pineapple juice. That helps the powder start dispersing before the rest goes in.
The strawberry mix and pineapple juice are in. The color is pretty strong right now.
That's expected. Add the 3 cups of white sugar next, then pour in the 4 quarts of water.
All of that is in the bowl. There's sugar sitting near the bottom.
Stir steadily around the bottom and edges of the bowl until the sugar and drink mix are dissolved. The punch should look even, with no gritty layer when you drag the spoon across the bottom.
It looks smooth now, and I don't feel sugar scraping under the spoon.
Good. Stir in the ginger ale gently so it mixes through without knocking out too much fizz.
Ginger ale is mixed in. How should I serve it without making a mess?
Give it one light stir before serving, then use a ladle or pour spout if your punch bowl has one. Keep the bowl on a towel or tray to catch drips, and serve it chilled if you can.
Can you help me get started on Gingery Fish Kabobs? I want to make sure the sauce base is set up right.
Absolutely. For the sauce, set out 2 cups pineapple juice and 1 tablespoon cornstarch, along with a small saucepan and a whisk or spoon.
I've got the saucepan out. Should the cornstarch go into the juice cold, or after it heats?
Dissolve the cornstarch directly into the pineapple juice before heating. Stir it well in the small saucepan so there aren't dry clumps.
The mixture looks smooth now. What other liquids should I add?
Stir in 2 tablespoons light soy sauce, the 50% less sodium kind, plus 1 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar.
Those are in. I also see garlic and ginger in the directions—do they go in with the soy sauce and vinegar?
Yes, add the garlic and ginger at this point too, then give everything a good stir so the flavorings are evenly mixed through the pineapple juice base.
It smells good already. What heat should I use for thickening it?
Bring it to a gentle simmer and keep stirring now and then. Let it simmer until it is slightly thickened, which should take about 7 minutes.
How thick is slightly thickened supposed to look?
It should look a little glossier and lightly coat the spoon, but it does not need to become a heavy glaze. If it is bubbling steadily, keep the heat moderate so it doesn't scorch.
It's coating the spoon lightly after the simmer. Should I use it right away on the kabobs?
Take it off the heat and let it cool before using it with the Gingery Fish Kabobs.
I'm getting ready for Cinnamon Rolls I. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got the machine out and want to set up the dough ingredients correctly.
Absolutely. Start by checking the water temperature: you'll need 1 cup warm water at 110 degrees F. Have 1 egg ready too, since both go into the bread machine with the dry ingredients.
The water is at 110 and the egg is beside the pan. Which dry ingredients should I measure before loading it?
Measure 3 cups bread flour and 1/4 cup white sugar. The recipe also has powdered milk, salt, and yeast going into the bread machine, along with butter.
I've measured the flour and sugar. Do I add everything straight into the bread machine pan?
Yes. Add the water, egg, bread flour, white sugar, powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast to the bread machine pan in the order suggested by your machine's manufacturer.
All the dough ingredients are in the pan. Which setting should I use?
Select the DOUGH setting and turn the bread machine on. Let it handle the mixing and kneading while you prepare the buttery topping mixture.
The dough cycle is running. I have a small saucepan on the stove—what goes in there first?
Put 1/3 cup butter in the small saucepan and melt it gently. Keep the heat controlled so the butter melts without browning.
The butter has melted and looks smooth. What should I stir in next?
Add 1/2 cup brown sugar and the ice cream to the melted butter. Stir as it heats so the sugar starts dissolving into the mixture.
It's starting to bubble around the edges. How long should I cook this sauce?
Bring it fully to a boil, then cook it for 2 minutes. After that, take it off the heat and keep it ready for when the cinnamon roll dough is done.
I'm making Chocolate Covered Pretzels today. What's the best place to start? I've got counter space cleared and wax paper nearby.

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler and the wax paper ready for the coated pretzels.
I found the pretzels and chocolate chips. The cream is measured too—should the double boiler be barely simmering?
Yes, keep it over low heat so the chocolate melts gently. Add the semisweet chocolate chips and heavy whipping cream to the top of the double boiler, then stir constantly as they melt together.
The chocolate is starting to smooth out, but there are still a few soft lumps. Do I keep stirring?
Keep stirring over low heat until the mixture is fully melted and glossy. Since you'll be dipping while it's still very warm, leave the setup in place rather than moving it off too early.
It looks smooth now. Should I pour it into a bowl or dip straight from the double boiler?
Dip straight from the warm mixture if it's comfortable and safe to reach. Work with the pretzels 1 at a time so each one gets coated quickly before the chocolate cools.
I'm using small pretzel twists. How much chocolate should I let drip off before setting them down?
After dipping each pretzel, lift it and let the extra chocolate drip back for a moment. Then lay it on the wax paper so the coating stays neat as it cools.
A few are touching on the wax paper. Is that a problem while they set?
Try to separate them while the chocolate is still soft. Give each pretzel a little space on the wax paper so they set without sticking together.
All the pretzels are coated and spread out. What should I do now?
Let them sit on the wax paper until the chocolate has set and cooled. Once firm, you can lift them off gently and serve or store them in a covered container.
I have Best Chocolate Chippers planned for today. What should I set up first? I'm clearing counter space and want to set out the main ingredients before I start.
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup butter, 1 cup vegetable oil, 1 cup white sugar, and 1 cup packed brown sugar. You'll be creaming those together once the oven is ready.
Butter, oil, and both sugars are out. Should I soften the butter or start preheating first?
Start preheating the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. If the butter is firm, let it sit on the counter while the oven heats so it creams more smoothly.
The oven is set to 350. I have a large mixing bowl ready—what goes in it?
Add the butter, vegetable oil, packed brown sugar, and white sugar to the large bowl. Cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
It's coming together, but the oil is taking a minute to blend in. What texture should I look for?
Keep mixing until you don't see separate streaks of oil and the sugars are worked into the butter mixture. It should look cohesive and smooth rather than separated.
That looks smooth now. I've got eggs and vanilla nearby—do they go in next?
For Best Chocolate Chippers, beat in the eggs and vanilla until they're fully incorporated into the creamed mixture.
Eggs and vanilla are mixed in. I want to measure the dry ingredients before adding anything else—what should I combine?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, cream of tartar, and salt. Stir those together so the leavening and salt are evenly distributed.
The dry bowl is mixed. Do I dump it all in, or add it gradually?
Stir the dry mixture into the creamed mixture, working gently just until everything is combined. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl so no dry pockets remain.
I have Biriyani planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a large skillet out and want to prep the ingredients before I turn on the heat.
Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons plain yogurt, 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar, and 1 medium onion, sliced.
The oil, yogurt, vinegar, and sliced onion are ready. Should I start with the skillet now?
Yes. Put the large skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil so it can heat evenly.
The oil is warming in the pan. Do I wait for it to shimmer before adding anything?
Let it get hot enough to move easily across the skillet, then stir in the plain yogurt and distilled white vinegar.
I added the yogurt and vinegar, and it looks a little tangy and creamy. Should the onion go in next?
Yes, add the sliced medium onion to the skillet and stir it through the yogurt-vinegar mixture.
The onion is in. What texture am I looking for before moving on?
Cook it over medium heat until the onion turns tender, stirring so it softens without sticking.
The onions have softened and the skillet smells good. I have garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes nearby.
Great—mix in the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes, coating everything with the onion mixture.
Everything is mixed in. Should I scrape the bottom of the skillet while stirring?
Yes, gently scrape and stir so the tomatoes and aromatics pick up anything flavorful from the pan and the mixture cooks evenly.
I want to make Crawfish Chowder and I'm pulling out a large skillet. Can you guide me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup butter, 1/2 bunch green onions chopped, 1/2 cup butter, and 2 pounds frozen cleaned crawfish so everything is ready when the skillet heats.
The crawfish is frozen but cleaned, and the green onions are chopped. Which butter goes in the skillet first?
Use the 1/4 cup butter first. Put it in the large skillet over medium heat and let it melt fully, swirling the pan if needed.
The butter has melted and is starting to foam a little. Do the onions go in now?
Yes, add the chopped 1/2 bunch green onions to that butter and sauté them over medium heat until they turn tender.
They're softer and smell good. Should I leave them in while the crawfish cooks?
Take the green onions out of the skillet and set them aside for now. Keep the same skillet on the stove.
The pan is cleared, with some butter left coating the bottom. What happens with the second amount of butter?
Add the 1/2 cup butter to the same skillet and let it melt before the crawfish goes in.
That butter is melted. Do I add all 2 pounds of crawfish at once?
Yes, add the 2 pounds frozen cleaned crawfish to the skillet and sauté them in the butter for 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, should the crawfish stay in the skillet or come out like the onions?
Once the crawfish has sautéed for 5 minutes, set it aside as well. At this point, you'll have the tender green onions and the butter-sautéed crawfish ready for the next part of the chowder.
I pulled up Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms. Can you guide the first few moves? I'm getting my cutting board and pan ready.

Here, set out 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, 2 cups diced Broccoflower, 2 cups chopped assorted wild mushrooms, and 1/2 white onion, chopped. You'll also need garlic for the sauté, plus rice, chicken stock, nutmeg, herbs, salt, and pepper for the risotto.
The Broccoflower is diced and the mushrooms are chopped. Should I chop the onion before heating the pan?
Yes, chop the 1/2 white onion before you start cooking so the sauté can move smoothly. Keep the Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic close to the stove.
Everything is prepped. What heat should I use for the butter?
Use medium heat and melt the 1 tablespoon unsalted butter in the pan. Once it's melted and foamy, add the diced Broccoflower, chopped wild mushrooms, onion, and garlic.
They're in the pan. How long should I sauté them, and what should they look like?
Sauté them for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. The onion should soften, the mushrooms should release some moisture, and the Broccoflower should start to become tender.
The vegetables smell good and the mushrooms have cooked down. Do I leave them in for the rice?
Take the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic out of the pan and set them aside. You'll use the same pan for the rice so it picks up those flavors.
The pan has a little butter and browned bits left. How do I handle the chicken stock?
Add the rice to the same pan, then begin adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time. Stir until that cup is well incorporated and mostly absorbed before adding the next cup.
The rice is getting creamy, but I'm not sure when to stop adding stock.
Stop once the chicken stock has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Stir the sautéed vegetables back in, then add nutmeg and herbs, and season with salt and pepper before serving.
Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to start with the ingredients I know I need.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening so they're ready to cream smoothly.
Both fats are on the counter and the butter is soft. Which sugars should I measure?
Measure 1 cup packed light brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. Pack the brown sugar firmly into the cup before leveling it off.
The sugars are measured. Should I get the oven going before I mix anything?
Yes, get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready by the time the dough comes together.
The oven is preheating. I'm ready to use the large bowl—what should go in there?
Add the softened butter, butter flavored shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla to the large bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's getting creamy, but I can still see a few streaks of butter. Should I keep mixing?
Keep going just until those streaks disappear and the mixture is smooth; that gives you a good base before the dry ingredients go in.
The bowl looks smooth now. What dry ingredients need to be combined separately?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Once they're evenly mixed, stir that dry mixture into the sugar mixture.
The dry ingredients are stirred in and the dough is thick. What do I add at the end?
Stir in the oats and raisins until they're distributed through the dough. Once they're mixed in, the cookie dough is ready for the next baking step.
Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I want to get the marinade started today.
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and start the marinade with 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt or sour cream, plus 1/4 cup lemon juice.
I've got sour cream and the lemon juice measured. What seasonings from the recipe should I add next?

Add 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 teaspoon celery seed. The recipe says to combine the first eight ingredients in the large bowl, so stir everything together until the marinade looks smooth and evenly mixed.
The bowl is mixed. Should the chicken go straight into that?
Yes. Place the chicken in the mixture and turn each piece so it's coated on all sides. Use tongs or clean hands, and make sure the marinade reaches the edges of each breast.
The chicken is coated, but the bowl is pretty full. Is it okay to leave it in there?
That's fine as long as it can be covered tightly. If the bowl is crowded, you can transfer everything to a covered container or a sealable bag so the chicken stays in contact with the marinade.
How long does it need to sit before I bake it?
Cover it and marinate it overnight in the refrigerator. Keep it chilled the whole time; that long rest is part of this recipe's method.
It's the next day, and I'm ready to prep the pieces for baking. What happens after marinating?
Remove the chicken from the marinade, letting the excess drip off, then coat each piece with crumbs. Press the crumbs on gently so they cling to the surface.
Should I save any of the marinade for later, or clean up as I go?
Discard the used marinade after the chicken comes out, since it held raw chicken. Wipe down the counter, wash the bowl and utensils, and keep the crumb-coated chicken ready for the baking stage.
Can you help me get started on Dutch Cream Waffles? I'm setting out bowls and measuring cups now.
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and measure in 1 cup all-purpose flour with 1/4 teaspoon salt. Give those a quick stir so the salt is evenly mixed through the flour.
Flour and salt are in the large bowl. For the eggs, do I need the yolks and whites separated before mixing?
Yes. Separate 3 egg yolks from 3 egg whites. Keep the yolks in a small mixing bowl, and set the whites aside so they stay separate.
The yolks are in the small bowl, and the whites are off to the side. Where does the cream come in?
Start beating the egg yolks on low speed, then add the cream while the mixer is running. Keep the speed low so it blends in without splashing.
It's combining, but the yolks still look a little streaky. Should I keep mixing?
Yes, keep beating that yolk-and-cream mixture for 1 minute. By the end, it should look more uniform and slightly loosened.
The minute is up. Should I pour it into the flour bowl all at once or slowly?
Add the yolk mixture to the flour mixture, then combine on low speed. Low speed helps pull the dry ingredients in without throwing flour out of the bowl.
The flour is mostly moistened, but I can still see a few dry patches near the sides.
Scrape the sides of the bowl, then continue on low just until those dry patches are incorporated. Once the mixture is together, increase to medium-high.
I've turned it up. What texture am I looking for before I stop?
Beat on medium-high until the batter is smooth. Once you don't see lumps or dry streaks, stop mixing so the Dutch Cream Waffle batter is ready for the next step.
Can you talk me through making Fire Side Coffee? I'm clearing space for the jar and the dry ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl, a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, a spoon, and a lidded jar. Measure 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer and 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix into your prep area.
Creamer and hot chocolate mix are measured. I also have the instant coffee nearby—how much should I use?
Use 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules. You'll also need 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon for the spice.
The cinnamon is ready. Should everything go straight into the bowl, or should I sift in batches?
Sift the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, and cinnamon together into the bowl. If your recipe card includes nutmeg with the spices, sift it in with them as well.
Some of the coffee granules are catching in the strainer. Should I press them through?
Yes, gently rub or press any larger bits through so the mix is even. Give the bowl a good stir afterward so the creamer, chocolate, coffee, and spice are evenly distributed.
The dry mix looks uniform now. I've got a clean jar with a lid ready.
Pour the mixture into the jar, tapping the jar lightly on the counter if you need it to settle. Seal it tightly with the lid so the powder stays dry.
Jar is sealed. I'd like to make one mug right away—what's the ratio?
For one cup, stir 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture into 1 cup of hot water until it dissolves.
It's mixed, but I might want it a little stronger and creamier. Is it okay to tweak it?
Yes, adjust to taste. Add a little more mix for a stronger, sweeter cup, or add more hot water if it's too intense.
Banana Bran Muffins is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got the bowl out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar first, since those get creamed together in the mixing bowl.
The butter is soft and the brown sugar is measured. Do I need to prep the bananas before turning on the oven?
Yes, mash 3 bananas and keep 1/4 cup milk nearby. You'll also be adding vanilla and eggs when the wet ingredients come together.
Bananas are mashed. Should I heat the oven now or prep the muffin pan first?
Go ahead and heat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). While it warms, you can get the pan ready.
I have a standard muffin pan. Is greasing enough, or should I use liners?
Either works for this recipe: grease the muffin pan well or line the cups with paper muffin liners.
Pan is lined, and the oven is heating. What texture am I looking for when I mix the butter and sugar?
In a large mixing bowl, cream the softened butter with the brown sugar until the mixture looks lighter and fluffy rather than dense or grainy.
It's starting to look fluffy. Should the mashed bananas go in all at once?
Yes, add the mashed bananas, the 1/4 cup milk, vanilla, and eggs to the creamed butter and sugar, then mix until everything is well combined.
The batter is mixed. Before I portion it out, should I scrape down the bowl?
Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl so the banana mixture is evenly blended, then you'll be ready to fill the prepared muffin pan.
I want to make Dilled Garlic today. Can you guide me while I set up the jars?
Absolutely. Have sterile containers ready, plus 2 pounds of peeled garlic. You'll also need 1 sprig of chopped fresh dill, cayenne pepper to taste, and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar.
The jars are sterile and the garlic is peeled. Should the dill and cayenne go directly into the jars with it?
Yes. Pack the garlic into the sterile containers with the chopped fresh dill and a little cayenne pepper, leaving about an inch of space at the top of each container.
I've filled them close to the top but left that inch. What saucepan should I use for the vinegar?
Use a medium saucepan. Pour in the 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar, then mix in the salt so it dissolves evenly as it heats.
The vinegar and salt are in the pan. Do I just warm it, or does it need to boil?
Bring the vinegar and salt mixture all the way to a boil. Keep an eye on it so you can pour it while it's still hot.
It's boiling now, and the jars are waiting. Should I ladle it in or pour straight from the pan?
Either works if you can do it safely, but pour carefully so the hot vinegar and salt mixture goes into the containers over the garlic, dill, and cayenne.
I'm worried about splashing because the garlic is packed in. Any tip before I pour?
Go slowly and aim down the inside of each container if possible. The goal is to cover the garlic mixture with the hot vinegar and salt mixture without disturbing the contents too much.
The hot vinegar mixture is in the containers now. Is that the whole recipe?

Yes, that completes the recipe steps: the sterile containers are filled with 2 pounds garlic, dill, and cayenne, and the boiled 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar with salt has been poured over the garlic mixture.
Help me stay organized for Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes. What comes first? I've got my soup pot ready.

Absolutely. Set out 1 recipe Fast Chicken Soup Base, 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, and 2 medium zucchini. You'll also need 1 tsp. dried basil.
I have the soup base made already, and the tortellini is still in the fridge. Should I dice the zucchini before heating the pot?
Yes, dice the 2 medium zucchini now so it's ready to go in quickly later. Keep the tortellini chilled until you add it, since it cooks fast.
The zucchini is diced, and the tomatoes are opened. What should happen with the soup base?
Pour or keep the Fast Chicken Soup Base in your soup pot and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium heat. You're looking for steady small bubbles, not a hard boil.
It's bubbling lightly around the edges. Do I add everything at once?
Yes. Add the 9 ounce package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 14.5 ounce can of diced tomatoes with their juices, the diced zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
Everything is in, and the tortellini is starting to float. Should I stir a lot?
Give it a gentle stir to keep the tortellini from sticking, then let the soup return to a simmer. Stir occasionally, but don't be rough with the pasta.
The pot is simmering again. How long should I cook it so the zucchini and pasta are right?
Simmer it for 10 to 20 minutes, until the tortellini is tender and the zucchini has softened but still holds its shape.
At about 12 minutes the tortellini tastes tender, and the zucchini is soft but not mushy. Is that enough?
Yes, that sounds ready. Turn off the heat, give the soup one final gentle stir, and serve it hot.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: I want to make Armadillo Eggs. Can you talk me through the setup before I start cutting peppers?
Here, set out 24 jalapeno peppers, 1 pound sausage, 2 cups all-purpose baking mix, and 1 (16 ounce) package of shredded Cheddar cheese.
I've got the sausage and jalapenos out. Should the oven be heating while I check the rest?
Yes, go ahead and set the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), so it is ready when the prep is done.
The oven is on. I found the baking mix, but I want to confirm the cheese amount.
Use the full 1 (16 ounce) package of shredded Cheddar cheese, along with the 2 cups of all-purpose baking mix.
Okay. What pan should I get ready for these?
Use a medium baking sheet and lightly grease it so the Armadillo Eggs do not stick.
The baking sheet is greased. How should I start on the jalapenos without cutting them in half?
Cut a slit in each jalapeno pepper, keeping the peppers mostly intact rather than splitting them open completely.
I've slit a few peppers. Do I leave the seeds in for the filling?
No, remove and discard the seeds and pulp from each jalapeno pepper after you make the slit.
That sounds manageable. Any cleanup tip while I finish all 24 peppers?
Keep a small bowl or scrap container nearby for the seeds and pulp, then continue until all 24 jalapenos are slit, cleaned out, and ready for the sausage, baking mix, and Cheddar.
I'm making Fire Side Coffee today. What's the best place to start? I'm setting out the dry ingredients now and want to mix it correctly.

Absolutely. This is a dry mix you'll store in a jar, then scoop into hot water when you want a cup. Measure out 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
I've got the creamer and hot chocolate measured. Should the instant coffee go in as whole granules?
Yes, use the instant coffee granules as they are. Add the 1 1/2 cups of granules to the bowl with the creamer and hot chocolate mix.
The cinnamon is ready too. Do I need a whisk, or is sifting better here?

Sifting is best for this recipe because it breaks up clumps and blends everything evenly. Sift together the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, cinnamon, and the nutmeg called for in the mixing step.
My sifter is small, so I'll have to do it in batches. Is that okay?
That's fine. Sift in batches into a large bowl, then gently stir the sifted mixture so the coffee, chocolate, creamer, and spices are evenly distributed.
It looks uniform now. What kind of container should I use for storing it?
Pour the mixture into a clean, dry jar and seal it with a lid. An airtight jar is ideal so the mix stays dry and scoopable.
I want to try one mug before I put the rest away. How much mix goes into the water?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Mix until it dissolves as much as possible.
If it tastes a little weak or too strong, what should I change?
Adjust it to taste: add a bit more mix for a stronger, sweeter cup, or more hot water if it's too intense. Once you like the balance, seal the rest of the dry mix in the jar.
I have French Spring Soup planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a large pot out and want to cook along.
Absolutely. Set the large pot on the stove, and gather 1/4 cup butter, 1 pound chopped leeks, 1 chopped onion, and 2 quarts water.
The leeks are chopped, but they look a little gritty. Should I rinse them before they go in?
Yes, rinse the chopped leeks well and drain them so grit doesn't end up in the soup. Once they're ready, melt the 1/4 cup butter in the large pot over medium heat.
The butter is melted and just starting to foam. Do I add both vegetables now?
Add the 1 pound chopped leeks and the chopped onion to the pot. Stir them through the butter so they're coated evenly.
They're sizzling gently. What texture am I looking for before I add liquid?
Cook the leeks and onion until they're tender, stirring now and then so they soften without sticking or browning too much.
They've softened and smell sweet. Should the 2 quarts water go in all at once?
Yes, pour the 2 quarts water into the pot and give everything a good stir to loosen anything from the bottom.
Water is in. I have potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice ready on the counter.
Add the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice to the pot, then stir so the rice and vegetables are distributed through the soup.
Everything is mixed in. Anything I should check before I let it cook?
Make sure nothing is clumped at the bottom, especially the rice, and keep the pot at a steady simmer so the vegetables and rice can cook evenly.
I'm making Dads BBQ Roast and have the beef out. Can you guide me without getting ahead of me?
Absolutely. Check that you have 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 envelopes of dry onion soup mix, and a 5 pound beef rump roast ready to go.
The roast is about 5 pounds, and I found the mustard. The onion soup mix packets are 1 ounce each—is that right?
Yes, use 2 of those 1 ounce envelopes. Pour the yellow mustard into a small bowl, then add both packets of dry onion soup mix.
Should I stir it until it's smooth, or will it stay a little grainy from the soup mix?
It will stay a bit textured from the onion soup mix. Stir until the mustard and seasoning are evenly combined, with no dry pockets of mix left.
Mixture is ready. What should I set up before I touch the beef?
Lay out two long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise, like a plus sign, so the roast can sit in the middle and the foil can come up around it later.
The foil is down. I'm trying not to make a mess—do I dry the roast on the foil?
Pat the roast dry first with paper towels, then place it in the center where the two foil sheets cross. Drying it helps the mustard mixture cling better.
It's centered on the foil now. Do I coat just the top, or all the sides too?
Coat it generously all over with the mustard and onion soup mixture. Use a spoon or clean hands to cover the top, sides, and any exposed ends.
There's a thick layer on it now, and some mixture is pooling near the bottom. Is that okay?
That's fine. Spread any pooled mixture back onto the roast if you can, then keep the roast centered on the crosswise foil so it's ready for the next stage.
I have Baked Aloha Chicken planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got the chicken legs out and want to set up before I start mixing anything.
Absolutely. For the sauce, measure 1/4 cup lemon juice and 1/4 cup light corn syrup, then keep 2 tablespoons soy sauce and 1 teaspoon salt nearby too.
Those are on the counter. Should I heat the oven before I open the pineapple?
Yes, go ahead and get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready when the chicken is sauced.
Oven is warming. I have a bowl ready—what goes into it besides the lemon juice and corn syrup?
Add the soy sauce, salt, ginger, and corn oil to the bowl with the lemon juice and corn syrup. Stir everything until the mixture looks smooth.
The sauce is smooth now. The crushed pineapple has a lot of liquid—do I drain it?
Keep the liquid. Stir in the crushed pineapple with its liquid so the sauce stays juicy and coats the chicken well.
Got it mixed in. I'm using a glass baking dish; is that okay for this?
That's exactly what you want here: an ovenproof glass baking dish. Arrange the chicken legs in it in a single layer if you can.
The chicken legs fit without crowding too much. Do I pour all of the pineapple sauce over them?
Yes, pour the sauce over the top of the chicken legs, making sure the pineapple and liquid are spread across the pieces.
Sauce is over the chicken and the oven is nearly at temperature. Anything else before it goes in?

Just check that the dish is ovenproof and the chicken is evenly covered. Once the oven reaches 350 degrees F, place the dish in and bake according to your recipe's remaining timing or doneness guidance.
I want to make Dutch Cream Waffles. Can you guide me without rushing? I'm starting with the dry ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and add 1 cup all-purpose flour with 1/4 teaspoon salt. Give them a quick stir so the salt is evenly mixed through the flour.
The flour and salt are in the bowl. For the eggs, do I need the yolks and whites separated before I start mixing?
Yes. Separate 3 egg yolks from 3 egg whites. Keep the yolks handy in a small mixing bowl, and keep the whites separate for later.
I've separated them. I also have the small bowl ready with the yolks. What should the mixer speed be?
Use low speed for the yolks. Start beating them gently, and while the mixer is running, add the cream slowly so it blends in smoothly.
The cream is going in now. Should I keep it on low the whole time?
Keep it on low while you're adding the cream, then continue beating that yolk-and-cream mixture for 1 minute.
It's been about 1 minute. The mixture looks even and a little thicker. Do I pour it into the flour next?
Yes, pour the yolk-and-cream mixture into the large bowl with the flour and salt. Start mixing on low speed so the flour doesn't puff out of the bowl.
It's combined but still a bit lumpy around the sides of the bowl. Should I scrape it down?
Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl, then keep combining on low until the dry patches are worked in.
The dry spots are gone. What texture am I aiming for before I stop mixing?
Increase to medium-high speed and beat until the batter is smooth. Once it looks even with no visible lumps, you're ready for the next part of the waffle process.
Arroz con Pollo II is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got a large skillet out and want to prep in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 1 tablespoon olive oil and a 2 to 3 pound whole chicken cut into pieces. You'll also want the skillet ready over medium-high heat when you start cooking.
The chicken is cut up. Before I turn on the heat, what aromatics should I chop or crush?
Chop 2 onions and crush 3 cloves of garlic. Keep them close by because they'll go into the skillet after the chicken is browned.
Onions are chopped and the garlic is crushed. Should the oil go in now?
Yes. Add the olive oil to the large skillet and heat it over medium-high heat until it's hot enough for the chicken to sizzle when it touches the pan.
The oil is shimmering a bit. Do I put all the chicken pieces in?
Add the chicken pieces and sauté them until they're lightly browned. Once they have some color, lift them out of the skillet and set them aside on a plate.
The chicken is browned and resting. There are browned bits in the pan—do I keep cooking in the same skillet?
Yes, use the same skillet. Add the chopped onion, crushed garlic, and green bell pepper, then sauté until the vegetables are soft.
The onions and pepper have softened. What goes in with them before the chicken comes back?
Stir in the tomato sauce, saffron, salt, and bouillon, mixing them through the softened vegetables. Then return the browned chicken pieces to the skillet.
The chicken is back in the sauce mixture. How long should it cook before I add the rice?
In this Arroz con Pollo II step, let it cook for 10 minutes. After that, add the rice and reduce the heat to low so it can continue cooking gently.
I have Barbecued Shredded Beef planned for today. What should I set up first? Can you help me get set up before I start cooking?
Absolutely. Set out a large roasting pan and gather 3 pounds beef roast and 2 chopped onions. You'll also need 2 cans or bottles of beer, 12 fluid ounces each, plus 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce.
The roast is ready and the onions are chopped. Should I heat the oven before I open the beer?
Yes, go ahead and bring the oven up to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). That low heat is right for this beef.
Oven is heating. Do I put anything in the pan before the meat?
Place the beef roast directly in the large roasting pan, then scatter the chopped onions over the top and around it.
The pan looks pretty full with the onions. What do I mix separately?
Use a large bowl and combine the Worcestershire sauce with liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir those together so the seasonings are evenly distributed.
I have that bowl mixed. Is the beer supposed to go in there too or straight into the pan?
Pour the beer into the bowl with the Worcestershire mixture, stir it together, and then add that liquid to the roasting pan.
Should I pour it over the top of the roast or more around the sides?
Pour it over and around the roast so the onions and beef both get some of the mixture. Try to keep everything contained in the roasting pan.
All right, the roast, onions, and beer mixture are in the pan. Anything else before it goes into the oven?

That covers the listed prep for Barbecued Shredded Beef: oven at 275 degrees F, roast in the pan, onions scattered over it, and the beer-Worcestershire mixture added. Put the roasting pan in the oven when it's fully preheated.
I'm about to start Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got bread ready, but I want to prep the topping in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the vegetables ready: finely chop 1 small onion and dice 1 medium tomato.
The onion is finely chopped and the tomato is diced. Should I cut the celery and bell pepper the same way?
Chop 1 stalk of celery, and finely chop 1 green bell pepper so the mixture spreads easily over the bread.
All the vegetables are prepped. Do I turn on the oven before mixing everything?
Yes. Preheat your oven's broiler so it's hot by the time the sandwiches are assembled.
The broiler is heating. I have a medium bowl out—what goes into it?
Add the onion, tomato, celery, and bell pepper to the bowl, then stir them together with the cheese, chili powder, and salt.
The mixture looks combined, but a little chunky from the vegetables. Is that okay?
That's fine for these sandwiches. Just make sure the cheese and seasonings are evenly distributed through the vegetables.
I'm ready to put the bread under the broiler. Should I use a baking sheet or something else?
Arrange the bread slices on a baking sheet or a broiling pan, keeping them in a single layer.
The bread is on the pan. How much topping should go on each slice?
Spoon 1/4 of the mixture onto each slice and spread it out to the edges so every bite gets the crunchy vegetable-cheese topping.
Carrot Pineapple Cake I is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got my mixing bowls out but want to stay on track.
Absolutely. Start by checking the dry ingredients you'll need for the recipe: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 teaspoon salt.
I found the flour and baking soda. I'm measuring the rest now—what should I set the oven to while I do that?
heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready by the time the batter is mixed.
Oven is heating. I have a 9x13 inch pan—does that sound right for this cake?
Yes, use a 9x13 inch pan. Grease it well, then flour it so the cake releases more easily after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. Should I combine the dry ingredients in one bowl before adding anything wet?
Yes. Mix together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon until they're evenly distributed.
The dry mix looks even. Do I need to sift it, or is whisking enough?
Whisking is fine here as long as you don't see clumps of baking soda or baking powder. The goal is an even dry mixture before the wet ingredients go in.
Okay, the center of the bowl is clear. What goes into the well?
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients, then add the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla there.
I've added the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla. Any mixing advice so I don't overdo it?
Stir from the center outward, gradually pulling in the dry ingredients. Mix just until everything is combined and there are no obvious dry streaks.
I want to make Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Pull out 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate, chopped.
I've got the dry ingredients on the counter. Should the oven be heating while I deal with the pans?
Yes, turn the oven on to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it can preheat while you prepare everything else.
I'm using round cake pans. What size does this recipe call for?
Use 2 round pans that are 9 inch each. Grease them well, then flour the inside so the cakes release more easily after baking.
The pans are greased and floured. For the flour mixture, do I just whisk it together?
This recipe says to sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt. Sifting will help combine them evenly and break up any clumps.
Just confirming: all 2 1/4 cups of flour go in with the baking soda and salt, right?
Right. Sift all 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour with the 2 teaspoons baking soda and the 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Where does the chopped unsweetened chocolate fit in at this point?
For now, just have the 6 chopped unsweetened chocolate squares ready. The steps we have so far only take you through prepping the pans and sifting the dry ingredients.
My sifted dry mix is in a bowl and the chocolate is chopped. What should I do with the flour mixture now?
Set the sifted flour, baking soda, and salt mixture aside. You're ready for whatever the next part of the cake method calls for.
I have Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got my cutting board out and want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms. If the mushrooms are not chopped yet, cut them fairly evenly so they cook at the same pace.
The mushrooms are chopped. I also see green onions and garlic on the counter—how should those be prepped?
You'll want 2 green onions, chopped, and 1 clove garlic, crushed. Keep them near the stove since they'll go into the saucepan with the mushrooms.
All prepped. Should I turn on the oven before I start cooking the filling?
Yes, set the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), so it is ready when you need it.
The oven is heating. What pan should I use for the stovetop part?
Use a medium saucepan. Put it over medium heat, then add the 2 tablespoons olive oil and let the oil warm briefly.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do the mushrooms go in by themselves or with the aromatics?
Add the mushrooms, chopped green onions, crushed garlic, and the cayenne pepper together, then stir so everything gets coated in the oil.
It smells good already. How long should I keep it on the heat?
Here, cook the mixture for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mushrooms and onions are tender.
What should I look for to know the mushrooms are tender enough?

Set a saucepan on the stove and measure 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1 3/4 cups water.

Yes, it will thicken as it cooks. Bring the mixture to a boil, then cook and stir it for 2 minutes, or until it has thickened.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup dates, pitted and chopped, plus 1 cup dark brown sugar. Those are the main dry-sweet ingredients for this start.

You'll also need 1/4 cup margarine and 1 cup boiling water. Keep the boiling water ready, because it gets mixed directly with the dates, sugar, and margarine.

Yes—heat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), so it's heating while you prep the loaf mixture.
Oven is heating. I'm using a 9x5 inch loaf pan; does it need anything?
Grease and flour the 9x5 inch loaf pan thoroughly, including the corners, so the loaf releases more easily later.
The pan is coated. I've got the bowl ready—what should go in together?
In a large bowl, combine the chopped dates, dark brown sugar, margarine, and the 1 cup boiling water.
Should the margarine be melted first, or will the hot water handle it?
The boiling water should soften and melt the 1/4 cup margarine as everything sits together. Stir just enough to bring the dates, sugar, margarine, and water into one mixture.

Let the mixture stand for 15 minutes. That pause gives the dates time to soften before you continue with any later cake steps.

Room temperature is fine. Add the softened butter to the bowl, then stir in the minced garlic and grated Parmesan until everything looks evenly mixed and spreadable.

You can use it right away if you want it soft for spreading. If you'd rather slice or scoop it neatly later, shape it into a small mound or log, cover it, and chill until firmer.

Give it one last stir, make sure the garlic and Parmesan are evenly mixed, and taste a tiny bit for seasoning. Serve it soft with the warm bread, or keep any extra covered in the fridge.

For setup, put out 1 (4 ounce) bar of chopped German sweet chocolate, 1/3 cup milk, 4 ounces softened cream cheese, 2 tablespoons white sugar, a large microwave-safe bowl, and a wire whisk.

Use only 2 tablespoons of the milk with the chopped chocolate in the microwave-safe bowl. Leave the rest of the 1/3 cup milk in the cup for when you whisk the filling together.

You can start the chocolate now, but let the cream cheese sit out while it heats. Softer cream cheese will blend more easily once the chocolate is melted.
I like that garnish plan—that's exactly the finished look I wanted, polished but not busy. What timing should I use in the microwave?
Microwave the chocolate with those 2 tablespoons milk on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stopping halfway through to stir. You're aiming for almost melted, not bubbling hot.

If the pieces look soft, don't heat it more yet. Stir steadily and let the warmth in the bowl finish melting them into a smooth, glossy mixture.

Yes. Whisk in the 4 ounces softened cream cheese, 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk until the mixture looks blended and even.
There are tiny pale flecks from the cream cheese. I don't want to overwork it, but should I keep going?
Keep whisking a little longer, especially around the sides and bottom of the bowl. The goal is a blended filling without obvious cream cheese streaks or sugar pockets.
That did it—the mixture looks uniform now. Is this when it gets folded with the whipped topping?
Not quite yet. Refrigerate the chocolate mixture for 10 minutes so it firms slightly before you fold in the whipped topping.
The 10 minute chill is done, and the bowl feels cooler and thicker. How do I fold in the topping without knocking it flat?

Add 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping and fold gently with broad strokes, turning the bowl as you go, until no streaks remain. When you serve it, keep that same restrained finish: one flavor accent and one textured accent, with no extra clutter on top.

messages.content: For this batch of Classic Peanut Butter Cookies, I'm treating it like a warm egg-or-pasta-style dish and adding cheese right before serving. What's the best way to add it this time?
Dice the cheese small, then gently fold it in after the pan is off the heat so it softens without getting greasy.
Perfect, that's just for tonight's version. Before I start mixing, what should I pull from the fridge?
Get out 1 cup unsalted butter and 1 cup crunchy peanut butter so they're ready to cream together.
Both are on the counter. Which sugars do I need measured before the bowl gets messy?
Measure 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them close to the butter and peanut butter.
The sugars are measured. Should I use the mixer bowl for the butter mixture?
Yes. Put the butter, peanut butter, white sugar, and packed brown sugar in the mixer bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks combined and lighter.
It's creamy and the sides of the bowl look mostly clean. What goes in after that?
Beat in the eggs next, mixing until they're fully incorporated into the batter.
The eggs are mixed in. What dry ingredients should I handle separately?
Here, in a separate bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
I've sifted the dry bowl. Do I dump it all in or add it more carefully?
For this batch of Classic Peanut Butter Cookies, stir the sifted dry ingredients into the batter, working gently so everything combines without overmixing.
The batter is together, and I'm getting close to serving the warm version. When should the cheese go in?
Once the dish is off the heat, fold in the small cheese cubes gently and serve while it's still warm.

messages.content: I'm treating Dutch Cream Waffles like a platter salad today, with cheese going on right before it hits the table. What's the best way to add it?
Leave the cheese chilled until serving, then shave thin curls over just one side of the platter.
Great, I'll keep the cheese aside for that. Before I pull out bowls, what dry ingredients should I measure?
Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Put them near a large mixing bowl.
Large bowl is out, and the flour and salt are measured. Do they go in together?
For Dutch Cream Waffles, add the flour and salt to the large mixing bowl and stir them together so the salt is evenly distributed.
Done. I have eggs on the counter too—how should I set them up?
Separate 3 eggs, keeping the 3 egg yolks and the 3 egg whites apart. You'll use the yolks for the next mixing step.
The yolks are in a small bowl, and the whites are separate. What happens with the cream?
With the mixer on low, beat the egg yolks in the small mixing bowl while you add the cream.
The cream is going in slowly and the mixer is still on low. How long should I keep beating?
Beat that yolk-and-cream mixture for 1 minute.
One minute is up. The mixture looks even—where does it go now?
Pour it into the flour mixture in the large bowl. Mix on low speed just to combine.
It's combined but a little streaky. What texture am I aiming for before I deal with the serving platter?
Increase to medium-high and beat until the batter is smooth. Keep the cheese chilled for the platter and shave it on only near serving.
I want to make Cinnamon Rolls I with the bread machine—can you stay with me while I set it up?

Absolutely. Start by checking the dough ingredients you listed: 1 cup warm water at 110 degrees F, 1 egg, 3 cups bread flour, and 1/4 cup white sugar. Keep the powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast nearby too, since they go into the machine with the dough.
The water is at 110 and the egg is out. Should the bread flour and sugar go in right away?
Yes, add everything to the bread machine pan in the order your manufacturer recommends: water, egg, bread flour, white sugar, powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast.
I've loaded the pan in that order. Which setting am I using?
Choose the DOUGH setting, then turn the bread machine on. That will mix and knead the cinnamon roll dough for you.
The machine is running. I'd like to prep the topping while it works—what pan or pot do I need?
Use a small saucepan. Melt 1/3 cup butter in it over heat while the dough cycle is going.
The butter is melted and starting to bubble a little. What goes into the saucepan next?
Stir in 1/2 cup brown sugar and the ice cream. Bring that mixture to a boil.
It just reached a boil. How long should I cook it?
Let it boil and cook for 2 minutes, stirring so the sugar dissolves evenly and the sauce stays smooth.
The sauce looks glossy after 2 minutes. Should I take it off the heat now?
Yes, take the saucepan off the heat. The dough can keep running on the DOUGH setting, and the butter-brown sugar-ice cream mixture is ready for the next part of the cinnamon rolls.
Before I get moving on Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad, what should I have ready?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided; 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, 6 ounces each; 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning; and 2 cloves garlic, crushed.
I've got the chicken and seasoning out. Should I use a nonstick pan or a regular skillet?
Use a large skillet if you have one. Put it over medium heat and warm 1 tablespoon of the olive oil until it looks hot and moves easily across the pan.
The oil is warmed. Do I season the chicken before it goes in?
In this Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad step, coat both sides of the chicken breasts with the Cajun seasoning, then lay them carefully into the hot oil.
They're in the skillet, and the seasoning is starting to smell toasted. When does the garlic go in?
Stir in the 2 crushed garlic cloves now, keeping them in the oil around the chicken so they flavor it without piling on one spot.
The garlic is sizzling. How long should I cook the first side?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on that side, keeping the heat at medium so the Cajun coating blackens without scorching.
It has been 5 minutes, and the underside looks dark and crusty. Should I flip now?
Yes, flip the chicken and cook the second side for another 5 minutes.
The second side is done. How do I know it's safe and ready for the salad?
Check that the juices run clear when pierced and the chicken is cooked through. Let it rest briefly, then slice it for the Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad.
I want to make Carrots and Onions Au Gratin. Can you help me get set up before I start slicing?
Absolutely. You'll need 1 (16 ounce) package of baby carrots, sliced, plus 2 medium onions, sliced. Have a pot ready for boiling and a baking dish for later.
The carrots and onions are sliced. What else should I pull from the fridge?
Get 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter. Once those are out, set your oven to preheat at 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
Oven is heating, and I have the cheese and butter measured. Do the vegetables go straight into the baking dish?
Not yet. Put the sliced carrots and onions into a pot, add enough lightly salted water to cover them, and bring the water to a boil.
How much salt should I use in the water? I don't want the vegetables too salty.
Use just a light salting—enough to season the water mildly. The recipe only calls for lightly salted water, so keep it modest before bringing the pot to a boil.
The pot is boiling now. How long should I let the carrots and onions cook?
Cook them for 5 minutes, checking that they turn tender but still feel firm rather than soft or mushy.
They're firmer than canned vegetables but not raw anymore. Is that the right texture?
Yes, that sounds right: tender but firm. Drain the carrots and onions well so extra water doesn't collect in the baking dish.
They're drained. How should I arrange them in the dish with the cheese and butter waiting?
Spread 1/2 the drained carrots and onions in the baking dish as the first layer. Keep the remaining vegetables, the Cheddar, and the butter nearby for the next part.
I want to make Empanadas, but I see the dough needs chilling. Can you help me start it today?
Absolutely. For the dough, set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1 (3 ounce) package cream cheese so they're easy to blend.
The butter is soft and the cream cheese is ready. Do I need anything else on the counter before mixing?
Yes—have 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour nearby. You'll also need 1 cup fruit preserves for the filling later.
Got it. I have a mixing bowl and a spoon. What texture am I aiming for with the butter and cream cheese?
Cream the butter and cream cheese together until they look smoothly blended, with no obvious streaks of either one.
It's blended and looks pretty even. Should I add all the flour at once?
Beat in the 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour until it becomes a soft dough. Mix just until the flour is incorporated and the dough holds together.
The dough has come together. It's soft, so I'm wondering how to pack it for the fridge.
Shape it into a smooth ball, then wrap it well in foil or cling wrap so it doesn't dry out.
Wrapped and ready. How long does it need to chill before I can use it?
Refrigerate the wrapped dough overnight. If needed, it can stay chilled for up to a week.
When I'm ready to bake, should I work with it straight from the refrigerator?
Take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it, so it has time to soften slightly before you handle it.
I'd like to make a Buttermilk Shake. Can you help me get it set up?
Absolutely. Pull out a blender and gather 1 pint vanilla ice cream, 1 cup buttermilk, 1 teaspoon grated lemon peel, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I have the blender on the counter, and the ice cream is still pretty firm. Is that okay?
That's fine. If it's very hard, let it sit for a few minutes just until it scoops easily, but don't let it melt. The shake should blend up cold and creamy.
The ice cream is scoopable now. Should the buttermilk go in before or after it?
Either order will work, but pouring the 1 cup buttermilk into the blender first can help the blades catch everything more smoothly.
Buttermilk is in. I'm adding the ice cream next—do I include the lemon peel and vanilla now too?
Yes, add the 1 pint vanilla ice cream, 1 teaspoon grated lemon peel, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract to the blender with the buttermilk.
Everything is in the blender container. How tight should the lid be?
Put the cover on securely and hold it in place with one hand, especially at the start, since the mixture is thick.
Lid is on. What speed should I use, and what texture am I looking for?
Process it on high until the shake looks smooth, with no big ice cream lumps left. Stop as soon as it's evenly blended.
It looks smooth and creamy now. Should I chill the glasses or just pour?
You can pour it straight into glasses now. Chilled glasses are nice if you have them, but the recipe is ready to serve once it's poured.
