Set the saucepan into the sink or bowl of ice water and stir the eggnog for 1 to 2 minutes so it cools quickly.
It's cooling and I'm stirring. Where does the vanilla fit in?

The recipe includes 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, so keep it measured and ready with the finished eggnog; the cooked mixture itself should be cooled quickly as directed before you move on to serving or chilling.
Can you help me get Cabbage Kielbasa Supper going in the slow cooker? I want to make sure I prep the vegetables right.
Absolutely. Shred 8 cups of cabbage, cut 3 medium potatoes into 1/2 inch cubes, and chop 1 medium onion. You'll also need 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, pepper, broth, and sausage for the slow cooker.
The cabbage is shredded and the potatoes are cubed. Does this need a particular size slow cooker?
Use a 5-qt. slow cooker. It may look very full once the cabbage goes in, but that's expected because the cabbage will cook down.
I've got the 5-qt. cooker out. Should the onion go in with the cabbage and potatoes or later?
Add the onion right away with the cabbage and potatoes. Put the cabbage, potato cubes, chopped onion, 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, and pepper into the slow cooker together.
Everything is in there with the salt and pepper. It's piled pretty high.
That's fine for this recipe. Pour the broth over everything, letting it run down through the cabbage and potatoes rather than trying to stir it aggressively.
Broth is poured in. Where should the sausage go?
Set the sausage on top of the vegetables. Since the cooker is full, just nestle it in lightly; the cabbage will soften and shrink as it cooks.
The sausage is on top. Do I cook it on high to get it started?
Keep it on low. Cover the slow cooker and cook for 8-9 hours, until the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through.
How will I know the potatoes and cabbage are done before serving?
Check that the potato cubes are tender when pierced and the cabbage has softened well. If the sausage is heated through too, the Cabbage Kielbasa Supper is ready to serve from the slow cooker.
I'm about to start Gingered Mango Salsa. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a cutting board out and want to prep it in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the ingredients together: 1 cup chopped peeled mango, 1/4 cup chopped red onion, 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro, and 1/4 cup lime juice.
The mango is peeled, but I haven't chopped it yet. Should it be diced small for salsa?
Yes, chop the mango into small bite-size pieces so it mixes evenly with the onion, cilantro, and lime juice.
Okay, I have 1 cup of chopped mango in a bowl. The red onion is next, right?
Right. Add 1/4 cup chopped red onion to the bowl with the mango.
The onion is in. I'm mincing the cilantro now—does it all go straight into the same bowl?
It does. Add 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro to the mango and red onion.
Cilantro is added. I measured the lime juice—should I pour in the whole 1/4 cup?
Yes, pour in the full 1/4 cup lime juice, then gently stir everything together until the mango, onion, cilantro, and juice are evenly combined.
It's mixed, and there's a little lime juice pooling at the bottom. Is that okay?
That's fine. The salsa should sit in the lime juice so the flavors can blend; just give it a gentle stir before serving.
How long should it sit before I put it out with chips?
Let it stand for 30 minutes before serving. After that, stir it once more and serve it chilled or at room temperature with your chips.
Crab Cake Sauce is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got the blender out but haven't measured anything yet.
Yes. Set out 1 cup sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, and 1/3 cup hot salsa. The recipe also blends in cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt, so have those nearby too.
I measured the sour cream and mayonnaise. Should they go straight into the blender jar?
Go ahead and add both to the blender. Since they're thick, put them in before the chunkier cottage cheese so the blades have something creamy to catch.
The sour cream and mayo are in. I'm adding the cottage cheese now—will it stay lumpy?
It should smooth out once blended. Add the 1/2 cup cottage cheese, then pour in the 1/3 cup hot salsa.
Salsa is in. How much cayenne, lemon juice, and yogurt am I supposed to use?
This recipe doesn't give amounts for those three, so add them carefully to taste: a small pinch of cayenne, a little lemon juice, and enough yogurt to blend with the rest without making it too thin.
Everything is in the blender. What consistency am I looking for?
Puree it until the sauce looks smooth and uniform, with no visible cottage cheese curds. Stop and scrape down the sides if the mixture clings to the jar.
It's mostly smooth, but I can still see tiny white flecks near the top.
Blend a little longer, then check again. If the top isn't moving, pause, scrape the sides and lid area down, and blend until the flecks disappear into the sauce.
Okay, it's smooth now. Can I serve it right away with the crab cakes?

Chill it before serving so the texture firms up and the flavors settle. Transfer it to a covered bowl or container, refrigerate it, then give it a quick stir before spooning it alongside the crab cakes.
I want to get Baked Fake Steak with Gravy right. What should I handle first? I've got the beef out but want to set things up in the right order.

Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and gather 3 pounds ground beef, 17 saltine crackers finely crushed, 1/2 cup milk, and 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder. You'll also want onion powder, salt, and pepper for seasoning.
I have the 3 pounds of ground beef and the crackers crushed. Should the milk go in with them right away?
Yes. Add the ground beef, the finely crushed saltine crackers, and the 1/2 cup milk to the large bowl together. Use clean hands or a sturdy spoon to start combining them gently.
The mixture is partly combined, but I don't want it to get tough. How much should I mix at this point?
Mix just until the crackers and milk are distributed through the beef. It should look fairly even, but you don't need to knead it heavily.
Okay, it looks even now. When do I add the garlic powder and the other seasonings?
Sprinkle in the 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder now, along with onion powder, salt, and pepper. Work those seasonings through the beef mixture until it's well blended.
The seasoning is mixed in. What pan should I use for shaping it?
Use a 10x15 inch jellyroll pan. Line it with waxed paper before you add the beef mixture so the surface is covered.
The waxed paper is in the 10x15 inch pan. Do I just drop the meat mixture in the center?
Place the beef mixture into the pan, then spread it outward toward the corners. Press it firmly so it forms an even layer rather than leaving loose pockets.
It's spread out, but the edges are a little uneven. Is that a problem before it cooks?
Just square up the edges as best you can and press the surface firmly once more. The important part is that the beef mixture is packed evenly into the pan.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: In this Asian Ginger Dressing step, for this version, add just the tiniest pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Asian Ginger Dressing, I'm using it over chilled fruit, so I'm considering cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. Which of those warm spices should go in?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Asian Ginger Dressing as a chilled fruit dessert with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. How should I use the warm spices?

messages.content: For this batch of Asian Ginger Dressing, I'm using it over chilled fruit, so I'm considering cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. Which of those warm spices should go in?
In this Asian Ginger Dressing step, for this version, add just the tiniest pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
Perfect, that's the fruit-dessert direction I want today. I have a 1 pint glass jar out—what should I prep first?
Mince 3 cloves of garlic and 2 tablespoons of fresh ginger root. Those can go straight into the jar once they're ready.
The garlic and ginger are minced. Should I measure the liquids into the jar now or keep them separate?
Measure them right into the jar: 3/4 cup olive oil and 1/3 cup rice vinegar.
Oil and vinegar are in with the aromatics. The jar still has room—what else belongs in there?
Add the soy sauce, honey, and water to the same jar with the garlic, ginger, olive oil, and rice vinegar.
The honey is clinging to the spoon, and I don't want leaks. Do I seal it before shaking?
Yes. Put on a tight fitting lid, then shake the jar well so the mixture starts to come together.
It's shaken, but the honey still looks a little streaky on the bottom. Is that okay?
That's expected. Remove the lid and microwave the jar for 1 minute, just long enough to dissolve the honey.
After microwaving, should I stir it, shake it, or let it sit first?
Let it cool first, since the jar and dressing will be warm.
It's cooled down now. I'm serving it with fruit—what's the last move before it goes to the table?
Shake it well once more before serving, so the dressing is blended and ready to spoon or pour over the chilled fruit.
I want to make the Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart dough. Can you guide me from measuring the dry ingredients?
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl and measure 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon light brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/8 teaspoon salt.
The flour and brown sugar are measured, and I have the cinnamon and salt nearby. Should I sift them together?
Yes. Sift the flour, light brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt into the bowl so the dry mixture is even and free of lumps.
They're sifted. The bowl smells like cinnamon now. What tool should I use for the butter?
Use a pastry cutter, two knives, or your fingertips. Cut in the butter gently until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs rather than a smooth paste.
Some bits are pea-sized and some are sandy. Is that close enough?
That sounds right for coarse crumbs. A mix of small sandy pieces and a few larger buttery bits is fine.
I'm ready for the ice water, but I don't want the dough to get tough. How should I add it?
Sprinkle the ice water over the crumb mixture, then toss it with a fork just until everything is evenly moistened. Keep the motion light instead of stirring hard.
It's damp in patches and starting to clump when I press it with the fork.
Good. Toss through the drier spots so the moisture spreads evenly, stopping once the mixture holds together when gently pressed.
The dough is holding together now. How do I wrap it so it's ready for the tart?
Pat the dough into a round, wrap it tightly in plastic, and keep the edges neat so it will be easier to roll later for the Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart.
I'm about to start Biga. Can you talk me through the prep? I've cleared space and want to make sure I set up the water and flour correctly.

Absolutely. Set out 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast, 1/2 cup warm water, 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour, and 1 1/4 cups cold water. You'll also want a small bowl for the yeast and a large bowl for the flour.
I have the small bowl out. Does the warm water go in there by itself first?
Yes. Pour the 1/2 cup warm water into the small bowl, then sprinkle the 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast over the top so it can hydrate evenly.
The yeast is sprinkled over the water. Should I stir it, or just leave it alone?
Leave it to stand until the yeast has dissolved and looks foamy, about 15 minutes. A little gentle swirl is fine if dry spots remain, but it mainly needs time.
While that sits, should I get the flour measured into the large bowl?
For Biga, yes, measure 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour into the large bowl while the yeast mixture rests.
The flour is in the bowl. Do I need to level it out or make space in the middle?
Make a well in the center of the flour, like a shallow crater, so the liquids can be poured into the middle instead of running straight to the sides.
The yeast mixture is foamy now. I also have the cold water measured.
Great. Pour the foamy yeast mixture into the well, then add the 1 1/4 cups cold water into that same center area.
Both liquids are in the well. Should I start mixing from the edges right away?
Yes, begin drawing flour from the edges into the liquid gradually so the biga comes together evenly. Keep the bowl steady and work slowly to avoid dry pockets.
Can you stay with me while I make Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds? I've cleared space by the stove.
Absolutely. Set out 6 Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cubed, along with 2 sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed. You'll also want a large pot ready.
The potatoes are peeled and cubed. Do the Yukon Golds and sweet potatoes go in together?
Yes, put both kinds of cubed potatoes into the large pot together so they cook in the same water.
Before I turn on the burner, what else should be on the counter?
Have 2 tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup heavy cream measured out or nearby. The recipe lists those along with the potatoes.
The pot is on the stove and all the cubes are inside. How much water am I adding?
Add enough water to cover the potatoes and sweet potatoes. They should be submerged, but you don't need to overfill the pot.
They're covered with water. Should I use high heat to get it going?
Bring the pot to a boil. Use enough heat to get the water bubbling steadily, and keep an eye on it so it doesn't boil over.
It has reached a boil and I'm standing by with a colander in the sink.
Good. Remove the pot from the heat, then drain the potatoes and sweet potatoes carefully in the colander.
They're drained. Do I need to get the oven ready now?
Yes. Preheat the oven broiler now, and keep the drained potatoes nearby while it heats.
Help me stay organized for Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth. What comes first? I've got a large pot out and want to make sure I start with the right amounts.
Absolutely. For this broth, measure 2 quarts water into the large pot and have 12 ounces beef shank ready nearby.
The water is measured, and the beef shank is still wrapped. Are there vegetables I should prep before turning on the stove?
Yes—chop 2 large onions and slice 2 large carrots. Keep them ready so the prep is done before the broth gets going.
The onions are chopped and the carrots are sliced. Do I add those right away with the water?
Start by bringing the 2 quarts water to a boil in the large pot. Hold the onions and carrots for the moment, since the next listed cooking step begins with the beef shank.
The pot is heating now. Should the beef go in while the water is still warming, or only once it boils?
Wait until the water reaches a boil, then place the 12 ounces beef shank into the pot.
The beef is in and the water came back up. How hard should it cook from here?
Reduce it to a simmer and let the beef shank cook gently for 1 1/2 hours. You want steady small bubbles rather than a hard rolling boil.
The 1 1/2 hours are up, and the broth smells good. What should I do with the pot now?
Take it off the heat and let it cool overnight. Once it is cool enough, refrigerate it for that overnight rest.
It cooled overnight in the fridge. The meat is firm now—how should I handle it?
Here, lift the meat out of the broth, trim off any gristle, and cut the meat into medium sized pieces. Set those pieces aside for the next part of the cawl.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Use only the tenderest lower herb pieces, chop them into very small bits, and keep the fresher upper green pieces separate.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Chunky Pizza Dip, I'm serving it more like an uncooked salsa-style topping, and I've got some lower cilantro or parsley pieces mixed in. What should I do with those?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut only the softest lower herb pieces into tiny bits and keep the upper green pieces separate.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chunky Pizza Dip as a raw salad, salsa, or uncooked topping with lower cilantro or parsley pieces. How should I handle them?

messages.content: For this batch of Chunky Pizza Dip, I'm serving it more like an uncooked salsa-style topping, and I've got some lower cilantro or parsley pieces mixed in. What should I do with those?
Use only the tenderest lower herb pieces, chop them into very small bits, and keep the fresher upper green pieces separate.
Perfect—just for this bowl tonight. I've got a large saucepan out; what should I prep before turning on the heat?
Measure 2 tablespoons olive oil and mince 3 garlic cloves. Keep them close to the stove so the garlic can go into the oil right away.
Garlic is minced. I'm opening cans now—remind me what tomato amounts I need.
You'll need 2 (14.5 ounce) cans petite diced tomatoes and 1/4 cup tomato paste.
The tomatoes and paste are on the counter. Should I use the saucepan or switch to something heavier?
A large saucepan is fine, and a Dutch oven works too. Add the olive oil and minced garlic, then heat them together until the garlic starts to sizzle and turn golden.
The garlic is lightly golden and I can smell it. Do the tomatoes go in all at once?
Yes. Add the petite diced tomatoes and the tomato paste, then stir in the basil and oregano. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
It's bubbling gently now. Do I cover it so it doesn't splatter everywhere?
Leave it uncovered so it can thicken. Let it simmer until it's sturdy enough for dipping, about 15 to 20 minutes.
If it looks chunky but a little loose near the end, should I keep reducing it?
Yes, give it a few more minutes within that window and stir occasionally. You're aiming for a thick, scoopable sauce rather than a watery one.
It's thick enough for chips now. What do I do before serving or storing it?
Take it off the heat, let it cool, then refrigerate it. Add your finely chopped tender lower herb pieces only to the portion you're serving this way.
Easy Fried Eggplant is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I have a large skillet out and I'm checking what to prep before the oil goes in.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons canola oil, 1 large eggplant that's peeled and sliced, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 cups dry bread crumbs. You'll want the egg and crumbs in separate shallow dishes so the slices can move quickly from coating to skillet.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced. Should I beat all 3 eggs now?
Yes, beat all 3 eggs now and place them near the bread crumbs. Keep the eggplant slices close by too, since they'll go from egg to crumbs and then straight into the hot oil.
I've got the eggs and the 2 cups of crumbs in dishes. How hot should the skillet be?
Pour the 2 tablespoons canola oil into the large skillet and heat it over medium-high heat. Give it a moment to get hot before you start adding coated eggplant.
The oil is heating. Should I coat several slices at once or work one by one?

Work in a small rhythm: dip each eggplant slice in the beaten egg, press it into the dry bread crumbs, then place it in the hot oil. Add only what fits comfortably in the skillet so the slices can brown instead of crowding.
The first few slices are in the pan. How long do they need before I turn them?
Fry them for 2 to 3 minutes on the first side, then flip and cook the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes. Look for a golden brown coating.
They're turning golden, but a couple edges are browning faster than the centers.
That can happen with thin edges. Keep the heat at medium-high unless they're darkening too quickly, and turn the slices as needed so each side reaches an even golden brown.
The batch looks done. Where should I put the cooked slices while I fry the rest?
Move the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain. Continue coating and frying the remaining slices the same way, then drain each batch on paper towels before serving.
I want to make Black Bean Lasagna Rolls. Can you help me get set up before I start cooking?
Absolutely. Put 8 uncooked lasagna noodles near the stove, and have 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese ready for the filling.
Noodles and Monterey Jack are on the counter. I'm checking the fridge and pantry—what else should be out?

You'll also need 1 (15 ounce) container part-skim ricotta cheese and 1 (4.5 ounce) can chopped green chiles, drained. Keep the black beans handy too, since they go onto the rolls after the cheese layer.
The chiles are drained, and I've got a pot ready for the pasta. Should I salt the water or add oil?
Cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions, but omit salt and fat. When they're done, drain them well so the filling won't slide around.
The noodles are cooked and draining. They're a little sticky—should I separate them before filling?
Yes, lay them out gently in a single layer if you can, so each noodle is easy to spread with filling. Try not to tear them while they're still warm and soft.
I've got them laid out. How do I mix the filling?
Combine the cheeses with the next 3 ingredients from the recipe, including the drained chopped green chiles, and stir well so the mixture is evenly blended.
On Black Bean Lasagna Rolls, the cheese mixture looks smooth with the chiles mixed through. How much goes on each noodle?
Spread the cheese mixture over one side of each noodle, dividing it as evenly as you can among all 8 noodles and leaving the edges manageable for rolling.
The noodles are covered with the cheese mixture. Where do the black beans come in?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on each noodle. Once they're distributed, the rolls are ready for the next assembly or baking step your full recipe calls for.
I'm starting Aaahh Potato Soup; can you walk me through the setup? I've got a pot out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. For this soup, set out 2 cubed Yukon Gold potatoes, 1 package of au gratin instant potato mix that's 5.5 ounces, 1 can of condensed chicken broth that's 10.5 ounces, and 1 1/2 cups water.
The potatoes are cubed, and I found the au gratin mix. Should I put everything in the pot cold?
Yes. Add the cubed Yukon Gold potatoes to the large saucepan or pot, then pour in the au gratin potato mix, the condensed chicken broth, and the 1 1/2 cups water.
It looks a little thick already. Are the potatoes supposed to be fully covered?
If the liquid doesn't cover the potatoes, add a bit more water just until they're covered. That helps them cook evenly while the soup thickens.
Okay, they're just covered now. What heat should I use?
Put the pot over medium heat. Let it cook gently, and stir occasionally so the au gratin mix doesn't settle or stick to the bottom.
How long should I expect it to simmer before the potatoes are done?
Cook it until the potatoes are tender, about 40 minutes. Check by piercing a potato cube with a fork; it should slide in easily.
It's been cooking a while and the soup is getting creamy. Should I stir more often near the end?
Yes, give it a stir a little more frequently as it thickens, especially along the bottom of the pot, but keep the heat at medium unless it starts sticking.
The potatoes are tender now. How do I finish the soup?
Stir in the cream, then heat it through gently until the soup is warm and smooth. Once the cream is incorporated and hot, it's ready to serve.
I'm setting up for Baked Apple Oatmeal; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got the casserole dish out but haven't started measuring yet.

Absolutely. Measure out 4 cups milk, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, 2 teaspoons butter or margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need cinnamon for the saucepan step, plus the remaining oatmeal ingredients ready to stir in after the milk mixture is heated.
The milk and brown sugar are measured. Should I grease the baking dish now or wait?
Go ahead and grease a 2-qt. casserole now so it's ready when the mixture is combined. That will make the transfer smoother later.
Dish is greased, and I have the butter, salt, and cinnamon beside the stove. What goes into the pan?
Put the milk, packed brown sugar, butter or margarine, salt, and cinnamon into a saucepan. Heat them together, stirring so the sugar dissolves and the butter melts into the milk.
It's warming and the butter is nearly melted. Am I trying to boil it?
No need to boil it. Just heat it until everything is blended and the milk mixture is hot, then you can move on to adding the remaining ingredients.
The mixture looks smooth now. I'm ready to add the rest—how gently should I mix?
Add the remaining ingredients to the saucepan mixture and fold or stir gently, just enough to combine without breaking everything down too much.
It's mixed and still a little loose. Do I pour it straight into the casserole?
Yes. Spoon the mixture into the greased 2-qt. casserole, spreading it evenly so it bakes at the same rate throughout.
The casserole is filled. What oven setting and timing should I use?
Cover the casserole and bake it at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes. After baking, let it sit briefly before serving so the oatmeal can settle.
I'm making Garlic Chicken Stir Fry today. What's the best place to start? I've got my wok out and want to prep everything before turning on the heat.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep them close to the stove because the cooking moves quickly.
I minced all 6 garlic cloves and chopped the green onions. Should I add everything at once once the wok is hot?
Not all of it at once. Heat the 2 tablespoons peanut oil in the wok or a large skillet first, then wait until the oil begins to smoke before adding the aromatics.
The oil is heating now. Which aromatics go in when it starts smoking?
As soon as it begins to smoke, quickly stir in 2 cloves of the minced garlic, the grated ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt. Stir right away so the garlic doesn't sit and scorch.
I've added the 2 cloves garlic with the ginger, onions, and salt. The pan smells strong already—how long do I cook this part?
Keep everything moving in the wok until the onion turns translucent, about 2 minutes. You're looking for the green onions to soften while the garlic and ginger stay fragrant.
The onions are softening but still a little bright green. Do I wait until they're fully limp?
No need to take them that far. Once they look translucent and softened, you're ready for the chicken. The goal is a quick stir fry, not deeply browned onions.
Okay, the onion looks translucent now. How should I add the chicken so it cooks evenly?
Add the chicken to the wok and spread it out as much as you can, then stir frequently so the pieces contact the hot surface. Cook until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes.
The chicken is mostly opaque after about 3 minutes. Anything I should check before serving?

Make sure there are no translucent-looking spots left on the chicken and everything is evenly coated with the garlic, ginger, green onions, and oil. Once it's opaque throughout, it's ready to serve hot.
I'm making Fruit Dip 2 today. What's the best place to start? I've got some fruit ready for serving, but I haven't started the dip yet.
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl and make sure you have 8 ounces cream cheese, 1/2 cup marshmallow creme, 2 cups frozen whipped topping that's thawed, and 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice.
The cream cheese is still pretty firm. Should I wait before mixing it?
Yes, let it soften a bit if you can. It will blend much more smoothly with the marshmallow creme and thawed whipped topping.
Okay, the cream cheese has softened. Do I add everything at once?
Add the cream cheese, marshmallow creme, and the thawed whipped topping to the bowl, then blend them together until the mixture looks smooth and creamy.
I'm using a hand mixer. Is that fine for this?
A hand mixer is fine. Use a low to medium speed so the whipped topping stays fairly fluffy while everything combines.
It's mixed, but it seems too thick for dipping fruit. What should I do with the pineapple juice?
Pour in the unsweetened pineapple juice gradually, using up to the 1/4 cup, and blend just until the dip loosens to a good dipping consistency.
It looks creamy now and clings to a spoon. Does it need to chill?
In this Fruit Dip 2 step, cover the bowl and chill the fruit dip for 1 hour so it firms slightly and the flavors settle.
After the hour, should I stir it or just serve it as is?
Give it a gentle stir after chilling, then serve it cold with your prepared fruit. Keep any leftovers covered in the refrigerator.
I'm starting Crab Quiche; can you walk me through the setup? I'm starting with a frozen crust and want to keep the timing straight.
Absolutely. Set out 1 (9 inch) deep dish frozen pie crust and 4 eggs so they're ready when you need them.
The crust and eggs are on the counter. What dairy or seasoning should I pull out?
You'll also need 1 cup heavy cream and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Keep pepper and hot sauce nearby too, since they get whisked into the egg mixture later.
I have the cream, salt, pepper, and hot sauce. Should I start heating the oven before touching the crust?
Yes. bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready for the crust.
The oven is heating. Do I bake the frozen pie crust by itself?
Bake the pie crust on its own for about 10 minutes, just until it's starting to brown.
It's been close to 10 minutes and the edges are only lightly browned. Is that enough?
Yes, lightly browned is the right point here. Remove the crust from the oven and let it cool before adding anything else.
The crust is cooling on the stove. While I wait, can I mix the filling?
Go ahead. In a large bowl, whisk together the 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon salt, pepper, and hot sauce until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The filling is smooth and the crust isn't hot anymore. Anything I should check before I pour?
Make sure the crust is only cooled, not steaming, and give the egg mixture one more quick whisk so the cream and seasonings stay evenly blended.
I want to make Biriyani and I've got a large skillet out. Can you guide me without dumping all the steps at once?
Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons plain yogurt, 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar, and 1 medium onion, sliced. Keep the skillet nearby since everything starts there.
The onion is sliced, and I found the yogurt and vinegar. Should I measure the oil before heating the pan?
Yes—measure the olive oil first so it's ready. Add the 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil to the large skillet, then heat it over medium heat.
The pan is warming. Do I add the onion right away or does something go in before it?
Before the onion, stir in the plain yogurt and distilled white vinegar. Use the full 3 tablespoons yogurt and 2 tablespoons vinegar, and mix them into the warm oil carefully.
It looks a little tangy and creamy in the skillet. Is that okay before I add the onion?
That's fine. Add the sliced medium onion now, spreading it through the mixture so it cooks evenly.
How soft should the onion get? I don't want to stop too early.
Cook the onion until it's tender. Stir occasionally so the slices soften in the skillet rather than sitting in one spot.
The onion has softened and the skillet smells sharp from the vinegar. What needs to go in next?
Mix in the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes. Stir them through the onion mixture so they're evenly combined.
Once those are stirred in, is there anything else from this part of the recipe I should check?
For this section, you've covered the listed steps: heated the oil, mixed in yogurt and vinegar, cooked the onion until tender, and added the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes.
I pulled up Broiled Egg Salad Sandwiches. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got the eggs cooked and want to set up the rest before I start mixing.
Absolutely. Chop 3 hard-cooked eggs, then have 1/4 cup crushed saltine crackers ready. You'll also need 1/4 cup chopped celery and 1 tablespoon diced pimientos for the egg mixture.
The eggs are chopped, and I crushed the crackers. Should the celery and pimientos go in the same bowl with them?
Yes, use 1 mixing bowl for those. Combine the chopped eggs, crushed saltines, chopped celery, and diced pimientos gently so the eggs don't get mashed too much.
It's mixed together. I see the dressing ingredients listed in the directions—do those stay separate for now?
Right. In another bowl, combine the mayonnaise, milk, salt, garlic salt, and pepper, then mix well until the dressing looks smooth and evenly seasoned.
The dressing is smooth. Should I pour it all in at once or fold it in slowly?
Add the dressing to the egg mixture and stir it in gently. You want everything coated, but keep some texture from the chopped egg, celery, and cracker crumbs.
The mixture is coated and still a little chunky. What should I put it on?
Spoon about 1/3 cup of the egg salad mixture onto each muffin half. Spread it lightly so it sits evenly on top rather than piling too high in the center.
I've filled the muffin halves. Should I grease the baking sheet before they go on it?
No greasing needed. Place the filled muffin halves on an ungreased baking sheet, leaving a little room between them so they're easy to lift off after broiling.
They're on the sheet. Is there anything I should check before broiling or serving?
Make sure each muffin half has roughly the same amount of topping so they heat evenly. Once broiled, serve them warm while the tops are still creamy and the muffin bases are firm.
I'd like to make Eggnog II. Can you guide me through it while I cook?

Absolutely. Set out 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also need a large saucepan, a spoon for stirring, and a sink or bowl you can fill with ice water later.
I have the saucepan out. Do the eggs and milk go in cold, or should I warm anything first?
No need to warm them separately. Add the beaten eggs, the 2 1/4 cups milk, and the 1/3 cup white sugar directly to the large saucepan.
Those are in the pan. Should I add the vanilla extract now too?
Keep the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract measured and nearby, but the cooking directions start with the eggs, milk, and sugar in the saucepan.
Okay, the pan is on the stove. What heat should I use?
Use medium heat, and stir the mixture as it cooks. Keep it moving so the eggs heat gently and evenly.
How will I know when the eggnog base is cooked enough?
Cook and stir until the mixture coats a metal spoon. It should cling lightly to the spoon instead of running off like plain milk.
It's starting to coat the spoon now. Do I keep it on the burner longer?
Once it coats the metal spoon, remove the saucepan from the heat.
The pan is off the heat. What should I do so it cools safely?
Cool it quickly by placing the pan in a sink or bowl of ice water and stirring for 1 to 2 minutes. After that, stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so the flavor is included.
I'm ready to cook Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats. What should be ready before I begin? My potatoes are already baked.
Absolutely. You'll need 4 medium baked potatoes, quartered lengthwise, plus 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing for coating the skins.
I've got the baked potatoes cut into quarters. What else should I put on the counter?
Set out 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese. If you want a fresh topping at the end, have sliced green onions ready too; they're optional.
Do I need a baking sheet for these, and should the oven be heating?
Yes, use a baking sheet to hold the potato skins steady. Go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
The oven is heating, and the potato quarters are on the sheet. How much potato should I scoop out?
Scoop the potato out of the skins, leaving enough of the potato shell intact so the quarters still hold their boat shape.
The skins are hollowed out. Where does the Ranch go?
Brush or spoon the 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing over the inside of the potato skins so they're coated.
They're coated, but I still have the scooped potato sitting in a bowl. Does it go back in?
Yes. Place the scooped potato back into the coated skins, dividing it among the boats.
They're filled again. What's the last topping before they go in?
Sprinkle the 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese over the potato boats, then add sliced green onions if you're using them.
Campfire Angel Food Yummies is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track?

Absolutely. You'll need 1 (10 inch) angel food cake cut into large cubes, 1 (5 ounce) can of sweetened condensed milk, and 1 cup coconut flakes. You'll also want toasting sticks for holding the cake over the coals.
The cake is cubed, and I have the condensed milk and coconut out. Should the fire be flaming or mostly coals?
Mostly coals are best. Hold the angel food cake cubes over the campfire coals on the toasting sticks, turning them so the outside browns without scorching.
Some cubes are browning fast on one side. How dark should I let them get?
Aim for lightly to deeply golden browned edges, depending on how toasted you like them. Since angel food cake is airy, keep rotating the cubes so they toast evenly instead of burning.
Okay, I have a few toasted pieces ready. Do I pour the condensed milk into a bowl?
Yes, that will make dipping easier. Put the sweetened condensed milk in a small bowl, and set the coconut flakes in another bowl or shallow plate nearby.
The cake is still warm on the sticks. Do I dip it while it's hot?
Warm is fine. Slide or hold each toasted cake cube carefully, dip it into the condensed milk, then roll it in the coconut flakes so the coconut clings to the sticky coating.
The coconut is sticking well, but a couple pieces are getting messy. Any serving trick?
Set the coated cubes on a plate or pass them out right away on the sticks. They're meant to be a little gooey, with toasted cake, sweet condensed milk, and coconut in each bite.
I still have more cake cubes left. Should I coat them all at once?

It's better to toast and coat them in small batches. Keep browning the remaining angel food cake cubes over the coals, then dip each one in the condensed milk and roll it in coconut flakes just before serving.
Can you talk me through making Blackened Tuna? I've got tuna steaks out and want to keep the timing straight.
For this batch of Blackened Tuna, you'll need 1 1/2 pounds of fresh tuna steaks, about 1 inch thick, plus 2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 tablespoons butter.
The steaks are about an inch thick, and I have the Cajun seasoning. Should I season them before heating the skillet?
Yes. Generously coat the tuna steaks all over with the Cajun seasoning so the surface is well covered before they hit the pan.
They're coated pretty heavily now. What kind of pan and heat should I use?
Use a large skillet and set it over high heat. Add the 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter to the pan.
The butter is melting into the oil. How hot does it need to get before the tuna goes in?
Let the oil and butter get very hot, nearly smoking. That high heat is what helps the seasoning blacken quickly.
It's just starting to smoke a bit. Do I lay the steaks in flat, or should I move them around?
Place the tuna steaks flat in the skillet and leave them in place so the seasoned side can blacken.
Once they're in the pan, how long am I cooking that side?
Cook on one side for 3 to 4 minutes, or until that side is blackened.
The surface is getting dark and crusty at around 3 minutes. Is that the look I'm going for?
Yes, that dark, blackened crust is the target. If it needs a little more color, let it go closer to 4 minutes, then take it off before the crust overcooks.
Can you help me put together Cucumber Sandwiches for a small tray?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (8 ounce) package cream cheese spread, 2 teaspoons ranch salad dressing mix, 12 slices pumpernickel rye bread, and 2 medium cucumbers.
I've got the bread and cucumbers out. Do I need a pan or anything heated?
No heat needed for these. You'll just want a bowl, a spoon or spatula for mixing and spreading, a peeler if you want the cucumbers peeled, and a knife for thin slices.
The bowl is ready. What goes in it first?
Add the cream cheese spread to the bowl, then sprinkle in the ranch salad dressing mix. Stir until the ranch is evenly worked through the cream cheese.
It's mixed and looks pretty smooth. Should I spread it thick or thin?
Spread an even layer on one side of each slice of pumpernickel rye bread. It should cover the surface, but it doesn't need to be piled on.
All 12 slices have the cream cheese mixture on one side. How should I prep the cucumbers?
Peel the cucumbers if you'd like, then slice them thinly. Thin slices make the sandwiches easier to stack and bite into.
The cucumber slices are ready. Do they go on every piece of bread?
Place the cucumber slices on six of the bread slices, right on top of the cream cheese spread.
Six slices are topped with cucumber. What's the best way to close them up?
Top those with the remaining six bread slices, cream-cheese side down, to make the sandwiches. Press lightly, then serve as whole sandwiches or cut them into smaller pieces for the tray.
I want to make Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers. Can you guide me from setup through shaping the patties?
Absolutely. Start by getting your grill heating on high so it's ready when the patties are formed.
The grill is heating. I'm pulling ingredients out now—what should be on the counter first?
Set out 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, 1 small chopped onion, and 1 egg.
I've got the cheeses, onion, and egg. Do I mix those before adding the meat?
Yes. Use a large bowl and stir together the Cheddar, Parmesan, chopped onion, egg, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper until they're evenly combined.
That mixture is in the bowl. It looks loose from the egg and sauces—is that okay?
That's fine. The ground beef will bring it together. Crumble the beef into the bowl so it's easier to mix without overworking it.
Should I use a spoon, or is it better to mix the beef by hand?
Mix it by hand, just until the beef and seasoning mixture are combined. Stop once it looks evenly distributed so the burgers stay tender.
The beef mixture is combined. How many burgers am I making from this?
Shape the mixture into 6 patties. Try to keep them similar in thickness so they cook evenly on the hot grill.
I have 6 patties shaped. Where does the bacon go?
Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty, securing it snugly around the outside. Once all 6 are wrapped, they're ready to go onto the preheated high-heat grill.
I want to make Almond Apricot Bread, and I've cleared space for mixing. Can you walk me through what to gather?

Absolutely. Start by pulling out 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 3 teaspoons baking powder. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready for the dry ingredients.
Those dry ingredients are on the counter. The recipe mentions salt in the bowl too—should I add it with these?
Yes, add the salt with the flour, both sugars, and baking powder. Whisk or stir them together in the large bowl so the leavening and sugars are evenly distributed.
The dry mix is combined. I also have the baby food nearby; what should I do with it before mixing the wet ingredients?
Measure out and set aside 1 tablespoon baby food for the glaze. Keep that separate, then use the remaining baby food for the batter.
The glaze portion is set aside in a small dish. What bowl should I use next?
Use another bowl for the wet mixture. Beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food until the egg is broken up and everything looks fairly smooth.
I've beaten the wet ingredients together. Should I pour them in all at once or gradually?
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, then stir gently. The key is to mix just until moistened, not until perfectly smooth.
There are a few small streaks of flour left. Is that okay for this bread?
A few small streaks are fine while you're folding, but stop once the dry spots are moistened. Overmixing can make a quick bread tougher.
The batter is evenly moistened now, and I stopped before it got glossy. Anything I should check before moving on?

Make sure the reserved 1 tablespoon baby food for the glaze is still separate, and scrape down the bowl so the batter is consistent. At this point, you've completed the mixing steps for the Almond Apricot Bread.
I want to make Basil Burgers on the grill tonight. Can you guide me while I get everything ready?

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil, 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt, and some pepper. You'll also need a bowl, something to mix with, a plate for the patties, and an outdoor grill.
I've got the beef in a bowl and the seasonings measured. Should the grill be heating before I mix?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the outdoor grill on high heat so it's ready by the time the patties are shaped.
The grill is heating. Do I add everything to the beef at once?

Add the Worcestershire sauce, dried basil, garlic salt, and pepper right into the bowl with the ground beef. Mix gently until the seasonings are spread through the meat; try not to overwork it so the burgers stay tender.
The mixture smells good and looks evenly seasoned. How should I portion it?
Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions and shape them into burger patties. Make them fairly even in thickness so they cook at the same pace.
The patties are shaped. Should I do anything to the grill grate before they go on?
Lightly oil the grill grate before adding the burgers. That helps prevent sticking, especially with fresh patties.
While working on Basil Burgers, they're on the grill now. How long should I cook them before checking?
Cook the burgers for about 6 minutes total, turning once during cooking. Use a thermometer if you can; the safe internal temperature is 160 degrees F, or 70 degrees C.
They've hit 160 and I'm taking them off. Any quick serving advice?
Let them rest briefly while you get the buns and toppings ready. Then serve the Basil Burgers hot, with the basil and Worcestershire flavor still nice and savory.
I'm getting ready for Fruited Ice Cream. Can you help me sequence the steps?

Absolutely. Set out 2 (14 ounce) cans of sweetened condensed milk, 5 cups milk, 2 cups heavy cream, and 2 tablespoons vanilla extract. You'll also need the freezer canister for your ice cream maker, plus the salt and fruit called for in the mixing step.
I've got the condensed milk, regular milk, cream, and vanilla on the counter. Should the canister be ready before I mix?
Yes, have the freezer canister ready according to your ice cream maker's setup. Once it's ready, pour in the condensed milk, milk, heavy cream, and vanilla.
The liquids are in. The condensed milk is pretty thick at the bottom—do I need to stir it first?
Give it a thorough stir right in the canister so the condensed milk blends evenly with the milk and cream. Scrape the bottom gently so there aren't thick streaks left behind.
That looks smooth now. When do the fruit and salt go in?
Add the salt and fruit to the canister with the milk mixture now, then stir just enough to distribute the fruit throughout.
Fruit is mixed in. Should I fill the canister all the way, or leave space?
Leave the amount of headspace your ice cream maker recommends, since the mixture expands as it freezes. If your canister is too full, freeze it in batches rather than overfilling.
Okay, it's loaded safely. How long should I run the machine?
Freeze it according to the manufacturer's directions for your specific ice cream maker. Watch for the mixture to thicken and churn into a soft ice cream texture.
It's churned and looks soft-serve. Is it ready to eat or should I do anything else?
You can serve it right away if you like a soft texture. For firmer scoops, transfer the Fruited Ice Cream to a freezer-safe container, cover it, and let it firm up in the freezer before serving.
Bahama Mama II is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got a glass and ice ready, but I want to measure it correctly.
Absolutely. For one drink, measure 1 fluid ounce dark rum and 1/2 fluid ounce apricot brandy into a mixing glass.
The rum and apricot brandy are in the mixing glass. What should I add for the fruity part?
Add 3 1/2 fluid ounces fruit punch, then pour in 1/2 fluid ounce pina colada mix.
Do I need to shake it, or is stirring better for this one?
Stir it well in the mixing glass until the rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and pina colada mix are evenly blended.
It looks mixed and kind of tropical pink-orange. Should the ice go in before or after?
Put fresh ice in your serving glass, then pour the blended drink over the ice.
Should I strain it, or just pour everything straight over the ice?
Since the recipe is just stirred liquids, you can pour it straight over the ice from the mixing glass.
The drink is over ice now. Any final adjustment before I serve it?
Give it a quick look to make sure it's blended, and serve it cold right away.
Great, so the whole process was just combine everything, stir, and serve over ice?
Yes. Combine the dark rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and pina colada mix in a mixing glass, stir to blend, and serve over ice.
I pulled up Easy Fried Eggplant. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got 1 large eggplant on the counter.
Absolutely. Peel the eggplant if you haven't already, then slice it into pieces ready for coating. You'll also need 2 tablespoons canola oil, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 cups dry bread crumbs.
For Easy Fried Eggplant, the eggplant is peeled and sliced. Should I set up the eggs and crumbs before heating the pan?
Yes, that will make the frying smoother. Put the 3 beaten eggs in one shallow dish and the 2 cups dry bread crumbs in another so you can dip each slice quickly.
Coating station is ready. What pan setup should I use?
Use a large skillet and add the 2 tablespoons canola oil. Heat it over medium-high heat until the oil is hot enough for frying.
The oil looks hot. Do I coat all the slices now or work as I go?
Work in a steady rhythm: dip an eggplant slice into the beaten egg, then press it into the dry bread crumbs, and place it carefully into the hot oil.
A few slices are in the skillet. How long should I leave them before turning?
Fry them for 2 to 3 minutes on that side, watching for a golden brown crust before you flip.
They're browning nicely. Same timing after I flip them?
Yes. Fry the second side for another 2 to 3 minutes, or until both sides are golden brown.
They're golden now. What should I do with them after they come out of the skillet?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain. Let the excess oil blot off for a moment, then they're ready to serve.
Before I get moving on Date Nut Bars, what should I have ready? I've got my mixing bowl out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Measure 2 cups sugar and 2 cups all-purpose flour into your large bowl, then add 2 teaspoons baking powder and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Those dry ingredients are in the bowl. Should the dates and nuts go in before the wet ingredients?
Yes, add the dates and nuts to the bowl with the sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt. Stir them around so they're evenly coated and distributed.
The dates are a little sticky, but they're mixed through. What do I add next?
Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla. Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened; don't worry if it takes some effort, because the batter is supposed to be very stiff.
It's definitely stiff. I don't want to overmix—should I stop once I don't see dry flour?
That's the right point to stop. As soon as there are no obvious dry pockets and everything looks moistened, leave it alone.
What pan should I use, and does it need anything before the batter goes in?
Use a greased 15-in pan. Scrape the stiff batter into it and spread it as evenly as you can, pushing it into the corners.
The batter is in the pan, but it's not perfectly smooth on top. Is that okay?
Yes, a slightly uneven top is fine. Just aim for an even thickness so the bars bake at the same rate.
Ready for the oven. What temperature and how long should I bake them?
Bake the Date Nut Bars at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes, until the top is golden brown. Let them cool before cutting so the bars hold together neatly.
I'm starting Cindis Egg Rolls; can you walk me through the setup? I've got a wok out, but I want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 pound ground pork and 4 cups shredded cabbage. Keep the wok ready for the pork, and use a large bowl for the vegetables.
The pork and cabbage are on the counter. What vegetables should I shred or slice before I turn on the heat?
Prep 1 large carrot, shredded, and 1/2 green bell pepper cut into thin strips. You'll also want onion, garlic, and ginger ready to mix with the cabbage, carrot, and bell pepper.
Carrot is shredded, pepper is sliced, and the aromatics are ready. Should I cook the vegetables first or the pork?
Cook the pork first. Put the ground pork in the large wok over medium-high heat and break it up as it cooks.
It's browning now and there's some fat collecting in the wok. What texture am I looking for before I stop?
For Cindis Egg Rolls, cook it until the pork is no longer pink and is crumbled through. Once it's cooked, drain it well and set it aside.
Pork is drained and sitting in a bowl. Do I wipe out the wok or start combining the filling somewhere else?
For this part, use a large bowl. Mix together the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, thin green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger.
The vegetable mixture is in the large bowl. Should the cooked pork go in there too right now?
Yes, you can keep the pork nearby to combine with the filling, but the next specific mix is the sauce: use a small bowl for the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses.
I've got the small bowl out. How smooth does that sauce need to be before I add it?
Whisk the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses until the mixture is smooth with no dry cornstarch clumps. Then it's ready to coat the egg roll filling.
I'd like to make Gelatin Fruit Salad. Can you guide me through it without rushing?

Absolutely. Set out a saucepan, a spoon or whisk, and a dish or mold for chilling. For ingredients, you'll need 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple, undrained.
I found the applesauce and cherry gelatin. Should the pineapple be drained before I open everything?
Keep the pineapple undrained; the juice goes into the salad. Go ahead and open the soda and pineapple, but pour slowly later so the mixture doesn't foam over.
The saucepan is ready. Do I put only the applesauce in it to start?
Yes, add just the 1 cup applesauce to the saucepan and heat it until it comes to a boil. Stir now and then so it heats evenly.
It's bubbling around the edges and steaming. Is that enough of a boil?
That works. Take the pan off the heat, then stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin. Keep stirring until the gelatin is fully dissolved and the mixture looks smooth.
The gelatin has dissolved, and the mixture is glossy. I'm worried about the soda fizzing.
Add the 12 ounce can of lemon-lime soda slowly, a little at a time, stirring gently as you pour. That should keep the fizz manageable.
Soda is mixed in. When should the crushed pineapple go in?
Stir in the 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple now, including its juice. Fold it through gently so the fruit is evenly distributed.
It's all combined in the bowl. How do I know when it's ready to serve?
Transfer it to your serving dish or mold, then refrigerate until firm. Once it holds its shape and doesn't slosh when gently moved, it's ready to serve chilled.
I'm ready to cook Broccoli Cheese Crepes. What should be ready before I begin? I'm starting with the batter ingredients on the counter.
Absolutely. For the crepe batter, set out 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I've got the eggs and water measured. Should the flour and salt go in separately or all at once?
They can go in together. Add the eggs, water, flour, and salt to a blender so the batter can come together smoothly.
Everything is in the blender. How smooth am I aiming for?
Cover the blender and process until the batter looks smooth, with no dry flour pockets or obvious lumps.
The batter looks smooth now. Do I use it right away?
Let it stand for 15 minutes. That rest helps the flour hydrate before you cook the crepes.
While it rests, I see the recipe mentions onion and butter. What should I do with them?
Use a small saucepan for that part. Saute the onion in butter until the onion is tender.
How can I tell the onion is tender enough without overdoing it?
It should look softened and smell mellow, not sharp. Keep the heat moderate and stir so the butter doesn't scorch.
The onion is softened. What's the next move for the sauce base?
Stir in flour until it's blended with the butter and onion, making a smooth base with no dry streaks.
Help me stay organized for Chicken Fried Chops 2. What comes first? I've got pork chops out and want to set up the coating before I start heating the skillet.

Absolutely. For the dredge, measure 1/2 cup all-purpose flour into a shallow bowl, then add 2 teaspoons salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground mustard, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Stir that mixture well so the seasoning is evenly spread through the flour.
The flour mixture is in a wide bowl. Should the chops go straight into it, or do I need another coating step?

For this recipe, just dredge the pork chops in that seasoned flour mixture. Press each chop lightly into the flour on both sides so it gets coated, then shake off any loose excess before it goes to the skillet.
They're coated. What kind of pan setup should I use for browning?
Use a skillet with oil in it, enough to brown the chops without crowding them. Once the oil is hot, lay the chops in carefully and brown them on both sides.
I'm browning them now. How dark should I let the crust get before turning?
Look for a firm golden-brown surface on the first side before you flip. You're not finishing them in the skillet here; you just want both sides browned before they go into the slow cooker.
Both sides are browned and I've got the slow cooker ready. Do I stack the chops or spread them out?
Place the browned chops in the slow cooker. If they fit in a single layer, that's ideal, but a little overlap is fine as long as they're settled in evenly.
They're in. The recipe mentions soup and water, but I'm not sure when to add them.
Combine the soup and water in a bowl until smooth, then pour that mixture over the chops in the slow cooker so the tops are covered.
The sauce is poured over. Anything I should do before putting the lid on?

Make sure the chops are sitting down in the soup-and-water mixture and scrape in any browned bits or coating left from the skillet if you want extra flavor. Then cover the slow cooker and continue with your slow-cooking time for the recipe.
I'm making Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version today. What's the best place to start? I've got 6 center cut pork chops trimmed of visible fat and I want to set up before I start.

Absolutely. Set the pork chops on a clean plate, and have 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/2 teaspoon seasoning salt nearby. You'll also need the egg mixture, flour for a light dredge, and bread crumbs for coating.
The oven is still cold. What temperature should I use, and should I prep the coating while it heats?
heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, you can arrange your coating station so the chops move from flour to egg to bread crumbs without much mess.
I have 1 egg beaten in a small bowl, but the recipe wording says "beaten with." Should I treat that as the egg mixture?
Yes—use the beaten egg as the wet dip, and if you're using egg substitute with it, keep that mixture together in the small bowl as the recipe indicates.
Before breading, do I rinse the pork chops or just season them?
Rinse the pork chops, then pat them dry really well so the coating sticks. Season them with the garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste.
They're dry and seasoned. Should the flour layer be thick or barely there?
Keep the flour layer light. Dredge each pork chop just enough to dust the surface, then shake off any extra before dipping it into the beaten egg mixture.
After the egg dip, how heavy should I go with the bread crumbs?
Coat them liberally with bread crumbs after the egg dip, pressing gently so the crumbs cling to both sides and the edges.
I'm trying to keep the counter clean—any quick setup tip before I coat all 6?

Line up the bowls in order: flour, beaten egg mixture, then bread crumbs, with the baking dish or tray at the end. Use one hand for dry ingredients and the other for the egg mixture to cut down on clumps.

source_seed.recipe_title: Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version

messages.content: I'm making E Z Cheezy Pie today. What's the best place to start? I've got the counter cleared but want to be sure I'm not missing anything.
Absolutely. Set out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells and 3 softened 8 ounce packages of cream cheese. You'll also need 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The pie shells are already baked, and the cream cheese has been sitting out. Should I turn the oven on anyway?
Yes, follow the recipe and bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Oven is heating. What bowl and mixer setup should I use for the cream cheese?
Use a medium mixing bowl. Add the softened cream cheese and whip it until it looks fluffy rather than dense or blocky.
It's mostly smooth but a little heavy at the edges of the bowl. Keep mixing?
Yes, scrape the sides of the bowl and keep whipping until the cream cheese is evenly fluffy throughout.
That texture looks better. Do I add the sugar all at once?
Add the 1/2 cup white sugar, then pour in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
Both are in the bowl. Should I mix gently or beat it more firmly?
Mix until the filling is smooth, with no visible streaks of sugar or vanilla and no cream cheese lumps.
It's smooth now. Since I have 2 shells, should I divide the mixture between them?
Yes, divide the smooth cream cheese mixture between the 2 baked 9 inch pie shells, spreading it evenly so each shell gets a level filling.
I'm making Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms and I've got a tray ready. Can you guide me without rushing? I want to keep the mushrooms from getting soggy.
Absolutely. Start by checking your ingredients: you'll need 3/4 cup melted butter total, divided, plus 1 pound fresh mushrooms with the stems removed. Pat the mushroom caps dry if they feel damp.
The mushrooms are cleaned and the stems are out. I have the melted butter too. What else should be on the counter?

For this batch of Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms, set out 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons and 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese. You'll also be mixing in crabmeat, lobster, and garlic for the stuffing.
Got it. Should I turn on the oven before I start mixing the filling?
Yes, get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). That way it's ready once the mushrooms are filled.
Oven is heating. I'm using a large baking sheet—do I line it or butter it?
Brush the large baking sheet with about 1/4 cup of the melted butter. Spread it around so the mushroom caps get a little richness underneath.
The pan is buttered. Should the mushrooms be packed close together or spaced out?
Arrange the mushroom caps in a single layer over the baking sheet. They can be close, but avoid stacking or overlapping them so they cook evenly.
They're all sitting cup-side up. I'm ready to make the stuffing—what goes in the bowl?
Here, in a medium bowl, combine the 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons, the remaining 1/2 cup melted butter, the 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic.
The filling looks buttery and chunky from the croutons. Is that the texture I want before spooning it in?
Yes, that sounds right: moist enough from the butter to hold together, with texture from the croutons and seafood. Spoon it into the mushroom caps evenly, then they'll be ready for the oven.
I'm starting Easy Fried Eggplant; can you walk me through the setup? I've got a large skillet out but haven't prepped anything yet.
Absolutely. Start by getting the ingredients together: 2 tablespoons canola oil, 1 large eggplant that's peeled and sliced, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 cups dry bread crumbs.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced, and I have the eggs cracked into a bowl. Should I beat them before setting up the bread crumbs?

Use a large mixing bowl. Add the softened butter and brown sugar, then cream them together until the mixture looks fluffy and lighter.

Yes. Add the mashed bananas along with the milk, vanilla, and eggs, then mix well until everything is evenly combined.

Give the bowl a final scrape along the bottom and sides so there are no streaks of butter or sugar, then you're ready to portion the batter into the prepared muffin pan.

Season the chicken pieces with garlic powder before they go into the pot, then place them in the hot oil to brown.

Brown the chicken on both sides. You're aiming for a good golden surface before moving the pieces out of the Dutch oven.

Transfer the browned chicken to paper towels so it can drain while you deal with the fat in the pan.

Don't wipe it clean. Spoon off the chicken fat, then return the pan to the stove so it's ready for the next part of the recipe.

Absolutely. Start by setting out the dry measured ingredients: 1 cup rye flour, 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup sugar, and 2 1/2 teaspoons baking powder. You'll also need salt, caraway seeds, cheese, an egg, milk, and oil.

Keep it a bit rough. Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened; a few small lumps are fine, and overmixing can make the muffins tougher.

Spoon the batter into the greased or paper-lined muffin cups until each one is about two-thirds full. That leaves room for the muffins to rise.

The oven is on, and I have the medium bowl out. Should I put the margarine and sugar in before measuring anything else?

Beat in 1 egg, then add 1/4 cup molasses. Mix until the color turns evenly dark and glossy, with no pale streaks hiding at the bottom of the bowl.

Great. I have the large bowl on the counter. Which dry ingredients go into it?

Measure in 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 3 teaspoons baking powder. Add the salt with those dry ingredients, then whisk everything together so the baking powder and sugars are evenly spread.
The sugars are a little clumpy from the brown sugar. Should I break those up before adding anything else?

Yes, press out the larger brown sugar clumps with the back of a spoon or your fingertips. Once the dry mixture looks fairly even, whisk in that restrained cardamom-and-ginger touch so it doesn't collect in one spot.
I really like that soft warm spice in sweet fruit breads; that's exactly what I wanted for this one.
That will fit nicely here. Keep it subtle, then let the apricot baby food and almond-style sweetness carry the main flavor of the bread.
Dry bowl is mixed. Before I open the baby food, remind me what gets held back for the glaze.
Spoon out 1 tablespoon of the baby food and set it aside for the glaze. The rest of the baby food will go into the wet ingredient bowl.
I've reserved the tablespoon. What should I combine in the second bowl?
Beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food in that second bowl. Mix until it looks smooth and even, without worrying about making it airy.
The wet mixture is smooth. Should I pour it all into the dry bowl at once?
Yes, pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients in one addition. Stir gently with a spatula just until the flour is moistened.
I can still see a couple of pale streaks near the edge. Do I keep stirring until the batter is totally smooth?
No, don't beat it smooth. Scrape around the edge and fold once or twice to catch dry pockets, then stop while the batter is thick and just moistened.
The batter looks thick and a little lumpy now, but I don't see loose flour. Is that ready to move on?
Yes, that texture is right for Almond Apricot Bread. A thick, slightly lumpy batter will help keep the loaf tender, and the reserved 1 tablespoon of baby food is ready for the glaze later.
I'd like to make Fire Side Coffee mix. Can you help me set up the dry ingredients and jar it properly?

Absolutely. Put a large bowl, a sifter or fine mesh strainer, measuring cups, a teaspoon, and a clean lidded jar on the counter. You'll need 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
I have the creamer and hot chocolate measured. Should I add the coffee granules straight into the same bowl?
Yes, add the 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules to the bowl with the creamer and hot chocolate mix. Keep the bowl dry so the mix stays powdery.
The coffee is in. The cinnamon is clumping a little in the spoon—does that matter?

That's exactly why sifting helps. Measure 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, then sift it together with the creamer, hot chocolate mix, and instant coffee until the color looks even. The written step also mentions nutmeg; if you're using it, sift it in with the cinnamon, but no amount is given in the recipe.
I'm sifting now, but some coffee granules are hanging back in the strainer.

Gently tap or stir them through if they'll pass. If a few larger granules remain, add them back to the bowl and whisk everything well so each scoop has coffee, chocolate, creamer, and spice distributed throughout.
The mix looks uniform. What's the best way to get it into the jar without making a mess?
Use a funnel or a folded piece of parchment as a chute, then pour the dry mixture into the jar. Leave a little headspace at the top so you can shake it later if it settles.
It's in the jar now. Do I just close it, or should I pack it down?
Don't pack it down. Seal the jar with a lid, then give it a gentle shake to settle the powder evenly while keeping it loose enough to scoop.
I want to try a mug before putting it away. How much mix goes into the water?
Stir 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture into 1 cup of hot water. Taste it, then adjust to taste with a little more mix for a stronger drink or more hot water if you want it lighter.

Use the crunchy topping in bigger bits and tuck it through the middle so it stays crisp and gives each bite some texture.
Great, I'm doing that version. Before I start boiling, what should I have on the counter?
Set out 1 1/2 pounds russet potatoes, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 egg, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley. You'll also want a large pot, a lightly floured work surface, and a rolling pin.
The potatoes are scrubbed, and the pot is nearly at a boil. Do I peel them now or leave them alone?
Leave the potatoes whole and in their skins. Put them into the large pot of boiling water and boil them for 25 to 30 minutes, until they're tender enough to handle for mashing later.
While they boil, should I mix the flour, egg, and parsley together?
Hold off on mixing them into anything yet. Just keep the flour, egg, and parsley ready; the recipe's next move is all about getting the cooked potatoes drained and cool enough to peel.
The timer is close to 30 minutes, and the potatoes feel tender. What should I do with the water?
Lift the potatoes out carefully, then discard the water from the pot. Let the potatoes sit until they're cool enough to handle without burning your fingers.
They're cooling on a plate. I'm trying to keep the counter from getting gummy—how much flour on the surface?
Use a light dusting of the all-purpose flour on the work surface. Once the potatoes are cool enough, peel them and place them right onto that lightly floured area.
The skins are off, and the potatoes are on the floured board. Do I need a masher, or is the rolling pin really the tool here?
Use the rolling pin. Press and mash the peeled potatoes with it on the lightly floured surface, working them until they're broken down evenly.
For serving as a wrap filling, should I add the crunchy center before or after the potato is mashed?
Mash the potatoes first. When you assemble the hand-held version, place the bigger crunchy pieces in the center layer so they don't get crushed into the potato mixture.

Keep the serving garnish to one flavorful accent and one crunchy accent; leave off any extra decorative toppings. For the dressing, set out a small bowl, a whisk, and your measuring cups and spoons.
I have the bowl and whisk out. Which dressing ingredients should I measure first?
Measure 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/4 cup orange marmalade, 3 tablespoons cider vinegar, and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise. Put them near the bowl so you can whisk the dressing all at once.
The marmalade is pretty thick. Should I warm it or just whisk harder?

No need to warm it unless it is stiff from the fridge. Add the marmalade with the mayonnaise and vinegar, whisk until it loosens, then stream in the vegetable oil and keep whisking until the dressing looks smooth.
I like that two-accent finish; that's exactly what I wanted for this salad. Once the dressing is smooth, does it go straight on the chicken?
Chill the dressing first. The recipe has you whisk the dressing ingredients until smooth, then chill it so it is ready when the salad is assembled.
Got it. The chicken is cooked and cooled, and I have raisins, almonds, and parsley nearby. Should I combine those now?
Wait until just before serving if you can. That keeps the almonds from softening and helps the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley stay distinct before the dressing goes on.
I'm about fifteen minutes from serving. What bowl should I use, and what goes in first?
Use a large bowl with enough room to toss without crushing anything. Add the chicken first, scatter in the raisins, almonds, and parsley, then give them a gentle lift with tongs or a wide spoon.
For the two accents, would parsley and almonds cover it, or should I add something else at the end?
Parsley can be the fresh, flavorful accent, and almonds can be the crunchy one. If you want the top to look finished, reserve a small pinch of each and skip any extra decorative add-ons.
The dressing has chilled and the serving bowl is ready. How do I bring it together without making it heavy?
Pour on part of the chilled dressing first, toss gently, then add more only if the chicken mixture needs it. Serve right away so the Garden Party Salad stays fresh, lightly coated, and crunchy.

Go with cinnamon and ginger, and skip cardamom for this batch.

Set out 1 cup chocolate hazelnut spread, 4 crepes, 4 bananas sliced, and 1 (7 ounce) can of pressurized whipped cream for serving.

Let the skillet warm gently over medium heat while you assemble the crepes, so it's ready when they're rolled.

Use 1/4 cup of chocolate hazelnut spread on each crepe, spreading it evenly enough to cover the center without making the edges messy.

Arrange 1 sliced banana down the center of each crepe, keeping the fruit in a neat strip so the sides can fold around it.

Roll each crepe around the banana filling, then place the rolled crepes into the warm skillet over medium heat.

Let them warm for about 90 seconds, just long enough for the filling to soften and the crepes to feel gently heated.
Once they're warmed, how should I serve them without making the plate look messy?
Move them to plates right away and add the pressurized whipped cream just before serving, so it stays fluffy against the warm chocolate-hazelnut and banana crepes.

I added a small shake, and that's enough heat for us. Do I do anything with the avocado pits I saved?

The pit is tucked into the bowl. We're not eating for 20 minutes, and I'm trying to keep the counter clear.

Take the pit out just before serving, give the guacamole a gentle stir, and transfer it to your serving bowl if you want a cleaner presentation.
I want to make A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie. Can you help me get set up at the blender?
Absolutely. Put your blender on the counter and have the fruit ready: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen mixed berries and 1 (15 ounce) can sliced peaches, drained.
The berries are still frozen, and I drained the peaches. Is there anything besides the fruit?
Yes, measure out 2 tablespoons honey. That is the only other ingredient you need for this smoothie.
Should I add the frozen berries or peaches to the blender jar first?
Either order will work. Add the frozen mixed berries and the drained sliced peaches to the blender jar, then drizzle in the honey.
All three ingredients are in. The frozen berries are sitting on top of the peaches.
That is fine. Secure the lid tightly before blending, since the fruit can shift around as the blades start.
Lid is on. How long should I blend it?
Blend until the mixture looks smooth, with no large pieces of frozen berry or peach remaining.
It is moving, but there are still a few berry chunks near the sides.
Stop the blender, scrape or nudge the mixture down if needed, put the lid back on, and blend again until it smooths out.
Now it looks thick and evenly blended. Is it ready to serve?
Yes. Once it is smooth, pour the smoothie into glasses and serve it right away while it is cold and bright from the frozen berries.

That is okay for this salsa. Stir the jalapeno and Anaheim chile slices into the lime-coated apples, then scrape the board clean before you work on the remaining add-ins.
The chiles are mixed in. I also see onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt in the instructions, but I don't have quantities for them.

Use them as finishing add-ins and keep each one modest: finely cut the onion, roughly chop the cilantro and walnuts, and mince or grate the ginger so it can spread evenly. Have the salt ready for a light sprinkle rather than a heavy pour.

Tap or scatter the grated ginger over the surface of the salsa instead of dropping it in one mound. Then add the onion, cilantro, walnuts, and salt across the top so everything is easier to fold in evenly.

Keep the salsa cool until you are ready to serve. Right before it goes out, give it one gentle fold to bring the lime juices back through the bowl, then serve the Fresh Apple Salsa while the apple pieces still have their crisp bite.
