I want to make Gelatin Fruit Salad. Can you talk me through what to set out before I start?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup applesauce and 2 (3 ounce) packages of cherry gelatin. You'll also need a saucepan and something to stir with.
I've got the saucepan, applesauce, and both gelatin boxes. Is there anything from the pantry or fridge I'm missing?
Yes—grab 1 (12 ounce) can of lemon-lime soda and 1 (8 ounce) can of crushed pineapple. Keep the pineapple undrained; the juice goes in too.
The pineapple can is open and I left the juice in. Do I pour the soda in right away?
Not yet. Start by putting the applesauce in the saucepan and bringing it to a boil over the stove.
It's heating now. Should I stir it while it comes up to a boil?
A few stirs are fine so it heats evenly and doesn't sit too long in one spot. Once it reaches a boil, take the pan off the heat.
Okay, the applesauce boiled and the pan is off the burner. Where does the cherry gelatin come in?
Stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin while the applesauce is hot. Keep stirring until the gelatin is fully dissolved and you don't see dry granules.
The mixture looks smooth and glossy. Should the soda go in fast or slowly?
Add the lemon-lime soda slowly so it doesn't foam up too much, then stir in the undrained crushed pineapple.
Everything is mixed together. What should I put it in, and how do I know when it's ready?
Pour it into your serving dish or mold, then refrigerate it until firm. It's ready when the salad holds its shape and no longer sloshes when you gently move the dish.

I want to make Almond Apricot Bread, but I'd like to set up the bowls and ingredients as I go. Can you walk me through it?

Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter for the dry ingredients. Measure in 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, 3 teaspoons baking powder, and the salt called for in the recipe.
The flour, both sugars, baking powder, and salt are in the large bowl. Should I whisk them together or just leave them layered?

Done. I also have the baby food nearby for the apricot part. How much do I need to hold back?
Before mixing the wet ingredients, set aside 1 tablespoon of the baby food for the glaze. Keep the remaining baby food for the batter.

Stir in the 3/4 cup white sugar, the 1/4 teaspoon salt, the 2 teaspoons vanilla extract, and the syrup. Mix until the sugar is worked evenly through the egg mixture.
The mixture is coming together, but I don't see a butter amount here. What should I do with the butter step?
Follow the recipe's direction to melt the butter or margarine, then add it to the egg mixture. Since no amount is listed here, use the amount from your recipe card or package notes if you have it.
Should the melted butter be piping hot when I pour it in?
Let it cool briefly if it's very hot, then pour it in slowly while stirring so it blends into the eggs without scrambling them.
The filling looks glossy now. Anything I should check before moving on with the pie?

Make sure the sugar, salt, vanilla, syrup, and melted butter or margarine are evenly mixed into the beaten eggs, with no streaks of butter sitting on top. Once it looks uniform, you're ready for the next pie assembly step.

Lower the beef shank into the boiling water carefully, then adjust the heat so it simmers rather than rolls hard.

Lift the meat out of the broth, trim away any gristle, then cut the meat into medium sized pieces and set it aside.

I want to make British Bread Pudding, and I've got a big mixing bowl out. Can you talk me through what to gather and when to start the oven?
Absolutely. Set out 6 1/4 cups cubed whole wheat bread and 1 1/4 cups milk, since those soak together early. You'll also need 1 egg, beaten, and 1/3 cup butter, softened.
The bread cubes are measured and the milk is ready. Should I preheat before I start soaking?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, so it's heating while you mix the pudding.
Oven is on. Do I just pour the milk over the bread in the bowl?
Yes. Put the cubed whole wheat bread in the large bowl, pour in the milk, and gently press or stir so the bread is evenly moistened.
It's all damp now, with a few firmer pieces around the edges. How long should it sit?
Let the bread and milk stand for 5 minutes. During that time, the drier pieces should soften and the mixture should look more evenly soaked.
While it soaks, I've got the beaten egg and softened butter nearby. What gets stirred in after the timer?
After the soak, stir in the beaten egg and softened butter. The recipe also calls for raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon to go in at this stage.

Mix well until the bread, milk, egg, butter, raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon are evenly distributed. It should look like a cohesive, moist pudding mixture rather than separate dry bread cubes.
I want to make Fresh Apple Salsa. Can you stay with me while I prep the ingredients?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl, then get 2 tart apples cored and cubed and 4 tablespoons lime juice ready. The lime juice will help coat the apples right away.
The apples are cubed. Should I add them to the bowl with the lime juice now?
Yes, put the cubed apples in the large bowl and stir them with the lime juice until the pieces are evenly coated.
They're coated and glossy. I also have the peppers washed—what should I do with them?
Seed and slice 1 fresh jalapeno pepper and 1 fresh Anaheim chile. Once they're sliced, stir both into the apple-lime mixture.
The chile slices are in. I'm seeing onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt on my counter too.
Good—stir in the onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt next, making sure they're spread through the apples and peppers rather than clumped in one spot.
The walnuts are sitting mostly on top. Do I need to chop or mash anything, or just keep it chunky?
Keep it chunky. This salsa should be mixed thoroughly, not mashed, so fold everything together until the walnuts, herbs, ginger, and salt are evenly distributed.
It smells bright and spicy. Should it look saucy or more like a chopped relish?
More like a chopped relish. The lime juice should lightly coat the ingredients, while the apple cubes and chile slices remain distinct.
Everything looks evenly mixed now. Is there anything else before serving?
You're done once it's thoroughly mixed. Give the bowl a quick scrape around the sides, then serve the Fresh Apple Salsa while the apples are crisp.
I want to make California Chicken, but I'd like to get the pan and oven timing right. Can you talk me through it?
Absolutely. Set the oven to preheat at 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready while you work on the chicken.
Oven is heating. What ingredients should I have next to the stove?
Have 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts ready, along with 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1 pinch salt.
I've got the chicken breasts and seasonings out. Should I start with the oil in a skillet?
Yes. Warm the olive oil in a skillet over the stove, then add the chicken. Add the onion flavoring there too, using the 1/2 teaspoon onion powder from your ingredients.

Cook it for about 15 minutes, watching for the chicken to brown and look just about done.

Give the chicken a final check to make sure it's browned and just about done from the skillet cooking, then serve it hot once the seasoning tastes right.

Go ahead and mash with the fork, pressing the avocado into the garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber until the mixture turns smooth.

A few tiny soft bits are fine, but keep mashing a little longer if you want it creamier. The target is a smooth dip-like texture.

Mix in red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper. Stir well so the herbs and seasoning are evenly spread through the avocado mixture.

Cook the mixture for 10 minutes, or until the mushrooms and green onions are tender. Once they have softened, you are ready for the next part of the puffs.

original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making French Spring Soup as simmered beans, sauce, or stew with chili, hot sauce, pepper flakes, spicy oil, jalapeno, or cayenne. How should I handle the chili?

messages.content: Tonight I'm doing French Spring Soup in a spicier, stew-like direction, with a little chili involved just for this pot. When should that heat go in?
Warm a small pinch of chili in the butter as it melts so the flavor opens up early, and don't add more chili as a topping later.
Perfect, that's the one-off version I want tonight. I have a large pot out—what should I prep first?
Get 1/4 cup butter measured and chop 1 pound of leeks. Keep the pot ready for medium heat.
The leeks are chopped. Do I need the onion ready before the pot goes on?
Yes, chop 1 onion before you start cooking so it can go in with the leeks once the butter is melted.
Butter, leeks, and onion are set. Anything liquid or bulky I should have nearby?
Have 2 quarts water close to the stove, and set out the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice so they're ready when the water goes in.
I'm turning on the burner now. How should the butter look before I add vegetables?
Melt the butter in the large pot over medium heat until it is fully liquid and glossy, then let that small pinch of chili warm in it briefly.
The butter is melted and the chili smells fragrant, not burnt. Leeks and onion next?
Add the chopped leeks and onion, stir them through the butter, and cook until they soften and turn tender.
They've softened and the pot bottom looks clear when I stir. Do I add the water all at once?
Yes, pour the full 2 quarts water into the pot and stir to lift up any buttery bits from the bottom.
Water is in. What goes in before I leave it to simmer?
Mix in the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice, stirring so everything is evenly distributed in the soup.
I'm making Crawfish Etouffee III and have a large saucepan ready. Can you walk me through the setup?

Absolutely. Set out 1 chopped onion, 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed tomato soup, 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup, and 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers. Keep the crawfish nearby for the later simmer.
The onion is chopped, and the cans are open. Should I start heating the pan now?
Yes. Put the large saucepan over medium heat, add the chopped onion, and sauté it until it turns clear.
The onion is softening but still a little white in the center. Do I wait longer?
Give it a bit more time on medium heat. You're looking for the onion to look clear and softened before adding the soups and tomatoes.
The onion looks clear now. Do the soups go in together?
They can go in together. Add the condensed tomato soup, the condensed cream of mushroom soup, and the diced tomatoes with green chile peppers to the saucepan.
Everything is in the pan, but the soups are thick. Should I stir until it's smooth?
Yes, stir well so the soups loosen into the tomatoes and the mixture looks evenly combined. Once it's blended and gently bubbling, let it simmer for 15 minutes.
It has simmered for 15 minutes and smells good. When should the crawfish go in?
Add the crawfish to the pan now, stirring it into the sauce so it's coated evenly.
The crawfish is mixed in. How long do I keep it going, and should the heat stay the same?
Keep it at a steady simmer and cook the crawfish in the sauce for 25 minutes. Stir occasionally so the etouffee heats evenly and doesn't stick to the bottom.
I'm making Cookie Bowl and want to get the setup right. What should I pull out before I touch the oven?
Set out 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup sliced almonds. You'll also need a 9x5 inch loaf pan or a metal bowl, foil, and a cookie sheet.
I have the flour, cocoa, salt, and almonds measured. Should I heat the oven now or prep the pan first?
Go ahead and get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, you can work on the pan setup.
The oven is heating. I'm using a 9x5 inch loaf pan—how exactly should it sit?
Turn the 9x5 inch loaf pan upside down so the outside becomes the mold for the cookie bowl.
It's upside down on the counter. Do I wrap the whole thing in foil?
Cover the outside of the upside-down pan with foil, smoothing it over the surface so the cookie bowl has a shaped base to bake against.
Foil is on. I'm worried about moving it without bending the foil.
Lift it carefully from the sides and place the foil-covered, upside-down pan onto a cookie sheet. The cookie sheet will make it easier to move in and out of the oven.
Pan is on the cookie sheet. What should I do with the measured dry ingredients?
Stir together the all-purpose flour, unsweetened cocoa powder, salt, and sliced almonds until the cocoa and almonds are evenly distributed.
The dry mixture looks evenly combined. Do I need to do anything else to it right now?
No further mixing is listed at this point. Set the flour, cocoa, salt, and almond mixture aside while the oven finishes reaching 350 degrees F.
I'm making Chai Butter Cookies and have a large mixing bowl ready. Can you help me get the ingredients organized?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup chai tea mix, 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also want the flour, baking powder, and salt ready for the dry mixture later.
The butter is softened, and the sugar and chai mix are measured. Do I add all three to the bowl together?
Yes. Put the butter, the 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and the chai tea mix into the large bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks light and fluffy.
It's starting to look paler, but there are still a few butter streaks. Should I keep mixing?
Keep going a little longer. You're aiming for a smooth, fluffy base with the chai mix evenly worked through before the eggs go in.
Okay, the mixture looks fluffy now. How should I handle the eggs?
Beat in the 2 eggs one at a time. Add the first egg and mix until it's fully incorporated, then add the second egg and mix well again.
Both eggs are mixed in, and the batter looks a bit looser. What happens with the dry ingredients?
Combine the flour, baking powder, and salt separately, then blend that dry mixture into the creamed mixture. Mix just until all of the dry ingredients have been absorbed.
I can still see a little flour on the side of the bowl. Should I scrape it down?
Yes, scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl, then mix briefly until no dry patches remain. Stop once the dough is evenly combined.
The dough has come together. Do I shape it now or chill it first?
Cover the dough and refrigerate it for 1 hour. Chilling will firm it up before you move on to shaping or baking.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Use only the tenderest lower herb pieces, mince them very small, and hold the upper green pieces apart so they don't get mixed in.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this Crawfish Chowder, I'm serving some of it like a cold salsa-style topping, and I've got lower cilantro or parsley pieces in the mix. What should I do with those just this time?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut only the softest lower herb pieces into tiny bits and keep the upper green pieces separate.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Crawfish Chowder as a raw salad, salsa, or uncooked topping with lower cilantro or parsley pieces. How should I handle them?

messages.content: For this Crawfish Chowder, I'm serving some of it like a cold salsa-style topping, and I've got lower cilantro or parsley pieces in the mix. What should I do with those just this time?
Use only the tenderest lower herb pieces, mince them very small, and hold the upper green pieces apart so they don't get mixed in.
Perfect, that's the special version I'm making tonight. For the chowder part, what should I pull out first?
Set a large skillet on the stove, then get 1/4 cup butter and 1/2 bunch green onions, chopped, ready beside it.
Skillet is out, and the chopped green onions are next to the 1/4 cup butter. Anything else before heat goes on?
Yes—keep the remaining 1/2 cup butter nearby, plus 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned. Those come in after the green onions are handled.
The crawfish is cleaned and waiting. What heat should I use for the skillet?
Put the skillet over medium heat and melt the 1/4 cup butter in it, letting it coat the bottom of the pan.
The butter is melted and foamy, but not browned. Do the onions go in now?
Add the chopped green onions to that butter and sauté them until they're tender, stirring so they soften evenly.
They've softened and smell sweet. Should I leave them in the skillet with the butter?
Scoop the green onions out of the pan and set them aside for now.
Onions are in a small bowl. The skillet still has a little buttery sheen—do I wipe it out?
No need to wipe it. Use the same skillet and melt the 1/2 cup butter in it.
The 1/2 cup butter has melted. How long should the crawfish cook?
Add the 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned, and sauté them in the butter for 5 minutes, then set them aside.
I'm making Chai Butter Cookies today. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup chai tea mix, 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready for creaming everything together.
The butter is out, but it's still a little cool. Should I wait before adding the sugar and chai mix?
Yes, give it a little time if it's too firm. For creaming, the butter should be soft enough to press easily, so it can blend smoothly with the 1 1/3 cups sugar and the chai tea mix.
Okay, the butter is softer now and I have the large bowl ready. What goes in together?
Add the butter, the 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and the 1 cup chai tea mix to the bowl. Cream them together until the mixture looks lighter and fluffier.
It's paler and fluffy around the edges. Do the eggs go in all at once?
Add the 2 eggs one at a time. Beat well after the first egg is mixed in, then add the second and mix again until everything is smooth.
Both eggs are mixed in. The batter looks creamy—what dry ingredients come next?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt. Once they're evenly mixed, blend that dry mixture into the creamed mixture.
Should I mix until it's completely smooth, or stop earlier?
Mix only until all of the dry ingredients have been absorbed. Once you don't see dry streaks of flour mixture, stop so the dough doesn't get overworked.
The dough has no dry patches now. What should I do with it before baking later?
Cover the dough and refrigerate it for 1 hour. That rest will firm it up and make it easier to handle when you're ready for the next stage.
I'm making Chocolate Madeleines and want to get organized before I start. What should I measure out?

Set out the dry ingredients first: 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt. You'll also need butter, vanilla, and sugar for creaming later, though the recipe doesn't give amounts for those.
The flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt are measured. Should I heat the oven before mixing?
Yes—heat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's ready when the batter is prepared.
Oven is set. I have a Madeleine pan out; does it need anything before batter goes in?
Butter one Madeleine pan well, getting into each shell-shaped cavity so the madeleines release cleanly.
The pan is buttered. For the dry bowl, do I just whisk everything together?
Use a sifter if you have one: sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together. That helps break up cocoa lumps and keeps the batter lighter.
I sifted them and the mixture looks even. What should happen with the butter?
Cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until the mixture looks smooth and lighter in texture. Keep scraping the bowl so everything blends evenly.
It's getting creamy, but there are a few streaks on the side of the bowl. Should I keep going?
Pause to scrape down the sides, then cream a little longer until the butter, vanilla, and sugar look uniform. You don't need to rush this part.
That looks consistent now. Is there anything else from the recipe before I combine more ingredients?
You've covered the listed prep: oven at 375 degrees F / 190 degrees C, one buttered Madeleine pan, the dry ingredients sifted together, and the butter creamed with vanilla and sugar.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Keep the crunchy topping in its own small packet or cup, then sprinkle it on after you open the container to eat.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For these Apple Blueberry Tarts, I'm packing them in containers and adding a crunchy topping like seeds, nuts, crumbs, chips, or crisp just for this batch. What's the best way to keep that topping from going soft?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Pack the crunchy topping separately and add it after opening the container.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Apple Blueberry Tarts as a packed container with seeds, nuts, crumbs, chips, or a crisp topping. How should I handle the crunchy topping?

messages.content: For these Apple Blueberry Tarts, I'm packing them in containers and adding a crunchy topping like seeds, nuts, crumbs, chips, or crisp just for this batch. What's the best way to keep that topping from going soft?
Keep the crunchy topping in its own small packet or cup, then sprinkle it on after you open the container to eat.
Perfect, that's exactly what I want for this batch. I've got containers ready—what should I prep first?
Start with the fruit: peel, core, and chop 2 medium cooking apples, and measure 2/3 cup fresh or frozen blueberries.
The apples are chopped, and the blueberries are measured. Should I season the fruit before I deal with the dough?
Yes. In a medium bowl, combine the apples, blueberries, 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute, and 1/4 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice. Set that bowl aside.
The fruit mixture is sitting aside. I still have the spice jar out—how much do I need for the flour bowl?
Use another medium bowl for the dry mixture. Stir together the whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice.
Dry bowl is mixed. Just to check, the total spice for the recipe is the 1/2 teaspoon amount, split between the filling and the flour mixture, right?
Right—keep the measured spice portions separate as you add them: 1/4 teaspoon goes with the fruit, and 1/8 teaspoon goes into the flour mixture.
Got it. My counter is getting crowded with the fruit bowl, flour bowl, oil, and milk. Which bowl gets the liquids?
Pour the oil and milk into the flour mixture all at once.
They're in the flour bowl. Should I beat it smooth or keep it gentle?
Keep it gentle: stir lightly with a fork just until the dough comes together.
The dough is coming together without looking overworked. For packing, when do I use the crunchy topping we talked about?
Leave the topping out of the tart container while it's packed. Put the tart in its container, keep the crunchy topping separate, and add it right before serving so it stays crisp.
I'm making Date Nut Bars and want to get organized before I mix. What should I measure out first?
Set out a large bowl and measure 2 cups sugar and 2 cups all-purpose flour into your prep area. You'll also need baking powder, salt, dates, nuts, eggs, butter, and vanilla for the batter.
The sugar and flour are ready. How much leavening and salt go with them?
Measure 2 teaspoons baking powder and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Those go with the sugar and flour in the dry mixture.
Should I combine the dates and nuts with the dry ingredients, or wait until later?
Add the dates and nuts to the large bowl with the sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt, then stir so everything is evenly distributed.
That bowl looks well mixed. I'm about to add the wet ingredients—what texture am I aiming for?
Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla, then stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened. Don't worry if it feels hard to stir; the batter is supposed to be very stiff.
It's thick and sticky, with no dry flour showing. What pan should I use?
Grease a 15-in pan, then spread the stiff batter into it as evenly as you can. A spatula or lightly buttered hands can help press it into the corners.
The batter is in the pan. What oven setting and timing should I use?
Bake it at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes. Start checking near 20 minutes, and look for the top to be golden brown.
If the edges brown before the middle looks done, should I leave it for the full time?

Use the visual cue over the clock: the bars should be golden brown. If they're browning fast, check carefully around the 20-minute mark, but don't exceed what they need just to reach that golden finish.
I'm making Dads Kickin Jamaican Wings Mon today. Can you help me get the marinade started and keep me on track?

Absolutely. Set out 3 tablespoons Jamaican jerk seasoning blend, 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, 3 cloves diced garlic, and a 1 inch piece of peeled fresh ginger, diced. You'll also want your blender ready.
The jerk seasoning and oil are measured, and I've got the garlic peeled. Does the ginger need to be really fine before blending?
Dicing the ginger is enough since it's going into the blender. Once the garlic and ginger are diced, add them with the jerk seasoning and oil.
I see green onions and jalapeno slices mentioned in the directions too. Do those go into the blender with everything else?
Yes. Put the jerk seasoning, vegetable oil, diced garlic, diced ginger, green onions, and jalapeno slices into the blender together.
Everything is loaded in the blender. What consistency am I looking for?
Blend until the mixture is thick and smooth, with the garlic, ginger, green onions, and jalapeno fully worked into the seasoning and oil.
The sauce looks smooth and pretty thick now. Should I pour it over the wings or coat them another way?
Dunk the wings directly in the mixture so they get well coated, then arrange them in a single layer on baking sheets.
They're coated and spread out on the baking sheets. Do I cover them before they go in the fridge?
Cover the baking sheets with aluminum foil, then refrigerate the wings for 8 hours, or leave them overnight.
They've marinated overnight. What oven setting should I use before baking?
bring the oven up to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C), while the wings stay arranged in their single layer on the baking sheets.
I'm making Butterscotch Basketball Cookies and want to keep the mixing in the right order. Can you walk me through the start?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup butter, softened. Use real butter here, no substitutes, so the dough creams properly.
The chips are measured and the butter is soft. Which sugars should I have ready?
Measure 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them near your mixing bowl with the softened butter.
I've got both sugars packed and measured. Do I melt the chips before I cream the butter?
Yes. Melt the 1 cup butterscotch chips in the microwave, stirring as needed until smooth, then let them cool for 10 minutes before they go into the dough.
On Butterscotch Basketball Cookies, they're melted and cooling. While I wait, can I start the butter mixture?
Go ahead. In your mixing bowl, cream the softened butter with the sugar and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks blended and lighter.
The butter and sugars look creamy now. What ingredients go in before the melted chips?
For Butterscotch Basketball Cookies, add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so everything is evenly combined.
The egg, milk, and vanilla are mixed in. The butterscotch has cooled for 10 minutes—should it go in all at once?
Yes, pour in the melted butterscotch chips and beat them into the mixture until the dough looks even throughout.
It looks evenly colored and smells very butterscotch. Anything I should check before moving on?
Check that there are no streaks of plain butter mixture or unmixed melted chips. Once it looks smooth and uniform, you're done with this part of the recipe.
I'm making Apple Blueberry Tarts today. Can you help me get organized before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 2 medium cooking apples, peeled, cored, and chopped, plus 2/3 cup fresh or frozen blueberries. You'll also want a medium bowl ready for the fruit mixture.
The apples are chopped and the blueberries are measured. What seasonings or sweetener should I put beside them?
Put out 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute and 1/2 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice. The spice gets divided during prep, so keep the measuring spoons handy.
I have both bowls out. How much spice goes into the fruit?
In one medium bowl, combine the chopped apples, blueberries, sugar substitute, and 1/4 teaspoon of the apple pie spice. Stir gently so the berries stay mostly intact, then set that bowl aside.
The fruit is mixed and sitting to the side. What goes in the second bowl?
Use the other medium bowl for the dry mixture: stir together the whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, and the remaining 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice until the spice is evenly distributed.
The dry ingredients look evenly mixed. Should I add the liquids slowly or all at once?
Add the oil and milk all at once to the flour mixture. Pour them in together rather than drizzling, so the dough can come together with minimal stirring.
They're in the bowl now. What should the mixing motion be like?
Use a fork and stir lightly, lifting and turning the mixture just until the dough comes together. Stop as soon as it holds; overmixing can make the tart dough less tender.
It's clumping into a soft dough with a few dry-looking bits. Is that okay?

Yes, that sounds right for this stage. Give it only a few more gentle fork strokes if needed, just enough to gather those dry bits into the dough, while keeping the fruit mixture set aside for assembly.
I'm making Chocolate Madeleines and want to get the small dry ingredients measured accurately. What should I set out?
Set out 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt. Keep a sifter or fine-mesh sieve nearby so the dry mixture ends up smooth.
The flour and cocoa are measured. Should I combine the baking powder and salt with them right away?
Yes, you can add the 1/2 teaspoon baking powder and the pinch of salt to the flour and cocoa, but wait to sift everything together until the pan and oven are handled.
I'm using one Madeleine pan. Does the oven need to be on before I butter it?
Go ahead and heat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it is ready by the time the batter is prepared.
The oven is heating. How thoroughly should I coat the Madeleine pan?
Butter the one Madeleine pan well, getting into each shell-shaped indentation so the cakes release cleanly after baking.
The pan is buttered, and the dry ingredients are still sitting in separate piles in the sieve.
Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together now. If any cocoa lumps remain, press them gently through so the mixture looks even and fine.
The sifted mix looks uniform and dark. What should I work on for the wet part?
Cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until the mixture looks smooth and a bit lighter. Scrape the bowl as needed so the sugar and vanilla are evenly worked into the butter.
The butter mixture is creamy. Is there anything I should check before I keep going with the batter?
Check that the oven is still at 375 degrees F / 190 degrees C, the Madeleine pan is buttered, and the sifted dry ingredients are ready to add when your next mixing step calls for them.
I'm making Banana Bran Muffins today. Can you help me get oriented before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar for the creaming step, plus a large mixing bowl and something sturdy to beat them together.
The butter is soft and the brown sugar is measured. What else should be nearby?
Have 3 bananas mashed and ready, along with 1/4 cup milk. The recipe also has you add vanilla and eggs with the bananas and milk, so keep those close too.
Should I heat the oven before I start with the bowl?
Yes, turn the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it can heat while you prepare the batter.
I've set it to 375. What should I do with the muffin pan?
Grease the muffin pan well, or line the cups with paper muffin liners if you'd rather make cleanup easier.
The liners are in. I'm ready to use the butter and sugar.
Put the softened butter and brown sugar in the large mixing bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks fluffy and a bit lighter.
It's starting to look fluffy, but there are a few small sugar streaks. Is that okay?
That's fine. Give it a little more mixing until it looks mostly even, but you don't need it perfectly smooth before adding the wet ingredients.
Okay, the butter and sugar look even now. How do I add the banana mixture?
Add the mashed bananas, 1/4 cup milk, vanilla, and eggs to the bowl, then mix well until everything is combined into a consistent muffin batter.
I'm making Aunt Mamies today. Can you help me organize the ingredients before I start?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (8 ounce) package of softened cream cheese and 1/2 cup softened butter so they're ready to beat together.
The cream cheese and butter are softened. What else needs to be within reach?
Have 2 cups all-purpose flour and 1 cup white sugar nearby. You'll also need a bowl for mixing, something to cover the dough, and a saucepan for the sugar-and-milk step later.
I've got the bowl ready. Do I start by mixing the cream cheese with the butter?
Yes. Beat the softened cream cheese with the margarine until the mixture is well blended and smooth-looking.
It's coming together, but I still see a few streaks. Should I keep going?
Keep beating until the streaks disappear and the mixture looks evenly combined. It doesn't need to be fluffy, just well blended.
That looks even now. Do I add all the flour at once?
Add the 2 cups of all-purpose flour and mix well, scraping the bowl as needed so there aren't dry patches left behind.
The flour is mixed in and it's more like dough. What should I do with it?
Shape the dough into a ball, cover it, and chill it for 2 hours so it firms up.
The dough is covered and chilling. When I get to the stovetop part, what am I watching for?
Use a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the white sugar with milk, stirring occasionally, until the milk boils and the sugar is dissolved.
I'm making Deep South Fried Chicken today. Can you help me set up and cook it in order?

Absolutely. Put a large cast iron skillet on the stove, and set out 1 cup shortening, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon ground black pepper. You'll also need a brown paper lunch bag for coating the chicken pieces.
I've got the skillet and the shortening. Should the flour mixture be ready before I heat the pan?
You can measure it now so you're not rushing at the stove. Add the 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon ground black pepper to the brown paper lunch bag.
The flour, salt, and pepper are in the bag. Do I shake the bag now or wait?
Give the closed bag a quick shake just to combine the flour, salt, and pepper evenly. Then keep it nearby for coating the chicken.
Okay, the seasoned flour is mixed. What do I do with the skillet?
Add the 1 cup shortening to the large cast iron skillet and heat it over medium-high heat.
The shortening is melting in the pan. How should I start coating the chicken without making a mess?
Work with 2 chicken pieces at a time. Put those pieces in the brown paper lunch bag, close the top securely, and shake until they're coated with the flour mixture.
The first 2 pieces are coated. Do they go straight into the skillet?
Yes. Carefully place those coated chicken pieces into the skillet with the hot shortening, leaving room so they sit in the pan rather than crowding on top of each other.
I still have more chicken pieces waiting. Should I coat all of them before adding more?
Keep repeating the same pattern: shake 2 chicken pieces in the bag to coat them, then place them in the skillet. Continue until all of the chicken is coated and in the skillet.
I'm making Cindis Egg Rolls today and I've got a wok ready. Can you help me set up the filling ingredients?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 pound ground pork and 4 cups shredded cabbage. Those are the main parts of the filling.
Pork and cabbage are ready. What vegetables should I prep before the wok gets hot?
Shred 1 large carrot, then cut 1/2 green bell pepper into thin strips. You'll also want onion, garlic, and ginger ready for the cabbage mixture.
The carrot is shredded and the pepper is sliced. Should the pork go into the wok by itself?
Yes. Put the ground pork in the large wok over medium-high heat and cook it there before mixing it with the vegetables.
It's cooking now and giving off some liquid. What texture am I looking for before I take it out?
Cook it until the pork is no longer pink and has broken up well. Once it's cooked through, drain it so the filling doesn't turn watery.
The pork is drained. Should I keep it in the wok or move it somewhere else?
Set the drained pork aside for the moment. In a large bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger.
The vegetables are in the bowl. Do I stir them hard or just toss them together?
Toss them together until the ingredients are evenly mixed, without crushing the cabbage too much. You just want the vegetables distributed through the bowl.
Got it. What should I do for the sauce or binder before combining everything?
In a small bowl, stir together the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses until the mixture is smooth. That gives you a ready sauce to add to the filling.
I'm making Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart and want to start with the crust mixture. Can you walk me through the setup?

Absolutely. Put a mixing bowl, sifter or fine mesh sieve, fork, pastry cutter or two knives, plastic wrap, and your measuring tools within reach. For the dry ingredients, measure 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon light brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/8 teaspoon salt.
I've got the bowl and sifter ready. Do the flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt all go through the sifter?
Yes. Sift the flour, light brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt together into the bowl so they're evenly combined and any lumps are broken up.
The dry mix looks even, but the brown sugar left a couple of tiny bits in the sieve. Should I press them through?
If they're soft, press them through gently with a spoon. If any bits are hard, discard those so the crust mixture stays fine and even.
Okay, the dry ingredients are sifted. I have cold butter here—what texture am I aiming for when I add it?
Cut the butter into the sifted mixture until it looks like coarse crumbs. You can use a pastry cutter, two knives, or your fingertips, but keep the butter from getting warm or smeary.
It's crumbly now with some pea-sized pieces. Is that close enough before adding the water?
Yes, that's right. Sprinkle the ice water over the crumbs rather than pouring it all in one spot, then toss with a fork until the mixture is evenly moistened.
When I toss it with the fork, should it become a smooth dough or stay a little shaggy?
It should stay a bit shaggy but hold together when you press a small amount between your fingers. Stop mixing once it's evenly moistened so the crust doesn't get tough.
It's holding together now. How should I wrap it so it's ready for the tart?
Gather the dough gently, pat it into a round, and wrap it tightly in plastic. Keep the shape fairly even so it will be easier to roll later for the Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart.
I'd like to make Fig Bars II. Can you help me get organized before I start mixing?

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup white sugar, 3 eggs, 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking powder. You'll also want the seasonings and vanilla ready for the dry mix and blending step: salt, cloves, cinnamon, allspice, and vanilla.
I've got the sugar, eggs, flour, baking powder, spices, and vanilla out. What pan and oven setup do I need?
Heat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C. While it warms, get a 9x13 inch baking pan and grease it, then dust it with flour so the bars release cleanly.
The oven is heating, and the pan is greased and floured. Should I start with the eggs or the flour mixture?
In this Fig Bars II step, start with the eggs and sugar. In a large bowl, beat the 3 eggs with the 1 cup white sugar until the mixture looks thick and pale.
How pale are we talking? Mine is lighter yellow and a little fuller than when I started.
That sounds right. You're looking for it to thicken slightly and lose the deep egg-yellow color, so a lighter, fuller mixture is the goal.
Okay, the egg mixture looks thick enough. What should I do with the dry ingredients?
Sift together the 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice. Sifting helps distribute the baking powder and spices evenly.
The dry ingredients are sifted. Do I stir them in all at once?
Add the sifted dry mixture into the beaten eggs and sugar, then blend it in gently. Add the vanilla along with it, mixing just until everything is combined.
The batter is combined with the vanilla. Should I worry if a few tiny flour streaks are still visible?
Give it a few more gentle folds until the flour streaks disappear, but don't overwork it. Once it's evenly mixed, spread the batter into your prepared 9x13 inch pan for baking.
Can you help me cook Baked Fish and Rice 2? I'm setting out the baking dish and want to make sure I start with the right amounts.
Absolutely. Grease an 11-in. baking dish, and have 1 1/2 cups boiling chicken broth and 1/2 cup uncooked long grain rice ready to go into it.
The dish is greased, and the broth is boiling. Do the seasonings go in with the rice right away?
Yes. Add the rice to the dish with the boiling chicken broth, then stir in 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder.
Everything is mixed in the dish. Should it be covered tightly before baking?
In this Baked Fish and Rice 2 step, cover the baking dish, then bake it at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, for 10 minutes.
While that's in the oven, should I prep the broccoli and toppings?
That's a good time to get the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, onions, fish fillets, and paprika ready, since they'll go on after the rice has had its initial bake.
The 10 minutes are up. The rice has absorbed some broth but still looks moist.
That's fine for this stage. Uncover it and add the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, and half of the onions over the rice mixture.
I added those. Should I stir them in or leave them layered?
Gently distribute them so they're added into the rice mixture, then place the fish fillets on top.
The fish is on top. What's the last thing before it goes back in?
Sprinkle the fish fillets with paprika. The recipe's listed steps end there, so from here you'd continue baking until the fish is cooked through according to its thickness and safe doneness.
I'm ready to cook Garlic Butter. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a bowl out, but I want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Let the butter soften if it hasn't already, then measure out 1 cup butter, 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 tablespoon garlic salt.
The butter is soft enough to press with a spoon. Should I melt it or keep it like this?
Keep it softened, not melted. That way it will mix into a spreadable garlic butter instead of turning oily.
Okay, I added the butter to the small bowl. Does the garlic go in before the cheese?
Yes. Add the minced garlic to the softened butter, then add the grated Parmesan cheese right after it.
It's in the bowl. Should I stir until it's totally smooth?
Stir until the garlic and Parmesan are evenly distributed through the butter. It may still look a little textured from the cheese, and that's fine.
I have the garlic salt ready. The recipe also mentions Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika—do those go in now too?
Yes, season the mixture with the garlic salt, Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika. Mix again so the seasonings are spread evenly throughout.
The color looks speckled now, and it smells strong. Should I taste it?
You can taste a tiny bit if you'd like, especially to check the saltiness. Since there's garlic salt and Parmesan, it should be savory, so avoid adding extra salt unless it really needs it.
For Garlic Butter, what's the best way to serve or store it once it's mixed?
Use it right away as a spread for bread, vegetables, or cooked foods, or scrape it into a small container and chill it until firm. Let it soften slightly before spreading if it has been refrigerated.
I want to make Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes. Can you guide me while I get everything set up?
Absolutely. Have your Fast Chicken Soup Base ready, plus 1 (9 ounce) package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, 1 (14.5 ounce) can of diced tomatoes, and 2 medium zucchini diced.
The soup base is made already, and I found the tortellini. Should I drain the canned tomatoes or use the whole can?
Use the diced tomatoes with their juices unless your soup base is already much thinner than you want. The tomato liquid helps flavor the broth.
Got it. I'm dicing the zucchini now—how small should the pieces be so they cook with the tortellini?
Cut the 2 medium zucchini into small, bite-size dice. That way they'll become tender during the same simmer as the tortellini.
Everything is prepped. What should be happening in the pot before I add the vegetables and pasta?
Put the prepared Fast Chicken Soup Base in the pot and bring it to a gentle simmer. You want steady small bubbles, not a hard boil.
It's simmering lightly. I have the tortellini, tomatoes, zucchini, and basil next to the stove.

Add the 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, the diced zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil. Stir gently so the tortellini don't stick together.
Once those are in, should I keep the heat the same or turn it down?
Keep it at a simmer and adjust the heat as needed so it stays gently bubbling. Let the soup cook for 10-20 minutes, until the tortellini and zucchini are tender.
How do I know when the texture is right before serving?

The tortellini should be tender all the way through, and the zucchini should be soft but not falling apart. Once that happens within the 10-20 minute simmer window, give the soup a final stir and serve it hot.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: Corned Beef Hash is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got a big skillet out but haven't started chopping yet.
Absolutely. Peel and dice 6 large potatoes, chop 1 medium onion, and cut 1 (12 ounce) can of corned beef into chunks. Keep 1 cup beef broth nearby too.
The potatoes are diced, but they're pretty uneven. Is that okay for this dish?
A little uneven is fine, but try to keep the pieces close enough in size that they soften together. Since they'll simmer until they're mashable, smaller chunks will cook more evenly.
Onion is chopped and the corned beef is in chunks. Should the skillet be hot before everything goes in?
Set the large deep skillet over medium heat, then add the potatoes, corned beef, chopped onion, and the 1 cup beef broth. Stir just enough to spread everything out in the pan.
Everything is in the skillet now. The broth doesn't cover the potatoes completely—is that a problem?
That's okay. The recipe uses the broth to simmer and soften the potatoes, not fully submerge them. Cover the skillet so the steam helps cook the top pieces too.
It's covered and simmering. What texture am I watching for so I don't stop too early?

Let it simmer until the potatoes are soft enough to mash easily with a spoon or fork, and the liquid is almost gone. If there's still a lot of broth, keep it covered a bit longer, then uncover briefly if needed to reduce.
The potatoes are soft now, and there's only a little liquid left around the edges.
Great. Mix everything well in the skillet so the softened potatoes, corned beef, and onion come together into a hash. The remaining moisture should help bind it without making it soupy.
It's mixed and looks hearty. Should I plate it right away or let it sit?
You can serve it right away once it's mixed well. Spoon the Corned Beef Hash onto plates while it's hot, scraping up any flavorful bits from the skillet.
I'm starting A 1 Chicken Soup; can you walk me through the setup? I've got a large pot out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 2 skinless chicken leg quarters, 1/2 cup chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need the chicken bouillon called for when the liquid goes in.
The oil, chicken, onion, and water are ready. Should the pot be heating before I add the chicken?
Yes. Put the large pot over medium heat, add the vegetable oil, and let it warm briefly. Add the chicken leg quarters and cook them until they're browned on both sides.
They're browning now. Do I need them cooked through at this point or just colored on the outside?
Just browned on the outside for now. The chicken will finish cooking during the simmer, so focus on getting color on both sides without rushing the heat higher.
Both sides have some good color. I have the chopped onion measured at 1/2 cup—does it go in with the chicken still in the pot?
Yes, leave the chicken in the pot. Stir in the chopped onion and cook it with the chicken for 2 minutes, stirring so the onion softens a bit and picks up the flavor in the pot.
The onion has cooked for 2 minutes and smells good. I'm ready to add the liquid.
Pour in the 2 quarts water, then add the chicken bouillon. Stir the bottom of the pot gently to loosen any browned bits, and bring everything up to a boil.
It's starting to boil. Should I keep it boiling hard or turn it down right away?
Once it reaches a boil, reduce the heat so the soup settles into a steady simmer. Let it simmer for 45 minutes.
During the 45 minutes, should the lid be on, and what should I look for before serving?

Keep it at a gentle simmer and use the lid as needed to control evaporation. By the end, the chicken should be fully cooked and tender, and the broth should have taken on flavor from the browned chicken, onion, water, and bouillon.
I'm making Gingery Fish Kabobs and want to start with the sauce or marinade. Can you guide me while I cook?
Absolutely. Set a small saucepan on the counter and gather 2 cups pineapple juice, 1 tablespoon cornstarch, 2 tablespoons light soy sauce that is 50% less sodium, and 1 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar.
I've got the pineapple juice and cornstarch out. Should the pan be on heat yet?
Not yet. Pour the pineapple juice into the small saucepan while it's still off the heat, then whisk in the cornstarch until it dissolves and you don't see dry clumps.
The cornstarch is mostly dissolved, but a little is sticking at the edge of the pan.
Scrape around the edge with your whisk or spoon and stir until the mixture looks smooth. It's worth getting it fully mixed before heating so the sauce thickens evenly.
Okay, it looks smooth now. I have the soy sauce and white vinegar measured.
Add the 2 tablespoons light soy sauce and the 1 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar to the pan. Stir them into the pineapple-cornstarch mixture.
Those are in. The recipe also mentions garlic and ginger—do they go in now?
Yes, add the garlic and ginger now, then stir everything together so the flavor is evenly distributed before you start simmering.
It's mixed. What heat should I use, and what am I looking for?
Bring it to a gentle simmer, stirring often. Let it simmer until it's slightly thickened, about 7 minutes; it should look a bit glossier and lightly coat the spoon.
It thickened after about 7 minutes. Do I use it right away on the kabobs?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the sauce cool before using it with the Gingery Fish Kabobs.
Help me stay organized for Crab Quiche. What comes first? I'm starting with a frozen crust and want to keep the timing straight.
For Crab Quiche, set out 1 (9 inch) deep dish frozen pie crust, 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need pepper and hot sauce for the egg mixture.
I've got the crust on a baking sheet and the eggs, cream, and salt measured. Should I heat the oven now?
Yes, bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready before the crust goes in.
The oven is heating. Do I need to thaw the frozen pie crust first?
Use the deep dish frozen pie crust as directed here and bake it once the oven reaches temperature. It's going in briefly before the filling, just to get a little color.
The oven just hit 350. How long should the crust bake, and what should I look for?
Bake the pie crust for about 10 minutes, until it is just starting to brown. Keep an eye on the edges so they don't get too dark.
It has a light golden edge after 10 minutes. Should I fill it right away?
Take the crust out of the oven and allow it to cool before adding the egg mixture.
While it cools, what bowl and mixing method should I use for the filling?
Use a large bowl. Whisk together the 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon salt, pepper, and hot sauce until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
The filling is whisked and the crust is cooling on the counter. Anything I should clean up or keep ready before I pour?
Keep the whisked filling nearby and leave the crust on the baking sheet for easier handling. Wipe up any spills around the bowl, then you'll be ready for the next stage once the crust has cooled.
I'm making Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I. Can you guide me while I get the mixing bowls out?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl for the creamed ingredients and another bowl for the dry ingredients later. For the base, you'll need 1 cup shortening and 1 cup packed brown sugar.
Shortening and brown sugar are in the large bowl. Should the white sugar go in there too?
Yes, add 1/2 cup white sugar to that same bowl, then have 2 eggs ready to go in with it.
The eggs are on the counter. Before I crack them, should I start the oven?
Go ahead and set the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's hot by the time the dough is mixed.
Oven is heating. I cracked in the eggs; what texture am I looking for when I mix this?
Cream the shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla thoroughly. Keep mixing until the mixture looks well combined and smoother, with no obvious streaks of shortening or egg.
It's looking creamy now. I have another bowl ready—what goes in that one?
Use the separate bowl for the dry ingredients, and mix them together there. Leave out the candy-coated milk chocolate pieces for this part; they don't go into the dry mix yet.
Dry ingredients are combined, and I kept the candies aside. Do I dump everything in at once?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix well, just until the dough comes together evenly.
The dough looks even now. Should I clean the second bowl or keep it nearby for anything else?

You can set the dry-ingredient bowl aside for cleanup now. The recipe's mixing sequence is complete: oven preheated, wet base creamed, dry ingredients mixed separately without the candies, then added to the creamed mixture and mixed well.

source_seed.recipe_title: Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I

messages.content: I want to make Festive Shortbread Logs. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl and a spoon or hand mixer. You'll need 1 cup butter, softened, and 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar to start.
The butter is soft and I measured the sugar. Should the bowl be big enough for all the flour too?
Yes, use a bowl with room to mix everything without spilling, because you'll eventually add 2 cups all-purpose flour.
Got it. I also have vanilla out—how much goes in?
You'll use 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Keep it nearby, but begin by creaming the softened butter with the confectioners' sugar until the mixture looks smooth and blended.
I'm using a hand mixer. The butter and sugar look pale and creamy now.
Great texture. Pour in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and mix just until it's evenly worked through the butter mixture.
The vanilla is mixed in. When I add the flour, should I dump it all in?
Add the 2 cups all-purpose flour gradually instead. Mix as you go so the dough comes together evenly and you don't get a flour cloud.
It's getting thicker and a little crumbly around the edges of the bowl.
That's normal for shortbread. Keep mixing until there are no dry streaks and the dough holds together when pressed.
The dough holds together now. How do I shape the cookies without it sticking everywhere?
Dust your hands lightly with flour, then scoop tablespoonfuls of batter and shape them into cookies. Set them on your prepared surface or baking sheet as you go.
I want to make Biga today. Can you guide me through it without rushing?
Absolutely. For this Biga, set out 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast, 1/2 cup warm water, 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour, and 1 1/4 cups cold water.
I've got the yeast and both waters. Should the warm water go into a mixing bowl or something smaller?
Use a small bowl for the warm water. Pour in the 1/2 cup warm water, then sprinkle the 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast over the surface so it can hydrate evenly.
The yeast is sprinkled over the water. Do I stir it, or just leave it alone?

Leave it standing until the yeast dissolves and gets foamy, about 15 minutes. If a few dry spots remain at the very top after a minute or two, you can gently nudge them into the water, but don't worry about vigorous stirring.
While that sits, should I get the flour ready in the larger bowl?
Yes. Measure 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour into a large bowl. Give yourself enough room in the bowl because you'll be adding the yeast mixture and 1 1/4 cups cold water next.
The flour is in the big bowl. The yeast bowl is starting to look foamy now.
Great—that foam is what you want before combining. Make a well in the center of the flour, like a little crater, so the liquids can sit in the middle instead of running straight up the sides.
I made the well. Do I pour in the yeast mixture first or the cold water first?
Pour the yeast mixture into the well, then add the 1 1/4 cups cold water right into the same center area. Keep the bowl steady so the liquid stays mostly in the well.
Everything is in the bowl now. Anything else I should check before moving on?

At this point, you've completed the listed prep for the Biga: the yeast bloomed in 1/2 cup warm water for about 15 minutes, the 3 1/2 cups flour are in the large bowl, and the yeast mixture plus 1 1/4 cups cold water have been poured into the well.
Can you help me prep Fried Chicken Tenders? I've got chicken out but want to set up the coating station correctly.
Absolutely. Set out three shallow bowls if you have them. In one bowl, add 1 cup all-purpose flour. In another, measure 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs.
The flour and breadcrumbs are in separate bowls. Do the seasonings go into the flour or the crumbs?

Mix the seasonings into the breadcrumbs: add 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper to the bowl with the Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs, then stir so the spices are evenly distributed.
Got it mixed. I only have a small bowl left for the wet part—is that fine?
Yes, a small bowl is exactly right for the wet mixture. Put the eggs and water in that bowl and whisk them together until the eggs are loosened and blended with the water.
The egg mixture is ready. Should I coat all the chicken at once or work piece by piece?
Work one piece at a time so the coating stays even. Dip a piece of chicken into the flour first, turning it so all sides get a light coating.
After the flour, do I shake off the extra or leave it thick?
Shake off any loose excess flour. You want enough flour to help the egg cling, but not so much that it clumps before the breadcrumb layer.
Okay, the first piece is floured. What's the order from here?
Move that piece into the eggs and water mixture, coat it fully, then let any excess drip back into the bowl. After that, press it into the seasoned bread crumbs so the crumbs cover the chicken well.
I've got a breaded piece now. Where should I put it while I do the rest?
Set the coated chicken aside on a plate or tray, then repeat the same order with each remaining piece: flour, eggs and water, then the seasoned bread crumbs.
I'm ready to cook Chicken Vegetable Stew. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a large pot out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into bite-size pieces. You'll also want 1 chopped onion ready to go.
The chicken is cut up and the onion is chopped. What vegetables should I pull out before I turn on the stove?
Grab 1/2 pound baby carrots and 4 potatoes. If the potatoes are large, cut them into stew-friendly chunks so they cook evenly with the chicken.
Potatoes are chunked and the baby carrots are ready. Do I add anything to the pot yet, or season first?
Put the chopped onion, chicken breast pieces, baby carrots, and potatoes into the large pot together. Once they're in, sprinkle in the salt and turmeric.
Everything is in the pot with the salt and turmeric. I have tomato paste too—how should that go in?
Dissolve the tomato paste in water before adding it, so it blends into the stew instead of staying in clumps. Pour that mixture into the pot over the chicken and vegetables.
That helped—the liquid looks more even now. Should I stir it a lot or leave it alone?
Give it a steady stir to coat the chicken, carrots, potatoes, and onion with the tomato mixture and seasonings. After that, you can let the pot settle so everything cooks together evenly.
I'm checking the smell now. It's good but mild. Is there anything optional I can add without changing the basic stew?
Yes. If you'd like, add garlic powder and ground black pepper to season. Keep it to taste, since those are optional seasonings for this stew.
Garlic powder and black pepper are in. Before serving, what should I look for in the pot?

Look for chicken pieces that are cooked through and potatoes and carrots that are tender when pierced. Stir once more so the onion, tomato-seasoned broth, chicken, and vegetables are evenly distributed before you serve the stew.
I want to make Aaahh Potato Soup, but I'd like you to guide me while I set everything up.

Absolutely. Put a large saucepan or pot on your counter, and get your ingredients together: 2 cubed Yukon Gold potatoes, 1 (5.5 ounce) package au gratin instant potato mix, 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed chicken broth, and 1 1/2 cups water.
The potatoes are cubed, and I found the au gratin mix. Should the pot be on the heat already?
Not yet. Add the cubed potatoes, the au gratin potato mix, the condensed chicken broth, and the 1 1/2 cups water to the pot while it's still easy to stir.
It looks a little thick in the pot, and the liquid doesn't quite cover the potatoes.
Add just enough more water to cover the potatoes if necessary. Stir so the dry mix is moistened and there aren't big pockets of seasoning stuck to the bottom.
Okay, the potatoes are covered now. What heat should I use?
Set the pot over medium heat. Let it cook there, stirring occasionally so the potato mix doesn't settle and scorch.
How long am I aiming for, and what should the potatoes feel like?
Plan on about 40 minutes. The soup is ready for the next step when the potato cubes are tender enough to pierce easily with a fork.
It's been simmering and the potatoes are soft. The soup looks creamy already from the mix.
Good. Keep the heat gentle, then stir in the cream and let it heat through. You don't need to boil it hard after adding the cream.
Once the cream is warm, can I serve it right away?
Yes. Give it a final stir, check that it's heated through, then ladle the Aaahh Potato Soup into bowls while it's hot.
I'm about to start Black Forest Dump Cake II. Can you talk me through the prep? I'm setting everything out on the counter now.
Absolutely. For the fruit layer, have ready 1 (21 ounce) can cherry pie filling and 1 (16.5 ounce) can pitted dark sweet cherries.
I've got both cans. Should I drain the dark sweet cherries or keep the liquid?
Keep the juice with the dark sweet cherries. The recipe uses the cherries including their juice when they go into the baking dish.
Good to know. What are the other ingredients before I open anything?
You'll also need 1 (18.25 ounce) package chocolate cake mix and 1 cup chopped walnuts.
Those are ready too. I have a glass 9x13 dish—what should I do with the oven?
The oven should be at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) before Black Forest Dump Cake II goes in.
The oven is heating. Do I need to grease the dish heavily?
Just spray the 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray so the cake doesn't stick.
The dish is sprayed. Which cherry can goes in first?
Pour the cherry pie filling into the dish first, then spread it out evenly across the bottom.
The pie filling is spread evenly. What should I do with the other cherries?
Add the pitted dark sweet cherries on top, including the juice, and spread them evenly over the cherry pie filling.
I'd like to make Empanadas, but I noticed the dough needs chilling. Can you guide me through what I should do today?
Absolutely. For the dough, set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1 (3 ounce) package cream cheese so they're easy to blend together.
They're both softened. Should I measure the dry ingredients and filling now too?
Yes. You'll need 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour for the dough and 1 cup fruit preserves for the filling later.
I have the flour sifted and the preserves set aside. What bowl and mixing texture am I aiming for?
Use a medium mixing bowl. Cream the softened butter and cream cheese together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended, with no obvious streaks of either one.
It's smooth now. Do I add all the flour at once or gradually?
Beat in the flour until it's fully incorporated. Stop once the dough comes together; you don't need to overwork it.
The dough is soft and a little sticky. Is that okay before chilling?
In this Empanadas step, that's fine. Shape it into a smooth ball, then wrap it tightly in foil or cling wrap so it doesn't dry out in the refrigerator.
How long should I refrigerate it if I'm not baking until tomorrow?
Refrigerate it overnight. If your plans change, the wrapped dough can stay chilled for up to a week.
When I'm ready to bake, do I use it straight from the fridge?
Take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it so it has time to soften enough to roll and handle.
Before I get moving on Chicken Fried Chops 2, what should I have ready? I've got pork chops out and want to set up the coating before I heat the skillet.
Absolutely. For the dredge, put a shallow bowl on the counter and add 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground mustard, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder.
I found the flour and salt, but I'm measuring the mustard and garlic powder now. Should these just be stirred together dry?
Yes, stir the dry ingredients together until the mustard and garlic powder are evenly mixed through the flour and salt. That gives the chops an even coating.
The bowl is mixed. Do I pat the pork chops dry before dredging them?
That's a good idea. Pat the pork chops dry, then press each chop into the flour mixture so both sides are coated. Shake off any loose excess before they go to the skillet.
I've got the coated chops on a plate. How much should I worry about fully cooking them in the skillet?
Use the skillet just to brown them on both sides in oil. You're looking for color on the outside, not necessarily cooking them all the way through at this point.
The oil is hot and I'm browning the 1st side now. Should I crowd the pan if they don't all fit?
Don't crowd them. Brown the chops in batches if needed so each one gets good contact with the skillet and develops a nice crust on both sides.
They're browned now. I have my slow cooker ready—do they go straight in?
Yes, transfer the browned pork chops into the slow cooker, arranging them so they sit fairly evenly in the insert.
What do I pour over them? I see the recipe mentions soup and water, but I don't want to miss the order.
Combine the soup and water together first, then pour that mixture over the chops in the slow cooker. After that, you're set up for the slow-cooker portion of the recipe.
I'm getting ready for Citrus Infused Guacamole. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got the avocados on the counter but haven't started yet.
Absolutely. You'll need 2 avocados, peeled, pitted, and mashed, plus 1/2 tablespoon lime juice, 1/2 tablespoon orange juice, and 1/2 tablespoon pineapple juice.
I have the three juices measured out. Should I use a mixing bowl or something smaller?
Use a large bowl so the mashed avocado has room to mix evenly with the juices and seasonings.
The avocados are peeled and pitted now. Do I mash them completely smooth?
Mash them to the texture you like. A mostly smooth base with a few small chunks works well for guacamole.
Okay, the mashed avocado is in the bowl. What goes in with it?
Stir in the lime juice, orange juice, pineapple juice, cumin, cilantro, and salt until everything is evenly combined.
It smells bright from the citrus. Is the hot pepper sauce required?
No, it's optional. If you're using it, mix in the hot pepper sauce now and taste as you go.
I added a little hot pepper sauce. What should I do with the avocado pits?
Place one of the avocado pits into the bowl; it can help keep the guacamole fresh for a bit.
We're eating soon, but I might need to hold it while I set out chips. What's the best way to serve it?
Serve it immediately if you're ready. If not, refrigerate the guacamole until serving, keeping the pit in the bowl while it waits.

messages.content: I'm making Crab Quiche and the frozen crust is still wrapped on the counter. Can you guide me from setup through the mixing?

Hold back a small splash of the 1 cup heavy cream, then whisk it in at the end only if the egg mixture needs loosening. Go ahead and heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and keep the 1 (9 inch) deep dish frozen pie crust nearby.
Oven is heating. Should I unwrap the crust now or wait?
Unwrap it now and place the frozen pie crust on a baking sheet so it is easier to move in and out of the oven.
The crust is on the baking sheet. What ingredients should I measure while the oven comes up?
Measure 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Also have the pepper and hot sauce ready for the whisked filling.
I like holding back that bit of cream; that works better for this texture. The oven just beeped—does the crust go in plain?
Yes, bake the crust by itself first. Put it in the 350 degrees F oven for about 10 minutes, just until it is starting to brown.
It has been about 10 minutes and the edge is only lightly colored. Is that enough?
That is right for this stage. Pull it from the oven and let the pie crust cool before you add the filling.
The crust is cooling on the rack. Should I crack the eggs into the big bowl now?
Yes. Crack the 4 eggs into a large bowl, then whisk them until the yolks and whites are fully combined.
The eggs are blended. How do I add the cream without making it too loose?
Pour in most of the heavy cream, keeping that small splash aside. Whisk in the 1/2 teaspoon salt, then add pepper and hot sauce to the bowl.
The mixture looks smooth but a little thick after the salt, pepper, and hot sauce. Should I use the reserved cream now?
Yes, whisk in the reserved splash of cream now, just enough to loosen the egg mixture. Once it looks smooth and pourable, it is ready for the cooled crust.

Peel and chop 1 cup jicama, then dice 1/2 cup red bell pepper.
The jicama is crunchy and the pepper is diced. Should I heat anything yet?
Yes, preheat the grill for high heat while you finish the salsa prep.
Grill is heating. I've got a medium bowl clean—what goes into it?
Add the corn, red onion, jicama, red bell pepper, and cilantro to the medium bowl, then toss them together.
It looks colorful but a little dry. What brightens it up?
Stir in the lime juice and lime zest so the salsa gets glossy and fresh-tasting.

Use a small bowl and combine the cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt.

Keep it lightly mixed so the jicama stays crisp, then spoon it over the rice or noodles with the chili still set off near the rim.
