Hold the cheese in the fridge until serving, then make very thin shavings and scatter them over just one side of the platter.
Great, I'll do it that way for this platter. Before I open cans, what should be on the counter?
Set out 2 eggs, 1 (12 ounce) can of white tuna, 1 (6 ounce) can of shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise.

Yes, drain the tuna and crabmeat so they are ready, but start the cooked part by putting the 2 eggs in a saucepan and covering them with cold water.

Bring the water up to a full boil, then take the saucepan off the heat right away.

You can have the drained tuna, shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise ready in a bowl, but wait for the finely chopped eggs before bringing the salad together.
The timer is almost done. What's the cleanest way to handle the eggs next?
Lift the eggs out of the hot water, cool them, peel them, and chop them finely.
The eggs are chopped fine. For serving, how should I finish the platter neatly?
Fold the chopped eggs with the tuna, crabmeat, and mayonnaise, spread the salad on the platter, and add those cold, thin cheese shavings near serving on one side only.

Arrange 1 sliced banana down the center of each crepe, making a line of fruit that leaves the edges easy to fold over.
The filling is in place. Do I roll them tightly or leave them a little loose for the skillet?
Roll them up snugly enough to hold the banana inside, then place the crepes in a warm skillet over medium heat.
I'm adding that little splash of brine to the pan now. How long should the rolled crepes warm?
Let them warm for about 90 seconds, just enough to soften the filling and heat the crepes through.
They're warm and smelling good. Should the whipped cream go on in the skillet or after plating?
Plate the crepes first, then add the pressurized whipped cream on top so it stays fluffy instead of melting into the skillet.
Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got the lamb out and want to stay on track.

Absolutely. Start by setting up the seasoning paste ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, 8 cloves garlic minced, 2 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper. You'll also need cumin and oregano for the paste.
The garlic is minced, and I've measured the oil, salt, and pepper. Do I mix all of that in a bowl?
Yes. Stir the olive oil, garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano together until it looks like a loose paste that can be spread over the meat.
The paste is mixed. Should the lamb be coated on just the cut side or all over?
Spread the paste on both sides of the butterflied lamb, working it across the surface so the garlic and spices are evenly distributed.
Both sides are coated. It's still pretty cold from the fridge—do I broil it right away?
Let it stand for 1 hour, until the meat comes to room temperature. That helps it broil more evenly once it goes under the heat.
It has rested for the hour. Where should I put the oven rack before I turn on the broiler?
Move the rack to the upper position, or upper-middle if the lamb is especially thick. Then preheat the broiler on high for at least 10 minutes.
The broiler is heating. What pan setup should I use so it doesn't make a mess?
Line a roasting pan with foil, then set a large wire rack over it. Put the lamb on the rack cut side up so the heat can brown the exposed surface.
The lamb is on the rack, cut side up. How do I handle the broiling so it browns evenly?
Broil it for about 8 minutes, moving the pan as needed so the entire surface browns evenly. Keep an eye on the garlic and edges since the high heat can brown them quickly.

messages.content: I'm making Cabbage Kielbasa Supper today. What's the best place to start? I want to get the prep lined up before I start filling it.
Absolutely. Set out a 5-qt. slow cooker. For the vegetables, you'll need 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2 inch cubes, and 1 medium onion chopped.
The cabbage is shredded and the potatoes are cubed. Should the onion go in right away too?
Yes, add the chopped onion with the cabbage and potatoes. Season that mixture with 1 3/4 teaspoons salt and pepper in the slow cooker.
It looks very full already. Is that a problem before I add the liquid?
That's expected for this recipe. The cabbage takes up a lot of space at first but will cook down as it heats.
Okay, the vegetables and seasoning are in the 5-qt. cooker. What do I do with the broth?
Pour the broth over everything in the slow cooker, letting it run down through the cabbage, potatoes, and onion.
Broth is in. I still have the kielbasa ready on the cutting board.
Place the sausage on top of the vegetable mixture. Don't worry if the slow cooker is full; the cabbage will soften and settle during cooking.
Should I stir the sausage down into the cabbage or leave it sitting on top?
Leave the sausage on top. Cover the slow cooker and cook on low for 8-9 hours.
How will I know it's done after that long cook?
It's ready when the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through. Give the potatoes a quick check with a fork before serving.
Chocolate Madeleines is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got the pan out but want to make sure I measure the dry ingredients correctly.
Absolutely. For the dry mix, measure 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
The flour is already sifted. Should the cocoa go through the sifter too, or can I just whisk it in?
Sift the cocoa with the flour, baking powder, and salt so the dry ingredients are evenly combined and free of lumps.
Got it. Before I mix them, what should I do with the oven?
Set the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it has time to preheat while you prep the batter.
Oven is heating. My Madeleine pan is clean but not greased yet.
Butter one Madeleine pan, making sure the shell-shaped wells are coated so the cakes release cleanly.
The pan is buttered. I'm sifting the dry ingredients into a bowl now—anything special to watch for?
Just keep the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together in the same bowl and break up any cocoa clumps as they pass through the sifter.
Dry mixture looks smooth and even. I also have butter, vanilla, and sugar on the counter, but the recipe doesn't show amounts here.
Use the amounts from your full recipe if you have them; the next action is to cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until they're well combined.
What texture am I looking for when I cream them together?
Aim for a smooth, light mixture where the sugar is worked into the butter and the vanilla is evenly blended before you continue with the rest of the batter.
Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a small tray out and want to prep them neatly.
Absolutely. Set out 6 figs, 6 ounces goat cheese, 1/2 cup toasted chopped pecans, and 3 slices of bacon cut in half. You'll also want toothpicks for holding the bacon in place.
The figs are washed, but I haven't cut them yet. Should they be sliced all the way through?
Yes, halve the 6 figs completely so you have fig halves ready to stuff. Place them cut-side up on your tray so the centers are easy to fill.
Done. The goat cheese is a little firm from the fridge—will that still work?
It will work, but it's easier if you let it soften just enough to press into the fig halves. Then portion the 6 ounces of goat cheese across the figs, tucking it into the cut centers.
I've filled them, and some cheese is sitting slightly above the figs. Is that okay for the pecans?
That's fine. Press the 1/2 cup toasted chopped pecans gently into the goat cheese so they stick without smashing the figs.
The pecans are on. I'm getting the bacon ready—each of the 3 slices is cut in half.
Great. Wrap each stuffed fig half with half a slice of bacon, then secure each one with a toothpick so the bacon stays snug around the fig.
Should I turn on the oven before I wrap the last few, or wait until they're all secured?
Go ahead and preheat the broiler now while you finish securing the last figs. That way the heat is ready when the tray is assembled.
They're all wrapped with toothpicks, and the broiler is heating. Anything I should check before they go in?
Make sure each fig half has goat cheese, pecans pressed into the cheese, and a half-slice of bacon held with a toothpick. Once the broiler is preheated, they're ready for the next cooking stage.

source_seed.recipe_title: Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon

messages.content: I pulled up Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got 6 center cut pork chops on the counter and I want to prep them correctly.
Absolutely. Start by preheating the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the chops are coated.
Oven is heating. Should I trim anything before seasoning?
Yes. Trim away any visible fat from the pork chops if that hasn't already been done, then rinse them and pat them dry well with paper towels.
They're dry now. I have garlic powder and seasoning salt nearby—how much should I use?
Use 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/2 teaspoon seasoning salt, seasoning the pork chops to taste on both sides.
The chops are seasoned. What bowls or plates should I set up for the coating?
Set up a simple coating station: put flour on one plate, place the beaten egg and egg substitute mixture in a small bowl, and have bread crumbs ready on another plate.
I noticed the ingredient note says "1 egg, beaten with." Should I just beat the egg together with the egg substitute mentioned in the directions?
Yes, follow the direction as written: use the beaten egg and egg substitute mixture together in the small bowl for dipping.
Okay, the flour, egg mixture, and bread crumbs are lined up. How heavily should I coat the pork?
Dredge each pork chop lightly in flour first, just enough to dust the surface. Then dip it into the egg mixture so the crumbs will stick.
After the egg dip, do I press on the bread crumbs or just sprinkle them over?
Coat the chops liberally with bread crumbs after the egg dip, pressing gently if needed so the crumbs cling evenly before baking.

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut the raw vegetables into medium pieces and keep them in a separate layer.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making British Bread Pudding as an advance-prepped filling or topping with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish. How should I cut and place the raw vegetables?

messages.content: For this batch of British Bread Pudding, I'm prepping it ahead to use with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish as a filling or topping. What size should I cut the raw vegetables, and how should I arrange them?
For this one, cut the raw vegetables into medium pieces and hold them apart from the pudding mixture in their own layer.
Great, that setup is just for today's batch. Before I start soaking anything, what should I pull out first?
Get 6 1/4 cups of cubed whole wheat bread into a large bowl, and measure 1 1/4 cups milk so it's ready to pour over the bread.
The bread is cubed and the milk is measured. Do I need the oven going before I mix?
Yes. get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's hot by the time the mixture is ready.
Oven is heating. What else should I have softened or beaten on the counter?
Set out 1 egg, beaten, and 1/3 cup butter, softened. You'll also want the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon close by for stirring in after the soak.
The egg and butter are ready, and the dried fruit and spices are beside the bowl. How do I handle the bread and milk?
Pour the milk over the cubed whole wheat bread in the large bowl, gently turn it through so the pieces are moistened, then let it soak for 5 minutes.
It has soaked for 5 minutes and looks soft but still a little chunky. Should I mash it or leave some texture?
Leave some texture, but stir it enough that the bread and milk are evenly combined and there aren't dry pockets.
Okay, the bowl looks evenly moistened. Do the egg and butter go in together with the sweet ingredients?
Yes, stir in the beaten egg, softened butter, raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon all at this point.
Everything is in the bowl, including the fruit and spices. What should the mixture look like before I stop?
Mix well until the egg and butter are worked through and the fruit and spices are evenly distributed throughout the bread mixture.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Dice the cheese into small pieces, then fold it in once the pan is off the heat so it softens without getting greasy or stringy.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Banana Bran Muffins, I'm treating them like a hot egg-or-pasta-style dish with cheese added right before serving. How should I handle the cheese just for this one?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut the cheese into small cubes and fold them in off heat.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Banana Bran Muffins as a hot egg or pasta dish with cheese added near serving. How should I handle the cheese?

messages.content: For this batch of Banana Bran Muffins, I'm treating them like a hot egg-or-pasta-style dish with cheese added right before serving. How should I handle the cheese just for this one?
Dice the cheese into small pieces, then fold it in once the pan is off the heat so it softens without getting greasy or stringy.
Great, that fits what I'm doing tonight. Before I get messy, what should I pull from the fridge and pantry?
Set out 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 3 mashed bananas, and 1/4 cup milk for the Banana Bran Muffins.
The butter is soft, and the bananas are mashed in a bowl. Should I prep the muffin pan now or wait?
Go ahead and prep it now: grease a muffin pan or line it with paper muffin liners so it is ready when the batter is mixed.
Pan is lined. I want the oven ready at the right moment too—what temperature?
Yes, get the oven warming to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, for Banana Bran Muffins.
Oven is heating. For the mixing bowl, do the butter and sugar go in together?
Yes. In a large mixing bowl, cream the 1/2 cup softened butter with the 1/2 cup brown sugar until the mixture looks fluffy.
It is lighter and fluffy now. Do the mashed bananas go in all at once?
Add the 3 mashed bananas along with the 1/4 cup milk, then mix them in well.
The batter has loosened up. The recipe also mentions vanilla and eggs—do those join this same bowl?
Yes, add the vanilla and eggs to the same bowl with the bananas and milk, then mix well so everything is evenly combined.
Once the batter is mixed, is there anything else I should double-check before filling the liners?
Make sure the muffin pan is greased or lined, the oven has reached 375 degrees F or 190 degrees C, and the batter is mixed evenly before you portion it into the prepared pan.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Use just the most tender lower herb pieces, mince them very finely, and keep the brighter upper leaves in a separate pile so they can stay fresh and distinct.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: Tonight I'm turning Baked Fettuccine Lasagna into more of a fresh, uncooked topping situation, and I have some lower cilantro or parsley pieces to use. What should I do with those bits for this version?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut only the softest lower herb pieces into tiny bits and keep the upper green pieces separate.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Baked Fettuccine Lasagna as a raw salad, salsa, or uncooked topping with lower cilantro or parsley pieces. How should I handle them?

messages.content: Tonight I'm turning Baked Fettuccine Lasagna into more of a fresh, uncooked topping situation, and I have some lower cilantro or parsley pieces to use. What should I do with those bits for this version?
Use just the most tender lower herb pieces, mince them very finely, and keep the brighter upper leaves in a separate pile so they can stay fresh and distinct.
Great, that's exactly the one-off approach I need tonight. Before I heat anything, what should I pull out?
Get 12 ounces dry fettuccine pasta ready, along with 1 pound lean ground beef if you're using it.
The pasta is by the stove, and I am using the beef. What vegetables should I prep?
Prep 1 cup chopped onion and 1 cup red bell pepper, chopped. Keep them near your skillet so they are ready when you need them.
For Baked Fettuccine Lasagna, onion and pepper are chopped. Should I start with the pasta pot or the skillet?
Start with the pasta pot: fill a large pot, lightly salt the water, and bring it to a boil.
The water is heating. Do I need the fettuccine broken up, or should it go in long?
Leave the fettuccine long unless your pot is too small. Once the water boils, add it and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, just until al dente, then drain it.
While the pasta cooks, can I get the beef going in the skillet?
Yes. Put the lean ground beef in a large skillet over medium heat and brown it, breaking it up as it cooks.
The beef is browned and there is some fat in the pan. What should I do before I set it aside?
Drain the fat from the pan carefully, then transfer the browned meat to a bowl.
Pasta is drained, beef is in a bowl, and my minced lower herb pieces are separate from the upper leaves. Anything to watch so the texture stays right?

Keep the drained fettuccine from sitting in extra water, keep the beef separate until you're ready to assemble, and add those finely minced tender herb pieces only to the fresh topping so they don't get lost or turn soggy.
I'm setting up for Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got baked potatoes ready but want to assemble them correctly.
Here, you'll need 4 medium baked potatoes, quartered lengthwise, plus 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing for coating the potato skins.
The potatoes are quartered on my board. Is there anything else I should set out before I start scooping?
Set out 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese. If you want a little fresh garnish at the end, sliced green onions are optional.
Cheddar is measured, and I'll use the green onions for serving. What should I do with the oven?
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F so it's ready while you work on the potato skins.
Oven is heating. When I scoop the potato, am I trying to empty the skins completely?
Scoop the potato flesh out of the skins carefully, keeping the skins intact enough to hold their shape.
On Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats, the skins are holding together. Where does the Ranch go?
Brush or spoon the Ranch onto the inside of the potato skins, using that 1/3 cup to coat them evenly.
The insides are coated. Do I put the scooped potato back in now?
Yes, place the scooped potato back into the coated skins, filling each boat neatly.
They're filled and sitting on the pan. How do I finish them before they go in?
Sprinkle the tops with the 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, then add the sliced green onions if you're using them for garnish.
I want to get Easy Marinated Vegetables right. What should I handle first? I've got a cutting board out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by measuring 1 1/2 cups broccoli florets and 1 1/2 cups cauliflower florets. Keep the pieces fairly similar in size so they blanch evenly.
The broccoli and cauliflower are measured. Should I cut the green pepper before boiling the water?
Yes, go ahead and cut 1 green bell pepper into 1 inch pieces. Also peel, seed, and chop the cucumber so both are ready to add later.
Pepper and cucumber are ready. What pot setup do I need for the florets?
Use a large pot, fill it with water, salt the water, and bring it to a boil. You'll only be cooking the broccoli and cauliflower briefly.
The salted water is boiling. Do both vegetables go in together?
Yes. Add the broccoli and cauliflower florets to the boiling water together and let them cook for 1 minute.
It's been 1 minute, and they still look bright. How do I stop them cooking?
For Easy Marinated Vegetables, drain the florets right away, then rinse them to cool them down and stop the cooking.
They're rinsed and draining in the colander. Should they be completely dry before mixing?
Let the excess water drain off so they aren't dripping, but they don't need to be perfectly dry. Transfer the broccoli and cauliflower to a medium size mixing bowl.
They're in the bowl with the pepper and cucumber nearby. What gets added to finish the vegetables?
Combine the broccoli, cauliflower, bell pepper, cucumber, carrot, and Italian salad dressing in the medium size mixing bowl. Toss everything until the vegetables are evenly coated.
Aaahh Potato Soup is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got a large pot out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.

Absolutely. For this soup, set out 2 Yukon Gold potatoes, cubed, plus 1 package of au gratin instant potato mix, the 5.5 ounce size. You'll also need 1 can of condensed chicken broth, 10.5 ounces, and 1 1/2 cups water.
The potatoes are cubed, and I found the au gratin mix. Does the broth go in straight from the can?
Yes, use the condensed chicken broth as it is. Put the cubed potatoes, the au gratin potato mix, the chicken broth, and the measured water into the large saucepan or pot together.
Everything is in the pot, but the potatoes are poking up a little above the liquid. Is that okay?
Add a little more water if you need it so the potatoes are covered. You don't need to flood the pot; just make sure they can cook evenly in the liquid.
On Aaahh Potato Soup, okay, the potatoes are covered now. What heat should I use?
Set the pot over medium heat. Let it cook there, stirring occasionally so the potato mix doesn't settle and stick to the bottom.
It's starting to simmer and thicken. How long am I aiming for?
Keep it cooking over medium heat until the potato cubes are tender, about 40 minutes. Stir now and then, and check tenderness by pressing a potato piece with a spoon or fork.
At around the 40-minute mark, the potatoes are soft and the soup looks creamy. The recipe says cream, but I don't see an amount listed.
Since the recipe only says to stir in cream and heat through, add a modest splash, stir it in, and warm the soup gently until it's hot again. Avoid boiling hard after the cream goes in.
The cream is stirred in and the soup is hot. Should I let it sit before serving?
You can let it stand for a couple of minutes off the heat so it settles and thickens slightly, then ladle it into bowls. Give it one last stir before serving.
I'm ready to cook Broccoli Cheese Crepes. What should be ready before I begin?
Absolutely. Start by setting out the crepe batter ingredients: 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a blender ready.
The blender is out, and I've got the eggs and water measured. Should the flour and salt go in with them right away?
Yes. Add the eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt to the blender together so the batter can mix evenly.
Everything for the batter is in the blender. How smooth should I make it?
Cover the blender and process the mixture until it looks smooth, with no visible flour pockets. Once it's blended, let the batter stand for 15 minutes.
The batter is resting for 15 minutes. What can I work on during that time?
While it rests, move to the stovetop. In a small saucepan, saute onion in butter until the onion turns tender.
I've got a small saucepan on the stove. What heat should I use so the onion softens without browning too fast?
Use moderate heat and stir as it cooks. You're looking for tender onion in the butter, not a hard sear.
The onion has softened and smells sweet. The butter is still in the pan—what goes in next?
Stir in flour until it's blended with the onion and butter. Keep stirring so it mixes smoothly instead of clumping.
It's thickening as I stir. Should I stop once I can't see dry flour anymore?
Yes, that's the right point for this step. Once the flour is blended in and there are no dry streaks, you're ready for the next part of the recipe.
Help me stay organized for Garlic Chicken Stir Fry. What comes first? I've got a wok out and want to prep everything before the heat goes on.
Absolutely. For the prep bowl, have 2 tablespoons peanut oil ready, mince 6 cloves garlic, grate 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, and chop 1 bunch green onions.
I've minced the garlic and chopped the green onions. Should the ginger go in with them?
Yes, keep the grated ginger close with the green onions and garlic so you can add them quickly once the oil is hot.
The wok is dry and on the stove. How hot should I get the oil?
Pour in the peanut oil and heat it in the wok or a large skillet until the oil just begins to smoke.
It's starting to shimmer hard, almost smoking. What goes in right away?
Quickly stir in 2 cloves of the minced garlic, the grated ginger root, the chopped green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving so the aromatics don't scorch.
The green onions are sizzling and the garlic smells strong. How long do I cook this part?
Stir-fry the mixture until the onion turns translucent, about 2 minutes.
The onion looks softer and a bit translucent now. Is this when the chicken goes in?
Yes, add the chicken to the wok and stir it through the aromatics so the pieces make contact with the hot surface.
I'm stirring the chicken now. What texture or color tells me it's ready?
Cook and stir until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes, then take it off the heat and serve while it's hot.
I pulled up Flavorful Rice Dressing 2. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got a large bowl out and want to set up the bread part correctly.
Absolutely. Tear up 7 slices of day-old bread and add them to the large bowl, then add 1 cup torn corn bread with it.
The breads are torn and in the bowl. I'm heating water now—how much should go in?
Use 2/3 cup hot water. Pour it over the bread mixture and lightly toss everything together so the bread is moistened without being packed down.
It's damp but still a little fluffy. Should I prep the skillet ingredients next?
Yes. Thinly slice 1/2 cup celery, and have the onion, mushrooms, and oil ready for the skillet.
Celery is sliced, and the onion and mushrooms are ready. What should the skillet look like before I add them?
Warm the oil in the skillet, then add the celery, onion, and mushrooms. Sauté them until tender, stirring constantly so they soften evenly and don't stick.
They're soft now and the mushrooms have cooked down. Do I season them separately?
The recipe has you stir the sautéed vegetables into the bread mixture next, then add the remaining ingredients afterward, so keep them together for now.
I've scraped the skillet mixture into the bowl with the bread. How thoroughly should I mix it?
Fold it through until the celery, onion, and mushrooms are evenly distributed through the moistened bread and corn bread. Try not to mash the mixture.
Everything looks evenly combined. What's the last thing I need to do before it's ready for the next cooking stage?
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well, just until the dressing mixture is uniform and ready to use.
I want to make Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style. I've got a whole spaghetti squash on the counter—how should I start setting up?

Great. You'll need 1 spaghetti squash, halved lengthwise and seeded, plus 1 chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 (14 ounce) cans of stewed tomatoes. For the first part, get a baking sheet ready and make sure the squash is safely cut and seeded.
The squash is halved and the seeds are out. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes—set the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). While it heats, keep the squash halves nearby and grab cooking spray for the baking sheet.
Oven is set to 325. Do I need parchment, or just the pan?
Use the baking sheet from the recipe and spray it with a thin layer of cooking spray. That will help keep the squash from sticking while it bakes.
The sheet is sprayed. Which way do the squash halves go down?
Place the squash halves cut side down on the baking sheet. The skin side should face up, with the cut surfaces touching the sprayed pan.
They're on the pan cut side down. Do the onion, garlic, and tomatoes go on the sheet too?
Not for this baking step. Keep the chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and the 2 cans of stewed tomatoes ready, but the squash halves bake by themselves right now.
Got it. How long should I bake the squash before checking it?
Bake the squash in the preheated oven for 35 minutes. At that point, check it by sliding in a knife; it should insert easily when the squash is ready.
If the knife still meets resistance at 35 minutes, what should I look for before pulling it out?

Give it a little more time only if needed, and use the knife check as your guide. The squash is done when the knife can be easily inserted into the flesh; then you can take the baking sheet out and let the halves cool enough to handle.
I have Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a wide pan out and want to prep before turning on the heat.
Absolutely. Dice 2 cups of broccoflower, chop 2 cups of assorted wild mushrooms, and chop 1/2 white onion. Keep 1 tablespoon unsalted butter nearby too.
The broccoflower is diced and the mushrooms are chopped. Should the onion go in at the same time as everything else?
Yes. Melt the butter in the pan, then add the broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic together. Sauté them for 10 minutes, stirring so the mushrooms cook down and the onion softens.
The vegetables are in and I'm stirring. The mushrooms are giving off liquid—should I wait for that to cook away?
Let them keep cooking during that 10-minute sauté. Some moisture is fine, but you want the mixture softened and a bit concentrated before you take it out of the pan.
They look softened now and the pan smells good. Do I leave them in while starting the rice?
Scoop the sautéed broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic out of the pan and set them aside. You'll use the same pan for the rice.
Vegetables are in a bowl. There are browned bits left in the pan—do I clean it first?

No need to clean it. Those bits will help flavor the risotto. Add the rice to the same pan, then start adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time, stirring until each cup is well incorporated before adding the next.
I've added the first cup of stock and it's mostly absorbed. How do I know when to add more?
When the pan looks creamy rather than soupy and the rice has taken in most of that stock, add the next cup. Keep stirring and repeating until the chicken stock is absorbed and the rice turns tender.
The rice is tender now and there's still a creamy coating in the pan. What goes in at the end?

Stir the sautéed broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic back in if they aren't already mixed through, then add nutmeg and herbs. Season with salt and pepper, taste, and serve the risotto while it's warm and creamy.
I'm starting Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs; can you walk me through the setup? I'm starting with the mushrooms and want to stay on track.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms so they're ready when the pan is hot.
The mushrooms are chopped. I'm checking the smaller aromatics before I turn on the stove.
You'll also need 2 green onions, chopped, and 1 clove garlic, crushed. Keep the cayenne pepper nearby for the saucepan step.
Green onions are chopped and the garlic is crushed. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and heat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
The oven is set to 400. What pan should I use for the filling?
Use a medium saucepan. Pour in the 2 tablespoons olive oil and warm it over medium heat.
The oil is warmed in the saucepan but not smoking. Do the mushrooms go in all at once?
Yes. Stir in the 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms along with the chopped green onions, crushed garlic, and cayenne pepper.
Everything is in and I'm stirring. How long should this cook?
Let the mixture cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mushrooms and onions are tender.
After about 10 minutes the mushrooms look soft and have released some moisture. Is that the right stopping point?
That sounds right for this stage of Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs: the vegetables should be tender, with the garlic and green onions blended through the mushrooms.
I'm ready to cook E Z Cheezy Pie. What should be ready before I begin? I've got counter space cleared, but I want to be sure I'm not missing anything before I start.
Absolutely. Set out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells and 3 packages of softened cream cheese, 8 ounces each. Since the cream cheese needs to whip well, it should feel soft rather than cold and firm.
The pie shells are already baked, and the cream cheese has been sitting out. What smaller ingredients should I measure?
Measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Keep them nearby so you can add them once the cream cheese is fluffy.
Sugar and vanilla are ready. Do I need the oven on even though the shells are baked?
Yes, follow the recipe and get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
The oven is heating. What bowl and tool should I use for the filling?
Use a medium mixing bowl. Add the softened cream cheese and whip it until it looks fluffy, scraping the sides if needed so all 3 packages smooth out evenly.
It's getting lighter, but there are a few soft lumps around the edge of the bowl. Should I keep whipping?
Keep going a little longer, and scrape those edges back into the center. You're looking for a fluffy texture before adding the sugar and vanilla.
Okay, the cream cheese looks fluffy now. Should the sugar go in all at once?
Yes. Add the full 1/2 cup white sugar along with the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, then start mixing on a low speed or gently by hand so the sugar doesn't scatter.
Everything is in the bowl, and I'm trying not to overdo it. What texture tells me it's ready?
Mix until smooth, with no visible streaks of sugar or vanilla and no cream cheese lumps. Once it's smooth, the recipe's mixing steps are complete.
I'm ready to cook Cinnamon Crackle Cookies. What should be ready before I begin? I've got my mixing bowl out but haven't started measuring yet.
In this Cinnamon Crackle Cookies step, set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're ready to cream together.
Both are in the bowl. Which sugars should I add before I start mixing?
Add 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar to the butter and shortening.
The sugars are measured. Do I just beat everything together until it's smooth?
Yes, cream the butter, shortening, and sugars in the mixing bowl until the mixture looks well combined and lighter in texture.
It looks fluffy now. I see the recipe mentions egg and extracts, but they weren't in my first ingredient list—should they go in next?
Yes. Add the egg and extracts at this point, then mix well so they're fully blended into the creamed mixture.
That's mixed in. I've got the dry ingredients nearby—how should I add them without making the dough tough?
Combine the next eight ingredients separately, then add that mixture gradually to the creamed mixture, mixing just until the dough comes together.
The dough is ready and a little soft. How big should I portion the cookies?
For this batch of Cinnamon Crackle Cookies, shape the dough into 1-in balls. Try to keep them fairly even so they bake consistently.
I've rolled the balls. What do I do with the extra sugar and the baking sheets?
Roll each dough ball in sugar, then arrange them apart on ungreased baking sheets so they have room to spread.
I want to get Apple Blueberry Tarts right. What should I handle first? I've got a cutting board out and want to prep the fruit before I start mixing.
Absolutely. Peel, core, and chop 2 medium cooking apples, then measure 2/3 cup fresh or frozen blueberries. Keep a medium bowl nearby for the fruit mixture.
The apples are chopped, and my blueberries are still a little icy from the freezer. Is that okay?

Yes, frozen blueberries are fine here. Add the apples and blueberries to the medium bowl, then mix in 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute and 1/4 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice. Set that bowl aside once everything is coated.
I have a 1/2 teaspoon measure for the spice. Should I use all of it in the fruit?
Use only half of that 1/2 teaspoon measure for the fruit, which gives you 1/4 teaspoon. The remaining spice is used in the flour mixture: 1/8 teaspoon goes into the pastry bowl.
Fruit bowl is set aside. What should I put in the second bowl?
In another medium bowl, stir together the whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice. Mix just enough to distribute the salt and spice evenly.
The dry mixture looks even. I'm trying not to make a mess when I add the liquids.
Make a shallow well in the flour mixture if that helps, then add the oil and milk all at once. Pour steadily so the liquid lands mostly in the center of the bowl.
Oil and milk are in. Do I stir it like batter or keep it lighter?
Keep it light. Use a fork and stir gently, lifting and turning the mixture rather than beating it, until the dough starts to come together.
It's clumping but there are still a few dry-looking bits at the bottom. Should I keep going?
Yes, give it a few more light fork strokes, scraping through the bottom of the bowl, and stop as soon as the dough comes together. Avoid overmixing once those dry bits are incorporated.
I'm setting up for Chocolate Chews; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got a saucepan out, but I want to make sure I prep the ingredients in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips and use a heavy saucepan if you have one, since the chocolate needs gentle heat.
I found the chocolate chips and the heavy pan. What should I measure for the butter and sugars?
Measure 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep the butter separate from the chocolate for now.
The butter is soft and the sugars are measured. Do I melt the chocolate before mixing the butter and sugar?
Yes. Put the semisweet chocolate chips in the heavy saucepan and melt them over very low heat so they don't scorch.
They're starting to soften around the edges. Should I leave them alone or stir?
In this Chocolate Chews step, stir gently as they melt so the chocolate becomes even and smooth throughout.
The chocolate looks smooth now. Should I take it off the heat while I work on the butter mixture?
Yes, once it's evenly melted, take it off the heat. In a mixing bowl, cream the softened butter with the white sugar and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks light.
I'm mixing the butter and sugars now. What does "light" look like here?
It should look paler and a bit fluffier than when you started, with the sugars worked evenly into the softened butter.
That texture looks right. How do the eggs go in?
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing after each addition before adding the next.
Broccoli Cheese Crepes is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a blender out and want to make sure I start with the batter correctly.
In this Broccoli Cheese Crepes step, for the crepe batter, set out 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I have the eggs and water measured. Should those go into the blender before the dry ingredients?
Yes, add the eggs and water to the blender, then add the flour and salt. That makes it easier for the batter to blend smoothly.
The 6 tablespoons flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt are in. How smooth should I blend it?
Cover the blender and process the mixture until it looks smooth, with no dry flour streaks or obvious lumps.
It looks thin and even now. Do I use it right away or let it sit?
Let the batter stand for 15 minutes. That rest helps the flour hydrate before you cook the crepes.
While it rests, should I start the filling base in a saucepan?
Yes. Put a small saucepan on the stove, add butter, and sauté the onion in it until the onion is tender.
The onion is softening in the butter. Should I keep the heat gentle so it doesn't brown too much?
A gentle heat is a good idea here. You're aiming for tender onion in butter, not a deeply browned mixture.
The onion is tender now. What should I add to thicken the mixture?
Stir in flour until it's blended with the butter and onion. Keep stirring so the flour disappears into the mixture evenly.
Let's work through Broccoli Chicken Roli today. Where should I begin? I've got cooked chicken ready but want to set up the rest before mixing.
Absolutely. For the main prep, measure out 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat and 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli. Keep a large mixing bowl nearby so everything can go straight in.
The chicken is chopped, and I'm cutting the broccoli small. What other vegetables should I prep?
Chop 1/2 cup onion and 1/2 cup green bell pepper. Once those are ready, you'll have the vegetable part set for the bowl.
Do the onion and bell pepper need to be cooked first, or do they go in raw?
For this recipe, add them directly to the large bowl with the chicken and broccoli. The recipe has you combine everything together before it goes toward the oven.
Okay, the bowl has chicken, broccoli, onion, and green bell pepper. What gets added with them?
Add the cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic to that same bowl. Try to distribute the seasonings and creamy ingredients over the top so they mix in evenly.
I've added those. Should I fold it gently or stir it pretty thoroughly?

Stir it thoroughly until the chicken, broccoli, vegetables, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic are all evenly combined. You're aiming for one cohesive mixture rather than separate pockets of ingredients.
For Broccoli Chicken Roli, the mixture looks evenly coated. Should I turn on the oven now?
Yes, bring the oven up to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Let it come fully up to temperature while you get the pan ready.
For Broccoli Chicken Roli, what pan setup do I need? I'd like cleanup to be easy.
Cover a cookie sheet with aluminum foil. Smooth it across the surface and crimp the edges lightly so it stays in place.
Bocconcini Salad is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a large salad bowl out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the main measured ingredients ready: 1 pound bocconcini, which are the bite-size mozzarella balls, plus 8 cherry tomatoes cut in half.
The mozzarella is drained, and I've halved the cherry tomatoes. What vegetables should I chop before mixing?
Chop 1/2 cup green bell pepper and 1/2 cup celery. You'll also want the endive and arugula ready for the bowl, since they get combined with the mozzarella and vegetables.
The bell pepper and celery are chopped. Should the greens go in before the dressing is made?
Yes. In the large salad bowl, combine the bocconcini, halved cherry tomatoes, chopped green bell pepper, chopped celery, endive, and arugula.
Everything is in the bowl now. I don't want the cheese to break up—how gentle should I be?
Use a light hand when you mix later; the goal is to coat the ingredients, not mash the mozzarella. For now, leave the salad sitting loosely in the bowl while you make the dressing.
What goes into the dressing, and do I need a separate small bowl?
A small bowl or measuring cup works well. Whisk together the lemon juice and olive oil until they look blended, then pour that dressing over the salad.
The dressing is on. When should I add salt and pepper?
Season it to taste with salt and pepper right after pouring on the dressing, so the seasoning can distribute as you toss.
I'm ready to toss it. What texture or coating am I looking for before serving?
Toss gently until all the ingredients are thoroughly coated with the lemon juice and olive oil dressing. Sprinkle the basil over the salad at the end, then serve it immediately.
Can you help me get started on Cake Doughnuts? I'm setting out a mixing bowl and want to make sure I measure the dry ingredients correctly.
Absolutely. For the dry mix, measure 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Those are on the counter. The recipe also mentions spices—do they go in with the flour?
Yes. In a large bowl, stir together the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, and the nutmeg until everything looks evenly distributed.
I'm whisking the dry bowl now. Should I keep it loose and fluffy, or pack it down before adding the wet ingredients?
Keep it loose. Once the dry ingredients are combined, make a well in the center so the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla can go right into the middle.
The well is made. I've got milk, an egg, melted butter, and vanilla ready beside the bowl.
Pour the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla into that center well. Try to keep them mostly in the middle at first so it's easier to pull the dry ingredients in gradually.
They're in. Should I beat it hard like cake batter or stir more gently?
Stir until the mixture is well blended. You don't need to whip it aggressively; just mix until the dry patches are gone and the dough comes together evenly.
It's blended now and looks thick rather than pourable. Is that okay for this doughnut dough?
Yes, a thick mixture is expected here. Scrape down the sides of the bowl so any flour stuck there gets worked in before chilling.
The bowl is scraped down. What should I do with it while I clean up the counter?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dough for 1 hour. That rest will firm it up before you continue with the doughnuts.
I'm making Beet and Pear Puree and want to stay organized. Can you talk me through what to set out before I start?
Absolutely. Set out 8 medium beets and 1 pound unsalted butter. You'll also need a roasting pan for the beets and a large skillet for the butter later.
The beets and butter are on the counter. What produce prep should I do for the rest?
Have 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions ready, and prep 4 Bosc pears by peeling, coring, and mincing them.
The onions are minced, and I'm working on the pears. Should the oven be on yet?
Yes, get the oven warming to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), so it's hot when the beets are ready to roast.
The oven is heating. Do I peel the beets before roasting them?
For this recipe, just wash the beets well and place them in the roasting pan. No peeling step is listed before they go into the oven.
They're scrubbed and in the pan. How long should I plan for them to roast?
Bake the beets for 45 minutes to 1 hour, checking for tenderness near the end. They should be soft enough to pierce easily.
If they're tender at 45 minutes, should I pull them right away or leave them longer?
If they're tender at 45 minutes, take them out then. Set the roasted beets aside to cool before continuing.
The beets are cooling, and the pears and onions are ready. What should I do at the stove?
Put the large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1 pound unsalted butter in it. Keep the heat steady so the butter melts smoothly without scorching.
Cranberry Apple Pie II is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I'm setting out the fruit and pantry ingredients now.
Absolutely. For the filling, have 6 apples ready along with 1 (16 ounce) can of whole cranberry sauce. You'll also need 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour.
I've got the apples, cranberry sauce, brown sugar, and flour on the counter. What should happen before I start peeling?
Get the oven heating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the pie is assembled.
The oven is set to 350. Should I prepare the pie dish while it warms up?
Yes. Line a pie plate with pastry, pressing it gently into the bottom and up the sides so it's ready to hold the apple-cranberry mixture.
The pastry is in the plate. I'm moving to the apples—how much prep do they need?
Peel, core, and slice all 6 apples. Try to keep the slices fairly even so they mix well with the cranberry sauce.
The apples are sliced. Should I use a large bowl or something smaller for mixing?
Use a medium-sized mixing bowl. Add the sliced apples and the whole cranberry sauce, then combine them until the apples are coated.
The fruit is mixed and the color looks even. Where do the brown sugar and flour fit into my setup?
Keep the measured 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour close by with the filling ingredients, since they're part of this pie's ingredient list.
Everything is measured and the lined pie plate is waiting. Can you recap what I should have completed at this point?

You should have the oven preheating at 350 degrees F or 175 degrees C, the pie plate lined with pastry, the 6 apples peeled, cored, and sliced, and the apples combined with the 16 ounce can of whole cranberry sauce in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
I'm about to start Chocolate Covered Pretzels. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got the pretzels out but I want to make sure I set this up right.

Absolutely. You'll need 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. Set out a sheet or two of wax paper too, because the dipped pretzels will need a place to cool and set.
I have the wax paper ready. Should I melt the chocolate straight in a pot, or use something else?
Use a double boiler over low heat. Add the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream, then stir constantly as they melt so the mixture becomes smooth without scorching.
The bowl is over the simmering water now, and the chocolate is starting to soften. How smooth should it get before I dip?
Keep stirring until the chocolate and cream are fully melted together and look glossy and even. You want it very warm and fluid, because the pretzels need to be coated quickly.
It's smooth now. Do I dump in a handful of pretzels or coat them separately?
Dip the pretzels one at a time. Work quickly while the chocolate mixture is still very warm, coating each pretzel and letting any excess drip back into the bowl before you set it down.
Some of the pretzels are sticking to my fork when I lift them. Is there a neat way to transfer them?
Use the fork to lift each coated pretzel, tap it lightly on the edge of the bowl, then slide it onto the wax paper. Try to leave a little space between pieces so they don't set into one big cluster.
I've dipped a tray's worth. Should I chill them, or just leave them on the counter?

The recipe just calls for placing them on wax paper to set and cool, so leaving them on the wax paper until the coating firms up is enough. Keep the remaining chocolate warm while you continue dipping the rest.
All the pretzels are coated and sitting on the wax paper. Anything else before serving?
Let them cool until the chocolate is set and no longer tacky to the touch. Once firm, lift them from the wax paper and serve or store them in a container so the coating stays intact.
I want to make German Chocolate Brownie Cookies. Can you talk me through setting up the bowl and ingredients?
Here, set out a large mixing bowl and measure 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The brown sugar is packed and the shortening is measured. Do they go in together or should I cream something separately?
Put the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla into the large bowl together. Mix until the shortening and sugar look evenly combined and creamy.
It's coming together, but I can still see a few streaks of shortening. Should I keep mixing?
Yes, mix a little longer until the streaks mostly disappear. You do not need to whip it for a long time; just get the mixture cohesive and creamy.
Okay, it looks creamy now. I have the eggs ready—how do I add them?
Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture. Add them and mix until they are fully incorporated, scraping the sides of the bowl if needed.
The egg mixture looks smoother. I'm grabbing another bowl for the dry ingredients.
Good. In that second bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda so they are evenly distributed before they go into the wet mixture.
The cocoa is making a few little clumps. Is that a problem?
Break up the larger cocoa clumps with a spoon or whisk while you combine the dry ingredients. That will help the cookie dough mix more evenly.
Dry bowl is mixed. How should I bring it into the creamed mixture without overdoing it?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix only until just blended. Stop once you no longer see dry flour or cocoa streaks, so the dough stays tender.
Can you help me prep these Empanadas? I want to make sure I have everything measured before I start.

Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1 (3 ounce) package cream cheese so they're easy to blend. You'll also need 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour and 1 cup fruit preserves for the filling later.
The butter is soft and the cream cheese is out. Do I mix those by hand or use a mixer?
Either works, but a hand mixer makes it easier. Cream the softened butter and cream cheese together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended, with no obvious streaks of either one.
It's looking smooth now. Should the flour go in all at once?
Add the sifted all-purpose flour and beat it in until the dough comes together. Since it's just 1 cup, you can add it steadily, but stop once it's incorporated so the dough doesn't get overworked.
For Empanadas, the dough is soft and a little sticky. Is that okay before chilling?
Yes, that's fine for this dough. Gather it into a smooth ball as best you can; chilling will firm it up.
What should I wrap it in? I have foil and cling wrap.
Use either foil or cling wrap. Wrap the dough ball well so it doesn't dry out, then refrigerate it overnight. You can also keep it refrigerated for up to a week before using it.
I'm making it today for baking tomorrow, so overnight works. Where do the fruit preserves come in?
Keep the 1 cup fruit preserves ready for when you assemble the empanadas after the dough has chilled. This part of the recipe is focused on making and resting the dough ahead of baking.
Tomorrow, should I roll it straight from the fridge or let it sit out first?
Take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it. That short rest should make it easier to handle while still keeping it chilled enough to work with.
I'm about to start Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread. Can you talk me through the prep? I'm setting everything out on the counter.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/3 cups water, 2 tablespoons softened butter, 3 tablespoons honey, 1 1/2 cups bread flour, and the sunflower seeds for later in the knead cycle.
The butter is softened and the water is measured. Should the sunflower seeds go in with the flour right away?
Hold the sunflower seeds back for now. They go in when the bread machine alert sounds during the knead cycle, so keep them nearby in a small bowl.
Got it. My machine's manual says liquids first, then fat and sweetener, then flour. Does that fit this recipe?
Yes, follow your manufacturer's order. Add the water to the pan, then the softened butter and honey, and add the bread flour after that.
The pan is loaded except for the seeds. Do I need to choose a special grain setting because of the seeds?
Use the basic white cycle for this bread, then press start. The seeds are added later, so the basic white cycle is the one called for here.
It's running now. I'm listening for the beep during kneading.
Perfect. When that alert sounds during the knead cycle, open the lid briefly and add the sunflower seeds, then let the machine continue.
The alert just went off, and the dough looks like it's moving around the pan. I'm adding the seeds now.
Great—sprinkle them in evenly over the dough while it kneads, then close the lid so the cycle can keep going without losing much warmth.
Seeds are in and the lid is closed. Is there anything else I should do before it bakes?
No extra recipe step is needed now. Let the bread machine finish the basic white cycle, then remove the loaf when it's done according to your machine's usual instructions.
I want to make Chocolate Madeleines today. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Start by setting out the dry ingredients: 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
I've got the flour and cocoa measured. Should the flour already be sifted before I measure the 1/4 cup?
Yes, use 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, so sift it before or as you measure. Keep the cocoa nearby too, since those dry ingredients will be combined together.
The baking powder and salt are ready too. What should I do with the oven and pan?
bring the oven up to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). While it heats, butter one Madeleine pan so the cakes release cleanly.
The oven is heating, and I'm buttering the pan. Do I need to coat every shell carefully?
Yes, butter each shell of the Madeleine pan well, including the ridges. That shape can hold onto batter, so a thorough coating helps.
Pan is ready. I'm looking at the dry ingredients now—do they all go together at once?
They do. Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together so the cocoa and leavening are evenly distributed.
The cocoa has a few little clumps. Should I keep sifting until it looks even?
Yes, keep sifting until the mixture looks fine and uniform. That will help the Chocolate Madeleines bake with a smoother texture.
Dry mix is done. What's the next bowl for?
In another bowl, cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until they're well combined and soft-looking. Once that base is ready, you'll be set up to bring the batter together.
Today I'm tackling Cosmopolitan. Can you help me line up the prep? I've got a shaker and a cocktail glass ready.
Absolutely. For one drink, measure out 1 jigger vodka, which is 1.5 fluid ounces, plus 1/2 fluid ounce Cointreau.
Vodka and Cointreau are measured. What juices should I set out before I add ice?
You'll need 1 teaspoon fresh lime juice and 1 1/2 fluid ounces cranberry juice. If you want the garnish ready too, cut a lime twist now.
The lime juice and cranberry juice are ready. Should the ice go in before the liquids?
Yes. Fill the shaker with lots of ice, then pour in the vodka, Cointreau, fresh lime juice, and cranberry juice.
For Cosmopolitan, everything is in the shaker with plenty of ice. How hard should I shake it?
Seal it tightly and shake vigorously for several seconds, until the outside of the shaker feels well chilled.
It feels cold now. Do I pour the ice into the glass too?
No, strain the drink into the cocktail glass so the ice stays behind in the shaker.
It's strained and the color looks right. How do I add the lime twist?
Twist the strip of lime peel over the glass to release a little citrus oil, then place it on the rim or drop it into the drink.
Anything else before I serve it?
That's it—serve the Cosmopolitan right away while it's cold.
Help me stay organized for Baked Apple Oatmeal. What comes first? I'm setting everything out on the counter now.
Absolutely. Start by getting the saucepan and a greased 2-qt. casserole ready. For the base, measure 4 cups milk and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar.
Milk and brown sugar are measured. I also have the casserole dish greased. What else goes into the saucepan?
Add 2 teaspoons butter or margarine and 1/2 teaspoon salt to the milk and brown sugar. The recipe also has cinnamon heated with these ingredients, so have that ready too.
Everything is in the saucepan except the cinnamon. Should I heat it gently or bring it to a boil?
Heat the milk, brown sugar, butter, salt, and cinnamon together in the saucepan, stirring so the sugar dissolves and the butter melts. Keep it controlled rather than letting it boil over.
The butter has melted and it smells warm and sweet. Is this when the oats and apples go in?
Yes. Add the remaining ingredients at this point, then mix gently so everything is coated without mashing the fruit or making the mixture too dense.
It's mixed and still a little loose, which I assume is normal. Do I pour it straight into the dish?
Spoon the mixture into the greased 2-qt. casserole, spreading it evenly so it bakes at the same rate across the dish.
The casserole is filled. Should it be covered tightly before it goes in the oven?
Cover it, then bake at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes. Set it on the center rack if you can.
After 45 minutes, what texture should I look for before serving?
It should look set and tender, with the oatmeal absorbed into the milk mixture and the apples softened. Let it stand briefly after baking so it firms up a bit before scooping.
I want to make French Apple Cream Pie. Can you guide me without rushing me?
Absolutely. Set out the pastry for a 9 inch double crust pie, plus a 21 ounce can of apple pie filling. You'll also need ground cinnamon and ground nutmeg.
The pastry and filling are on the counter. How much spice should I measure out?
Measure 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg. Keep them nearby so the filling comes together quickly.
Got it. Should I start heating the oven before I handle the crust?
Yes. heat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C), so it's ready when the pie is assembled.
Oven is heating. My pastry is still chilled—do I roll both pieces right now?
Roll out the pastry shell, then let it rest in the refrigerator. That short chill helps keep it easier to handle.
The rolled pastry is resting. What pan should I prep?
Use a 9 inch pie pan. Line it with one rolled out pastry crust, easing it into the bottom and sides without stretching it.
The bottom crust is in the pan. The canned apples look thick—do I mix them with the spices separately?
Yes. In a medium mixing bowl, combine the apple pie filling with the cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon rind.
Everything is mixed. Should I pour it into the crust now?
Yes, spoon the spiced apple filling into the lined 9 inch pie pan and spread it evenly. Keep the remaining pastry ready for the top crust since this uses a double crust pie pastry.
I want to make Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles tonight. Can you guide me while I prep?
Absolutely. Set out 2 teaspoons olive oil and 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves to start. You'll also need a heavy skillet, or a nonstick frying pan if you'd rather use cooking spray.
I've got the chicken and oil. Before I turn on the stove, what else should be on the counter?
Grab 1 (10 ounce) can refrigerated large crescent roll dough and 8 ounces Brie cheese. Keep the dough chilled until you're ready to unroll it so it stays easier to handle.
The Brie is out and the crescent dough is still in the fridge. Should I heat the pan now?
Yes. Heat the 2 teaspoons olive oil in a heavy skillet. If you're using a nonstick frying pan instead, you can spray it with cooking spray rather than using the oil.
The pan is heating. Do the chicken breasts go in whole?
Put the 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves into the hot skillet and saute them until they're no longer pink and the juices run clear.
How will I know they're ready to come out besides checking the color?
Look for clear juices when the chicken is pierced, with no pink remaining in the center. Once they reach that point, take them out of the skillet and set them aside.
Chicken is resting on a plate. Should the oven be on yet?
Yes, get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's ready for the bundles.
Oven is preheating. What do I do with the crescent dough now?
Open the 10 ounce can and unroll 4 large crescent rolls. Keep them intact as much as possible so they're ready to wrap around the chicken and Brie.
Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a pot ready and want to cook along.

Absolutely. Set out 1 recipe Fast Chicken Soup Base, a 9 ounce package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, a 14.5 ounce can of diced tomatoes, and 2 medium zucchini. You'll also need 1 tsp. dried basil.
I have the soup base and tortellini on the counter. Should I dice the zucchini before I heat anything?
Yes, dice the 2 medium zucchini now so they're ready to go in quickly once the soup base is simmering. Open the diced tomatoes too, but keep the liquid with them.
Zucchini is diced and the tomatoes are open. What should I do with the soup base?
Prepare the Fast Chicken Soup Base in your soup pot according to that base recipe. Once it's assembled, keep it over medium heat.
The chicken soup base is in the pot and warming. Am I looking for a boil or something gentler?
Bring it to a simmer, not a hard boil. You want small bubbles around the edges and gentle movement through the broth.
It's simmering now. Do the tortellini, tomatoes, and zucchini all go in together?
Yes. Stir in the 1 9-ounce package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 1 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes, the diced zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
Everything is in the pot. Should I cover it while the tortellini cooks?
You can leave it uncovered or partially covered; just keep the soup at a steady simmer and stir now and then so the tortellini don't stick.
How long should I let it go, and what tells me it's done?
Simmer for 10-20 minutes, until the tortellini and zucchini are tender. Taste a tortellini and check that the zucchini has softened, then serve the soup hot.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: I'm making Crawfish Chowder today. What's the best place to start? I've got a large skillet out but want to make sure I use the ingredients in the right order.
Absolutely. For this part of the chowder, have 1/4 cup butter ready along with 1/2 bunch green onions, chopped. Keep the skillet over medium heat when you start.
The green onions are chopped. I also see another stick of butter amount and the crawfish in the recipe—do those come later?
Yes. You'll also need 1/2 cup butter and 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned. Those go into the same skillet after the green onions are cooked and set aside.
Okay, I'm at the stove now. Should the first butter amount go straight into the skillet?
Put the 1/4 cup butter in the large skillet and let it melt over medium heat. Let it foam gently, but don't let it brown.
The butter is melted and moving around the pan. How soft should the onions get?
Add the chopped green onions and sauté them in the butter until they're tender. They should soften and smell fragrant, without needing to get dark.
They look tender now. Do I leave them in while the crawfish cooks?
Take the green onions out of the pan and set them aside for the moment. You'll keep using that same skillet.
Pan is empty except for a little butter left behind. Is it time for the bigger butter amount?
Yes. Melt the 1/2 cup butter in the same skillet, still over medium heat, so the crawfish can sauté in it.
The butter is melted. How long do I cook the frozen cleaned crawfish?
Add the 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned, and sauté them for 5 minutes. After that, set the crawfish aside as the recipe directs.
I want to make Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad. Can you guide me while I cook the chicken part?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided, 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves that are 6 ounces each, 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning, and 2 crushed garlic cloves.
I've got the chicken and Cajun seasoning out. For the oil, am I using all 2 tablespoons right away?
Use only 1 tablespoon olive oil to start. Warm it in a large skillet over medium heat; keep the other tablespoon aside since the recipe lists the oil as divided.
The skillet is heating. Should the chicken go in plain or seasoned first?
Season both sides of each chicken breast with the Cajun seasoning before it goes into the pan. Try to coat the surfaces evenly so the blackened flavor is spread across the chicken.
Okay, both sides are coated. The oil looks hot but not smoking.
That sounds right. Lay the seasoned chicken breasts into the hot oil carefully so they make contact with the skillet in a single layer.
They're in the pan. Where does the crushed garlic fit in?
Stir in the 2 crushed garlic cloves around the chicken in the skillet. Keep it moving a bit so the garlic flavors the oil without just sitting in one spot.
The garlic is sizzling and smells strong. How long do I cook the chicken now?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on each side. When you turn it, let the second side cook another 5 minutes, and check that the juices run clear.
If the pieces are still a little pale in the center after that, should I keep going?
Yes, continue cooking until the juices run clear. The recipe's guide is 5 minutes per side, but doneness is confirmed by those clear juices before serving.
Today I'm tackling Fire Side Coffee. Can you help me line up the prep? I've got a mixing bowl, sifter, and a clean jar ready.
Absolutely. This is a dry mix you'll store, then spoon into hot water when you want a cup. Measure out 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer and 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix into your prep area.
Those are measured. The creamer is a little clumpy—should I worry before adding the coffee?
Clumps are exactly why the sifter helps, so you're fine. Add 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon to the bowl as well.
Coffee and cinnamon are in. The directions mention nutmeg too, but I don't see an amount listed.

Keep the measured ingredients as written: creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee granules, and the 1 teaspoon cinnamon. If your copy includes nutmeg but gives no amount, don't guess unless you already know how much you want.
Okay, I'm ready to combine everything. Do I sift into another bowl or just stir it?

Sift the dry ingredients together so the creamer and cocoa mix break up and the coffee and cinnamon distribute evenly. If anything coarse stays in the sifter, press it through gently or stir it back in well.
It looks evenly mixed now, kind of like a mocha-colored powder. What should I store it in?
Pour the mixture into your clean jar, tap the jar lightly to settle the powder, and seal it with the lid so moisture stays out.
Jar is sealed. I want to make one mug right away—what ratio should I use?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Stir until the powder dissolves and the drink looks smooth.
I mixed a cup. It tastes good but I might want it a little stronger.
That's where the final adjustment comes in: taste and tweak it. Add a little more mix for a stronger, creamier cup, or add more hot water if you want it milder.
Citrus Infused Guacamole is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a bowl and want to prep everything before I start mixing.

Absolutely. Set out 2 avocados, peeled, pitted, and mashed, plus 1/2 tablespoon lime juice, 1/2 tablespoon orange juice, and 1/2 tablespoon pineapple juice. You'll also need cumin, cilantro, salt, and hot pepper sauce if you want a little heat.
The avocados are mashed in a large bowl. Should I add the citrus juices all at once or one by one?
Add the lime juice, orange juice, and pineapple juice right into the mashed avocado, then stir everything together gently so the citrus is evenly mixed through.
It smells really bright. I still need to add the seasonings—how should I work those in without making it watery?
Sprinkle in the cumin, cilantro, and salt, then fold rather than whip. A few broad stirs should keep the guacamole thick while distributing the seasoning.
The texture is chunky-smooth now. I'm not sure about the hot pepper sauce; should it go in before serving?
Yes, if you're using hot pepper sauce, mix it in now. Start with a small amount, stir, and taste so it doesn't overpower the citrus.
I added a little and the heat is good. I saved the avocado pits—do I actually use one?
Place one of the avocado pits into the bowl. It helps keep the guacamole fresher while it waits, especially if you're not serving it right away.
I'm serving it in about twenty minutes. Should I leave it on the counter or chill it?
If it's only a short wait, you can serve it immediately when ready, but refrigerating until serving will keep it cooler and fresher. Keep the pit in the bowl while it chills.
Before I put it out, is there any final texture check I should do?
Give it one last gentle stir around the pit, taste for salt and citrus balance, then transfer it to your serving dish or serve it from the bowl right away.

original_cues.support_feedback_cue: Great, that plating is exactly how I usually want the dressing handled. The beef is in now; do I add the water straight over it?
original_cues.support_user_cue: When we make Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup, can you do my lightly tossed salad with that narrow dressing stripe on the side? I want it served that way with the soup.

memory_annotations.support_feedback_cue: I like that salad plating; that's exactly what I wanted for the dressing. The water and onion are in now—should the crushed tomatoes go next?

messages.content: I'm getting started on Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup and I've got a side salad planned too. What should I pull onto the counter before I open anything?

Keep the salad lightly coated and add a narrow dressing stripe along one side of the plate. For the soup, set out 1 1/2 pounds cubed beef stew meat, 2 cups water, 1 small chopped onion, 1 (28 ounce) can crushed tomatoes, plus the mixed vegetables, potatoes, bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil.
The slow cooker insert is clean, and the beef is still wrapped. Do I need to brown it first, or does it go in as-is?
For this recipe, place the cubed beef stew meat directly into the slow cooker. Spread it out a bit so the other ingredients can settle around it.
Beef is in the insert. The onion is chopped pretty fine, and I have the water measured.
Pour the 2 cups water over the beef, then scatter in the chopped onion so it starts mixing into the liquid.
I like that salad plating; that's exactly what I wanted for the dressing. The water and onion are in now—should the crushed tomatoes go next?
Yes, open the 1 (28 ounce) can of crushed tomatoes and pour it in slowly over the beef and onion to avoid splashing.
The tomatoes are in, but they're sitting in one thick mound. Should I stir now or wait until the vegetables are added?
Give it a gentle stir now just to loosen the tomatoes, then add the mixed vegetables and potatoes and stir again so they're distributed through the slow cooker.

Dry mixture is ready. I've got the oil and milk beside the bowl—do they go in separately?
Add the oil and milk all at once to the flour mixture rather than gradually. That helps you stir the dough briefly instead of overworking it.
What texture am I looking for when I stir it? I don't want to make it tough.
Stir lightly with a fork just until the dough comes together. Stop as soon as you don't see loose dry flour; it should look gathered and soft, not heavily mixed or smooth.
I pulled up BBQ Chicken Wings. Can you guide the first few moves? I'm starting by setting out the sauces.
Absolutely. For the marinade, measure out 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce and 1 cup oyster sauce into reach, since those make up the base.
I've got those two on the counter. What other measured ingredients should I pull out before I dirty the bowl?
Add 1/4 cup soy sauce and 1/4 cup ketchup to your lineup. You'll also need garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar for the bowl.
Large mixing bowl is ready. Do I just combine everything before the wings go in?
Yes. In the large bowl, stir together the teriyaki sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar until the marinade looks evenly mixed.
The marinade looks smooth and glossy. Should the chicken wings go straight into that bowl?
Put the chicken wings into the bowl and turn them so they're well coated. Cover the bowl tightly before refrigerating.
How long should they sit in the fridge? I'm trying to plan whether to cook tonight or tomorrow.
Let the wings marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight. Overnight is great if you want the flavor to soak in more deeply.
They've marinated overnight, and I'm ready to grill. What setting should I use?
Preheat the grill for low heat. Give it time to settle there so the wings can cook more gently instead of scorching right away.
Before I put the wings on, should I do anything to the grate to keep the sauce from sticking?
Yes, lightly oil the grill grate just before adding the wings. That will help the coated chicken release more easily as it cooks.
I'm ready to cook Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a pot out and want to follow it closely.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 recipe Fast Chicken Soup Base, 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, 2 medium zucchini diced, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
I have the soup base ready to start, and the tortellini is still in the fridge. Should I dice the zucchini before heating anything?

Yes, dice the 2 medium zucchini now so everything can go in smoothly once the soup is simmering. Open the 14.5-ounce can of diced tomatoes too, but don't drain it unless your soup base is already thinner than you want.
Zucchini is diced and the tomatoes are open. How should the soup base look before I add the rest?
Prepare the Fast Chicken Soup Base fully, then set it over medium heat. You're looking for it to come up to a gentle simmer, with small bubbles breaking the surface rather than a hard boil.
It's bubbling lightly around the edges now. Do I add the tortellini straight from the package?

Yes. Add the 9-ounce package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini straight in, along with the diced tomatoes, the diced zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil. Stir gently so the tortellini doesn't stick together.
Everything is in the pot. The simmer slowed down after adding the cold tortellini and vegetables.
That's normal. Let it come back to a gentle simmer, then keep it there. Avoid a rolling boil so the tortellini stays intact and the zucchini cooks without turning mushy.
Once it's simmering again, how long should I cook it, and what texture am I checking for?

Simmer for 10-20 minutes, until the tortellini are tender and the zucchini is softened but still holding its shape. Start checking near 10 minutes, especially since refrigerated tortellini can cook quickly.
It's been about 12 minutes. The tortellini look plump, and the zucchini is tender when I press it with a spoon.
That sounds ready. Give the soup a final gentle stir, then serve it hot. If it sits a few minutes before serving, keep the heat low so the tortellini don't overcook.

No, paint them before baking. Have the unbaked cookies ready on the baking sheet so you can brush the color on once the paint is mixed.
They're cut out and on the tray. How do I mix the paint without making it too thin?
Pour the 2 tablespoons evaporated milk into the small bowl, add the 4 drops red food coloring, and stir until the color looks even throughout.

Give it a few more gentle stirs, scraping around the sides and bottom of the bowl. It should look like evenly tinted milk.

Dip the brush lightly and tap off any excess against the bowl. Then paint a thin layer onto the unbaked cookies so the designs don't puddle.
