Use a lighter touch and reload the brush with a small amount of paint. Try gliding over the surface rather than pressing into the cookie dough.

Once the paint is on the cookies, bake them according to your cookie dough recipe. Rinse the brush and bowl soon after, since the milk and food coloring can dry on them.

After the steaks have had their skillet time, stir in the garlic and wine, keeping the pan over the heat.

Use a mixer or beat firmly by hand for 3 minutes, until the batter looks evenly combined and there are no obvious dry pockets.
The batter is smooth after 3 minutes. Do I need to do anything else before it goes in the pan?
Give the bowl one final scrape from the bottom and sides, then pour the batter into the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan and spread it evenly.

Put the medium saucepan over medium heat, then add the 2 tablespoons olive oil.

Add the mushrooms, green onions, crushed garlic, and cayenne pepper together, then stir so everything gets coated in the oil.

For this batch of Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs, cook the mixture for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mushrooms and onions are tender.

Let it cook until the vegetables are tender at the 10-minute mark; a little moisture is fine, but the mixture should look softened and cooked through.

Take the chicken out of the marinade, letting excess marinade drip back into the bowl so the coating will cling better.

Use a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the 1/4 cup butter, 1/3 cup maple syrup, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, along with the ginger, lemon juice, and vanilla.

Give it an occasional stir so the butter blends smoothly with the maple syrup and spices. Keep it over medium heat until the mixture comes to a boil.

Let it reach a boil, then take it off the heat carefully. You're looking for the mixture to be hot and combined before it goes over the apples.

Drizzle the hot mixture equally over the apples, aiming some into the cored centers and some over the tops so each apple gets a share of the maple-cinnamon sauce.

Make sure the apples are spaced in the 9x13 inch baking dish and that the syrup mixture is distributed fairly evenly. Then they're ready to bake in the preheated 350 degrees F oven.
I'm making Asian Turkey Burgers and want to prep everything before I start mixing. What should I set out?

Yes, chop the onion finely so it blends into the patties instead of leaving large pieces. Add it to the bowl with the egg white, soy sauce, and dry bread crumbs.

Go ahead and combine those ingredients in the bowl until the egg white and soy sauce are worked through the bread crumbs and onion.
The mixture looks evenly damp. How do I add the turkey without making the burgers tough?
Crumble the turkey over the mixture, then mix just until combined. Use a light hand and stop as soon as everything is distributed.
It's mixed, but a little sticky. What shape am I aiming for?
Shape the mixture into four patties. Try to keep them even in thickness so they cook at the same rate in the skillet.

Use nonstick cooking spray on the nonstick skillet. Once the pan is coated, place the patties in without crowding them.

Cook the patties until they're no longer pink in the center. Turn them as needed so both sides cook evenly, then serve the Asian Turkey Burgers hot.

I'm making Basil Burgers on the outdoor grill. Can you talk me through what to set out before I start?

Absolutely. Put out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil or enough to suit your taste, 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt, and some pepper. You'll also want a mixing bowl, something to shape 4 patties on, oil for the grill grate, and a thermometer if you have one.

Yes, go ahead and preheat the outdoor grill for high heat while you season and shape the burgers.

Add the Worcestershire sauce, dried basil, garlic salt, and pepper to the ground beef in the bowl. Mix gently just until the seasonings are spread through the meat so the burgers don't get tough.

Divide the mixture into 4 portions and form them into burger patties. Press them together firmly enough to hold, but don't pack them too hard.

Lightly oil the grill grate. That helps the patties release when you turn them.

I flipped them once. What temperature am I aiming for before serving?
Cook the burgers to an internal temperature of 160 degrees F, which is 70 degrees C, or to your desired doneness. Let them come off the grill once they hit that mark, then serve them right away.

Aim for an evenly moistened mixture where the bread and corn bread still have some shape. It should be mixed, not mashed.

Add the remaining ingredients called for in your recipe, then mix well until they're evenly distributed through the rice dressing.

Just set the bag aside for the moment, keeping it upright so the popcorn doesn't spill.

You're aiming for an even coating that clings without crushing the popcorn, with the peanuts distributed throughout before it goes onto the greased cookie sheets.

Pour the 2 tablespoons cooking oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat. Let it warm enough to move easily across the bottom of the pot.

Yes—stir a small amount of the chili into the warm oil briefly, just until fragrant, then keep moving so it doesn't scorch.

Add the chicken to the pot and spread the pieces out as well as you can. Brown them on all sides, giving the 1 inch pieces enough contact with the pot to pick up color.

I want to make Gingered Mango Salsa. Can you talk me through getting it ready for serving?
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl and measure 1 cup chopped peeled mango, 1/4 cup chopped red onion, 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro, and 1/4 cup lime juice.
The mango is peeled and chopped. Should the onion and cilantro go in the same bowl with it?
Yes, put the mango, red onion, and minced fresh cilantro into the bowl together. Try to keep the pieces small enough that each scoop gets a little of everything.

Pour in the full 1/4 cup lime juice, then gently stir until the mango, onion, cilantro, and juice are evenly combined.

That's fine for this salsa. Give it another gentle fold so the lime juice coats the ingredients, then let the bowl sit so the flavors can come together.
How long should it sit, and does it need to be covered?
Let it stand for 30 minutes before serving. If it's sitting on the counter, loosely cover the bowl to keep it protected while it rests.
I'm planning to serve it with chips. Should I stir it again after the wait?
Yes, after the 30 minutes, give it a quick stir so the lime juice redistributes through the mango, onion, and cilantro.
Anything I should check before I put it out?
Check that everything is evenly combined and bright-looking, then transfer it to a serving bowl or leave it in the mixing bowl with a spoon for serving.
I want to make Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes. Can you talk me through what to get ready on the counter?
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 pounds of new potatoes, already cut into wedges, plus 4 tablespoons butter. You'll also want a skillet for melting the butter and something to toss or coat the potatoes in.
The potatoes are wedged and the butter is measured. What seasonings should I pull out?
Grab 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, along with salt and pepper to taste. Keep them close to the stove so they can go straight into the melted butter.
Got it. Should the oven be heating while I work with the butter?
Yes, bring the oven up to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). That way it's ready once the potatoes are coated.
Oven is set. For the skillet, how hot should it be before the butter goes in?
Use a hot skillet, then add the 4 tablespoons butter and let it melt. Keep an eye on it so it melts evenly rather than sitting in one spot.
The butter is melted and starting to smell good. Do I season it in the pan?
Yes. Stir the fresh rosemary into the melted butter, then add salt and pepper to taste. Give it a quick stir so the rosemary is distributed through the butter.
The rosemary is mixed in. Should I add the potato wedges directly now?
Add the potato wedges and coat them evenly with the melted butter mixture. Turn them over well so all the cut sides get some butter and seasoning.
They look glossy, but a few pieces still seem plain on one side. Is that okay?
Give those pieces one more turn through the rosemary butter until the potatoes are evenly coated. Once they're coated all over, they're ready for the preheated 450 degrees F oven.

I want to make Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon on the grill. What should I set out before I get started?
Set out a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank, 6 salmon fillets that are 4 ounces each, 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, and 1 large red onion, chopped.
I found the cedar plank, but it is dry. Does it need any prep before the salmon goes on?
Yes. Submerge the untreated cedar plank completely in water so it can soak through before it goes near the grill.
How long should I leave the plank in the water?
Let it soak approximately 12 hours, or overnight. That gives the cedar time to absorb enough water for grilling.
The plank has soaked overnight, and I have the salmon fillets ready. Should I do anything with the grill yet?
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat while you keep the soaked plank nearby and ready to place on the grate.
While the grill heats, should the onion and olive oil be measured now?
Yes, have the 1 large chopped red onion ready and keep the 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil measured so everything is close at hand when you assemble the salmon.
The grill is hot. What happens to the cedar plank first?
Place the prepared soaked plank on the grill, then sprinkle the plank with coarse salt.
I've salted the plank. Is this a good point to keep the salmon and toppings close by?
Exactly. Keep the 6 salmon fillets, olive oil, and chopped red onion within reach so you can continue smoothly once the cedar plank is positioned on the high-heat grill.
I want to make California Chicken tonight. Can you talk me through what to set out and when to start cooking?

Absolutely. Put out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1 pinch salt. You'll also want a skillet ready, plus pepper nearby for seasoning at the end.
The chicken breasts are on a plate and I have the oil, onion powder, salt, and pepper next to the stove. Does the oven need to be on?
Yes, get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready while you brown the chicken.
Oven is heating. Should I season the chicken before it goes in the skillet?
You can sprinkle the chicken with the 1/2 teaspoon onion powder now so it hits the hot oil with some flavor. Keep the salt and pepper for adjusting to taste later.

Warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in the skillet until it looks loose and lightly shimmery, then add the chicken breasts. Lay them in carefully so they make good contact with the pan.
They're in the skillet and sizzling. Do I just leave them alone?
Let them cook, turning as needed, for about 15 minutes total or until the outside is browned and the chicken is just about done.
After 15 minutes they're browned, but I want to make sure the texture is right before I stop.

They should look browned on the outside and nearly cooked through, with the meat firming up rather than feeling soft or raw. Since the oven is already at 350 degrees F, you can keep the heat plan ready while you check doneness.
Okay, they look just about done. What should I do before serving?
Season the chicken with the pinch of salt and add pepper to taste. Let it sit briefly so the juices settle, then serve the California Chicken while it's hot.

I want to make Baked Apple Oatmeal. Can you talk me through what to put on the counter and when to start baking?

Absolutely. Set out 4 cups milk, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, 2 teaspoons butter or margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need a saucepan, a greased 2-qt. casserole dish, and your remaining oatmeal ingredients ready to stir in.
I've got the milk, brown sugar, butter, and salt measured. Does the casserole dish need to be greased before I heat anything?
Yes, go ahead and grease the 2-qt. casserole now so it's ready. That way, once the oatmeal mixture is combined, you can spoon it straight in without pausing.
Dish is greased. I'm at the stove with the saucepan—what goes in there?
Pour the milk into the saucepan, then add the packed brown sugar, butter or margarine, salt, and cinnamon. Warm it gently, stirring so the sugar dissolves and the butter melts into the milk.
The butter is almost melted and the milk looks sweetened. Should I let it boil?
No need to boil it. Just heat it until everything is blended and warm, then take care with the next mixing step so the oatmeal mixture stays gently combined.
Okay, it's warm and smooth. I still have the remaining ingredients waiting—how do I add them?
Add the remaining ingredients to the warm milk mixture and mix gently. Fold rather than beat, just enough to distribute everything evenly.
It's mixed and looks loose but even. Do I pour or scoop it into the dish?
Spoon it into the greased 2-qt. casserole, spreading it into an even layer so it bakes consistently.
The casserole is filled. What oven setting and bake time should I use?
For this batch of Baked Apple Oatmeal, cover the casserole and bake it at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes. When the time is up, let it sit briefly before serving so the oatmeal can settle.
I want to make Fried Chicken Tenders. Can you help me get the breading station set up without making a mess?
Absolutely. Set out three shallow bowls if you have them. Put 1 cup all-purpose flour in one bowl, and keep 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs nearby for the second bowl.
I've got the flour bowl ready and the bread crumbs measured. Do the spices go into the flour or the crumbs?
Mix the spices into the bread crumbs: add 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper to the separate shallow bowl with the Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs.
The crumb mixture is stirred together. What should I use for the wet bowl?
Use a small bowl for the eggs and water. Beat them together enough that the mixture is smooth and easy for the chicken to pass through.
Okay, I have chicken pieces on a plate. What order should I coat them in?
Work with one piece at a time: coat the chicken in the flour first, then dip it into the egg-and-water mixture, then cover it with the seasoned bread crumbs.
The first piece has some bare spots after the crumbs. Should I press the coating on?
Yes, gently press the bread crumbs onto the chicken so the coating sticks, especially around the edges. Then set that coated piece aside before starting the next one.
Should the bowls stay close together, or is it better to spread them out?
Keep them in a line so the motion is simple: flour bowl, egg-and-water bowl, then seasoned bread crumb bowl, with a clean plate or tray at the end for the coated chicken.
All the tenders are breaded and waiting on the tray. Is there anything else from this prep before cooking them?
That completes the breading prep for this recipe: each chicken piece has gone through the flour, the eggs and water, and the seasoned bread crumbs, then been set aside.
I want to put together the Easy Bake Oven Cookie Mix. What should I set on the counter before I start?

Set out 1 1/2 cups quick-cooking oats, 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 teaspoon baking soda, and 3/4 cup packed brown sugar. You'll also need a medium bowl, a spoon, shortening, and re-sealable bags or containers for storing the mix.
I've got the oats and flour measured. Should the brown sugar be loose or packed into the measuring cup?
Pack the brown sugar into the cup so you have 3/4 cup packed brown sugar. Once it's measured, add it to the bowl with the oats, flour, and baking soda.
Everything dry is in the medium bowl. Do I need to sift it or just stir?
Just stir the oats, flour, baking soda, and brown sugar together until the baking soda and sugar are evenly distributed through the mixture.
The dry mix looks combined, but there are a few little brown sugar clumps. Is that okay?
Break up any obvious brown sugar clumps with the spoon as you stir. It doesn't need to be perfectly powdery, but you want the dry ingredients mixed evenly before adding the shortening.
For Easy Bake Oven Cookie Mix, i'm ready for the shortening. What texture am I aiming for when I cut it in?
Cut in the shortening until the mixture resembles cornmeal. Use a pastry cutter, fork, or your fingertips, and keep working it through the oats and flour mixture.
It's sandy now, but I can still see a couple small pieces of shortening.
Keep cutting it in a little longer. There should be no lumps of shortening left, so scrape around the bottom and sides of the bowl and work those pieces into the mix.
That looks even now. How do I portion it for storage?
Measure 1/2 cup of the mixture into each re-sealable bag or container. Seal them well, label them as Easy Bake Oven Cookie Mix if you like, and store the portions until you're ready to use them.

I want to make Banana Orange Bars, but I'd like to get the batter organized before I start mixing. What should I put on the counter?
Set out 2 cups mashed ripe bananas, 1 2/3 cups sugar, 1 cup vegetable oil, and 4 eggs. You'll also want a mixing bowl, a beater or sturdy whisk, and a greased 15-in. baking pan ready for the batter.

Beat the bananas, sugar, oil, and eggs until they're well blended. It doesn't need to be perfectly silky, especially because bananas can leave a little texture, but the eggs and oil should be fully incorporated.

Exactly. Fold until the dry ingredients are well mixed into the banana mixture and there aren't visible pockets of floury dry mix. Scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl once or twice.

Make sure the batter is level in the 15-in. pan and the corners are filled. Wipe any drips from the rim, then it's ready for the next baking stage according to your recipe.

Both slices are open on the plate. Which spread goes where?
Spread the 1 tablespoon mayonnaise over one slice of toast, then spread the 2 teaspoons Dijon-style mustard over the other slice. Try to cover close to the edges so each bite has some sauce.
The spreads are on. I have 3 slices of smoked turkey breast—should I fold them or lay them flat?
Either works, but folding the 3 turkey slices gives the sandwich a little more height. Arrange the turkey on one side of the bread, keeping it mostly within the crust so it closes neatly.
Turkey is on the mayo side. I'm about to add guacamole, but I don't want it sliding everywhere.
Spread the guacamole directly over the turkey in a fairly even layer. Keep it a little thinner at the edges so it doesn't squeeze out when you close the sandwich.
That looks stable. I still have salad greens, bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese waiting.
Pile those on over the guacamole: add the salad greens, then the bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese. Press them lightly into the guacamole so the stack holds together.
Everything is stacked. Any trick to closing and serving it without making a mess?

Bring the mustard-coated slice down over the filled side, press gently with your palm, and tuck in any loose greens or sprouts. Slice the Awesome Turkey Sandwich in half if you want an easier grip, then serve right away while the toast still has some crunch.
I'm about to start Chicken Eileen. Can you talk me through the prep? Can you help me get set up before I start handling the chicken?

Absolutely. Set out 1 (6 ounce) package of herb-seasoned dry bread stuffing mix, 8 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, and 16 medium slices of mozzarella cheese. You'll also want a baking dish, something for preparing the stuffing, paper towels, and a way to pound the chicken evenly.
I've got the stuffing mix and the chicken out. The mozzarella is still in the fridge—does it need to be ready now?
Yes, bring out the mozzarella before assembly so it's easy to layer. You'll use 16 medium slices total, with a slice going onto each chicken breast before the stuffing.
Okay, cheese is out. Should I preheat the oven before I make the stuffing?
Go ahead and heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). That way it's ready once the chicken is assembled.
The oven is heating. I'm opening the stuffing mix now—how should I prepare it?
Prepare the herb-seasoned dry bread stuffing mix according to the package directions. Once it's made, keep it nearby so you can scoop it onto the chicken.
Stuffing is done and smells good. I'm ready to work with the chicken breasts.

Wash the chicken, pat it dry well with paper towels, then pound each breast half out to about a 1/2 inch thickness. Try to keep the thickness even so the pieces roll or fold more neatly around the filling.
They're flattened to about 1/2 inch. Do I put the mozzarella or the stuffing down first?
Place a slice of mozzarella cheese on each chicken breast first, then add a scoop of the prepared stuffing on top of the cheese.
I've got cheese and stuffing on the chicken. Is there anything else from the recipe before it goes in the dish?

That covers the listed assembly for Chicken Eileen: each of the 8 chicken breast halves should have mozzarella and prepared stuffing layered on it. Arrange them in the baking dish for the next cooking step from your recipe source.
I'm making Chocolate Cheesecake II and want to get the crust started. What should I pull out before I preheat anything?
Set out 1 1/2 cups chocolate cookie crumbs, 2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/4 cup melted butter, and 1/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips. You'll also need a 9 inch springform pan and a small mixing bowl.
I have the crumbs and sugar measured, but my butter is still solid. Should I melt the 1/4 cup now?
Yes, melt the 1/4 cup butter so it can blend evenly with the crumbs and sugar. While that cools slightly, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Oven is heating to 350, and the melted butter is ready. Do I need to do anything to the pan before mixing?
Lightly grease the 9 inch springform pan so the crust releases more easily later. A thin, even coating on the bottom and sides is enough.
The pan is greased. For the crumb mixture, should the chocolate chips go in with it?

For this crust step, mix the 1 1/2 cups chocolate wafer or cookie crumbs with the 2 tablespoons sugar and the melted butter in a small bowl. Keep the 1/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips set aside for now.
The mixture looks like damp sand and clumps when I squeeze it. Is that the texture I want?
That texture is right. It should hold together when pressed, without looking greasy or loose.
How high should I press it up the springform pan?
Press the crumb mixture firmly across the bottom and about 1 1/2 inch up the sides of the prepared 9 inch springform pan. Use the bottom of a measuring cup if you want a flatter, tighter crust.
The crust is packed in, but the top edge is a little uneven. Is that a problem?
A slightly uneven edge is fine. Just make sure the bottom is compact and the sides are pressed in well enough to hold their shape before you continue with the cheesecake.
I'm making Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I. Can you help me get set up at the counter?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup shortening, 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also want your mixing bowls, measuring cups, and a mixer or sturdy spoon ready.
The shortening and both sugars are measured. Should the eggs go in right away?
They'll go in with the creaming step. Before mixing, get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's hot when the dough is ready.
Oven is heating. I have one large bowl out—do I need another bowl too?
Yes, keep a separate bowl nearby for the dry ingredients. In the large bowl, start by thoroughly creaming together the shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla.
I'm using the mixer now. What texture am I looking for before I stop creaming?
Mix until the shortening, sugars, eggs, and vanilla look well combined and fairly smooth, with no big streaks of shortening left.
That looks blended. What goes in the second bowl?
Use the second bowl for the dry ingredients. Mix those together there, but leave out the candy coated milk chocolate pieces for now.
Dry ingredients are stirred together, and the candies are still on the side. How do I combine the bowls without making a mess?
Add the dry mixture into the creamed mixture gradually, mixing as you go. Scrape the sides of the bowl so everything comes together evenly.
The dough is coming together and I don't see dry patches. Is that mixed enough?

Yes—once the dry ingredients are fully added to the creamed mixture and mixed well, you're at the end of the listed steps. Fold in the candies after that if your full recipe calls for them before scooping and baking.

source_seed.recipe_title: Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I

messages.content: I'm making Armadillo Eggs and want to get organized before touching the peppers. What should I pull out?
Set out 24 jalapeno peppers, 1 pound sausage, 2 cups all-purpose baking mix, and 1 (16 ounce) package of shredded Cheddar cheese. You'll also want a medium baking sheet ready.
I have the jalapenos and sausage on the counter. Should the oven be heating while I prep?
Yes, get the oven warming to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), so it can come up to temperature while you work on the jalapenos.
The oven is set. Do I need to do anything to the baking sheet before the peppers go near it?
Lightly grease the medium baking sheet. A thin, even coating is enough to help keep things from sticking later.
Done. The jalapenos are washed and dried; how do I start cutting them without making a mess?
Cut a slit in each jalapeno pepper lengthwise. Keep the pepper mostly intact so it can hold the filling later.
Some of the peppers are narrow. Should I cut them all the way open or just enough to reach inside?
Just enough to reach inside. The goal is a slit in each jalapeno pepper, not two separate halves.
I've slit a few, and the seeds are right there. What should I do with the inside?
Remove and discard the seeds and pulp from each jalapeno. A small spoon or the tip of a knife can help scrape them out cleanly.
All right, I'll keep a bowl nearby for the seeds and pulp. Anything I should double-check before moving on?

Make sure all 24 jalapenos have a slit, the seeds and pulp are discarded, the medium baking sheet is lightly greased, and the oven is holding at 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Keep the sausage, baking mix, and shredded Cheddar nearby for the next stage.
I'm making Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms. Can you talk me through the prep before I put the pan on?

Absolutely. Set out 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, 2 cups diced Broccoflower, 2 cups chopped assorted wild mushrooms, and 1/2 white onion, chopped. You'll also want your garlic ready, plus rice, chicken stock, nutmeg, herbs, salt, and pepper for the risotto part.
The Broccoflower is diced and the mushrooms are chopped. Should the onion go in with them or later?
Keep the chopped onion with the Broccoflower, mushrooms, and garlic. They all sauté together in the butter, so having them near the stove will make that part smooth.
I've got a wide pan out. How hot should I start it, and what goes in first?
Use medium heat and melt the butter in the pan. Once it's melted and coating the bottom, add the Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic.
They're in the pan now. How long am I cooking this mixture?
Sauté the vegetables and garlic for 10 minutes, stirring now and then so the mushrooms soften, the onion turns fragrant, and the Broccoflower starts to get tender without scorching.
The pan has some moisture from the mushrooms. Is that okay before I start the rice?
Yes, that's normal. When the 10 minutes are up, remove the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic from the pan and set them aside.
The vegetables are in a bowl. Do I clean the pan before cooking the rice?

No need to clean it. Use the same pan so the rice picks up the flavor left behind. Start cooking the rice there, adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time and stirring until each cup is well incorporated before adding the next.
The stock is mostly absorbed and the rice tastes tender. What should I stir in at the end?

Stir the sautéed Broccoflower, wild mushrooms, onion, and garlic back in if they're not already combined, then add nutmeg and herbs. Season with salt and pepper, give it a final stir, and serve while the risotto is creamy and warm.
I'm making Chicken with Vegetables in the slow cooker. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start loading it?
Absolutely. Have 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms ready, plus the chicken: 4 drumsticks with the skin removed and 4 thighs with the skin removed.
The mushrooms are sliced, and the drumsticks and thighs are skinned. What vegetables should I prep next?
Slice 4 celery ribs. You'll also want the zucchini, carrots, and onion ready to add with the liquids and seasonings.
Celery is sliced, and I've got the other vegetables nearby. Do the mushrooms go in before the celery?
Yes. Put the sliced mushrooms into the slow cooker, then add the chicken pieces on top or nestled in with them.
The chicken and mushrooms are in. Should I layer the celery over the meat or stir it in?
Add the celery now along with the zucchini, carrots, and onion. It's fine if they sit around and over the chicken; the slow cooker will soften everything as it cooks.
Vegetables are in. I still have tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper on the counter.
Pour in the tomato juice and broth, then add the garlic, paprika, and pepper. Try to distribute the seasonings across the top so the flavor spreads as it cooks.
Everything is in the cooker. What setting and timing should I use?
Here, cover the slow cooker and cook on low for 5 hours, or until the meat juices run clear.
When it's done, what's the best way to handle the chicken and vegetables?
Lift out the chicken and vegetables carefully and keep them warm until you're ready to serve.
I want to make Banana Orange Bars, but I'd like to get my ingredients and pan sorted before mixing. What should I pull out?
Set out 2 cups mashed ripe bananas, 1 2/3 cups sugar, 1 cup vegetable oil, and 4 eggs. You'll also need a mixing bowl and a greased 15-in. baking pan for the batter.
The bananas are mashed and the sugar is measured. Do the oil and eggs go in with those right away?
Yes. Add the bananas, sugar, vegetable oil, and eggs to the mixing bowl together, then beat them until the mixture looks well blended.
What texture am I aiming for after beating it—totally smooth or just combined?
Aim for well blended. It can still show a little banana texture, but the eggs and oil should be fully incorporated so the mixture looks even.
I'm at that stage. The recipe mentions dry ingredients, but I only have the wet ingredients listed here—how should I handle that part?
Use whatever dry ingredients are part of your recipe, combine them separately, then fold them into the banana mixture until everything is well mixed. Fold gently so you don't overwork the batter.
The batter is mixed. Should I prepare the pan before adding anything else?
Make sure the 15-in. baking pan is greased. Once it's ready, pour the banana batter into the pan and spread it evenly into the corners.
There's also a note that says "spread over bars." When does that happen?
That sounds like a topping or spread added over the bars. If you have that component prepared, spread it over the bars as directed after the base is in the pan.
Everything is in the greased pan now. Any last check before it goes in to bake?
Check that the batter is level in the 15-in. pan and that any spread is even across the top. You're ready to bake according to the rest of your recipe's baking directions.
I'm making Eggnog Blend and want to do the stovetop part carefully. What should I set out before I turn on the burner?
Set out 4 cups half-and-half, 1 cup white sugar, 11 beaten egg yolks, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also want a saucepan, a whisk, and something to chill the mixture in overnight.
The half-and-half and sugar are measured. Should the pan be hot before they go in?
Keep the saucepan over low heat, then stir the half-and-half and sugar together in the pan. Low heat matters here because the mixture will later take the egg yolks without scrambling them.
It's warming slowly and the sugar seems to be dissolving. When do the yolks go in?
Whisk in the 11 beaten egg yolks once the dairy-sugar mixture is warm but not boiling. Keep whisking as it cooks so it turns into a light custard.
What should I watch for so I don't overcook it?

Look for a lightly thickened custard texture, not a bubbling boil. Do not boil it; if it starts steaming hard or threatening to bubble, lower the heat or briefly move the pan off the burner while whisking.
It's lightly thickened now and coats the whisk a little. Do I take it off right away?
For Eggnog Blend, yes, remove it from the heat now. Let it cool, then transfer it to the refrigerator and chill it overnight.
Should I stir in the vanilla before it chills or wait until tomorrow?
Wait until the mixture is chilled. After the overnight chill, stir in the vanilla extract along with the cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream.
So tomorrow I'm just mixing everything into the cold custard base?
Exactly. Keep the custard cold, stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream until blended, then serve it chilled.
I'm making Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style. Can you help me get set up before I start cutting anything?

Absolutely. Set out 1 spaghetti squash, 1 chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 (14 ounce) cans stewed tomatoes. You'll also want a baking sheet, cooking spray, a sturdy knife, and a spoon for scraping out the seeds.
The squash is halved lengthwise and seeded, and the onion is already chopped. Should the oven be on yet?
Yes, bring the oven up to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), so it's ready by the time the squash is on the pan.
Oven is heating. I have the baking sheet out—do I need parchment or just the spray?
For this recipe, just coat the baking sheet with a thin layer of cooking spray. That will help keep the cut sides of the squash from sticking.
The pan is sprayed. Which way should the squash halves face?
Place the squash halves cut side down on the sprayed baking sheet. Try to keep them stable so the flat cut surfaces are touching the pan evenly.
They're on the sheet cut side down. What should I do with the tomatoes, onion, and garlic right now?
Keep the chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and the 2 cans of stewed tomatoes nearby for the lasagna-style part later. The recipe's baking step starts by softening the squash first.
Got it. How long does the squash bake, and what texture am I looking for?
Bake it in the preheated oven for 35 minutes, or until a knife can be easily inserted into the squash. That easy knife slide is the doneness check.
If the knife still catches after 35 minutes, should I pull it anyway or give it more time?
Give it a little more time if needed, using the recipe's cue as your guide: the squash is ready when a knife can be easily inserted.
I want to make A 1 Chicken Soup. Can you help me get set up before I start heating the pot?

Absolutely. Put a large pot on the stove and set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 2 skinless chicken leg quarters, 1/2 cup chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need the chicken bouillon for the boiling step.
The pot is ready, and the chicken leg quarters are out. Should I add the oil before the chicken?
Yes. Add the 2 tablespoons vegetable oil to the large pot and warm it over medium heat, then lay in the chicken pieces.
They're in the oil now. What am I looking for before I move on?
Let the chicken brown on both sides. Give it enough contact with the pot so it picks up color before you turn it.
Both sides have some browning. I have the chopped onion measured at 1/2 cup.
Stir the onion into the pot with the browned chicken and cook it for 2 minutes more.
The onion has softened a bit after those 2 minutes. Do I pour in all the water now?
Yes, pour in the 2 quarts water, then add the chicken bouillon and bring the pot up to a boil.
It's starting to bubble around the edges. Should I wait for a full boil?
Let it reach a clear boil, with steady bubbling across the pot, before you lower the heat.
It's boiling steadily now. How do I handle the simmer so the soup finishes right?
Reduce the heat until the soup is simmering gently, then let it cook for 45 minutes.
I'm making Fresh Apple Walnut Cake and want to get the dry ingredients and pan ready before I deal with the apples.
Great plan. Set out 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a 9x13 inch pan ready.
The flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt are on the counter. Should the oven be warming while I measure?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready when the cake batter is assembled.
Oven is heating. For the pan, do I just spray it, or does this one need more prep?
Grease and flour the 9x13 inch pan. Make sure the corners and sides are coated so the cake releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. I've got a mixing bowl out—what goes in there first?
Sift together the 3 cups flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt into the bowl. That helps distribute the leavening and spice evenly.
The dry mix looks even, but a little cinnamon is clumped on the sifter. Should I press it through?
Yes, gently press any small cinnamon clumps through the sifter or break them up with a spoon, then give the sifted dry ingredients a light stir.
Dry ingredients are done. I'm moving to the apples now—what should I combine them with?
Combine the apples with the white sugar, then set that mixture aside. Letting it sit briefly helps the apples start releasing some juice.
The apples and white sugar are mixed and resting. Anything I should clean up or keep nearby before continuing?
Keep the sifted dry ingredients, the sugared apples, and the prepared 9x13 inch pan within reach. You can clear away the flour bag, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt now if they've all been measured.
I want to make Famous Caramel Cookie Bars. Can you talk me through setting everything up before I start melting anything?

Absolutely. Set out 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 individually wrapped caramels that have been unwrapped, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a baking sheet or tray and a small saucepan.
The cookies are on the counter, but I'm not sure how to arrange them on the tray.
Place the shortbread cookies flat on the baking sheet or tray in a single layer, leaving just a little space between them so you can spoon caramel over each one without them sticking together.
All 40 cookies fit on the tray. Should the caramel go straight into the pan by itself?
Put the 35 unwrapped caramels into the small saucepan with the 1/4 cup water. Keep the heat at medium-low so the caramel melts gently instead of scorching.
It's starting to soften around the edges. How often should I stir?
Stir frequently as it melts, scraping the bottom and sides of the saucepan so the caramel and water come together into a smooth mixture.
The caramel looks smooth now, but it's pretty warm and pourable.
That's the texture you want. Spoon a thin line of caramel over each shortbread cookie, working carefully so each cookie gets a neat strip rather than a thick puddle.
I've topped the cookies with caramel. Do the milk chocolate chips go on now?

This recipe's listed finishing step is to chill the cookies once the caramel is on them. Keep the 4 cups milk chocolate chips set aside unless you're planning an extra topping, because the provided directions don't include a chocolate step.
Got it. How long should I leave the tray in the refrigerator?
Place the cookies in the refrigerator until the caramel is set. Once the caramel feels firm enough to hold its shape, they're ready to serve or store.
I want to make Banana Bran Muffins. Can you talk me through setting up and mixing the batter?
Absolutely. Put your oven rack near the center and gather the main ingredients you listed: 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 3 mashed bananas, and 1/4 cup milk.
The butter is soft, and I mashed the bananas in a bowl. Should I get the pan ready before mixing?
Yes. get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it can come up to temperature while you work.
Oven is heating. I have a muffin pan, but I'm not sure whether to grease it or use liners.
Either works for this recipe: grease the muffin pan well, or line the cups with paper muffin liners if you want easier cleanup.
I'll use liners. For the bowl, do I start with the bananas or the butter?
Start with the butter and sugar. In a large mixing bowl, cream the 1/2 cup softened butter with the 1/2 cup brown sugar until the mixture looks lighter and fluffy.
It's looking pale and a bit airy now. How fluffy does it need to be?
That sounds right. It doesn't need to be whipped like frosting; just evenly blended, softened, and a little fluffy so the sugar is worked into the butter.
Okay, I still have the mashed bananas and the 1/4 cup milk beside me. Do they go in together?
Yes. Add the 3 mashed bananas and the 1/4 cup milk to the bowl. The recipe step also calls for adding vanilla and eggs here, so add those with the bananas and milk, then mix well.
The batter is coming together, though the banana makes it a little lumpy. Is that fine?

Yes, small banana lumps are fine for Banana Bran Muffins. Mix until everything is well combined, then you're ready to portion the batter into the prepared muffin pan once the oven reaches 375 degrees F.
I want to make Dads Flat Bread and I'm setting up the counter. What should I pull out first?
Set out 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast and 2 cups warm water, divided. Aim for the water to be 110 degrees to 115 degrees so the yeast can dissolve properly.
The yeast is out, and I'm checking the water temperature now. What other measured ingredients should be nearby?
Measure 1/3 cup sugar and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also want salt, rye or whole wheat flour, and all-purpose flour within reach for the dough mixing.
I have a large mixing bowl ready. How much of the warm water goes in with the yeast?
Pour 1/2 cup of the warm water into the large mixing bowl and dissolve the active dry yeast in it. Give it a gentle stir so there aren't dry clumps stuck to the bowl.
The yeast is dissolved and looks even. What goes into the bowl with it?
Add the sugar, vegetable oil, salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining warm water. Beat the mixture until it looks smooth.
It's smoothing out, but the dough still seems loose. Should I add more flour all at once?
Add the remaining all-purpose flour gradually, just enough to turn it into a soft dough. Stop when it holds together but still feels tender rather than stiff.
The dough is soft and pulling together. Do I flour the board heavily?
Lightly flour the surface so the dough won't stick, then turn the dough out onto it. Keep a little extra flour nearby for your hands if the dough feels tacky.
It's on the floured surface now. How long should I knead, and what texture am I looking for?
Knead until the dough is smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. It should feel springy and cohesive, not rough or shaggy.
Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks is on deck today. What should I do first? I've got the swordfish out and want to set up the marinade properly.
Absolutely. For the marinade, measure 3 tablespoons soy sauce and 1/2 cup vegetable oil into a medium bowl.
Those are in the bowl. I also have sherry and fresh ginger on the counter—how much of each goes in?
Add 2 tablespoons sherry and 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root. If your garlic is ready, add it with those, then whisk everything together until the mixture looks blended.
The ginger and garlic are mixed in, and the marinade looks smooth. What kind of bag should I use?
Use a large resealable bag, big enough for the swordfish steaks to sit in a single layer if possible. Pour the whisked marinade into the bag.
The marinade is in the bag. Should I add the fish carefully or just drop the steaks in?
Place the swordfish steaks into the bag gently so they don't splash marinade out. Press out some excess air, seal the bag, and shake or turn it to coat the steaks well.
They're coated, but some marinade is pooling at the bottom. Is that okay?
Yes, that's fine. Lay the sealed bag flat and turn it once or twice so the marinade spreads over the fish rather than staying in one corner.
I've got it lying flat. How long does it need in the refrigerator?
Refrigerate the bag and let the swordfish marinate at least 4 hours. Keep it chilled the whole time.
Should I do anything while it marinates, like turn the bag or prep cleanup?
If you think of it, flip the bag once during the 4 hours to keep the coating even. Wipe down any marinade drips and refrigerate the fish until you're ready for the next cooking step.
I want to make Asian Ginger Dressing. Can you guide me while I set up the ingredients?
Absolutely. Start by getting a 1 pint glass jar or something larger with a tight-fitting lid, since you'll be mixing and shaking the dressing right in it.
Jar is ready. I've minced 3 cloves of garlic—how much ginger should I prep?
Mince 2 tablespoons of fresh ginger root. Once that's ready, add both the garlic and ginger to the jar.
Done. I also have olive oil and rice vinegar out; what are the amounts?
Pour in 3/4 cup olive oil and 1/3 cup rice vinegar. The recipe also calls for soy sauce, honey, and water to go into the jar with them.
Everything is in the jar, including the honey. Should I stir it before heating?
No need to stir yet. Put the tight-fitting lid on and shake the jar well so the garlic, ginger, oil, vinegar, soy sauce, honey, and water start combining.
It's shaken, but the honey still looks a little settled at the bottom.
That's expected. Remove the lid, then microwave the jar for 1 minute—just long enough to dissolve the honey.
Lid is off, and I microwaved it for 1 minute. It's warm now.
Let it cool before serving. As it cools, the flavors will settle together and it'll be easier to handle safely.
Once it cools, do I shake it again or just pour it over the salad?
Shake it well again right before serving, then pour or spoon it over your salad, noodles, or vegetables.
I'm making Easy Pot Roast today. Can you guide me through it while I get set up?

Absolutely. You'll need a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast, 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. You'll also want a medium sized oven bag and whatever vegetables you plan to place around the meat.
I've got the roast, the soup mix, Worcestershire, and an oven bag. The water is measured too. What should I do before touching the meat?
get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it can come up to temperature while you prep the roast.
The oven is heating. Should the roast go straight into the bag as-is?
Before it goes in, score the roast on the top and sides with shallow cuts. Then place it into the medium sized oven bag.
Scored and in the bag. The cuts are shallow across the top and sides. What do I mix for the liquid?
Combine the 2 cups water, the 1 ounce package of dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. Stir them together, then pour that mixture over the roast in the bag.
The soup mixture is poured over the roast. I have carrots and potatoes ready—where do they go?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag so they sit in the seasoned liquid and cook alongside the roast.
They're tucked around it now. Should I try to cover the roast with vegetables or keep them mostly to the sides?
Keep them mostly around the sides rather than piled heavily on top, so the roast stays settled in the bag and the liquid can coat it well.
Got it. Anything else to check before I close the bag and put it in the oven?

Make sure the roast is in the medium sized oven bag, the water-soup-Worcestershire mixture is poured over it, and the vegetables are arranged around the meat. Once the oven reaches 350 degrees F/175 degrees C, it's ready to go in.
I want to get Chili For Two right. What should I handle first? I've got a small saucepan ready.

In this Chili For Two step, set out 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can of chili beans. Keep the beans undrained since the liquid goes into the chili.
The beef is thawed and the onion is chopped. Should I heat the pan before adding everything?
Yes, put the saucepan over medium heat, then add the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic together. Cook them while breaking up the beef and stirring so the garlic doesn't sit in one spot.
How do I know when the beef mixture is ready to drain?
Cook it until the meat is no longer pink and the onion has softened a bit. Once it reaches that point, carefully drain off the excess fat from the saucepan.
It's drained. Do the chili beans go in with the liquid from the can?
They do. Stir in the entire 15.5 ounce can of chili beans, undrained, so the sauce and beans heat together with the beef mixture.
The beans are mixed in. Should I leave the heat at medium?
Keep it on medium just long enough to bring the chili to a boil. Stir occasionally, especially along the bottom, so it heats evenly.
It's bubbling now and looks pretty thick. What's the simmer supposed to look like?
Reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan, and let it simmer gently. You want small, steady bubbles rather than a hard boil.
How long should I leave it covered, and is there anything to check before serving?
Simmer it for 10-15 minutes, or until everything is heated through. Give it a stir near the end, make sure it's hot all the way through, then serve the Chili For Two while it's warm.
I'm making Fruit Dip 2 today. What's the best place to start? I've got a mixing bowl out but want to make sure I'm starting with the right ingredients.
For Fruit Dip 2, set out 8 ounces cream cheese, 1/2 cup marshmallow creme, 2 cups frozen whipped topping that has been thawed, and 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice.
The whipped topping is thawed, and the cream cheese is still a little firm. Is that okay for blending?
It will blend more smoothly if the cream cheese has softened a bit. Once it's workable, put the cream cheese in the bowl with the marshmallow creme and the thawed whipped topping.
All three are in the bowl. Should I use a spoon, whisk, or mixer?
Use a mixer if you have one, or a sturdy spoon if not. Blend until the cream cheese, marshmallow creme, and thawed topping are combined into a smooth, fluffy mixture.
It's mostly smooth now, but it looks thick for dipping fruit.
That's where the pineapple juice comes in. Add the unsweetened pineapple juice gradually, using enough of the 1/4 cup to loosen it to a dipping consistency.
Should I pour in the whole 1/4 cup at once?
Add it a little at a time and stir after each splash. Stop when the dip is soft enough for fruit to scoop without becoming runny.
The texture looks right now. Do I serve it immediately or chill it?
Cover the bowl and chill the fruit dip for 1 hour so it firms slightly and the flavors come together.
After the 1 hour chill, what's the best way to put it out?
Give it a quick stir, transfer it to a serving bowl if you like, and serve it cold with fruit for dipping.
Let's work through Adriennes Tom Ka Gai today. Where should I begin? I've got a large saucepan out and want to prep before turning on the heat.
Absolutely. Set out 2 teaspoons peanut oil, 2 cloves garlic thinly sliced, 2 tablespoons grated fresh ginger root, and 1/4 cup chopped lemon grass. Keep the saucepan ready for medium heat.
While working on Adriennes Tom Ka Gai, the garlic is sliced and the ginger is grated. Should the lemon grass go in with those aromatics?
Yes. Once the peanut oil is hot in the large saucepan over medium heat, the garlic, ginger, and lemon grass will go in together with the red pepper, coriander, and cumin.
I'm heating the oil now. How long should I give the spices and aromatics once they hit the pan?
Stir them in and cook until they smell fragrant, about 2 minutes. Keep them moving so the garlic doesn't scorch.
It smells strong and the garlic is just starting to color. I have the chicken and onion ready beside the stove.
For this batch of Adriennes Tom Ka Gai, add the chicken and onion to the saucepan. Cook while stirring until the chicken turns white and the onion looks translucent, about 5 minutes.
The chicken is no longer pink on the outside, and the onion has softened. Should I lower the heat before adding the greens?
You can keep it around medium as long as nothing is sticking or browning too fast. Stir in the bok choy so it gets coated with the aromatics and juices.
The bok choy is in, but the stems still look pretty crisp. What texture am I aiming for?
Cook it until the bok choy begins to wilt, which should take 5 to 10 minutes. The leaves should soften, while the stems can still have a little bite.
It's wilting now and there's a nice aroma from the ginger and lemon grass. Anything I should check before serving?
Make sure the chicken pieces are cooked through and the onion is translucent. Once the bok choy has wilted to your liking, take the saucepan off the heat and serve the Tom Ka Gai hot.
Let's work through Frosted Ruby Punch today. Where should I begin? I want to get the frozen ring started correctly.
Absolutely. You'll need 4 cups cranberry juice for the ice ring, plus 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups lemon juice, and 1 cup orange juice for the punch base.
I have a 5-cup ring mold out. Does all the cranberry juice go straight into it?
Yes, pour the 4 cups cranberry juice into the 5-cup ring mold, leaving a little room at the top so it can expand as it freezes.
It's filled and level. How long should I freeze it?
Put the mold in the freezer and freeze it overnight, until the cranberry juice is solid enough to unmold as an ice ring.
For the punch bowl tomorrow, should I mix the juices before adding anything bubbly?
Yes. In the punch bowl, combine the 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups lemon juice, and 1 cup orange juice first. Stir until the sugar is dissolved.
How will I know the sugar is dissolved enough?
The liquid should look smooth rather than grainy, and you shouldn't feel sugar scraping along the bottom when you stir.
Once that's smooth, when does the ginger ale go in?
Stir in the ginger ale after the sugar has dissolved, so the punch stays fizzy and the base is already evenly sweetened.
What's the best way to serve it with the frozen cranberry ring?
Remove the cranberry ice ring from the mold and float it in the punch bowl. It will chill the Frosted Ruby Punch and add that ruby-colored centerpiece as it melts.
I pulled up Eclairs II. Can you guide the first few moves? I want to get the setup right before I start heating anything.
Absolutely. Pull out 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup water, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need a medium saucepan and a cookie sheet.
I've got the ingredients on the counter. Should the oven be on already?
Yes, bring the oven up to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) so it's ready when the dough stage is done.
On Eclairs II, the oven is heating. What should I do with the cookie sheet?
Grease the cookie sheet evenly, especially the spots where the eclair dough will sit, so they release cleanly after baking.
Cookie sheet is greased. I'm at the stove with the saucepan now.
Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to the medium saucepan.
They're both in the pan. Should I stir right away or wait for the butter to soften?
Start heating the pan and stir as it warms. Bring the mixture to a boil, keeping it moving so the butter melts completely into the water.
It's starting to bubble, but I still see a little butter around the edges.
Keep stirring until those butter pieces disappear completely. You want the butter fully melted before you move on.
The butter is fully melted and the mixture is boiling. Is this the point where I'm ready for the dry ingredients?
Yes. You've completed the listed setup and stovetop step: oven at 450 degrees F (230 degrees C), greased cookie sheet, and the 1/2 cup butter with 1 cup water brought to a boil until fully melted.
I want to make Dutch Cream Waffles. Can you guide me while I set up the bowls?

In this Dutch Cream Waffles step, put a large mixing bowl on the counter for the dry ingredients and a small mixing bowl for the yolk mixture. Measure out 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
The flour and salt are measured. Should they go straight into the large bowl together?
Yes, add both to the large mixing bowl and stir them together so the salt is evenly distributed through the flour.
Done. I also have eggs here, but I want to be sure I separate them correctly.
Separate 3 eggs, keeping the 3 egg yolks for the small bowl and the 3 egg whites separate as well. Try not to let any yolk get into the whites.
The yolks are in the small bowl, and the whites are set aside. What speed should I use?
Start the mixer on low with the egg yolks. While it runs, add the cream slowly so the yolks loosen up evenly.
The cream is going in smoothly. How long should I keep beating it?
Keep it on low and beat the yolk-and-cream mixture for 1 minute. It should look blended and slightly lighter.
That minute is up. Do I pour it into the flour bowl all at once?
Yes, add the yolk mixture to the flour and salt. Mix on low speed first so the flour doesn't puff out of the bowl.
It's mostly combined but still a little streaky. Should I scrape the sides before increasing the speed?
Scrape down the sides, then beat on medium-high until the batter is smooth. Stop once it looks even and no dry flour streaks remain.
Today I'm tackling Fiery Fish Tacos with Crunchy Corn Salsa. Can you help me line up the prep? I want to get the salsa components organized before I heat anything.
Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl for the salsa and gather 1 cup corn, 1/2 cup diced red onion, 1 cup peeled, chopped jicama, and 1/2 cup diced red bell pepper.
I've got the corn and onion measured. The jicama is peeled, but I'm still chopping it—should it be small like the pepper?
Yes, chop the jicama into bite-size pieces so it mixes evenly with the corn, red onion, and diced red bell pepper. The goal is a crunchy salsa that can sit neatly in the tacos.
The vegetables are ready. Should I start the grill now or mix the salsa first?
Go ahead and preheat the grill for high heat now. While it heats, you can assemble the crunchy corn salsa.
Grill is heating. I have a medium bowl on the counter—what goes in it?
Add the corn, diced red onion, chopped jicama, diced red bell pepper, and cilantro to the medium bowl. Toss them together until the colors are evenly mixed.
The bowl looks good and crunchy. I have lime juice and zest ready—do those go in together?
Yes. Stir in the lime juice and zest, folding everything so the citrus coats the corn, onion, jicama, bell pepper, and cilantro.
It smells bright now. Do I season the salsa or make the spicy mix separately?
Make the spicy mix separately in a small bowl: combine cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt.
Small bowl is mixed. Anything I should check before serving this with the fish tacos?
Give the salsa one more gentle stir so the lime and zest are distributed, keep the cayenne-pepper mixture ready for the fish, and make sure the grill is still at high heat before cooking.

messages.content: I'm making Barbecued Shredded Beef and want to get it set up without missing anything. Can you guide me while I prep?

Absolutely. Set out a large roasting pan and gather the main items: 3 pounds beef roast, 2 chopped onions, 2 cans or bottles of beer that are 12 fluid ounces each, and 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce.
The roast is out, and I've chopped the onions. Should I turn the oven on before I assemble the pan?
Yes, heat the oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C), so it's ready by the time the beef and liquid are in the roasting pan.
Oven is heating. Do I need to sear the roast, or does it go straight into the pan?
For this recipe, put the beef roast straight into the large roasting pan. Scatter the chopped onions over the top and around the roast.
The onions are spread over it. I see Worcestershire sauce in the recipe—what do I mix it with?
In a large bowl, combine the 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce with liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
I've got that mixed. The bowl looks pretty concentrated—does the beer go in there too?
Yes. Pour in the 2 cans or bottles of beer, 12 fluid ounces each, then stir so the seasonings are evenly mixed into the liquid.
The beer mixture is stirred. Should I pour it over the roast or just into one side of the pan?
Add the mixture to the roasting pan, pouring it around and over the beef so the onions and roast are surrounded by the seasoned beer liquid.
Everything is in the roasting pan now. Before I put it in the oven, can you recap what should be in there?

You should have the 3 pounds beef roast in the large roasting pan, topped with 2 chopped onions, with the beer mixture added: 2 12-fluid-ounce beers stirred together with 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. The oven should be at 275 degrees F, or 135 degrees C.
I want to make German Sweet Chocolate Pie. I've got the chocolate bar out, but can you guide me so I don't overheat it?
Absolutely. You'll need 1 (4 ounce) bar German sweet chocolate, chopped, plus 1/3 cup milk. Put the chopped chocolate in a large microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of the milk.
The bowl is ready and the milk is measured. Do I microwave it all at once?
Microwave it on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, just until the chocolate is almost melted. Stop and stir halfway through the heating time so it melts evenly.
It looks mostly melted after stirring, with a few soft pieces left. Is that okay?
Yes, that's the right texture. Stir it gently; the remaining warmth should smooth out those last bits without needing much more heat.
What should I add next? I have cream cheese on the counter.
Add 4 ounces softened cream cheese, 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk from the 1/3 cup. Use a wire whisk to beat everything together until the mixture is blended.
The cream cheese is mixing in, but I'm seeing a few tiny pale streaks. Should I keep whisking?
Keep whisking a little longer, scraping around the sides of the bowl if needed, until the chocolate mixture looks evenly combined.
It's smooth now. Does it need to chill before I fold anything in?
Yes. Refrigerate the mixture for 10 minutes so it firms up slightly before the whipped topping goes in.
The timer is done, and the bowl feels cool. How do I keep it light when adding the topping?
Gently fold in 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping with a spatula. Turn the mixture over itself slowly until no streaks remain, trying not to deflate it.
Help me stay organized for E Z Cheezy Pie. What comes first? I've got counter space cleared but want to make sure I start with the right things.
Absolutely. Set out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells and 3 packages of softened cream cheese, 8 ounces each. The cream cheese will mix much more smoothly if it's truly softened.
The pie shells are already baked, and the cream cheese has been sitting out. What else should I put on the counter?
You'll also need 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. A medium mixing bowl and a hand mixer or sturdy whisk will help.
I have the sugar, vanilla, bowl, and mixer ready. Should the oven be on even though the shells are baked?
Yes, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, keep the baked shells nearby and focus on the filling.
Oven is heating. The cream cheese is in the bowl—what texture am I aiming for before adding anything?
Whip the softened cream cheese in the medium mixing bowl until it looks fluffy and lighter, with no firm chunks clinging to the beaters.
It's looking fluffy now, though there are a couple streaks on the side of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides, then add the 1/2 cup white sugar and the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the whipped cream cheese.
Sugar and vanilla are in. Should I mix slowly or turn the mixer up?
Start on low so the sugar doesn't scatter, then increase to medium and mix until the filling is smooth.
The mixture looks smooth and creamy. Do I need to do anything else to the filling before using the pie shells?
No extra ingredients are needed for this recipe. Once the filling is smooth, it's ready to go with the 2 baked 9 inch pie shells.
I'm making Garlic Chicken Stir Fry and I've got a wok out. Can you guide me without rushing the prep?

Absolutely. Before the heat goes on, set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep the chicken nearby too, since it cooks quickly once it hits the wok.
The garlic is minced, but I noticed the cooking step only uses 2 cloves at the start. Should I add those first?
Yes, have 2 cloves of the minced garlic ready for the hot oil along with the ginger and green onions. The pan will be very hot, so it helps to keep that small pile right beside the stove.
Oil is measured. How hot should the wok be before I add anything?
Heat the peanut oil in the wok or a large skillet until it just begins to smoke. That's the cue to work quickly so the aromatics sizzle instead of sitting in warm oil.
It's starting to smoke a little. What goes in right away?
Stir in the 2 cloves minced garlic, the 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving right away so the garlic doesn't scorch.
The onions are bright and sizzling. What texture am I watching for?
Stir fry until the green onion becomes translucent, about 2 minutes. You want it softened and fragrant, not browned.
It's been about 2 minutes and the onion looks translucent. Is the chicken next?
Yes. Add the chicken now and stir constantly so the pieces spread through the aromatics and cook evenly.
How do I know when to stop cooking the chicken?
Cook and stir until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes. Once there's no raw-looking surface, take it off the heat and serve it right away.

Remove the bay leaf, then spoon the chicken into the warm tortillas with only a little of the pan liquid for moisture. Add the finely diced raw toppings last so they keep their crunch, and serve the tacos right away.
I'm ready to cook Enchilada Style Burritos. What should be ready before I begin? I'm starting with frozen bean and cheese burritos.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 frozen prepared bean and cheese burritos, a greased 13-in baking dish, 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1 3/4 cups water.

No thawing needed. Put the frozen burritos straight into the greased 13-in baking dish, then set the dish aside while you make the sauce.

Use a saucepan. Add the 2 tablespoons butter or margarine and melt it over the heat, keeping an eye on it so it melts without browning too much.
The butter is melted and foamy. Do I add the flour all at once?
Yes. Stir in the 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour and keep stirring until the mixture looks smooth, with no dry flour streaks.
It's smoothing out, but it's pretty thick. How do I add the water without lumps?
Pour in the 1 3/4 cups water gradually while stirring the whole time. Adding it slowly helps the flour mixture loosen into a smooth sauce.
The water is mixed in now. What texture am I looking for before it goes over the burritos?
Bring the sauce to a boil, then cook and stir it for 2 minutes, or until it has thickened.
It's been boiling and I stirred for 2 minutes. It's thicker now—am I done with the guided part?
Yes. At this point the recipe's prep is complete: the frozen burritos are arranged in the greased dish, and the thickened sauce is ready to use with them.

Cover the serving bowl and refrigerate the Artichoke Hummus until you're ready to serve. Keep the tiny raw vegetable pieces separate until the last minute so they stay crisp.
I'm making Feta Chicken Salad and want to prep it without getting ahead of myself. Can you guide me through it?

The chicken is already diced, and I've got the celery on the board. Should the red onion go in right away too?
Yes. Add the diced cooked chicken, diced celery, and diced red onion to the serving bowl. Give them a quick toss so the onion and celery are distributed through the chicken.
What about the red bell pepper? I don't want it to get lost in the mix.
Seed and dice the red bell pepper, then fold it into the serving bowl with the chicken mixture. A gentle stir is enough so the pieces stay distinct.
Okay, the bowl looks colorful now. What do I need for the creamy part?
In the separate bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the dressing looks evenly combined.
Should I mash the feta completely or leave some texture?
Leave a little texture if you like. Stir until the dressing is cohesive, but small bits of feta are fine and work well in this salad.
The dressing is mixed. Do I pour all of it over the chicken bowl now?
Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture, then stir to blend. Scrape the sides and bottom of the serving bowl so everything gets lightly coated.
It's coated now. How do I know if it needs anything else before serving?
Taste a bite, then season with salt and pepper as needed. Once the seasoning tastes balanced, it's ready to serve.

Let Chicken with Vegetables cook covered on low for 5 hours; it is ready when the meat juices run clear.

Today I'm tackling Cranberry Apple Pie II. Can you help me line up the prep? I've got the pie plate out and want to get organized before I start peeling apples.

Line the pie plate with the pastry now, pressing it gently into the bottom and sides so it sits evenly without stretching too much.

For Cranberry Apple Pie II, peel, core, and slice all 6 apples. Try to keep the slices fairly even so they mix well with the cranberry sauce.

Regular pie slices are fine; aim for pieces thin enough to soften in the pie but sturdy enough to hold some shape when combined with the sauce.

Use a medium-sized mixing bowl. Add the sliced apples and the whole cranberry sauce, then gently fold them together so the apples are coated without getting crushed.

Keep the measured 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour ready with the filling ingredients. Once those are incorporated according to your next pie step, the lined pie plate will be ready for filling.

Peel and chop enough jicama for 1 cup, then dice 1/2 cup red bell pepper. Add both to your prep area with the corn and onion.

Add the corn, diced red onion, chopped jicama, diced red bell pepper, and cilantro to the medium bowl. Toss them together gently so the pieces stay crisp.

Stir in the lime juice and lime zest. Mix just until everything is lightly coated so the salsa stays fresh-tasting.
Done. The bowl smells bright from the lime. Is there a seasoning mix for the fish?
In a small bowl, combine cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt. That will give the tacos their fiery seasoning.
The spice bowl is mixed. Anything I should check before I start grilling the fish?
Make sure the grill is still at high heat, keep the corn salsa chilled or off to the side, and have the cayenne, black pepper, and salt mixture ready to season the fish just before cooking.

I'm making Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread today. What's the best place to start? I've got the pan out and want to load it correctly.

The water, butter, honey, and bread flour are measured. Should the sunflower seeds go in with everything else?
Hold the sunflower seeds back for now. Add the other ingredients to the bread machine pan in the order your machine's manufacturer recommends.

Yes, add the sunflower seeds now while the dough is kneading. Sprinkle them into the pan so the machine can work them evenly through the dough.

I want to make Beet and Pear Puree, but I'd like to set everything up before turning on the stove. What should I pull out?

Put the large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1 pound unsalted butter in it. Keep the heat moderate so the butter melts evenly rather than browning quickly.

Wait until the butter is fully melted in the large skillet over medium heat. Then you'll be set up for the minced Vidalia onions and minced Bosc pears that are already prepped.

Combine the dry ingredients separately, then fold them into the banana mixture. Use gentle turns with a spatula so everything gets well mixed without overworking the batter.

messages.content: I'm baking Almond Apricot Bread as a fruit-forward breakfast quick bread or muffin, and I want warm spices in this version. Which spices should I use?
For Almond Apricot Bread, go with cinnamon and ginger, and skip cardamom for this batch.
Great, that's the direction I'm taking today. I've got my large mixing bowl out—what dry ingredients should go in it?
Add 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, 3 teaspoons baking powder, and salt to the large bowl.
The flour, both sugars, baking powder, and salt are in. Should I mix those before touching the wet ingredients?
Yes, combine them well in the bowl so the baking powder and sugars are evenly distributed.
I also have the baby food on the counter. Do I use all of it in the batter?
Not quite—set aside 1 tablespoon baby food for the glaze, then keep the remaining baby food for the batter.
Okay, the 1 tablespoon is reserved. I have another bowl ready for the wet mixture.
In that second bowl, beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food.
Should that wet mixture be completely smooth before I add it to the dry bowl?
Beat it until the egg is fully blended and the mixture looks cohesive; it does not need to be overly worked.
The wet bowl is mixed. What's the best way to combine it without making the bread tough?
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir gently, stopping as soon as everything is just moistened.
So a few small streaks or lumps are better than stirring too much?
Exactly—keep the batter lightly mixed rather than smooth; once the dry ingredients are moistened, stop stirring.
