Great, that's exactly the direction I want today. I'm clearing counter space—what dry ingredients should I measure first?
Measure out 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Keep them together so they're ready to sift.
The flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt are measured. Should I get the pan and oven handled before mixing?
Yes. Heat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, and pull out a 9x13 inch pan.
Oven is heating, and I found the pan. How should I prep it so the cake releases cleanly?
Grease the 9x13 inch pan well, then dust it with flour and tap out any excess so there aren't thick patches.
Pan is greased and floured. I have the bowl with the dry ingredients nearby—what texture should I look for after sifting?
Sift the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together until the mixture looks even, light, and free of little baking soda or spice clumps.
The sifted mix looks uniform. I'm moving to the fruit—do the apples get mixed into the dry bowl now?
Not yet. In a separate bowl, combine the apples with the white sugar, then set that bowl aside.
The apples and white sugar are combined and resting. Should I cover them while I clean up the flour on the counter?
You can loosely cover the bowl while it sits. That keeps the apples protected while the sugar starts drawing out some juice.
I've got the oven hot, the pan ready, the dry ingredients sifted, and the sugared apples set aside. Anything I should double-check before continuing?

Double-check that the oven is still at 350 degrees F, the 9x13 inch pan is evenly greased and floured, and the dry mixture stayed separate from the apple-sugar bowl until the recipe has you combine them.
Let's work through Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies today. Where should I begin? I'm setting up the counter and want to be sure I start with the right ingredients.

Absolutely. Put out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening, plus your sugars: 1 cup packed light brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. Those will get creamed together for the dough.
The butter is soft and I've measured both sugars. Should I turn the oven on before mixing?
Yes, go ahead and set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). That way it's ready by the time the cookie dough is mixed.
Oven is heating. I have a large mixing bowl out—do the fats and sugars all go in together?

They do. In the large bowl, cream together the softened butter, butter flavored shortening, packed light brown sugar, and white sugar. Add the eggs and vanilla too, then keep mixing until everything looks smooth.
It's starting to come together, but I can still see a few streaks of shortening. Should I keep beating it?
Keep going a little longer. You're aiming for a smooth, evenly blended sugar mixture before the dry ingredients go in, so the butter and shortening shouldn't sit in separate streaks.
Okay, the mixture looks smooth now. What dry ingredients should I combine separately?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Stir them together well so the spices and baking soda are evenly distributed.
The dry bowl smells spicy and looks evenly mixed. Do I dump it all into the sugar mixture?
Add the dry mixture to the sugar mixture and stir until it's incorporated. Mix enough to bring the dough together, but don't keep working it longer than needed once the flour disappears.
The dough is thick now. I still have oats and raisins waiting—are those last?
Yes. Stir in the oats and raisins until they're spread evenly through the dough. After that, the cookie dough is ready for portioning and baking in the preheated 350 degrees F oven.
I'm making Almond Buttercrunch and want to set up before the sugar gets hot. What should be on the counter?

Set out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a saucepan, a spoon or heatproof spatula, a candy thermometer if you have one, and a large buttered cookie sheet ready before you turn on the heat.
The cookie sheet is buttered and the saucepan is ready. Do the almonds go in later or right away?
They go in right away. Put the butter, white sugar, and 1 cup chopped almonds into the saucepan together, then keep the heat low so the butter melts and the sugar mixture warms gradually.
It's starting to melt around the edges. Should I stir the whole time?
Yes, stir constantly while it's coming up to a boil. Scrape the bottom and corners of the pan so the sugar and butter heat evenly with the almonds.
It just reached a boil and looks glossy. Do I keep stirring now?
Once it boils, stop stirring, and don't shake the pan. Let it cook undisturbed from here so the candy can reach the hard-crack stage cleanly.
I've got a thermometer clipped on. What temperature am I watching for?
Heat it to 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. If you're checking without relying only on the thermometer, a small drop of syrup in cold water should form hard, brittle threads.
It's at 302 F and the cold-water drop snaps into threads. Is that enough?
Yes, that fits the target range and texture. Take it off the heat carefully now—the syrup will be extremely hot.
Pan is off the burner. How do I get it out without making a mess?

Pour the hot mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet in a steady stream, then let it spread out on the sheet. Keep your hands clear of the syrup, and leave the measured milk chocolate chips nearby for the recipe.
Can you help me cook Coq au Vin alla Italiana? I've got a large skillet out, but I want to make sure I set up the chicken and coating correctly.

Absolutely. Put 4 pounds of dark meat chicken pieces on your work area, along with 1 tablespoon vegetable oil for the skillet. You'll also need 5 cloves crushed garlic and 1/2 cup all-purpose flour for dredging.
The chicken is on a tray, and the flour is measured. Should I heat the pan before dealing with the garlic?
Yes. Set the large skillet over heat and add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil so it can get hot before the chicken goes in.
The oil is warming. Do I add all the crushed garlic now or save some?
Add 1/2 of the crushed garlic to the skillet now. Keep the rest aside for later use if you continue the recipe beyond these steps.
The garlic is in and starting to smell good. What should I do with the flour while that cooks?
Season the 1/2 cup all-purpose flour with poultry seasoning, then stir it so the seasoning is evenly distributed before you coat the chicken.
The seasoned flour looks mixed. Should the chicken be wet or dry before I dredge it?
Pat the chicken pieces dry if they're damp, then dredge each piece in the seasoned flour so it gets a light, even coating.
On Coq au Vin alla Italiana, i've coated a few pieces. How crowded can the skillet be when I brown them?
Give the chicken pieces some space in the skillet so they brown instead of steaming. Work in batches if needed, especially with 4 pounds of dark meat chicken.
The first batch is in the pan. How long should I brown it before turning or pulling it out?
Brown the dredged chicken in the skillet for 4 or 5 minutes, watching for a golden surface before you move on to the next batch.
Can you help me put together Double Fudge Brownie Mix? I'm setting it up as a jar mix.
Absolutely. Set out a 1 quart or 1 liter jar first, since the ingredients will be layered right into it.
Jar is ready. What should I measure before I start layering?
Measure 2 cups white sugar and 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder. Keep them separate so the layers stay distinct.
Got them measured. Are there more dry ingredients for the jar?
Yes. You'll also need 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1 cup chopped pecans.
Everything is on the counter. Does the order matter when I add it?
It does for this mix. Layer the ingredients in the jar in the order listed: white sugar, unsweetened cocoa powder, all-purpose flour, then chopped pecans.
The sugar is in, and I'm about to add the cocoa. Should I pack the layers down?
You can gently tap the jar on the counter to settle each layer, but don't mash them together. The goal is tidy, visible layers.
The jar is filled with the pecans on top. What should go on the tag?
Attach a tag that says to get the oven warming to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Should I include anything else before I close it up?
For the recipe details you have, make sure the jar is sealed, the tag is attached securely, and the preheat instruction is easy to read.
I'm making Chocolate Crisps and want to set everything out before I turn on the stove. Can you guide me?
Absolutely. Put out 1 tablespoon butter, softened, plus 1 egg white. You'll also want a small saucepan, a medium sized bowl, and cookie sheets.
I've got the butter and egg white out. What else should be on the counter?
Add 1/4 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to your setup. Those are the remaining ingredients for the Chocolate Crisps.
The ingredients are measured. Should I deal with the oven before browning the butter?
Yes—get the oven warming to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C), so it can warm while you prepare the butter.
Oven is heating. I have two cookie sheets; do they need anything?
Grease the cookie sheets so the crisps won't stick later. A light, even coating is enough.
Sheets are greased. For the butter, should I use the softened tablespoon I measured?
Use that 1 tablespoon butter. Place it in a small saucepan over medium heat and melt it until it becomes lightly browned.
It's melted and starting to smell nutty. How brown should I let it get?
Stop when it's lightly browned, not dark. You're looking for a gentle golden color and a toasted aroma, then take it off the heat.
Okay, it's lightly browned. Where should I put it so I can keep going?
Pour the browned butter into a medium sized bowl. That keeps it ready to combine with the egg white, sugar, and vanilla as you continue.
I have A 1 Chicken Soup planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a large pot out and want to make sure I'm setting up the ingredients correctly.
Absolutely. Put 2 tablespoons vegetable oil by the stove, and have 2 skinless chicken leg quarters ready to brown in the pot.
The chicken and oil are ready. What else should I have chopped or measured before I turn on the heat?
Measure 1/2 cup chopped onion and 2 quarts water. Also keep the chicken bouillon close, since it goes in when the water is added.
Everything is on the counter now. Should I start with the oil over medium heat?
Yes. Warm the oil in the large pot over medium heat, then add the chicken leg quarters and let them brown on both sides.
The chicken is browning, but I'm not sure how dark to let it get before adding anything else.
You're looking for browned surfaces on both sides, not fully cooked meat yet. Once both sides have color, stir in the chopped onion.
The onion is in the pot. How long should I cook it with the chicken?
Cook the onion with the chicken for 2 minutes more, stirring so it softens and picks up some of the browned flavor from the pot.
The onion has softened a bit. Do I add all the water at once?
Yes, pour in the 2 quarts water and add the chicken bouillon, then bring the pot up to a boil.
It's boiling now. What should the soup do from here so the chicken finishes properly?
Reduce the heat so the soup simmers steadily, then let it cook for 45 minutes. Keep the pot at a gentle simmer rather than a hard boil.
I'm making BBQ Chuck Roast today. Can you help me get set up before I open anything?

Absolutely. Put out 1 (5 pound) chuck roast, 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer. You'll also want a large bowl for the marinade, something to cover it with, and room in the refrigerator.
I've got the roast and the sauces on the counter. The beer is a 12 fluid ounce bottle—is that the right amount?
Yes, that matches the recipe. The beer gets mixed with the barbeque sauce and teriyaki sauce to make the marinade for the chuck roast.
What goes into the bowl with those liquids? I don't want to miss the seasoning part.
In the large bowl, mix the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt until everything is evenly combined.
The marinade is mixed and smells pretty strong. Do I put the whole 5 pound roast straight into it?
Yes. Place the chuck roast into the marinade, turn it so it's coated well, then cover the bowl and refrigerate it for six hours.
During the six hours, should I just leave it alone or check it?
Here, turn it often while it marinates so different sides stay in contact with the sauce mixture.
It's been chilling, and I'm getting the grill ready. What kind of heat should I set up?
Preheat the outdoor grill for indirect heat, so the roast won't sit directly over the flame the whole time.
The grill is heating. What do I do with the roast and the leftover marinade when I take it out?
Remove the roast from the marinade, then pour the marinade into a saucepan. Keep the roast separate while you move on to the grilling stage.
I'd like to make Feta Chicken Salad. Can you guide me while I get the ingredients ready?
Absolutely. Put a serving bowl on the counter and gather 3 cups diced cooked chicken, 2 large stalks celery for dicing, 1 red bell pepper to seed and dice, and 1/2 red onion to dice.
The chicken is already diced, and I've chopped the celery and red onion. Should the bell pepper be small dice too?
Yes, seed the red bell pepper and dice it into small pieces so it blends easily through the salad rather than leaving big crunchy chunks.
Vegetables are chopped. Which bowl should I use for mixing everything?
Use the serving bowl for the main mixture. Add the diced cooked chicken, diced celery, and diced red onion to that bowl, then give them a light toss.
Those are mixed. I still have the diced red bell pepper on the board.
Keep it nearby with the other prepared vegetables while you make the creamy feta mixture, then you can fold everything together evenly when the dressing goes on.
Okay, I've got a smaller bowl ready for the dressing. What goes in there?
In the separate bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the mixture looks creamy with the feta distributed throughout.
The dressing is mixed; it's creamy but still has little feta bits.
That's just right for this salad. Pour the mayonnaise-sour cream-feta-dill mixture over the chicken mixture, add the diced red bell pepper, and stir gently until everything is coated.
It's all combined now. How do I know if it needs anything else before serving?
Taste a spoonful, then season with salt and pepper as needed. Once the seasoning tastes balanced, the Feta Chicken Salad is ready to serve.
I'm making Dilled Garlic today. What's the best place to start? Can you help me get set up without missing anything?

Absolutely. Put out 2 pounds of peeled garlic, 1 sprig of chopped fresh dill, cayenne pepper to taste, and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar. You'll also need sterile containers and a medium saucepan.
The garlic is peeled and the jars are sterile. Should the dill and cayenne go in with the garlic right away?
Yes. Pack the sterile containers with the garlic, chopped fresh dill, and cayenne pepper. Leave about an inch of space at the top of each container.
I've filled them to just below the top. The cayenne is sprinkled in lightly—does that sound right?
That works, since the cayenne is to taste. Keep the containers nearby while you make the vinegar mixture.
I have the medium saucepan ready. What goes into it?
Pour in the 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar, then mix it with salt in the saucepan.
The vinegar and salt are mixed. How hot should I get it?
Bring the vinegar and salt mixture to a boil. Stay close so you can pour it while it's still hot.
It's boiling now. Do I pour it straight over the garlic mixture?
Yes. Carefully pour the hot distilled white vinegar and salt mixture into the containers over the garlic, dill, and cayenne.
The containers are filled with the hot vinegar mixture. Is that the main cooking part done?
Yes, that completes the recipe steps: the garlic mixture is packed in sterile containers, the vinegar and salt were boiled, and the hot mixture has been poured over the garlic.
I'm making Banana Chip Muffins I and want to set up my bowls before I get batter everywhere. What should I pull out first?
Set out a large mixing bowl for the dry ingredients and a small bowl for the egg mixture. For the dry bowl, measure 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour and 1/2 cup white sugar.
Flour and sugar are in the big bowl. I've got the baking powder and salt beside me too—how much goes in?
Here, add 1 tablespoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt to that same large bowl.
Done. I also see chocolate chips in the directions, but I don't have a measured amount listed here. Should they go with the dry ingredients?

Yes, add the chocolate chips to the large bowl with the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Since no amount is listed, use the amount your recipe notes or the amount you planned, without changing the other measurements.
Everything dry is in the bowl. Do I stir it a lot or just lightly toss it?
Mix it thoroughly so the baking powder and salt are evenly distributed through the flour and sugar. Once it looks uniform, make a well in the center of the dry mixture.
The well is made. For the small bowl, am I just cracking the egg in and whisking?
Crack the egg into the small bowl and beat it until it looks frothy, with small bubbles and a lighter texture.
The egg is foamy now. I have cooking oil, milk, and bananas ready—do they all go into that egg bowl?
Yes. Mix the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the frothy egg until the wet mixture is combined.
Should I mash the bananas completely before mixing them in, or is a little texture okay?
Mash them enough to blend into the wet ingredients, but a little banana texture is fine for muffins. After that wet mixture is combined, you'll be ready to bring it together with the dry bowl.
I'm making Bocconcini Salad for lunch. Can you help me get set up without making a mess?
Absolutely. Put a large salad bowl on the counter, plus a small bowl or cup for whisking the dressing. Have 1 pound bocconcini ready, and halve 8 cherry tomatoes if they aren't already cut.
The mozzarella balls are drained, and the tomatoes are halved. What vegetables should I prep next?
Chop enough green bell pepper for 1/2 cup and enough celery for 1/2 cup. You'll also want the endive and arugula ready to go into the salad bowl with them.
I've got the bell pepper and celery measured. Should the greens go in before the dressing?
Yes. Add the bocconcini, halved cherry tomatoes, chopped green bell pepper, chopped celery, endive, and arugula to the large salad bowl. Give the bowl enough room so you can toss without spilling.
Everything is in the bowl. The bocconcini are sitting on top—do I mix them now or wait?
You can gently fold the ingredients together once or twice now, just to distribute the mozzarella and vegetables. Save the thorough tossing for after the dressing goes on.
Okay, I'm ready for the dressing. What goes into it?
Whisk together the lemon juice and olive oil in the small bowl until they look blended. Pour that over the salad, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
The dressing is on, but I don't want to bruise the arugula. How much tossing is enough?

Use a light lifting motion from the bottom of the bowl and turn the salad until everything is thoroughly coated with the dressing. Stop once the greens look glossy and the bocconcini and vegetables are evenly dressed.
Looks coated and fresh. How should I serve it?
Sprinkle the basil over the salad right at the end, then serve immediately so the greens stay crisp and the bocconcini tastes fresh.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip. Can you guide me through it while I set up the casserole dish?

Absolutely. Put out a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish, and gather 1 cup mayonnaise, 8 ounces sour cream, 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, and 1 (14 ounce) can of artichoke hearts. Drain and chop the artichoke hearts before mixing.
The mayo, sour cream, soup mix, and drained artichokes are on the counter. Should I start heating the oven now?
Yes, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it heats, you can get the cheese and crab meat ready for the dip.
Oven is heating. Do I need a separate bowl, or can everything go straight into the casserole dish?
You can mix it right in the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish. Add the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat.
The sour cream and mayo are in. Should the soup mix be stirred in before the artichokes?
That works well. Stir the soup mix into the mayonnaise and sour cream until it's evenly distributed, then fold in the chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat.
Everything is combined now, but the top looks a little uneven. Should I smooth it out?
Yes, spread the mixture into an even layer in the casserole dish so it bakes consistently. You don't need to cover it.
The oven is at 350. How long does it bake uncovered?
Bake it uncovered for 30 minutes at 350 degrees F.
Timer is almost done. Once it comes out, should it sit for a while or go straight to the table?
For this batch of Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, serve it immediately while it's hot and creamy.
I'm about to start Caramelized Apple Bites. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got apples and caramels out, but I want to keep the steps straight.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 individually wrapped caramels, unwrapped and chopped, plus 2 tablespoons light corn syrup. Set those near a medium microwave-safe bowl.
The caramels are unwrapped and chopped. Should the apples be ready before I melt anything?
Yes, have 2 apples peeled, cored, and diced before you start heating the caramel mixture so you can coat them while it's still warm and fluid.
Apples are diced. Do I put everything in the bowl together?
Not yet. Put just the chopped caramels and the light corn syrup into the medium microwave-safe bowl.
They're in the bowl. How long should I microwave them?
In this Caramelized Apple Bites step, microwave the bowl on high for approximately 30 seconds, just until the caramels are melted into the corn syrup.
After 30 seconds, there are a couple soft caramel lumps around the edge. Is that okay?
That's okay as long as they're mostly melted; give the mixture a careful stir so the remaining soft pieces blend into the warm caramel syrup.
It looks smooth now. Do the apples go in while the caramel is still warm?
Yes. Add the diced apples to the bowl and toss them until they're coated with the caramel and light corn syrup mixture.
The apple pieces are coated and glossy. Can I serve them right away?
Let the Caramelized Apple Bites cool before serving so the coating can settle and they're comfortable to eat.
I'm making Eggplant Mixed Grill. Can you help me get organized before I start marinating everything?

Absolutely. Set out a large resealable plastic bag and gather the marinade ingredients: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil.
I've got the oil and herbs out. The bag is on the counter too—what else goes into the marinade?
Add the vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic to the bag with the olive oil, parsley, oregano, and basil. Mix everything right in the bag so the herbs and seasonings are evenly distributed.
Should I prep the vegetables before sealing the bag?
Yes. Put the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper into the bag with the marinade.
The vegetables are in. The bag looks pretty full—do I just shake it?
Seal it tightly first, then turn and gently move the bag around so the marinade coats the vegetables without crushing them.
How long does it need to sit, and should it stay cold?
Marinate it for 2 hours in the refrigerator. Turn the bag occasionally during that time so the vegetables keep getting coated.
I'm close to the end of the marinating time. When should I deal with the grill?
Preheat the grill for high heat while the vegetables finish marinating, so it's ready when you take the bag out of the refrigerator.
The grill is heating. Is there anything I should do to the grate before the vegetables go on?
Lightly oil the grill grate before adding the marinated vegetables. That helps keep the eggplant, peppers, mushrooms, onion, and asparagus from sticking.
I'm making Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic. Can you guide me without rushing through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup olive oil, 8 cloves garlic minced, 2 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper. You'll also need cumin and oregano for the paste, plus the butterflied leg of lamb.
I've got the lamb and seasonings out. Should I mix everything in a bowl or rub it on separately?
Mix the olive oil, minced garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano together into a paste. That helps the seasoning spread evenly instead of landing in salty or garlicky patches.
The paste is ready. The lamb has a cut side and a smoother outside—where should I put it?
Rub the paste over both sides of the lamb, including the cut side and the outside. Try to coat the thicker areas well, since they can use the extra seasoning.
It's coated. Do I put it under the broiler right away?
Let it stand for 1 hour, until the meat comes to room temperature. That rest gives the seasoning time to sit on the surface and helps the lamb cook more evenly.
The hour is almost up. What should I set up in the oven?
Move the oven rack to the upper or upper-middle position, depending on how thick the lamb is. Then preheat the broiler on high for at least 10 minutes so it's fully hot before the meat goes in.
I'm lining the pan now. What's the best arrangement so it browns instead of sitting in juices?
Use a large wire rack set over a foil-lined roasting pan. Place the lamb on the rack cut side up, so heat can hit the surface directly and drips fall into the pan.
The broiler is hot and the lamb is on the rack. How do I handle the actual broiling?
Broil it for about 8 minutes, moving the pan as needed so the entire surface browns evenly. Keep an eye on the garlic and edges, since broilers can brown fast.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic

messages.content: I'm ready to cook Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2. What should be ready before I begin? I'm setting out my mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Start by gathering the measured ingredients listed for the dough: 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup confectioners' sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil.
The butter is soft, and I've got both sugars measured. Should the oil go in with them right away?
Yes. Put the softened butter, both sugars, and the vegetable oil into a large mixing bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
It's coming together, but it still looks a little glossy from the oil. Is that okay?
That's fine for this mixture. Keep mixing until there are no obvious streaks of butter or dry sugar pockets, and the oil is worked through.
Okay, the bowl looks consistent now. I have eggs and vanilla nearby—do those go in next?
Yes, add the eggs and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so the wet ingredients are fully blended.
The batter loosened up after the eggs and vanilla. What dry ingredients should I add?
Add the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and cream of tartar. Mix them in gradually so they don't puff out of the bowl, and stop once the dough is evenly combined.
The dough is thick now. I see pecans on the counter, but I'm not sure if they're required.
They're optional. If you want pecans in the cookies, stir them in now; if not, you can leave the dough as it is.
I'll skip the pecans this time. Anything else I should do before portioning the dough?
Give the dough one final scrape around the sides and bottom of the bowl to make sure everything is incorporated, then you're ready to portion it for baking according to your usual cookie-pan setup.
I want to get Cake Doughnuts right. What should I handle first? I've got a large mixing bowl out and want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. For the dry ingredients you'll need 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Those are on the counter. The recipe also mentions spices—should I add them with the dry ingredients?
Yes. In the large bowl, stir together the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, and nutmeg until everything looks evenly mixed.
The dry mix looks even. Do I need a separate bowl for the wet ingredients?
No separate bowl is needed for this part. Make a well in the center of the dry mixture, then pour in the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla.
I made the well and added the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla. How much should I stir it?
Mix it just until well blended. Scrape around the sides and bottom of the bowl so there aren't dry pockets of flour, but don't keep beating once it comes together.
It's thick and a little sticky, but I don't see dry flour. Is that okay?
That sounds right for cake doughnut dough at this stage. If the ingredients are well blended, you're ready to chill it.
What should I cover the bowl with before chilling?
Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap, a lid, or another snug cover so the dough doesn't dry out in the refrigerator.
Got it covered. How long does it need to rest before I keep going?
Refrigerate the covered dough for 1 hour. After that chill, it should be firmer and easier to handle for the next part of making the doughnuts.
Can you help me cook Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken? I've got the chicken out but want to make sure I'm not missing anything.

Absolutely. For this recipe, you'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, salt and pepper to taste, 2 teaspoons olive oil, and 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions.
I have the chicken breasts and the can of diced tomatoes. Should I open the tomatoes now or wait?
You can open the can now and keep it nearby, but the first bit of cooking is just about seasoning and browning the chicken.
Okay, chicken is on a cutting board. Do I season one side or both?
Season both sides of each chicken breast with salt and pepper, using enough to lightly cover the surface.
Both sides are seasoned. What pan setup should I use?
Use a large skillet and add the olive oil. Heat the 2 teaspoons of oil over medium-high heat until it looks hot and shimmery.
The oil is shimmering, and the skillet looks ready. Should all the chicken go in at once?
Place the chicken in the skillet in a single layer. If the pan is crowded, work in batches so the pieces can brown instead of steam.
They're in the pan. What am I looking for before turning them?
Let the chicken cook until the underside browns, then turn each piece once and brown the other side as well.
Both sides have some color now. Do the tomatoes go in yet?
Not yet for this step. Remove the browned chicken from the pan and set it aside, keeping the skillet ready for whatever comes next.

source_seed.recipe_title: Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken

messages.content: I'm ready to cook Dilled Garlic. What should be ready before I begin? I've got peeled garlic ready, but I want to make sure I set up the jars correctly.

Absolutely. You'll need 2 pounds of peeled garlic, 1 sprig of chopped fresh dill, cayenne pepper to taste, and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar. Make sure your containers are sterile before you start filling them.
The containers are sterilized. Should the dill go in loose with the garlic, or layered?
Loose is fine. Add the peeled garlic, chopped fresh dill, and a little cayenne pepper to each sterile container, distributing everything fairly evenly.
How full should I pack the containers? I don't want them overflowing when the vinegar goes in.
Fill them to within an inch of the top. That gives enough room for the hot vinegar mixture while keeping the garlic covered.
They're filled about an inch from the top now. What should I put on the stove?
In a medium saucepan, combine the 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar with salt. Stir it so the salt begins to dissolve.
There wasn't a salt amount listed here. Should I still mix salt into the vinegar?

Yes, the cooking directions call for vinegar and salt in the saucepan, but they don't give a specific salt quantity. Use the amount specified by your source if you have it; otherwise, don't guess if you're preserving for storage.
I've got the vinegar and salt in the pan. Do I just warm it, or does it need a full boil?
Bring the vinegar and salt mixture to a boil. Once it's boiling, it's ready to pour while hot.
The vinegar mixture is boiling now. How do I finish filling the containers?
Carefully pour the hot distilled white vinegar and salt mixture into the containers over the garlic, dill, and cayenne mixture, keeping that headspace near the top.
I want to make Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken today. Can you guide me without rushing? I'm starting with the sauce ingredients.

Absolutely. For the glaze, measure out 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum. You'll also be combining them with mustard and garlic, then seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
I've got the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, and rum measured. Should I use a small bowl or something bigger?
Use a medium bowl so there's room to stir without splashing. Add the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, dark rum, mustard, and garlic to the bowl.
Everything is in the bowl. The molasses is kind of thick—do I need to whisk it a lot?
Yes, mix it well until the molasses is fully blended into the ketchup and juice. Once it looks smooth and glossy, season with salt and pepper to taste.
The glaze is smooth now. What baking dish should I use for the chicken?
Use a 9x13 inch baking dish and lightly oil it so the chicken doesn't stick during marinating and baking later.
The dish is oiled and the chicken pieces are in it. Do I pour all the glaze over them?
Use about 1/2 of the prepared glaze for now. Brush it over both sides of the chicken pieces so they're evenly coated, and save the rest for later use.
I brushed both sides. Some glaze is pooling in the corners—should I wipe that out?
No need to wipe it out unless it's excessive. A little extra glaze in the dish is fine; just make sure the chicken itself has a good coating on both sides.
How long does it need to sit before I cook it? I'm planning around dinner.
Cover the dish and refrigerate it to marinate for at least 2 hours, or leave it overnight if that works better for your schedule.
I'm starting Carrot and Coriander Soup II; can you walk me through the setup? I've got a large saucepan out but haven't started chopping yet.
Absolutely. Cut 4 large carrots into 1 inch pieces, and chop 1/4 large onion. Once those are ready, keep them near the saucepan.
The carrots and onion are prepped. Do I need anything else before the pan goes on the stove?
Yes—measure 1 quart vegetable broth and chop 1/2 cup fresh cilantro. Those go into the saucepan with the carrots and onion.
So everything goes in together, including the cilantro?
That's right. Add the carrots, chopped onion, vegetable broth, and chopped fresh cilantro to the large saucepan all at once.
It's all in the pot. Should I cover it, or just bring it up uncovered?
Bring it to a boil, then cook until the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes. A lid is optional, but keep an eye on it so it doesn't boil over.
It's been close to 10 minutes. How soft should the carrots be before I stop?
They should be tender enough that a fork goes in easily. Once they're there, remove the saucepan from the heat.
The carrots are tender and the pot is off the burner. Can I blend it right away?
Let the soup cool slightly first. It doesn't need to be cold—just give it a short rest so it's safer to puree.
Okay, it has cooled a bit. What's the best way to get the texture smooth?
Puree the soup until smooth using a blender or food processor. Work carefully if it's still warm, then serve once the texture is silky.
Let's work through Date Nut Bars today. Where should I begin? I've got a large mixing bowl out and want to be sure I measure the dry ingredients correctly.
Absolutely. Measure 2 cups sugar and 2 cups all-purpose flour into the large bowl, then add 2 teaspoons baking powder and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
The sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt are in the bowl. Do the dates and nuts go in before the wet ingredients?
Yes. Stir the dates and nuts into those dry ingredients now so they're evenly distributed before the batter gets stiff.
They're mixed through. I'm ready for the eggs and flavoring, but I don't want to overmix it.
Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla, then stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened. The batter is supposed to be very stiff, so stop once there are no dry pockets.
Before I continue with Date Nut Bars, it's thick and sticky, with no dry flour showing. What pan should I use?
In this Date Nut Bars step, use a greased 15-in pan. Scrape the stiff batter into it and spread it as evenly as you can, pushing it into the corners.
The pan is greased and the batter is spread out. Should the oven be fully preheated before it goes in?
Yes, have the oven at 350 degrees F before baking. Put the pan in once it's preheated.
It's in the oven at 350. How long should I set the timer for?
Set it for 20 minutes to start, then check. It may need up to 25 minutes total, and you're looking for the bars to be golden brown.
At 20 minutes the edges are coloring, but the center still looks a little pale. Should I leave it longer?
Give it a few more minutes, checking before it reaches 25 minutes. Pull the pan when the top is golden brown, then let the bars cool before cutting so they hold together neatly.
I'm about to start Garden Potato Salad. Can you talk me through the prep? I've already cooked and peeled the potatoes, but I want to keep the order straight.
Absolutely. Cube the 6 large cooked, peeled potatoes and put them near a large mixing bowl. You'll also want 4 hard-cooked eggs sliced, 2 celery ribs sliced, and 6 green onions with the tops sliced.
The potatoes are cubed, and I've got the eggs sliced. Should the celery and green onions go in the same bowl?
Yes. Add the potatoes, sliced hard-cooked eggs, celery, and green onions to the large bowl. The recipe also has you combine them with radishes, salt, and pepper, then set that bowl aside.
I don't see an amount for the radishes or seasoning. Should I just add them carefully?
Right—since the recipe doesn't give amounts for the radishes, salt, or pepper, add them to suit the salad, then gently toss so the potatoes and eggs don't break down too much.
For Garden Potato Salad, the bowl is mixed and set aside. What pan do I need for the dressing?
Use a saucepan for the dressing. In it, combine eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt before you put it over the heat.
Are those dressing eggs raw, separate from the sliced hard-cooked eggs in the salad?
Yes, treat the dressing mixture as separate from the sliced hard-cooked eggs already in the bowl. The recipe has the dressing ingredients combined in the saucepan so they can cook together.
The dressing ingredients are in the saucepan. How hot should I make it, and what texture am I watching for?
Cook and stir the dressing over medium heat. Keep it moving as it heats, and stop when it has thickened.
It's thickened now. Do I pour it over the potatoes while it's hot?
Let the dressing cool first. Once cooled, you can use it with the prepared potato mixture and serve the Garden Potato Salad as planned.
Can you help me get started on Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake? I want to make sure I set up the ingredients correctly before I bake.
Absolutely. For this part of the cake, pull out 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 6 (1 ounce) squares of unsweetened chocolate, chopped.
I've got the flour, baking soda, and salt on the counter. Should the chocolate already be chopped before I turn on the oven?
Yes, chop the unsweetened chocolate before you get moving so it's ready when you need it. Once that's handled, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
The oven is heating to 350, and the chocolate is chopped. What pans should I prepare?
Use 2 round 9 inch pans. Grease them well, then dust them with flour so the cake layers release cleanly after baking.
I greased both pans, but I'm not sure how much flour to leave in them after dusting.
Add a light coating of flour, rotate each pan so it covers the greased surface, then tap out the extra. You want a thin, even film rather than loose piles.
That makes sense. The pans are ready. Should I mix the dry ingredients in a bowl now?
Yes. Sift together the 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt into a bowl.
I sifted them once, but there are a few tiny bits left in the sifter. Is that okay?
A few small bits are fine, but press through any soft clumps so the flour, baking soda, and salt are evenly combined.
The dry mixture looks even now. Do I add the chopped chocolate to it?
Not yet. Set the sifted dry ingredients aside, and keep the 6 chopped unsweetened chocolate squares ready for a later step.
I want to make Date Nut Bars, but I'd like someone to keep me on track while I mix and bake them.

Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and gather the dry ingredients: 2 cups sugar, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need dates, nuts, eggs, butter, and vanilla for the batter.
I've got the sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt measured. Should the dates and nuts go in with those?
Yes. Add the dates and nuts to the same large bowl with the sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt, then stir everything together so the fruit and nuts are evenly coated.
The dates are a little sticky, but they're mixed through the dry ingredients now. What should I add next?
Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla to the bowl. Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened; don't worry if it feels hard to mix, because this batter is supposed to be very stiff.
It's definitely stiff and thick. I don't see dry flour anymore, though.
That sounds right. Grease a 15-in pan well, especially the corners, so the bars release cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. Any trick to spreading such a stiff batter?
Spoon the batter into the greased 15-in pan in several mounds, then press and spread it evenly across the pan. A lightly buttered spatula can help keep it from dragging.
It's spread out evenly now. What oven setting and time should I use?
Bake the Date Nut Bars at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes. Start checking near 20 minutes; they're ready when the top is golden brown.
If they're golden at the edges but a bit pale in the center, should I pull them?
Give them a few more minutes within that 20-25 minute window until the center also looks golden brown. Once baked, let the pan cool enough that the bars can set before cutting.
Broiled Egg Salad Sandwiches is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got hard-cooked eggs ready, but I'd like to go one small step at a time.
Absolutely. Chop 3 hard-cooked eggs and put them in a mixing bowl. Add 1/4 cup crushed saltine crackers, 1/4 cup chopped celery, and 1 tablespoon diced pimientos.
The eggs are chopped, and the celery is pretty finely cut. Should the crackers be powdery or still a little crumbly?
A little crumbly is ideal. Crush them enough to mix evenly, but they don't need to be a fine powder. Once they're in the bowl with the eggs, celery, and pimientos, give everything a gentle toss.
That bowl is mixed. I see the instructions mention a second bowl—what goes in there?
In the second bowl, combine the mayonnaise, milk, salt, garlic salt, and pepper. Stir until the dressing looks smooth and evenly seasoned.
I've mixed the dressing. It looks loose but creamy. Do I dump it all in at once?
Yes, stir the dressing into the egg mixture. Fold it in gently so the chopped eggs stay chunky while the crackers and celery get coated.
The filling is together now. It's scoopable and not runny. What should I prep for broiling?
Set out the muffin halves and an ungreased baking sheet. Spoon about 1/3 cup of the egg salad mixture onto each muffin half.
Should I spread the 1/3 cup flat or leave it mounded?
Spread it just enough to cover the muffin half evenly, with a slight mound in the center. That helps it sit neatly on the baking sheet.
They're all on the ungreased sheet. Anything else before they go under the broiler?
Make sure the portions are balanced and the muffin halves are stable on the sheet. Then they're ready for the broiler according to your recipe's broiling directions.
I'm making Broccoli Coleslaw and want to do it in a relaxed order. What should I set out first?
Set out 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, and 1/2 cup white sugar. You'll also need a small bowl for the dressing and a large bowl for the vegetables.
Got the oil, vinegar, sugar, and bowls. I also have the ramen package—do I use the seasoning?
Yes. Use 1 (3 ounce) package of chicken flavored ramen noodles. Crush the noodles, but keep the seasoning packet separate for the dressing.
Should I mix the dressing before I touch the vegetables?
That works well. In the small bowl, combine the olive oil, distilled white vinegar, white sugar, and the seasoning packet from the ramen noodles.
The sugar is sitting at the bottom a bit. How smooth does it need to be?
Mix it well so the seasoning is evenly distributed and the sugar starts dissolving into the oil and vinegar. It doesn't have to look creamy, just well combined.
Can I serve it soon, or does the dressing need time in the fridge?
Refrigerate the dressing at least one hour before serving. If you're planning ahead, overnight is also fine.
Before I continue with Broccoli Coleslaw, while that chills, what goes into the big bowl?
In the large bowl, combine the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds. Toss them together so the mix is evenly distributed.
I'm ready to add the crunchy part. Do the ramen noodles go in right before serving?
Yes, stir in the crushed ramen noodles when you're ready to finish the coleslaw, then add the chilled dressing and toss everything together before serving.
I'm making Brownie Mix in a Jar III today. What's the best place to start? I've got the jar ingredients out but want to go step by step.

Absolutely. For the jar mix, set out 1/2 cup flaked coconut, 1/2 cup white sugar, 2 cups packed brown sugar, and 2 cups all-purpose flour. Keep the flour handy because it gets mixed with salt and baking powder before the wet ingredients go in.
The coconut and both sugars are measured. Should I combine the flour with anything before I open the butter?
Yes. In your mixing bowl, stir the flour together with the salt and baking powder until they look evenly distributed. That keeps the batter from having salty or powdery pockets.
Done. The dry mixture looks even. I have regular butter and a tub of light margarine—does either work?
Use 3/4 cup butter or regular margarine, but don't use diet margarine. Add it to the dry mixture and work it in until the mixture starts coming together.
I used butter. It's a little thick and crumbly right now; is that expected before the eggs?
That's fine at this point. Slightly beat 2 eggs in a small bowl, then mix them in along with 2 teaspoons vanilla. The batter should loosen and become more spreadable as you stir.
The eggs and vanilla are in, and the batter is glossy but still pretty dense. What pan should I prep?
Spray a 9 x 13 inch metal pan well, especially the corners. Scrape the batter into the pan and spread it into an even layer so the edges and center bake consistently.
I'm spreading it now, but it's dragging a bit on the spatula. Any trick to get it into the corners?
Use short strokes and press rather than smear. If your spatula is sticking, lightly spray the spatula or use the back of a spoon to nudge the batter into the corners.
The pan is filled evenly. Anything I should clean up or check before it goes in?

Check that no dry flour remains in the bowl and that the batter is level in the sprayed 9 x 13 inch metal pan. Wipe any batter off the rim of the pan, then you're ready to bake according to your recipe's baking directions.

You can make a shallow thumbprint in the center of each patty. That helps them cook flatter on the grill without changing the seasoning plan.

Yes, lightly oil the grill grate right before the patties go on. Lay the burgers on the hot grate and cook for about 6 minutes total, turning once.

Do not press them down; that squeezes out juices. Just flip once and let the high heat do the browning.

Check the center with a thermometer and look for 160 degrees F, or 70 degrees C, unless you are intentionally cooking to another doneness. Pull them off when they hit that point and serve the Basil Burgers hot.
I'm making BBQ Chicken Wings and want to get the marinade set up without missing anything. Can you guide me?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and measure in 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce, 1 cup oyster sauce, 1/4 cup soy sauce, and 1/4 cup ketchup.
Those sauces are in the bowl. The recipe mentions more flavorings—what should go in before the wings?
Add the garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar to the bowl, then stir everything until the sauce looks evenly combined.

Yes, place the chicken wings directly in the bowl and turn them so they're well coated in the marinade.

In this BBQ Chicken Wings step, cover the bowl and refrigerate the wings for 8 hours or overnight so the marinade has time to soak in.

Preheat the grill for low heat, giving it a little time to settle so the wings cook gently rather than scorch.

Yes. Lightly oil the grill grate before adding the wings.

You've covered the listed prep: marinade mixed, wings marinated in the refrigerator, grill preheated on low heat, and grate lightly oiled. You're ready to place the wings on the grill.
Enchilada Style Burritos is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I'm starting with frozen bean and cheese burritos and want to keep the steps straight.

For Enchilada Style Burritos, you'll need 6 frozen prepared bean and cheese burritos, a greased 13-in baking dish, 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1 3/4 cups water.
I've got the burritos and the baking dish. Should they thaw at all before they go in?
No thawing needed. Place the frozen burritos directly in the greased 13-in baking dish, then set the dish aside while you make the sauce.
They're in the dish. I'm using butter—what size pan should I grab for the sauce?
Use a small to medium saucepan. Add the 2 tablespoons butter and melt it over the heat, keeping an eye on it so it melts without browning.
The butter is melted. Do I dump the flour in all at once or slowly?
Stir in the 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour and keep stirring until the mixture looks smooth, with no dry flour patches.
It's smooth now, kind of like a paste. How do I add the water without making lumps?
Gradually stir in the 1 3/4 cups water. Add a little at a time at first while stirring, then continue adding the rest as the mixture loosens.
The water is mixed in and it looks thinner. What texture am I waiting for?
Bring it to a boil, then cook and stir for 2 minutes, or until it thickens enough to coat the spoon lightly.
It has thickened after the 2 minutes. Is there anything else I should check before using it with the burritos?
Check that the sauce is smooth and evenly thickened, then it's ready for the burritos waiting in the greased dish. Give the saucepan a final stir so the texture is even before you pour or use it.
I'm about to start BBQ Chuck Roast. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a 5 pound chuck roast on the counter and want to make sure I start it right.
Absolutely. For this recipe, you'll need that 1 (5 pound) chuck roast, plus 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer.
I have the barbeque sauce and teriyaki sauce measured. Should I use a big mixing bowl for the marinade?
Yes, use a large bowl. Combine the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt, then stir until everything is evenly mixed.
For BBQ Chuck Roast, the marinade is mixed and smells pretty strong. Do I put the roast straight into that bowl?
Place the roast into the marinade so it's well coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate it for six hours, turning the roast often so all sides spend time in the marinade.
When I turn it during those six hours, should I just flip it with tongs and cover it again?
That's right. Use tongs to turn it, spoon a little marinade over any exposed spots if needed, then cover it again and return it to the refrigerator.
The roast has marinated for six hours. I'm getting the grill ready now—what setup do I want?
Preheat an outdoor grill for indirect heat. Set it up so the roast won't be sitting directly over the flame or hottest coals.
The grill is heating for indirect cooking. What do I do with the roast and the leftover marinade?
Remove the roast from the marinade, letting the excess drip back into the bowl, and pour the marinade into a saucepan.
So the roast goes toward the cooler side of the grill, and the marinade is saved in the saucepan?
Yes. Keep the grill arranged for indirect heat, move the marinated chuck roast out of the bowl, and keep that marinade in the saucepan for the next part of the cooking process.

The recipe simply says to press the crumbly mixture into the 9 inch square baking pan, so spread it across the bottom and press it into an even layer.

I have the onion, bell pepper, carrot, and garlic on the cutting board. Should the pot be heating while I finish slicing the carrot?
Yes. Put a large pot over medium heat and add the 2 tablespoons vegetable oil so it can warm while the carrot gets thinly sliced.
The carrot slices are thin now, and the oil has been warming for a minute. What should I look for before adding the vegetables?
Look for the oil to loosen and lightly shimmer across the bottom of the pot. Once it does, add the onion, green bell pepper, carrot, and garlic.
I like that garnish setup for this soup; the soft center with the crisp bit off to the side works better than an even sprinkle. The oil is shimmering now—do I add everything at once?
Yes, add the onion, bell pepper, carrot, and garlic together. Stir them right away so they get coated in the oil and start softening evenly.
They're in the pot and sizzling gently. Should I keep moving them constantly?
Stir occasionally rather than nonstop. Let the vegetables cook for 5 minutes, until the onion, bell pepper, carrot, and garlic are tender.
The onion is turning translucent and the carrot bends a little when I press it with the spoon. Is that tender enough?
That sounds right for moving on. Mix in 1 can of black beans and the chicken broth, scraping the bottom of the pot as you stir.
The beans and broth are in, and the bottom of the pot feels clean when I stir. What about the other can of beans?
Don't add the remaining can whole yet. Transfer those beans to a blender and puree them until smooth so they can thicken the soup.
Should I blend the beans with any broth from the pot, or just use the beans by themselves?
If the blender needs help catching, add a small splash of the soup broth, but keep the goal a smooth bean puree. Then stir that puree back into the pot.
The puree is smooth and stirred in. How should I serve it so it looks finished?
Ladle the soup into bowls once it looks cohesive and thickened. Add the soft topping in the middle, then place the crisp topping off to one side so the bowl has a deliberate, uneven finish.

messages.content: Bacon Wrapped Hotdogs is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track?
Absolutely. You'll need 10 hot dogs cut into thirds, 15 slices of bacon cut in half, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Have a slow cooker and toothpicks ready too.
I've got the hot dogs cut up, but I'm still slicing the bacon. Each strip just gets halved, right?
Yes, cut each bacon slice in half. Once that's done, wrap one half-slice of bacon around each hot dog piece.
Should the bacon overlap much when I wrap it?
A little overlap is fine. Wrap it snugly enough that it stays around the hot dog, then secure each one with a toothpick.
They're all wrapped and toothpicked. Do I need to brown them before the slow cooker?
No browning is needed for this recipe. Place the wrapped hot dog pieces into the slow cooker and set it to low heat.
Should I pile them in, or keep them in a single layer?
You can arrange them in the slow cooker without worrying about a perfect single layer. Try to spread them out enough so the brown sugar can reach them.
Okay, they're in. When does the brown sugar go on?
Pour the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar over the hot dogs now, coating the top as evenly as you can.
How long should I let them cook, and what am I watching for?
Cook them on low for 5 to 6 hours, until the bacon is cooked through. Before serving, keep the toothpicks visible so people can remove them easily.
I want to make Curried Winter Squash. I already have cooked squash, but I need help keeping the steps organized.
Great. Measure out 3 cups of cooked, mashed winter squash and put it near a medium microwave-safe bowl. You'll also need 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder.
The squash is mashed and measured, and I found the curry powder. What else should be on the counter?
Set out 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, plus 2 tablespoons maple syrup. Those are the remaining main ingredients for the squash mixture.
Should the butter be melted before I add it, or can it go in as-is?
It can go in as-is if it's soft enough to stir in, since the microwave will heat everything through. If it's very cold, cut it into smaller pieces so it blends more evenly.
Okay, I've got the medium bowl ready. What goes into it together?
Add the mashed winter squash, curry powder, butter or margarine, and maple syrup to the bowl. Stir until the curry and syrup are evenly worked through the squash.
It's mixed, but the top looks a little streaky from the curry. Is that fine before microwaving?
Give it a few more folds, scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl, so the seasoning is distributed. Once it looks mostly uniform, it's ready to heat.
The mixture looks even now. How long should it be in the microwave?
Microwave it on high until heated through, about 5 minutes. If your microwave heats unevenly, pause partway through and stir, then continue heating.
It's hot now. I noticed the recipe mentions coconut—do I need it?
Coconut is optional. If you want it, sprinkle some on top just before serving; otherwise, spoon the Curried Winter Squash into a serving dish and serve it warm.
I'm making Aaahh Potato Soup and I've got a large pot out. Can you help me get organized before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Set out 2 cubed Yukon Gold potatoes, 1 (5.5 ounce) package of au gratin instant potato mix, 1 (10.5 ounce) can of condensed chicken broth, and 1 1/2 cups water.
The potatoes are cubed, and the au gratin mix is open. Should everything go in the pot dry, or do I start with the liquids?
You can put them all in together: the cubed potatoes, the au gratin potato mix, the condensed chicken broth, and the water. Use a large saucepan or pot so there's room to stir.
It looks a little thick already. Should the potatoes be fully under the liquid?
Yes, check the level once everything is combined. If the potatoes aren't covered, add just enough extra water to cover them.
They're covered now. What heat should I use, and do I need to keep stirring constantly?
Put the pot over medium heat. Stir occasionally so the mix doesn't settle or stick, but you don't need to stand there stirring nonstop.
About how long should I plan for this to cook?
Let it cook until the potatoes are tender, about 40 minutes. A fork should slide into the potato cubes easily when they're ready.
If it thickens too much while it cooks, is it okay to loosen it with water?
Yes, if it gets too thick before the potatoes are tender, add a small splash of water and stir it in, keeping the heat at medium.
The potatoes are soft now. I noticed the recipe says cream at the end, but I don't see an amount listed—how should I handle that?
Stir in the cream gently at the end and heat it through without boiling hard. Since no amount is given, add it gradually until the soup looks creamy and smooth, then serve it hot.

Keep the milk chocolate finish centered on the poured buttercrunch, and leave the crisp almondy edge visible off to one side. For setup, measure 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips, then butter a large cookie sheet so it is ready for the hot candy.
The cookie sheet is buttered, and I've got the saucepan on the stove but not heated yet. Which ingredients go into the pan first?
Add the butter, white sugar, and the 1 cup chopped almonds to the saucepan together. Keep the heat low at the start so the butter can melt while you stir the sugar and almonds evenly through it.
I've added those, and the butter is just starting to melt around the almonds. Should the chocolate chips be nearby now?
Yes, keep the 2 cups milk chocolate chips close, but don't add them to the saucepan. They are for the softer chocolate finish after the buttercrunch is poured onto the buttered sheet.
I like that centered chocolate finish with the crunchy almondy part left to one side; that's exactly what I wanted for this dessert. What texture am I watching for while it heats?
At first it will look grainy and uneven, with melted butter pooling around the sugar and chopped almonds. Stir constantly over low heat until the mixture fully comes together and reaches a boil.
It's thicker now, glossy in spots, and I'm seeing bubbles starting near the edge. Do I keep moving the spoon through it?
Keep stirring only until it is truly boiling across the mixture. Once it boils, stop stirring, and do not shake or jostle the saucepan.
I've stopped stirring, and the thermometer is clipped on. What temperature range am I aiming for?
Cook it to 300 to 310 degrees F, or 149 to 154 degrees C. You can also check by dropping a small amount of syrup into cold water; it should form hard, brittle threads.
The thermometer is climbing slowly, and I'm worried about scorching. Should I scrape the bottom at all now?
No, not after the boil. Let it cook undisturbed, watch the temperature closely, and keep your buttered cookie sheet clear so you can pour right away when it reaches the hard-crack stage.
It just hit 300, and the cold-water drop snapped into brittle threads. What's the safest move from here?
Take the saucepan off the heat carefully and pour the hot mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet immediately. Spread or tilt it just enough to make an even layer without overworking the candy.
It's on the sheet and still warm. How should I handle the chocolate chips so the middle stays softer?

Scatter the 2 cups milk chocolate chips mainly over the center of the warm buttercrunch so they soften there, then smooth that center area gently. Keep one side more open so the crisp almond buttercrunch remains visible, and let the candy set until firm before breaking it up.

A few clumps are fine. Break up the bigger ones with your fingers or a spoon, then toss the cheese through the flour so it is spread out before the milk and egg go in.

Perfect. Once the wet mixture is smooth, start stirring in more flour a little at a time, using the remaining flour only until the dough turns soft and begins pulling together.

Add small handfuls rather than dumping in the rest. Stop when the dough is soft, holds together, and feels tacky but not like batter; you may not need every bit if it firms up first.

That is the point to switch to your hands. Gather it into a loose ball, sprinkle the counter with flour, and turn the dough out onto the floured surface.

I'd like to make Festive Shortbread Logs. Can you guide me while I set up?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and 2 cups all-purpose flour.

A mixer will make creaming easier, but a sturdy spoon works too if the butter is truly softened. Put the butter and confectioners' sugar into a mixing bowl and beat or stir until they look smooth and creamy.
It's coming together, but I still see a few streaks of sugar. Is that okay?
Keep creaming a little longer until the mixture looks evenly blended and soft. It doesn't need to be fluffy like cake batter, just smooth and combined.
Okay, the butter and sugar look smooth now. I have the vanilla open.
Add the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the bowl and mix it in until the dough base looks even again.
Vanilla is mixed in. The flour is measured, but I'm worried about dumping it all in at once.
Good instinct. Add the 2 cups all-purpose flour gradually, a bit at a time, mixing after each addition so it blends in cleanly and the dough doesn't puff flour everywhere.
The flour is mostly in, and the dough feels thick. Should I keep mixing?
Mix just until the flour is fully incorporated and the dough looks uniform. Once there are no dry patches, stop so the shortbread stays tender.
The dough is ready. How do I shape the cookies without them sticking all over my hands?
Lightly flour your hands, then scoop tablespoonfuls of batter and shape them into cookies. Keep the flour light—just enough to prevent sticking while you form the shortbread logs.
I'm setting up for Crustless Spinach Quiche 2; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Here, set out 3 ounces reduced fat cream cheese and let it be softened before mixing. You'll also need 1 cup fat-free milk, 1 cup egg substitute, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.

Beat the cream cheese in the small mixing bowl until it loosens up and looks creamy enough to blend without big lumps.

Add the fat-free milk along with the egg substitute and pepper, then beat everything together until the mixture looks smooth.

A little foam is fine. Keep beating just until the base is evenly combined; you don't need to whip extra air into it.

Stir in the remaining ingredients gently so they're distributed through the cream cheese, milk, egg substitute, and pepper mixture.
Everything is mixed together. How do I transfer it without making a mess?
Pour or spoon the mixture into the prepared quiche pan coated with nonstick cooking spray, scraping the bowl with a spatula so the filling settles evenly.

Break the Parmesan cheese by hand into uneven pieces for the part that goes into the spinach and the part that tops the bake. Also get a towel or strainer ready, because the thawed spinach needs to be drained and squeezed very well before it goes in the bowl.
Got it. I have three frozen spinach packs thawed, but I want to make sure that matches the recipe.
Yes, use 3 packages of frozen chopped spinach, 10 ounces each. After thawing, press out as much moisture as you can so the bake holds together instead of getting watery.
The spinach is squeezed pretty dry and sitting in my mixing bowl. What goes with the eggs?
Beat 3 eggs in a separate bowl with 1/2 teaspoon onion salt and 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg. Whisk until the seasoning looks evenly blended through the eggs.
I like those rough Parmesan pieces here—that's exactly what I wanted for this dish. The egg mixture is ready; should I pour it straight onto the spinach?
Yes, pour the beaten eggs over the squeezed spinach. Add 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, then mix well so the spinach is coated with the egg, onion salt, nutmeg, and cheese.
Some of the spinach is still packed into little clumps from squeezing it. Is that a problem?
Break the clumps apart with a fork while you mix. You don't need it perfectly smooth, but the eggs and 1/4 cup Parmesan should reach through the whole bowl.
The bowl looks evenly mixed now. I'm looking at the bread crumbs—do they go in with the spinach too?
Keep the bread crumbs out of the spinach mixture. Combine the bread crumbs with the remaining Parmesan cheese so they can become the topping.
Should I crumble more Parmesan into that topping bowl, or use the finer bits left on the cutting board?

Use both if you have them: the finer bits help cover the surface, and the larger hand-broken pieces give the topping a more rustic texture. Toss them gently with the bread crumbs rather than crushing them smaller.
The spinach mixture is in the baking dish. Do I pack it down before adding the topping?
Spread it into an even layer, but don't press it hard. Then scatter the bread crumb and remaining-Parmesan mixture over the top instead of stirring it in.

Leave the surface a little uneven and don't smooth the topping flat. Once the squeezed spinach, beaten egg mixture, 1/4 cup Parmesan, bread crumbs, and remaining Parmesan are assembled that way, it's ready to bake according to your usual setup.
I'm making Coq au Vin alla Italiana and have a large skillet ready. Can you help me pace the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 4 pounds of dark meat chicken pieces, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 5 cloves of crushed garlic, and 1/2 cup all-purpose flour so everything is within reach.
The chicken is still a little damp from the package. Should I do anything before it hits the flour?
Pat the chicken pieces dry with paper towels. That will help the flour cling and help the pieces brown instead of steaming in the skillet.
Got it. I've got the flour in a shallow dish—what should go into it?
Season the 1/2 cup all-purpose flour with poultry seasoning, then stir it around so the seasoning is evenly spread through the flour.
The flour is seasoned. Should I start heating the pan now or coat the chicken first?
Start heating the skillet now. Add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to the large skillet and let it warm while you keep the chicken nearby for dredging.
The oil is shimmering a bit. Where does the garlic come in?
Add 1/2 of the crushed garlic to the skillet and let it hit the oil briefly, just enough to start smelling fragrant without letting it burn.
The garlic smells good. I'm ready to put the chicken in, but I don't want the coating too thick.
Dredge each chicken piece in the seasoned flour, shake off the excess, and place the pieces into the skillet in a single layer if you can.
The chicken is in the skillet. How long am I browning it before I check?
Brown the chicken parts in the skillet for 4 or 5 minutes, looking for a golden surface before you turn or move them.
I'm making Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles and I've got chicken out. Can you talk me through it as I cook?
Absolutely. Check that you have 2 teaspoons olive oil, 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves, 1 (10 ounce) can of refrigerated large crescent roll dough, and 8 ounces Brie cheese ready to go.
The chicken and Brie are in the fridge, and the crescent dough is still chilled. Should I start with the pan?
Yes. Put a heavy skillet on the stove and heat the 2 teaspoons olive oil in it. If you're using a nonstick frying pan instead, you can spray it with cooking spray rather than using the oil.
I'm using the heavy skillet. How hot should I let the oil get before adding the chicken?
Let it warm until the oil looks loose and shimmery in the pan, then add the 4 chicken breast halves in a single layer so they sauté instead of steaming.
The chicken is in. What am I watching for so I don't pull it too early?
Sauté the chicken breasts until they're no longer pink and the juices run clear. Once they reach that point, move them off the heat and set them aside.
They look cooked through and I've set them on a plate. Should the oven be on now?
Go ahead and bring the oven up to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), while the chicken rests.
Oven is heating. Do I open the crescent dough while I'm waiting?
Yes. Open the 1 (10 ounce) can of refrigerated large crescent roll dough and unroll 4 large crescent rolls on your work surface.
The 4 crescent rolls are unrolled. Should I keep the Brie nearby for assembling the bundles?
Keep the 8 ounces Brie cheese close by, along with the cooked chicken, so you're set up to assemble the Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles once the oven reaches 375 degrees F.

Make 3 small garnish clusters around the platter so it feels intentional without covering the chicken and potatoes.

Cut up the 1 (3 1/2) pound broiler-fryer chicken if it isn't already, and cut the 1 pound new potatoes into chunks.
The chicken is cut and the potatoes are in chunks. What else should I pull out so I'm not scrambling later?
Have 2 tablespoons cooking oil ready for browning, plus 1 cup half-and-half cream for the pan sauce. Keep salt and pepper nearby too.
I've got a large skillet out. Should the oil go in before the chicken and potatoes?
Yes. Set the large skillet over medium heat, add the cooking oil, then brown the chicken and potato chunks together in the oil for 10-15 minutes.
If the pan looks crowded, what should I watch for while they brown?
Give the pieces enough contact with the skillet to pick up color, turning them as needed. You're looking for browned surfaces on the chicken and potatoes during that 10-15 minute window.
They've got some color now, and there are drippings in the skillet. Do I leave everything in?
Lift the chicken and potatoes out of the skillet and set them aside for the moment, leaving the drippings behind.
There's more fat in the pan than I want for the cream. How much should stay?
Pour off the excess and keep only 1 tablespoon of drippings in the skillet.
Okay, the pan is down to that amount. How do I make the sauce and bring it back to the platter idea?

Add the 1 cup half-and-half cream to the drippings, season with salt and pepper, and stir to mix. When you plate the chicken and potatoes, keep the top mostly open and place those 3 small garnish clusters around the shared platter.
I want to make Fig Bars II today. Can you guide me while I set up the ingredients and pan?
Absolutely. Have 1 cup white sugar, 3 eggs, 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking powder ready. You'll also want a large mixing bowl, a sifter, and a 9x13 inch baking pan.
I've got the sugar, eggs, flour, and baking powder measured. Should the oven be heating before I mix anything?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C. That way it's ready by the time the batter is mixed.
The oven is on. I'm using a metal 9x13 pan—what should I do to keep the bars from sticking?
Grease the 9x13 inch baking pan well, then dust it with flour and tap out any extra. Try to coat the corners and sides, not just the bottom.
Pan is greased and floured. For the eggs and sugar, am I looking for a certain texture?
In a large bowl, beat the 3 eggs with the 1 cup white sugar until the mixture turns thick and pale. It should look lighter in color and a bit fuller than when you started.
It's paler now and ribbons a little when the beaters lift. Do I sift the dry ingredients straight in?

Sift together the 7/8 cup all-purpose flour and 1 teaspoon baking powder, along with the salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice called for in the directions. Sifting helps them blend evenly before they go into the egg mixture.
The dry ingredients are sifted. Should I dump them all in or fold them gradually?
Add the sifted mixture to the beaten eggs and sugar, then blend it in gently. Include the vanilla at this point too, and mix just until everything is incorporated.
The batter looks smooth with no dry streaks. Is there anything I should check before it goes into the pan?

Scrape the bowl once to make sure no flour is hiding at the bottom, then spread the batter evenly into the prepared 9x13 inch pan. Since the recipe steps stop after mixing, the next practical move is to bake it in the preheated 325 degrees F oven and watch for the bars to set.
