messages.content: I pulled up Cabbage Kielbasa Supper. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got the cooker out but want to prep in the right order.
Absolutely. Use a 5-qt. slow cooker for this one. Start by shredding 8 cups of cabbage, then cut 3 medium potatoes into 1/2 inch cubes.
The cabbage is shredded and the potatoes are cubed. Should I chop the onion before loading the slow cooker?
Yes. Chop 1 medium onion, then add the cabbage, potatoes, and onion to the slow cooker. Season them with 1 3/4 teaspoons salt and pepper.
The cooker is already looking pretty full with the vegetables. Is that okay?
That's expected for Cabbage Kielbasa Supper. The cabbage starts bulky, but it will cook down as the slow cooker runs.
Everything is in with the salt and pepper. Where does the broth go?
Pour the broth evenly over the cabbage, potatoes, and onion so it can settle down through the vegetables.
Broth is in. I have the kielbasa ready—do I stir it into the cabbage?
Don't stir it in. Place the sausage on top of the vegetables; it can sit above the cabbage while everything cooks down.
The sausage is on top and the lid just fits. What setting and time should I use?
Cover it and cook on low for 8-9 hours, until the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through.
When I check it near the end, what texture should I be looking for in the potatoes and cabbage?
The potatoes should be tender when pierced, and the cabbage should be softened and reduced. If that's true and the sausage is heated through, it's ready to serve.
I want to make Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats with the baked potatoes I already have. Can you guide me through it?

Absolutely. Set out 4 medium baked potatoes, quartered lengthwise, plus 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing, 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, and sliced green onions if you want them for topping.
The potatoes are baked and quartered. Should I heat the oven before I start filling them?
Yes, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F so it's ready while you assemble the potato boats.
Oven is heating. For the potato quarters, am I removing all the potato or leaving some in the skins?
Scoop the potato out of the skins, working gently so the skins stay intact enough to hold the filling.
On Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats, the skins are hollowed out. Where does the Ranch go?
Brush or spoon the Ranch onto the inside of the potato skins, using the 1/3 cup to coat them evenly.
They're coated inside. Do I put the scooped potato back now?
Yes. Place the scooped potato back into the coated skins, keeping each quarter shaped like a little boat.
The filling is back in the skins. How much cheese should go on top?
Sprinkle the 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese over the potato boats, dividing it across all the pieces.
Cheddar is on. Are the green onions required, or just for serving?
They're optional. Add sliced green onions at the end if you want a fresh topping, then serve the cheesy potato boats warm.
I want to make Black Forest Dump Cake II. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start?
Absolutely. Put out 1 (21 ounce) can cherry pie filling, 1 (16.5 ounce) can pitted dark sweet cherries, 1 (18.25 ounce) package chocolate cake mix, and 1 cup chopped walnuts.
I found the cherries and cake mix. What pan and oven temperature should I be using?
Use a 9x13 baking dish, and get the oven preheating to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
The oven is heating. Should I grease the dish before the fruit goes in?
Yes, spray the 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray so the fruit layer is easier to serve later.
The dish is sprayed. The cherry pie filling is thick—do I just pour it in?
Dump the cherry pie filling into the prepared dish, then spread it evenly across the bottom with a spatula or spoon.
It's spread out, though the edges are a little thinner than the middle.
That is fine; just nudge a bit of the filling toward the corners so the bottom layer is fairly even.
I'm opening the pitted dark sweet cherries now. Should I drain the can?
Do not drain them for this step. Repeat the fruit layer with the pitted dark sweet cherries, including the juice.
So the cherry juice goes right over the pie filling in the same dish?
Yes. Pour the cherries and their juice over the cherry pie filling, then spread them gently so the fruit is distributed across the dish.
I'd like to make Artichoke Hummus. Can you help me get set up at the food processor?
Absolutely. Set out the food processor bowl and start with 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, drained, plus 1 clove garlic.
The chickpeas are drained and the garlic is peeled. What else goes in?
Add 1/2 cup drained marinated artichoke hearts and measure out 2 tablespoons lemon juice.
Should the artichoke hearts be chopped before I add them?
They can go in as they are if your processor is a standard size. Just make sure they're drained so the hummus doesn't get too loose.
Everything is in the processor bowl except the lemon juice. Is that okay to add now?
Yes, pour in the 2 tablespoons lemon juice now. The recipe has you combine all ingredients except parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks in the work bowl of the food processor.
The lid is on. How long should I pulse it?
Pulse in short bursts until the mixture becomes smooth, stopping to scrape down the sides if needed so the chickpeas and artichokes blend evenly.
It's mostly smooth, but I can still see a few small bits near the edge.
Scrape those bits back toward the blade, then pulse a few more times until the texture looks smooth throughout.
The hummus looks smooth now. What should I do with it before serving?
Transfer it to a serving bowl, cover it, and refrigerate until you're ready to serve.
I'm ready to cook Date Loaf Cake. What should be ready before I begin? I've got the loaf pan out, but I want to make sure I prep it in the right order.
Absolutely. For this Date Loaf Cake, you'll need 1 cup dates, pitted and chopped, 1 cup dark brown sugar, 1/4 cup margarine, and 1 cup boiling water.
The dates are chopped, and I have dark brown sugar and margarine ready. Should I turn on the oven before mixing anything?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's ready while the date mixture rests.
Oven is heating. My pan is a 9x5 inch loaf pan—does it need anything before I fill it later?
Grease and flour that 9x5 inch loaf pan now. It'll help the loaf release cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. For the mixing bowl, do the dates go in before the boiling water?
Use a large bowl and add the chopped dates, dark brown sugar, and margarine. Then pour in the 1 cup boiling water.
I'm pouring the boiling water in now. Should I stir until the margarine melts?
Give it a careful stir so the brown sugar starts dissolving and the margarine softens into the hot mixture.
The bowl is hot and the dates are soaking. What texture am I looking for at this point?
It should be a warm, loose date mixture with the sugar mostly dissolved and the margarine melting through. The dates will soften as it sits.
Okay, I'll leave it on the counter. How long should the mixture stand before I do anything else?
Let the mixture stand for 15 minutes. That gives the dates time to soften and the hot mixture time to settle before the next stage.
I'm making Fried Beef Ribs today. Can you help me set up so I don't miss anything before the oil gets hot?

Absolutely. Set up 3 quarts peanut oil for frying, plus the seasoning: 2 tablespoons salt, 3 tablespoons coarse ground black pepper, and 2 tablespoons cayenne pepper. You'll also want bowls ready for the seasoning mix, flour, and eggs.
I've got the peanut oil and spices out. Should I start heating the fryer before mixing the bowls?
Yes. Pour the peanut oil into the deep-fryer and heat it to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it comes up to temperature, you can organize the coating stations.
The fryer is climbing toward 375, and I have a medium bowl free for the spices. What goes in there?
In that medium bowl, combine the salt, coarse ground black pepper, cayenne pepper, garlic salt, and onion salt. Stir them well so the heat and seasoning are evenly mixed.
The seasoning blend is mixed. I'm trying to keep the counter tidy—where should the flour go?
Put the flour in its own separate bowl or on a plate. Keep it apart from the seasoning bowl so the dredging setup stays easy to manage.
Flour is on a plate next to the spice bowl. Do the eggs need to be beaten in something wide?
Use a large bowl for the eggs and whisk them until the yolks and whites are fully combined. A wider bowl makes dipping the ribs easier.
The eggs are whisked. Can you recap the station order before I bring the ribs over?

You're set up with the seasoning mixture in a medium bowl, flour on a separate plate or bowl, and whisked eggs in a large bowl. Keep the fryer steady at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, before frying.
The oil is at temperature now. Any last safety or texture checks before I start cooking the ribs?

Make sure the oil stays at 375 degrees F and avoid crowding the fryer. Lower the ribs in carefully, keep the coating stations close but not near the hot oil, and have a tray ready for the fried beef ribs when they come out.

messages.content: I'm putting Bahama Mama II into a one-off gift box setup with fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, and other desserts. For this presentation, what should I do on top?
For this batch, give it a light glaze across the whole surface, but keep one corner unglazed.
Perfect, that's only for this gift-box version. I'm ready to mix the drink too—what should I measure first?
Measure 1 fluid ounce of dark rum and 1/2 fluid ounce of apricot brandy, and have a mixing glass ready.
The mixing glass is out. Should those go straight in, or should I set up the rest before pouring?
Set up the rest first so the drink comes together smoothly: 3 1/2 fluid ounces fruit punch and 1/2 fluid ounce pina colada mix.
I've got the fruit punch and pina colada mix measured. Do I need a shaker, or is stirring enough here?
Stirring is enough for Bahama Mama II. Pour the dark rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and pina colada mix into the mixing glass.
They're all in the glass. How blended should it look before serving?
Stir until the pina colada mix is evenly worked through and the color looks consistent, with no thicker streaks clinging to the glass.
That looks smooth now. Should I add ice to the mixing glass or the serving glass?
Put the ice in the serving glass, then pour the blended Bahama Mama II over it.
I'm serving it beside the dessert platter. Any garnish or extra topping needed for the drink?
The recipe doesn't call for a garnish, so keep it simple and serve it over ice as mixed.
Got it. Just to confirm, the drink itself is done once it's stirred and poured over ice?
Yes. Once the rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and pina colada mix are stirred together and served over ice, Bahama Mama II is ready.
Can you help me cook Biriyani today? I've got a large skillet out and want to make sure I start in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons plain yogurt, 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar, and 1 medium onion, sliced. Keep the skillet nearby for cooking over medium heat.
The oil, yogurt, vinegar, and sliced onion are ready. Should the skillet be hot before anything goes in?
Yes. Put the large skillet over medium heat, then add the 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil and let it warm so it spreads easily across the pan.
The oil is shimmering lightly but not smoking. Do I add the onion yet or the yogurt mixture?
Add the 3 tablespoons plain yogurt and 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar to the skillet with the warm oil, and stir them in gently.
It looks a little loose and glossy in the pan. Is that okay before the onion goes in?
That's fine. Add the 1 medium sliced onion now, spreading it through the skillet so it cooks evenly in the yogurt-vinegar mixture.
The onion slices are starting to soften around the edges. How tender should they get?
Cook them until they're tender throughout, stirring occasionally so they soften without sticking to the skillet.
The onions are soft now and the mixture is coating them. What should I have ready for the next addition?
Have the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes ready to go in together. Once the onion is tender, mix those into the skillet.
They're in the pan now. Should I stir hard or just fold everything together?
Stir steadily but not aggressively, just enough to combine the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes with the tender onions and the yogurt-vinegar mixture.

messages.content: For today, I'm turning Chocolate Madeleines into a platter-style salad and adding cheese right before serving. What's the best way to treat the cheese?
Leave the cheese chilled until the end, then make thin shavings and scatter them over just one side of the platter.
Great, I'll keep that for serving. Before I start mixing, what dry ingredients should I set out?
Set out 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
I've got the flour and cocoa measured. Should the oven be on already?
Yes—preheat it to 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, so it's ready when the batter is mixed.
Oven is heating. Which pan am I using, and how should I prep it?
Use one Madeleine pan and butter it well, getting into each shell-shaped indentation.
The pan is buttered. I'm looking at the dry bowl now—what texture am I aiming for?
Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together until the mixture looks fine, even, and free of cocoa lumps.
The dry mix looks smooth. What happens with the butter side of things?
Cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until they're blended into a soft, cohesive mixture.
Should I worry about the cheese while the madeleine mixture is coming together?
Not yet. Keep it cold and unshaved for now so it stays firm for those thin pieces at serving.
That helps. Before I clean up, can you recap the order so I don't miss anything?

Preheat to 375 degrees F / 190 degrees C, butter one Madeleine pan, sift together the 1/4 cup flour, 1/4 cup cocoa, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and pinch of salt, then cream the butter with the vanilla and sugar. Save the chilled cheese for thin shavings on one side of the platter right before serving.

messages.content: Tonight I'm packing Easy Fried Eggplant as part of a brothy bowl for later, so I want the special packed version just this time. How should I handle the finish?
For this packed bowl, keep both garnishes in separate small containers, then add them only after the bowl has been reheated.
Great, that's exactly what I need for this one. Before I heat anything, what should I pull out first?
Set up 2 tablespoons canola oil and 1 large eggplant, peeled and sliced. You'll also want a large skillet ready for the oil.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced, and the skillet is on the stove. What do I need for the coating station?
Put 3 eggs, beaten, in one shallow dish and 2 cups dry bread crumbs in another so you can dip the slices cleanly.
Coating dishes are ready. How hot should the skillet be before I start dipping?
Heat the canola oil in the large skillet over medium-high heat until it's hot enough to sizzle when the coated eggplant goes in.
Oil is heating. Do I coat all the slices the same way?
Yes. Dip each eggplant slice into the beaten egg first, then press it into the dry bread crumbs so it's coated before it goes into the hot oil.
I've got the first batch coated and in the pan. What texture and color am I watching for?
Fry the slices for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, until the bread crumbs turn golden brown and the eggplant feels tender inside.
The first side is golden, and I'm turning them carefully. Should I crowd the remaining slices?
Keep them in a single layer if you can. If the skillet is full, work in batches so the coating fries instead of steaming.
Last batch is browned. How do I keep them from getting greasy before packing the bowl?
Move the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain. Once it has shed the excess oil, pack it with your brothy bowl components and keep those two garnishes separate until after reheating.
I'm making Crab Cake Sauce to go with dinner. Can you talk me through it from the ingredients onward?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, and 1/3 cup hot salsa. You'll also need a blender for getting the sauce smooth.
I've got the blender ready. Should the sour cream and mayo go in before the chunky things?
Yes, that will help it blend easily. Add the sour cream and mayonnaise to the blender first, then spoon in the cottage cheese and hot salsa.
The cottage cheese is in. The recipe mentions cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt too—do those go in now?
They do. Add the cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt to the blender with the sour cream, mayonnaise, cottage cheese, and salsa.
For Crab Cake Sauce, everything is in the blender. What texture am I aiming for?
Puree it until the sauce is smooth, with no obvious cottage cheese curds left. Stop and scrape down the sides if any thick spots cling to the blender jar.
It's blending but still has a few tiny flecks from the salsa. Is that okay?
Tiny salsa flecks are fine; the main goal is a smooth, creamy base. If the dairy is fully blended and it pours or spoons evenly, you're there.
The sauce looks creamy now. Should I serve it right away with the crab cakes?
Chill it before serving. Transfer it to a covered bowl or container and put it in the refrigerator so the sauce firms up slightly and tastes cool with the crab cakes.
I'll refrigerate it. Any serving tip once it's cold?
Give it a quick stir after chilling, then spoon it into a small serving bowl alongside the crab cakes. Keep it cold until it's time to eat.
I'm starting Banana Chip Muffins I; can you walk me through the setup? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to set up the dry ingredients first.
Absolutely. Measure 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour into your large bowl, then add 1/2 cup white sugar. Give the bowl a little shake so the ingredients sit evenly before you add the rest.
Flour and sugar are in. I'm checking the leavening and salt now—how much should I measure?
In this Banana Chip Muffins I step, add 1 tablespoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt to that same large bowl.
Done. The recipe name says banana chip muffins, but I don't see a chocolate chip amount here. Should I still add them?

Yes—use the recipe's direction and measure the chocolate chips into the large bowl with the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Since no amount is listed here, just don't invent a measurement; use whatever amount your recipe source provides or the amount you planned to use.
The dry bowl has flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and chocolate chips. Should I stir hard or just fold it together?
Mix it thoroughly so the baking powder and salt are evenly spread through the flour. Once it looks consistent, make a well in the center of the dry mixture.
I made the well. For the egg, do I crack it straight into the center or use another bowl?
Use a small bowl for the egg. Beat it there until it looks frothy, then you'll be ready to combine it with the wet ingredients.
The egg is frothy. I have cooking oil, milk, and bananas nearby—do they go into the egg bowl?
Here, mix the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the frothy egg until the wet mixture is combined.
The banana mixture is together now. Before I pour, should the dry ingredients still have that center well?
Yes, keep the well in the dry ingredients. Pour or add the egg, oil, milk, and banana mixture into that center area, then continue with the muffin batter from there.
I want to get Absolutely Awesome BBQ Sauce right. What should I handle first? I've got a saucepan out and want to make sure I measure everything correctly.

Absolutely. Measure 1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup chile sauce, 1/2 cup rum, and 1/4 cup soy sauce. You'll also be mixing in ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, dry mustard, and pepper once the pan is on the stove.
The brown sugar is packed in the cup, and the chile sauce, rum, and soy sauce are measured. Should the pan be hot before I add them?

Set the saucepan over low heat before you start combining everything. Add the brown sugar, chile sauce, rum, soy sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, dry mustard, and pepper, then stir so the sugar starts dissolving into the liquids.
It's all in the saucepan, but the brown sugar is clumping a little. Is that okay at low heat?
Yes, that's fine. Keep the heat low and stir steadily for a minute or two; the clumps should loosen as the sauce warms. Scrape along the bottom and corners so the sugar doesn't sit in one spot.
The sauce is smoother now and starting to smell strong from the rum and spices. Do I raise the heat?
Keep it gentle rather than turning it up high. Let it come to a low simmer, then simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally so it thickens evenly and doesn't scorch.
When you say occasionally, how often should I stir during the 30 minutes?
Give it a stir every few minutes, especially around the sides and bottom of the saucepan. You're looking for a steady simmer, not a hard boil.
The 30 minutes are up, and it looks glossy and a bit thicker. What should I do before putting it away?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the BBQ sauce cool. Once it's no longer hot, transfer it to a clean container.
I've got a jar ready. Should I serve it now or chill it first?
You can use a little right away if you like, but the recipe's final step is to refrigerate it until ready to use. Seal the jar, chill it, and give it a stir before serving.
Apple Butter V is on deck today. What should I do first? Can you help me get set up before I start cooking?
Absolutely. For this apple butter, set out 6 pounds of tart apples, cored and sliced, plus 6 cups of apple cider. You'll also want a Dutch oven ready since the apples start there.
The sliced tart apples are ready, and I have the cider. Are there any ingredients I should measure now?
Yes—measure 3 cups of white sugar and 2 teaspoons of ground cinnamon so they're ready when you need them.
I've got the Dutch oven on the stove. Do the apples go in before any liquid?
Yes. Put the cored, sliced apples directly into the Dutch oven.
The pot is pretty full with the 6 pounds of apples. Should I add all the cider at once?
Pour in the full 6 cups of apple cider over the apples. It will help them cook down and soften.
Cider is in. What heat should I use to get this moving?
Bring the apple and cider mixture to a boil, then keep it cooking over medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
After about 30 minutes, what texture am I looking for before I stop cooking?
The apples should be soft enough to press easily, with the mixture looking loosened and tender rather than firm slices floating in cider.
They're soft now. What tool do I use to make it smooth?
Press the softened apple mixture through a food mill. That's the finishing step for this stage of Apple Butter V.
I have Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a pot ready but want to make sure I add things in the right order.

Absolutely. Set up your Fast Chicken Soup Base first, since that's the foundation of the soup. You'll also need 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, 2 medium zucchini diced, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
The soup base is made. Should the tomatoes be drained before they go in?

Use the diced tomatoes as part of the soup mixture; add the 1 (14.5 ounce) can when the base is simmering. The recipe doesn't call for draining, so keep the tomato juices unless you specifically want a less tomato-rich broth.
Got it. The zucchini is diced too. How hot should the soup base be before I add the tortellini?
Bring the prepared Fast Chicken Soup Base to a gentle simmer—not a hard boil. You want steady small bubbles so the tortellini can cook without getting roughed up.
It's simmering gently now. Do I add everything at once?
Yes. Stir in the 1 9-ounce package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 1 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes, the 2 medium diced zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
Everything is in the pot. Should I keep the lid on while it cooks?
Let it simmer gently for 10-20 minutes until the tortellini and zucchini are tender. You can leave the lid slightly ajar if you want to limit splattering while still letting you watch the texture.
How will I know the zucchini is done without turning mushy?
Check it with a spoon or fork around the 10-minute mark. It should be tender enough to bite easily but still hold its diced shape; keep simmering only as needed, up to 20 minutes total.
The tortellini look puffed and the zucchini is tender. Is it ready to serve?
Yes, once everything is tender, the soup is ready. Give it a gentle stir, taste the broth, and ladle it into bowls while the tortellini are still soft and hot.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: Caramelized Apple Bites is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got a microwave and a couple of apples ready.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 individually wrapped caramels, unwrapped and chopped, plus 2 tablespoons light corn syrup for the coating.
I found the caramels and corn syrup. Should I prep the apples before melting anything?
Yes, prep them now so they're ready to toss right away: use 2 apples, peeled, cored, and diced.
The apples are diced. What size bowl should I use for the caramel?
Use a medium microwave-safe bowl. Put the chopped caramels and the light corn syrup into it together.
They're in the bowl. How long should I heat them?
Microwave the bowl on high for approximately 30 seconds, just until the caramels have melted into the corn syrup.
After 30 seconds it's mostly melted, with a couple soft bits. Should I stir it?
Give it a careful stir to smooth the mixture. The residual heat should help those soft bits blend in without changing the recipe timing much.
It's smooth now. Do the apples go straight into the warm caramel?
For Caramelized Apple Bites, add the diced apples to the bowl and toss them until they're coated with the caramel and light corn syrup mixture.
The apple pieces are coated and glossy. Is there anything else before serving?
Let the caramelized apple bites cool before serving so the coating can settle and they're comfortable to eat.
Before I get moving on Cranberry Apple Pie II, what should I have ready? I want to get the counter organized before I start.

Absolutely. Set out 6 apples, a 1 (16 ounce) can of whole cranberry sauce, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour. You'll also want a pie plate, pastry for lining it, a peeler, a knife, and a medium-sized mixing bowl.
I've got the apples, cranberry sauce, sugar, and flour out. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready when the pie is assembled.
The oven is on. I have a pie plate and pastry here—how should I handle that part?
Place the pastry into the pie plate and press it gently into the bottom and up the sides so it sits evenly without stretching too much.
The pastry is in the plate. For the apples, do I need them diced small or sliced?
Peel the 6 apples, remove the cores, and slice them. Aim for fairly even slices so they mix well with the cranberry sauce.
I'm peeling them now. Should I put the slices straight into the pie shell?
Use the medium-sized mixing bowl first. Once the apples are peeled, cored, and sliced, add them to that bowl rather than directly to the pastry.
The apple slices are in the bowl. Do I stir in the cranberry sauce now?
Yes. Add the whole cranberry sauce to the apples and combine them gently until the apple slices are coated and the cranberry sauce is distributed through the bowl.
It's mixed together. I still have the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup flour measured—are those part of my setup for the filling?

Keep both measured and ready with the filling ingredients. At this point, the recipe has you preheated to 350 degrees F, the pie plate lined with pastry, the 6 apples peeled, cored, and sliced, and the apples combined with the 16 ounce can of whole cranberry sauce in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
I want to make Chunky Pizza Dip—can you help me set up the saucepan and ingredients before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Use a large saucepan or Dutch oven, and have 2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 minced garlic cloves ready by the stove.
Garlic is minced, and I've got the Dutch oven out. What tomato ingredients should I open?
Open 2 cans of petite diced tomatoes, 14.5 ounces each, and measure out 1/4 cup tomato paste.
The cans are open and the tomato paste is measured. Should the oil go in cold or after the pot heats?
Add the olive oil and minced garlic to the pan together, then heat them until the garlic starts to sizzle and turn golden.
The garlic is sizzling now, and the edges are just starting to look golden. What goes in before it gets too dark?
Add the petite diced tomatoes, the 1/4 cup tomato paste, basil, and oregano, then stir and bring everything to a simmer.
It's stirred together, but the tomato paste is still in a few streaks. Should I keep breaking it up?
Yes, stir it into the tomatoes until the paste is evenly blended, then let the mixture come up to a steady simmer.
It's bubbling gently now. Do I cover it while it thickens?
Leave it uncovered and simmer until the sauce is thick enough for dipping, about 15 to 20 minutes.
After 20 minutes it looks chunky and thick enough for chips or bread. What should I do with it if I'm serving later?
Let the Chunky Pizza Dip cool, then refrigerate it until you're ready to serve.
I want to make Atomic Canuck Chili, but I'd like to get my skillet and slow cooker workflow straight before I start.

Absolutely. Set out a large skillet for the stovetop and your slow cooker for after browning. For the main measured ingredients, you'll need 2 pounds lean ground beef, 1/2 large onion diced, 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper, and 3 tablespoons garlic powder.
The beef and onion are ready. Should the onion go in right away with the meat, or wait until the beef browns?

Put the onion in right away with the beef. Warm the large skillet over medium heat, then add the ground beef, diced onion, crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper so they cook together.
The skillet is heating. Do I need to add oil before the beef goes in?
The recipe doesn't call for oil. Since you're using ground beef and you'll drain the fat afterward, add the beef mixture directly to the skillet and break it up as it browns.
It's browning now, and there's some liquid and fat in the pan. How cooked should it be before I move it?
Cook it until the beef is browned and the onion has softened in the skillet. Once that's done, drain off the fat carefully before transferring the beef-and-onion mixture into the slow cooker.
Drained and in the slow cooker. I've got mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans, tomato paste, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbecue sauce lined up.
Great. Stir the mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans with their liquid, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce into the slow cooker with the browned beef mixture.
Should I drain the kidney beans, or does the liquid belong in the chili?
Keep the kidney bean liquid in. The recipe specifically has the kidney beans going in with liquid, which helps build the chili base in the slow cooker.
Everything is stirred together. I want it spicy but not impossible to eat—how do I handle the last seasoning?
Season the chili with hot sauce and more crushed red pepper, adding them gradually and tasting as you go. Once the heat level suits you, let the slow cooker carry the chili from there.

memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this Chocolate Cream Dessert, I'm making it ahead today and adding a crumb, streusel, or crisp topping just for this batch. Should the topping go on before it sits?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Hold the topping separately and add it just before reheating or serving.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chocolate Cream Dessert as a make-ahead dish with crumbs, streusel, or a crisp topping. When should I add the topping?

messages.content: For this Chocolate Cream Dessert, I'm making it ahead today and adding a crumb, streusel, or crisp topping just for this batch. Should the topping go on before it sits?
Keep that topping in its own container and sprinkle it on right before you reheat or serve this one, so it stays crisp.
Perfect, that's what I want for tonight's dessert. What should I pull out first for the base?
Start with the crust ingredients: 1/4 cup cold margarine and 1 cup all-purpose flour. You'll also want an 11-in baking dish and nonstick cooking spray nearby.
I've got the dish and spray out. Should the cream cheese and sweetener come to the counter now too?
Yes. Set out 1 (8 ounce) package light cream cheese, softened, plus 2 tablespoons heat-stable granular sugar substitute so they're ready when you assemble the dessert.
The margarine is still cold and the flour is measured. How do I work them together without overdoing it?
Put the flour in a bowl and cut in the cold margarine until the mixture looks crumbly, with small coarse bits rather than a smooth paste.
It looks like loose crumbs now. How firmly should I pack it into the pan?
Press the crumbly mixture evenly into the 11-in baking dish that's coated with nonstick cooking spray. Aim for an even layer, but don't mash it down so hard that it becomes dense.
The layer is even. What oven setting and timing am I using?
Bake it at 350 degrees F for 15-18 minutes, watching for the crust to turn lightly browned.
It's lightly browned at the edges. Do I add the crisp topping while it cools?
Not yet. Let the baked base cool completely, and keep the crisp topping separate until just before reheating or serving.
Once it's fully cool, is that the end of the make-ahead part?

Yes. After it cools completely, cover the base for make-ahead storage, keep the softened cream cheese and sugar-substitute filling components for assembly as needed, and add the topping only at serving time.
I'm making Dads Kickin Jamaican Wings Mon. Can you help me set up the marinade and timing?

Absolutely. Start by gathering 3 tablespoons Jamaican jerk seasoning blend, 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, 3 cloves diced garlic, and 1 (1 inch) piece of peeled fresh ginger, diced. You'll also need green onions and jalapeno slices for the blender mixture.
I've got the jerk seasoning and oil measured, and the garlic is diced. Should the ginger be chopped small before blending?
Yes, dice the peeled ginger so the blender can catch it easily. Add the jerk seasoning, vegetable oil, diced garlic, diced ginger, green onions, and jalapeno slices to the blender.
Before I continue with Dads Kickin Jamaican Wings Mon, everything is in the blender. What texture am I looking for?
Blend until the mixture turns thick and smooth, more like a paste than a thin sauce. Stop and scrape the sides if bits of garlic, ginger, or jalapeno are sticking.
It's blended into a thick paste. I have the wings ready on the counter.
Dunk the wings in the jerk mixture so they're coated well, then arrange them in a single layer on baking sheets. Try not to stack them, so the coating stays even.
The wings are coated, but I'm short on space. Can they touch a little on the baking sheets?
A little touching is okay, but keep them as close to a single layer as you can. If they overlap too much, use another baking sheet so the marinade isn't rubbed off.
They're spread out now. Do I cover the trays before chilling?
Yes. Cover the baking sheets with aluminum foil, then refrigerate the wings for 8 hours or overnight so the jerk mixture has time to season them deeply.
They've been refrigerated overnight. What oven setting should I use before they go in?
set the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Keep the wings arranged in that single layer on the baking sheets while the oven heats.
I pulled up Country Fried Chicken. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got the chicken ready but want to set up the coating station correctly.
Absolutely. For the seasoned flour, measure 1/3 cup all-purpose flour into a large resealable plastic bag. Add 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika.
I've added the flour and seasonings to the bag. Should I mix them before the chicken goes in?
Yes, seal the bag with some air inside and shake it until the flour, garlic salt, pepper, and paprika look evenly blended.
The bag looks evenly mixed. What should I use for the wet dip?
Use a shallow bowl so the pieces are easy to dip. Beat the egg and milk together until the mixture looks smooth and combined.
The egg and milk are beaten in a shallow dish. Do I coat all the chicken at once?
Work with just a few pieces at a time. Put them into the seasoned flour bag, seal it, and shake until each piece has a light coating.
A few pieces are coated with flour. They look covered but not thickly packed on.
That's right. Take those pieces out, dip them into the egg-and-milk mixture, and let any extra drip back into the bowl.
They're dipped now. Do they go straight to cooking or back into the bag?
Return them to the flour mixture in the bag and shake again. That second coating helps build the country-fried crust.
The first batch has its second coating. Should I repeat that for the rest of the chicken?
Yes. Keep going in small batches: flour shake, egg-and-milk dip, then back into the flour mixture for one more shake. Once all the pieces are coated, they're ready for the cooking stage.
Help me stay organized for Easy Pavlova. What comes first? I want to get the ingredients and pan ready before I start whisking.
Absolutely. Set out 4 egg whites, 1 1/4 cups white sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and 1 teaspoon lemon juice. You'll also want a baking sheet and parchment paper.
I've got the egg whites and sugar measured. The vanilla and lemon juice are still in the cupboard.
Grab those too: 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and 1 teaspoon lemon juice. Keep them nearby so you don't have to stop once the egg whites are beaten.
All the ingredients are on the counter. Should I prep the oven or the parchment next?
Get the oven going now: preheat it to 300 degrees F, which is 150 degrees C. While it heats, you can prepare the baking sheet.
Oven is set to 300. I have a rimmed baking sheet—will that work with parchment?
Yes, that's fine. Line the baking sheet with parchment paper so the pavlova has a nonstick surface.
The parchment is on the sheet, but it's curling at the corners a bit.
That's okay. Smooth it as best you can, then draw a 9 inch circle on the parchment paper to guide the shape of the pavlova.
Circle is drawn. Should I flip the parchment so the pencil mark doesn't touch the mixture?
If you used pencil or pen, flip the parchment over so the 9 inch circle is still visible through the paper but the mark won't touch the meringue.
Ready to mix. What texture am I aiming for with the egg whites?
In a large bowl, beat the 4 egg whites until they're stiff but not dry. They should hold peaks, but still look smooth rather than grainy or clumpy.
I want to make Dilled Garlic. Can you help me set up the jars and ingredients before I start?
Absolutely. Have sterile containers ready, plus 2 pounds peeled garlic, 1 sprig chopped fresh dill, cayenne pepper to taste, and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar.
The garlic is peeled and the containers are sterile. Should the dill be chopped before it goes in?
Yes, chop the fresh dill from the sprig, then add it to the sterile containers along with the peeled garlic.
How full should I pack the containers with the garlic and dill?
Fill each sterile container with the garlic, chopped fresh dill, and cayenne pepper, leaving about an inch of space at the top.
I added a little cayenne and left that headspace. What pan should I use for the vinegar?
Use a medium saucepan. Pour in the distilled white vinegar and mix it with the salt called for in the recipe.
The vinegar and salt are in the saucepan. Am I just warming it or does it need to boil?
Bring the vinegar and salt mixture to a boil so it is hot when it goes into the containers.
It has reached a boil. Do I let it cool at all before pouring?
No cooling step is listed here. Carefully pour the hot distilled white vinegar and salt mixture into the containers over the garlic mixture.
Should the liquid cover the garlic after I pour it in?
Pour enough of the hot vinegar mixture into the containers with the garlic mixture so the packed garlic is covered while still respecting the space near the top.
I want to make British Bread Pudding. Can you help me get the ingredients organized before I start?
Absolutely. Set out 6 1/4 cups cubed whole wheat bread and 1 1/4 cups milk, since those get combined early for soaking.
Bread is cubed and the milk is measured. What else should be beside the bowl?
Have 1 beaten egg ready, plus 1/3 cup softened butter. You'll also be stirring in raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon once the bread has soaked.
Got it. Should I heat the oven before I mix the bread and milk?
Yes, set the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's ready when the pudding mixture is prepared.
The oven is heating. What size bowl should I use for the bread?
Use a large bowl so the 6 1/4 cups of bread cubes have room to absorb the milk evenly without spilling when you stir.
The bread is in the large bowl. Do I pour in all the milk at once?
Pour in the full 1 1/4 cups milk, gently turn the bread through it, and let the mixture sit for 5 minutes to soak.
It has soaked for 5 minutes and the bread looks softened. What goes in now?
Stir in the beaten egg and the 1/3 cup softened butter, then add the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
Everything is added, but I can still see a few streaks of butter and spice.
Keep mixing until the bread mixture looks evenly combined, with the fruit and spices distributed throughout and no obvious butter streaks.
Before I get moving on Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I, what should I have ready? I'm setting out the mixing bowls now.

Absolutely. Start by pulling together 1 cup shortening, 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also need vanilla for the creaming step, plus the dry ingredients and the candies for later.
I've got the shortening, both sugars, eggs, and vanilla ready. Should I heat the oven before I start mixing?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's ready when the dough is mixed.
Oven is on. For the wet mixture, do the sugars go in with the shortening right away?
They do. Put the shortening, packed brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla in your main mixing bowl, then cream them together thoroughly until the mixture looks well blended.
It's starting to come together, but I can still see a few streaks of shortening. Keep mixing?
Yes, keep creaming a little longer. You want the shortening and sugars worked evenly through the eggs and vanilla before adding anything dry.
The mixture looks smoother now. What should I do with the dry ingredients?
Use a separate bowl for the dry ingredients. Mix them together there, but leave out the candies for now.
Dry bowl is mixed, and I kept the candies aside. Should I dump all of it into the creamed mixture?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture, then mix well until the dough is evenly combined. Don't add the candies during that dry-ingredient mixing step.
The dough looks even. Is there anything else from the recipe before I move on to portioning?

That covers the listed prep: oven at 375 degrees F or 190 degrees C, creamed shortening with both sugars, eggs, and vanilla, dry ingredients mixed separately without the candies, then added to the creamed mixture and mixed well.

source_seed.recipe_title: Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I

messages.content: I'm making Crab Cake Sauce to serve with dinner. Can you guide me through it?
In this Crab Cake Sauce step, set out a blender and gather 1 cup sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, and 1/3 cup hot salsa.
I've got the blender out, and the sour cream and mayo are measured. Should the cottage cheese go in as-is?
Yes, add the cottage cheese as-is. The blender will smooth it out with the sour cream, mayonnaise, and salsa.
The salsa is hot salsa. Do I pour all 1/3 cup in right away?
Use the full 1/3 cup hot salsa for the recipe. Add it to the blender with the sour cream, mayonnaise, and cottage cheese.
The written directions also mention cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt, but I don't see amounts for those here. What should I do?

Since the recipe doesn't give quantities for those, don't guess large amounts. If you have them and want to follow the direction closely, add only small taste-based touches, then blend and adjust after tasting.
For Crab Cake Sauce, everything is in the blender. What texture am I aiming for?
Puree until the sauce looks smooth and creamy, with no visible cottage cheese curds. Stop and scrape down the sides if anything is clinging to the blender jar.
It's smooth now. Should I serve it right away with the crab cakes?
Chill it before serving. Transfer the sauce to a covered bowl or container and refrigerate it so the texture firms up slightly and the flavors settle.
Good idea. Any serving or cleanup tips while it chills?
Serve it cold alongside the crab cakes, either in a small bowl for dipping or spooned lightly over the top. Rinse the blender right away so the creamy sauce doesn't dry onto the blades.
I'm making Basic Chicken Stock and have a Dutch oven ready. Can you talk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Put together 1 pound chicken parts, 1 large onion, 3 stalks celery with some leaves, and 1 large carrot. You'll also need salt, cloves, and 6 cups water for the pot.
The chicken is thawed, and I've got the vegetables on the cutting board. Should I peel the onion or just cut it?
Peel off the papery outside if you like, then quarter the onion so the pieces can flavor the stock well.
Onion is quartered. The celery has leaves on the inner stalks; should those go in too?
Yes, include some of those celery leaves. Scrub the celery and carrot, then chop both into 1 inch chunks.
The carrot and celery are in chunky pieces now. Do I put everything straight into the Dutch oven?
Yes. Add the chicken pieces, quartered onion, chopped celery, chopped carrot, salt, and cloves to the large soup pot or Dutch oven.
I've added the chicken and vegetables. The salt and cloves are going in now. How much water comes next?
Pour in 6 cups water, making sure the ingredients are settled in the pot.
The water is in, but a few vegetable pieces are floating above the chicken. Is that okay?
That's okay for stock. Just press them down gently so everything is mostly in contact with the water.
Before I turn on the stove, can you recap what should be in the pot so I can check it?
You should have chicken parts, quartered onion, celery and carrot cut into 1 inch chunks, salt, cloves, and 6 cups water in the Dutch oven.
I have Applesauce Bread I planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got two loaf pans out and want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it can heat while you prep. This recipe uses two 9 x 5 inch loaf pans, so keep both nearby.
The oven is heating. Before I start mixing, what should be on the counter?
Measure out 3 cups all-purpose flour, 3 eggs, 2 cups white sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil. You'll also need applesauce, plus sour cream or buttermilk for the mixing step later.
I have the flour, eggs, sugar, oil, and applesauce. Should I prep the pans now or wait?
Prep them now: grease and flour both 9 x 5 inch loaf pans so the batter can go straight in once it's mixed.
Pans are greased and floured. For the wet mixture, do the eggs go in whole with the sugar?
Yes. Crack in the 3 eggs, add the 2 cups white sugar and 1 cup vegetable oil, then beat them together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
It's glossy and the sugar looks mostly mixed in. Do I add flour next?
Before folding in the flour, blend in the applesauce, then add either sour cream or buttermilk. Stir until that mixture is uniform.
I'm using buttermilk, and the batter base looks loose but even. How careful should I be from here?
Keep the mixing steady and avoid overworking it once the 3 cups all-purpose flour go in. Stir just until you don't see dry flour streaks.
The batter is mixed. Should I divide it evenly between the 2 pans?
Yes, split the batter evenly between the prepared pans, smoothing the tops lightly. Then bake in the preheated 350 degrees F oven and start checking for doneness when the loaves look set and browned.
I'm making Basic Chicken Stock and have a large Dutch oven out. Can you walk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Put these on the counter: 1 pound chicken parts, 1 large onion, 3 stalks celery with some leaves, and 1 large carrot. You'll also need salt, cloves, and 6 cups water.
The chicken parts are ready, and I found the onion. Should I peel it or just cut it?
Quarter the onion. If the outer skin is loose or papery, remove that so it doesn't shed into the pot.
Onion is quartered. The celery still has leaves attached, and the carrot is scrubbed.
Good. Chop the scrubbed celery and the carrot into 1 inch chunks. Keep some of those celery leaves in the mix; they can go into the pot too.
The vegetables are cut. Should the chicken go in before the vegetables?
Yes. Place the chicken pieces in the large soup pot or Dutch oven, then add the onion, celery, and carrot around them.
Everything is in the Dutch oven except the seasonings. What goes in now?
Add the salt and cloves to the pot with the chicken and vegetables. The recipe doesn't give exact amounts for those, so use the amounts you planned or have from your recipe source.
Seasonings are in. I'm measuring the water—how much exactly?
Add 6 cups water to the pot. Pour it in gently so the vegetables and chicken stay settled rather than splashing.
The water is added, and the pot looks full but not overflowing. Is that all for this part?
Yes, that completes the listed setup for Basic Chicken Stock: chicken pieces, quartered onion, celery, carrot, salt, cloves, and 6 cups water are all in the pot.
I'm making Chicken Fiesta Salad and have a skillet out. Can you help me pace the prep and cooking?

Absolutely. Set out 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, 1 packet of dry fajita seasoning that's 1.27 ounces, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, and 1 can of black beans, 15 ounces, rinsed and drained.
The chicken and seasoning are on the board. Should I use the whole fajita packet on the chicken?
Use only 1/2 of the fajita seasoning on the chicken. Rub it evenly over both chicken breast halves so the surfaces are coated before they go into the pan.
Coated. I'm trying not to overcook them—what heat and timing should I use?
Heat the vegetable oil in your skillet over medium heat. Add the seasoned chicken and cook it for 8 minutes on each side, or until the juices run clear.
They've had 8 minutes on the first side and I just flipped them. Should I cover the skillet?
You can leave it uncovered and keep the heat at medium. Let the second side cook its 8 minutes, then check that the juices run clear before taking the chicken out.
The chicken is cooked through and resting on a plate. I rinsed and drained the black beans—where do they go?
Put the black beans into a large saucepan. Add the corn, salsa, and the other 1/2 of the fajita seasoning, then stir everything together.
The bean mixture is in the saucepan. Do I need to simmer it for a while or just heat it?
Just heat it over medium heat until it's warm throughout, stirring occasionally so the beans, corn, salsa, and seasoning heat evenly.
It's warmed through now, and the chicken has rested. How should I bring it together for serving?

Slice or portion the cooked chicken, then serve it with the warm bean, corn, and salsa mixture for the Chicken Fiesta Salad. Keep any juices from the rested chicken if you want to spoon them over the top.
I'm making Baked Fish and Rice 2 and have an 11-in. baking dish out. Can you help me start without rushing it?
Absolutely. Grease the 11-in. baking dish, and have 1 1/2 cups boiling chicken broth and 1/2 cup uncooked long grain rice ready beside it.
While working on Baked Fish and Rice 2, the dish is greased, and the broth is boiling. Do the seasonings go in with the rice right away?
Yes. Add the rice to the dish, then stir in the boiling chicken broth, 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder so everything is evenly combined.
It's mixed in the baking dish. Should it be covered tightly, and what oven setting am I using?
For Baked Fish and Rice 2, cover the dish and bake it at 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, for 10 minutes.
The 10 minutes are almost up. What should I have ready for the next part?
Have the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, and onions ready. When the dish comes out, you'll add the broccoli, Parmesan, and half of the onions over the rice mixture.
I pulled it out and added the broccoli and Parmesan. For the onions, just half now and save the rest?
Right, use half of the onions at this point and keep the remaining onions aside for later if you plan to use them as a topping.
The rice mixture is topped and spread out. How should I place the fish?
Lay the fish fillets over the rice and broccoli mixture in an even layer so they sit on top rather than being stirred in.
The fillets are on top. Is there anything else before it goes back in?
Sprinkle the fish fillets with paprika, then it's ready for the next bake according to your recipe's remaining timing or doneness cues.
I'm making Cookie Paints for a batch of cutout cookies. Can you talk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Set out a small bowl, a spoon for stirring, a clean paintbrush, 2 tablespoons evaporated milk, and 4 drops red food coloring.
I've got the evaporated milk measured. Should the coloring go in all at once?
Yes, add the 4 drops of red food coloring directly into the 2 tablespoons of evaporated milk in the small bowl.
The drops are in the bowl. Do I whisk it or just stir?
Just stir it well with a spoon until the color looks evenly blended through the evaporated milk.
It's a smooth pinkish-red now. Is that ready to use on the cookies?
Yes. Dip the clean paintbrush lightly into the mixture so it coats the bristles without dripping heavily.
My cookies are shaped and still unbaked on the tray. Is this the right time to paint them?
That's exactly the right time. Paint the mixture onto the cookies before baking, using light strokes so the designs stay neat.
Some of the color is pooling in a corner of one cookie. Should I wipe it off?
You can gently spread the pooled spot with the brush or dab off a little excess, then smooth the color over the surface.
The designs are painted on. Anything else before the tray goes into the oven?
Let any shiny wet spots settle for a moment, then bake the cookies according to your cookie dough recipe. The paint is already mixed and applied.
I'm making Dipping Sauce to go with snacks. Can you help me set up without overcomplicating it?
Absolutely. Put a small mixing bowl on the counter and measure out 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons ketchup, 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish, and 1/4 teaspoon paprika.
I've got the bowl, mayo, ketchup, horseradish, and paprika ready. Do I need anything else before mixing?
Yes. The recipe also has you combine in salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper, so keep those nearby to season the sauce as you stir it together.
Should the mayonnaise go in before the horseradish, or does the order matter here?
The order is not critical for this sauce. Add the mayonnaise to the small bowl, then add the ketchup, prepared horseradish, paprika, salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
The ketchup and horseradish are in with the mayo. I'm adding the paprika now—how much stirring should I do?
Stir until the sauce looks evenly blended, with no streaks of mayonnaise or ketchup and the paprika and seasonings distributed throughout.
It's looking smooth and pale orange. Should I taste it before it goes in the fridge?
You can taste a tiny bit if you want to check the balance, but keep the recipe base as mixed: mayonnaise, ketchup, prepared horseradish, paprika, salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
I'm happy with the flavor. What container should I use for storing it?
Transfer it to a small covered container, or cover the bowl tightly if that's what you mixed it in.
The container is covered. Where should it sit until serving?
Store it covered in the refrigerator until you're ready to serve the Dipping Sauce.
I'm making Famous Caramel Cookie Bars. Can you help me get organized before I start?
For this batch of Famous Caramel Cookie Bars, set out 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 individually wrapped caramels with the wrappers removed, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips.
I've unwrapped the caramels, but the cookies are still in the package. Do I need a pan or just a tray?
Use a baking sheet or tray. Arrange the shortbread cookies on it in a single layer so each one is ready for a stripe of caramel.
The cookies are lined up. Should I leave space between them?
A little space helps keep the caramel from running into the next cookie, but they do not need to be far apart.
Okay. I have a small saucepan out for the caramels—what goes in it?
Add the 35 unwrapped caramels and the 1/4 cup water to the small saucepan.
What heat should I use so the caramel doesn't scorch?
Put the saucepan over medium-low heat and stir frequently while the caramels melt into the water.
It's mostly smooth now, with just a few soft bits left. Should I keep stirring?
Yes, keep stirring over medium-low until it looks fully melted and smooth enough to spoon.
The caramel is smooth. How much should I put on each cookie?
Spoon a thin line of caramel over each shortbread cookie, then place the cookies in the refrigerator until the caramel is set.
I'm making Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea and have a big pot out. Can you help me start with the right amounts?
Absolutely. Put 1 pound of fresh or frozen cranberries in the large pot, then add 3 quarts of cold water.
For Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea, the cranberries and water are in the pot. Should I add the juices before heating?
Hold the juices for later. Heat just the cranberries and water for now; bring the pot to a boil.
It's coming up to a boil. What should I watch for with the berries?
Once it boils, cook only until the cranberries pop, about 5 minutes. You're looking for the skins to split rather than a long simmer.
Most of them have popped after about 5 minutes. Do I keep it on the burner?
No, take the pot off the heat. Let it stand at room temperature until the liquid is cold, which will take several hours.
While it cools, I want to check the rest: I have orange juice and pineapple juice ready. How much of each goes in?
You'll stir in 2 cups orange juice and 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice after the cranberry liquid has cooled and been strained.
The pot is cold now. What's the neatest way to strain it?
Set a strainer over a large bowl or pitcher and pour the mixture through it, catching and removing the cranberries while keeping the liquid.
The cranberries are strained out and I've got the liquid in a pitcher. How do I finish the tea?
Stir the orange juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice, and sugar into the strained cranberry liquid until the sugar dissolves. Then it's ready to serve chilled or over ice.
I'm making Banana Orange Bars and have a mixing bowl out. Can you help me work through the ingredients and pan setup?
Absolutely. For the batter, measure out 2 cups mashed ripe bananas, 1 2/3 cups sugar, 1 cup vegetable oil, and 4 eggs. You'll also want a greased 15-in. baking pan ready for later.
The bananas are mashed, but they're a little lumpy. Is that okay before I add the sugar?
A few soft lumps are fine. Add the sugar to the mashed bananas, then pour in the vegetable oil and crack in the eggs so everything can be beaten together.
All four eggs are in with the bananas, sugar, and oil. How blended should this look?
Beat the bananas, sugar, oil, and eggs in the mixing bowl until the mixture looks well blended, with the eggs fully incorporated and no separate streaks of oil showing.
The wet mixture is smooth enough now. The recipe mentions dry ingredients, but I don't see them listed here—what should I do with that step?
Follow the recipe's direction at that point: combine the dry ingredients you're using for the bars in a separate bowl, then fold them into the banana mixture until everything is well mixed.
When I fold them in, should I stir hard or keep it gentle?
Keep it gentle but thorough. Use broad turns with a spatula, scraping the bottom and sides, until the dry mixture disappears into the banana mixture.
The batter is mixed. The next line says to spread over bars, which sounds a little odd—how should I handle that?
Treat that as the next recipe action: spread the prepared mixture evenly over the bars or bar base you're working with, making the surface as level as you can.
It's spread evenly now, and I've greased the 15-in. pan. What's the last move?
Pour the mixture into the greased 15-in. baking pan, guiding it into the corners and smoothing the top so the bars bake in an even layer.
I'm making Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men and want to get the dough started. Can you walk me through it while I set up?
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and gather 1/2 cup margarine and 1/2 cup sugar to begin the base of the dough.
I've got the bowl out, and the margarine is soft enough to mix. Do I need the wet ingredients nearby too?
Yes. Keep 1/2 cup molasses and 1 egg yolk ready, since they'll go in right after the margarine and sugar are creamed.
Before I add the molasses, how smooth should the margarine and sugar mixture look?
Cream the margarine and sugar together in the large bowl until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended, with no obvious streaks of margarine.
Okay, that mixture is smooth. I separated the egg and have just the yolk.
Great. Stir the molasses and the egg yolk into the creamed margarine and sugar until everything is combined.
It's darker and sticky now. Should I mix the dry ingredients separately or add them straight in?
Combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg together first, then blend that dry mixture into the molasses mixture.
I'm adding the dry mix gradually because the dough is getting thick. Is that okay?
That's a good approach. Keep blending until the dough is smooth and the dry ingredients are fully worked into the molasses mixture.
The dough looks even now. What should I do with the bowl before shaping anything?
Cover the bowl and chill the dough for at least one hour before you move on to rolling or cutting the gingerbread men.
I'm making Cookie Jar Gingersnaps and have a large mixing bowl out. Can you help me set up the dough?
Absolutely. Put 3/4 cup shortening and 1 cup sugar within reach, since those get mixed together at the start.
Shortening and sugar are measured. Are there any wet ingredients I should have ready before I begin mixing?
Yes—set out 1 egg and 1/4 cup molasses. After the shortening and sugar are creamed, those go in next.
I've got the egg and molasses next to the bowl. How should the shortening and sugar look once I cream them?
Beat the shortening and sugar in the large mixing bowl until they're evenly combined and look smooth and fluffy rather than streaky.
The mixture is lighter and smooth now. Should I add the egg by itself or with the molasses?
Add the egg and molasses to the creamed mixture, then beat until the dough base looks uniform and the molasses is fully blended in.
That's mixed in. I still need to bring in the dry ingredients—what belongs together?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt so the leavening and spices are evenly distributed.
The dry bowl smells gingery and everything is stirred together. Do I dump it all into the wet mixture?
Add the dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture, mixing as you go so the dough comes together evenly without pockets of flour.
The dough is mixed and a little sticky. What shape should I make before baking?
Roll teaspoonfuls of dough into balls. Keep them fairly even in size so the gingersnaps bake consistently.
I'm making chicken pot pie ix and have the chicken breasts out. Can you help me get started without rushing?
Absolutely. Cut 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into cubes, and set out 1 cup sliced carrots so they're ready to go into the saucepan.
The chicken is cubed, and I sliced the carrots. Do the peas need to thaw first?
No need to thaw them for this part. Measure 1 cup frozen green peas and also have 1/2 cup sliced celery ready.
Peas and celery are measured. Should I turn on the oven before the saucepan step?
Yes, bring the oven up to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C), so it's heating while you prepare the filling ingredients.
Oven is set to 425. What kind of pan am I using on the stove?
Use a saucepan large enough to hold the cubed chicken, carrots, frozen peas, and celery with room for water to cover them.
Everything fits in my saucepan. Should I stir it together before adding water?
Yes, combine the chicken, carrots, peas, and celery in the saucepan so they're evenly distributed.
They're mixed. How much water should I pour in, and how long does it cook?
Add enough water to cover the chicken and vegetables, bring it to a boil, and let it boil for 15 minutes.
The timer's done after 15 minutes. What should I do with the saucepan now?
For this batch of chicken pot pie ix, remove the saucepan from the heat, drain the chicken and vegetables, and set them aside for the next part of the pot pie.
I'm making Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce. Before I start heating anything, can you help me get organized?

Absolutely. Put out 1 medium head of garlic, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, and 1/2 cup white wine. You'll also want either a clay garlic roaster or a piece of aluminum foil for the garlic.
I've got the garlic, oil, chicken, and white wine on the counter. Should the oven be on already?
Yes, go ahead and bring the oven up to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), so it's ready for roasting the garlic.
The oven is heating. How much of the garlic head am I supposed to cut off?
Slice just the top off the head of garlic—only enough to remove the papery tip and expose the tops of the cloves. Try to keep the head intact.
Some cloves are showing now, but there's still paper around the sides. Is that okay?
That's fine. Leave the outer layers around the sides as long as the clove tops are exposed, because the garlic will roast as a whole head.
What do I do with the olive oil?
Drizzle the 1 tablespoon olive oil over the exposed cloves so it can seep down into the head of garlic.
I don't have a clay garlic roaster. Can I still roast it properly?
Yes. Wrap the oiled garlic head in aluminum foil and place it in the preheated oven.
How long should I leave it in, and how will I know it's ready for the sauce?
Roast it for 20 minutes, or until the cloves are soft and slip from their skins when pushed. That roasted garlic will be ready to use for the sauce with the chicken and white wine.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce

original_cues.support_feedback_cue: Yes, that herb cut is what I meant.
original_cues.support_user_cue: For Fancy Brussels Sprouts, I want the herbs worked through instead of just sitting there.

messages.content: I'm making Fancy Brussels Sprouts tonight. Can you help me get organized before I turn on the stove?

Chop the fresh parsley very fine, add some with the cooking liquid, and fold the rest through near the end with a little left to scatter over the sprouts. Set a saucepan on the stove, then measure 1 cup water, 1/4 cup minced fresh parsley, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I've got the saucepan out. Should I trim the brussels sprouts now too?
Yes, trim the stem ends and pull off any rough outer leaves. Keep the water chestnuts and butter nearby as well, since they go in after the sprouts are tender.
The parsley is minced and the sugar and salt are measured. How do I start the pan?

Pour the 1 cup water into the saucepan, add the sugar, salt, and the portion of parsley you're cooking in the liquid, then set it over medium heat. Let it come all the way to a boil before adding the sprouts.
I like handling the parsley that way—fine pieces worked in and a fresh bit at the end is exactly what I wanted here. The pan is starting to bubble.
Great. Once it reaches a steady boil, add the brussels sprouts and stir just enough to coat them in the seasoned liquid.
The sprouts are in. Do I leave the lid off while they cook?
Cover the saucepan and lower the heat so it simmers rather than boils hard. Cook them for 6-8 minutes, until the sprouts are tender.
I'm at about 6 minutes. What's the best way to tell if they're ready?

Pierce one with a fork or the tip of a knife. If it slides in easily but the sprout still holds its shape, drain them; if the center feels firm, give them another minute or two, up to 8 minutes total.
They're tender now, and I'm draining them. Should I save any of the cooking water?
No need to save it for this dish. Drain the sprouts well, return them to the warm pan, then add the water chestnuts and butter.
The butter is melting and the water chestnuts are warming through. How should I finish the parsley part?
Fold in the reserved minced parsley once everything is hot, then sprinkle the last little bit over the top before serving. Taste for salt and serve the Fancy Brussels Sprouts warm.
I'm making Chicken Pot Pie II 2 and want to get organized before I start. What should I pull out?
Set out 3 skinless, bone-in chicken breast halves and 1 (14.5 ounce) can of chicken broth. You'll also need a pot large enough to hold the chicken with water covering it.
Chicken and broth are on the counter, and I've got a medium pot. Are there more ingredients?
Yes—grab 3 potatoes and 1 yellow onion. Keep salt, pepper, and garlic powder nearby for seasoning the chicken.
The potatoes and onion are ready. Do I prep those right away or start with the chicken?
Start with the chicken. Wash the chicken breasts in water, then place them in the pot and add just enough water to cover the chicken.
They're in the pot now, and the water is just over the top of the chicken. How much seasoning should I add?
Season the pot with some salt, pepper, and garlic powder. The recipe doesn't give exact amounts, so sprinkle them in evenly rather than making a heavy layer.
Seasoning is in. Should I add the chicken broth at this point?
The listed broth is part of the recipe ingredients, so keep the 1 (14.5 ounce) can ready. For this step, the instruction is simply chicken covered with water and seasoned in the pot.

Yes, add the broccoli and cauliflower florets to the boiling water together and leave them in for one minute.

Drain the florets immediately, then rinse them to cool them down and stop the cooking.

Combine the broccoli, cauliflower, bell pepper, cucumber, carrot, and Italian salad dressing in the medium size mixing bowl.

Place the flour in a separate bowl or on a plate. Spread it out a bit so the ribs can be coated evenly instead of landing in one thick pile.

Crack the eggs into a large bowl and whisk them until the yolks and whites are fully combined. That gives you a smooth egg coating before the flour and seasoning steps.

Yes, let the peanut oil reach 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, before frying so the coating sets quickly and the ribs don't soak up extra oil.

Add the dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture, stirring between additions so the dough comes together evenly instead of clumping.

Preheat your outdoor grill for indirect heat. That means you want the roast cooking away from direct flames or the hottest coals rather than sitting right over them.

messages.content: I'm making Escargots Vol au Vent tonight. What should I have ready on the counter before I start handling the snails?

For the tender lower herb pieces, mince the parsley or cilantro stems into tiny, uneven flecks and mix them into the seasoned butter. Set out 12 helix snails without shells, 1/2 cup softened butter, 2 cloves finely chopped garlic, and 1 finely chopped green onion, plus parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine for the bowl.
The butter is softening now, and I've got the garlic cloves peeled. Should I turn the oven on before I chop everything?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it's ready when the filling is mixed.

Go ahead and drain them now. Rinse the escargots gently in cold water, then leave them to drain again so they don't bring extra moisture into the butter.
I like that you're using those tender lower pieces here; that's exactly what I wanted, because I usually save them instead of tossing them.
They work well in this filling as long as they're tender. Keep the flecks small and leave out any tough or woody bits so the escargots stay delicate.
The oven is heating, and the snails are draining. How fine should I chop the garlic and green onion?
Chop both finely so they spread through the softened butter rather than landing in big bites. The green onion should be small enough to blend with the herbs and spices.
I've got a medium mixing bowl out. Does the butter go in first, or should I combine the wine and seasonings separately?
Put the softened butter in the mixing bowl first. Stir in the garlic, green onion, parsley, the minced tender herb flecks, pepper, nutmeg, and wine so everything gets worked into the butter.
The wine is making the butter look a little loose at the edges. Should I whisk it harder?
Mash and stir it instead of whisking hard. You want the butter to stay cohesive while carrying the garlic, green onion, herbs, pepper, nutmeg, and wine evenly.
The escargots are drained and not dripping anymore. Do they go into the bowl now?
Yes, once the butter mixture looks fairly even, fold the drained escargots in gently so they get coated without breaking up.
I can see little green flecks throughout, and the snails are coated. Is there anything else to check before I move on?

Give it one last thorough mix so the seasoning is evenly distributed and the butter looks cohesive. With the oven at 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, the escargot filling is ready for the next part of the vol au vent.
I'm making Chicken Stuffed Buns for a casual dinner. Can you guide me without rushing the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 6 large sourdough buns and 2 cups cooked, diced boneless chicken breast halves so the filling comes together quickly.
The chicken is diced and the buns are on the counter. What cheeses should I have ready?
You'll need 1 softened 8 ounce package of cream cheese and 1 cup shredded Pepper Jack cheese. Keep Parmesan cheese nearby too, since it goes into the filling with garlic and spinach.
Got it. Should I turn the oven on before I start cutting the buns?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready once the buns are stuffed.
Oven is heating. I have a bread knife and a small bowl for scraps—how should I cut them?
Slice the top off each sourdough bun, and keep those tops because they'll be saved for covering the stuffed buns later.
The tops are off. I don't want to tear the sides—how much bread should I remove?
Hollow out each bun gently, leaving enough of a shell to hold the chicken-cheese mixture without collapsing.
They look like little bowls now. What should the filling texture be like when I mix it?

In a medium bowl, combine the cooked diced chicken, softened cream cheese, shredded Pepper Jack cheese, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and spinach. Mix until the cream cheese coats everything and the filling looks scoopable.
That sounds manageable. Once it's mixed, should I pack the filling tightly or keep it loose?
Spoon it into the hollowed buns firmly enough to fill the shells, but don't mash it down hard. Add the saved tops back on when they're filled, then they're ready for the heated oven.
I'm making Chicken with Vegetables in the slow cooker. Can you help me get the prep organized before I start loading it?
Absolutely. Set up your slow cooker and have 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms ready, along with the chicken: 4 drumsticks with the skin removed and 4 thighs with the skin removed.
The mushrooms are sliced and the chicken pieces are skinned. What vegetables should I have beside the mushrooms?
You'll need 4 celery ribs, sliced. The cooking step also calls for zucchini, carrots, and onion, so have those ready to add with the celery.

Put the mushrooms and the chicken directly into the slow cooker together. A simple even layer is fine; the slow cooking will let everything settle and release juices.
