Add the celery, zucchini, carrots, and onion to the slow cooker. Then pour in the tomato juice and broth, and add the garlic, paprika, and pepper.
Everything is in the crock. Should I stir it, or leave the chicken pieces where they are?
You can gently nudge the vegetables and liquid around the chicken so the seasonings are distributed, but don't worry about fully stirring or breaking up the pieces.
Lid is on. What setting and how long should I use?
For Chicken with Vegetables, keep it covered on low for 5 hours, or until the meat juices run clear.
When it's done, what's the best way to hold it if we aren't eating immediately?
For Chicken with Vegetables, remove the chicken and vegetables from the slow cooker and keep them warm until serving.
I'm making apple butter spice cake and want to get the topping organized before I start. What should I pull out?

For the topping, set out 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and 1/2 cup chopped pecans. Keep a small bowl handy so you can mix them together once the pan is ready.
Those are on the counter. What pan and oven setup do I need?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C. While it heats, spray or grease one 9x13 inch pan so the cake releases cleanly.
The oven is heating and the pan is greased. Should I mix the pecan topping now?
Yes. Stir the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and chopped pecans together until the spices are evenly distributed through the sugar and nuts.
The topping smells good. For the cake batter, do the dry ingredients go together separately?
They do. Sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a separate bowl so the leavening and salt are evenly blended before they go into the batter.
Dry bowl is sifted. I've got butter and sugar ready in the mixer—how should that part look?
Blend the butter and sugar together until they're combined and a bit lighter. Add the eggs next and beat well so the mixture is smooth before you add the flavorings.
Eggs are beaten in. Where do the apple butter and vanilla fit?
Add the apple butter and vanilla now, then mix in the wheat germ or bran cereal. Scrape the bowl if needed so everything is evenly incorporated.
That's mixed. How do I bring in the sifted dry ingredients and sour cream without overdoing it?

Add the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream, mixing well after each addition. Keep the mixer controlled and stop once the batter is evenly combined, then it's ready to go into the prepared 9x13 inch pan with the topping as directed.
I want to make Artichoke Hummus. Can you help me get set up before I start blending?
Absolutely. Drain 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, also called garbanzo beans, and have 1 clove of garlic ready. You'll want a food processor for this one.
The chickpeas are drained and the garlic is peeled. What else goes into the processor?
Add 1/2 cup drained marinated artichoke hearts and measure out 2 tablespoons lemon juice. Those are the remaining ingredients listed for the hummus.
Should the artichoke marinade go in too, or should I drain the pieces pretty well?
Drain the marinated artichoke hearts before measuring the 1/2 cup, then put the drained pieces in the food processor with the chickpeas, garlic, and lemon juice.
Everything is in the processor bowl. I noticed the directions mention parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks—what do I do with those?
For the blending step, combine all the ingredients in the work bowl except parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks. Those are kept out of the processor rather than blended into the hummus.
Got it. How smooth should I make it when I pulse?
Pulse until the hummus is smooth. Stop and scrape down the sides as needed so the chickpeas and artichokes blend evenly.
It looks creamy now, with just a few tiny artichoke bits. Is that okay?
Yes, that texture works. Once it's smooth enough for you, transfer the Artichoke Hummus into a serving bowl.
It's in the bowl. I'm not serving it for another hour—how should I hold it?
Cover the serving bowl and refrigerate the hummus until you're ready to serve.

Finish the potato noodles on a sheet pan in the oven or under the broiler, then leave them uncovered briefly before serving. For the starting step, bring a large pot of water to a boil and keep the potatoes whole in their skins.
Before I turn on the burner, what exactly should I measure out?
Have 1 1/2 pounds russet potatoes, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 egg, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley ready. You'll also want a little flour for the work surface later.
The pot is on. Should I peel the potatoes first, or do they go in as they are?
Put them in unpeeled. Once the water is boiling, add the whole potatoes in their skins and boil them for 25 to 30 minutes, until they're tender.
I like that sheet-pan finish—that's exactly what I wanted so I'm not stuck watching a pan at the end. The potatoes are in the water now; can I set up the board?
Yes. Lightly flour a clean work surface, and set out a rolling pin for mashing. Keep a colander, tongs, or a slotted spoon nearby for lifting the hot potatoes out.

The listed method just calls for boiling the whole potatoes in water, so you can keep it plain and stay close to the recipe.

Remove the potatoes from the pot and discard the water. Let the potatoes sit until they're cool enough to handle safely.

Yes, peel them while they're still warm but manageable. After peeling, place the potatoes on the lightly floured surface.
They're peeled on the board. I'm tempted to grab a potato masher, but the recipe mentions a rolling pin—does that matter?
Use the rolling pin here. Press and roll over the potatoes until they're evenly mashed, adding just enough flour underneath to keep them from sticking.

Add the 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 egg, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley after the potatoes are mashed, and mix gently just until the dough comes together. When the noodles are ready for browning or holding, spread them on the sheet pan so the surface stays open to the air instead of steaming.
I want to make Chicken Spinach Bake. I've got frozen chopped spinach thawing—can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. You'll need 3 (10 ounce) packages of frozen chopped spinach, thawed, plus 3 eggs for the base.

Set out 1/2 teaspoon onion salt and 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg. You'll also be using Parmesan cheese later in the mixture and topping.

Get it as dry as you can: drain it well, then squeeze out the excess moisture so the bake doesn't turn watery.

Yes. In a mixing bowl, beat the 3 eggs with the onion salt and ground nutmeg until the seasoning is evenly blended.
The eggs are beaten and smell a little nutmeggy. Does the spinach go straight in?
It does. Add the squeezed spinach to the egg mixture along with 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, then mix everything well so the spinach is evenly coated.

Yes—combine the bread crumbs with the remaining Parmesan cheese. That mixture will be ready to sprinkle over the spinach bake.
Should the bread crumbs and Parmesan be fully blended or left a little streaky?

Blend them enough that the Parmesan is distributed through the bread crumbs, but it doesn't have to be perfectly uniform. Once that's combined, your spinach mixture and topping are both ready for assembly.
I want to get Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men right. What should I handle first? I've got a large mixing bowl out and want to start by checking the ingredients.
Absolutely. For the wet base, set out 1/2 cup margarine, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup molasses, and 1 egg yolk.

Use just the egg yolk for this recipe. Keep the white aside for something else, then have the yolk ready near the bowl.
All right, the yolk is separated. What goes into the bowl first?
Put the margarine and sugar in the large bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's looking smooth but still a little grainy from the sugar. Is that fine before I add anything sticky?
Yes, that's fine. Once the margarine and sugar are well combined, stir in the 1/2 cup molasses and the egg yolk.
The molasses is mixed in and the batter looks dark and glossy. I'm ready for the dry ingredients.
For Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men, in a separate bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg.

Add the dry mixture into the molasses mixture and blend until the dough is smooth, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed.

Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour. That will firm it up so it's easier to roll and cut later.

Keep it simple: a light pineapple accent for flavor, such as a few tiny bits of pineapple or a small drizzle of juice around the edge, plus one texture accent like a modest sprinkle of finely chopped nuts. If the dip already looks smooth and inviting, it's also fine to serve it plain.

messages.content: I'm making Black Bean Chili and have a large saucepan out. Can you guide me from prep through the stovetop steps?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 chopped onion, 2 red bell peppers that are seeded and chopped, and 1 jalapeno pepper that's seeded and minced.
The onion is chopped, and I'm seeding the peppers now. Should the jalapeno be very fine?
Yes, mince the jalapeno so it spreads through the chili instead of landing in big bites. Keep the red bell peppers chopped into small pieces, and have the onion nearby for the pan.
All the peppers and onion are ready. I also see mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn in the cooking step—should those be ready before I heat the pan?
Yes, have the mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn ready to add with the onion and peppers. The recipe doesn't give amounts for those, so use the prepared portions you have for this chili.
Everything is next to the stove. How hot should I get the pan before adding vegetables?
Put the large saucepan over medium-high heat and add the olive oil. Let the oil warm until it looks loose and shimmery, but don't let it smoke.
The oil is shimmering. Do I add all the vegetables together or start with the onion?
Add the onion, red bell peppers, jalapeno, mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn together. Sautee them for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onions turn translucent.
They've been cooking and the onion is starting to look clear. What seasonings go in at this point?
Season the vegetables with black pepper, cumin, and chili powder. Stir well so the spices coat the vegetables and warm in the pan.
The spices smell good and the vegetables look softened. What do I stir in to complete this part?
Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt. Mix from the bottom of the saucepan so everything is evenly combined, then let it continue heating gently from there.
I'm making Campagnard Sauce and want to use it later today. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 2 cloves garlic, minced, plus 1/2 cup goat cheese. You'll also want a mixing bowl and something to blend or stir the sauce smooth.
Garlic and goat cheese are on the counter. What else should I mince or measure before I start?
In this Campagnard Sauce step, mince 1 celery stalk, then measure 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar. Keep olive oil nearby too, since it gets stirred in with the sauce ingredients.
The celery is minced pretty fine, and the vinegar is measured. Should the goat cheese go in whole or softened first?
If it's very cold, let it soften for a few minutes so it mixes more easily. Then add the goat cheese to the bowl with the minced garlic, minced celery, balsamic vinegar, and olive oil.
Everything is in the bowl now. It looks a little chunky from the cheese and celery.
That's expected at this point. Stir it together thoroughly so the vinegar and olive oil start loosening the goat cheese and coating the garlic and celery.
It's combined, but I haven't seasoned it yet. How much salt and pepper should I use?
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Start lightly, stir, taste, and adjust until the tangy vinegar and goat cheese taste balanced.
The flavor is good. I'd like the texture smoother before refrigerating it.
Blend it well until the sauce is smooth. Scrape down the sides as needed so the garlic, celery, goat cheese, balsamic vinegar, and olive oil all become evenly incorporated.
It's smooth now. I'm not serving it immediately—what should I do with the bowl?
Cover the sauce and refrigerate it. Give it a quick stir before serving in case it firms up slightly while chilled.

I'm making Adobo Chicken with Ginger and have a Dutch oven out. Can you guide me without rushing the simmering part?

Absolutely. Set up your ingredients first: 1 (3 pound) whole chicken cut into 8 pieces, 1/2 cup soy sauce, 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar, and 1 bulb garlic, peeled and crushed. You'll also be combining them with ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns in the pot.

Use the garlic peeled and crushed, so it can flavor the sauce as it cooks. Put the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns into the Dutch oven together.

Yes, that's fine for this method because you'll baste the chicken later. Place the Dutch oven over medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil.

You can gently shift the chicken once or twice so the soy sauce and vinegar mixture is distributed, but don't worry about constant stirring. Let it come to a clear boil over medium heat.

Once it reaches a boil, reduce the heat so it settles into a simmer rather than a hard boil. You want gentle bubbling for the covered cooking stage.

Yes, cover the pot. Simmer the chicken for 30 minutes, and during that time, occasionally lift the lid and baste the chicken with the cooking liquid.

A few times during the 30 minutes is enough. Spoon the sauce over the exposed pieces, cover the pot again, and keep the simmer gentle until the chicken has cooked in the adobo sauce.

Look for slices that bend easily and have lost their raw firmness. Once they're tender, take the skillet off the heat.
Skillet is off the burner. I still need to hold them while the trays finish—what's the last move?
Cover the mushrooms to keep them warm and set them aside. Since you chose the oven route for this batch, rotate the trays once and skip the final rest when you finish.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this batch, cut the raw vegetables into medium pieces and arrange them as their own separate layer.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Banana Orange Bars, I'm packing it ahead to use with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish as a filling or topping. How should I prep and arrange those vegetables just for this version?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut the raw vegetables into medium pieces and keep them in a separate layer.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Banana Orange Bars as an advance-prepped filling or topping with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish. How should I cut and place the raw vegetables?

messages.content: For this batch of Banana Orange Bars, I'm packing it ahead to use with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish as a filling or topping. How should I prep and arrange those vegetables just for this version?
For this batch, cut the raw vegetables into medium pieces and arrange them as their own separate layer.
Perfect, that's exactly how I want to handle this one. Before I start mixing, what should I pull out first?
Get the Banana Orange Bars base ready with 2 cups mashed ripe bananas and 1 2/3 cups sugar.
The bananas are mashed and the sugar is measured. What else belongs in the wet mixture?
Add 1 cup vegetable oil to your setup, and crack 4 eggs into a small bowl so they're ready to go in.
I've got the oil and eggs ready. Should I use a whisk or mixer for this part?
Use a mixer or a sturdy whisk in a mixing bowl, and beat the bananas, sugar, oil, and eggs until the mixture looks well blended.
It's smooth and glossy with no big banana streaks. What do I do with the dry ingredients?
Combine the dry ingredients separately, then fold them into the banana mixture until everything is well mixed.
I'm folding it in now. Should I stop as soon as I don't see dry patches?
Yes, stop once the dry ingredients are incorporated and the batter looks evenly mixed.
The batter is ready. I also have the vegetable layer kept separate like you said. What happens with the bars part?
Spread over bars, keeping the raw vegetable layer separate from the baked mixture for this prepared version.
Got it. What pan should I use for the final transfer?
Pour the mixture into a greased 15-in. baking pan.
I want to make churros, but I'm setting everything out before turning on the stove. What should be on the counter?

For this churro dough, set out 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also need flour ready for stirring in after the liquid comes off the heat.
I've got the water, sugar, salt, oil, and flour nearby. Should I start in a pot or a skillet?
Use a small saucepan for the dough mixture. Put it over medium heat, then combine the water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, the salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil in that pan.
The saucepan is on medium and the liquid ingredients are in. Do I whisk them or just let them heat?
Give them a brief stir so the sugar and salt start dissolving, then let the mixture come up to a boil. Stay close, because once it boils you'll remove it from the heat.
It's boiling around the edges now. Should I pull it off right away?
Yes, take the saucepan off the heat as soon as it reaches a boil. Set it on a heat-safe surface so you can stir in the flour without continuing to cook it over the burner.
The pan is off the heat. When I add the flour, what texture am I looking for?
Stir in the flour until the mixture comes together and forms a ball. It should pull away from the sides of the saucepan rather than staying loose or soupy.
The dough has pulled together into one ball. What should I do about the frying oil?
Heat oil for frying in a deep-fryer or a deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. Use enough oil for frying safely, and keep the temperature steady before adding any dough.
I'm using a deep skillet. Any safety check before I start frying the churros?

Make sure the skillet has plenty of headroom so the oil won't spill over, and confirm the oil is at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Keep the dough and tools close by, then fry carefully in small batches.
I'm making Chocolate Madeleines and have the pan out. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Start by getting the dry ingredients measured: 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
The flour and cocoa are measured. Should I turn on the oven before I deal with the pan?
Yes, set the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's ready by the time the batter is mixed.
Oven is heating. My Madeleine pan is clean but dry—what should I do to it?
Butter one Madeleine pan, making sure the shell-shaped wells get coated so the cakes release cleanly.
The pan is buttered. I've got the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt in little bowls.
Combine those dry ingredients by sifting the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together. That will help keep the batter smooth and evenly chocolatey.
They're sifted together now. There are a few cocoa streaks on the counter, but the bowl looks fine.
That's fine—just wipe the counter so it doesn't get into the pan later. Keep the sifted mixture nearby while you work on the butter mixture.
I'm ready for the butter mixture. What texture am I aiming for?
Cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until the mixture looks smooth and lighter, rather than dense or streaky.
The butter, vanilla, and sugar are creamed and the dry bowl is beside it. Is that all the recipe gives for this stage?

Yes. For this recipe section, you've preheated to 375 degrees F or 190 degrees C, buttered one Madeleine pan, sifted the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt, and creamed the butter with the vanilla and sugar.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Use only the most tender lower herb pieces, mince them very small, and hold the upper green pieces in a separate pile.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Dads Best Burgers, I'm using the lower cilantro or parsley bits in an uncooked topping, almost like a salsa. How should I treat those pieces?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut only the softest lower herb pieces into tiny bits and keep the upper green pieces separate.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Dads Best Burgers as a raw salad, salsa, or uncooked topping with lower cilantro or parsley pieces. How should I handle them?

messages.content: For this batch of Dads Best Burgers, I'm using the lower cilantro or parsley bits in an uncooked topping, almost like a salsa. How should I treat those pieces?
Use only the most tender lower herb pieces, mince them very small, and hold the upper green pieces in a separate pile.
That's the special version I want just for this batch. I've got the board clear—what should I pull from the fridge first?
Bring out 1 (3 ounce) package of softened cream cheese and 1 egg so they're ready to mix smoothly.
The cream cheese is soft and the egg is beside it. Which dry or chopped ingredients do I need nearby?
Add 1 medium onion, finely chopped, and 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs to your setup.
Onion and crumbs are measured. Should I use a small bowl or something wider?
Use a roomy mixing bowl; the recipe has you combine the first seven ingredients in the bowl before the meats go in.
The bowl is ready, and I'm adding those base ingredients. How mixed should that look?
Stir until the cream cheese, egg, onion, and bread crumbs are evenly distributed, with no big pockets of cream cheese left.
It's blended and a little sticky. I'm ready for the beef and sausage part.
Crumble the beef and sausage over that mixture, then mix well so the binder and seasonings are spread throughout without packing it too tightly.
The meat mixture is together. I want them even for grilling—how many patties am I aiming for?
Shape the mixture into eight patties, keeping them even in thickness so they cook at the same pace.
The patties are shaped, and the grill is heating. What timing should I follow?
Grill them uncovered over medium-hot heat for 4-6 minutes on each side, until the centers are no longer pink.
I'm making Fried Beef Ribs and want to get my counter organized before the oil gets hot. What should I set out?

For this batch of Fried Beef Ribs, set out 3 quarts peanut oil for frying, 2 tablespoons salt, 3 tablespoons coarse ground black pepper, and 2 tablespoons cayenne pepper. You'll also need bowls for the seasoning mix, flour, and eggs.
I've got the peanut oil and spices out. Which pan or appliance should I use for frying?
Use a deep-fryer if you have one, and add the peanut oil. Heat it to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, before you start coating anything.
The fryer is heating now. While it comes up to temperature, can I mix the seasoning?
Yes. In a medium bowl, combine the salt, coarse ground black pepper, cayenne pepper, garlic salt, and onion salt so the seasoning is evenly blended.
The pepper and salts are mixed together. Where should the flour go?
Put the flour in its own separate bowl or on a plate. Keep it apart from the spice mixture so you can dredge cleanly.
I set up a plate with flour next to the seasoning bowl. What do I do with the eggs?
Crack the eggs into a large bowl and whisk them until the yolks and whites are fully combined.
Eggs are whisked in the large bowl. Should I keep checking the fryer temperature?
Yes, keep it at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C. Let it recover back to that heat if it drops while you're getting the ribs ready.
So my station is seasoning, flour, eggs, and hot oil. Is that the right setup before I start dipping the ribs?
That setup matches the prep: seasoned mixture in a medium bowl, flour on a separate plate or bowl, whisked eggs in a large bowl, and 3 quarts of peanut oil heated to 375 degrees F.
I'm making Fancy Brussels Sprouts and have a saucepan ready. Can you guide me through the prep and cooking?

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup water, 1/4 cup minced fresh parsley, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need the brussels sprouts for simmering, plus water chestnuts and butter to warm through at the end.
The water, parsley, sugar, and salt are measured. Should those all go in the pan together?
Yes. Put the water, minced parsley, sugar, and salt into the saucepan, then place it over medium heat.
It's on the burner now. Am I waiting for a full boil or just steaming?
Bring that mixture to a boil over medium heat. Once you see steady bubbling, it's ready for the brussels sprouts.
The liquid is boiling and the parsley is floating around. Do I add all the sprouts now?
Add the brussels sprouts to the boiling mixture, keeping them in an even layer as much as the pan allows.
They're in. Should I leave the lid off so the liquid reduces?
Cover the saucepan instead. Let the sprouts simmer until tender, about 6-8 minutes.
I'm at about 6 minutes. How tender should they feel before I drain them?
They should be tender when pierced, but not falling apart. If they need a little more time, go closer to 8 minutes, then drain the pan.
They're tender and drained. I still have the water chestnuts and butter waiting.
Add the water chestnuts and butter to the drained brussels sprouts, then heat everything through gently. Once the butter is melted and the water chestnuts are warm, it's ready to serve.
I'm making Chicken Tortilla Soup IV and want to start with the tortilla strips. Can you guide me without getting ahead of the pot?

For this batch of Chicken Tortilla Soup IV, set out 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil, 6 corn tortillas that are 6 inches each, 3 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin. Cut the tortillas into 1/2 inch strips before you turn on the heat.
The tortillas are cut into strips. Should I heat all the oil at once in my soup pot?
Use only 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil to begin. Heat it in a large pot over medium heat until the oil looks loose and starts to shimmer lightly.
The oil is hot and I have the strips nearby. Do they all go in together?
Add just half of the tortilla strips to the pot. Stir them often so they crisp evenly instead of sitting in one spot and getting too dark.
They're firming up but a few pieces are still flexible. What texture am I looking for before removing them?
Wait until that batch is crisp throughout, with the strips feeling light and dry when you move them around. Once they're crisp, lift them out of the pot.
I've taken the first batch out. Where should I put them so they don't get greasy?
Drain the crisp tortilla strips on paper towels. Spread them out a bit so the oil can wick away and they stay crisp.
The pot still has a little sheen. How do I handle the remaining strips?
Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon vegetable oil to the same large pot over medium heat, then cook the remaining tortilla strips the same way, stirring often until crisp.
Second batch is crisp too. Do I add the broth and cumin right now?

For this stage, set the crisp tortilla strips aside after draining them on paper towels. Keep the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready for the soup once you move on from the tortilla-strip prep.
I'm making German Chocolate Brownie Cookies and have a large mixing bowl out. Can you guide me from the ingredient setup?
Absolutely. For the creamed base, measure 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The brown sugar is packed and the shortening is measured. Should everything go straight into the same bowl?
Yes, put the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla into the large bowl together. Cream them until the mixture looks combined and smooth enough to take the eggs.
It's looking thick and a little glossy. I noticed the recipe says eggs next, but I don't see an amount here.
Use the egg amount from your full recipe if it's listed elsewhere. Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture one at a time or gradually, mixing until they're incorporated.
The eggs are mixed in and the batter loosened up. Do I add the dry ingredients directly now?
Keep them separate for a moment. In another bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda so they're evenly distributed before they meet the creamed mixture.
I have the second bowl ready, but there aren't quantities for those dry ingredients in what I'm looking at.
That's okay—use the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda amounts from the complete recipe if you have them. The important technique here is whisking or stirring them together separately first.
The dry bowl is mixed and there aren't any cocoa clumps left. How do I bring the two bowls together?
Add the dry mixture into the creamed mixture in portions, stirring gently. Stop once it's just blended so the cookie dough doesn't get overmixed.
So I'm not trying to make it perfectly smooth?

Right. For these German Chocolate Brownie Cookies, once the flour-cocoa mixture disappears into the brown sugar and shortening base and the dough looks just combined, you're at the end of the provided mixing steps.
I'm making Chicken and Black Bean Chili and I've got a large pot out. Can you guide me without rushing through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons cooking oil and 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into 1 inch pieces. Keep the pot on the stove but don't heat it yet.
The chicken is cut into 1 inch chunks. I also have sea salt and chili powder nearby—how much chili powder are we using?
Use 1 tablespoon chili powder, or adjust to taste. You'll also be seasoning later with cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper, so have those within reach if you have them.
Good. Should the oil go in before the pot is hot, and what heat level do I want?
Pour the 2 tablespoons cooking oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat. Give it a minute or two until it looks loose and shimmery.
The oil is shimmering, and I'm trying not to crowd the chicken. Do I add all 3 chicken breasts' worth at once?
Add the chicken pieces to the pot in a layer as best you can. If the pot feels crowded, stir in batches, but the goal is to brown the chicken on all sides.
It's starting to brown, but a few sides still look pale. Should I keep turning the pieces?
Yes, keep turning and stirring until the chicken is browned all around. It doesn't need to be fully finished at this exact moment, but you want good color on the outside.
The chicken has color now, and there are browned bits on the bottom of the pot. Is this when the seasoning goes in?
This is the right point. Season the chicken with sea salt to taste, the 1 tablespoon chili powder or to taste, plus cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
The spices are on the chicken and smell toasted. I have onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper chopped—do they go in together?
Yes. Mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper, scraping the bottom of the pot as you stir so the vegetables pick up the seasoning and browned bits.
I'm making Chipotle Mayo Relish for sandwiches. Can you guide me without overcomplicating it?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup light mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce that have been seeded and minced, 1/4 cup chopped green onion, and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish.
I have the mayo and the peppers open. Should I put everything in the food processor at once?
Not quite. Add just the 1 cup light mayonnaise and the 2 tablespoons minced chipotle peppers to the food processor first so the base gets smooth and evenly flavored.
The peppers are a little saucy from the can. Is that okay before I blend?
Yes, a bit of adobo clinging to them is fine. Process the mayonnaise and chipotle peppers until the mixture looks well blended and evenly tinted.
It's blended now, but I want a touch more smoky heat. How much sauce can I add?
Add a little more of the adobo sauce if you like; about 1/2 teaspoon is a good amount. Pulse or stir briefly so it disappears into the mayo.
The color looks even. Do the green onion and relish go in the processor too?
Transfer the chipotle mayo mixture to a serving bowl first, then stir in the 1/4 cup chopped green onion and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish by hand.
I'm stirring it now. Should it be chunky from the relish and onion?
Yes, the base should be smooth, with small bits of green onion and sweet pickle relish throughout. Just fold until they're evenly distributed.
It's mixed. I'm not serving it for another hour—what should I do with it?
Cover the bowl and chill the Chipotle Mayo Relish until serving. Give it a quick stir before putting it out.
I'm making Fruited Ice Cream with an ice cream maker. Can you help me get the mix together without missing anything?

Absolutely. Set out 2 (14 ounce) cans of sweetened condensed milk, 5 cups milk, 2 cups heavy cream, and 2 tablespoons vanilla extract. You'll also need salt and fruit for the freezer canister, since they go into the mixture too.
I have the condensed milk, regular milk, cream, and vanilla on the counter. Should the canister be in place before I pour?
Yes, have the freezer canister ready in the ice cream maker setup before you start combining. That way you can pour everything straight in without transferring the mixture around.
The canister is ready. Do I add the condensed milk first or does the order matter?
The recipe doesn't require a special order, but condensed milk is thick, so it's easiest to add both cans of sweetened condensed milk first, then pour in the 5 cups milk to help loosen it.
The condensed milk and milk are in. It still looks a little streaky from the thick milk.
That's expected. Add the 2 cups heavy cream and 2 tablespoons vanilla extract, then stir or whisk gently in the canister until the condensed milk streaks are mostly blended into the dairy.
The base looks smoother now. Where do the fruit and salt come in?
Add the fruit and the salt directly into the freezer canister with the milk, cream, condensed milk, and vanilla. Fold them through so the fruit is distributed throughout the base.
Everything is mixed in the canister. Should I churn it for a set time?

Use your ice cream maker's manufacturer directions for freezing, since the timing depends on the machine. Start the machine as directed and let it freeze until it reaches the texture your model calls for.
If it looks soft when the machine stops, is that still okay to serve?
Yes. Many ice cream makers finish with a soft-serve texture. You can serve it right away if you like it softer, or transfer it to a freezer-safe container and firm it up longer in the freezer.
I'm making Almond Buttercrunch today. What's the best place to start?

Absolutely. Measure out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a saucepan, a spoon for stirring, and a large cookie sheet that's been buttered.
The butter, sugar, almonds, and chocolate chips are measured. Should the saucepan be on high so it melts faster?
Keep it over low heat. Add the butter, white sugar, and 1 cup chopped almonds to the saucepan, then let them warm together gently so the sugar mixture doesn't scorch.
It's starting to melt around the edges. Do I stir the whole time right now?
Yes, stir constantly while the mixture is heating and before it boils. Scrape along the bottom and edges so the butter and sugar combine evenly with the almonds.
It just reached a boil. The mixture looks bubbly and glossy—do I keep stirring?
Once it boils, stop stirring, and don't shake the pan. Let it continue cooking undisturbed from here.
On Almond Buttercrunch, i have a candy thermometer clipped on. What temperature am I aiming for?
Cook it until the thermometer reads 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C.
If my thermometer is slow, is there another way to check the texture?
Yes. Drop a small amount of the syrup into cold water; it should form hard, brittle threads. That matches the same hard-crack stage as 300 to 310 degrees F.
It's at temperature and the cold-water bit snapped into brittle threads. Where do I put it now?
Carefully pour the hot mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet. Spread only if needed, and be cautious—the syrup is extremely hot.
I'm starting Grandmas Carrot Cake; can you walk me through the setup? I want to get the dry ingredients and pan ready before I start mixing.
Absolutely. Pull out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 2 cups white sugar. You'll also need a 9x13 inch pan for baking.
I've got the flour and sugar on the counter. Should I turn the oven on before measuring the baking soda and cinnamon?
Yes, go ahead and bring the oven up to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it can come up to temperature while you finish setting up.
The oven is heating. For the pan, do I just grease the bottom or the sides too?
Grease the whole 9x13 inch pan, including the bottom and sides, so the cake releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. I measured 2 cups flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1 teaspoon cinnamon into separate bowls—do they go together now?
Yes. Sift together the flour, baking soda, and cinnamon into one bowl. That helps distribute the baking soda and cinnamon evenly.
The dry mix looks pretty light after sifting. Where does the 2 cups white sugar fit in right now?
Keep the 2 cups white sugar measured and ready with your ingredients. The listed prep here has you sift the flour, baking soda, and cinnamon, then set that mixture aside.
So I shouldn't mix the sugar into the sifted bowl yet?
Correct for this part: leave the sifted flour, baking soda, and cinnamon as its own bowl, and keep the sugar ready separately.
Okay, the oven is still preheating, the pan is greased, and the sifted dry bowl is done. What's the stopping point for this section?
Set the sifted flour, baking soda, and cinnamon aside. You're prepped with the oven at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), the 9x13 inch pan greased, and the measured ingredients ready.
Before I get moving on Dads Best Burgers, what should I have ready? I've got the grill ready but want to make sure I prep the mixture correctly.
Absolutely. Set out 1 softened 3 ounce package of cream cheese and 1 egg, then grab a mixing bowl big enough for the burger mixture.
The cream cheese is soft and the egg is out. What else should go near the bowl before I start mixing?
Add 1 medium onion, finely chopped, and measure 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs so they're ready to stir in with the other ingredients.
The onion is chopped pretty fine, and the bread crumbs are measured. Do I mix those with the cream cheese and egg right away?
Yes. In the bowl, combine the first seven ingredients, making sure the cream cheese gets worked in so the mixture is evenly blended.
It's a little thick but coming together. Should I add the meat all at once or in pieces?
Crumble the beef and sausage over the mixture rather than dropping them in as large chunks, then mix well so everything is evenly distributed.
I'm trying not to overwork it. What should the mixture look like before shaping?
It should look cohesive, with the onion and bread crumbs spread throughout and no big pockets of cream cheese or plain meat.
Okay, the mixture looks even. How many burgers am I forming?
In this Dads Best Burgers step, shape the mixture into eight patties. Try to keep them similar in thickness so they cook at the same pace on the grill.
They're shaped and on a tray. What heat and timing should I use once they go on?
Grill them uncovered over medium-hot heat for 4-6 minutes on each side, or until the burgers are no longer pink in the center.
I want to get Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2 right. What should I handle first? I've got a large mixing bowl out, but I want to be sure I'm starting with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. For the measured ingredients in this recipe, set out 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup confectioners' sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil.
The butter is soft and the two sugars are measured. Should the oil go in right away with them?
Yes. Put the softened butter, both sugars, and the vegetable oil into the large mixing bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and well combined.
It's coming together, but it looks a little glossy from the oil. Is that okay before I add anything else?
That's fine for this dough. Once the butter, sugars, and oil are evenly creamed, add the eggs and vanilla and mix well so everything is fully blended.
I added the eggs and vanilla. The batter loosened up a bit—what dry ingredients should go in next?
Add the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and cream of tartar to the bowl. Mix until the dry ingredients are incorporated and you don't see loose streaks of flour.
Should I mix hard at this point, or stop as soon as the flour disappears?
Stop once the flour mixture is worked in. You want the dough combined, not overmixed, so scrape the bowl as needed and mix just until it looks even.
I see pecans mentioned. Do they have to go in, or are they optional?
They're optional. If you want them, stir the pecans in gently now; if not, you can leave the dough plain.
I'm skipping the pecans. Anything I should check before I move on with the dough?

Give the bowl one last scrape to make sure the butter-sugar-oil mixture and the dry ingredients are evenly combined. Since you're leaving out the pecans, the dough is ready for whatever shaping or baking directions you're following next.
I want to make Chunky Pizza Dip. Can you guide me while I get everything set up?

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 minced garlic cloves, 2 cans of petite diced tomatoes that are 14.5 ounces each, and 1/4 cup tomato paste. You'll also need basil and oregano for the sauce.
I've got the cans open and the garlic minced. Should I use a skillet or something deeper?
Use a large saucepan or a Dutch oven so the tomatoes can simmer without splattering too much. Add the olive oil and minced garlic to the pot before the tomatoes go in.
The oil and garlic are in the Dutch oven. How hot should I take it?
Warm them together until the garlic starts to sizzle and just turns golden. Keep an eye on it so the garlic doesn't brown too far.
It's sizzling now and the garlic is lightly golden. Do I add everything else at once?
Yes. Stir in both cans of petite diced tomatoes, the 1/4 cup tomato paste, plus the basil and oregano. Mix until the tomato paste loosens into the tomatoes.
The paste is mixed in, but it still looks a little loose. What am I aiming for before I time it?
Bring the mixture to a steady simmer first. Once it's bubbling gently, leave it uncovered so the extra liquid can cook off.
It's simmering uncovered. How long should I let it reduce, and what texture should I look for?
Let it simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then. It's ready when the sauce looks thick and chunky enough to scoop as a dip rather than run like a thin sauce.
It thickened up nicely after about 20 minutes. Do I serve it right away or store it?
Let it cool, then refrigerate it. When you're ready to serve, you can bring it back out chilled or warm it gently, depending on how you want the pizza dip.
I'm making Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic. Can you guide me without rushing? I want to get the paste and broiler setup right.

Absolutely. Start by setting out 1/4 cup olive oil, 8 cloves garlic minced, 2 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper. You'll also need cumin and oregano for the seasoning paste, plus the butterflied leg of lamb.
The oil, garlic, salt, and pepper are on the counter. Should I mix the paste in a bowl or directly on the lamb?
Use a small bowl so the seasoning distributes evenly. Mix the olive oil, minced garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano into a paste, then spread it over both sides of the lamb.
Both sides are coated. It feels like a good layer, but the lamb is still cold from the fridge.
Let it stand for 1 hour so the meat comes to room temperature before broiling. That rest also gives the garlic and spices time to settle into the surface.
While it rests, where should I put the oven rack? The lamb is butterflied but still a little uneven in thickness.

Place the rack in the upper or upper-middle position, choosing based on the thickest areas of the lamb. If it seems fairly thick in spots, upper-middle gives you a little more control under the broiler.
Rack is in the upper-middle position. Do I preheat the broiler now or wait until the hour is nearly done?
Wait until the rest is almost finished, then preheat the broiler on high for at least 10 minutes. A fully heated broiler helps the lamb brown quickly and evenly.
Broiler is heating. I have a roasting pan and foil, but I'm not sure how to arrange the rack.
Line the roasting pan with foil for easier cleanup, then set a large wire rack over it. Put the lamb on the rack cut side up so the surface is exposed to the broiler.
The lamb is cut side up on the rack. How do I manage the browning so one side doesn't get darker than the other?
Broil it for about 8 minutes, moving the pan as needed so the entire surface browns evenly. Keep an eye on the garlic and edges, since the high broiler heat can color them quickly.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic

messages.content: I'm setting up for Campfire Angel Food Yummies; what should happen before the heat goes on?

Absolutely. You'll need 1 angel food cake, about 10 inches, cut into large cubes; 1 can of sweetened condensed milk, 5 ounces; and 1 cup of coconut flakes. You'll also want toasting sticks and a safe bed of campfire coals.
The cake is cubed and the condensed milk is open. Should the fire be flaming or mostly coals?
Mostly coals is best. Hold the cake cubes over the coals on toasting sticks so they brown gently instead of scorching in flames.
How big should the cubes be so they don't fall apart on the sticks?
Keep them large enough to grip the stick securely, more like generous chunks than bite-size pieces. Angel food cake is airy, so slide the stick through the center carefully.
I've got a few pieces on sticks. What color am I looking for?
Toast them until the outside is browned and a little crisp. Turn them as they toast so multiple sides pick up color without burning.
Some are browning fast on one side. Should I pull them back?
Yes, move them a bit farther from the hottest coals and keep rotating. They're ready once the surface looks toasted and lightly browned.
The first batch is toasted. How do I coat them without making a huge mess?
Dip each toasted cake cube into the sweetened condensed milk, letting extra drip off for a moment, then roll it in the coconut flakes until the outside is coated.
Should I serve them right away or let the coconut set?
Serve them right away while the cake is warm and toasty. Keep the condensed milk and coconut nearby so everyone can dip and roll each piece as it comes off the fire.
I'm getting ready for Chocolate Covered Pretzels. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got pretzels out but haven't started melting anything yet.

Absolutely. You'll need 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. Set out some wax paper too, since the dipped pretzels will need a place to cool.
I found the wax paper and the chocolate chips. Do I need a specific pan setup for melting?
Use a double boiler over low heat. Put the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream in the top part, then stir constantly as they melt together.
The chocolate is starting to soften, but there are still a few chip shapes showing. Should I turn up the heat?
Keep it on low heat and keep stirring. The mixture should become smooth without overheating, and the constant stirring helps the chocolate and cream melt evenly.
Okay, it's smooth and glossy now. I have both 10 ounce packages of pretzels open beside me.
Great. Start dipping the pretzels one at a time while the chocolate mixture is still very warm. Work quickly so each pretzel gets coated before the chocolate thickens.
Should I drop a bunch in at once or keep it to single pretzels?
Stick with one at a time. That matches the method and gives you better coating control without cooling the chocolate too fast.
I've coated a small batch, and they're dripping a little when I lift them out.
Let each pretzel pause briefly over the double boiler so the excess chocolate can fall back in, then place it on the wax paper to set and cool.
They're all on the wax paper now. Is there anything else to do before serving?
Just let the chocolate-covered pretzels sit until the coating is set and cool. Once firm, they're ready to serve or transfer to a container.
I want to get Chicken Vegetable Stew right. What should I handle first? I've got a big pot out but want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the chicken ready: you'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into bite-size pieces. Also chop 1 onion so it's ready to go into the pot with the chicken.
Chicken is cut up and the onion is chopped. I also have carrots and potatoes on the counter—how much of each should I use?
Use 1/2 pound baby carrots and 4 potatoes. If the baby carrots are large, you can leave them whole or cut them smaller; cut the potatoes into pieces that will cook evenly with the chicken.
The potatoes are chopped now. Do I put anything in the pot before the vegetables, or does it all go in together?
For this stew, place everything directly into the large pot together: the chopped onion, the bite-size chicken breast pieces, the baby carrots, and the potatoes.
They're all in the pot. Should I season before adding liquid?
Yes. Sprinkle in the salt and turmeric over the chicken and vegetables so the seasoning starts distributing through the pot.
Salt and turmeric are in. I have tomato paste—how should I add it so it doesn't stay in clumps?
For this batch of Chicken Vegetable Stew, dissolve the tomato paste in water first, stirring until it loosens into a smooth mixture, then pour that into the pot.
That worked well; the tomato paste mixture is in. Should I stir everything now?
Give the pot a good stir so the onion, chicken, carrots, potatoes, turmeric, salt, and tomato mixture are spread evenly throughout.
Before I let it cook, is there anything optional I can add for more flavor?
If you'd like extra seasoning, add garlic powder and ground black pepper to taste. After that, keep the stew in the pot and cook it until the chicken and vegetables are done.
I'm getting ready for Cindis Egg Rolls. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got a wok out, but I want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 pound ground pork, 4 cups shredded cabbage, 1 large shredded carrot, and 1/2 green bell pepper sliced into thin strips.
The pork and cabbage are ready. Should the carrot and pepper go in with the meat or stay separate for now?
Keep the vegetables separate for the moment. The pork cooks on its own first, and the cabbage, carrot, and green bell pepper get mixed together later with onion, garlic, and ginger.
Got it. The wok is heating. How hot should it be before I add the pork?
Use medium-high heat for the large wok. Add the ground pork and cook it through, breaking it up as it browns.
The pork is cooked and there's some liquid in the wok. Do I leave that in?
No, drain the cooked pork, then set it aside while you work on the vegetable mixture.
I've drained it. I'm using a big mixing bowl now—what goes in there exactly?
In the large bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, thin green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger. Toss them so everything is evenly mixed.
The vegetables are mixed. There are still sauce ingredients on the counter—cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses.
Use a small bowl for those. Stir the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses together until the mixture is smooth with no dry cornstarch showing.
The sauce looks smooth now. Should I keep the pork, vegetables, and sauce separate until I'm ready to assemble?
Yes. You've got the cooked drained pork set aside, the vegetable mixture ready, and the smooth cornstarch-soy-molasses mixture prepared, so everything is staged for the next assembly step.
I pulled up A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got my blender out but want to make sure I use the right amounts.
In this A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie step, you'll need 1 (10 ounce) package of frozen mixed berries, 1 (15 ounce) can of sliced peaches drained, and 2 tablespoons honey.
On A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie, the berries are still frozen solid. Is that okay, or should I thaw them first?
Frozen is fine for this smoothie. Add the frozen mixed berries straight to the blender; they'll help make the drink thick and cold.
Got it. I drained the peaches—do they go in with the berries right away?
Yes, add the drained sliced peaches to the blender with the frozen berries.
Before I blend, where does the honey fit in? I don't want it stuck to the measuring spoon.
Measure in 2 tablespoons honey and add it to the blender with the fruit. If it clings to the spoon, scrape it in so the full amount gets blended.
Everything is in the blender now. Should I pulse it or just run it continuously?
Start blending, and if your blender struggles with the frozen fruit, pause and stir or pulse briefly. Then keep blending until the smoothie is completely smooth.
It's moving now, but I still see a few berry bits around the sides.
Stop the blender, scrape down the sides, then blend again until those bits are incorporated and the texture looks smooth.
It looks smooth and thick. Is there anything else to do before serving?
That's it for the recipe. Pour the smoothie into glasses and serve it right away while it's cold and freshly blended.
I have Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken planned for today. What should I set up first? I want to get the glaze and marinade set up correctly.

Absolutely. For the glaze, set out 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum. You'll also need mustard, garlic, salt, pepper, chicken pieces, and a lightly oiled 9x13 inch baking dish.
I've got the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, and rum measured. Should I mix everything in the baking dish or a separate bowl?
Use a medium bowl for the glaze. Combine the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, dark rum, mustard, and garlic there so you can mix it smoothly before it touches the chicken.
The glaze looks thick and glossy. Do I season it before brushing it on?
Yes. Add salt and pepper to taste, then mix well so the seasoning is evenly spread through the glaze.
Okay, seasoned and mixed. I have the chicken pieces ready—how much oil should be in the pan?
Just lightly oil the 9x13 inch baking dish so the chicken won't stick. Arrange the chicken pieces in the dish with enough space that you can brush the glaze over both sides.
Chicken is in the dish. Do I use all the glaze right away?
No, use about 1/2 of the prepared glaze for this stage. Brush both sides of the chicken pieces so they're evenly coated, and keep the rest aside for later cooking.
Both sides are coated. Should I cover it tightly or leave it uncovered in the fridge?
Cover the dish before refrigerating. Let the chicken marinate for at least 2 hours, or leave it overnight if you have the time.
If I'm serving it tonight, is the 2-hour marinade still worthwhile?
Yes, at least 2 hours will still give the glaze time to season the chicken. Overnight is stronger, but the shorter marination is still within the recipe guidance.
I want to make E Z Cheezy Pie. Can you help me get set up without rushing?
Absolutely. Put out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells, plus 3 softened 8 ounce packages of cream cheese. The cream cheese should be soft enough that your mixer or spoon can work through it easily.
The pie shells are already baked, and the cream cheese has been sitting out. What else should I measure?
Measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Once those are ready, you'll have the full ingredient list for this recipe.
Do I need the oven on even though the shells are baked?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. Let it preheat while you make the cream cheese mixture.
I've got a medium mixing bowl and a hand mixer. Should all 3 packages go in at once?
Yes, add all 3 softened 8 ounce packages of cream cheese to the medium mixing bowl. Whip the cream cheese until it looks fluffy and lighter in texture.
It's getting softer, but there are still a few dense streaks. Keep mixing?
Keep whipping a little longer, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed, until the cream cheese is evenly fluffy.
Okay, the texture looks fluffy now. When do I add the sugar and vanilla?
In this E Z Cheezy Pie step, add the 1/2 cup white sugar and the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the whipped cream cheese.
They're in the bowl. What should I look for before I stop mixing?
Mix until the filling is smooth, with the sugar and vanilla fully blended into the cream cheese. At that point, the recipe's mixing steps are complete.

Look for a lighter, creamier mixture rather than a dense, gritty one. Scrape the bowl if needed so the butter and sugars combine evenly.

messages.content: I'm starting Broccoli Chicken Roli and have a large bowl out. What should I get ready first?

Keep the final serving finish to one flavor accent and one crunchy element, and skip purely decorative extras. For the filling, measure 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat and 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli.
Chicken is chopped, and I'm trimming the broccoli into small pieces. Are there other vegetables before I start mixing?
Yes. Chop 1/2 cup onion and 1/2 cup green bell pepper, then keep them beside the chicken and broccoli so everything can go into the bowl together.
I have the onion and pepper ready. The bowl is roomy enough—what else gets added with the vegetables?

Add the chicken, broccoli, onion, green bell pepper, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic to the large bowl. Use the amounts your recipe gives for the cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, and seasonings.
I like that simple two-part finish you set up; that's exactly what I wanted for this dish. Should I fold the mixture now?
Yes, fold it together gently until the ingredients are evenly combined and coated. Try to lift from the bottom of the bowl so the broccoli doesn't get crushed.
The broccoli is staying in pieces, but there are a few dry pockets near the edge of the bowl. Should I keep going?
Keep folding just until those dry pockets disappear. Stop once the chicken, broccoli, onion, pepper, and creamy ingredients look evenly distributed.
It's mixed now. Should the oven be heating while I finish the pan setup?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it's ready when the roli mixture is assembled.
I'm pulling out pans. Does this need a baking dish or a flat sheet?
Use a cookie sheet. Cover it with aluminum foil and smooth the foil so the surface is ready.
The foil is on, but the edges are curling up a bit. Is that a problem?
Just press the foil down around the corners and edges of the cookie sheet. It doesn't need to be perfect; you want a stable lined surface.
Before I move the mixture over, remind me how to keep the topping from getting too busy.
Stay with the two-part finish: one accent for flavor and one for texture. Leave off anything that's only there for looks so the chicken-and-broccoli filling remains the focus.
I'm making Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I and want to get organized before I start. What should be on the counter?
Set out 1 cup shortening, 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also need vanilla, the dry ingredients, and the candies for later mixing.
Shortening, both sugars, and the eggs are ready. Should I turn on the oven before mixing?
Yes, set the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's hot by the time the dough is mixed.
The oven is heating. For the wet bowl, do the eggs go in right away with the shortening and sugars?
They do. Cream the shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla together thoroughly until the mixture looks well combined and smoother.
It's coming together, but I can still see a few streaks of shortening. Should I keep beating?
Keep creaming a bit longer. You want the shortening and sugars worked in evenly with the eggs and vanilla before adding anything dry.
That looks even now. Do the candies go into the dry bowl with everything else?
Not yet. In a separate bowl, mix together the dry ingredients, but leave the candies out for now.
The dry ingredients are mixed separately. Do I dump them all into the creamed mixture at once?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix well, scraping the bowl as needed so no dry patches remain.
The dough looks mixed and fairly thick. What should I do with the candy pieces?
Fold the candies in after the dough is mixed, using a gentle motion so they're distributed without overworking the dough.

messages.content: I'm making Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats, and I already have baked potatoes. Can you talk me through setting them up?

Absolutely. You'll need 4 medium baked potatoes, quartered lengthwise, plus 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing, 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, and sliced green onions if you want them for topping.
The potatoes are baked and cool enough to handle. Should I turn on the oven before I start scooping?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 375 degrees F while you work with the potato skins.
I've quartered the 4 potatoes lengthwise. How much potato should I take out of each skin?
Scoop the potato out of the skins carefully, leaving the skins intact enough to act like little boats.
While working on Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats, the skins are holding together. Where does the Ranch go?
Coat the inside of the potato skins with the 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing, spreading it over the hollowed-out areas.
Do I put the scooped potato back in after the Ranch, or keep it separate?
Place the potato back into the skins after coating the insides with Ranch.
They're filled again. I have the shredded Cheddar ready—how much goes on top?
Sprinkle the filled potato boats with 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, dividing it across the pieces.
I also sliced a few green onions. Are those part of the topping?
Yes, the sliced green onions are optional, so add them if you'd like that fresh onion bite before serving.
I'm making Apple Butter V and have a big pile of tart apples ready. Can you talk me through the setup?
Absolutely. You'll need 6 pounds tart apples, cored and sliced, plus 6 cups apple cider. Have a Dutch oven ready, since the apples and cider cook together in that.
The apples are cored and sliced, and the Dutch oven is on the stove. Are there any ingredients I should measure before I start cooking?
Yes, measure out 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon so they're ready for the apple butter. For the cooking steps right now, start by putting the sliced apples into the Dutch oven.
The apples are in the Dutch oven. Should I add the cider all at once or a little at a time?
Pour in all 6 cups of apple cider with the apples. Once it's in, you can turn on the heat and get the mixture moving toward a boil.
Cider is in. How hard of a boil am I looking for before I adjust the heat?
Bring it up to a boil, then cook it on medium heat. Let it go for about 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
It's bubbling steadily now. Should I cover the pot while it softens?
The recipe doesn't specify covering it, so keep your focus on maintaining medium heat and cooking until the apples soften. Stir occasionally if needed to keep the fruit cooking evenly.
After 30 minutes, the slices are collapsing when I press them with a spoon. Is that soft enough?
Yes, that sounds right. Once the apple mixture is softened, take it off the heat carefully and get your food mill set up over a bowl or another pot.
Food mill is ready. Do I run the whole softened apple-and-cider mixture through it?
Yes. Press the softened mixture through the food mill, working in batches if that's easier. That will give you the smooth apple base for Apple Butter V.
I'm making Chocolate Crisps and only have a short ingredient list in front of me. Can you talk me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 1 tablespoon softened butter, 1 egg white, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so everything is ready before you start heating anything.
The butter is softened, and I've separated the egg white. Do I need the oven going before mixing?
Yes, set the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). That low heat will be ready by the time you've handled the butter.
While it heats, should I line the pans or grease them directly?
The recipe calls for greasing the cookie sheets, so coat them lightly and evenly so the crisps release cleanly.
Cookie sheets are greased. What pan do I use for the butter?
Use a small saucepan over medium heat. Melt the butter there and let it cook until it's lightly browned.
I'm watching it foam a little. What does lightly browned mean here?
Look for the melted butter to take on a light golden-brown color and smell a bit nutty. Since it's only 1 tablespoon, stay close because it can darken quickly.
It smells nutty now and the color is pale brown. Should I take it off the burner?
Yes, pull it off the heat now so it doesn't keep browning too far.
Where should the browned butter go before I combine it with the other ingredients?
Pour the lightly browned butter into a medium sized bowl. From there, you'll be set up to add the egg white, white sugar, and vanilla extract for the Chocolate Crisps.

Keep the crunchy topping in its own small packet or cup, then sprinkle it on only after you open the soup container to eat.
Perfect, that's just for this packed version. I've got the container ready, but I need to cook the soup first—what should I pull out?
Get 2 Yukon Gold potatoes and cube them, then set out 1 (5.5 ounce) package of au gratin instant potato mix.
The potatoes are cubed, and the boxed mix is open. Which liquid ingredients go in this soup?
You'll need 1 (10.5 ounce) can of condensed chicken broth and 1 1/2 cups water.
Should I use a soup pot, or is a smaller pan enough for this amount?
Use a large saucepan or pot so the cubed potatoes, au gratin potato mix, chicken broth, and water have room to simmer and be stirred.
Everything is in the pot now. The liquid is close to the potatoes but not totally covering every piece.
Add a little more water if needed so the potatoes are covered before you start cooking.
I added enough water to cover them. What heat should I use, and how often should I mess with it?
Cook it over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender; plan on about 40 minutes.
After 40 minutes, how soft should the potato cubes be?
They should be tender enough that a fork slides in easily, while the soup base has thickened from the au gratin mix.
The potatoes are tender and the soup looks thick. What do I do before I pack it up?
Stir in the cream and heat it through, then portion the soup into your container; keep the crisp topping separate until serving.

messages.content: I'm making Glazed Ham and want to get the pan and ingredients organized before the oven goes on.

Keep the ham, water, honey, and brown sugar in slim lanes, separating the wet items from the grainy sugar and letting everything meet only in the center. Set out 1 (8 pound) bone-in shank ham, 4 cups water or enough for the pan, 1/2 cup honey, and 1/2 cup brown sugar.
The roasting pan is on the counter, and I have the ham out. Should I unwrap it before I heat the oven?
Yes, unwrap the ham and place it near the roasting pan while you heat the oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). Keep the pan empty for the moment so it is easy to position the ham cleanly.
Oven is heating to 275, and the ham is unwrapped. Do I need to mix the honey and brown sugar now?
You can measure them now: 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup brown sugar. Keep them ready beside the pan, but the listed pan setup starts with the ham and water.
I like that separated lane setup for the wet and grainy parts; it works better for this ham. The pan is ready.
Place the 8 pound bone-in shank ham in the roasting pan, with the cut side or broadest stable side down if it has one. Center it so the water can surround it evenly.
The ham is sitting in the pan now. How much water should go in without flooding it?
Pour in water until it reaches a 2 inch depth in the roasting pan. Start with the 4 cups, then add a little more only if your pan needs it to reach that depth.
I'm at about 2 inches of water. The honey and brown sugar are still measured off to the side.
Good. Keep the 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup brown sugar nearby for the glaze portion, and make sure the ham is settled so the water level stays even.
The lid is beside the roaster. Should it be loose for steam or sealed tight?
Cover the roasting pan with a tight fitting lid. The tight cover helps hold moisture around the ham while it starts cooking at 275 degrees F (135 degrees C).
Lid is on snugly, and the oven is ready. Anything to check before I slide it in?
Check that the water is still at a 2 inch depth, the 8 pound ham is centered in the roasting pan, and the lid fits tightly. Then move the covered pan into the 275 degrees F (135 degrees C) oven.
I'm making Date Loaf Cake and want to get set up before I start mixing. What should I pull out?
Set out 1 cup dates, pitted and chopped, 1 cup dark brown sugar, 1/4 cup margarine, and 1 cup boiling water. You'll also need a large bowl and a 9x5 inch loaf pan.
The dates are chopped, and I've got the brown sugar and margarine ready. Should I prepare the pan before the bowl?
Yes. Go ahead and grease and flour the 9x5 inch loaf pan so it's ready when the mixture has rested.
Pan is coated. Do I need the oven on yet even though the mixture rests?
Turn it on now: get the oven warming to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Oven is heating. For the bowl, do the dates and sugar go in together?
They do. In a large bowl, combine the chopped dates with the 1 cup dark brown sugar.
They're in the bowl. The margarine is still firm; should I add it as is?
Add the 1/4 cup margarine to the bowl with the dates and brown sugar. The boiling water will help soften and melt it into the mixture.
I've got the kettle boiled. Is it the full cup of water going in?
Yes, pour in 1 cup boiling water, then stir everything together so the dates, brown sugar, margarine, and water are combined.
It's stirred and looks glossy with some softened date pieces. What happens before it goes into the pan?
Let the mixture stand for 15 minutes. That gives the dates time to soften further and lets the mixture settle before you continue.
I'm making Gelatin Fruit Salad and have a saucepan ready. Can you talk me through the ingredients and steps?
For this batch of Gelatin Fruit Salad, set out 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple with the juice left in.
The pineapple is crushed and still undrained. Should I open the soda now or wait?
You can open it now if you like, but add it later. Start by pouring the applesauce into the saucepan and heating it until it comes to a boil.
The applesauce is heating. Do I need to stir it while it warms?
Yes, stir it occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't stick. Once it reaches a boil, take the saucepan off the heat.
It just started bubbling, and I moved it off the burner. What goes in next?
Stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin. Keep stirring until the gelatin is fully dissolved and the mixture looks smooth.
I don't see any granules now. Is it okay to pour in the soda quickly?
Add the 12 ounce can of lemon-lime soda slowly, stirring gently as you pour so the fizz doesn't overflow.
The soda is mixed in without spilling. Does the pineapple go in with all the juice?
Yes, add the entire 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple undrained, then stir until the fruit is evenly distributed.
It's all combined. What kind of dish should I chill it in?
Pour it into a serving bowl or mold, cover it, and refrigerate until firm. Once set, it's ready to serve chilled.
I'm making Butterscotch Basketball Cookies and I've got a microwave and mixing bowl ready. Can you keep me on track?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup softened butter, making sure it's real butter with no substitutes.
While working on Butterscotch Basketball Cookies, the chips are measured, and the butter is soft enough to press with a finger. What sugars should I pull out?
You'll need 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Pack the brown sugar firmly into the measuring cup so it holds its shape when turned out.
Both sugars are measured. Should I melt the butterscotch before starting the mixer?
Yes. Put the 1 cup butterscotch chips in a microwave-safe bowl and melt them gently, stirring as needed so they smooth out without scorching.
They're melted and glossy. Do I use them right away?
Let the melted butterscotch cool for 10 minutes before adding it to the dough, so it doesn't warm the butter mixture too much.
While it cools, can I start with the butter and sugars?
Yes. In your mixing bowl, cream the 1 cup softened butter with the 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar until the mixture looks blended and creamy.
The butter and sugars look smooth. I see egg, milk, and vanilla in the directions—do those go in now?
They do. Add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so everything is evenly combined.
That's mixed. The butterscotch has cooled for the full 10 minutes—how do I bring it in?
Beat the melted butterscotch chips into the dough until the color and texture look even throughout.

For this batch, brush on a light glaze across the whole surface, but keep one corner bare.

Start with the binder and seasoning: 1 egg white and 1 tablespoon soy sauce.
Those are out. I have a mixing bowl ready—what else goes in before the turkey?
Add 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs and 1 tablespoon finely chopped onion to your setup.
Bread crumbs and onion are measured. Should I combine those with the egg white and soy sauce now?
Yes. In the bowl, combine the first seven ingredients so the mixture is evenly moistened before the meat goes in.
The mixture looks damp and crumbly. How do I add the turkey without making the burgers tough?

The patties are shaped. What pan setup should I use?

messages.content: I'm plating Adobo Chicken with Ginger for dinner tonight, and I might add a garnish or little finishing touch. What would look best?
Choose a single garnish and set it a little to one side of the chicken rather than scattering extras around the plate.
Great, that's the look I want for this meal. Before I turn on the stove, what should I have ready?
Set out a Dutch oven, then get the 1 (3 pound) whole chicken cut into 8 pieces. Keep the 1/2 cup soy sauce nearby too, since it goes in right away.
The chicken pieces are in a bowl, and the soy sauce is measured. What else belongs beside the pot?
Measure 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar, and have 1 bulb garlic peeled and crushed. You'll also need the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns ready for the same pot.
I've got the vinegar measured and the garlic crushed. Should I brown the chicken first?
No browning for this version. Put the chicken straight into the Dutch oven with the soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Everything is in the Dutch oven now. Should the lid be on while I bring it up?
Leave it uncovered while you bring it to a boil over medium heat so you can see when the liquid starts bubbling steadily.
It's beginning to bubble at the edges but not all over. Do I wait for a full boil?
Yes, let it reach a clear boil over medium heat. Once it does, turn the heat down until the liquid settles into a gentle simmer.
The boil is there now, and I've lowered the burner. How gentle should the simmer look?
Aim for small, steady bubbles around the chicken rather than a hard rolling boil. That keeps the pieces cooking in the adobo liquid without getting rough.
It's simmering gently. What's the timing from here, and do I need to move the pieces around?

Cover the Dutch oven and simmer for 30 minutes, basting the chicken occasionally with the sauce so the pieces stay coated. When you plate it, add that single off-center garnish and keep the rest clean.
I'm making Fresh Apple Cake and want to get organized before I start mixing. What should I pull out first?
Set out 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil and 2 cups white sugar. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready, since those get beaten with the eggs and vanilla.
Oil and sugar are measured. I see eggs and vanilla too—how much of each goes in?
You'll need 3 eggs, beaten, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract. Beat the eggs in a small bowl first so they blend evenly into the batter.
Before I crack the eggs, should the oven already be on?
Yes, turn the oven on to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C. That gives it time to come fully up to temperature while you prep the pan and batter.
Oven is heating. What pan am I using for this cake?
Use one 10 inch tube pan. Grease it well, getting into the center tube and around the bottom edge so the cake releases cleanly.
The pan is greased. I'm ready to start the wet mixture—what goes into the bowl together?
Add the vegetable oil, beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white sugar to the bowl, then beat them together until the mixture looks smooth and the sugar is well incorporated.
That mixture looks glossy and fairly even. What dry ingredients should I prep next?
Sift together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Sifting helps distribute the leavening and spices evenly before they meet the wet ingredients.
I've got the dry ingredients sifted. Anything I should watch for before combining everything later?
Keep the wet bowl, sifted dry mixture, and greased 10 inch tube pan nearby. Since the oven is already set to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), you're lined up for the next stage of the Fresh Apple Cake.
