The bacon is draining on paper towels, and there's grease left in the skillet. How much should stay in the pan?
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon grease in the skillet.
I'd like to make French Spring Soup. I have a large pot ready—can you guide me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup butter, 1 pound chopped leeks, 1 chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice for the later addition.
On French Spring Soup, the leeks are chopped, but they look a little gritty. Should I deal with that before the pot goes on?
Yes—rinse the chopped leeks well and drain them so grit doesn't end up in the soup. Once they're ready, put the large pot over medium heat and melt the butter.
The butter is melted in the pot. It's not browned, just bubbling lightly.
That's right for this soup. Add the chopped leeks and the chopped onion, then stir them through the butter so they soften evenly.
How soft should the leeks and onion get before I add anything else?
Cook them until tender, stirring now and then. They should look softened and relaxed rather than crisp or browned.
They're tender now and the pot smells sweet. Do I pour in all the water?
Yes, pour the 2 quarts water into the pot and stir along the bottom to loosen any buttery onion or leek bits.
Water is in. I've got the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice sitting beside the stove.
Mix the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice into the pot, making sure the rice is distributed instead of clumping in one spot.
Everything is mixed in. Should I keep it over medium heat for now?
Keep it cooking gently and stir occasionally so the rice doesn't settle heavily on the bottom. Once the vegetables and rice are tender, the French Spring Soup is ready to serve.
I'm making Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken and have the chicken breasts on a cutting board. Can you guide me through it?

In this Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken step, you'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, salt, pepper, 2 teaspoons olive oil, and 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions.
I have the chicken, oil, and the can of tomatoes. Should I season the chicken before the skillet gets hot?
Yes. Pat the chicken dry if it's wet, then season both sides of each chicken breast with salt and pepper.
Both sides are seasoned. What kind of pan should I use?
Use a large skillet so the chicken has room to brown. Add the olive oil to the skillet and set it over medium-high heat.
The oil is in and starting to shimmer a little. Do I add all the chicken at once?
Place the chicken breasts in the skillet in a single layer. If they fit without crowding, cook them all together; otherwise brown them in batches.
They fit in the pan. Am I just searing them right now?
Right. Cook the chicken, turning it once, so each side gets browned.
One side is browned, and I just flipped them. Should I open the tomato can yet?
You can open it and keep it nearby, but for the steps we're following here, let the second side brown before moving the chicken.
The chicken is browned on both sides. What should I do with it while I get ready for the tomatoes?
Remove the chicken from the pan and set it aside on a clean plate. Keep the skillet available for whatever comes next with the tomato mixture.

source_seed.recipe_title: Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken

messages.content: I'm getting ready for Best Macaroni Salad. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got a large pot and a mixing bowl ready.

Absolutely. Set the pot up for salted boiling water, and gather 1 (16 ounce) package macaroni, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup cucumber that's peeled, seeded, and chopped, and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion.
The macaroni and mayonnaise are on the counter. I still need to prep the cucumber.
Peel the cucumber, scoop out the seeds, and chop enough to make 1 cup. Keep the dried minced onion nearby too, since it gets stirred in after the pasta is dressed.
The water is boiling now. How should I cook the macaroni for the salad texture?
Add the macaroni to the salted boiling water and cook it until al dente, so it's tender but still has a little firmness. That helps it hold up once mixed with the dressing.
On Best Macaroni Salad, the pasta is cooked. Do I drain it hot or cool it down first?
Drain it, rinse it under cold water, and let it drain well. Cooling it stops the cooking and keeps the mayonnaise from getting thin or oily.
The macaroni is rinsed and not dripping much anymore. What goes into the bowl first?
Put the cooled pasta into the large bowl, add the 1/2 cup mayonnaise, and mix until the macaroni is evenly coated.
It's coated, but the bowl still has plenty of room. When do I add the cucumber and onion?
Stir in the chopped cucumber and the 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. If you're including the ham and cheese from the recipe directions, fold those in at this point as well.
Everything is in the bowl now. How much mixing does it need before serving?
Mix it well, just until the cucumber, onion, ham, and cheese are evenly distributed through the macaroni. Give the bowl a quick scrape around the sides, then it's ready to serve or chill.
I want to make Fried Chicken Tenders, and I'm setting up the breading station now. What should I put out first?
Put a shallow bowl on the counter for 1 cup all-purpose flour. Set another shallow bowl nearby for 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs, but don't mix that one yet.
The flour bowl is ready, and I measured the bread crumbs into a second shallow bowl. What seasoning goes into that?
Stir 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper into the bread crumbs so the coating is evenly seasoned.
The crumb mixture looks speckled and even. Do I need a third bowl for the wet part?
Yes. Use a small bowl for the eggs and water, and beat them together enough that the mixture is smooth for dipping.
I've got flour, egg mixture, and seasoned crumbs lined up. Which order should the chicken go through?
Work with one piece of chicken at a time: coat it in the flour first, dip it into the eggs and water, then cover it with the seasoned bread crumbs.
Should I shake anything off between bowls, or just move each tender straight through?
A light shake after the flour helps keep the coating from getting clumpy. After the egg dip, let the extra drip off briefly before pressing the chicken into the bread crumbs.
Some crumbs are sticking to my fingers while I coat the pieces. Any way to keep the station cleaner?
Use one hand for the flour and bread crumbs and the other hand for the egg bowl, if you can. Keep setting each coated piece aside as you finish it so the bowls stay easier to manage.
All the tenders are breaded and sitting aside. Is that the end of the prep from this recipe?
Yes. The prep is complete once each chicken piece has been coated in flour, the egg-and-water mixture, and the seasoned bread crumbs, then set aside.

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Keep the sauce thick and spread it in a thin layer on the bread or wrap.

messages.content: For this batch of Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, I'm using it inside a wrap instead of serving it as a bowl dip. Since it's a creamy filling, how thick should I make it so it doesn't leak?
For this wrap version, leave the mixture on the thicker side and smear only a light, even layer onto the wrap or bread so it holds together.
Perfect, that's exactly the approach I want just for this one. What should I pull from the fridge first?
Start with the cold creamy base: measure out 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream.
Those are measured. I have a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish out too—what pantry items or cans do I need next?
Add 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix to the counter, plus 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts. Drain the artichokes and chop them before mixing.
Artichokes are drained and chopped. Should I heat the oven before I combine everything?
Yes. get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready once the dip is assembled.
Oven is heating. What goes into the casserole dish together?
In the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish, combine the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat.
I'm folding it together now. Since I'll spread it in wraps, should I add anything to loosen it?
No need to loosen it for this use. Keep it cohesive and thick; just mix until the cheese, crab meat, and artichokes are evenly distributed.
The mixture looks even and thick. Do I cover the dish before it goes in?
For Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, bake it uncovered for 30 minutes at 350 degrees F.
After 30 minutes, how should I handle it for serving in the wraps?
Serve it immediately while warm. Spoon a small amount onto the bread or wrap and spread it thinly so the creamy crab-artichoke filling stays in place.
Before I get moving on Curried Winter Squash, what should I have ready? I have cooked squash ready but haven't measured anything yet.
Absolutely. Measure out 3 cups cooked, mashed winter squash and put it near a medium microwave-safe bowl.
The squash is mashed and measured. What seasonings and extras should I set out?
Set out 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder, 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
I've got the curry powder, butter, and maple syrup. Does everything go into the bowl together?
Yes. Add the mashed squash, curry powder, butter or margarine, and maple syrup to the medium bowl, then stir until the curry is evenly mixed through the squash.
The butter is still in small pieces. Is that okay before microwaving?
That's fine. It will melt as it heats; just spread the mixture out a bit in the bowl so it warms evenly.
What microwave setting and timing should I use?
Microwave it on high until heated through, about 5 minutes. If your microwave heats unevenly, pause once to stir, then continue heating.
It's hot now and smells like curry. The top looks a little plain—anything else before serving?
If you'd like, sprinkle coconut over the top. It's optional, so you can skip it if you want the squash as-is.
I'll leave the coconut off. How should I serve it?
Give the squash one final stir, spoon it into a serving dish or individual bowls, and serve it warm.
Chocolate Cream Dessert is on deck today. What should I do first? I'm starting with the crust ingredients on the counter.
Absolutely. For the crust, you'll need 1/4 cup cold margarine and 1 cup all-purpose flour. Keep the margarine cold so it cuts into the flour cleanly.
I have the flour measured, but the margarine is still in the fridge. Is that okay?
Yes, that's ideal. Take out 1/4 cup cold margarine and cut it into the 1 cup flour in a bowl until the mixture looks crumbly, with small bits of margarine worked through the flour.
The texture looks like coarse crumbs now. What dish should I use?
Use an 11-in baking dish, and coat it with nonstick cooking spray before adding the crumb mixture.
The dish is sprayed. Do I just scatter the crumbs in, or pack them down?
Press the crumb mixture evenly into the bottom of the prepared 11-in baking dish so it forms a crust layer.
It's pressed in and looks even. What temperature should the oven be?
Set the oven to 350 degrees F. Once it's ready, bake the crust for 15-18 minutes, or until it is lightly browned.
While that bakes, what are the remaining ingredients for the dessert?
You'll need 1 (8 ounce) package light cream cheese, softened, and 2 tablespoons heat-stable granular sugar substitute for the next part.
The crust is lightly browned after about 18 minutes. Should I take it out now?
Yes, take it out when it's lightly browned, then let the crust cool completely before adding anything else on top.
Country Fried Chicken is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got chicken ready, but I want to set up the coating station correctly.

Absolutely. Put a large resealable plastic bag on the counter for the dry coating, and set out a shallow bowl for the wet dip. For the dry mix, measure 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika.
The bag is open in a bowl so it won't spill. Do the flour and seasonings all go in there together?
Yes. Add the flour, garlic salt, pepper, and paprika to the resealable bag, then close it and give it a quick shake so the seasoning is evenly mixed through the flour.
Dry coating is mixed. What should I do with the shallow bowl?
Use the shallow bowl for the egg and milk. Beat them together until the mixture looks smooth enough to coat the chicken evenly.
The egg and milk are beaten. Should I coat all the chicken at once or work in batches?
Work a few pieces at a time. Add a few pieces of chicken to the flour bag, seal it well, and shake until the chicken is coated all over.
The first pieces have a dry coating now. Do they go straight into the egg mixture?
Yes. Take those coated pieces out of the bag, dip them into the beaten egg and milk mixture, and let the excess drip off for a moment.
They're dipped and a little wet on the outside. Do I put them back in the same flour bag?
Return them to the flour mixture in the bag, seal it again, and shake to coat them a second time. That double coating helps build the country-fried crust.
Got it. Should I repeat that exact order for the rest of the chicken?
Yes—keep going in small batches: flour bag, egg-and-milk dip, then back into the flour bag for another shake. Once each piece is double-coated, set it aside while you finish the remaining chicken.
I'm making Gingered Mango Salsa today. What's the best place to start? I've got a cutting board out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Start by prepping the produce: you'll need 1 cup chopped peeled mango and 1/4 cup chopped red onion.
The mango is peeled and chopped, and I measured the red onion. What else goes into the bowl?
Add 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro and measure out 1/4 cup lime juice. Those complete the salsa ingredients.
Should I mix the lime juice in with everything right away or hold it back?
Mix it in right away. Put the mango, red onion, cilantro, and lime juice together in a bowl and stir gently so the mango stays in pieces.
The salsa is combined. It looks pretty juicy from the lime—should I drain any off?
No need to drain it. The lime juice is part of the salsa and helps the flavors come together while it rests.
How long should I let it sit before serving?
Let it stand for 30 minutes before serving. Keep it covered while it rests so the onion, cilantro, lime, and mango can meld.
Should it rest on the counter or in the fridge?
Either works for a short rest, but if your kitchen is warm or you're not serving right away after the 30 minutes, put it in the fridge.
After it rests, do I need to do anything before bringing it to the table?
Give it one gentle stir, taste the balance of mango and lime, and serve it chilled or at room temperature with chips, tacos, fish, or grilled chicken.
I want to make Chai Butter Cookies. Can you guide me while I get the ingredients set up?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup chai tea mix, 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready for creaming everything.
The butter is on the counter, but it's still a little firm. Does that matter for the creaming step?
It will cream best if it's softened enough to press easily. Once it's workable, add the butter, the 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and the chai tea mix to the large bowl.
Okay, those are in the bowl. What texture am I aiming for when I mix them?
Cream them together until the mixture looks lighter in color and fluffy, rather than dense or streaky. Scrape the bowl if butter clings to the sides.
It looks fluffy now and the chai mix seems evenly blended. Do the eggs go in next?
Yes. Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each egg so the dough base stays smooth.
Both eggs are mixed in. The bowl looks a little loose but even.
That's right for this point. In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt before adding them to the creamed mixture.
I've combined the dry ingredients. Should I dump them in all at once or add gradually?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and blend until all of the dry ingredients have been absorbed. Stop once no dry patches remain so you don't overwork the dough.
The dough has come together. It's soft and there's no loose flour left.
Cover the dough and refrigerate it for 1 hour. That chill time will firm it up before you shape or bake the cookies.
Can you talk me through Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing? I've got a rotisserie chicken and want to assemble it without missing anything.
Absolutely. Pull the skin and bones from the rotisserie chicken, then shred the meat into bite-sized pieces until you have 4 cups. Put that in a medium bowl.
The chicken is shredded in the bowl. What vegetables should I cut for the salad part?
Dice 2 medium celery ribs into small pieces, then slice 2 medium green onions thinly. Add both to the bowl with the chicken.
Celery and green onions are in. Do the peanuts go in before the dressing or at the end?
Add them now: stir in 1/4 cup chopped honey-roasted peanuts with the chicken, celery, and green onions so the base is evenly mixed.
The salad base is mixed. I have a small bowl ready for the dressing—what goes into it?
Whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, sugar, red pepper, cilantro, and mint in the small bowl. Add 2 Tbs. water as you whisk so the dressing loosens up.
It smells good, but I want to make sure the texture is right. Should it be thick or pourable?
It should be pourable enough to coat the shredded chicken evenly. If the herbs are suspended and the sugar is dissolved, you're in good shape.
The dressing is smooth and pourable. Should I add all of it to the chicken mixture?
Yes, pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and toss gently until the chicken, celery, onions, and peanuts are coated throughout.
Everything is coated. How should I plate it for serving?
Serve the dressed chicken salad on a bed of Boston lettuce, then add any suggested accompaniments alongside. Give the bowl a final toss right before plating so the dressing is evenly distributed.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing

messages.content: Can you help me get started on Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake? I want to make sure I have the dry ingredients and pans ready before I begin.
Absolutely. For this part of the cake, set out 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate, chopped.
I found the flour and baking soda, but I'm checking the salt and chocolate now. Should the chocolate be chopped before I heat the oven?
Yes, go ahead and chop the unsweetened chocolate now so it's ready when you need it. Once that's done, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
The chocolate is chopped, and the oven is heating to 350. What pans should I pull out?
Use 2 round 9 inch pans. Grease them well, then dust them with flour so the cake layers release cleanly later.
I've got 2 9 inch pans on the counter. Do I need to flour the sides too, or just the bottoms?
Flour both the bottoms and the sides after greasing. Tap out any loose excess flour so it leaves only a light coating.
The pans are coated. I'm ready to mix the dry ingredients—what goes into the sifter?
Add the 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt to the sifter.
All three are measured. What texture am I looking for after sifting?
Sift them together until the flour, baking soda, and salt look evenly combined and free of obvious lumps.
The dry mixture looks even now. Should I keep it in the bowl or do something else with it?
Set the sifted dry mixture aside for now. Keep the chopped unsweetened chocolate nearby as well, since both are prepped for the next stage of the cake.
I'm making Arroz con Pollo II and have a large skillet ready. Can you guide me without rushing the prep?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 tablespoon olive oil and a 2 to 3 pound whole chicken that's already cut into pieces. Keep a plate or bowl nearby for the chicken after browning.
The chicken pieces are out, and I've got the oil measured. What vegetables should I prep before the skillet gets hot?
Chop 2 onions and crush 3 cloves garlic. The cooking instructions also call for green bell pepper, so have that ready too before you start sautéing.
Onions are chopped, garlic is crushed, and the pepper is ready. What heat should I use for the pan?
Put the large skillet over medium high heat and add the olive oil. Let the oil warm until it moves easily across the pan, but don't let it smoke.
The oil is shimmering a little. Should I add all the chicken pieces now?
Add the chicken pieces in a single layer if they fit comfortably. Sauté them until they're lightly browned, then remove them from the skillet and set them aside on that plate.
The chicken is browned and resting. There are browned bits in the skillet—do I leave them?
Yes, leave those browned bits for flavor. Add the onion, garlic, and green bell pepper to the skillet and sauté until the vegetables soften.
The vegetables are soft and smell good. What goes in before the chicken comes back?
Stir in the tomato sauce, saffron, salt, and bouillon, scraping the skillet gently as you mix. Then return the browned chicken pieces to the skillet.
The chicken is back in the sauce. How long should it cook before I deal with the rice?
For this batch of Arroz con Pollo II, let it cook for 10 minutes. After that, add the rice and reduce the heat to low so it can continue cooking gently.
I want to make Avocado Tzatziki—can you guide me while I get the ingredients ready?
Absolutely. Put a medium bowl on the counter and start with 1 large avocado, peeled and pitted, plus 2 cloves garlic, minced.
The avocado is prepped and the garlic is minced. What should I add beside those?
Juice 1 lemon, and keep 1/4 cup sour cream nearby if you want the creamier version. The recipe also has cucumber going into the bowl with the avocado mixture.
I have the lemon juice and sour cream ready. Do I put everything straight into the bowl?
Yes. In the medium bowl, combine the avocado, garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber.
They're in the bowl. I'm not using a blender—what texture am I aiming for with a fork?
Mash it with a fork until it's smooth. A few tiny bits are fine, but it should look like a cohesive dip rather than separate pieces.
While working on Avocado Tzatziki, it's mostly smooth now. What seasonings go in?
Season it with red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper, then mix well so the herbs and spices are spread through the avocado base.
The herbs are mixed in. Should I taste it now or wait?
You can taste a small spoonful now to check the salt, pepper, lemon, and heat, but it still needs to chill before serving.
How long does it need in the fridge, and should I cover the bowl?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the Avocado Tzatziki for 1 hour before serving.
I'm making Buffalo Chicken Wings I and want to time the frying and sauce so the wings stay crisp. Can you guide me?
Absolutely. Set out 24 chicken wings and get 2 quarts of vegetable oil ready for deep frying in a large skillet or deep fryer.
The wings are on a tray, and I have the oil. What should I have nearby for the sauce?
Keep 4 tablespoons butter, 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar, hot sauce, salt, and pepper within reach. The sauce comes together after the wings are cooked.
I'm using a deep fryer. How long should the wings cook once they go in?
Fry the chicken wings in the hot oil until they're done, about 10 minutes. Work carefully so the oil doesn't splash, and avoid crowding if your fryer is small.
They've been frying and look browned. What should I do when I lift them out?
Remove the chicken from the fryer or skillet and let it drain. If you used a skillet, remove and drain the oil too, then reserve the cooked chicken.
The wings are draining on a rack. Do I start the Buffalo sauce in the same skillet?
Yes. With the oil drained out, melt the butter in the skillet, then stir in the distilled white vinegar and hot sauce.
The butter, vinegar, and hot sauce are mixed. Should I season the sauce or the wings?
Season with salt and pepper to taste at this point, then use the sauce to coat the reserved fried wings.
They're coated and glossy. Anything to check before I serve them?
Make sure the wings are cooked through from the frying step, then serve them while they're hot and freshly coated.
Today I'm tackling Garlic Butter. Can you help me line up the prep? I've got a bowl and a spatula out, but I want to be sure I'm measuring everything right.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butter and let it be soft enough to mash easily with the spatula. You'll also need 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 tablespoon garlic salt.
The butter is softened, and I have the minced garlic. Should the Parmesan go in right away too?

Yes. Put the softened butter in the small bowl, add the 1 tablespoon minced garlic, and add the 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese. Mash and stir until the garlic and cheese are spread evenly through the butter.
It's mixing together, but the butter is sticking to the sides of the bowl. Is that okay?
That's fine. Scrape down the sides as you mix so there aren't plain streaks of butter left. You're aiming for a smooth, spreadable mixture with little bits of garlic and Parmesan throughout.
For Garlic Butter, okay, it looks pretty even now. When do I add the garlic salt?
Sprinkle in the 1 tablespoon garlic salt and stir it through the butter mixture. Since garlic salt is the main seasoning amount given, mix well so one bite isn't much saltier than another.
The recipe also mentions Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika. Do I add those now?

Yes, add the Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika now, then fold everything together until the color and seasonings look evenly distributed. The recipe doesn't give exact amounts for those, so season lightly and adjust to taste.
The texture is soft and spreadable. Should I whip it more or leave it like this?
If it's already spreadable and evenly seasoned, you can leave it as is. For a fluffier texture, stir or beat it a little longer, but don't melt the butter.
I'm planning to use it on bread tonight. Any serving or cleanup tips before I put it away?

Spread it directly onto bread, or spoon it into a small container and chill it if you want it firmer. Scrape the bowl well with the spatula, cover the garlic butter, and keep it refrigerated until you're ready to use it.
I want to make Chai Butter Cookies today. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Put out a large mixing bowl and gather 1 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup chai tea mix, 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and 2 eggs.
The butter, chai mix, sugar, and eggs are on the counter. Should the mixing bowl be large enough for the dough too?
Yes, use a large bowl since the dry ingredients will be blended into the creamed mixture later. Add the butter, 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and chai tea mix to it.
They're in the bowl. What texture am I looking for when I cream them?
Beat them together until the mixture looks lighter in color and feels fluffy rather than dense or streaky.
It's pale and fluffy now. I have the 2 eggs ready beside the mixer.
Add the eggs one at a time. After the first egg goes in, mix until it's well incorporated, then repeat with the second egg.
Both eggs are mixed in, and the batter looks smooth. What should I do with the dry ingredients?
Combine the flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl, then blend that dry mixture into the creamed mixture.
The dry mixture is going in. Should I stop as soon as I don't see flour anymore?
Keep blending just until all of the dry ingredients have been absorbed into the dough. Try not to keep mixing once it has come together.
The dough is together and the bowl is scraped down. Does it need to rest before I bake with it?
Yes. Cover the dough and refrigerate it for 1 hour so it can firm up before you continue.
I'm about to start Churros. Can you talk me through the prep? I'm setting up my counter now.
Absolutely. For the dough base, measure out 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also want a small saucepan for starting the mixture.
I've got the water, sugar, salt, and vegetable oil measured. Should the saucepan be on the stove already?
Yes—put the small saucepan over medium heat. Add the water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, then stir so the sugar and salt start dissolving.
The mixture is heating and looks clear now. Am I waiting for a simmer or a full boil?
Let it come to a boil. Once it reaches that point, take the saucepan off the heat right away.
It boiled and I moved it off the burner. The pan is still hot—what do I add next?
Stir in the flour while the mixture is off the heat. Keep mixing until it pulls together and forms a ball.
It's thickening, but there are a few dry streaks of flour around the edge. Should I keep going?
Yes, keep stirring and scraping the sides of the saucepan until those dry bits are incorporated and the dough gathers into one ball.
The dough is in a ball now. I'm getting the frying setup ready—what temperature should the oil be?
In this Churros step, heat the frying oil in a deep-fryer or deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
I'm using a deep skillet. Any quick check before I start frying?
Make sure the oil is steady at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), and keep the dough ready nearby so you can fry once the temperature is right.
I'm ready to cook Dads Best Burgers. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a bowl out and want to make sure I'm not missing anything before I start.

Absolutely. Set out 1 softened 3 ounce package of cream cheese, 1 egg, 1 medium onion finely chopped, and 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs. You'll also want your ground beef and sausage ready for mixing, plus a grill heated to medium-hot.
The cream cheese is soft, and the onion is chopped. Should I mix the egg with the cream cheese first or add everything together?

Use the bowl to combine the first seven ingredients together before adding the meats. Since the cream cheese is softened, stir it with the egg first to loosen it up, then work in the chopped onion and dry bread crumbs so the mixture is even.
It's looking thick and a little sticky. Is that okay for the base?
Yes, that texture is fine. It should be cohesive enough to help bind the burgers once the beef and sausage go in.
I'm ready to add the meat. Do I dump it in all at once?
Crumble the beef and sausage over the mixture instead of adding them in one solid piece. That makes it easier to mix well without overworking any one section.
The meat is mixed in, but I don't want the patties to fall apart on the grill. How many should I shape?
Shape the mixture into eight patties. Press them firmly enough to hold together, but don't pack them so tightly that they become dense.
I've got eight patties on a tray. Should the grill be covered while they cook?
Grill them uncovered over medium-hot heat. Cook each side for 4-6 minutes, turning once, until the burgers are no longer pink.
If one looks thicker than the others, should I leave it on a bit longer?
Yes. Use the 4-6 minutes per side as the guide, but a thicker patty may need the longer end of that range. The key doneness cue from the recipe is that it's no longer pink.
I have Garden Party Salad planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a mixing bowl out, but I want to make sure I start with the dressing correctly.
Absolutely. Set out a small bowl for the dressing and measure 1/4 cup vegetable oil and 1/4 cup orange marmalade into it.
The oil and marmalade are in the bowl. The marmalade is a little thick—what should I add before whisking?
Add 3 tablespoons cider vinegar and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise to the same small bowl. Those will help loosen the marmalade as you whisk.
Everything for the dressing is together. Should I whisk it until it's fully blended or leave it a bit streaky?
Whisk the first six ingredients until the dressing is smooth, with no visible streaks of mayonnaise or marmalade. Once it looks even, chill it.
It's smooth now and I'm putting it in the fridge. Do I assemble the salad right away?
Wait until just before serving to assemble it so the texture stays fresh. When you're close to serving, use a large bowl for the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley.
I'm about ready to serve, and the large bowl is out. Should the dressing go in all at once?
Yes, add the chilled dressing to the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley, then toss gently until everything is coated.
The salad is coated, but I don't want to crush the almonds. Any tip for the final toss?
Use broad, light turns from the bottom of the bowl, just enough to distribute the dressing without overmixing.
Looks good. Is there anything else I should do before bringing it to the table?
Give the bowl a quick check for any dry spots, spoon a little dressing from the bottom over them if needed, and serve the Garden Party Salad right away.
I'm setting up for Adriennes Tom Ka Gai; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got a large saucepan out and want to prep before turning on the stove.

Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 teaspoons peanut oil and slicing 2 cloves garlic thinly. You'll also want 2 tablespoons grated fresh ginger root and 1/4 cup chopped lemon grass ready to go, since the aromatics cook quickly.
Garlic is sliced, ginger is grated, and the lemon grass is chopped. Should the oil go in now?
Yes. Put the large saucepan over medium heat and warm the peanut oil in it. Give it a moment to shimmer before adding anything else.
The oil looks hot and moves easily around the pan. Do the garlic and ginger go in together?
They do. Stir in the garlic, ginger, lemon grass, red pepper, coriander, and cumin. Keep everything moving and cook until the mixture smells fragrant, about 2 minutes.
It smells bright and spicy now, and nothing is browning too much. What should I add next?
Add the chicken and onion to the saucepan. Stir as they cook, and keep going until the chicken turns white and the onion looks translucent, about 5 minutes.
The chicken has turned white, but there's a little moisture in the pan. Is that okay before adding the greens?
That's fine for this soup-style dish. As long as the chicken is white and the onion is translucent, you can stir in the bok choy.
Bok choy is in. How soft should I let it get?
Cook it just until it begins to wilt, which should take 5 to 10 minutes. Stir occasionally so the leaves soften evenly while the stems keep a little texture.
The leaves are wilted and the stems still have some bite. Should I take it off the heat now?
Yes, that sounds right. Take the saucepan off the heat once the bok choy has just wilted, then serve it while everything is hot and fragrant.
I'm making Crustless Spinach Quiche. Can you guide me through the setup before I turn anything on?
Absolutely. Set out 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 1 chopped onion, 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach that's thawed and well drained, and 5 beaten eggs.
The spinach is thawed, but it still feels wet. Should I drain it more before starting?
Yes, press out as much extra liquid as you can so the quiche doesn't turn watery. A clean towel or fine strainer works well for squeezing the thawed chopped spinach.
Got it. I also have a 9 inch pie pan ready. What should happen with the oven?
heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready by the time the filling is prepared.
Oven is heating. Do I need to prep the pan before the skillet work?
Yes. Lightly grease the 9 inch pie pan, including the sides, so the crustless quiche releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. I'm moving to the stove—what size pan and heat level should I use?
Use a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil and let it warm until it moves easily across the pan.
The oil looks shimmery. Should the onion go in by itself?
Yes, add the chopped onion now. Cook it while stirring occasionally, letting it soften rather than brown too hard.
How will I know the onions are soft enough before I deal with the spinach and eggs?
They should look more translucent and feel tender when stirred. Once the onions are soft, you're ready to continue with the drained spinach and the 5 beaten eggs.
I want to make Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts. Can you guide me through the prep without rushing?

Absolutely. Set out the syrup ingredients first: 1 cup white sugar, 1 cup water, 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons orange flower water. For the almond prep, you'll also need a pot, a strainer, baking sheets, and an oven that can hold a low temperature.
Before I continue with Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts, the sugar, water, lemon juice, and orange flower water are on the counter. Should I start with the syrup or the almonds?
Start with the almonds. Put a pot on the stove with 6 cups of water and bring it to a boil; that water is for loosening the skins.
The pot is heating now. Do I need to keep the baking sheets ready already?
Yes, keep the baking sheets nearby so you can spread the almonds out after peeling. Once the 6 cups of water are boiling, take the pot off the heat before adding the almonds.
It just reached a boil, and I've moved the pot off the burner. I'm adding the almonds now.
Good. Let the almonds sit in that hot water for about 5 minutes. They should soften just enough that the skins slip off more easily.
While they soak, should the oven be preheating?
Yes, set the oven to 200 degrees F, which is 95 degrees C. It's a low heat meant to dry and lightly toast them rather than roast them quickly.
The 5 minutes are up. The water looks a little cloudy—do I drain them right away?
Drain them now, then peel the almonds while they're still warm enough to handle comfortably. Pinch each almond gently so the skin slides off.
They're peeled. Some are damp from draining—how should I arrange them on the pans?

Spread the peeled almonds in a single layer on the baking sheets. Bake them at 200 degrees F, or 95 degrees C, until they're completely dry and toasted; check occasionally so they dry evenly before you use them for the tarts.
I want to make Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea. Can you help me set it up before I start heating anything?
Absolutely. Put a large pot on the stove and gather 1 pound fresh or frozen cranberries plus 3 quarts cold water. You'll simmer those together to make the cranberry base.
I've got a big pot, the cranberries, and the water. Are the juices added at the beginning too?
Hold the juices for later. You'll need 2 cups orange juice and 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice, but they get stirred in after the cranberry liquid has cooled and been strained.
Got it. The cranberries are still frozen—can they go straight into the pot with the cold water?
Yes, fresh or frozen cranberries are fine here. Add the 1 pound cranberries to the pot with the 3 quarts cold water, then set it over heat.
They're in the pot now. Should I cover it, or just bring it up uncovered?
Bring the pot to a boil; uncovered is fine as long as you keep an eye on it. Once it boils, cook just until the berries pop, about 5 minutes.
I'm hearing them pop, and the water is turning red. Do I keep boiling for stronger flavor?
No need to keep it going much longer. When the berries have popped after about 5 minutes, take the pot off the heat so the liquid doesn't get overly harsh.
The pot is off the burner. It's really hot—what should I do while it cools?
Let it stand at room temperature until cold, which will take several hours. Once it's cold, you'll strain out the cranberries.
It has cooled and I'm ready to strain. After that, what goes into the cranberry liquid?
Strain out the cranberries, then stir the 2 cups orange juice, 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice, lemon juice, and sugar into the liquid. Mix until the sugar is dissolved, then it's ready to serve or chill.
I'd like to make Chocolate Madeleines. Can you guide me while I get the pan and ingredients set up?
Absolutely. Set out one Madeleine pan, and for the dry mix measure 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour and 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder.
The pan is out, and I measured the flour and cocoa. What should I add to that bowl?
Add 1/2 teaspoon baking powder and 1 pinch salt to the same dry-ingredient area so everything is ready to sift together.
Got it. Should I heat the oven before I butter the pan?
Yes—set the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it has time to come up to temperature while you prep.
The oven is heating. For the Madeleine pan, do I need to coat every shell?
Butter one Madeleine pan, making sure each shell is coated so the cakes release cleanly after baking.
The pan is buttered. My flour and cocoa look a little clumpy—what texture am I aiming for?
Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together. You want the mixture to look even and fine, with the cocoa fully dispersed.
That dry mix looks smooth now. I also have the butter, vanilla, and sugar waiting—what do I do with them?
In this Chocolate Madeleines step, cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until the mixture looks blended and lighter in texture.
Once that is creamed, should I scrape the bowl before continuing?
Yes, scrape down the sides so the butter, vanilla, and sugar are evenly combined, and keep the sifted dry ingredients nearby for the next stage.
I'm getting ready for Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers. Can you help me sequence the steps? I've got the grill available and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the grill heating on high so it's ready when the patties are formed.
The grill is heating. What should I set out on the counter before I start mixing?

Set out 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, 1 small chopped onion, and 1 egg. You'll also need ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper, ground beef, and bacon for wrapping.
I have the cheeses, onion, and egg ready in a large bowl. Do the sauces go in before the beef?
Yes. Mix the Cheddar, Parmesan, chopped onion, egg, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper together in the large bowl before adding the meat.
It's mixed, but it looks pretty loose from the egg and sauces. Is that okay before I add the beef?
That's fine. Crumble the ground beef into the bowl, then mix it in by hand just until the seasonings and cheese are evenly worked through.
Should I pack the beef mixture tightly, or keep it a little loose?
Keep it gently mixed rather than overpacked. Once combined, divide the mixture into 6 patties.
I've shaped the 6 patties. How do I handle the bacon so it stays on?
Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty, keeping it snug against the edge so it holds its shape when it goes onto the hot grill.
They're wrapped and the grill is hot. Anything I should check before putting them on?
Make sure each patty is evenly shaped and the bacon is secure, then take them to the high-heat grill and cook them as your recipe directs from there.
I want to make Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Start by clearing a little counter space and pulling out the main wet-mixture ingredients: 1 cup shortening, 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 2 eggs.
The shortening and both sugars are on the counter. Should the brown sugar be firmly pressed into the measuring cup?
Yes, pack the brown sugar into the cup so it holds its shape when tipped out. Keep the white sugar loose and level, and have the eggs ready nearby.
Got it. I also have a mixing bowl and hand mixer out. Should I turn on the oven before mixing?
Yes. get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it is hot by the time the dough is ready.
Oven is heating. What should go into the bowl first?
Add the shortening, packed brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla to the bowl, then cream them together thoroughly until the mixture looks blended and smoother.
It is starting to look creamy, but I can still see a few streaks of shortening. Keep mixing?
Keep going a little longer, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed. You want the shortening, sugars, eggs, and vanilla evenly combined before adding anything dry.
The mixture looks even now. I have another bowl ready for the dry ingredients—what happens there?
In that separate bowl, mix together the dry ingredients, but leave out the candy pieces for now.
The dry bowl is mixed. Do I add it all at once to the creamed mixture?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix well, stopping to scrape the bowl so everything is incorporated evenly.

messages.content: I'm starting the Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms and want to keep the timing smooth. What should I get ready before I heat the pan?

For the herbs at the end, mince them finely, stir most of them into the risotto near the finish, and save a little for a fresh sprinkle. Put a wide pan on the stove, keep a sturdy spoon nearby, and set out the butter, Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, garlic if you're using it, rice, chicken stock, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
I have the vegetables on the board. Remind me of the amounts before I start chopping.

Use 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, 2 cups diced Broccoflower, 2 cups chopped assorted wild mushrooms, and 1/2 white onion, chopped. If garlic is going into your sauté, mince it now so it can cook with the vegetables.
The Broccoflower florets are uneven, and the mushrooms are a mix of sizes. How small should I cut them?

Dice the Broccoflower into small, even pieces so it cooks in the same window as the mushrooms. Chop the mushrooms into bite-size pieces, and keep the onion fairly fine so it softens into the risotto base.
I like that herb approach; it works better for this risotto than leaving big leaves scattered across the top. Should the butter go in over high heat or something gentler?

Go with medium heat. Melt the 1 tablespoon butter, then add the Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic, and sauté for 10 minutes, stirring often enough that the onion softens and the mushrooms cook down without scorching.
The mushrooms are releasing a lot of liquid after a few minutes. Should I drain it off?
Don't drain it. Let the moisture cook down in the pan, stirring as it reduces, and stop once the vegetables are softened and most of the liquid has evaporated rather than waiting for hard browning.
The 10 minutes are up, and the vegetables look tender. Do they stay in the pan for the rice?
Lift the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic out of the pan and set them aside in a bowl. Keep the same pan for the rice so the flavor left on the bottom works into the risotto.
The pan has those browned bits and a little butter left. How do I start the rice without washing that away?

Add the rice directly to that same pan and stir it briefly through the flavorful coating. Then begin adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time, stirring until each cup is well incorporated before you pour in the next.
I'm not sure when a cup of stock is absorbed enough. What should I look for?

Drag your spoon through the rice; if it leaves a brief trail and you don't see loose stock pooling around the edges, it's ready for the next 1 cup. Keep repeating that rhythm until the rice is tender.
The rice is tender now, and the pan looks creamy rather than soupy. How should I bring the vegetables and seasoning back in?

Fold the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, and onion back in gently. Stir in the nutmeg and the finely minced herbs, season with salt and pepper, loosen with a small splash of stock if it tightens up, and finish with the herbs you held back.
Let's work through Caramel Shortbread Squares today. Where should I begin? I've got a 9 inch square pan out.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 350 degrees F, which is 176 degrees C, so it can heat while you prep the shortbread base.
On Caramel Shortbread Squares, oven is heating. What ingredients should I measure before I start mixing?
Measure 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour for the crumbly mixture. The recipe also lists 1/2 cup butter, so keep that nearby too.
The 2/3 cup butter is soft, and I've measured the sugar and flour. What texture am I aiming for in the bowl?
In a medium bowl, mix the 2/3 cup softened butter with the 1/4 cup white sugar and the 1 1/4 cups flour until everything looks evenly crumbly rather than smooth or creamy.
It's crumbly and pretty even. Should I grease the pan or just press it in?
The recipe only says to press it into the 9 inch square baking pan, so spread the crumbs across the bottom and press them into an even, compact layer.
I'm pressing it in now, but the corners are a little thinner than the middle.
Use your fingertips or the bottom of a flat measuring cup to nudge some of the mixture into the corners, keeping the thickness as even as you can across the pan.
The base looks level. How long does it bake?
Bake it in the preheated oven for 20 minutes.
After the 20 minutes are up, what should I do with the pan?
Take the pan out carefully and set it on a heat-safe surface or rack. Let the shortbread base cool before cutting or adding anything else, since it will be fragile while hot.
I have Garden Party Salad planned for today. What should I set up first? I've got a small bowl and a large serving bowl out.
Absolutely. Start by setting up the dressing ingredients: 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/4 cup orange marmalade, 3 tablespoons cider vinegar, and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise.
I measured the oil and marmalade. Should the marmalade be warmed or just spooned in?
Just spoon it in as is. If it's very stiff, stir it briefly to loosen it, but the whisking will help smooth it into the dressing.
The vinegar and mayonnaise are measured too. Do they all go into the small bowl together?

Yes, add the vegetable oil, orange marmalade, cider vinegar, and mayonnaise to the small bowl. The recipe says to whisk the first six ingredients until smooth, then chill; with the ingredients you have listed, whisk these dressing ingredients until the mixture looks smooth and blended.
It's mostly smooth but a little glossy around the edges. Is that okay before chilling?
That's fine. Give it another short whisk to pull in any oil at the edges, then cover the bowl and chill the dressing until you're ready to serve.
While the dressing chills, what should I put in the large bowl?
Just before serving, use the large bowl for the salad mixture: combine the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley there.
Should I toss those together before adding the dressing?
Yes, lightly toss the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley first so they're evenly distributed. Then pour the chilled dressing over the top.
The dressing is on. How thoroughly should I mix it, and can I serve right away?
Toss until everything is lightly coated without crushing the ingredients. Since the recipe has you add the dressing just before serving, bring it to the table right away once it's evenly dressed.
I'm making Cinnamon Chocolate Cake 2 and have a mixing bowl and saucepan out. Can you help me get started?
Absolutely. Measure the dry ingredients into the mixing bowl: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cinnamon, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
The flour and sugar are in, but I want to make sure the cinnamon and salt go in with them, right?
Yes, add the cinnamon and salt to that same bowl, then stir the 4 dry ingredients together so they're evenly combined.
Dry bowl is mixed. What should I put in the saucepan?
In the saucepan, combine the water, oil, butter, and cocoa. The recipe doesn't list amounts for those here, so use the quantities from your source if you have them.
While working on Cinnamon Chocolate Cake 2, they're in the pan. What heat should I use, and what am I looking for?
Set the saucepan over medium heat and bring that mixture to a boil, stirring as needed so the cocoa and butter blend smoothly.
It's just starting to bubble around the edges. Should I wait for a full boil?
Yes, let it reach a clear boil, then take it off the heat so you can pour it over the dry mixture.
Okay, it boiled and I poured it into the flour mixture. The batter looks streaky.
Mix it well until the dry ingredients are fully moistened and the chocolate mixture looks evenly worked through.
That's smoothed out. What goes in before I'm done mixing?
Add the eggs, buttermilk, vanilla, and baking soda, then mix well again until the batter is combined and ready for the next baking step.

messages.content: I'm making Empanadas and want to get the dough started today. What should I put on the counter first?

Use the oven or broiler with a sheet pan for the filled empanadas, then let them sit uncovered briefly before serving. For today's dough, set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1 (3 ounce) package cream cheese so they're easy to blend.
Butter and cream cheese are out. Do I need the dry ingredient now too?
Yes. Have 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour ready, but don't add it until the butter and cream cheese are smoothly creamed together.
Got it. I also see fruit preserves in the recipe—should those be out yet?
Keep 1 cup fruit preserves nearby for the filling later, but focus on the dough first. Start by creaming the softened butter and cream cheese until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
I like that sheet-pan-and-uncovered-rest move here; that works better for this dish. The butter and cream cheese are looking smooth now.
Great. Beat in the sifted flour next, a little at a time if that's easier, until the dough comes together without dry streaks.
The flour is mixed in, and the dough feels soft. Should I knead it?
No kneading is needed. Shape it gently into a smooth ball, just enough to bring the dough together without overworking it.
It's in a ball. What should I wrap it with?
Wrap the dough well in foil or cling wrap so it doesn't dry out in the refrigerator.
Wrapped and ready. How long does it need to chill?
Refrigerate it overnight. If you're not baking right away, the dough can stay chilled for up to a week.
Before I continue with Empanadas, when I'm ready to bake, do I use it straight from the fridge?
Take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it. That gives it time to soften enough to roll and fill with the fruit preserves.

Yes, add 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder right into the broth and rice, then give it a gentle stir so the rice is evenly distributed.

It does not need to be perfect, but keep the rice in an even layer so it cooks evenly under the broth. Cover the dish tightly once everything is mixed.

Then keep them in the early mixture before the cover goes on. They will soften with the rice instead of sitting loose on top.

Put it in the oven at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, and bake it covered for 10 minutes.

Have the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, and onions ready. When the dish comes out after 10 minutes, you'll add the broccoli, the Parmesan, and half of the onions.
The timer just went off and I can see some broth still around the rice. Do I stir the broccoli in or layer it?
Uncover it carefully, then add the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, and half of the onions over the rice mixture. Spread them gently without pressing the rice down.
For the onions, I only put in half at this point, right?
Right, use half of the onions here with the broccoli and Parmesan. Keep the mixture loose so the fish can sit neatly on top.
The fish fillets are on a plate and patted dry. How should I arrange and season them?
Lay the fish fillets over the rice and broccoli mixture in a single layer, then sprinkle them with paprika. Continue baking until the fish is cooked through and the rice is tender.

For the cardamom-ginger accent, use only a tiny pinch of cardamom or one quick swirl with a thin ginger slice so it stays behind the fruit. Put a mixing glass, a jigger, a spoon, fresh ice, and your serving glass within reach, then line up the dark rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and pina colada mix.

Yes. Pour in 3 1/2 fluid ounces of fruit punch, then add 1/2 fluid ounce of pina colada mix.

Stir until the rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and pina colada mix look fully blended and smooth. You do not need to shake it.
It looks even, and the pina colada mix isn't streaky anymore. Should I add the ice to the serving glass now?
Yes, fill the serving glass with fresh ice, then pour the blended Bahama Mama II over the ice.
Do I need to strain it as I pour, especially if I used the ginger slice for a quick swirl?
If you used a ginger slice, leave the slice behind in the mixing glass. Otherwise, just pour the drink over the ice; there is nothing else that needs straining.
The drink is over ice. Any final adjustment before I hand it off?
Give it one gentle stir in the serving glass so the cold settles through evenly. Serve it right away while the fruit punch is bright and the warm spice stays subtle.

messages.content: I'm making Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches and have the bread out. Can you stay with me from chopping through the broiler?

With the raw add-ins, chop the onion, celery, and green bell pepper finely so the topping stays crunchy but spreads evenly. Set out a medium bowl and a baking sheet or broiling pan, then keep the bread slices nearby.
Got it. I've got the bowl and pan out, and the vegetables are on the board. What exact amounts should I cut?
Use 1 small onion, finely chopped; 1 medium tomato, diced; 1 stalk celery, chopped; and 1 green bell pepper, finely chopped. Keep the tomato in neat dice so it doesn't turn watery in the bowl.
The onion and pepper are very small, the celery is chopped, and the tomato is diced. Should I heat anything while I finish?
Yes, turn on your oven's broiler now so it can preheat while you mix and top the bread.
I like the small raw pieces here; that works better for this dish because every bite gets a bit of crunch. What should I add to the bowl with them?
Put the onion, tomato, celery, and bell pepper into the medium bowl, then add the cheese, chili powder, and salt. Stir gently until the cheese and seasoning are distributed through the vegetables.
The mixture is combined, but it still looks loose and chunky. Is that right, or should I press it together?
Leave it loose. You want the cheese to help the topping cling, but the chopped vegetables should still keep their texture.
The bread slices are ready, but I'm not sure whether to crowd them on the pan.
Lay the bread slices flat on the baking sheet or broiling pan with a little space around each piece. That gives the broiler room to crisp the edges.
They're spaced out now. How do I divide the topping so they cook evenly?
Spoon 1/4 of the mixture onto each slice of bread. Spread each portion all the way to the edges so the corners don't dry out before the topping heats.
A little topping wants to mound in the middle. Should I flatten it?
Yes, nudge it into an even layer rather than pressing hard. Aim for the same thickness across each slice so the vegetables heat at the same pace.
They're topped edge to edge and the broiler is hot. Anything else before I slide the pan in?
Check that no topping is spilling off the bread, then place the pan under the preheated broiler. Watch closely and serve the sandwiches when the topping is hot and the bread looks crisp.
Cookie Jar Gingersnaps is on deck today. What should I do first?
Absolutely. Put out a large mixing bowl and measure the main wet ingredients: 3/4 cup shortening, 1 cup sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses.
The shortening and sugar are measured. Should they go into the bowl before the egg?
Yes. Add the shortening and sugar to the large mixing bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks well blended and a little lighter.
It's coming together, but there are still a few streaks of shortening. Is that okay?
Keep mixing a bit longer so the sugar is worked evenly through the shortening. It does not need to be fluffy like cake batter, just smoothly creamed.
Okay, the mixture looks smoother. I have the egg cracked and the molasses ready.
Beat the egg into the creamed mixture, then add the molasses and mix until the dough base looks evenly dark and glossy.
The molasses is mixed in. What should I combine separately?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt. Stir those dry ingredients together so the spices and leavening are evenly distributed.
Dry bowl is mixed. Do I dump it all in at once?
Add the dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture, mixing between additions. Stop once the dough is evenly combined and no dry patches remain.
The dough is ready. How do I shape the cookies for the jar?
Scoop teaspoonfuls of dough and roll each one into a ball. Line them up as you go so they're ready for the next baking step.
I'm ready to cook Avocado Tzatziki. What should be ready before I begin? I've got a bowl and fork out, but I want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the main ingredients ready: 1 large avocado, peeled and pitted, and 2 cloves garlic, minced. Since this is mashed rather than blended, a medium bowl and fork are perfect.
The avocado is peeled and the garlic is minced. What should I set up next before I start mixing?
Juice 1 lemon, and if you're using it, measure out 1/4 cup sour cream. You'll also want the cucumber ready for the bowl, since it gets combined with the avocado mixture.
I have the lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber ready. Do I add everything at once?
Yes. Put the avocado, minced garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber into the medium bowl together.
They're all in the bowl. Should the avocado be chunky or totally smooth?
Mash it with the fork until the mixture is smooth. Press the avocado against the side of the bowl as you go so the garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber are worked through evenly.
It's mostly smooth now, with a little texture from the cucumber. What seasonings go in?
Add red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper, then mix well so the herbs and seasoning are spread throughout the tzatziki.
I mixed that in. Should I taste it now or wait until it chills?
You can taste it now to check the salt, pepper, lemon, and red pepper flakes, but the flavors will come together more after chilling.
Good to know. How long does it need in the fridge before I serve it?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the Avocado Tzatziki for 1 hour before serving. After that, give it a quick stir and serve it chilled.

Cut the fresh cilantro very fine, stir most of it in near the end, and save a small bit to scatter over the salsa before serving. Set out peeled mango, red onion, fresh cilantro, and lime juice so everything is ready to measure.
The mango is peeled and sitting on the board. What amount am I aiming for once it's chopped?
Chop the peeled mango into small pieces until you have 1 cup. Try to keep the pieces fairly even so the salsa scoops nicely.
I've got the mango measured. The onion is next, right—how finely should I cut it?
Yes, chop the red onion small and measure 1/4 cup. Smaller pieces will blend in with the mango instead of dominating each bite.
I like the way you're handling the cilantro here—that's exactly what I wanted for this salsa. What are the cilantro and lime measurements?
Measure 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro and 1/4 cup lime juice. Keep back that little sprinkle of cilantro for the top, then use the rest in the salsa.
The cilantro is minced and the lime juice is measured. Should anything go into the bowl in a certain order?
Add the 1 cup chopped mango and 1/4 cup chopped red onion to the bowl first, then pour in the 1/4 cup lime juice.
Okay, the mango, onion, and lime are in. When should I add the cilantro?
Add most of the 1/4 cup minced cilantro now, leaving the reserved bit aside for serving. That keeps the salsa mixed through but still fresh-looking on top.
It smells bright already. Do I need to stir it firmly to combine everything?
Fold it gently until the mango, red onion, lime juice, and cilantro are evenly combined. Avoid pressing too hard so the mango stays intact.
The texture looks good, but the lime is pooling a little at the bottom. Is that okay?
That's fine. Let the salsa stand for 30 minutes before serving so the lime juice can mingle with the mango, onion, and cilantro.
After the 30 minutes are up, what should I do right before it goes to the table?
Give it one gentle stir, spoon it into the serving bowl, and scatter the reserved cilantro over the top just before serving.

Set out 2 beef top sirloin steaks, each 8 ounces, along with 3 tablespoons crushed black peppercorns, 1 tablespoon lemon pepper, 1 teaspoon salt, butter, garlic, wine, and a large skillet.
The peppercorns are already crushed, but they look chunky. Should I break them down more or leave them like that?
Chunky is fine here; it gives the steak a bold crust. If any pieces are huge, tap them once or twice, but keep most of the peppercorns coarse enough to press into the surface.
Okay, steaks are unwrapped. Do I season them wet from the package or dry them first?
Pat both steaks dry first so the seasoning sticks. Then press the crushed black peppercorns firmly into both sides of each steak.
I like that move with the lower cilantro pieces; it uses those tender bits instead of wasting them, and they tuck into the pan really nicely.
That will work well with the garlic and wine. Keep the chopped pieces close by, and sprinkle the peppercorn-coated steaks with the lemon pepper and salt on both sides.
Some lemon pepper landed on the cutting board around the steaks. Should I scrape that back on, or toss the loose bits?
If it touched raw steak juices, do not return it to the spice container or save it. You can press a little onto the steaks right away, then clear and wipe the board before the skillet goes on.
The steaks are seasoned and the board is cleared. How hot should the pan be before butter goes in?
Use a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the butter and let it melt until it foams lightly at the edges without browning hard.
The butter is foaming now. Do the garlic and chopped herb bits go in together?
Yes, stir in the garlic with the finely chopped lower cilantro pieces or parsley. Keep everything moving so the garlic turns fragrant and the herb bits soften into the butter instead of scorching.
It smells good, but the garlic is cooking fast. Is this when I add the wine?
Add the wine now and stir it into the garlic butter. Let it cook for 1 minute so the sharp edge of the wine softens.
After that minute, what should I be looking for before I spoon anything over the steaks?

Look for the pan mixture to smell savory and peppery, with the wine no longer smelling raw. Spoon that garlic-wine butter, including the softened chopped lower pieces, over the peppercorn-coated steaks and serve when the steak texture is where you want it.

messages.content: I'm making Fig Bars II and want to get organized before I crack the eggs. Can you walk me through the setup?

Keep these fig bars in the oven for the cooking, then let the baked bars rest uncovered briefly before serving. To start, preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, or 165 degrees C, and pull out a 9x13 inch baking pan.
The pan is out. What should I gather for the batter so I'm not searching mid-mix?

Set out 1 cup white sugar, 3 eggs, 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking powder. You'll also need flour for dusting the pan, plus the recipe's dry seasonings and vanilla when you combine everything.
Got it. Before the bowl work, should I prep the pan now or wait?
Prep it now while the oven heats. Grease and flour the 9x13 inch baking pan so the bars release more cleanly after baking.
I like that oven-and-rest plan for this; it works better for bakes like these.
Great, we'll keep it simple and steady. With the pan ready, move to the large bowl and beat the 3 eggs with the 1 cup white sugar.
I'm beating them now. How will I know when the eggs and sugar are ready?
Stop when the mixture looks thick and pale, not thin or glossy. It should have a little body and look lighter than when you started.
It's pale and a bit fluffy. Do I sift the flour by itself?
Sift the 7/8 cup all-purpose flour with the 1 teaspoon baking powder, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice. That keeps the leavening and spices evenly spread before they go into the egg mixture.
The dry mix is sifted. Do I fold it in, or beat it like the eggs?
Blend the sifted dry mixture into the egg-sugar mixture gently enough that you don't knock out all the air. Add the vanilla at this stage as the recipe directs.
The batter looks combined, with no dry streaks. Anything I should check before it goes in the pan?
Make sure there are no pockets of flour at the bottom of the bowl, then spread the batter evenly in the greased and floured 9x13 inch pan. Keep the layer level so it bakes evenly.
Once it bakes, should I cut it right away or leave it alone for a bit?
Let the baked bars sit uncovered briefly before cutting and serving. That short rest helps them settle, so you can slice without fussing over them while they're still too delicate.
I'm making Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version tonight. Can you coach me through the prep without rushing?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 6 center cut pork chops, and trim away any visible fat if that hasn't already been done.
The chops are trimmed. What seasonings should be on the counter?
You'll need 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/2 teaspoon seasoning salt. Keep them nearby so you can season the pork after it's dried.
Got those out. Should I turn on the oven before handling the meat?
For this batch of Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version, yes, get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready by the time the chops are coated.
Oven is heating. I'm at the sink with the pork chops—what's the cleanest way to prep them?
Rinse the pork chops, then pat them dry really well with paper towels. Once dry, season them with the garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste.
They're seasoned and the counter is wiped down. What bowl setup do I need for coating?
Use a small bowl for the beaten egg and egg substitute mixture. The ingredient list notes 1 egg, beaten with, so keep that beaten mixture ready for dipping.
I also have flour and bread crumbs out. What order should the coating go in?
Coat each chop in this order: dredge it lightly in flour, dip it into the egg mixture, then coat it liberally with bread crumbs.
How heavy should the bread crumb layer look before I put them in the baking dish?
Aim for an even, generous crumb coating all over each pork chop, while keeping the flour layer light underneath. Once they're coated, they're ready to arrange for baking in the preheated oven.
