messages.content: For tonight, I'm treating Baked Salmon with Herbs more like an uncooked topping or salsa-style garnish, and I want the lower cilantro or parsley pieces toned down. What should I do with those bits?
Use just the tenderest lower herb pieces, mince them very small, and hold the brighter upper green pieces aside so they stay distinct.
Perfect, that's just for this batch. I've got my board clear—what should I pull out first?
Start with the crumb mixture ingredients: 2 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs and 4 minced garlic cloves.
The bread crumbs are measured and the garlic is minced. What else belongs with that mixture?
Add 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese and 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes to your counter setup.
I have those ready. Should I prep the pan before mixing so I don't have messy hands?
Yes. Line a 15-in baking pan with foil, then coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray.
Pan is lined and sprayed. For the bowl, am I combining everything dry first?
Combine the bread crumbs, garlic, Parmesan cheese, parsley, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
The dry mix smells good. I see butter in the directions—how do I work it in without clumps?
Add the butter and toss the mixture until the crumbs are evenly coated.
The crumbs look evenly coated now. Where does the salmon go?
Place the salmon on the prepared foil-lined pan.
Got it on the pan. Should I keep the separated upper herb pieces away from the crumb bowl for serving?
Yes, keep those upper green pieces separate so you can add them cleanly at the end without mixing them into the buttered crumbs.
I want to make Cabin Hash for dinner. Can you talk me through getting it started?
Absolutely. Have 12 medium potatoes peeled, cooked, and cubed, plus 3 cups of cubed fully cooked ham ready near the stove.
The potatoes are already cooked and cubed, and the ham is diced. What else should I set by the skillet?
Set out 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup butter or margarine. You'll also want a large skillet and a spatula for frequent stirring.
Should the butter go in before everything else, or do I add it with the potatoes?
Melt the butter or margarine in the large skillet, then add the potatoes, ham, and chopped onion together so they can cook and brown evenly.
How hot should I keep the skillet while the potatoes brown?
Use a steady medium heat. Stir often so the onion softens and the ham warms while the potato cubes get lightly browned instead of sticking.
The potatoes are starting to color, but a few pieces are sticking to the bottom.
Scrape gently as you stir and keep the pieces moving. Once the potatoes are lightly browned, you're ready for the next addition.
They look lightly browned now. I noticed the recipe mentions broccoli—when does that go in?
Add the broccoli now and stir it through the hash. Keep it in the skillet just until the broccoli is heated through.
Everything is hot. What should I do before serving it?
Season the Cabin Hash with salt and pepper, taste to adjust, and serve it warm with sour cream on the side if you'd like.
I'm making Beet and Pear Puree and have the beets out. Can you walk me through what I should prep before anything goes on the stove?
For this batch of Beet and Pear Puree, you'll need 8 medium beets, 1 pound unsalted butter, 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions, and 4 Bosc pears that are peeled, cored, and minced.
The pears still need peeling and mincing. Should I start the oven while I do that?
Yes, go ahead and set the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). While it heats, you can finish peeling, coring, and mincing the Bosc pears.
The oven is heating, and I have a roasting pan ready. Do the beets need trimming or just washing?
Wash the beets well, then place them in the roasting pan. The recipe's next move is simply getting the cleaned beets into the pan for roasting.
They're in the pan now. How long should I roast them, and what texture am I checking for?
Bake them for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until they're tender. You're looking for a knife or skewer to slide in without much resistance.
If they finish closer to the 45-minute mark, do I handle them right away?
Once they're tender, set them aside to cool. Give them enough time that they're safe to handle before you continue.
While the beets cool, I want to get the stovetop part ready. What pan should I use for the butter?
Use a large skillet over medium heat, then melt the 1 pound unsalted butter in it.
The butter is starting to melt. Should the minced Vidalia onions and pears be waiting nearby?
Yes, keep the 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions and the 4 peeled, cored, minced Bosc pears close by so they're ready for the next stage after the butter is melted.
I want to make Best Ever Tuna Salad for lunch—can you talk me through the prep without rushing?
Absolutely. Set out 2 eggs, a saucepan, and enough cold water to cover the eggs. You'll also need 1 (12 ounce) can white tuna for the salad.
The eggs and tuna are out. Before I start heating anything, what else should be on the counter?
Add 1 (6 ounce) can shredded crabmeat and 1/2 cup mayonnaise to your setup. Have a bowl ready for mixing once the eggs are cooked and chopped.
I've got the crabmeat, mayo, and a mixing bowl. How should the eggs go into the pan?
Place the eggs in the saucepan in a single layer, then cover them with cold water so they're fully submerged.
They're covered with cold water now. Should I leave the pan uncovered while it heats?
Yes, bring the water to a boil uncovered. As soon as it reaches a boil, remove the saucepan from the heat right away.
The water just started boiling, and I moved the pan off the burner. What happens next?
Here, cover the saucepan and let the eggs stand in the hot water for 10 to 12 minutes.
While the eggs sit, should I drain the tuna and crabmeat?
Yes, drain the white tuna and shredded crabmeat well so the salad doesn't turn watery. You can place them in the mixing bowl while you wait.
The timer is done. What's the best way to handle the eggs now?

Remove the eggs from the hot water, cool them, peel them, and chop them finely. Then combine the chopped eggs with the tuna, shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise until everything is evenly mixed.
I'm making Cinnamon Crackle Cookies and have a mixing bowl out. Can you walk me through the ingredients before I start?
For this batch of Cinnamon Crackle Cookies, set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're ready to cream together.
Both fats are in the bowl. Which sugars should I measure?
Measure 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Add them to the bowl with the butter and shortening.
The sugars are measured in. What texture am I aiming for when I mix this?
Cream the butter, shortening, and sugars until the mixture looks blended and a bit fluffy, with no big streaks of butter or shortening left.
That looks smooth and lighter now. Do the egg and extracts go in together?
Yes, add the egg and extracts, then mix well so they're fully incorporated into the creamed mixture.
The wet mixture is combined. I've got the dry ingredients nearby—how should I add them?
Combine the next eight ingredients separately, then add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture. Mix as you go so the dough comes together evenly.
The dough is mixed. Should I prep the baking sheets before shaping?
Yes, use ungreased baking sheets. Keep a little sugar nearby too, since the dough balls need to be rolled in sugar before they go on the sheets.
How big should I make each cookie?
Shape the dough into 1-in balls, roll each one in sugar, and arrange them on the ungreased baking sheets.
I want to make Asian Turkey Burgers tonight. Can you guide me from the ingredient check through cooking them?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 egg white and 1 tablespoon soy sauce, since those will go into the bowl for the burger mixture.
Egg white and soy sauce are ready. I'm checking the pantry—what dry ingredient should I measure?
Measure 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs. You'll also need 1 tablespoon finely chopped onion ready to mix in.
The bread crumbs are measured, and I chopped the onion pretty fine. Should I use a mixing bowl now?
Yes. Put the egg white, soy sauce, dry bread crumbs, and finely chopped onion into a bowl, combining the first seven ingredients called for in the recipe.
They're in the bowl. How much should I stir before adding the turkey?
Stir just enough to evenly moisten the crumbs and distribute the onion through the egg white and soy sauce mixture.
The mixture looks evenly damp. Do I fold in the turkey or really work it in?
Crumble the turkey over the mixture, then mix just until combined. Try not to overwork it so the patties stay tender.
The turkey is mixed in and still looks fairly loose. How should I portion the burgers?
Shape the mixture into four patties. Press them together gently so they hold, keeping the thickness as even as you can for consistent cooking.
I've got four patties formed. What's the best way to cook them in the skillet?
Coat a nonstick skillet with nonstick cooking spray, then cook the patties until they're no longer pink in the center. Turn them as needed so both sides brown and the burgers cook through.
I want to make Chocolate Covered Pretzels. Can you talk me through getting the ingredients and setup ready?

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler, a spoon or spatula for constant stirring, and wax paper for cooling the coated pretzels.
I've got the pretzels and chocolate chips. Is the cream just going in with the chocolate?
Yes. Put the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream together in the top of the double boiler. Keep the heat low so the chocolate melts gently instead of seizing or scorching.
The water underneath is barely simmering. Should I stir the whole time?
Keep stirring constantly while the chocolate and cream melt. You're looking for a smooth, glossy mixture that stays very warm and fluid enough to coat the pretzels quickly.
It's melted and looks shiny. Should I dump in a bunch of pretzels or do them separately?
Dip the pretzels 1 at a time. Work quickly while the chocolate mixture is still very warm, coating each pretzel before placing it down.
Some extra chocolate is dripping off each one. Is that okay?
That's fine. Let the excess drip back into the double boiler for a moment, then lay each coated pretzel on wax paper so it can set cleanly.
My wax paper is ready on the counter. Do they need to go in the fridge?
The recipe just has you place the pretzels on wax paper to set and cool. Leave them there until the chocolate firms up and they lift off easily.
Once they're cool, what's the best way to serve or store them?
After they're set and cool, transfer the chocolate covered pretzels to a serving plate or an airtight container. Keep the layers separated with wax paper if you stack them so the coating stays neat.
I want to make Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds. Can you stay with me while I prep the potatoes?
Absolutely. Peel and cube 6 Yukon Gold potatoes and 2 sweet potatoes, then keep them nearby for the pot.
The potatoes are cubed. Should I grab the dairy before I start boiling anything?
Yes. Set out 2 tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup heavy cream so they're ready when you need them.
I've got the butter and cream out. What size pot should I use for the cubed potatoes?
Use a large pot, since both the Yukon Gold potatoes and sweet potatoes need room to be covered with water.
They're in the pot now. How much water should go in?
Add enough water to cover the potatoes and sweet potatoes fully, with a little space at the top so it won't slosh when it heats.
Water is covering them. Do I put it straight on high heat?
Put the pot on the stove and bring the water to a boil. Keep an eye on it as the cubes start moving around.
It's boiling now, and the pot is pretty steamy. What do I do at this point?
Remove the pot from the heat, then drain the potatoes and sweet potatoes carefully.
They're drained. I'm clearing the stovetop—what needs to happen before the oven part?
For Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds, preheat the oven broiler so it's ready for the next stage of the dish.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this batch, add just the smallest pinch of ginger; leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: Tonight I'm turning Candy Bar Squares into a cold fruit-style dessert, and I only want this batch to lean on one warm spice if any. Between cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, and nutmeg, what should I do?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Candy Bar Squares as a chilled fruit dessert with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. How should I use the warm spices?

messages.content: Tonight I'm turning Candy Bar Squares into a cold fruit-style dessert, and I only want this batch to lean on one warm spice if any. Between cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, and nutmeg, what should I do?
For this batch, add just the smallest pinch of ginger; leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
Great, that's the one-off version I wanted. Before I get mixing, what should I pull from the fridge and pantry?
Gather 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup white sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 2 eggs. Put a mixing bowl and beaters nearby too.
The butter is soft and the sugars are measured. Should I heat the oven even though I'm serving it chilled later?
Yes. Set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so the base bakes properly before it cools for serving.
Oven is warming. Should the butter and both sugars go in together, and what texture am I looking for?
Beat the butter with the white sugar and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks pale, lighter, and fluffy.
It's fluffy now, and I have the eggs cracked into a cup. Add them all at once?
Blend in the eggs and mix well, scraping the bowl so the egg mixture is even.
Done. I don't want to overwork it—how do I handle the dry ingredients?
Mix in the flour, baking soda, and salt just until they disappear into the egg mixture.
Where does that tiny ginger pinch fit in so it stays subtle?
Stir that tiny pinch of ginger into the dry ingredients before they meet the wet mixture; keep it light so it doesn't take over the chilled dessert.
I've got a sticky bowl and beaters. Any quick cleanup or cooling note before I move on?
Scrape down the bowl and beaters right away, then let the baked squares cool completely before serving them as your chilled fruit dessert.
I want to make Eclairs II, and I've got my saucepan out. Can you talk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Set your oven to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C, so it can heat while you prep the dough base.
Oven is heating. What ingredients should I put on the counter before I start?
You'll need 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup water, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
I have the butter, water, flour, and salt measured. Should I prepare the baking sheet yet?
Yes, grease a cookie sheet now so it's ready when the mixture is done.
Cookie sheet is greased. For the stove part, does everything go in at once?
Start with just the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water in a medium saucepan.
They're in the saucepan. What heat level am I aiming for?
Heat the saucepan until the butter and water come to a boil, stirring as it warms so the butter melts completely.
The butter is mostly melted but there are a few small pieces floating. Should I keep stirring?
Yes, keep stirring until those pieces disappear completely, then let the mixture reach a full boil.
It's boiling now and the butter is fully melted. Is this the point where I stop this stage?
Yes. You've completed the listed prep: oven at 450 degrees F or 230 degrees C, greased cookie sheet, and the butter-water mixture brought to a boil with the butter fully melted.
I'm about to start Chicken and Black Bean Chili. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a large pot out and want to prep as I go.

Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 tablespoons cooking oil and 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into 1 inch pieces. Keep the chicken pieces fairly even so they brown at the same pace.
The chicken is cut up. Should I season it before it goes into the pot, or wait?
For this recipe, wait until after the chicken is browning. Also have sea salt to taste and 1 tablespoon chili powder, or more to taste, ready nearby.
Got it. The oil is measured—what heat should I use?
Pour the oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat. Give it a minute or two until it looks glossy and moves easily across the bottom.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do I add all the chicken at once?
Add the chicken pieces to the pot in a single layer if you can. Let them brown on all sides, stirring and turning as needed so the surfaces pick up color.
Some pieces are sticking slightly, but they're starting to brown. Is that okay?
Yes, a little sticking is normal while they brown. Keep the heat at medium and turn the pieces gently; once they're browned on the outside, you can move on.
The chicken has color on all sides now. What spices go in?
Season the chicken with sea salt, chili powder, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir well so the spices coat the chicken and bloom in the oil.
The spices smell good. I have onion plus green and yellow bell pepper chopped—do they go in now?
Yes. Mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper, scraping the bottom of the pot as you stir so the vegetables pick up the seasoned bits.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Go with the oven for this batch; switch the trays around once during baking, and don't do a final rest.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For tonight's batch of Chocolate Crisps, I'm using two trays and only want the special approach this time. Between stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan, which route should I take?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use the oven route, rotate the trays once, and skip the final rest.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chocolate Crisps as a two-tray recipe with stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan routes. Which route should I take?

messages.content: For tonight's batch of Chocolate Crisps, I'm using two trays and only want the special approach this time. Between stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan, which route should I take?
Go with the oven for this batch; switch the trays around once during baking, and don't do a final rest.
Perfect, just for this batch. I have the two trays out—what should I pull from the fridge or pantry first?
Start with 1 tablespoon butter, softened, and 1 egg white. Keep a small saucepan and a medium sized bowl nearby too.
The butter is soft and the egg white is separated. Should the sweet stuff be measured now?
Yes. Set out 1/4 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so everything is ready before the heat goes on.
Sugar and vanilla are on the counter. Before I touch the butter, should the oven be warming?
Yes—bring the oven up to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). With two trays, leave enough rack space so you can rotate them easily.
Oven is heating and the racks are spaced. How should I prep the trays?
Grease the cookie sheets lightly so the crisps release cleanly after baking.
Both sheets are greased. What texture am I looking for with the butter in the pan?
Put the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and melt it until it's lightly browned. Watch for a nutty smell and a pale golden-brown color.
It's foaming and just turning tan at the edges. Do I keep it on longer?
As soon as it's lightly browned, take it off the heat so it doesn't burn.
The medium bowl is ready beside the stove. Where does the browned butter go?
Pour the browned butter into the medium sized bowl. Keep the egg white, sugar, and vanilla close by for the next mixing move.
I want to make Chicken Spinach Bake and I've got frozen chopped spinach thawing. Can you talk me through what to have ready?
Absolutely. You'll need 3 packages of frozen chopped spinach, 10 ounces each, thawed, plus 3 eggs. Also set out 1/2 teaspoon onion salt and 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg.
The spinach is thawed but pretty wet. Should I deal with that before mixing anything?
Yes, take care of the spinach first. Drain it well, then squeeze out as much excess moisture as you can so the bake doesn't turn watery.
I'm squeezing it in batches over the sink. How dry should it feel?
It should feel damp but not dripping. If liquid is still running out when you press it, keep squeezing a bit longer.
Okay, the spinach is no longer dripping. What bowl work comes next?
In a mixing bowl, beat the 3 eggs with the 1/2 teaspoon onion salt and 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg until the seasoning is evenly blended.
The egg mixture is smooth. Do I fold the spinach straight into that?
Yes. Add the squeezed spinach to the egg mixture along with 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, then mix everything well so the spinach is evenly coated.
It's mixed together. I also have bread crumbs and more Parmesan nearby—are those for the top?
That's right. Combine the bread crumbs with the remaining Parmesan in a separate bowl so you have an even crumb-and-cheese mixture.
The topping is combined. Anything I should check before putting it together?
Give the spinach mixture one last stir to make sure there are no dry clumps, then spread it evenly in your baking dish and scatter the bread crumb and remaining Parmesan mixture over the surface.
I want to make Drunken Fruit Salsa. Can you help me time the prep so it has enough chill time?
Absolutely. Since it needs to refrigerate for 1 to 3 hours, start early enough that the fruit can sit and the flavors can blend before serving.
I've got a mango and strawberries out. How should I cut them?
Peel 1 medium mango and finely dice it. For the strawberries, chop enough fresh berries to make 3/4 cup.
The mango is diced, and I measured the strawberries. What else goes into the bowl?
Peel and finely dice 1 kiwi, then seed and finely chop 1 jalapeno pepper so it mixes evenly without big spicy pieces.
Should I use any special bowl for mixing since there's rum involved?
Use a glass bowl. Add the mango, strawberries, kiwi, jalapeno, mint, and rum, then stir everything together gently so the fruit stays intact.
I'm adding the mint and rum now. Should it look saucy or more like chopped fruit?
It should still look like a finely chopped fruit salsa, just lightly moistened and glossy from the rum and fruit juices.
It's mixed. Do I cover it before putting it in the fridge?
Yes, cover the glass bowl and refrigerate it for 1 to 3 hours. Stir it once or twice during that time to redistribute the juices.
After it chills, is there anything else to do before serving?
Give it one final gentle stir, check that the fruit is evenly coated, and serve it chilled.
I want to make Apple Butter V, and I've got a Dutch oven ready. Can you talk me through what to prep?
Absolutely. Core and slice 6 pounds of tart apples, then measure out 6 cups of apple cider so it's ready to pour in.
The apples are cored and sliced, and the cider is measured. Are there any other ingredients before I start cooking?
Yes—set out 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon. Keep them nearby for later in the apple butter process.
All right, the sugar and cinnamon are on the counter. Should the apples go in the pot by themselves?
Put the sliced apples into the Dutch oven first. A wide Dutch oven is helpful because it gives the apples room to soften evenly.
The pot looks pretty full with the apples. Do I add the cider right away?
Yes, pour in the 6 cups of apple cider over the apples. It will help them cook down and soften without scorching at the start.
On Apple Butter V, cider is in. What heat should I use to get it going?
In this Apple Butter V step, bring the mixture to a boil, then cook it over medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
I'm at about the 30 minute mark. What should the texture be like before I move on?
The apple slices should be very soft and collapsing when pressed with a spoon. If any pieces still feel firm, give them a few more minutes on medium heat.
They're soft now and the mixture is hot. How do I handle the food mill part?
Carefully press the softened apple mixture through a food mill. Work in batches if needed, and keep the bowl or pot underneath steady so you catch all the smooth apple base.
I want to make Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken and I'm checking the sauce ingredients before I start. Can you talk me through it?

Absolutely. For the glaze, measure out 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum. You'll also need mustard and garlic for the bowl, plus salt and pepper to season.
I've got the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, rum, mustard, and garlic out. Should I mix the glaze in something large?
Use a medium bowl. Add the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, dark rum, mustard, and garlic, then stir until the molasses loosens up and the mixture looks smooth and glossy.
The molasses is thick and settling at the bottom. Is that okay, or should I keep stirring?
Keep stirring and scrape the bottom of the bowl so the molasses fully blends into the ketchup and pineapple juice. Once the color is even, season with salt and pepper to taste and mix well again.
The glaze looks even now. What baking dish should I use for the chicken pieces?
Lightly oil a 9x13 inch baking dish, then place the chicken pieces in it with enough space that you can brush the glaze onto both sides.
I oiled the dish and arranged the chicken. Do I use all the glaze at this point?
Use about 1/2 of the prepared glaze now. Brush it over one side of the chicken, turn the pieces carefully, and brush the other side too.
Both sides are coated, and I still have the rest of the glaze in the bowl. What happens next?
Cover the baking dish and put it in the refrigerator to marinate. Let it chill for at least 2 hours, or leave it overnight if you want a longer marinade.
If I'm serving it later tonight, is the 2-hour marinating time enough?
Yes, at least 2 hours works for this recipe. Keep the dish covered in the fridge until you're ready to continue cooking, and save the remaining glaze separately for later use.
I'm making Biga and want someone to pace me through the early mixing. What should I have out?

Set out 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast, 1/2 cup warm water, 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour, and 1 1/4 cups cold water. You'll also want a small bowl for blooming the yeast and a large bowl for the flour.
I've got the yeast and both waters measured. Does the warm water go in with the flour right away?
For Biga, not yet. Pour the 1/2 cup warm water into the small bowl, then sprinkle the 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast over the top so it can hydrate evenly.
The yeast is sprinkled over the warm water. Should I stir it or leave it alone?
You can leave it to stand. Give it about 15 minutes, until the yeast has dissolved and the surface looks foamy.
Okay, I'll wait. While that sits, should I prep the flour bowl?
Yes. Measure 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour into a large bowl so it's ready when the yeast mixture is foamy.
The flour is in the large bowl, and the yeast mixture is starting to foam. What should the bowl look like before I pour?
Make a well in the center of the flour, like a shallow crater. That gives the yeast mixture and the 1 1/4 cups cold water a place to land before everything spreads through the flour.
The well is made. Do I add the cold water separately or with the yeast mixture?
Pour the foamy yeast mixture into the well, then add the 1 1/4 cups cold water into that same center area.
Both liquids are in the well now. Is there anything else from this part I need to check?
For this stage, you've completed the listed setup: the yeast bloomed for about 15 minutes, the 3 1/2 cups flour is in the large bowl, and the yeast mixture plus cold water are in the center well.
I'm starting Baked Aloha Chicken; can you walk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Set the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you mix the sauce.
Oven is heating. I have a glass baking dish out—what should I measure for the sauce?
Measure 1/4 cup lemon juice and 1/4 cup light corn syrup into a mixing bowl.
Those are in the bowl. The corn syrup is a little sticky on the measuring cup.
That's fine—scrape in what you can. Add 2 tablespoons soy sauce and 1 teaspoon salt to the same bowl.
Soy sauce and salt are added. Does anything else go into that mixture before the pineapple?
Yes. Stir in the ginger and corn oil with the lemon juice, corn syrup, soy sauce, and salt, then mix until the sauce looks smooth.
The sauce is smooth now. I opened the crushed pineapple—do I drain it?
Don't drain it. Stir the crushed pineapple into the sauce with its liquid so the mixture stays juicy.
Pineapple and liquid are mixed in. How should I arrange the chicken legs?
Lay the chicken legs in the ovenproof glass baking dish in a single layer if they fit, then pour the pineapple sauce evenly over the top.
The chicken is sauced in the dish. Should I wipe the rim before it goes in?
Yes, wipe any drips from the outside or rim of the dish, then place it in the preheated 350 degrees F oven.
I want to make Easy Pot Roast and I've got a 4 pound boneless chuck roast thawed. Can you stay with me while I prep it?
Absolutely. Set the roast on your work surface, and gather 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce.
The water, soup mix, and Worcestershire sauce are out. Should I heat the oven before I handle the meat?
Yes, go ahead and set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it is ready when the roast is bagged.
Oven is heating. I have a medium oven bag open—what should I do to the roast before it goes in?
Score the roast across the top and along the sides with shallow cuts, then place it into the medium sized oven bag.
The roast is scored and sitting in the bag. Do I mix the liquid in a bowl first or pour everything in separately?
Mix it first: combine the 2 cups water, the dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and the 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce until the soup mix is dispersed.
The mixture is ready, and the bag is still upright. Where should the liquid go?
Pour the mixture directly over the roast inside the oven bag, letting it run over the scored top and down the sides.
Liquid is in. I've got vegetables cut up beside the pan—how do they fit in?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat in the bag so they sit alongside the roast rather than piled only on top.
The vegetables are tucked around it. Is there anything else from the recipe before it goes into the oven?
From the recipe steps, you've completed the setup: oven at 350 degrees F / 175 degrees C, roast scored and bagged, liquid poured over it, and vegetables arranged around the meat.
I want to make Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches. Can you stay with me while I prep the vegetables and get them onto the bread?
For this batch of Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches, start by getting the vegetables ready: finely chop 1 small onion, dice 1 medium tomato, chop 1 stalk celery, and finely chop 1 green bell pepper.
The onion and tomato are done, but the celery and bell pepper are still whole. Should they be pretty small?
Yes, keep the celery chopped and the green bell pepper finely chopped so the topping spreads evenly and gives the sandwiches a crunchy texture.
Vegetables are cut. What should I do with the oven before I mix everything?
Preheat your oven's broiler so it is ready when the bread is topped.
Broiler is heating. I have a medium bowl out—what goes in it?
Add the onion, tomato, celery, bell pepper, cheese, chili powder, and salt to the medium bowl, then stir everything together until the vegetables are evenly coated and mixed.
The mixture looks colorful and a little chunky. Is that the right texture?
That sounds right for Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches. It should be mixed enough to hold together on the bread while still keeping the chopped vegetables distinct.
I'm ready for the bread. Do I need a special pan?
Use a baking sheet or a broiling pan, and arrange the slices of bread on it in a single layer.
Bread is on the sheet. How much topping should go on each slice?
Spoon 1/4 of the mixture onto each slice of bread, spreading it out to the edges so every sandwich gets an even topping under the broiler.
I want to make Feta Chicken Salad for lunch. Can you walk me through what to prep before I start mixing?

Absolutely. Set out 3 cups diced cooked chicken, 2 large stalks celery diced, 1 red bell pepper that's seeded and diced, and 1/2 red onion diced. You'll also need mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, dill, plus salt and pepper for the end.
The chicken is already diced, and I'm chopping the celery now. Should I use a serving bowl right away?
Yes, grab a serving bowl large enough to toss everything comfortably. Add the diced cooked chicken and the diced celery as they're ready.
The celery and chicken are in. I still have the red bell pepper and onion on the board.
Go ahead and seed and dice the red bell pepper, then dice the 1/2 red onion. Add the red onion to the serving bowl with the chicken and celery.
Do I add the red bell pepper to that bowl too, or keep it aside?
Add the diced red bell pepper to the serving bowl too. The main mixture should have the chicken, celery, red onion, and bell pepper together before the dressing goes on.
That bowl is full and colorful. What should I use for the creamy part?
Use a separate bowl for the dressing. Stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the feta is distributed and the mixture looks creamy.
The feta is a little crumbly in the dressing. Is that okay, or should it be completely smooth?
A little crumbly is fine; feta usually keeps some texture. Just stir until the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta, and dill are evenly combined.
The dressing is mixed. How do I bring it together without mashing the chicken?
Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture, then fold and stir gently until everything is coated. Taste it, then season with salt and pepper as needed before serving.
I want to make Cookie Paints for a batch of cutout cookies. Can you stay with me while I mix it?
Absolutely. You only need 2 tablespoons evaporated milk and 4 drops red food coloring, plus a small bowl, a spoon, and a clean paintbrush for the cookies.
I found the evaporated milk and the red coloring. Should the bowl be tiny, or does it need extra room?
A small bowl is perfect. There just needs to be enough room to stir without splashing, since the mixture is only a few spoonfuls.
I measured the milk into the bowl. Do I add all the coloring at once?
Yes, add the 4 drops red food coloring directly into the evaporated milk.
The drops are in, but the color is streaky around the edges.
Stir it until the red is evenly blended through the milk. Scrape around the sides of the bowl with the spoon so no darker streaks remain.
It looks smooth and pinkish red now. Do I brush it on baked cookies or raw dough?
Brush it onto the cookies before baking. Use the paintbrush to apply a thin, even layer or small designs on the unbaked cookies.
The brush is leaving a little puddle in one spot. Is that a problem?
Just dab off the extra with the brush and spread it out lightly. A thin coating will bake more neatly than a wet puddle.
I've painted the tops and the cookies are ready for the oven. Anything else before I bake them?
You're set. Bake the cookies according to your cookie dough recipe, since this paint recipe only covers mixing the color and applying it before baking.
I want to make Banana Chip Muffins I. Before I start mixing, can you help me lay out the dry ingredients?
Absolutely. Put a large bowl on the counter and measure out 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Those are measured. The recipe name says banana chip, but I don't see an amount for chocolate chips here—do they go in with the dry stuff?

Yes, the instructions say to measure the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and chocolate chips into the large bowl. Use the chip amount your recipe version calls for, since no quantity is listed in what you have here.
Okay, the chips are in the bowl with the flour mixture. Should I stir gently or really combine it?
Mix the dry ingredients thoroughly so the baking powder and salt are evenly spread through the flour and sugar. Once it looks uniform, make a well in the center of the mixture.
I made the well. I've got a small bowl ready—what happens with the egg?
Crack the egg into the small bowl and beat it until it looks frothy, with bubbles on the surface and the yolk fully broken up.
The egg is foamy now. I also have bananas, milk, and cooking oil nearby.
Good. Mix the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the beaten egg. Mash or break up the bananas enough that they blend into the liquid mixture.
How smooth should the banana mixture be before I pour it in?
It doesn't need to be perfectly smooth; a few small banana bits are fine. Aim for a wet mixture that's combined enough to pour evenly into the well in the dry ingredients.
Wet mixture is ready and the dry bowl has the well. Anything I should watch for before combining?

Keep the well open, pour the wet mixture into the center, and stir just until the dry ingredients are moistened. The key prep from this recipe is measured dry ingredients with chocolate chips, a well in the center, frothy beaten egg, then oil, milk, and bananas mixed in.
I want to make Eggnog II. Can you stay with me while I prep the ingredients?
Absolutely. Set out 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. The cooking starts with the eggs, milk, and sugar in a saucepan.
Ingredients are measured. What tools should I have ready before I turn on the stove?
Use a large saucepan and a metal spoon for checking the texture. It also helps to set up a sink or bowl with ice water now, since the pan needs to cool quickly once it comes off the heat.
The saucepan is on the stove, and the ice water bowl is beside me.
Pour the beaten eggs into the saucepan, add the 2 1/4 cups milk, and stir in the 1/3 cup white sugar until everything looks evenly combined.
It's mixed together and still cold. What heat level should I use?
Turn the burner to medium heat. Keep stirring as it warms so the egg mixture cooks evenly and doesn't settle on the bottom.
It's starting to steam a little. What texture am I looking for?
Keep cooking and stirring until the mixture coats a metal spoon. When you lift the spoon, it should leave a thin layer clinging to the metal rather than running off immediately.
The spoon has a light coating now, and the mixture looks slightly thicker.
Take the saucepan off the heat right away. Don't let it keep cooking on the burner once it reaches that coating stage.
Pan is off the stove. How do I cool it without waiting forever?
Place the pan in the sink or bowl of ice water and stir the eggnog for 1 to 2 minutes so it cools quickly. After that, you can transfer it for serving or chilling.
I'd like to make Black Bean Lasagna Rolls—can you walk me through the setup before I start boiling anything?
Absolutely. Put a pot of water on for the lasagna noodles, and gather 8 uncooked lasagna noodles plus 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese.
The noodles and Monterey Jack are out. What dairy and canned ingredients should I pull from the fridge and pantry?
You'll need 1 (15 ounce) container part-skim ricotta cheese and 1 (4.5 ounce) can chopped green chiles, drained. Keep your black beans nearby too, since they'll be spooned onto the rolls later.
Do I salt the pasta water or add oil so the noodles don't stick?
For this recipe, cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions while omitting salt and fat. Stir them gently as they cook, then drain them well.
The noodles are draining. Should I cool them before spreading the filling?
Let them sit just until they're comfortable to handle and lay them flat so they don't fold over on themselves. While they cool slightly, mix the filling.
I'm ready to mix—what exactly goes into the bowl?
Combine the cheeses with the drained chopped green chiles and the other listed filling ingredients, stirring well so the ricotta, Monterey Jack, and chiles are evenly distributed.
The cheese mixture looks creamy with the chiles mixed through. How much should I put on each noodle?
Spread the cheese mixture over one side of each lasagna noodle in an even layer, leaving a little space at the edges so it doesn't squeeze out too much when rolled.
All 8 noodles are coated. Where do the black beans go?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on the noodles. Once they're distributed, the noodles are ready to roll up gently into lasagna rolls.
I'm ready to cook Cindis Egg Rolls. What should be ready before I begin? I've got my wok out and want to prep everything in a sensible order.
Absolutely. Set up the filling ingredients first: 1 pound ground pork, 4 cups shredded cabbage, 1 large shredded carrot, and 1/2 green bell pepper sliced into thin strips.
The pork and cabbage are ready. Should the carrot and pepper go in with the cabbage before I start cooking?
Yes, keep the cabbage, shredded carrot, and thin green bell pepper strips together in a large bowl for the vegetable mix. You'll also be adding onion, garlic, and ginger to that bowl.
Got it. I'm at the stove now—how hot should the wok be for the pork?
Heat the large wok over medium-high heat, then cook the ground pork in it until it's cooked through and no longer pink.
The pork is cooked and there's some liquid in the wok. Do I keep that?
Drain the cooked pork, then set it aside so it doesn't make the filling watery.
While that rests, I'm mixing the vegetables. Just to confirm: cabbage, carrot, pepper, onion, garlic, and ginger all together?
That's right. In a large bowl, mix the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, thin green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger until everything is evenly combined.
The bowl is pretty full, but it's mixed. What should I do for the sauce part?
Use a small bowl for the sauce mixture. Stir together the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses until the mixture is smooth with no dry cornstarch pockets.
Should that smooth sauce be ready before I combine it with the pork and vegetables?
Yes. Keep the drained pork, the mixed vegetables, and the smooth cornstarch-soy-molasses mixture ready so the filling can come together cleanly without lumps or excess moisture.
I'm starting Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf; can you walk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 12 ounces of chopped raw bacon and 1 small white onion, chopped. If the onion is not chopped yet, get that done before the skillet goes on.
The bacon is chopped, and I'm chopping the onion now. What else should be on the counter?
You'll also need 5 button mushrooms, chopped, plus 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef. Keep the beef chilled until you're ready to mix later.
Mushrooms are ready, and the beef is still in the fridge. Should I heat the oven yet?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, so it is ready when the meatloaf is assembled.
Oven is heating. I've got a skillet out for the bacon—what kind of heat should I use?
Put the chopped bacon in the skillet over medium heat. Cook it until the pieces are browned, stirring now and then so they color evenly.
It's starting to sizzle and there's a lot of fat in the pan. How browned should the bacon get?
Look for browned pieces rather than pale, soft bacon. Once most of the bits have browned, you're ready to take them out.
The bacon looks browned. What's the cleanest way to pull it from the grease?
Use a slotted spoon to lift the bacon out of the skillet, then transfer it onto paper towels so the excess grease can drain.
Bacon is draining on paper towels, and the skillet still has plenty of grease. How much do I keep?
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon grease in the skillet. That leaves just enough fat for the next part without making the meatloaf greasy.
I want to make Carrots and Onions Au Gratin. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 (16 ounce) package of baby carrots, sliced, and 2 medium onions, sliced. Those are the vegetables you'll cook first.
The carrots are sliced, and I'm working through the onions. What else should be on the counter?
Have 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter ready as well. You'll also want a pot, lightly salted water, a colander for draining, and a baking dish.
Got it. Should I turn the oven on before I boil the vegetables?
Yes—heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready when the vegetables are prepared.
Oven is heating. How much water should I put in the pot?
Add the sliced carrots and onions to the pot, then pour in enough lightly salted water to cover them. Put the pot over heat and bring it to a boil.
They're in the water now. Once it boils, how long am I aiming for?
Cook them for 5 minutes, just until they're tender but still firm. You don't want them turning mushy before they go into the baking dish.
What's the best way to check that texture?
Pierce a carrot slice with a fork. It should give a little but still hold its shape; the onion slices should look softened, not falling apart.
They seem tender but firm. What do I do right after draining?
Drain the carrots and onions well, then spread 1/2 of the drained mixture into your baking dish in an even layer.
I want to get Barbecued Shredded Beef right. What should I handle first? I've got a beef roast out and want to set everything up before I start.
Absolutely. You'll need a 3 pounds beef roast and 2 onions, chopped. Have a large roasting pan ready too, since the roast and onions go straight into it.
The pan is on the counter and the onions are chopped. What liquids and seasonings should I pull out?
Grab 2 (12 fluid ounce) cans or bottles beer and 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce. You'll also use liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper when you mix the sauce.
Got it. Should I heat the oven before arranging the meat?
Yes, bring the oven up to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C) so it's ready by the time the roast is assembled.
Oven is heating. Does the roast need anything done to it before it goes in the pan?
Place the beef roast in the large roasting pan as it is, then scatter the chopped onions over the top and around it.
The onions are spread over the roast. I have a mixing bowl out—what goes in there?
In the large bowl, combine the Worcestershire sauce with the liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir those together so the seasoning is evenly mixed.
That mixture is ready. Do I add the beer to the bowl or straight to the pan?
For Barbecued Shredded Beef, pour the beer into the bowl with the Worcestershire mixture, stir it together, then add that liquid to the roasting pan.
The liquid is in the pan around the beef and onions. Anything I should check before it goes into the oven?
Make sure the roast is settled in the pan, the onions are scattered over it, and the beer mixture is poured in evenly. Once the oven is at 275 degrees F, the pan is ready to go in.

For the tender lower cilantro and parsley pieces, chop them into tiny uneven bits and stir them into the mustard and dry onion soup mix so they become part of the coating. Set out 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 (1 ounce) envelopes dry onion soup mix, the 5 pound beef rump roast, a small bowl, paper towels, and two long sheets of aluminum foil.
The mustard is measured in the bowl, and the two soup mix envelopes are still sealed. Should I add both packets at once?
Yes, empty both dry onion soup mix envelopes into the mustard. Stir until it looks thick and evenly speckled, with no dry pockets at the bottom of the bowl.
The herbs are still in little stemmy clusters. Should I pick through them before chopping?
Pick out anything tough or woody, but keep the tender lower pieces. Give those a small, uneven chop so they blend into the mustard mixture without turning pasty.
I folded them in, and the coating looks chunky but spreadable. Is that the right texture before I touch the roast?
That sounds right. It should be thick enough to cling to the beef, with the onion soup mix and herb bits suspended throughout rather than loose or watery.

Lay two long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise on the counter, making a wide plus sign. Leave enough overhang so the roast can sit in the center and still have foil around it later.
The roast is out of the package, but there's moisture on the surface and in a few creases.
Pat the 5 pound beef rump roast dry all over with paper towels, including the sides and creases. The drier surface will help the mustard coating grip instead of sliding off.
It's dry now. Do I need to season the meat separately before the mustard goes on?
No separate seasoning is needed for this recipe. The dry onion soup mix in the mustard coating brings the seasoning, so you can place the roast straight onto the crossed foil.
Should the roast sit fat side up, or does that not matter for coating it?
Set it in the center of the foil in whatever position gives you the easiest access to the top and sides. The important part is that the roast is centered and stable while you coat it generously.
I'm holding the bowl of mustard mixture now. Do I spread a thin layer first or pile it on?

Spoon it on generously and spread it over the top and sides of the roast, using the mustard, dry onion soup mix, and tender herb pieces as one coating. Cover the surface well before you move on to wrapping or cooking.

messages.content: I've got the ingredients out for Delicious Artichoke Dip, but I want to keep the steps tidy. Where should I begin?

For the artichoke dip, use the oven, broiler, or a sheet pan to give it a hot finish, then let it rest uncovered briefly before serving. Get the oven heating to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), and put a medium mixing bowl and shallow baking dish within reach.
The oven is set, and the bowl is ready. Should I start with the creamy stuff or the cheese?
Start with the creamy base so it blends cleanly: add 1/2 cup mayonnaise and 1/2 cup sour cream to the bowl. Give them a short stir just to loosen them together.
That's mixed lightly. I have the Parmesan grated and the artichoke hearts draining in a colander.
Add 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese to the bowl, along with the onion from the recipe step. Stir until the mayonnaise, sour cream, Parmesan, and onion look smooth and evenly combined.
I like that hot finish with the brief uncovered rest; that's exactly what I wanted for this dip. The Parmesan mixture is smooth now.
Great. Check the 1 (14 ounce) can of drained artichoke hearts; if the pieces are very big, give them a rough chop so they spread through the dip more evenly.
They were pretty large, so I chopped them into bite-size pieces. Do I fold them in gently?
Yes, fold the artichoke hearts in gently so the dip stays chunky but spreadable. Try not to mash them into the creamy base.
The texture looks good now. The recipe mentions lemon juice, salt, and pepper, but I don't want it to get runny.
Add the lemon juice, salt, and pepper in small amounts, stirring gently after each addition. Stop once it tastes bright and balanced without loosening the mixture too much.
It tastes balanced. My shallow baking dish is glass and clean—should I grease it first?
If that dish tends to cling, give it a light coating before adding the dip. Spoon the mixture in and spread it into an even layer so the center heats at the same pace as the edges.
It's spread out evenly. Should I cover it with foil, or leave the surface exposed?
Leave it uncovered so the top can heat and brown. Bake it in the 400 degrees F oven, then use the broiler briefly at the end only if you want extra color and can watch it closely.
Got it. Once the top is hot and browned, what should I do before serving?
Take the dish out when the dip is hot through and the surface looks lightly browned. Let it sit uncovered for a short rest, then serve it while the inside is still creamy.

messages.content: I'm getting Cabbage Kielbasa Supper into the slow cooker tonight. Can you walk me through the prep before I start filling it?

Chop the tender lower cilantro stems and leaves, or parsley if that is what you have, into small irregular bits and add them at the start so they soften into the cabbage mixture. Then shred enough cabbage for 8 cups, cut 3 medium potatoes into 1/2 inch cubes, and chop 1 medium onion.
I've got the cutting board full. Should the potatoes be rinsed after cubing, or can they go straight in?

They can go straight in once they are cut into even 1/2 inch cubes. If they are very starchy or have been sitting a while, a quick rinse and pat dry is fine, but it is not necessary for this slow-cooker dish.
The cabbage looks like a lot for my 5-qt. cooker. Do I need to hold some back?
Use the full 8 cups if the lid can close. The cooker will look crowded at first, but the cabbage will cook down as it softens.
I like that lower-stem herb move here; that's exactly what I wanted for this dish.
Great—it works well with the long cook because those small tender pieces mellow into the broth instead of staying sharp. Scatter them through the cabbage so they do not clump in one corner.
I'm ready to season the vegetables. How much salt should I measure?
Measure 1 3/4 teaspoons salt. Add it with the cabbage, potato cubes, chopped onion, pepper, and herb pieces, then toss lightly in the slow cooker so the seasoning spreads around.
The vegetables are in and loosely mixed. Where does the broth fit in?
Pour the broth over everything in the slow cooker. You do not need to stir hard afterward; just let it run down through the cabbage and potatoes.
Some cabbage is still dry on top after the broth. Should I press it down?
Give the top a gentle nudge so more cabbage is moistened, but do not compact it. Leaving it loose helps the heat move through while the cabbage collapses during cooking.
I have the sausage ready now. Do I bury it or leave it visible?
Place the sausage on top of the cabbage mixture. It will heat through there while the potatoes, onion, cabbage, and herbs cook underneath.
Once the lid is on, what timing should I use, and what should I check at the end?

Cover and cook on low for 8-9 hours. Before serving, check that the vegetables are tender, the potatoes are soft all the way through, the cabbage has reduced, and the sausage is heated through; then give the brothy vegetables a light stir to distribute the onion, pepper, salt, and herb pieces.
Help me stay organized for Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup. What comes first? I've got the slow cooker out and want to set things up in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the main items ready: 1 1/2 pounds cubed beef stew meat, 2 cups water, 1 small onion chopped, and 1 (28 ounce) can crushed tomatoes.
The beef is cubed and the onion is chopped. Should I brown the meat first, or does it go straight into the slow cooker?
For this recipe, place the beef straight in the slow cooker. No browning step is listed, so you can add the cubed stew meat directly.
Beef is in. I have the water measured in a cup—does all of it go in now?
Yes, pour in the full 2 cups water over the beef in the slow cooker.
Done. The crushed tomatoes are opened, and I also have mixed vegetables and potatoes nearby.
Stir in the chopped onion, the 28 ounce can of crushed tomatoes, the mixed vegetables, and the potatoes so everything is distributed through the cooker.
It's looking pretty full. Should I stir it a lot or just enough to combine?
Just stir enough to combine the beef, onion, tomatoes, mixed vegetables, potatoes, and water. You don't need to overmix it.
I'm ready to season. What goes in before I put the lid on?
Season the soup with bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil. Sprinkle them evenly over the mixture, then give it one more gentle stir.
Everything is seasoned and mixed. Is there anything else from the recipe before I start the slow cooker?

That covers the listed prep: beef in the slow cooker, water added, onion, crushed tomatoes, mixed vegetables, and potatoes stirred in, then bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil for seasoning. Put the lid on and cook according to your slow cooker setting.

messages.content: I'm making Cinnamon Bread I this afternoon. Can you help me get organized before I start mixing?

Keep the spice layer to a modest cardamom-and-ginger note so the fruit stays in front and the spice sits quietly behind it. For the bread itself, set out a large mixing bowl, measuring cups, and one 9x5 inch loaf pan.
The bowl and loaf pan are out. Should I heat the oven now or measure first?
Go ahead and heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). While it warms, grease the 9x5 inch loaf pan so the batter can go in as soon as it's beaten.
Oven is on and the pan is greased. Which dry ingredients should I pull together?
Measure out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. Keep them near the mixing bowl so you can add everything smoothly.
I like that cardamom-and-ginger note here; that's exactly what I wanted for this kind of sweet bread. What else goes into the bowl?
Add the measured flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, and baking soda to the large mixing bowl. Then include 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
Everything is in the bowl, but I'm checking the mixing time before I turn on the beaters.
Beat the mixture for 3 minutes. Aim for an even batter with no dry pockets clinging to the sides of the bowl.
The batter looks mostly smooth. Should I scrape the bowl during those 3 minutes?
Yes, pause once if flour is stuck along the sides, scrape it down, then keep beating so the full 3 minutes is still covered.
It's smooth now and the pan is ready. Do I pour it straight in?
Yes, scrape the batter into the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan and level the top lightly so it bakes evenly.
The top is leveled. Anything I should remember before it bakes?
Make sure the oven is still at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), then place the pan in the oven. Keep the added cardamom and ginger gentle so they support the cinnamon rather than overpowering the loaf.
I'm about to start Easy Alfredo Sauce I. Can you talk me through the prep? I've got a medium saucepan out and want to keep it simple.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pint heavy whipping cream, 1/2 cup butter, and 1 1/2 cups grated Parmesan cheese. Those are the only ingredients for this sauce.
The cream and butter are ready, but my Parmesan is still in the fridge. Should I measure it before heating anything?
Yes, measure the Parmesan first so you can add everything together smoothly. You'll need 1 1/2 cups grated Parmesan cheese.
All measured. Does the butter need to melt before the cheese goes in?
No need to melt it separately. Put the heavy whipping cream, butter, and grated Parmesan cheese together in the medium saucepan.
Everything is in the pan. What heat should I use so the cream doesn't scorch?
Use medium-low heat. Stir as it warms, letting the butter melt and the Parmesan blend into the cream.
It's starting to look creamy, but there are a few little cheese bits. Is that okay?
That's okay while it's still coming together. Keep it over medium-low heat and continue stirring until the sauce looks smooth.
It's smooth now and coating the spoon. Should I keep cooking it longer to thicken?
Once it's smooth, remove the saucepan from the heat. The sauce will thicken upon standing.
Good to know. I'm serving it with pasta—should I wait a minute before tossing it?
Yes, let it stand briefly off the heat so it can thicken a bit, then toss it with the pasta while it's still warm and creamy.
I'm setting up for Asian Ginger Dressing; what should happen before the heat goes on? I've got a clean jar out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Use a 1 pint glass jar or something larger so there's room to shake. Add 3 cloves garlic, minced, and 2 tablespoons minced fresh ginger root to the jar.
Garlic and ginger are in. For the liquids, what should I measure next?
Pour in 3/4 cup olive oil and 1/3 cup rice vinegar. Then add the soy sauce, honey, and water called for in the recipe to the same jar.
Everything is in the jar, but the honey is sitting thick near the bottom. Should I stir it first?
You can skip stirring for now. Put on a tight fitting lid and shake the jar really well so the garlic, ginger, oil, vinegar, soy sauce, honey, and water start to combine.
I shook it, and it looks mixed except for a little honey still clinging to the glass.
Take the lid off before heating, then microwave the jar for 1 minute. The goal is just to dissolve the honey, not to cook the dressing.
The minute is up. The jar feels warm and the honey looks dissolved.
Great. Let the dressing cool for a bit with the lid off or loosely set aside, so it's not hot when you serve or store it.
How cool should it be before I use it on salad?
Let it come down to a comfortable serving temperature. Once it's cooled, put the lid back on and shake well again right before serving.
After shaking, it's smooth but I can see bits of ginger and garlic. Is that right?
Yes, that's expected for Asian Ginger Dressing with minced fresh ginger root and minced garlic. Serve it right after the final shake, or keep it in the jar and shake again before using.
I'm getting ready for Black Bean Lasagna Rolls. Can you help me sequence the steps? I'm getting the pot and a baking dish out now.

Absolutely. Set up 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese, a 1 (15 ounce) container of part-skim ricotta cheese, and a 1 (4.5 ounce) can of chopped green chiles, drained.
I found the noodles and both cheeses. Should I start boiling water before mixing anything?
Yes. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions, but omit the salt and fat. When they're done, drain them well so they're easy to roll.
The noodles are cooking. For the filling, do the ricotta and Monterey Jack go together?
They do. Combine the ricotta and Monterey Jack in a bowl, then add the drained chopped green chiles along with the next ingredients for the filling, stirring until everything is well mixed.
I've drained the noodles. They're a little slippery—how should I lay them out?
Lay the noodles flat in a single layer, with one side facing up for filling. If they're sticking, separate them gently so they don't tear.
How much of the cheese mixture should go on each noodle?
Divide the cheese mixture evenly among the 8 noodles, spreading it over one side of each noodle in a thin, even layer.
I have the black beans ready. Do they go on top of the cheese before rolling?
Yes. Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on each noodle, keeping the layer balanced so the rolls hold together.
Should I roll them tightly or leave them a bit loose?
Roll them snugly enough to hold the filling, but not so tight that the cheese mixture and black beans squeeze out. Place each roll seam-side down as you finish it.
I'm making Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs and I've got a cutting board out. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms. If the mushrooms aren't chopped yet, get them into small, even pieces so they cook at the same pace.
The mushrooms are chopped, and the oil is measured. What aromatics do I need ready?
Have 2 green onions chopped and 1 clove garlic crushed. Keep them close to the stove with the mushrooms, since they'll all go into the pan together.
Got it. Should I turn on the oven before I start the pan?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C. That way it's hot by the time the mushroom mixture is ready.
For Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs, oven is heating. What pan setup should I use for the mushrooms?
Use a medium saucepan over medium heat. Pour in the olive oil and let it warm briefly so it coats the bottom of the pan.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do the mushrooms go in alone or with everything else?
Stir in the mushrooms, chopped green onions, crushed garlic, and cayenne pepper together. Mix so the oil lightly coats the vegetables and the garlic isn't sitting in one spot.
They're in the pan. How often should I stir, and what am I looking for?
Cook the mixture for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. You're looking for the mushrooms to become tender and release their moisture.
If there's still liquid in the pan near the end, should I keep it on medium?
Yes, keep it over medium heat and give it a few more stirs while staying close. Once the mushrooms are tender, you're ready to move on with the puff assembly or serving step you have planned.

messages.content: I'm getting ready to make Eggplant Mixed Grill, and the vegetables are on the board. How should I start so everything marinates evenly?
Cut the onion and bell peppers into small, even dice so they scatter through the vegetables without getting mushy. After that, gather the marinade ingredients and a large resealable plastic bag.
I've got the bag out. Which measured ingredients should go in first?
Add the measured herb mixture first: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil.
The herbs are chopped and the oil is measured. Do I stir those together before adding the rest?
Stir them right in the resealable bag, then add the vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic. Squeeze the outside of the bag gently to combine the marinade without making a mess.
That's exactly what I wanted—the small, even dice makes these add-ins work better for this dish. Should the onion go into the bag now?
Yes, add the diced onion now so it starts soaking up the herb-and-oil mixture. Keep the bag open on the counter while you prep the rest of the vegetables.
I still have asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and both bell peppers to deal with. What order would you add them?
Add the asparagus and mushrooms next, then the eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper. Try to spread them around the bag instead of packing one vegetable in a tight layer.
The bag is getting pretty full. How do I coat everything without tearing it?
Press out some extra air, seal the bag firmly, and turn it slowly with both hands. Flip and tilt it until the marinade reaches the eggplant, mushrooms, asparagus, onion, and both bell peppers.
Can it sit out while I clean up the cutting board, or should it go cold right away?
Put it in the refrigerator to marinate for 2 hours. Turn the bag occasionally during that time so the vegetables stay evenly coated.
When the 2 hours are almost done, what should I do outside at the grill?
Preheat the grill for high heat. Once it is hot, lightly oil the grill grate so the marinated vegetables release more easily.
Any final cue for texture before I serve the mixed grill?

Grill the vegetables until they look tender and nicely cooked. As you move them around, keep the smaller onion and pepper pieces distributed through the vegetables instead of letting them collect in one bite.
I pulled up French Spring Soup. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got a large pot out and want to prep everything before I turn on the stove.
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup butter, 1 pound chopped leeks, 1 chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice ready to add later.
While working on French Spring Soup, the leeks are chopped, but they look a little gritty. Should I rinse them before they go in?
Yes, rinse the chopped leeks well and drain them so they don't carry grit into the soup. Once they're clean, keep them near the stove with the chopped onion.
Everything is washed and chopped now. How do I start cooking without browning the vegetables too much?
Put the large pot over medium heat and melt the butter gently. Let it fully melt and coat the bottom of the pot, but don't let it darken.
The butter is melted and foamy. Do the leeks and onion go in together?
Yes, stir in the leeks and onion together. Cook them over medium heat, stirring now and then, until they're tender and softened.
They're soft and smell sweet, and there's no browning on the bottom. Is it time for the liquid?
It is. Pour the 2 quarts water into the pot, scraping gently along the bottom as you stir so the softened vegetables mix into the broth.
The water is in. I have potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice prepped in bowls—do they all go in now?
Add the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice to the pot, then stir everything together so the rice doesn't clump and the vegetables are distributed evenly.
After I stir those in, should I keep the pot covered or leave it open while it cooks?

Once everything is mixed in, bring the soup along gently and keep an eye on the texture of the vegetables and rice. You can partially cover the pot if you want to limit splatter, stirring occasionally so nothing settles on the bottom.
I'm making Chocolate Covered Banana Pie and want to get the crust going without missing anything. Can you guide me?
Absolutely. Put a 9 x 13 inch pan nearby and gather 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers, 1/2 cup chopped pecans, 2/3 cup melted butter, and 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips.
Before I continue with Chocolate Covered Banana Pie, the wafers are crushed and the pecans are chopped. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), so it's ready when the crust is pressed into the pan.
The butter is melted. Do I mix everything together now, including the chocolate chips?

For this part, combine the crushed cookie crumbs, chopped pecans, and melted butter or margarine. Keep the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips measured and ready for the recipe, but they are not part of this crust-mixing step.
The crumb mixture looks evenly damp and a little nutty. How firmly should I pack it?
Press it evenly into the 9 x 13 inch pan, using the bottom of a measuring cup or your fingers to make a compact, level layer.
It's spread across the pan, but the corners are a little loose. Is that okay before baking?
Give the corners a little extra pressure so the crust holds together, then place the pan in the preheated oven.
The pan is in. How long should I set the timer for?
In this Chocolate Covered Banana Pie step, bake it at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, for 5 minutes.
Before I continue with Chocolate Covered Banana Pie, the timer just went off and the crust smells toasted. What should I do with it now?
Take the pan out carefully and let the crust cool completely before adding anything else or continuing with the pie.
I want to make Argentine Chimichurri Bread in my bread machine. Can you talk me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Put the bread machine pan on the counter, and measure the liquids first: 1 cup water, 1 1/2 tablespoons white wine vinegar, and 3 tablespoons olive oil.
Those are measured. The vinegar smells pretty sharp—does it all go in?
Yes, use the full 1 1/2 tablespoons white wine vinegar. It goes into the bread machine pan along with the water and olive oil, following the order your machine's manufacturer recommends.
I also see cayenne on the list. How much should I add?
Add 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper. It's a small amount, so level it off rather than heaping it.
My machine booklet says liquids first, then dry ingredients. Should I pour these in that way?

Yes. Since your booklet recommends liquids first, add the 1 cup water, 1 1/2 tablespoons white wine vinegar, and 3 tablespoons olive oil to the pan before the remaining ingredients, then include the 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper in the order your machine calls for.
The pan is loaded. Do I need to stir anything before it goes into the machine?
No stirring is needed unless your bread machine manual specifically asks for it. Set the pan into the machine securely so it can mix during the cycle.
Which program should I choose on the control panel?
Select the Basic or White Cycle, whichever name your machine uses for its standard white bread setting.
Okay, Basic is selected. Anything else before I start it?
Make sure the pan is locked in place and the lid is closed, then press Start. From there, let the bread machine run the cycle.
I'm making Carrots and Onions Au Gratin and I've got a baking dish ready. Can you help me get organized?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (16 ounce) package of sliced baby carrots and 2 medium sliced onions for the vegetables.
The carrots are sliced and the onions are cut. What else should I pull from the fridge?
You'll also need 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter.
Got it. Should I turn the oven on before I start boiling anything?
Start Carrots and Onions Au Gratin by heating the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. I'm at the stove with a pot—how much water should go in?
Put the sliced carrots and onions in the pot, then add enough lightly salted water to cover them.
They're covered with salted water. Do I just bring it up to a boil now?
Yes. Bring the pot to a boil with the carrots and onions in the lightly salted water.
It's boiling. I don't want the carrots mushy—how long should they cook?
For this batch of Carrots and Onions Au Gratin, cook them for 5 minutes, just until the vegetables are tender but still firm.
They feel tender but not soft. What do I do before the cheese and butter come in?
Drain the carrots and onions well, then spread 1/2 of the drained mixture into your baking dish.

messages.content: I'm making Chicken Stuffed Buns tonight, and I've got the sourdough buns and cooked chicken out. Can you help me get organized before I start cutting anything?

Use the oven or a sheet pan for the stuffed buns, with a quick broiler touch only if you want extra browning, then let them sit uncovered briefly before serving. Set your oven to preheat at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and make sure you have 6 large sourdough buns and 2 cups cooked, diced boneless chicken breast ready.
The oven is heating, and the chicken is already diced. What should I pull from the fridge next?

Grab 1 (8 ounce) package of softened cream cheese and 1 cup shredded Pepper Jack cheese. If your cream cheese is still cool, cube it and let it sit out for a few minutes so it mixes more smoothly with the chicken.
Cream cheese is soft enough, and the Pepper Jack is measured. Do I need to prep the buns now or mix the filling first?
Prep the buns now so they're ready to fill. Slice the top off each sourdough bun, keep those tops nearby, and try to make the cuts level so they sit back on neatly.
I like that sheet-pan and uncovered-rest approach for these buns; that works better for this dish. The tops are off—how much bread should I take out?
Hollow out each bun, leaving a sturdy shell instead of scraping it paper-thin. Keep enough bread around the sides and bottom to hold the creamy chicken filling without collapsing.
The shells look sturdy, but I have a pile of bread pieces from the centers. Should I save them?
Yes, set them aside for now. They can help steady the buns on the pan, or you can use a little as a soft crumb topping if you want texture, but the main recipe just needs the hollowed shells.
Buns are hollowed and lined up on the pan. How do I make the filling?

In a medium bowl, combine the diced chicken, softened cream cheese, shredded Pepper Jack cheese, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and spinach. Stir until the cream cheese coats the chicken evenly and the greens and cheeses are spread through the mixture.
It's mixing, but the cream cheese is a little streaky. Should I keep working it?

Keep folding and pressing the mixture against the side of the bowl until it looks creamy rather than clumpy. If the bowl feels cold, let it stand briefly, then stir again so the filling becomes easier to spread.
The filling looks creamy now. What's the best way to assemble without making a mess?

Spoon the chicken mixture into the hollowed buns, keeping the filling level with the top so the saved lids can sit back on. Arrange them on the sheet pan, bake in the 350 degrees F oven until heated through, and let the buns rest uncovered briefly before serving.
I'm making Dutch Cream Waffles and want to set up before I start mixing. What should I put out?

Set out 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, 3 separated egg yolks, and 3 separated egg whites. You'll also need a large mixing bowl for the dry ingredients and a small mixing bowl for the yolks.
The yolks and whites are separated. Should the flour and salt go together before I touch the eggs?
Yes. In the large mixing bowl, combine the flour and salt so they're evenly distributed before the wet mixture goes in.
Done. For the yolks, do I beat them first or start adding cream right away?
Put the egg yolks in the small mixing bowl, start beating them on low speed, and add the cream while the mixer is running.
I'm adding the cream on low now. How long should that mixture be beaten?
Keep beating it for 1 minute. It should look more blended and a little smoother by the end.
The yolk and cream mixture is blended. Does it go into the flour bowl all at once?
Yes, add the yolk-and-cream mixture to the flour and salt mixture in the large bowl.
Once it's in there, should I keep the mixer low so flour doesn't fly everywhere?
Exactly. Combine it on low speed at first, just until the dry ingredients start to moisten.
It's mostly incorporated but still a little uneven. What texture am I aiming for before I stop?
Increase to medium-high and beat until the batter is smooth, with no obvious dry streaks or lumps from the flour mixture.
I want to make Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes. Can you talk me through it while I get set up?

Absolutely. Pull out 1 1/2 pounds of new potatoes and cut them into wedges if they aren't already prepped. You'll also need 4 tablespoons butter, 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, plus salt and pepper to taste.
The potatoes are washed and wedged. Should I turn the oven on before I start with the butter?
Yes, set the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C), so it's hot by the time the potatoes are coated.
Oven is heating. I've got a skillet on the stove—how hot should it be for the butter?
Use a hot skillet, then add the 4 tablespoons butter and let it melt. Keep an eye on it so it melts smoothly rather than browning too far.
The butter is melted and bubbling a little. Do I add the rosemary straight into the skillet?
Yes. Stir in the 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, then season with salt and pepper to taste right in the melted butter.
It smells good. Should the potato wedges go into the skillet or should I pour the butter over them?
Either approach works as long as the wedges get coated evenly. Add the potatoes to the skillet if there's room, or put them in a bowl and pour the rosemary butter over them.
I'm using a bowl so I don't crowd the skillet. What texture am I looking for on the potatoes before they go further?
They should look evenly slicked with the melted butter, with rosemary, salt, and pepper distributed across the cut sides and skins.
They're coated now. Any quick check before I move them to my baking pan?
Give the bowl one more toss so no wedges are sitting dry, then spread the potatoes out evenly in the pan while the oven finishes reaching 450 degrees F, or 230 degrees C.
