Perfect, that fits what I'm doing. I've got the wraps ready; what should I prep first for the chicken?
Cut 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite-size pieces, and measure out 1 cup of lemonade.
Chicken is cut and the lemonade is measured. Which liquids go by the stove with it?
Put 2 tablespoons olive oil and 1 tablespoon lime juice next to the skillet. You'll also need Worcestershire sauce for the pan.
I have a large skillet out. What heat should I use before adding everything?
Set the large skillet over medium heat, then add the chicken, lemonade, olive oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce together.
On Chicken Tacos, everything is in the skillet and starting to bubble lightly. What seasonings go in?
Season the mixture with garlic powder, onion powder, and a bay leaf, stirring so the flavor reaches all the chicken pieces.
The seasonings are mixed in. How long should I let the chicken cook?
Let it simmer until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear, about 15 to 20 minutes.
While that simmers, should I do anything with the tortillas for the wraps?
Yes, warm the tortillas in the oven or microwave until they're soft and flexible.
The tortillas are soft and the chicken looks cooked through. How should I assemble these with the sauce?
Spread that thick creamy sauce in a thin layer on each tortilla, spoon in the chicken, remove the bay leaf if it's still in the pan, and roll the wraps while they're warm.
I'm making Apple Pie 2 today. Can you talk me through what I need and when to start heating it?
Absolutely. Set out a large pot, 1 gallon apple juice, 1 gallon apple cider, 3 cups white sugar, and 8 cinnamon sticks.
The pot is ready, and I have the juice and cider measured. Do the sugar and cinnamon go in right away?
Yes. Pour the apple juice and apple cider into the large pot, then add the white sugar and cinnamon sticks so everything heats together.
It's all in the pot. Should I stir before turning on the burner?
Give it a good stir to start dissolving the sugar, then turn on the heat and bring the mixture to a boil.
It's heating now, and the cinnamon sticks are floating. Am I looking for a full boil or just steam?
Bring it to a boil, not just steam. Once it reaches that boil, remove the pot from the heat.
It boiled, and I moved it off the burner. Do I strain the cinnamon sticks now?
The recipe doesn't call for straining at this point. Let the juice mixture cool completely before adding anything else.
Cooling is taking a while. Is it important that it be completely cool before the next ingredient?
Yes, wait until the juice mixture is completely cool. Then stir in the grain alcohol.
It's cool now. I stirred in the grain alcohol gently—anything else for this recipe?
That completes the listed steps for Apple Pie 2. Make sure everything is well mixed, then you can portion or store it as needed.
I'm making Bocconcini Salad for right away—can you talk me through the prep so I don't miss anything?
Absolutely. Set out 1 pound bocconcini, the bite-size mozzarella balls, plus 8 cherry tomatoes. Halve the tomatoes if they aren't already cut.
Mozzarella is drained and the tomatoes are halved. What other vegetables should I chop before I grab the bowl?
Chop 1/2 cup green bell pepper and 1/2 cup celery. You'll also want the endive and arugula ready for the salad bowl.
I've got a large salad bowl out. Should the mozzarella go in whole, or should I cut it smaller?
If the bocconcini are already bite-size, leave them whole. Add them to the large salad bowl with the halved cherry tomatoes, chopped bell pepper, chopped celery, endive, and arugula.
Everything is in the bowl, but it looks pretty delicate. How should I make the dressing?
In a small bowl, whisk the lemon juice and olive oil together until they look blended. Pour that over the salad, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Dressing is on. I'm worried about smashing the cheese and tomatoes—what's the best way to toss it?
Use two large spoons or salad servers and lift from the bottom, turning the ingredients gently until everything is thoroughly coated with the dressing.
It's coated now. Should I let it sit for a few minutes, or is this one better served fresh?
This salad is meant to be served immediately, so don't let it sit long once dressed.
Got it. What's the last touch before I bring it to the table?
Sprinkle the basil over the top, give the bowl a final light check for salt and pepper, and serve the Bocconcini Salad immediately.
I'm making Chocolate Covered Banana Pie and want to get the crust started correctly. Can you talk me through the ingredients and pan setup?

Absolutely. Set out 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers, 1/2 cup chopped pecans, 2/3 cup melted butter, and 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips. You'll also need a 9 x 13 inch pan for pressing the crumb mixture into.
The wafers are crushed, but I'm not sure how fine they should be before I mix them.
Aim for small, even crumbs so they pack together well, but they don't need to be powdery. Once they're ready, put the crushed cookie crumbs in a bowl with the chopped pecans.
Got it. The pecans are chopped and in the bowl with the crumbs. Does the butter go in all at once?
Yes, pour in the 2/3 cup melted butter all at once, then stir until the crumbs and pecans are evenly coated and the mixture looks like damp sand.
The crumb mixture is holding together when I press it. Should I grease the pan first?
The recipe just has you press the mixture into the 9 x 13 inch pan. Spread it across the bottom, then press firmly so the crust is even from corner to corner.
I've packed it into the pan. Should the oven be at 375 degrees F now?
Yes. Bake the crust at 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, for 5 minutes.
It's in the oven. What should I watch for during those 5 minutes?
Since it's a short bake, look for the crust to set lightly and smell toasty. It doesn't need to get dark; pull it out when the 5 minutes are up.
The crust is out and smells toasted. Do the chocolate chips go on while it's hot?
For the instructions here, let the baked crust cool. Keep the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips ready for the next part of the pie once the crust is no longer hot.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Slice the raw vegetables into slender, lengthwise sticks, then set them on the plate in separate color groups.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: For today, I'm serving Fig Bars II on a snack plate with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish alongside it. What's the best way to cut and arrange those vegetables?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Cut the raw vegetables into long thin sticks and group them by color.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Fig Bars II as an assembled snack plate with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish. How should I cut and place the raw vegetables?

messages.content: For today, I'm serving Fig Bars II on a snack plate with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish alongside it. What's the best way to cut and arrange those vegetables?
Slice the raw vegetables into slender, lengthwise sticks, then set them on the plate in separate color groups.
Great, I'll plate the vegetables that way. For the bars themselves, what should I pull out before I start mixing?
Set out 1 cup white sugar and 3 eggs, since those get beaten together until the mixture turns thick and pale.
Sugar and eggs are ready. What dry ingredients do I need measured?
Measure 7/8 cup all-purpose flour and 1 teaspoon baking powder. You'll sift those with the salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice before they go into the egg mixture.
I've got the flour and baking powder measured. Should I deal with the oven before the pan?
Yes—set the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), then you can prepare the pan while it heats.
The oven is warming. I'm using a rectangular pan; what size and prep should it get?
Use a 9x13 inch baking pan, and grease and flour it so the bars release cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. How should the eggs and sugar look before I stop beating?
Beat the 3 eggs with the 1 cup white sugar in a large bowl until the mixture is noticeably thick and pale, not just lightly combined.
That mixture is pale now. How do I add the dry ingredients without making it lumpy?
Sift together the flour, baking powder, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice, then blend that into the egg mixture along with the vanilla.
Once the batter is combined, how should I keep the snack plate tidy while the bars bake?
Keep the cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish sticks grouped by color on the serving plate, and leave space for the Fig Bars II so the vegetables stay neat and separate.
I'd like to make a Cold Cocoa Smoothie. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start blending?
Absolutely. Put your blender on the counter and get 1 1/2 scoops vanilla ice cream and 1 1/2 cups milk ready first so the base can go straight in.
The blender is out, and I've measured the ice cream and milk. What should I grab for the chocolate part?
You'll need 2 tablespoons instant hot chocolate mix. Also set out 1/4 cup whipped cream, since that goes into the blender too.
Got it. The recipe mentions crushed cookies as well—do they go in with everything else?
Yes. Add the ice cream, milk, whipped cream, instant hot chocolate mix, and the crushed cookies to the blender together.
Everything is in the blender. Should I pulse it or just let it run?
Blend it until the mixture looks smooth, with no big streaks of hot chocolate mix or chunks of ice cream left.
It's blending now. The sides have a little cocoa stuck to them—should I stop and scrape?
If you see dry mix clinging to the sides, stop the blender, scrape it down, then blend again briefly until the smoothie is even and creamy.
The texture looks smooth and cold. What kind of glass should I use?
Use a large chilled glass if you have one. Pour the smoothie in right away so it stays thick and frosty.
It's poured into the chilled glass. Anything else before I serve it?
That's all the recipe calls for. Serve the Cold Cocoa Smoothie immediately while it's still cold and smooth.
I'm making California Chicken with 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts. Can you guide me from the prep stage?
Absolutely. Set out the chicken breasts, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, a pinch of salt, and some pepper for seasoning at the end.
Everything is out. Do I need the oven for this, or just a skillet?
Have both ready: heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and place a skillet on the stove for browning the chicken.
The oven is heating. How should I start the chicken in the pan?
Warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in the skillet, then add the chicken breasts. Sprinkle in the 1/2 teaspoon onion powder as the chicken starts cooking.
The chicken is in the skillet and the onion powder is on it. Should I move it around a lot?
Let it sit long enough to brown before turning. Cook it for about 15 minutes total, turning as needed, until the outside is browned and the chicken is just about done.
It's browning, but I want to be sure I'm not overcooking it. What texture am I looking for?
You want the chicken firming up and browned on the surface, but not dried out. Since the recipe says just about done after 15 minutes, keep an eye on the thickest pieces.
The pieces look browned now. What seasoning goes on before I serve it?
Add the pinch of salt, then season with pepper to taste. Keep it light at first, since you can always add a little more at the table.
Should I let it rest, or plate it right away?
Let it rest briefly after seasoning so the juices settle, then plate the California Chicken while it's still hot.
I pulled up Fresh Apple Salsa. Can you guide the first few moves? I've got a cutting board out and want to prep it in the right order.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tart apples, 4 tablespoons lime juice, 1 fresh jalapeno pepper, and 1 fresh Anaheim chile. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready so the apples can go straight into lime juice after cutting.
The apples are cored and cubed. Should I add them to the bowl before slicing the peppers?
For this batch of Fresh Apple Salsa, put the cubed apples in the large bowl and stir them with the lime juice right away so they're well coated.
They're glossy with lime now. For the jalapeno, do I leave the seeds in?
Seed the fresh jalapeno, then slice it. Do the same with the fresh Anaheim chile: seed it and slice it before adding either one.
Both peppers are seeded and sliced. Do they go in together, or should I add one at a time?
You can add them together. Stir the jalapeno and Anaheim chile slices into the apple-lime mixture until they're evenly scattered through the bowl.
The peppers are mixed in. The recipe also mentions onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt—do those all go in now?
Yes, stir in the onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt at this point. Fold everything through so the herbs, nuts, and seasoning don't clump in one spot.
It smells fresh, but the walnuts are sitting near the top. Should I keep stirring or be gentle with the apples?
Use a gentle but thorough mixing motion, scooping from the bottom and turning the salsa over until the walnuts and seasonings are distributed without mashing the apple cubes.
Looks evenly mixed now. Is there anything else before I serve it?

That's it for the recipe: once everything is mixed thoroughly, the Fresh Apple Salsa is ready to serve. Give the bowl a quick scrape around the sides so every bite gets apple, lime, chile, and the added mix-ins.
I'm ready to cook Apple Cranberry Crisp 2. What should be ready before I begin? I've got an 8 inch square baking dish ready but haven't started prepping yet.
Absolutely. Start by getting 2 pounds of Granny Smith apples peeled, cored, and thinly sliced. You'll also need 3/4 cup cranberries for the fruit mixture.
The apples are sliced and the cranberries are measured. What should I pull out for the seasoning?
Measure 1/4 cup white sugar and 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon. The fruit mixture also gets nutmeg, so keep that nearby too.
Should I heat the oven before I mix the fruit?
Yes. get the oven warming to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), and butter the 8 inch square baking dish so the crisp is ready to assemble.
The oven is heating and the dish is buttered. Do I combine everything in one bowl?
Use a large bowl for the apples and cranberries. Add the white sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg, then toss until the fruit is evenly coated.
The apples look coated, but there's a little sugar at the bottom of the bowl. Is that okay?
That's fine. Give it one more gentle toss so the loose sugar and spice catch on the apple slices, then transfer the fruit into the prepared baking dish.
Should I press the fruit down or leave it loose in the dish?
Spread it evenly into the baking dish. A light leveling is enough; don't pack it down hard, since the fruit should bake into an even layer.
The fruit is in the dish. What do I do with the bowl now?
Use that same bowl for the topping mixture: combine the oats, flour, and brown sugar. Once mixed, it will be ready to go over the fruit.
I'm making Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup today. Can you talk me through it while I get the slow cooker ready?
Absolutely. Set out the slow cooker, then start with 1 1/2 pounds of cubed beef stew meat, 2 cups of water, 1 small chopped onion, and a 28 ounce can of crushed tomatoes.
The slow cooker is on the counter, and I have the beef and water measured. Should the meat go in by itself?
Yes, place the cubed beef stew meat directly into the slow cooker as the base of the soup.
The beef is in. Do I pour the water around it or over the top?
Pour the 2 cups of water right over the beef so it settles into the bottom of the slow cooker.
Done. I've got the chopped onion and the crushed tomatoes open beside me.
Stir in the chopped onion and the 28 ounce can of crushed tomatoes. Add the mixed vegetables and potatoes at this point too, so everything is combined before seasoning.
The vegetables and potatoes are mixed in, but the slow cooker is getting pretty full. Should I stir more?
Give it a gentle stir just until the onion, tomatoes, mixed vegetables, and potatoes are evenly distributed around the beef. No need to overwork it.
It looks evenly mixed now. What seasonings go in before I put the lid on?
Season the soup with bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil, sprinkling them over the top and stirring lightly so they blend into the liquid.
All seasoned. Is there anything else to check before it starts cooking?

Make sure the beef is in the slow cooker with the water, onion, crushed tomatoes, mixed vegetables, potatoes, bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil all added. Once it's covered, you're ready to let the slow cooker do the rest.

source_seed.recipe_title: Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Go with the oven approach for this batch: use the 2 trays, rotate them once during baking, and don't add a final rest.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Armadillo Eggs, I'm doing it as a special two-tray setup and I can use the stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan approach. Which way should I go tonight?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use the oven route, rotate the trays once, and skip the final rest.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Armadillo Eggs as a two-tray recipe with stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan routes. Which route should I take?

messages.content: For this batch of Armadillo Eggs, I'm doing it as a special two-tray setup and I can use the stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan approach. Which way should I go tonight?
Go with the oven approach for this batch: use the 2 trays, rotate them once during baking, and don't add a final rest.
Perfect, that's the version I need just for this cook. I've cleared counter space—what ingredients should I pull first?
Start with the main items: 24 jalapeno peppers and 1 pound sausage. Keep a bowl nearby for the pepper seeds and pulp.
The peppers are washed and the sausage is out. What else needs to be ready before my hands get messy?
Set out 2 cups all-purpose baking mix and 1 (16 ounce) package shredded Cheddar cheese. Those should be within reach once you start assembling.
I've got the baking mix and Cheddar next to the peppers. Should I heat the oven now or prep the trays first?
Heat the oven now to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C, so it can come up to temperature while you work on the peppers.
Oven is heating. Since I'm using 2 trays, how should I handle the pans?
Lightly grease the baking sheets so the Armadillo Eggs release cleanly. Since you're splitting them across 2 trays, coat both surfaces evenly.
Trays are greased. I'm about to cut the jalapenos—what kind of cut am I making?
Cut a slit lengthwise in each jalapeno pepper. Try not to slice them completely in half; you just want an opening for cleaning and filling.
Some of the peppers are pretty hot-smelling already. What should I remove from inside?
Remove and discard the seeds and pulp from each pepper. A small spoon or the tip of a knife works well, and gloves are helpful with 24 jalapenos.
The peppers are cleaned out, and I'll keep the trays separate. Anything special to remember when they go in?
Yes—keep the oven route you chose for this batch: spread them across the 2 trays, rotate the trays once so they cook evenly, and skip the final rest when they come out.
I'm making Caramel Shortbread Squares and want to keep it simple. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour for the shortbread mixture.
I've got those measured. The recipe also lists another butter amount—does that need to be out too?
Yes, have the 1/2 cup butter on the counter as well, even though the baked base step uses the softened 2/3 cup butter with the sugar and flour.
What pan and oven setup should I use before I start mixing?
Use a 9 inch square baking pan, and set the oven to 350 degrees F (176 degrees C).
The oven is heating and the pan is nearby. What texture am I aiming for in the bowl?
In a medium bowl, mix the 2/3 cup softened butter with the 1/4 cup white sugar and 1 1/4 cups flour until the mixture looks evenly crumbly, not like a smooth batter.
It's crumbly now, with no big dry patches. Do I need to grease the pan or just press it in?
The recipe's next direction is simply to press the crumbly mixture into the 9 inch square baking pan. Pat it into an even layer so the squares bake uniformly.
It's pressed in, but the corners are a little thinner than the middle. Should I fix that?
Yes, gently nudge some of the thicker center mixture toward the corners and edges so the layer is level across the pan.
That looks more even. How long should it bake?
Bake it at 350 degrees F for 20 minutes. After that, let the pan cool enough to handle before cutting the shortbread into squares.
I'm making Delicious Artichoke Dip and want to keep it moving. What should I pull out before I start mixing?

Set out 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 (14 ounce) can of artichoke hearts, drained. You'll also want a medium mixing bowl and a shallow baking dish nearby.
The mayo, sour cream, Parmesan, and drained artichokes are on the counter. Should the oven be on before I combine anything?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the dip is ready to bake.
Oven is heating. For the bowl, do I add the artichokes right away or start with the creamy ingredients?
Start with the creamy base: in the medium-sized mixing bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, Parmesan cheese, and onion until they're evenly combined.
I've got that mixed. It looks thick and cheesy; is that the texture I want before adding the artichokes?
Yes, thick and cohesive is right. Once those ingredients are combined, mix in the artichoke hearts along with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Should I chop the artichoke hearts smaller, or just fold them in from the drained can?
The recipe only says to use the drained artichoke hearts, so you can fold them in as they are. Stir gently enough to spread them through the dip without turning the mixture soupy.
Everything is mixed now. What dish should I use so it bakes evenly?
Transfer the mixture into a shallow baking dish and spread it into an even layer. That gives the dip more surface area and helps it heat through consistently.
It's in the shallow dish. Anything I should check before it goes into the oven?

Make sure the oven has reached 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, and that the dip is spread fairly evenly in the dish. Then it's ready to bake according to the recipe's next timing or doneness guidance.
I'm making Garden Potato Salad and already have the potatoes cooked. Can you guide me through the prep without getting ahead of me?
Absolutely. Start by getting the salad components ready: 6 large potatoes, cooked, peeled, and cubed, plus 4 hard-cooked eggs sliced.
The potatoes are cubed and the eggs are sliced. What vegetables should I slice before mixing?
Slice 2 celery ribs and 6 green onions with their tops. You'll also want the radishes ready, along with salt and pepper for seasoning the bowl.
I've got a large mixing bowl out. Do the potatoes and eggs go in before the celery and onions?

Yes. Add the potatoes and sliced eggs to the large bowl, then add the celery, green onions, radishes, salt, and pepper. Gently combine everything so the potatoes don't break down too much, then set the bowl aside.
The salad mixture is together. What pan should I use for the dressing?
Use a saucepan for the dressing. In it, combine eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt before you turn on the heat.
The dressing ingredients are in the saucepan. What heat level am I aiming for?
Set the saucepan over medium heat. Cook and stir the mixture steadily until it thickens.
How will I know it has thickened enough?
It should look more cohesive and cling lightly as you stir rather than staying thin and watery. Once it reaches that thickened stage, take it off the heat.
It's off the heat now. Do I pour it on the potatoes while it's hot?
Let the dressing cool first. Once cooled, it's ready to use with the prepared potato mixture.
Buttermilk Shake is the recipe for today. Can you talk me through it from the top? I've got the blender out but haven't measured anything yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pint vanilla ice cream, 1 cup buttermilk, 1 teaspoon grated lemon peel, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The ice cream is still firm. Should I wait for it to soften before it goes in the blender?
Let it sit just a few minutes if it's rock-hard, but don't let it melt. It only needs to be scoopable enough for the blender to handle.
Okay, I measured the buttermilk and grated the lemon peel. Does everything go in at once?
Yes. Put the vanilla ice cream, buttermilk, grated lemon peel, and vanilla extract all into the blender container together.
I'm adding them now. Should the lid be tight before I start?
Definitely cover the blender securely before turning it on, since the mixture will move quickly once it starts blending.
Lid is on. What setting should I use, and what texture am I watching for?
Process it on high until the shake looks smooth, with no visible lumps of ice cream and the lemon peel evenly mixed through.
It looks smooth after blending. Do I need to stir it or strain it?
No straining is needed. If it looks even and pourable, you can pour it straight into glasses.
I have the glasses ready. Any serving tip before I pour?
Pour the Buttermilk Shake into the glasses right away while it's cold and thick, then serve immediately.
Before I get moving on Gelatin Fruit Salad, what should I have ready? I've got a saucepan out but haven't opened anything yet.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple. Keep the pineapple undrained, since the juice goes in too.
I measured the applesauce and the gelatin packets are ready. Should the soda be cold or does it matter?
Cold is fine. Just have it opened and nearby, because you'll add it slowly after the hot applesauce has dissolved the gelatin.
The pineapple can is open, and I left the juice in. What do I do with the applesauce?
Pour the 1 cup applesauce into the saucepan and heat it until it comes to a boil. Stir now and then so it heats evenly and doesn't stick.
It's bubbling around the edges and starting to boil. Do I keep it on the burner while adding the gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat first. Then stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin until the mixture looks smooth and the granules are dissolved.
The gelatin is dissolved; it's glossy and there aren't any grains on the spoon. How slowly should I add the soda?
Pour in the 12 ounce can of lemon-lime soda gradually, stirring gently as you go. It may foam a bit, so slow pouring helps keep it under control.
The soda is mixed in without overflowing. Does the crushed pineapple go in right away?
Yes, stir in the 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple, including all the juice. Mix just enough to distribute the fruit through the gelatin mixture.
It's all combined. Should I use one bowl or smaller dishes for chilling?
Either works. Pour it into a serving bowl or individual dishes, then refrigerate until firm. Once it's set, it's ready to serve chilled.
I'm making Fiery Fish Tacos with Crunchy Corn Salsa. Can you walk me through the prep while I get the grill ready?
Absolutely. Set the grill to preheat on high heat, then start gathering the salsa ingredients: 1 cup corn and 1/2 cup diced red onion.
The grill is heating, and I've got the corn and onion measured. What should I chop next for the salsa?
Add 1 cup peeled, chopped jicama to your board, then dice 1/2 cup red bell pepper. Those will give the salsa its crunch and color.
Jicama is chopped and the red bell pepper is diced. What bowl should I use?
Use a medium bowl. Put in the corn, red onion, jicama, red bell pepper, and cilantro, then toss them together so everything is evenly mixed.
The salsa mix is in the bowl. It looks dry right now—what brings it together?
Stir in the lime juice and lime zest. Fold it through gently so the zest spreads around instead of clumping in one spot.
Done. Should I season the salsa now or make the spice mix separately?
Make the spice mix separately in a small bowl: combine cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt.
I've got the cayenne, black pepper, and salt together. Should the grill still be on high?
Yes, keep the grill preheated for high heat while you finish organizing the salsa and seasoning. That way it's ready when the fish goes on.
The salsa is mixed and the seasoning bowl is ready. Anything I should check before I start grilling the fish?
Give the salsa one more gentle toss and check that the lime zest is distributed. Keep the seasoning nearby, and make sure the grill is fully hot before you cook the fish for the tacos.

source_seed.recipe_title: Fiery Fish Tacos with Crunchy Corn Salsa

messages.content: I'm making Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic. Can you guide me while I get the seasoning paste started?
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup olive oil, 8 cloves garlic minced, 2 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper. You'll also be mixing in cumin and oregano for the paste.
The oil and minced garlic are in a bowl, and I've measured the salt and pepper. Do I just stir everything together?
Yes. Mix the olive oil, garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano until it becomes a spreadable paste rather than a loose puddle.
The paste looks thick and garlicky. Should I coat only the top of the lamb?
Coat both sides of the butterflied leg of lamb. Spread the paste evenly so the surface is covered, including the cut side and the outer side.
Both sides are coated. It's still cold from the fridge—how long should it sit?
Let it stand for 1 hour, until the meat comes to room temperature. Keep it arranged so the paste stays on the lamb rather than pooling underneath.
The hour is nearly up. Which oven rack should I use for broiling?
Move the rack to the upper or upper-middle position, depending on the lamb's thickness. Then preheat the broiler on high for at least 10 minutes so it's fully hot.
The broiler is heating. What pan setup do I need so cleanup isn't awful?
Line a roasting pan with foil, then set a large wire rack over it. Place the lamb on the rack cut side up so the heat can brown the exposed surface.
The lamb is on the rack cut side up, and the broiler is hot. How do I manage the browning?
Broil it for about 8 minutes, moving the pan as needed so the entire surface browns evenly. Watch closely because the garlic paste can darken quickly under high heat.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic

messages.content: I'm making Adriennes Tom Ka Gai and I'd like you to walk me through it while I prep the saucepan.
Absolutely. Set a large saucepan on the stove, and gather 2 teaspoons peanut oil plus 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced.
The saucepan is out, and I've sliced the garlic. What aromatics should I prep before turning on the heat?
Grate 2 tablespoons fresh ginger root and chop 1/4 cup lemon grass. Keep the red pepper, coriander, and cumin close by too, since they'll go in with those aromatics.
The ginger and lemon grass are ready. Should the oil go in cold, or do I heat the pan first?
Put the 2 teaspoons peanut oil into the large saucepan and warm it over medium heat.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do I add everything aromatic at once?
Yes—stir in the garlic, ginger, lemon grass, red pepper, coriander, and cumin. Cook them together until fragrant, about 2 minutes, stirring so the garlic doesn't catch.
It smells strong and the garlic is just starting to soften. What texture am I looking for before adding the chicken?
Once the aromatics smell fragrant and look softened, stir in the chicken and onion. Keep stirring and cook until the chicken turns white and the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
The chicken is white on the outside and the onion looks translucent. The pan is a bit crowded—can I add the bok choy now?
Go ahead and stir in the bok choy. Let it cook until it begins to wilt, which should take 5 to 10 minutes depending on how full the pan is.
The bok choy has softened but still has some shape. Is that where I should stop cooking?
Yes, that matches the recipe: stop once the bok choy begins to wilt. Give everything a final stir so the chicken, onion, and aromatics are evenly mixed, then serve it hot.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Cut the browned pieces a little finer, then fold the darker bits evenly through the filling so they add crunch and flavor without clumping.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For these Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches, I'm turning them into a filling with some seared and roasted add-ins—potato, tofu, vegetables, that kind of skillet-browned stuff. For this batch only, how should I handle the dark edges?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Chop the browned pieces smaller and mix the darker bits through the filling.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches as a sandwich filling with pan-seared, roasted, baked, potato, tofu, vegetable, or skillet components. How should I manage the browning?

messages.content: For these Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches, I'm turning them into a filling with some seared and roasted add-ins—potato, tofu, vegetables, that kind of skillet-browned stuff. For this batch only, how should I handle the dark edges?
Cut the browned pieces a little finer, then fold the darker bits evenly through the filling so they add crunch and flavor without clumping.
Great, that's the direction I want tonight. I've got a knife, bowl, and sheet pan out—what should I prep first?
Start with the vegetables: finely chop 1 small onion, dice 1 medium tomato, chop 1 stalk celery, and finely chop 1 green bell pepper.
The onion and bell pepper are going to be pretty small. Should the tomato stay chunkier so the filling isn't watery?
Yes, dice the tomato rather than mincing it. If it's very juicy, leave the excess liquid on the cutting board so the mixture stays spreadable.
Vegetables are cut, and I've got the browned add-ins chopped smaller too. Do I heat the oven now or mix first?
Turn on the broiler now so it's hot by the time the sandwiches are assembled.
Broiler is heating. I'm using a medium bowl—what goes into it?
Add the onion, tomato, celery, green bell pepper, cheese, chili powder, and salt to the bowl, along with those finely chopped browned bits.
I'm stirring it now. What texture am I aiming for before it hits the bread?
Aim for a cohesive, scoopable mixture with the cheese and vegetables evenly distributed all the way through.
The filling looks even. Should the bread go straight on the sheet pan, or do I need something under it?
Arrange the bread slices in a single layer on a baking sheet or broiling pan, leaving a little space so the edges can crisp.
Bread is laid out. How much filling should I put on each slice?
Spoon 1/4 of the mixture onto each slice, spreading it right out to the edges so every sandwich broils evenly.
I'm making Chicken Vegetable Stew and have a large pot ready. Can you guide me as I prep?
Absolutely. Set out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into bite-size pieces, plus 1 chopped onion. Those can go near the pot since they'll be added right away.
The chicken is cut up and the onion is chopped. What vegetables should I wash or peel?
You'll need 1/2 pound baby carrots and 4 potatoes. Rinse the carrots, and scrub or peel the potatoes depending on how you like them in stew.
I scrubbed the potatoes. Should I cut them before they go in?
Yes, cut the potatoes into stew-sized chunks so they cook evenly with the chicken and carrots.
Everything is chopped and sitting by the stove. What goes into the pot first?
Put the chopped onion, bite-size chicken breast pieces, baby carrots, and potato chunks into the large pot together.
They're all in the pot. I see salt and turmeric in the recipe—do I add both now?
Yes, sprinkle in the salt and turmeric over the chicken and vegetables, then give everything a light stir so the seasoning starts to coat the ingredients.
Done. I've got tomato paste here too; how do I add it without clumps?
For this batch of Chicken Vegetable Stew, dissolve the tomato paste in water first, stirring until it loosens into a smooth mixture, then pour that into the pot.
The tomato mixture is in. Is there anything optional I can add before it cooks?
If you'd like a little more seasoning, add garlic powder and ground black pepper to taste, then stir the stew so the seasonings are distributed.
I'm making German Sweet Chocolate Pie and have the chocolate bar out. Can you guide me through it while I set up?

Absolutely. Chop 1 (4 ounce) bar of German sweet chocolate, and get a large microwave-safe bowl ready. You'll also need 1/3 cup milk, but only 2 tablespoons of it go in with the chocolate at the beginning.
The bowl is ready. Should the cream cheese be out now too?
Yes, set out 4 ounces cream cheese so it's softened, plus 2 tablespoons white sugar. Softened cream cheese will whisk in much more smoothly once the chocolate is melted.
I've got the sugar measured and the cream cheese feels soft. How do I melt the chocolate without scorching it?

Put the chopped German sweet chocolate in the large microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of the milk. Microwave on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stopping halfway through to stir. You're looking for the chocolate to be almost melted, not boiling hot.
It still has a few soft-looking pieces after stirring. Is that okay?

That's fine. Stir it well so the residual heat melts those last bits. Once it looks mostly smooth, you can whisk in the softened cream cheese, the 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk from the 1/3 cup.
When I whisk those in, what texture am I aiming for?
Whisk until the mixture is blended and even, with no obvious cream cheese lumps or dry sugar pockets. It should look like a smooth chocolate mixture before it chills.
The mixture is smooth now. Do I chill the bowl before adding the topping?
Yes. Refrigerate the chocolate mixture for 10 minutes. That short chill helps it firm slightly so the whipped topping folds in without turning runny.
The 10 minutes are up, and I have the whipped topping ready. How gentle do I need to be?

Add 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping and fold gently with a spatula, turning the mixture over itself rather than stirring hard. Stop when no streaks remain, so the filling stays light and evenly chocolate.
I'm making Easy Punch for a group. Can you walk me through what to set out before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put a large punch bowl on the counter, then set out 4 (0.13 ounce) packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder and 2 (46 fluid ounce) cans of pineapple juice.
The bowl is ready, and I have the strawberry drink mix and both cans of pineapple juice. What else belongs in the bowl?
You'll also need 3 cups white sugar and 4 quarts water. Keep a long spoon or ladle nearby so you can stir everything thoroughly.
I've measured the sugar, and the water is in a pitcher. Should I add things in any particular order?
Add the strawberry drink mix, pineapple juice, sugar, and water to the large punch bowl. Pour slowly so the bowl doesn't splash over while you combine them.
Everything is in the punch bowl, but I can still see some sugar settling near the bottom.
Keep stirring across the bottom and around the edges until the sugar and drink mix are fully dissolved. The punch should look evenly colored with no gritty layer left behind.
The color looks even now, and I don't feel much sugar at the bottom with the spoon. What comes after that?
Stir in the ginger ale gently so you keep some of the fizz. Add it close to serving time if you want the punch to stay bubbly.
I'm adding the ginger ale now. Should I stir hard enough to mix it completely?
Use a gentle fold-and-stir motion just until it's combined. Avoid vigorous stirring, since that can knock out the carbonation.
It's mixed and looks ready. Any serving tips before I put it out?
Serve it chilled from the punch bowl with a ladle. If it will sit out for a while, keep extra chilled punch or ginger ale nearby to refresh the bowl as needed.
I'd like to make Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth. Can you guide me from the beginning?
In this Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth step, set out a large pot and measure 2 quarts water. You'll also need 12 ounces beef shank for the broth base.
I've got the pot, water, and beef shank ready. Are the vegetables going in today too?
Have them prepared and nearby: 2 large onions, chopped, and 2 large carrots, sliced. The recipe has you start by building the broth with the water and beef first.
The onions are chopped and the carrots are sliced. Should I fill the pot now?
Yes. Pour the 2 quarts water into the large pot, put it on the stove, and bring the water to a boil.
The water is heating. Do I add the beef before it boils or wait?
In this Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth step, wait until the water reaches a boil, then place the 12 ounces beef shank into the pot.
It's boiling now, and the beef is in. How strong should the heat be?
Lower the heat so it simmers steadily rather than rolling hard. Let the beef shank simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
I'll set a timer for that. After the simmer, am I doing anything else tonight?
Once the 1 1/2 hours are up, take the pot off the heat and let the broth cool overnight.
The broth cooled overnight. What should I do with the meat now?
Lift the meat out of the broth, trim away any gristle, and cut the meat into medium sized pieces. Set those pieces aside for the next stage of the cawl.
I'm making Chocolate Covered Banana Pie today. Can you help me get the crust part started?
Absolutely. Set out 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers, 1/2 cup chopped pecans, and 2/3 cup melted butter. You'll also need 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips for the pie, plus a 9 x 13 inch pan.
In this Chocolate Covered Banana Pie step, the wafers are crushed, but I'm not sure how fine they should be before I mix them.
Aim for small, even crumbs so they press together easily with the butter. A few slightly larger bits are fine, especially with the chopped pecans mixed in.
I've got the crumbs in a bowl with the pecans. Do I pour in all the melted butter at once?
Yes, pour in the full 2/3 cup melted butter, then stir until the vanilla wafer crumbs and pecans look evenly moistened.
The mixture looks damp and sandy. What pan prep do I need?
Use the 9 x 13 inch pan and press the crumb mixture across the bottom in an even layer. Push it into the corners so the thickness is consistent.
Should I pack it firmly with my hands or use something flat?
Either works, but the bottom of a measuring cup makes it easier to compact the crust evenly without leaving ridges.
The crust is pressed in. What oven temperature and time am I using?
Here, bake it at 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, for 5 minutes.
It just came out of the oven. Do I add the chocolate chips while it's warm?
For the recipe step you're on, let the crust cool after baking. Keep the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips ready for the chocolate-covered pie portion once the cooled crust is needed.
I'm making Gingered Mango Salsa—can you help me get it ready without overcomplicating it?
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl and measure 1 cup chopped peeled mango into it when you're ready.
The mango is chopped and in the bowl. Should the onion go in raw?
Yes, add it raw: stir in 1/4 cup chopped red onion so it stays crisp and gives the salsa a little bite.
Got it. I have cilantro rinsed—how much should I mince?
Mince enough fresh cilantro to make 1/4 cup, then add it to the mango and red onion.
The cilantro is in. I'm squeezing limes now; what amount am I aiming for?
You need 1/4 cup lime juice. Pour it over the ingredients once it's measured.
Everything is in the bowl. Do I need to mash the mango or keep it chunky?
Keep it chunky. Gently toss everything together so the lime juice coats the mango, onion, and cilantro evenly.
It's mixed and looks bright. Can I serve it right away?
Let it stand for 30 minutes before serving. That rest gives the lime juice time to pull the flavors together.
Should I cover the bowl while it sits on the counter?
Yes, cover the bowl lightly while it stands, then give the salsa one more gentle stir before serving.
I'd like to make Famous Caramel Cookie Bars. Can you stay with me while I get organized?

Absolutely. Set out 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 individually wrapped caramels, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips. Go ahead and unwrap the caramels before you start heating anything.
The caramels are unwrapped, and I have a tray ready. Should the cookies be spaced out or touching?
Place the shortbread cookies on a baking sheet or tray in a single layer. A little space between them helps when you spoon the caramel on, but they do not need much room.
All 40 cookies are lined up. What pan should I use for melting the caramel?
Use a small saucepan. Add the 35 unwrapped caramels with the 1/4 cup water, then set the pan over medium-low heat.
They're in the saucepan now. How often should I stir so they don't stick?
Stir frequently while the caramels melt in the water. Keep the heat at medium-low so the mixture smooths out gently instead of scorching.
The caramel is mostly melted but still has a few soft lumps. Should I keep it on the heat?
Yes, keep stirring over medium-low heat just until the lumps disappear and the caramel looks smooth enough to spoon.
It's smooth now. I'm worried about putting too much on each cookie.
Spoon a thin line of caramel over each cookie. Aim for a narrow stripe rather than a thick layer so the caramel sets neatly.
The caramel is on the cookies. Do they sit out, or should I chill them right away?
Place the cookies in the refrigerator until the caramel is set. Once the caramel feels firm, they're ready to serve or store.
I'm making Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken. Can you stay with me while I get it started?
Absolutely. Set out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, plus salt and pepper for seasoning.
Chicken is out on a plate. Are there any pantry items or cans I need before I heat the pan?
Yes—grab 2 teaspoons olive oil and 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions.
I have the oil and the can. Should I open the tomatoes now or focus on the chicken first?
Focus on the chicken first. Season both sides of each chicken breast with salt and pepper so they're ready to go straight into the skillet.
Both sides are seasoned. What kind of pan setup should I use?
Use a large skillet and heat the 2 teaspoons olive oil over medium-high heat.
The skillet is hot and the oil is moving around easily. Do the chicken breasts go in all at once?
Place the chicken in the skillet in a single layer if they fit. Let them brown, then turn them once to brown the other side.
They're browning, but I don't want to keep flipping them. Just one turn, right?
Right—turn each piece once, just enough to get color on both sides.
Both sides have some browning now. What do I do with the chicken before adding anything else?
Remove the chicken from the pan and set it aside for the next part of the recipe.

source_seed.recipe_title: Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken

messages.content: I'm making Escargots Vol au Vent today. Can you stay with me while I get the snails and butter ready?
Absolutely. Set out 12 helix snails without shells and 1/2 cup softened butter so both are ready to work with.
The snails are out of the package, and the butter is soft. What aromatics should I chop?
Finely chop 2 cloves of garlic and 1 green onion. You'll be mixing them into the butter, so smaller pieces will spread through it better.
Garlic and green onion are chopped. Do I need the oven on before I rinse anything?
Yes, get the oven heating to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the mixture is prepared.
Oven is heating. The escargots look a little wet—how should I handle them?
Drain the escargots, rinse them under cold water, then drain them again well. You want them clean and not carrying extra water into the butter mixture.
They're rinsed and sitting in the strainer. Should I pat them dry or start the butter bowl?
Let them finish draining while you start the bowl. Add the softened butter, chopped garlic, chopped green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine to a mixing bowl.
I've got everything in the bowl, including the parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine. What texture am I aiming for?
Mix thoroughly until the butter looks evenly seasoned and the garlic, green onion, herbs, spices, and wine are distributed throughout.
The butter mixture is smooth with little green bits throughout. Anything I should check before using it with the snails?
Make sure the escargots have drained again after the cold rinse, and give the butter mixture one last stir so the seasonings stay even before you combine or portion it for the vol-au-vent.
I'd like to make Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts today. Can you guide me while I set up?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup water for the syrup, and keep a pot handy for blanching the almonds.
Sugar and water are measured. Is there anything floral or acidic that goes into this?
Yes—measure 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice and 2 tablespoons orange flower water. Those will flavor the syrup.
Those are ready. For the almonds, what pot setup do I need?
Fill a pot with 6 cups of water and bring it to a boil. That hot water is for loosening the almond skins.
The water is boiling now. Should I keep the burner on when I add the almonds?
Here, take the pot off the heat, then add the almonds to the hot water.
They're in the pot off the burner. How long should they sit?
Let the almonds soak for about 5 minutes. After that, drain them and peel off the skins.
I'm peeling them now. Some are damp—do they need to be dry before toasting?
Yes, spread the peeled almonds out on baking sheets so moisture can escape as they bake.
The almonds are spread out. What oven temperature am I using, and what should they look like?
Bake them at 200 degrees F, which is 95 degrees C, until they're completely dry and toasted.
I'd like to make Festive Shortbread Logs. Can you stay with me while I get started?

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and 2 cups all-purpose flour. You'll also want a mixing bowl, a spoon or mixer, and a little extra flour for your hands when shaping.
The butter is soft, and I've got the sugar measured. Should they go in together?
Yes. Put the softened butter and confectioners' sugar into the mixing bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and lighter, with no big streaks of butter left.
It's getting creamy, but a bit of sugar is still on the sides of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides, then mix a little longer so the butter and confectioners' sugar are evenly combined before you add anything else.
That looks even now. I have the vanilla open.
Add 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the bowl and mix just until it's worked through the butter-sugar mixture.
The vanilla is mixed in. Do I dump in all the flour?
Add the 2 cups all-purpose flour gradually instead of all at once. Mix as you go so the dough comes together evenly and doesn't puff flour out of the bowl.
The dough is thick and a little crumbly near the bottom. Is that okay?
That's normal for shortbread. Keep mixing until the flour is fully incorporated and the dough holds together when pressed gently.
It holds together now. How do I form the logs without everything sticking to my hands?

Lightly flour your hands, scoop tablespoonfuls of batter, and shape each portion into a small log-shaped cookie. Place them as you shape them, and dust your hands again only if the dough starts sticking.
I'm making Cinnamon Crackle Cookies and have my mixer out. Can you talk me through the dough from the start?
For Cinnamon Crackle Cookies, set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're ready to cream together smoothly.
Both are in the mixing bowl. Which sugars go in with them?
In this Cinnamon Crackle Cookies step, add 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar to the bowl with the butter and shortening.
The sugars are measured. What texture am I looking for once I start mixing?
Cream the butter, shortening, and both sugars until the mixture looks blended and lighter, with no big streaks of fat left in the bowl.
It looks smooth and fluffy now. I see the recipe mentions egg and extracts, but they weren't in my first pile.
Go ahead and add the egg and extracts at this point, then mix well so they're fully worked into the creamed mixture.
That's mixed in. I've got the dry ingredients nearby; should they all go in at once?
Combine the next eight ingredients together in a separate bowl first, then add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture.
The dough is coming together and getting thicker. Do I stop as soon as the dry streaks disappear?
Yes, stop once the dry ingredients are incorporated. Overmixing isn't needed here; you just want an even cookie dough.
Ready to portion it. How big should I make the cookies, and what do I do with the baking sheets?
Shape the dough into 1-in balls, roll each ball in sugar, and place them spaced apart on ungreased baking sheets.
I'm making Flavorful Rice Dressing 2 and have a large bowl out. Can you walk me through what to prep first?
Start by tearing 7 slices of day-old bread and 1 cup of corn bread into rough pieces. Put them in the large bowl so they're ready to soften.
The breads are torn and in the bowl. How wet should I make them?
Pour in 2/3 cup hot water and lightly toss everything together. You're just moistening the bread, not mashing it into a paste.
That looks damp but still chunky. I also have celery on the board—how much goes in?
Use 1/2 cup thinly sliced celery. Keep it ready for the skillet with the onion and mushrooms.
Skillet is on the stove. Do I cook the celery by itself or with the other vegetables?
Sauté the celery, onion, and mushrooms together in oil until they're tender, stirring constantly so the pieces soften evenly and don't catch.
The vegetables are tender and the bread mixture is waiting. Should I drain anything before combining?
If there's a lot of extra oil in the skillet, leave the excess behind, then stir the sautéed vegetables into the bread mixture.
They're mixed in. The bowl smells good, but the texture is still loose in spots.
Fold it gently from the bottom of the bowl so the moist bread and vegetables are evenly distributed without crushing the dressing.
Okay, it's more even now. What's the last thing I should do before it's ready for the next stage?
Add the remaining ingredients called for in your recipe and mix well, stopping once everything is evenly combined.
I'm making Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread in my bread machine. Can you help me set it up without missing anything?

Absolutely. For the ingredients listed here, put out 1 1/3 cups water, 2 tablespoons softened butter, 3 tablespoons honey, and 1 1/2 cups bread flour. You'll also need sunflower seeds ready for later in the knead cycle.
I've got the water measured and the butter softening. Does the order matter in the bread machine pan?
Yes, use the order recommended by your bread machine's manufacturer. Add everything except the sunflower seeds to the pan in that order.
My machine usually starts with liquids, so I'll add the water, honey, and butter before the flour. Should the sunflower seeds stay out completely for now?
Keep the sunflower seeds out for now. They go in only when the machine sounds its alert during the knead cycle.
The pan is loaded with the water, softened butter, honey, and bread flour. Which cycle should I choose?
In this Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread step, select the basic white cycle on the bread machine, then press start.
It's running now. I'm staying nearby for the beep—what am I listening for?
Listen for the add-in alert during the knead cycle. When it sounds, open the lid briefly and add the sunflower seeds.
If the dough is moving around while I add them, do I need to stop the machine?
No need to stop it unless your machine's manual says to. Just add the sunflower seeds when the alert sounds, then let the basic white cycle continue.
The seeds are in. Is there anything else I should do while it finishes?

At this point, let the bread machine complete the cycle. The key recipe steps are done: ingredients went in except the sunflower seeds, the basic white cycle was started, and the seeds were added at the knead-cycle alert.
I'm making Easy Marinated Vegetables and have a pot, colander, and mixing bowl out. Can you guide me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups broccoli florets and 1 1/2 cups cauliflower florets, since those will get a quick blanch before everything is mixed.
The broccoli and cauliflower are measured. Should I cut the bell pepper and cucumber before starting the water?
Yes, that's a good time to do it. Cut 1 green bell pepper into 1 inch pieces, then peel, seed, and chop the cucumber.
Pepper is in chunks, and the cucumber is peeled and chopped. What should happen at the stove?
Fill a large pot with water, salt it, and bring it to a boil. Keep the colander nearby so you can drain the florets right away.
The salted water is boiling. Do both florets go in together?
They do. Add the broccoli and cauliflower florets to the boiling water at the same time, and let them cook for just one minute.
One minute is up. They look brighter but still firm.
That's what you want. Drain the florets in the colander, then rinse them so they stop cooking and cool down for the salad.
They're rinsed and draining. Should they be dry before I add the other vegetables?
Let them drain well so the dressing doesn't get watered down. Once they're not dripping, move the broccoli and cauliflower to a medium size mixing bowl.
They're in the bowl with the bell pepper and cucumber. How do I bring it all together?
Add the carrot and Italian salad dressing, then toss everything together in the medium size mixing bowl until the broccoli, cauliflower, bell pepper, cucumber, and carrot are evenly coated.
Carrot Pineapple Cake I is what I'm cooking today. Can you keep me on track? I've got my mixing bowls out and want to make sure I start in the right order.
For Carrot Pineapple Cake I, set your oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you prep the pan and dry ingredients.
The oven is heating. What pan should I use, and do I need to line it?
For Carrot Pineapple Cake I, use a 9x13 inch pan. Grease it well, then dust it with flour so the cake releases more easily after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. I'm measuring the dry ingredients now—what goes in that bowl?
Measure in 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 teaspoon salt.
I have those in the bowl. The recipe mentions cinnamon in the mixing step—should that go with the dry ingredients too?
Yes, mix the cinnamon in with the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt so the spices and leavening are evenly distributed.
Should I whisk them or just stir with a spoon?
A whisk is best here because it breaks up small clumps and spreads the baking soda and baking powder through the flour mixture.
On Carrot Pineapple Cake I, the dry mix looks even. How do I add the wet ingredients without making a mess?
For this batch of Carrot Pineapple Cake I, make a well in the center of the dry mixture, then add the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla into that well.
Once everything is in the well, should I beat it hard or fold it together?
Start gently from the center and pull the dry ingredients in gradually. Mix until the batter comes together evenly, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed.
I'm making Fresh Apple Cake today. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil, 2 cups white sugar, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract. You'll also want a 10 inch tube pan ready for the batter.
The oil, sugar, eggs, and vanilla are on the counter. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and heat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). That way it's ready by the time the batter is prepared.
Oven is on. I found the tube pan—what should I do to it so the cake releases cleanly?
Grease the one 10 inch tube pan well, making sure to coat the center tube and the edges where cake can stick.
Pan is greased. I've got a large bowl out; do the wet ingredients go in there with the sugar?
Yes. In the large bowl, beat together the vegetable oil, beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white sugar until the mixture looks evenly combined.
It's mixed and glossy, but the sugar still looks a little grainy. Is that okay?
That's fine for this stage. Keep it evenly blended, but you don't need to dissolve every grain of sugar before moving on.
What dry ingredients should I prepare next? I don't want to dump them straight in if they need sifting.
Sift together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a separate bowl so the leavening and spices are distributed evenly.
The dry bowl is sifted. Before I combine anything, can you recap where I should be?

You should have the oven preheated to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), one greased 10 inch tube pan, a wet mixture of oil, eggs, vanilla, and sugar, and a separate sifted mixture of flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
I want to make Cookie Bowl. Can you guide me through what to set out before I start?
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup sliced almonds.
I've got the dry ingredients on the counter. Do I need to start heating the oven yet?
Yes, get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready when the bowl form is prepared.
While it heats, what pan or bowl should I use for shaping it?
Use either a 9x5 inch loaf pan or a metal bowl. Turn it upside down, then cover the outside with foil.
Should the foil be tight around the outside, or just loosely covering it?
Wrap it snugly around the outside so the surface is covered and the shape is easy to work over.
Okay, the pan is upside down and foiled. Where does it go?
Set the covered upside-down pan or bowl onto a cookie sheet.
I'm ready to mix. Which ingredients go together at this point?
Stir together the flour, cocoa powder, salt, and sliced almonds until the dry mixture looks evenly combined.
The mixture looks uniform. Do I do anything else with it right now?
For this part of the recipe, just set that dry mixture aside while the oven finishes preheating and the foiled form is ready on the cookie sheet.
I want to make California Chicken tonight. Can you guide me while I get set up?

Absolutely. Put out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1 pinch salt. You'll also want a skillet, and go ahead and get the oven warming to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
The oven is heating, and the chicken breasts are on a plate. Should the skillet be hot before I add anything?
Yes, warm the skillet over medium heat, then add the 1 teaspoon olive oil so it can coat the pan lightly before the chicken goes in.
The oil is shimmering a bit. Do I season the chicken before it hits the pan?

Sprinkle on the 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, then place the chicken breasts in the skillet. If you're following the recipe wording, this is the point where the chicken and onion flavor go into the pan together.
They're in the skillet now. How long should I leave them cooking?
Cook them for about 15 minutes total, turning as needed, until the chicken is browned and just about done.
What should the surface look like when it's browned enough?
Look for a golden-brown color on the outside rather than pale spots. The chicken should feel firmer than when it started, but the recipe's cue is browned and just about done.
I'm seeing good color. Should I add the salt now or wait?
Add the 1 pinch salt now, along with pepper to taste if you want it, so the seasoning lands while the chicken is still hot.
The chicken looks finished in the skillet. Anything else before serving?
Let it rest briefly after cooking so the juices settle, then serve the California Chicken hot. If any pieces look less done than the others, give those a little extra skillet time before plating.
I'm ready to cook Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes. What should be ready before I begin? I've got the potatoes out but want to make sure I prep them right.
Absolutely. Cut 1 1/2 pounds of new potatoes into wedges, keeping the pieces fairly similar in size so they coat evenly later.
The wedges are cut. What should I set up next—oven or skillet?
Get the oven preheating to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C. While it heats, place a skillet on the stove so it can get hot.
Oven is heating, and the skillet is hot. How much butter goes in?
Add 4 tablespoons butter to the hot skillet and let it melt fully. Swirl the pan a little if needed so it melts evenly without sitting in one spot.
The butter is melted and bubbling a bit. When do I add the rosemary?
Stir in 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, then add salt and pepper to taste. Give it a quick stir so the rosemary seasons the butter.
It smells good. Should I season heavily, or keep it light?
Keep it balanced: enough salt and pepper to season the butter, but not so much that it overwhelms the fresh rosemary and potatoes.
I'm ready to add the potatoes. Do they go straight into the skillet?
Yes. Add the potato wedges to the melted rosemary butter and turn them until every piece is evenly coated.
Some wedges have more butter than others. What's the best way to even that out before roasting?
Use a spoon or spatula to scoop the butter from the bottom of the skillet back over the potatoes, then toss gently until the wedges look evenly glossy and coated.
